events.title: Weekly 22nd Street Bridge Bannering Over Hwy 94 | Wednesday Mornings - Visibility Brigade
events.description:
We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: ICE Out of SLO County! Show Up and Speak up at the County Board Meeting

location.venue: SLO County Board Of Supervisors Chambers, Katcho Achadjian Government Center

events.description:
Action Alert: Speak up About ICE Commandeering County Property!

Please plan to attend the Board of Supervisors meeting on one or two Tuesdays a month at 9:00 AM at 1055 Monteret Street in SLO.

The board voted to prohibit ICE from using county-owned or controlled property as a staging area, processing location, or operations base for federal immigration enforcement. The resolution also stipulates that non-public areas of any County facility may not be used for immigration enforcement without a valid warrant, writ, or order signed by a judicial officer.

We encourage you to attend meetings in person or via zoom or to submit written comments to urge the county to enforce this resolution at the jail. Currently, ICE conducts raids in the public lobby and transfers individuals via non-public sally ports without judicial warrants. If enforced, this resolution could end these operations. The sheriff facilitates these raids and has even cordoned off an area in the lobby for ICE agents to use for their operations.

How to take action:

  - Attend a Meeting: 9:00 AM. And make submit a slip to make a comment for General Comment on a Non agenda item.
  - Submit Written Comments: Boardofsups@co.slo.ca.us
  - Review the Full Resolution: https://agenda.slocounty.ca.gov/iip/sanluisobispo/file/getfile/178340

events.title: UTSA Main Campus Voter Registration Events -  Tuesdays & Thursdays

address_lines: Paseo Principal in front of the McKinney Humanities Building (MH)

events.description:
⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!

Ready to do the work that actually works?
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact Voter Mobilization shift at UTSA! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will:

Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day
Shift Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

1pm-1:30pm: Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

2:00pm-4pm Voter Mobilization | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

4:00-4:15pm: Debrief | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

events.title: Northwest Vista College Voter Registration Event

address_lines: Across the lake from the Wildcat Cafe near Live Oak Hall

events.description:
Are you serious about turning the tide in Texas? Are you tired of sitting on the sidelines and ready to make a difference?

## Sign up here to join us in registering eligible Northwest Vista College students to VOTE!
___
All volunteers are welcome! 

*HOWEVER*, to *register voters* at this event, you **MUST** be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (**VDR**) in at least **Bexar County**.

If you're interested in becoming a Volunteer Deputy Registrar, you can take our [VDR Training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

### How to prepare:

If this is your first time volunteering with Powered by People, please sign up for our quick [**New Volunteer Zoom Training**](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)!
This will help you get up to speed with how we run events and how to use REACH.

Then, review our [**REACH Guide**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hgXy1A-xYafd4donvC18mGerT05S2yXICe5TLCX2hSE/edit?tab=t.0) as it has helpful information on using REACH in the field.
___
### Where we'll be:

**PARKING:** Lot 8 near Redbud Hall Circle is recommended. All parking at Northwest Vista College is free for both students and visitors, including [Prickly Pear Parking Garage](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oZZ7yKFtSoV5s9m66).

**MEETING LOCATION:** 
Outside of [Live Oak Hall](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fqodE1RmxiEgdSZV6) across the lake from the [Wildcat Cafe](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DCzho1s6JevHiFTM7).
___
### What to bring:
Please bring your **fully charged phone** with REACH installed, water, and comfortable shoes.

If you are a *Volunteer Deputy Registrar*, please bring your **VDR number** for Bexar County (and any nearby counties where you have VDR reciprocity). 

Clipboards, pens, voter registration forms, and other materials will be provided at the event, but feel free to bring your own just in case.

*In 2024 Adam Gray flipped the seat by only 187 votes. Let's talk to Democrats now to hold CD13 in 2026, as we take back the House majority!*

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. At the staging location you will receive brief training and all the supplies you will need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a fully charged smartphone is a must.

Read more about how Adam Gray always puts the Central Valley first - https://gray.house.gov/

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: PPT & T4APA! Communications Committee
events.description:
Building the narrative of Transit Justice in our community is a critical part of our work. The Communications Committee hosts monthly virtual working meetings to tell the story of PPT’s campaigns, successes, and struggles. During these meetings, attendees help produce content that communicates our work to the public— including writing blogs, editing videos, creating content for our social media channels, curating photography, and doing graphic design.

Since 2025, the Communications Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Communications Committee if...
- You love writing and/or social media content creation
- You have experience with photography, graphic design, or web design

## 2026 Training Series

In 2026, our Communications Committee will be conducting a Comms Training Series! Each meeting will focus on a different core skill for communications work within organizing and justice movements. 

Here is a look at our syllabus for the year. We will release RSVP links on a rolling basis, so stay tuned to sign up for future dates! 


**September: Telling your story in social media videos**

Organizing is all about sharing your story—and short-form social media videos are where people are listening. It's easier than you think to tell your story in a social media video; no experience or special equipment required, just a smartphone or tablet! This is a great opportunity to practice for the upcoming Week Without Driving.

**October: Photographing and videoing the movement**

What makes a good photograph, or video, for our work? Review great photos and videos. In this session, we'll tips and tricks for documenting direct actions.

**November: Letters to the Editor and Op-Eds**

Details TBD

### Past Workshops in 2026 (including so you can see what we've already learned!*

**January: Narrative Change Theory: Communications + Organizing**

**February: Telling an Effective Transit Story**

**April: Social Media Strategy for the Movement**

**May: Documenting Direct Actions on Social Media**

**June: Preparing for Harrisburg 2026 Day of Action**

**July: Designing for the Movement**

**August: Canva Bootcamp**
events.accessibility_notes:

ASL and Spanish interpretation is available on request, but must be booked in advance. Given availability constraints for our interpreters, we are most likely to successfully book with 2 weeks or more of lead time. If interpreters are not available, Closed Captioning will be available for virtual meetings. Please email clair@pittsburghforpublictransit.org when registering to request interpretation.

events.title: ICE Out of SLO County! Abolish ICE!
events.description:
Rally and vigil every Sunday between 10 am - 11:30 am at the corner of Hwy 1 and Kansas Avenue. Join us for a rally to protest ICE activity in our beloved community and to hold vigil for those in our community abducted by ICE. The sheriff chooses to allow ICE agents into the jail to abduct people despite CA laws that would allow him not to cooperate. Despite the Board’s vote to stop commandeering the jail to make warrantless arrests, it continues unabated. The SLOSO facilitates 3 to 4 ICE abductions of people released from the jail per week. They account for over half of all the kidnappings in the county. People are detained out the jail who are being cited and released pending arraignment. They are denied due process and are guilty of no crime. Kidnappings at the jail are no different than the kidnappings in our community.

It IS happening here! ICE is in our community multiple times a week abducting people from the SLO County jail. Imagine you are waiting for a loved one to be released from the SLO county jail.  But before you can be reunited with them, they are kidnapped by masked secret police from the jail right before your eyes. Everyone deserves the right to be released from the jail safely regardless of immigration status. 

People taken at the jail are being denied due process and legal representation. They are separated from their children, families and loved ones. Don't turn your back on what is happening in our community. Everyone who is released from the jail should be released regardless of where they were born.

Bring large signs and banners centering calls for abolishing ICE and keeping it out of SLO and everywhere. If featuring signs with names of people murdered by ICE, please list all the people murdered by ICE. And the countless people harmed and disappeared whose names we do not know. Please stay off the road and stay safe.

events.title: EDF Action 2026 Environmental Book Club
events.description:
Join us the second Saturday of each month for our environmental book club!  We will be discussing these books and documentaries in 2026: 

JAN: Here Comes the Sun
By Bill McKibben 
Available on Amazon Paperback and Audible audio book 

The book explores the rapid, cheap growth of solar and wind power and how it offers humanity a genuine, hopeful chance to overcome the climate crisis and build a better civilization, despite fossil fuel industry opposition.

FEB:  A Future We Can Love 
By Susan Bauer-Wu 
Available on Amazon paperback + free audio book with Audible membership

Inspired by a conversation between the Dalai Lama and Greta Thunberg spoke for the first time in January 2021, millions of people around the world took notice. This book captures the lessons that came from that interaction. 


MAR: The Fragile Earth
By David Remnick, Henry Finder 
Available at local library, Hoopla and Amazon Paperback or Audible audio book

A collection of essays that tell the story of climate change—its past, present, and future—taking readers from Greenland to the Great Plains, and into both laboratories and rain forests.

APR: The Genius of Earth Day
By Adam Rome
Available at local library, Hoopla, Amazon + free audiobook with Audible membership.

The story of the first Earth Day is inspiring: it had a power, a freshness, and a seriousness of purpose that are difficult to imagine today. Earth Day 1970 created an entire green generation. 

MAY 9th:  Amplify
By Adam Met 

SPECIAL GUEST:  ADAM MET, PhD, Activist, Musician and Author

JUN: Unsettled by Steven Koonin 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback or Audible audio book

Koonin was the top science advisor to the Obama administration.  When it comes to climate change, the media, politicians, and other prominent voices have declared that “the science is settled.” In reality, the climate is changing, but the why and how aren’t as clear as you’ve probably been led to believe. Koonin takes listeners behind the headlines, dispels popular myths, and unveils little-known truths. 

JUL: Documentary:  Ice on Fire | Free on Youtube (1:37)
(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AP2IE8Upehc) 
Narrated by Leonardo DiCaprio

"Ice on Fire" explores the many ways we reduce carbon inputs to the atmosphere and, more importantly, how to "draw" carbon down, bringing CO2 out of the atmosphere and thus paving the way for global temperatures to go down. Through visiting visionaries and scientists young and old, the film explores the deep hope that we can turn away from the brink.  

AUG: Running Out By Lucas Bessire
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback

The imminent depletion of the Ogallala and other aquifers around the world is a defining planetary crisis of our times. Running Out explores aquifer depletion and the deeper layers through which it gains meaning and force. Anthropologist Lucas Bessire journeyed back to Western Kansas, where five generations of his family lived as irrigation farmers and ranchers, to try to make sense of this vital resource and its loss.

SEPT: Half Earth 
By Edward O. Wilson 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

In order to stave off the mass extinction of species, including our own, we must move swiftly to preserve the biodiversity of our planet. In this "visionary blueprint for saving the planet" (Stephen Greenblatt), Half-Earth argues that the situation facing us is too large to be solved piecemeal and proposes a solution commensurate with the magnitude of the problem: dedicate fully half the surface of the Earth to nature. 

OCT: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind (watch the movie or read the book)
Movie: Find it on Youtube or Netflix 
Book: Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

Born to a family of farmers, Malawian agricultural engineer William Kamkwamba made headlines in 2001 when he built a functioning windmill out of old bicycle parts and scraps. (At the time, he was just 14 years old.) The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind, based on Kamkwamba’s memoir of the same name, tells the amazing true story of how he built a wind turbine and saved his small farming village from famine.

NOV: The Talking Earth (young adult)
by Jean George 
Available at the local library, on Hoopla and Amazon Paperback + Audiobook

Billie is a member of the Seminole Tribe, in a quest to identify facts over legend, she goes out into the Everglades alone, to stay until she can believe. In the wilderness, she discovers that she must listen to the land and animals in order to survive. With an otter, a panther cub, and a turtle as companions and guides, she begins to understand that the world of her people can give her the answers she seeks.

DEC:  A look back at our list of books - what did we learn? What is most memorable from our reading? 

_________________________________________________________
BOOK CLUB 2025 (For reference only) 

January 11th: [Documentary] Living the Change: Inspiring Stories for a Sustainable Future (Free Full Documentary)

February 8th: [Book] No is Not Enough, by Naomi Klein (Available on amazon, Hoopla, local library)

March 8th: [Book] The Language of Climate Politics, by Genevieve Guenther (available on amazon, Hoopla and local library)

April 12th: [Book] Silent Spring - Rachel Carson Let’s revisit the book that started our book club AND the environmental movement!

May 10th: [Podcast] How to save a planet - listen to a few episodes and come to the meeting to share what you learned. (https://gimletmedia.com/shows/howtosaveaplanet/episodes#show-tab-picker) find it on spotify: https://open.spotify.com/show/1KzrasExlM5dgMYwgFHns6

June 14th: [Book] It’s not that Radical | climate action to transform our world - Mikaela Loach

July 12th: [Documentary]: Climate extremes (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U8pLrRkqbb0)

August 9th: [Book] Earth for All, by Sandrine Dixson Decleve (available on Amazon)

September 13th: [Book] What if We Get it Right, by Ayana Elizabeth Johnson (Available in book and audio on Amazon)

October 11th: [Podcast] Climate Rising (https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/a-preview-of-cop29-what-business-leaders-should/id1482781075?i=1000675873770)

November 8th: [Book] The Good Ancestor, by Roman Krznaric (available on Amazon and Hoopla audio)

December 13th: Year end wrap up - what did we learn? 2026 Book Club

events.title: Overpass Visibility Brigade Action: Hwy 13 Oakland
events.description:
Start your week off getting in "Some Good Trouble"! Join us for an overpass visibility event in Oakland over Hwy-13 @Joaquin Miller/Lincoln Mountain/Monterey.

We’ll use huge letters to spell out an inspiring message for passing cars during the morning commute and wave to cars honking in support. Bring your signs as we will also be on the four corners waving to drivers as they pass by.

Message TBD in response to current events.

Here's what you need to know:

- Street parking is available on Mountain Blvd. and Joaquin Miller. Parking on Woodminster is available but meters start at 8:00 a.m. 

- It can be cool and windy on the overpass.

- Photos and video of this event may be shared publicly. If you'd rather not appear in photos/video, please tell the organizer (Jenny). 

- ** If police or counter-protesters visit the event: Rather than engage with them yourself, please let the organizer (Jenny) speak with them. If you're comfortable doing so, take video of the interaction from a safe distance. **  

- We use whistles on the overpass to signal "help" or "heads up." To avoid confusion, we do not use whistles as protest noisemakers. 

- Take care not to drop anything through the fence onto the roadway. Hold pompoms, signs, flags, etc inside -- not through -- the fencing.

- Be aware of traffic on the overpass. The intersection is very busy, with school traffic in both directions, and there are limited crosswalks. For safety, always cross in the crosswalk and do not jaywalk.

- Note that flying a drone over the freeway (i.e., to take photos/video) is not permitted. 

- Overpass visibility is a practice of nonviolent civil resistance. By participating in IEBOVB actions, you are indicating that you will refrain from violence.

To help plan overpass events/messages and learn how to get involved in other resistance projects, ** join Indivisible East Bay's Slack **  (https://join.slack.com/t/indivisibleeb/shared_invite/zt-3a7m0uwys-imIj1Pe5ySPuhpbtl0Eyow), where you'll find an #overpass_visibility_brigade channel.

events.title: Civic Watch: Anderson County Election Commission
events.description:
Election oversight works best when the public is paying attention.

The Anderson County Election Commission is a public body responsible for overseeing local election administration, approving key decisions, and conducting official election business in public meetings.

This Civic Watch event is a simple invitation for neighbors to attend, observe, and better understand how local election administration works. No speeches. No pressure. Just public participation in a public meeting.

If you’d like to attend with others, we’ll gather a few minutes beforehand and sit together.

What to expect:
• Observe the meeting and follow the agenda
• Take notes if you’d like
• Learn how decisions are made
• Public comment may be available depending on the meeting agenda, but participation is entirely optional

Why some residents are paying closer attention:
Earlier this year, the Anderson County Commission issued a vote of no confidence in the Administrator of Elections — an unusual action that raised broader public interest in how election administration is functioning locally.

How to follow official Election Commission business:
Meeting agendas, minutes, notices, and official information are posted by the Anderson County Election Commission here:
https://www.acelection.com/commissioners/

Current Election Commissioners:
D. Jane Miller (Chair)
William “Bear” Stephenson (Secretary)
William T. Gallaher
Marion Stanford
David Bradshaw

Administrator of Elections:
Mark Stephens

This is a civic observation event open to anyone interested in transparency, public process, and local government.

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Palmer Park
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has bathrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.
* Access to water, but please bring a filled water bottle. 

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

location.venue: Spartanburg County Administrative Building, Council Chambers

events.description:
Decisions that impact our community get made in public meetings, often with little public input in the room. The Spartanburg County Democratic Party is building a "Civic Watch" team to attend key local meetings, take notes for the party and the public, and sign up to speak during public comment when timely issues come up.

The Spartanburg County Legislative Delegation is made up of state House and Senate members representing Spartanburg County. They meet periodically throughout the year to address local legislative matters that require General Assembly action.

By attending these meetings as a volunteer observer, you'll help ensure our community stays informed about decisions being made by our state legislators on local issues. Whether you choose to speak during public comment, take notes, or simply be a presence in the room, your participation matters.

No prior experience is necessary—just a willingness to show up and pay attention to what's happening in your community.

We also ask that attendees purchase something to eat or drink to thank our generous hosts at Pilot Project (and don’t forget to tip your server!).

Let’s write, connect, and make an impact - together.

events.title: Arizona Native Democrats: Café 6
events.description:
Arizona Native Democrats invites you to join us for the relaunch of Café 6, a recurring community conversation space kicking off in February and held on the first and third Tuesday evenings from 5:30–6:30 PM.

Originally rooted in Legislative District 6, Café 6 has grown alongside our movement. While the name remains the same, this space is no longer limited to LD6. Café 6 is now an open gathering for Tribal and rural communities across Arizona, reflecting our expanded organizing work and statewide reach.

Café 6 is a space to learn together, share knowledge, and engage in meaningful dialogue about the issues impacting our communities. Each session will feature guest speakers who may include advocates, organizers, community leaders, candidates, policymakers, or subject-matter experts. Topics may include (but are not limited to):

- Voting rights and civic engagement
- Water rights and environmental justice
- Climate change and energy issues
- Sacred lands and cultural protection
- Arizona-specific policy and legislative updates
- Campaigns, advocacy efforts, and community organizing work

These conversations are designed to be accessible, educational, and interactive, with time for participants to listen, ask questions, and engage in discussion. Whether you are deeply involved in advocacy or just beginning to learn about these issues, Café 6 is a welcoming space for you.

All are encouraged to join, sign up, listen in, participate, and invite friends or community members who may be interested. Café 6 is about building understanding, strengthening community, and staying connected to the work happening across Indian Country in Arizona.

events.title: Weekly Phone Bank: Calls to Action with Arizona Native Democrats
events.description:
Join Arizona Native Democrats for our weekly phone bank focused on action, empowerment, and movement-building in Native and tribal communities across Arizona.

Our phone banks have evolved beyond traditional volunteer recruitment. Based on strong community feedback, we now center our calls around real, timely calls to action that give people an opportunity to participate, speak up, and feel connected to something larger than themselves. These conversations are about sharing information, uplifting Native voices, and inviting community members to take meaningful action on issues that directly impact them.

Each week, our calls will focus on a current issue, campaign, or community priority, which may include:

- Contacting elected officials around urgent legislative or policy matters
- Supporting tribal sovereignty, environmental justice, or voting rights
- Sharing updates that affect specific tribes, regions, or Native communities
- Encouraging community members to take a simple but powerful next step

Arizona Native Democrats work across multiple tribal nations, and as we continue to expand our organizing efforts statewide, our calls may be directed to specific tribes or geographic areas depending on the issue at hand. Volunteers will always receive clear scripts, background context, and support before making calls.

Out-of-state volunteers are welcome and encouraged to join. These phone banks are a powerful way to stand in solidarity with Native communities, support grassroots organizing, and help move collective action forward, no prior experience required.

events.title: PPT & T4APA! Research Committee
events.description:
The Research Committee is the brain of PPT’s policy work, hosting weekly working meetings to conduct data and policy research in support of our campaigns. During these meetings, attendees analyze data, investigate policies active in other cities, and assemble reports that recommend action that can improve our transit system. [Check out the Research Committee’s past work](https://www.pittsburghforpublictransit.org/research-and-resources/) to see the types of projects you might collaborate on as part of the Research Committee.

Right now we have a few concurrent projects, namely:

- Identifying a ridership growth goal for Pittsburgh Regional Transit that matches the ridership growth in other similar transit systems, with recommendations for ways that they can meet that goal.

-Evaluating the Busline Refresh Draft 2.0 and publishing our research and feedback.

- Identifying the root causes of the drop in Pittsburgh Regional Transit service reliability to raise up solutions that work for transit riders and workers.

-Publishing a white paper about what local tax or referenda options should be available Pennsylvania municipalities in order to raise revenue for transit.

Since 2025, the Research Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Research Committee if...
- You have a knack for crunching numbers
- You consider yourself a policy wonk
- You love chasing research topics down a rabbit hole
- You have an academic or professional background in data, research or planning (although none is required to join the committee!)

**Note:** Research committee meetings often involve working closely with documents, on Google Docs or sourced from the internet. Please keep this in mind if that might pose an accessibility challenge for you.

events.title: Every Saturday Pullman Rally for Sanity #Indivisible #NoKings #HandsOff #MoveOn #50501

location.venue: On the sidewalk in front of Neill Public Library North Grand Avenue & Northeast Olsen Street, Pullman, WA 99163

events.description:
This is a local Indivisible event!

Hello, people who care about democracy! My name is Syd and I call myself the reluctant activist, because I'd really rather be home resting, crocheting and managing my health issues but I'm instead forced to fight fascism in America. Someone said that the best way to not feel hopeless is to get up and do something. I'll be the one with the flower pin in my hat and the loud voice. 

With the rapid assaults on our rights, the government cuts designed to hurt the poor and vulnerable, endlessly funding genocide and starting wars, I feel it's important that we protest this insanity. Since May of 2025 we have held a rally every Saturday. We meet from 12-2 on the sidewalk in front of the Neill Public Library. It's at the intersection of N Grand and Olson NE across from the Cougar Plaza.

We won't give up our rights to peacefully protest. We need to remind this administration that it's the people who have the power, it's supposed to be Congress that writes laws and declares war, that protest is legal but human trafficking is not. This Big Beautiful Killer Bill is the opposite of what our government should do for the people. Republicans are choosing to let people go hungry, lose insurance and frankly, die. Not to balance the budget, they're doing it to reward the wealthiest.

I know these are scary times and I appreciate your bravery. I have rallied here multiple times and usually the worst pushback is a few harsh words from a moving vehicle (that I can't hear). I simply reply with "I love you!" as loudly as I am able. It's fun and it prevents any hate from sticking to us. Mostly we get a lot of honking and waving. I find it invigorating, especially when we are surrounded by a lot of other rally-goers. I'm not downplaying the new steps towards full fascism this administration has taken and I don't want you to. Please take the necessary steps to protect yourself and your identity if you feel the need.

It's important that our protest remain on the sidewalk, stay at least 18" from the curb for your safety and to not block the traffic or crosswalks so we don't give the police a reason to arrest anyone. If someone tries to instigate trouble don't confront them and remain peaceful. Yell for me. If you have a whistle, blow it. Keep back and stay safe. Record video if you are able, so that authorities will be able to ID the agitator. 

Again, I expect no problem at our little events, I expect colorful, creative signs, lots of bubbles, sidewalk chalk and numbers of like-minded people who care about our country.  Get your feelings out on your signs, enjoy the marker fumes and chalk dust or use one of our many signs. Bring water. It's thirsty work.

If you have any questions contact me on the Rally4Sanity Facebook page 
p.s. Despite what Tr*mp and Fox News say, I have never received a paycheck for rallying against his theft of power, but I have noted his history of projection. Has he paid people to rally for him?

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in PA-10 York, PA with SwingLeftHoCoMD
events.description:
Knock on doors with Ground Truth in PA-10 York, PA with SwingLeftHoCoMD

October continues persuasion canvassing for the democratic candidate.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just wear comfortable shoes, bring a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.  If you've never canvassed before, we will pair you with an experienced partner. ***As people confirm their attendance, this spreadsheet will be updated with pairings:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/155_MgsRvJqq5yXQmHvso655AC_saL2htZEyLDU47lYY/edit?usp=sharing

We require you to attend the Ground Truth training that you received with your confirmation email and also listed below in the additional info.
We only want to spend 30 minutes or less before hitting the streets so we need you to prepare ahead of time based on your experience level.

Here are 2 carpool links to sign up to drive or to sign up for a ride:

Canvass Driver from your home location (or central parking area) to the meetup location. Sign-Up Form: https://airtable.com/app6LEMSyAjnXE8lo/shrLjEsy5IIHfWRh6?prefill_Which+local+group+are+you+working+with%3F=SwingLeft+Howard+County+MD

Drivers should use a clear and concise car title, which will be used on its own within the tool to identify a particular car. We recommend including the date, time, general departure location, and possibly group affiliation. For example, “8/13 at 9am from Glendale.”

Canvass Rider from one of the above locations to the meetup location Sign-Up Form https://airtable.com/app6LEMSyAjnXE8lo/shrRT1pQ8R1Ewmo4I/tblrmBdfIzuzTKqpt

After we finish canvassing, please plan to stay for a late lunch to meet more of your fellow canvassers and swap stories before heading home. Place is: 
Parma Pizza and Grill
1041 Haines Rd.
York, PA  17402
––

**About the program**

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Add Your Name: Tell Congress Pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act
events.description:
Add Your Name: Tell Congress Pass H.R. 14 — John Lewis Voting Rights Act

## H.R. 14 — John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act (PASS)

### TAKE ACTION NOW: Restore Voting Rights. Defend Democracy.

Democracy is not real if eligible voters can be blocked, targeted, or erased from the process. We are demanding Congress pass the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and restore strong federal protections against voter suppression and discrimination.

---

### Legislation  
**H.R. 14 — John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2025**  
https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/14

---

### What’s at risk  
Across the country, communities are facing:  
- discriminatory election rule changes  
- voter roll purges  
- manipulated district maps  
- targeted barriers that make voting harder, not easier  

And when voting access is weakened, our communities lose power over the decisions that shape our lives—schools, healthcare, safety, housing, and economic opportunity.

---

### Why this fight matters  
Voter suppression doesn’t always look like violence. Sometimes it looks like “policy.”  
Sometimes it looks like “procedure.”  
But the outcome is the same: **people locked out of democracy.**

---

### What we demand  
Congress must **PASS H.R. 14** and restore modern voting rights protections.

---

### The Advocacy League position  
✅ **SUPPORT / PASS**

---

events.title: Add Your Name: Tell Congress Stop the SAVE Act
events.description:
# Add Your Name: Tell the Senate STOP H.R. 22 (SAVE Act) — Protect Voting Rights

## TAKE ACTION NOW: Stop the SAVE Act. Protect Voter Access.

The SAVE Act **(H.R. 22)** is a voter suppression scheme disguised as “election security.” This bill would create new barriers to voter registration and threatens to block eligible voters from participating in federal elections through paperwork requirements and restrictive processes.

This is not how democracy is protected. This is how democracy is restricted.

---

## LEGISLATION
**H.R. 22 — SAVE Act (Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act)**  
https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/22

---

## WHAT’S AT RISK
H.R. 22 would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote in federal elections — adding new obstacles that will predictably hit hardest for:
- low-income voters  
- seniors  
- voters with name changes  
- voters who don’t have easy access to original documents  
- communities already targeted by voter suppression tactics  

This bill would make voting harder, not safer — and that is unacceptable.

---

## WHY THIS FIGHT MATTERS
Voter suppression doesn’t always look like intimidation at the polls.  
Sometimes it looks like “paperwork.”  
Sometimes it looks like “rules.”  
Sometimes it looks like “compliance.”  

But the outcome is the same: **eligible voters blocked from the ballot box.**

We refuse to let the freedom to vote become something only the privileged can easily access.

---

## WHAT WE DEMAND
The U.S. Senate must **REJECT H.R. 22 (SAVE Act)** and stop voter suppression.

---

## THE ADVOCACY LEAGUE POSITION
❌ **OPPOSE / STOP**

---

## TAKE ACTION NOW
**Add your name. Share this petition.**  
Tell the Senate: **STOP H.R. 22 (SAVE Act). Protect voter access. Protect democracy.**

Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities—just communicate with your Compost Manager.

* This site has public restrooms

events.description:
Join our States Win monthly Zooms to connect virtually as volunteers and neighbors, get the latest candidate/campaign news, hear about upcoming volunteer actions, and learn about the strategic importance of state legislatures as firewalls to Tr*mp's fascism, as we work to flip states from #redtoblue! 

Each month, we will share updates, important good news and be joined by a special guest speaker and/or highlight a special education topic key to our work.

Past Speaker Series guests have included: CA Attorney General Rob Bonta, Former U.S. Senator Barbara Boxer, Former U.S. Attorney General Janet Napolitano, Former Ohio Democratic Chair David Pepper, and VA State Senator Danica Roem.

We host virtual events on **Zoom the first Tuesday** of each month; in-person **Happy Hours on the last Tuesday** of each month; and in-person **Postcard events** on alternating third Sunday afternoons and Monday evenings each month;  plus marches, parties, auctions and more!

Since 2016, we've been building enduring progressive power in the states to improve people's lives by supporting over 185 state legislative candidates and community-based organizations led by people of color on the ground, like [Carolina Federation Fund, We are Down Home, Tennessee Immigrant & Refugee Rights Coalition (TIRRC) and The Equity Alliance](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sd016-nc-tn-sf?refcode=mobilize), who do critical grassroots work year round.

Last year, we won all 32 of our races—not only turning Virginia into a Democratic trifecta, but also flipping critical seats in Iowa and Mississippi to break GOP supermajorities. In Minnesota, we preserved Democratic control in a pivotal special election. 

In 2024, we flipped critical seats in the North Carolina House and the Wisconsin Senate, breaking GOP supermajorities. In Pennsylvania, we defended our hard-fought Democratic majority in the House, and in Minnesota, we preserved Democratic control in a pivotal special election. 

Before that, we helped to flip VA's House of Delegates blue, while also keeping a blue hold the State Senate, ensuring that 35 million women in the south didn't lose vital healthcare access from the ONLY southern state without an abortion ban.
 
In 2022, our volunteers supported 18 state legislative races in battleground states and ALL of our candidates won—including in Arizona and Nevada, where the candidates we supported directly were running (each chapter gets paired with two or more races each year).

To learn more about the impact and strategy of States Win in the lead up to the 2031 redistricting, visit [StatesWin.org] (https://stateswin.org/our-approach/#our-plan).

events.title: Saturday Stand Up
events.description:
Every Saturday, we stand on the curb and show our signs, count friendly beeps from passing cars and trucks.  And chat and get caught up with each other.  We have had about a dozen people lately, though we expect to have more this particular Saturday because of the problems in Minnesota.  The community to have a safe space to share our opinions.  

Our protest activity is lawful and safe.  The police know we are here because of my weekly emails to the liaison patrol officer.  We use the buddy system, so we are not out here alone.  We stay on the sidewalk.  We do not block the sidewalk.  We obey traffic rules.  We do not go on private property.  We do not do any violence or graffiti.  We remain aware of our surroundings and talk about what we see.  If someone approaches us to explain why we are stupid and wrong, we take one step away, turn partway toward them, and let them talk.  We do not respond, or if we feel compelled to respond, we say something neutral like “Have a nice day.”  Remaining excessively cheerful de-escalates many situations.  If something is escalating uncomfortably, some of us video, and some call 911.  And we help each other remember the rules. 

Bozeman Rising is a grassroots network of community members who are leading initiatives, mobilizing neighbors, and advancing Indivisible’s One Million Rising strategy to resist authoritarianism and build a fair and equitable society.

events.description:
**One voter and one conversation at a time ... that's how Democrats win!**

Studies have shown that turnout increases by up to 9 percentage points through door-to-door canvassing! 
 
Are you thinking about canvassing, but don't feel quite ready? If you've never canvassed before, or just need a refresher, join the Bay Area Coalition on Tuesdays, to talk about what your canvassing day will look like, including ..........

YOU CAN HELP SAVE OUR DEMOCRACY!

events.description:
**Join Swing Left Peninsula and the Bay Area Coalition as we call voters to encourage participation in the 2026 midterm elections and help take back the House.** We call California's CA=22 House District to turn out voters for Randy Villegas. We call other districts, ones where we'll have the most impact, as well.

We’ll provide training, support, a script and a list of voters to call. You’ll need a computer with a microphone (or a phone to use with your computer) to make calls.

If you have questions about this event, please RSVP and respond to confirmation email you receive to reach out to the host.


_By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. Our emails share timely, impactful actions (letter parties, phone banks, canvasses, voter registrations, and more) for strategic, toss-up races that will help us win back the House and other important races._

_Every email we send includes an unsubscribe link. If you don't want to be on our list, we want you to unsubscribe! (Please don't mark this email as spam, or we will have trouble reaching the people who DO want to hear from us.) You won't be resubscribed by us._

events.title: Sponsor a PhoneBanker as we Dial for Democracy in 2026
events.description:
### Can't make calls? You can still make a difference. 

**Sign up to sponsor a phonebanker!**

By supporting volunteer dials with your dollars, you'll help us recruit volunteer phone bankers and give callers the incentive to keep dialing! BONUS: your sponsorship donations go directly to our candidates and partner organizations, providing early $$ to hire staff and connect with even more voters. A DOUBLE-WIN!

**Here's how it works**:     

1.  Sign up today to sponsor a phonebanker. (Phonebanking begins May 4; your donation will help us recruit new phonebankers now.) 

2. Pick the number of phone bankers you'd like to sponsor. (We're looking to sponsor 10 phonebankers per week!)

3. Let us know if we can include your name on the sponsor list we share with other volunteers and our phone bank team.
 
4. Donate [here](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sd045-churches-grafstein-mari?refcode=sponsor). All sponsor dollars go directly to our candidates and partner organizations via ActBlue.

5. We'll keep you posted about our phone bank successes! 


**More about our candidates**: 
As of April 2026, we have two fabulous candidates (with more to come): NC State Sen. Lisa Grafstein, a leading voice on reproductive rights, civil rights, and disability justice, and our alum, former MI State Rep. Jaime Churches, a beloved educator and passionate advocate for kids who's running to regain her seat after a narrow loss in 2024.

If you have questions email us any time at team@stateswinmari.org.

Activities include writing postcards, creating protest posters, and doing whatever else is needed to support the candidates and get people involved in politics. Meet friends. Do Stuff.
Every 4th Tuesday of the month.

events.title: Change Begins With ME Overpass Alliance-Wednesdays

location.venue: Clairemont Mesa Blvd overpass at I-15

events.description:
Make some "Good Trouble" - Join us for an overpass visibility event at Clairemont Mesa Dr. over I-15. 

We use huge letters to spell out an inspiring message for passing cars during the evening commute and wave to cars honking in support. 

Messaging changes weekly in response to current events.

It can be windy on the overpass; bring a jacket.

Parking:  Street parking is available on Chesapeake Dr or Murphy Canyon Dr. off of Clairemont Mesa Blvd.  Walk to bridge.

RSVP to get updates.

We are committed to peaceful protest.  While bannering, please do not leave banners unattended or hang banners over bridge rails.  Please be considerate of pedestrians & don't feed the trolls.

Photos and video of this event may be shared publicly.

Safety is our top priority.  Please complete our Liability Waiver here - https://bit.ly/CBWM_OVERPASSALLIANCE_WAIVER

Sign up, show up, and stand up for justice.  We look forward to being visible with you!

events.description:
Join We Are One Sullivan every Saturday from 1pm – 2pm at 414 Broadway, Monticello to come together, lift our voices, and stand for democracy, justice, and community in the face of the continuing atrocities created by the Trump administration. 
We show up, we stand tall, and we remind one another that we are not alone. Bring your joy, your anger, your love, your sign and, if you can, a donation of non-perishable food or personal hygiene items for the St. John’s Episcopal Church Food Pantry.

events.title: Ridgefield Roundabout Rally
events.description:
Ridgefield Roundabout — Peaceful Stand for Justice and Democracy
Please join your fellow community members at the Rosauers Roundabout (at the intersection of Pioneer Street and S. Royle Road) for a peaceful, lawful rally. This rally is intended as a local alternative to the large No Kings Day 4 Rally in Vancouver also happening on this date. Our theme, too, is: No Kings — Vote Early. 
Bring a sign, bring a friend, and bring your resistance energy. Costumes are always welcome. Come with or without a sign and stand up for justice, showing our neighbors that"Enough is enough!" and  we demand accountability. Together, we are stronger.

events.title: Defenders of Democracy Santa Ana

address_lines: West MacArthur Boulevard & South Bristol Street

events.description:
Let's show our community that we support our immigrant neighbors and all human rights as we work toward a better Orange County!

Every Saturday 9:30 -11:00AM.
Corner of Bristol & MacArthur

**MEET YOUR HOSTS**

Defenders of Democracy is part of the **[OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition)**. We will gather for events and actions as our group grows. Please invite a friend!

**[The OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition)** is a collaboration between the **[Indivisible](https://indivisible.org/)** groups in and touching Orange County, CA. We are non-partisan, all-volunteer, grassroots groups of residents in OC who are fighting fascism and holding elected officials accountable, from city councils and school boards all the way up to Congress. We partner with other community organizations to uplift and support our neighbors while we work toward progressive electoral change and a democracy that works for ALL people.

events.title: Phone Bank For Marni Von Wilpert (CA48) and Take Back The House
events.description:
*In partnership with the California Democratic Party, the Bay Area Coalition, Indivisible WLA, Blue Future, Jewish Democratic Council of America, Voters of Tomorrow, Malibu Democratic Club, Social Security Works, High School Democrats of America, Chop Wood Carry Water, Beach Cities Democrats, TriCounties Democratic Club, Pacific Palisades Democratic Club, Los Cerritos Democratic Club LA-OC, Asian Dems of Los Angeles County, and Los Angeles County Democratic Party* 

Join us every Tuesday as we call target voters in CA-48 to Elect Marni Von Wilpert to Take Back the House!

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient so you'll need a computer, laptop or tablet and internet access to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

events.title: HB4Democracy Sundays at City Hall
events.description:
Join us Every Sunday from 1:00-2:30 at the corner of Main and Yorktown.

On Sunday afternoons we stand shoulder to shoulder with our Huntington Beach Neighbors in solidarity with all of Orange County.

Peaceful, joyful, loud.

**Meet your hosts:**

**HB4Democracy** is part of the **[OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition)**. We are cultivating community. As our movement grows, we will gather for events, community building and civic engagement. We encourage all to bring friends and neighbors.

The **[OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition)** is a collaboration with all of the Indivisible groups in and adjacent to Orange County, CA. We are a non-partisan, grassroots group of local community volunteers. We are residents of Orange County who are fighting fascism and holding elected officials accountable, including city councils, school boards, and congressional representatives. We believe in protecting our democracy and our constitution.

We partner with other community organizations like OC Huddle for this event, to uplift and support our neighbors while we work towards a progressive electoral shift that works for ALL people. 

Every Sunday we accept donations of toiletries and dry goods for our local immigrant population.

events.title: ICE Is Not Welcome Here! Cary ICE Office

Please bring signs; no swastikas please.

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country and let ICE know they are not welcome!

See you every Friday morning engaging drivers in Cary.

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/

events.title: ICTX Unload & Unwind
events.description:
"Unload & Unwind" is a low-pressure, conversational space for community members and local candidates to connect as real people. No stiff podiums, no formal debate clocks, and no rehearsed stump speeches.

We’re inviting local candidates to join our circle, share what’s on their minds, and honestly vent about the grueling campaign trail if they need to. For community members, it’s a rare chance to get to know the folks on your ballot outside of a high-stress town hall environment.
Come for the community, stay for the real talk, and leave the political pressure at the door.

### What to expect:

- **A Casual Circle:** A relaxed, roundtable-style layout where everyone is on the same level.
- **Real Conversations:** Time for candidates to unwind and share their perspectives, followed by casual, open-ended mixing and mingling.
- **A Safe Space:** This is a supportive environment focused on empathy, civic connection, and humanizing the people who step up to run for office.

Come as you are. Cameras on or off, pajamas or your evening gown, whatever helps you recharge. Let’s clear out the noise so we can stay in the fight for the long haul.



###### Who is Indivisible Centex? We’re a non-partisan, pro-democracy, grassroots movement educating and empowering Central Texans to find their voice, stand up for their neighbors, and take action together to strengthen our community and our democracy.

events.description:

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. # Who are we?

We are a faction within the Democratic Party, and we consider ourselves both **Democrats** and **Socialists**.

**This group is not a space for discussing leaving the Democratic Party**. If that is your goal or perspective, this organization is probably not the right fit for you. 

We are active members of our local Democratic Clubs, and this space is dedicated to learning how to navigate and work effectively within the Democratic Party.

The agenda for the meeting is available here: https://socialists.us/direct/list/agenda?ZoomAgenda. 

We’ll be happy to answer any questions about our Manifesto and how it is built from the bottom up. You can read the Manifesto here: https://socialists.us/manifesto.

therefore, we believe in Free Education, Universal Health Care, Anti-Death Penalty, Pro-Abortion, Universal Basic Income, the Right to Unionize, the sanctity of the Separation of Church and State, and the belief that the Government should make life bearable for all and ensure citizens' Liberties.

events.title: Know Your Rights with Law Enforcement on Campus
events.description:
Last year, universities and colleges begun signing agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), granting campus police the authority to conduct immigration enforcement. Now, 11 out of the 12 Florida Public Universities have signed this agreement, along with 7 colleges, and more stating their intent to sign on.

This collaboration raises critical concerns for immigrant students, faculty, and staff, who may face increased surveillance, questioning, and even detainment on campus.

There has also been heavy policing around students exercising their first amendment right. Due to this, all students should attend ensure they know their rights.

This "Know Your Rights on Campus" training is designed to empower students, educators, and community members with the knowledge and tools to protect themselves and others.

Participants will learn: 
- Understanding the legal agreements between universities & ICE. 
- Your constitutional & legal rights regardless of status. 
- How to respond if approached by officers. 
- Where to find Emergency plans, legal resources, and how to support peers facing enforcement actions. 
- How to push back against harmful agreements and demand an end to university-ICE collaboration.

Knowledge is power. Knowing your rights helps protect your community and resist unjust enforcement on campus.

events.title: Stand Up To End Cost, Corruption and Chaos
events.description:
Congresswoman Ann Wagner took office 13 years ago, yet she has never held a town hall, and remains out of touch with her constituents. Late last year, she denied a formal request for a meeting with her District Office for a National Lobby Day.  She has remained steadfast in her support for the current administration’s egregious and harmful policies and actions. 

We now face a slide toward authoritarianism, a threat to life as we know it. But we are not powerless. As Americans, we still have our voices and our vote. Mid-terms are coming and we have a chance to vote Ann Wagner out of office, shifting the majority in Congress and saving our democracy. Now, more than ever, we must come together and say "no" to the harmful policies that Wagner has supported. 

This weekly protest began in early 2025. Until recently, it was known as the “Where’s Ann” event. We continue to meet weekly, regardless of the weather. We stand in solidarity as we send the message that Ann must be voted out. Bring your signs reflecting your own concerns or borrow ours. Now that the primary election is over, signs in support of specific candidates are appropriate. Indivisible St. Louis is endorsing Fred Wellman for U.S. Congress. This event is for everyone, regardless of where you live. Join us on Sundays, from 1-3 pm, at the corner of Manchester & Weidman. Help us Flip The Seats!

Currently, the protest is from 11am-1pm at Manchester & Weidman. Plans are to remain in this time slot at least until November 3, 2026.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to people’s needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

events.title: Cease and Desist: Trademark & Activism
events.description:
A lawyer claiming to represent Democrats Abroad has sent us a cease-and-desist letter, which raises serious questions about the line between activism and trademark law.

https://socialists.us/docs/letters/2026-02-24-ParisDemAbroad-CeaseAndDesist.pdf

One of our members was previously sued by the Campbell Corporation for using its trademark in political speech. Now we are facing a similar situation.

Is this attempt by a Democrat living outside the United States an effort to intimidate Socialists who are Democrats abroad, and effectively block our Socialist candidate from receiving the 21 votes at the Democratic National Convention?

Should we push back against these entities and raise this issue at the next law or rules meeting? We could argue that Democrats Abroad, through this non-democratic behavior, is engaging in intimidation and should therefore forfeit its 21 votes.

This discussion is not only about how to respond to the cease-and-desist letter, but also about launching a broader conversation on the use of trademarks in political speech and the ownership of creative labor.

For reference: https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2025/11/campbells-stipulated-order-reinforces-trademark-protection-in-political-speech

events.title: Inspire America To Vote
events.description:
Voter engagement in America is at a critical crossroads. Today, nearly 100 million citizens who are eligible to vote are not participating in our democracy. That is nearly half of all eligible voters sitting on the sidelines, their voices unheard in shaping the future of our country. This represents not just lost opportunities, but a deep challenge for the health of our democracy. Many of these citizens feel disconnected, frustrated, or overwhelmed by the voting process, while others may simply not realize the power their participation holds. Whatever the reason, the result is the same: millions of Americans are not contributing to decisions that affect their communities, their families, and the nation as a whole.

The goal of Inspire America To Vote is to address this challenge head-on. We believe that voter engagement is not just about encouraging people to cast a ballot—it is about fostering meaningful conversations that can inspire, educate, and empower those who have not yet taken that step. To do this effectively, we must equip ourselves with the tools, strategies, and confidence to engage in productive dialogue with non-voting citizens. It requires understanding their concerns, breaking down barriers, and showing them that their participation matters.

This event is designed to help you become a more effective advocate for civic engagement. We will explore how to connect with people in ways that are respectful, motivating, and action-oriented. By learning to communicate the importance of voting and inspiring those around us, we can transform apathy into action and ensure that more voices are represented in our democracy. Every conversation counts, and together we can help close the gap between eligible citizens and active voters, strengthening the foundation of our democratic process for generations to come.

This is our moment to step up, engage, and inspire. The work we do here will ripple across communities, turning potential into participation, and apathy into action.

Inspire America To Vote will feature a diverse lineup of guest speakers and motivational leaders provided by [Keynote Speaker](https://keynotespeakers.info/) and [Motivational Speaker](https://motivationalspeakerz.com/) who bring years of experience in civic engagement, community organizing, and voter advocacy. These speakers have worked directly with communities across the country, helping non-voters understand the power of their voice and how they can make a meaningful impact through participation. Their insights will provide attendees with real-world strategies for engaging citizens who have historically been disengaged from the voting process. Each speaker brings a unique perspective, from grassroots organizers who have successfully mobilized local neighborhoods, to national experts who have shaped voter outreach campaigns on a larger scale.

Motivational speakers will also play a central role in the event, inspiring attendees to take action in their own communities. These speakers understand the psychological barriers that prevent people from voting—apathy, distrust, confusion—and they will share practical techniques for addressing these challenges with empathy and effectiveness. Through stories of personal experience, case studies, and actionable advice, attendees will leave with a renewed sense of purpose and the confidence to motivate others to participate in democracy.

The sessions will focus not only on theory but on applied best practices. Speakers will break down successful outreach methods, from leveraging social networks and community relationships to using persuasive communication techniques that resonate with individuals across diverse demographics. Attendees will gain hands-on knowledge in facilitating conversations about civic responsibility, addressing objections, and encouraging first-time voters to engage with the process.

In addition to formal presentations, the event will include interactive workshops and Q&A sessions, allowing attendees to directly learn from experts and explore how to tailor strategies to their own communities. These opportunities for dialogue will ensure that participants leave equipped with both the knowledge and practical tools needed to implement voter engagement initiatives effectively.

By combining motivational inspiration with concrete expertise, Inspire America To Vote will provide a comprehensive learning experience. Attendees will not only be energized by the speakers’ passion but will also walk away with clear, actionable steps they can take immediately to reach non-voting citizens. This event is designed to create a ripple effect—arming committed individuals with the skills, strategies, and motivation necessary to strengthen voter participation and ensure that every eligible citizen understands the power and importance of their voice in shaping the future of our country.

events.title: Calling All Resistance Knitters/Crocheters - Melt the Ice Hat Knit-In
events.description:
In the 1940s, Norwegians quietly defied Nazi occupation by knitting and wearing red, pointed hats with tassels. A simple garment became an act of protest.

More recently, knitters in Minnesota revived this tradition during a surge of ICE activity—using red hats as a visible sign of solidarity and resistance.

We carry that work forward here. Proceeds from the sale of our patterns and finished hats and bandanas are donated to CASA de Maryland, supporting immigrant communities through advocacy and assistance.

Join us as we knit, crochet, sew and craft in solidarity. We will keep gathering—as long as there is a need to resist.

🧶 **Resistance Knit-In (Ongoing)**  
📅 **When:** Sundays (ongoing)  
⏰ **Time:** 2–4 pm  
📍 **Where:** The Shops at Kenilworth – Common Area  

**How:** Supplies if you have them for the Melt the Ice Hat, Pin or Baltimore Bandana and/or the Blue Wave Hat . Knit and crochet patterns can be found on Ravelry. Beginners welcome, and supplies may be available to share.

events.title: Take a Stand Tuesdays - South Cary
events.description:
Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy in south Cary every Tuesday from 7:30-9am as we gather to demonstrate at the intersection of Kildaire Farm Road and 1010. Park in the parking lot of Walgreens (3441 Kildaire Farm Road), but please don’t use any prime customer parking spaces. We will stand on the sidewalk on the corner next to Walgreens.

This peaceful visibility event is intended to motivate people to take an active role in defending our democracy. Inaction supports the regime, so our goal is to connect with drivers on their morning commutes and inspire them to make the shift from idle bystander to engaged participant. We also want to give people who are currently uncertain or afraid the courage they need to TAKE A STAND and get involved to protect our democracy.

This is a positive and nonviolent demonstration. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement.

Please bring positive signs only. Some examples: “Stand up, you are not alone!” “Courage is contagious!” “Dissenting is patriotic!” If you've never done this before, we're happy to help you. We will have extra signs for anyone who needs one. Feel free to bring a friend.

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/


We look forward to seeing you every Tuesday morning encouraging and motivating drivers in south Cary!

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Santa Fe Dam Park
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities; whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This site has public restrooms
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

This is a peaceful, nonviolent event. We ask all participants to engage respectfully, avoid confrontation, help de-escalate any tensions, and follow all local laws and safety guidance.

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We’re launching an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

We're heading to the Central Valley, to California's 13th Congressional District ("CA-13"). In 2024 Adam Gray flipped this House seat by only 187 votes. Let's talk to voters to help hold CA-13, as we take back the House majority!

We will be canvassing in Los Banos in the Central Valley, even though the "location" for this event is shown as San Carlos. Carpools will leave Peninsula locations around 7:00-7:30am, to be in Los Banos for the event's 9:00am start time. Carpools will return around 2:30-3pm.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

How do we "Go Deep"?  By practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

_By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. Our emails share timely, impactful actions (letter parties, phone banks, canvasses, voter registrations, and more) for strategic, toss-up races that will help us win back the House and other important races._

location.venue: SW corner of Grant & El Camino
address_lines: Grant Road & East El Camino Real

events.description:
The damage being done to our communities and our democracy shows up in specific patterns: attacks on the press, scapegoating whole groups of people, abuse of police power, elections being undermined. These are warning signs of authoritarianism.

The *Signs of Fascism Street Theater Protest* is a way to make those patterns visible in the most literal sense. We will stand in silence along a busy street, each person holding a stark, simple sign naming one warning sign of fascism. Without chanting or waving, we just present a visible list of dangers that people can’t easily ignore or explain away.

Please make sure to **RSVP**: the meeting place may change and we need to be able to notify you.

Here’s what to expect:

- Wear black (preferably) or very dark clothing so the focus stays on the words.  
- Hold provided “Signs of Fascism” posters.

- Some of us will offer a small handout to those who pass by which explains what the signs mean and how people can get involved.

events.description:
QPP is an action-oriented community for queers and allies joined together in solidarity, providing mutual aid-based survival work — rooted in principles of racial justice, gender justice, disability justice, economic justice and class justice — and creating a place of true belonging and community.

🌈

Here are our group norms:

Respect Worth/Dignity: We respect the worth and dignity of others and that guides our interactions with everyone in the group.

Intent: We assume others are acting with good intent. If someone says or does something insensitive or hurtful, we help them learn.

Accountability: We know that we can all make mistakes, and we endeavor to act with grace to acknowledge them and repair any damage done.

Embrace Growth Mindset: We strive to see mistakes or conflicts as opportunities to learn and grow.

Intergenerational Respect: We acknowledge that, while the lived experiences of group members of various ages will differ, we will give everyone's thoughts and actions due consideration. No one is too young or too old to contribute or to have great ideas.

Confidentiality: We agree that stories stay and learning leaves. We can apply what we learn from others in the group, we cannot share their stories.

Step Forward/Step Back: We strive to promote equitable participation in the group using the "step forward/step back" framework. If you frequently speak up in conversations, consider stepping back to make room for other voices. If you typically remain quiet in conversations, consider stepping forward to make your voice heard.

Leadership Rotates: We do not have a hierarchical structure. Working groups (including leadership!) are all made up of volunteers, and involvement in them is not set in stone. If you want to be involved in a working group, please let someone in that group know. (Planning consists of volunteers.) Choose how you best think you can contribute, and let someone know.
