events.title: Swing Blue Alliance Frontline Update
events.description:
## The Power of Talking with Voters
With 8 years of experience on the frontline of innovation, Swing Blue Alliance is your go-to for taking effective action in the upcoming midterm elections.  

### Don't miss our featured speakers! 

- Rebecca Riccio:  why canvassing and phone banking remain critical tools for reaching voters
- Lucy Hochschartner: Why canvassing is essential in Maine
- Former State Senator Terence Everitt: Voter protection and engagement in North Carolina. 

We’ll also share the latest from Virginia and concrete ways to put your time and energy to work before Election Day. The Frontline Update runs from 10:00–10:30 AM ET.

This is a focused, 30-minute meeting designed to deliver high-impact updates quickly and clearly, followed by optional time for Q&A.

---


## Frontline Update 
**Where grassroots volunteers get informed, inspired, and mobilized**

The Frontline Update is Swing Blue Alliance’s monthly virtual gathering for volunteers across the country who are ready to turn urgency into action.

Each month, we bring you inside the work that’s shaping the next elections — and the future beyond them.

### What You’ll Get

**The Latest on Key Races**  
Hear directly from campaign leaders, partner organizations, and Swing Blue Alliance team leads about the most critical state and local races on the horizon. From state Supreme Courts to House of Delegate races to emerging battlegrounds, you’ll learn what’s at stake — and why it matters now.

**Campaign Spotlights**  
We regularly highlight election campaigns where early volunteer engagement can make a decisive difference. You’ll meet candidates, organizers, and grassroots partners building power in places that are too often overlooked.

**Clear, Immediate Actions**  
We don’t just talk about strategy — we plug you in. Whether it’s canvassing, phone banking, postcarding, fundraising, protest organizing, or message testing, you’ll leave every meeting with concrete ways to take action.

**The Bigger Strategy**  
The Frontline Update connects the dots between today’s volunteer opportunities and our long-term strategy to defend democracy, protect voting rights, and build durable Democratic power.

### Who It’s For

- New volunteers looking for a place to start  
- Experienced organizers ready for their next assignment  
- Grassroots leaders who want to stay aligned and informed  
- Anyone who believes democracy is worth fighting for  

Whether you can give an hour a week or lead a team, this is where you find your place in the fight.

---

**Join the next Frontline Update and be part of what comes next.**

events.description:
Here in Pennsylvania, countless communities are fighting data centers in their backyards — and now, **we're brighting the fight against data centers to Harrisburg.**

We're pushing back against a litany of bad bills crafted by the state legislature, including bills that would stifle the public's ability to control their communities' destiny on data center development, and we're fighting to win a real three-year moratorium on data center development.

Join the weekly Singing Resistance demonstration held by Knox County, Maine's locally-organized creative protest group called The Audacity. We will gather at Chapman Park (Corner of Park and Main Streets, next to the Walgreens) every Saturday at Noon in Rockland, Maine as long as Trump remains in the White House. events.title: HOUSE MAJORITY RUNS THROUGH CALIFORNIA | Phone Banks!
events.description:
**In 2025, California made history by passing Prop 50. Now it’s time to turn that victory into lasting change by Taking Back the House!**

We're going to reach out to voters in our targeted districts early to hear their issues, concerns and ideas. And we'll be using some of the best practices from **Deep Canvassing** to have more engaged and meaningful conversations. 

**Join our virtual phone banks with the Bay Area Coalition and other California Democratic Party partners and help stop the Trump / MAGA authoritarian takeover.**  

We need your help! Virtual phone banks using the Scale to Win dialer have become an essential part of campaigns. Whether you’re new to phone banking or an expert, you have a place with our people-powered campaigns. The good news is, phone banking is easy to learn and can be done from the comfort of your own home. We'll provide training on both the deep canvassing script and how to use Scale to Win.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Welcome to the Housing Committee!

We are here because we know housing is a real and urgent issue in our community—whether you, a family member, a friend, or a neighbor has been impacted. This work is personal, and it brings us together with a shared purpose.

You are stepping into the next stage of your journey as a member, where you will actively develop and exercise your leadership. In this space, we come together to deepen our understanding of housing issues and take collective action.

Together, we will evaluate the systemic challenges driving the housing crisis, both locally and statewide. Our work includes advancing solutions such as rent control and supporting the creation of a Tenant Protection Office—efforts that aim to bring stability, accountability, and fairness to our communities.

We are also committed to building our learning through conversation—by listening to those most impacted by the housing crisis and engaging with different perspectives, including opposition. This helps us sharpen our analysis, strengthen our strategies, and act with clarity and purpose.

This work cannot be done alone. It is only through collective power, shared leadership, and consistent action that we can create meaningful change. As a committee, we are taking the initiative to challenge and shift the systems that impact our housing conditions.

Your voice, experiences, and leadership are essential to this work. We look forward to building power together.

events.description:
¡Bienvenidos al Comité de Vivienda!

Estamos aquí porque sabemos que la vivienda es un problema real y urgente en nuestra comunidad—ya sea que tú, un familiar, un amigo o un vecino haya sido afectado. Este trabajo es personal y nos une con un propósito compartido.

Estás dando el siguiente paso en tu camino como miembro, donde desarrollarás y ejercerás tu liderazgo activamente. En este espacio, nos reunimos para profundizar nuestro entendimiento de los temas de vivienda y tomar acción colectiva.

Juntos, evaluaremos los desafíos sistémicos que impulsan la crisis de vivienda, tanto a nivel local como estatal. Nuestro trabajo incluye impulsar soluciones como el control de renta y apoyar la creación de una Oficina de Protección al Inquilino—esfuerzos que buscan traer estabilidad, responsabilidad y equidad a nuestras comunidades.

También estamos comprometidos a fortalecer nuestro aprendizaje a través de la conversación—escuchando a quienes están más impactados por la crisis de vivienda y dialogando con diferentes perspectivas, incluyendo la oposición. Esto nos ayuda a afinar nuestro análisis, fortalecer nuestras estrategias y actuar con claridad y propósito.

Este trabajo no se puede hacer en solitario. Solo a través del poder colectivo, el liderazgo compartido y la acción constante podemos lograr un cambio significativo. Como comité, estamos tomando la iniciativa para desafiar y transformar los sistemas que afectan nuestras condiciones de vivienda.

Tu voz, tus experiencias y tu liderazgo son esenciales en este trabajo. Esperamos construir poder juntos.

events.title: Indivisible Rutherford NC Meeting
events.description:
Join us for our next Indivisible RuCo planning meeting — an open gathering for any members of Indivisible RuCo who want to help shape our upcoming community actions, volunteer projects, and advocacy events. We’ll discuss priorities for the months ahead, assign roles for upcoming initiatives, and share ideas for outreach and education in Rutherford County.

This is your chance to get involved, bring your perspective, and help make sure our work reflects the needs and values of our community. Whether you’ve been organizing for years or are brand new to civic engagement, your voice matters here. We welcome participants of every race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, and background, affirming our commitment to inclusion, equity, and mutual respect.

Update (July 25, 2026): To provide additional clarity, these coalition meetings include the community business of several local partner organizations. Rather than asking our members to attend multiple meetings each month, we coordinate shared planning, announcements, and collaboration in a single gathering whenever possible.

While we regularly welcome guest speakers and invite prospective members who would like to learn more about our work, these are meetings of the coalition's membership. As with any membership organization, we reserve the right to remove individuals whose conduct is disruptive or compromises the safety, inclusion, or productive functioning of the space. We are committed to maintaining an environment where members can organize, collaborate, and participate in good faith.

events.title: Badass Bridge Brigade-Seminary Road
events.description:
Join the Badass Bridge Brigade, Good Trouble MoCo, and Indivisible for our weekly message on Seminary Road bridge over 495. 

Bring your signs and flags* Organizers will have the MAIN MESSAGE for the day that will be hung on the fence first for viewing from the highway. If you wish to add a sign for the highway, for best visibility, letters need to be a minimum 2ft in height and bright colored letters on a dark background.

Bring flags, signs, and pom poms. For passing cars on the bridge – for greatest impact – keep sign messages short and clearly printed.

*If you hang a sign for the highway, you must stay with your sign and take it down at the end of the event.

MEET AT: Seminary Bridge overpass for a banner drop and sign wave from 12:30 pm to 2:00 pm, weather permitting. We will not be out if there is heavy rain, snowy sleet, or lightning and thunder.

TRANSPORATION/PARKING: Parking is available in the neighborhood. Keep in mind that parking is not allowed on the bridge – those with mobility concerns can be dropped off and picked up. Closest metro is the Forest Glen Metro on the Red Line. It is about a 0.7 mile walk. It is also on RideOn Route 5.

RESTROOMS: Are not available.

This is a peaceful, family friendly event. 

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Standing Up For Democracy and Social Justice in Estacada
events.description:
Every Saturday from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM, we gather for an hour of peaceful visibility on the corner of Highway 224 and City Hall in Downtown Estacada.

We’d like to believe we’re standing in peace — but these days, we’re standing in protest and for our democracy.

It’s fun. It’s energizing. And honestly? It’s better than doing nothing.
This may be our last chance to stand up for our rights — locally, visibly, and together. No one’s coming to save us. It’s up to us to lead. And the best place to start is right here in our own community.

✨ What to expect:
– Supportive honks and waves from passing cars
– Friendly conversation and good company
– Bring a sign if you want — or just bring yourself
– It’s only one hour, but it means something

It might feel small — but it’s something. And sometimes something is everything. Please join us. There’s real power in showing up.

*** Note from Estacada Progressives: Instead of signing up for each week, consider making a calendar event on your device that will remind you so that we can keep costs of operating low for our small group. We show up every week, rain or shine! Please consider joining our Facebook Group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/estacadaprogressives ***

events.title: Together We Sing
events.description:
Join us each Thursday evening 6:00-7:00

With all that is going on in our world, human beings are challenged to the core, and our nervous systems are in overdrive. There is so much fear, anger, and ranting about what people are against and what others are doing that is ruining our lives. Against-energy is exhausting! I'm weary from the pounding of toxic negativity. I am for Peace on Earth and Goodwill to ALL! I want to know what you are for. From the deepest place of integrity, human dignity, and decency, what are you for? We cannot think, feel, or act from our deepest selves when our nervous systems are ragged with hyper-stimulation. I want to create a place for people to gather as a community with the common desire to feel welcome, safe, and to nourish our nervous systems.

I am a singer, singing coach, and rhythm circle facilitator. I envision gathering in a circle as friends, with the common ground of being human, and singing in a way that soothes our nervous systems and lifts our spirits.

You don't need to have a "great" voice or read music. I will teach you simple and beautiful songs. When we sing together, our breathing regulates, and the vibration created in our singing works together to shift the nervous system out of fight-flight-freeze into rest, digest, and coherence (the quality of forming a unified whole)... community!

I weave a spirit of play, rhythm, and movement into my teaching.

Interesting fact: Play is as vital to survival as food and water. The Science of Play, by Stuart Brown

 

Cullie Treichler

events.title: States Win CA Peninsula Virtual Phonebank!
events.description:
Join States Win CA Peninsula every Saturday at 10am PT to elect Democrats in majority making State Legislature districts! Read about our candidates and races below. 

[**Meet Hadley Haas:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/hadley-haas/) Hadley is a Pittsburgh native, parent, and advocate who turns personal challenges into action. Democrats hold the PA House by just one seat. HD 44 is a top flip opportunity in suburban Allegheny County—a district shifting toward pragmatic leadership. Electing Hadley strengthens the Democratic majority and protects progress on gun safety, reproductive freedom, and economic relief.

[**Meet Chris Thomas:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/chris-thomas/) Chris comes from a working-class family of veterans, coal miners, and educators. He worked construction before becoming a middle school math and science teacher, where he saw how underfunded schools hurt students. Now a community organizer across Montgomery and Berks counties and a volunteer firefighter, Chris knows what it means to show up for neighbors. Republicans control the PA State Senate. SD 24 is increasingly competitive as suburban and small-town voters reject gridlock and rising costs. 

[**Meet Robyn Vining:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/robyn-vining/) Robyn's race is the most flippable Senate district in Wisconsin this cycle under the fair maps that took effect in 2024. Robyn has already proven she can win tough races, flipping her Assembly district and defending it in multiple close contests, and now she’s bringing that same strength to the fight for the Senate. Winning this seat is essential to building a Democratic majority.

[**Meet Jenna Jacobson:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/jenna-jacobson/) Representative Jenna Jacobson’s commitment to public service was shaped by her mother, a single parent and pastor who balanced raising two children while relying on food stamps and pursuing her education. Breaking the GOP’s legislative grip and building a governing majority capable of delivering real progress for working families across Wisconsin is not possible without electing Jenna and flipping this seat.

[**Meet Kristie O'Brien:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/kristie-obrien/) Kristie is a lawyer, mediator, and mom who is running for the Arizona State Senate in Legislative District 13. This race is a critical opportunity for Democrats to flip a key Arizona State Senate seat and move closer to winning a majority in the chamber. Legislative District 13 is one of the most competitive districts in the state, with recent statewide Democratic candidates carrying the district even as Republicans narrowly held legislative seats. 

[**Meet Sarah Pounds:**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/sarah-pounds/) The path to reclaiming a Democratic House majority, and a full trifecta, runs through Michigan House District 54. In 2024, Democrats lost with a razor thin margin here. This year, both Republicans and Democrats have named HD-54 a top target. Sarah Pounds is exactly the candidate this moment calls for: a public school educator with firsthand experience of the kitchen-table issues this district cares about—fully funded schools, lower costs, and protected reproductive freedom. Investing in Sarah now is how Democrats turn the narrowest of losses into the majority they need.

[**Meet Trevor Jung**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/trevor-jung/) Wisconsin State Senate District 21 presents a critical pickup opportunity on the path to flipping the chamber and building a Democratic majority that can move the state forward. Electing Trevor Jung would all but guarantee Democratic control while adding a proven local leader focused on lowering costs, investing in public education and workforce development, and ensuring economic growth benefits Wisconsin families, not special interests. 

**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank!

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

Investing in Sarah now is how Democrats turn the narrowest of losses into the majority they need.

[**Meet Trevor Jung**](https://stateswin.org/candidates/trevor-jung/) Wisconsin State Senate District 21 presents a critical pickup opportunity on the path to flipping the chamber and building a Democratic majority that can move the state forward. Electing Trevor Jung would all but guarantee Democratic control while adding a proven local leader focused on lowering costs, investing in public education and workforce development, and ensuring economic growth benefits Wisconsin families, not special interests.

events.title: 📢✊ After We March, We Organize! 🔥 Solidarity Warriors Indivisible Action Group 🗽
events.description:
Mass demonstrations like 🚫👑 No Kings prove one thing beyond doubt: the people are AWAKE and FIRED UP! 🔥 But rallying in the streets is just the beginning. The real power comes from what we do after the march. Research shows that no movement with 3.5% of the population in continuous mobilization has ever failed 📊 — but only when they go beyond demonstrations into mass noncooperation, noncompliance, and strategic action that dismantles the pillars holding up authoritarianism. That's exactly what we're here to build. 🛠️ Come learn the organizing skills we wish we had known from the start — and let's transform that protest energy into lasting, unstoppable change. 💪

📚🎤 Every week, we feature guest speakers and training on topics like:

🛡️ How to Protest Safely
🌎 Immigrant Rights
🪶 Indigenous History
🔐 Cybersecurity
✊ Community Organizing Tactics
and much more!

🌟 About Solidarity Warriors:
We're an action-focused, Indivisible group 💥 born after the November election and proud lead organizers of No Kings 2 in Denver 🏔️. We're people from across the nation — many in Colorado — united by one commitment: action over grievance. 🎯 We don't just talk about what's wrong — we plan, organize, and partner with marginalized communities to make things right. ✊🏽

🚨 Come ready to answer one question: What are YOU going to DO?
👉 Join us. The movement needs you. 🗽✊🔥

events.title: Knock doors for Randy Villegas, CD22 | October 9, 10, 11 in Porterville!
events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 9 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm or 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm

 - Saturday, October 10 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Sunday, October 11 | 9:30 am to 2:30 pm

New to canvassing?  We will train you (and we are lots of fun).  Bring a friend.  Or two.  Be a part of the change we're all looking for.

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 9 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm or 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm

 - Saturday, October 10 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Sunday, October 11 | 9:30 am to 2:30 pm

New to canvassing?  We will train you (and we are lots of fun).  Bring a friend.  Or two.  Be a part of the change we're all looking for.

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: Weekly 6th Ave Bridge Bannering Over I-5 | Mondays
events.description:
There is street parking, but a lot of it is metered; Linda will have quarters with her on the bridge in case you need some.  There aren't meters on the bridge itself so try to nab a spot there first. 

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

events.title: Knock on doors with Indivisible Oregon using Deep Listening - Woodstock (SE Portland)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Swing Left and Indivisible Oregon for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We’ve launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

events.title: States Win Chicago & Friends Phonebank!
events.description:
### Let's flip Wisconsin blue!

Join States Win Chicago on Wednesdays at 5pm CT to make calls for our candidates, Robyn Vining and Brandy Tollefson.

**Meet Robyn Vining:** Robyn has built a reputation as a tireless advocate for public education, healthcare access, common-sense gun reform, and economic fairness. States Win has proudly partnered with Robyn across multiple cycles, and she has a proven record of flipping
and holding competitive seats. Now, she is taking that to the next level in her race for State Senate. Robyn’s race is the most flippable Senate district in Wisconsin this cycle! Winning this seat is *essential* to building a Democratic majority in Wisconsin. 

**Meet Brandy Tollefson:** Brandy is running to flip AD-88 to help lower costs for families, expand access to affordable health care, and fight for all kids to get the education they deserve. Electing Brandy would bring a working mom, school board leader, and advocate for public education and affordable healthcare to Madison.

**Meet Carol Glanville:** Carol has built a strong record of delivering for West Michigan families, from securing more than $100 million in investments for her district to fighting for quality public education, accessible health care, and lower costs for working families. First elected to the Michigan House in 2022, Carol flipped her seat blue for the first time in 30 years. Carol is now running to flip State Senate District 30. Winning this seat is essential to protecting and expanding the Democratic majority in the Michigan Senate and continuing progress for working families across the state.

**Meet Becky Nichols:** Becky is an educator, former Menasha Common Council member, former Winnebago County Board supervisor, and longtime community advocate running to flip Wisconsin Assembly District 53. Electing Becky would bring practical, community-driven leadership to Madison and help build a Democratic majority that delivers real results for working families.

**Why phonebank:** The data proves it: phonebanking is THE BEST volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. We also help improve our candidate’s data! 

**Come one, come all:** No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

Let's do this! **Join States Win Portland**, **States Win Eugene**, **States Win Puget Sound** & friends and collaborators in the Pacific Northwest and around the nation **every Saturday 11am-12:30pm PT** to help our candidates Lisa Grafstein and Lindsey Prather.

**Grow Democratic Power in the North Carolina House**

Rep. Prather won her seat in 2024 by a narrow margin, reflecting the district’s competitive nature and the political crosscurrents in Buncombe County and surrounding communities. With Republicans controlling both legislative chambers and a Democrat in the governor’s office, defending HD 115 is essential to preserving the governor’s veto power and protecting public education, reproductive freedom, and fair representation in one of the South’s most closely watched battleground states.

Rep. Grafstein seat is critical to protecting Democrats’ fragile numbers in the Senate as Democrats continue to fight to break the Republican supermajority. A leading voice on reproductive freedom, voting rights, and disability justice, Lisa is one of Republicans’ top targets heading into the 2026 midterms.


**Why phonebank:** 

The data proves it. Phonebanking is *the best* volunteering option for remote voter contact. We identify supporters and let them know why their vote matters, speak with undecided voters, and recruit local volunteers. Every call helps us clean our lists, which makes for a faster, more efficient phonebank!

**Come one, come all:** 

No experience necessary. Each Zoom phonebank includes training and check-ins for first-timers (experienced callers can jump right in). We'll share successes and address questions throughout, all while contacting voters in crucial state legislative races. Our veteran phonebank leaders will help you get comfortable, increase your effectiveness, and make sure you have a great experience.

events.title: Clay County School District Board Meetings
events.description:
You’re Invited! 
Advocate for Students and Public Education

Local school boards play a critical role in shaping the future of our schools. Decisions about funding, curriculum, and policy directly impact students, families, and communities. 

Families for Strong Public Schools is expanding its School Board Monitoring Program statewide and is looking for engaged community members to help promote transparency, accountability, and student-centered decision-making. 

This program empowers volunteers to attend school board meetings, observe discussions, and submit brief monthly reports on key issues, including: 
-Budget allocations and funding priorities 
-Curriculum and instructional policies 
-Community engagement and transparency 

We need advocates who are willing to show up, pay attention, and help ensure decisions are made in the best interest of students and families. 

Why Get Involved? 

By participating, you can: 
-Speak up for students and families 
-Monitor whether funding and curriculum decisions meet the needs of all students Support transparency, equity, and strong public education 

Your voice matters. 

When communities show up, school boards listen. Together, we can help ensure local decisions reflect the values and priorities of the people they serve. Let’s build a stronger future for our students right here in Clay County—one meeting at a time.

It’s up to us to make sure that when Gina is elected, she has State Representatives who want to work with her to fight for working class Texans! 

In response to popular demand, we are expanding our volunteer phone bank to another night to increase volunteer opportunities. Please help spread the word by inviting your friends.

Log on from a computer at home, and use your cell phone to call voters to tell them about Gina's labor endorsed, people-powered campaign for a Texas that works for working people, not billionaires. 

You will need a computer and cell phone for this process. Headphones and/or a quiet space where you can put your phone on speaker are strongly encouraged but not required. 

A full training will be provided ahead of each phonebank. The zoom link will be available upon RSVP! 

Fair Shot PAC is a state PAC working to elect pro-labor and pro-union candidates who will fight to give Texas workers a fair shot inside the Capitol in Austin.

events.title: Extraordinary Times Call for Ordinary People! Join Woodburn Hubbard Aurora Indivisible!
events.description:
The cure for worry and hopelessness is action! If you've been waiting for the right time to do something, this is the right time. Join Woodburn Hubbard Aurora Indivisible and trade feelings of fear and anxiety for a sense of accomplishment and a few rays of hope when you see concrete results from taking effective, targeted action.

Join our little, dedicated family of Woodburn and North Marion County neighbors determined to help our communities cope with the damage caused by ICE, and take steps to prevent more kidnappings, raids and assaults. We also address the problems that may happen out of public view, and take coordinated action to address those issues-- issues like the use of supposedly de-activated Flock cameras to lead ICE to find and disappear our neighbors. We also are working to keep a watchful eye on our schools and communities, and are ready to do our best to prevent and manage raids and other incidents.

If you're worried about risk, we have actions you can take sitting on your couch.

Don't have much time? We have impactful actions that will take a minimum of your time but yield powerful results.

Not a joiner? Neither are we but we just couldn't sit back and do nothing while the world around us crumbles. Join us anyway.

We welcome newcomers and are totally open to new and creative ideas. We are a new chapter that really needs all hands on deck. We are a warm, friendly group with a tight focus on problem-solving.

Email WoodburnIndivisible@Yahoo.com with any questions. A friendly human named Ruth, our chapter co-chair, will patiently answer your questions and tell you our meeting times and locations. Join us!

events.description:
ChalkWalk | Saugatuck @ 4:30pm | Hosted by: Good Trouble Indivisible

Create Public Awareness With Us!

Good Trouble Indivisible’s ChalkWalk is a creative public-awareness action using sidewalk chalk to encourage people to pause, read, think, and talk about what is happening in our country.

GTI ChalkWalks transform ordinary sidewalks into a continuing public message. As people walk through downtown Saugatuck, they stop to read, take photographs and videos, ask questions, share their thoughts, and have meaningful conversations with us. 

These peaceful public-awareness actions help bring important issues out into the open—where they can be seen, considered, and discussed.

There are many ways to participate, and you do not need to be an artist or get down on the sidewalk to help.

👉 Help chalk or outline the prepared words. 

👉 Hold a sign of your choosing about democracy, freedom, justice, or another current issue.

👉 Hand out Good Trouble Indivisible cards and information.

👉 Talk with passersby about current events and our work.

👉 Take photographs or video that we can share on social media and our website.

👉 Simply stand with us and help create a visible community presence.

Participants who would like to speak with the public will be given information and talking points. 

Come help for the entire event or stop by for however long you can. 

ChalkWalk is peaceful, lawful, protected FREE SPEECH…welcoming, and open to everyone who believes that public awareness matters—and that silence and inaction are not our only choices.

Bring a democracy sign to hold if you like.  Chalk and handout materials will be provided by Good Trouble Indivisible. 

We hope you will join us—and help turn our sidewalks into important conversations.

Good Trouble Indivisible is a Michigan nonprofit corporation and a chapter of the National Indivisible. 

http://GoodTroubleIndivisible.org

Inspired by the timeless wisdom that "the rich and the poor meet together; the Lord is the Maker of them all," we invite you to an event celebrating community, compassion, and shared humanity.

Just as we are called to "invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind" to our feasts, and to "open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all who are destitute," this gathering is a testament to our commitment to judge righteously and defend the rights of the poor and needy.

Come, let's share a meal, share stories, and share our collective hope for a more inclusive future. Because if a brother or sister is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, simply saying, “Go in peace, be warmed and filled,” isn't enough. It’s time to act, together.?

events.title: Messaging Storm - Weekly Calls to Congress
events.description:
## Messaging Storm
 
### 7 October 2026

**A coordinated call to our Elected Officials**

U.S. Capitol Switchboard (202) 224-3121

### Action - Oppose Changes to the 2030 U.S Census
**Action 1** Tell Congress to oppose the proposed changes to the U.S. Census

**Action 2** Sign on to an organizational letter opposing these changes.

**Action 3**  Leave a public comment for the Census Bureau at the Department of Commerce, that you oppose the proposed changes to the U.S. Census.

### Background
The original intent of the census by the founding fathers, held every 10 years, was to empower the people over their government; since our inception, every resident, regardless of citizenship status, has been counted to set the number of representatives in Congress. The Trump administration wants to limit the census to only citizens and legal green card holders, while also eliminating the collection of race, ethnicity and sexual orientation as important demographic information. These changes only serve this administration by continuing to whittle away at diversity, equity, and inclusion, instead of serving the people as the founding fathers intended. The concern is these proposed changes aim to reduce the representation in diverse, urban areas, as well as dilute the demographic knowledge of our society, including scientific research impacts on different populations.    

### Call Script 
**(adapted from [5calls.org](https://5calls.org/issue/head-start-childhood-education/))**

Hi, my name is [NAME] and I’m a constituent from [CITY, ZIP].
I'm calling to urge [REP/SEN NAME] to oppose the proposed Census rule changes by the Department of Commerce. These changes would erase immigrant representation across the country and worsen civil rights protections for all Americans. The additional elimination of race, ethnicity and sexual orientation from the demographic information would risk diluting our scientific understanding on the health and environmental impacts of different populations as many researchers rely on census data to aid in their research. 
Thank you for your time and consideration.

**Leave full address if leaving a voicemail so your opinion is tallied.**

### Organizational Letters Opposed to the Rule Changes

[Action Network](https://actionnetwork.org/letters/tell-the-census-bureau-stop-the-census-power-grab-2/?source=group-coalition-on-human-needs&referrer=group-coalition-on-human-needs)
 
[League of Women Voters](https://www.lwv.org/take-action/oppose-unconstitutional-census-rule-change)

[Legal Defense Fund](https://www.naacpldf.org/press-release/ldf-condemns-proposed-changes-to-u-s-census-process-that-would-likely-severely-limit-black-representation/)

[National Education Association](https://www.nea.org/advocating-for-change/action-center/take-action/preserve-fair-accurate-census)

[National Council of Nonprofits](https://www.councilofnonprofits.org/form/protect-2030-census)

### [Public Comment Script](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/07/2026-16134/reducing-federal-burden-for-head-start-programs)

**IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS** - please include the agency name, docket number and RIN number below. If submitting via email to Deregulation@acf.hhs.gov, please include the docket number and/or RIN number in the **SUBJECT LINE.**

The council for Nonprofits has an excellent resource guide with additional points for writing your public comment [here](https://www.councilofnonprofits.org/files/media/documents/2026/Census_Comment_Guide_09142026_2.pdf)

Department of Commerce

Census Bureau

15 CFR Parts 60 and 70

[Docket No. 260903-0005]

RIN 0607-AA75

I am writing to oppose the proposed changes to the 2030 Census. These changes would erase immigrant representation across the country and worsen civil rights protections for all Americans. Choosing to eliminate certain non-citizens is a violation of the 14th Amendment which requires “whole number of persons in each State” to be counted for congressional apportionment. 

Additionally, the elimination of race, ethnicity and sexual orientation from the collected demographic information would risk diluting our scientific body of research. Researchers across fields, including health, education, psychology, sociology and environmental, rely on census data to aid in their research. This data also influences policy and access to resources. Accurate and comprehensive Census data is a means of ensuring all people in the U.S. have equitable protections and consideration. 

I ask the Census Bureau to eliminate these proposed rule changes in order to protect a complete, accurate and fair 2030 Census for everyone living in the United States. 

Respectfully,
 
[NAME]

**Resources**

Census in the Constitution. (n.d.). [United States Census Bureau.](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/census-constitution.html)

Join us to remind people that democracy is on the line. Meet up on local Lancaster, PA, overpasses. Overpass messages change each week based on current events AND the enduring themes we need to remember.

events.title: Are Your Friends Registered to Vote?

sponsor.name: Building Bridges for America Action Fund

events.description:
### More than a quarter of eligible voters are not registered to vote.

#### In key states like North Carolina and Georgia, the number is even higher.

### You can help!

### Three Easy Steps:

- **STEP ONE:  Who Needs to Hear from You?**  
_Go through your contact lists, your email directories, your family connections, your personal network.  Is everyone registered to vote?  Has anyone moved recently?  Who needs reminders to do things?  Does everyone know that voting matters to you?_

- **STEP TWO:  Reach Out**  
_Reach out personally.  Let them know:  Voting is important to you.  Ask them to join you as a regular voter.  Share the [National Voter Registration Form](https://www.eac.gov/voters/national-mail-voter-registration-form).  It's usable almost everywhere, to register or update voter registration.  And it's available in nearly 20 languages.  Local election information is available at [eac.gov](https://www.eac.gov/voters/register-and-vote-in-your-state)._ 

- **STEP THREE:  Follow Up**  
_A week later, touch base again.  Ask if they've checked their registration.  Thank them!  You have built a bond around your shared values._

Research backs it up:  Personal contact WORKS.  These calls are some of the most effective tools we have to build progressive power.

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Knock doors with Michael Mazzocco in District 4

Two hours, a partner, and a short walk. That is how this race gets won, one porch at a time. You do not need a script memorized or a political background. You need comfortable shoes and a willingness to listen. We handle the rest.

### Why it matters here

District 4 is the only majority-renter district in Phoenix, and it is the first open council seat since 2013. The people most affected by what the city does next are the ones least likely to get a knock on the door. When you walk a route, you reach them. That is the whole game.

### Why Michael

Michael Mazzocco has lived and worked in D4 for nearly 20 years. He built the Greater Phoenix Equality Chamber of Commerce from a volunteer board into a fully staffed organization, seven years on the board and four as president. He has raised millions for Valley nonprofits. He would be the first Native American to serve on the Phoenix City Council.

events.summary: Phone bank with Michael Mazzocco for Phoenix City Council, D4.
events.description:
## Phone Bank for Michael Mazzocco — Phoenix City Council, D4

District 4 voters live on the phone. **25,525 calls for service for homelessness** inside D4 last year — about 2,100 every month. **83,410 active voters**. Picking up the phone is how we hear what's actually happening on every block in D4.

### Why Michael

Michael Mazzocco has lived and worked in D4 for nearly 20 years. Mayor Gallego appointed him chair of Phoenix's Human Relations Commission. He built the Greater Phoenix Equality Chamber of Commerce from a volunteer board into a fully staffed organization — seven years on the board, four as president. He's raised millions for Valley nonprofits. He'd be the first Native American to serve on the Phoenix City Council.

He's running on **affordable rents**, **homelessness solutions that actually work**, an **Office of Economic Empowerment** to put local businesses back in D4 storefronts, **scaling the Community Safety Plan** — the city program that cut violent crime 40% along the I-17 / 27th Avenue corridor — to the rest of D4, and shade where the heat is worst.

### Why your call matters

First open council seat since 2013. This race is won by reaching voters where they are — and most of them aren't standing on a doorstep at 10am Saturday. They're on the phone.

### What you'll do

Dial D4 voters from home using our web dialer over Zoom. Real conversations, no robocalls. Tested script, trained at the top of every shift. Most volunteers reach 50–80 voters per shift.

**Bring:** laptop with Chrome, headphones, charged phone for backup. Weekend afternoon shift, done by 5. Zoom + dialer login arrives 24 hours before.

### Can't dial?

events.summary: Text bank with Michael Mazzocco for Phoenix City Council, D4.
events.description:
## Text Bank for Michael Mazzocco — Phoenix City Council, D4

District 4 has **83,410 active voters** and the first open council seat since 2013. **55.3% are renters** — the only majority-renter district in Phoenix. **64.9% of D4 families with kids under 6** have every parent working. They're juggling jobs, kids, and a 14-hour city day. They don't sit by the phone. They read texts.

### Why Michael

Michael Mazzocco has lived and worked in D4 for nearly 20 years. Mayor Gallego appointed him chair of Phoenix's Human Relations Commission. He built the Greater Phoenix Equality Chamber of Commerce from a volunteer board into a fully staffed organization — seven years on the board, four as president. He's raised millions for Valley nonprofits. He'd be the first Native American to serve on the Phoenix City Council.

He's running on **affordable rents**, **homelessness solutions that actually work**, an **Office of Economic Empowerment** to put local businesses back in D4 storefronts, **scaling the Community Safety Plan** — the city program that cut violent crime 40% along the I-17 / 27th Avenue corridor — to the rest of D4, and shade where the heat is worst.

### Why your message matters

One thoughtful text reaches a voter we'd otherwise never hear from. Real conversations, not blasts. Most volunteers send and follow up on 80–100 texts in a single 90-minute shift.

### What you'll do

Text D4 voters from our web platform. Replies queue up and you triage them with the team on Zoom. Tested script, trained at the top of every shift.

**Bring:** laptop or tablet, charger, a quiet spot. Web-based — nothing to install. Login arrives 24 hours before. Weeknight shift, 90 minutes.

ICE personnel depart from District Ave. in unmarked vans with tinted windows on missions to abduct immigrants across New England. Immigrants may also show up at the office for appointments. events.description:
Piloted in 2021, "WELLderness: An Outdoor Wellness Series" was developed to bring members of the community together (in person and online) to engage in activities that would have a positive impact on their physical and mental health and well-being. Throughout the year, people have the opportunity to participate in FREE events that center around fostering better connections to self and the environment.

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ 

"Listening to Nature: A Gateway to Connection"

Join Christine for this immersive sound experience. You'll start by learning about resonance, which refers to the process of attuning to and harmonizing with both body sensations and the energy of those around us. As a group you'll select one of the 8 principles of resonance as your focus for the session. Next, you'll relax and enjoy Christine's musical sound accompaniment as you engage with the natural environment. The session will end with a guided meditation. 

From Christine: "By practicing attentive listening in the gardens, participants will enhance their ability to listen actively to reduce conflict and the judgmental voice. This session highlights the importance of accompaniment, making it easier to regulate emotion. Active participation attempts to enable compassionate connection to promote trust, safety and healing. The formation of traumatic memory happens when we feel alone. Accompaniment starts to happen when one person consents to let another travel with them, emotionally or physically, for more than one resonant exchange ultimately fostering a sense of peace, well-being, and a stronger bond with nature, all essential for human health and vitality."

Christine Maila is a certified Resonant Healing Practitioner. Christine supports clients with unconscious contract/sacred vow work and time travel empathy, as well as other Resonant Healing practices. She draws on her mindfulness practices and background in education while supporting others in moving forward in their lives with more autonomy, inspiration, love and freedom. 

View her profile here: https://sarahpeyton.com/practitioner/christine-g-maila/

events.description:
Piloted in 2021, "WELLderness: An Outdoor Wellness Series" was developed to bring members of the community together (in person and online) to engage in activities that would have a positive impact on their physical and mental health and well-being. Throughout the year, people have the opportunity to participate in FREE events that center around fostering better connections to self and the environment.

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

We will begin with a short yoga warm up to prepare our minds and bodies for the wild edible plant walk. Next, we will tour the park stopping along the way to connect with wild edible treats, discuss their culinary, medicinal, and ecological benefits. We will end with a gentle grounding yoga practice to further our connection to earth and all of her gifts.

Candise Jordan is a Health & Fitness Coach, Forest Garden Educator, and Bioregional Herbalist. She has instructed fitness and yoga for over 20 years. Her studies in nutrition lead her to permaculture gardening and foraging. 

Visit her website here: https://farm-forage-feast.teemill.com/

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

Things to note: 

Registration is free and required to attend. 

The park is accessible by car and there is a large visitor parking lot available for use. By Metro, the park entrance is 1.0 mile from the Deanwood Metro Station and 1.3 miles from the Minnesota Ave Station, both on the Orange Line. By foot or bike, access the park via the Anacostia River Trail.

Participants should bring a yoga mat, water bottle, snack, bug spray, sun protection, and/or anything else one may carry when spending time outdoors. Wear comfortable clothing and shoes for being outdoors. Extra yoga mats are available to borrow if needed. 

Contact: For all other questions or concerns reach out to Alivia Villari via email at alivia@fokag.org.

More about Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens: Check out our website (www.kenaqgardens.org) and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and Twitter (@kenaqgardens).

PLEASE READ COMPLETELY before attending!

Make sure not to block the Tesla driveway entrances. We will stay completely on the public sidewalk and off of Tesla property, and cross only with lights. Signs, drums, flags, and similar items are welcome.

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

Wear your favorite wig, big hat, or costume. We want to have fun and to feel like a party during our demonstrations!

No one voted for Musk. Join the peaceful Tesla Takedown movement!

Please Note: Photos may be taken and published at this event, including by attendees and professional photographers. If you prefer not to have your image captured or shared, please take your own precautions (e.g., wear a mask, hat, or wig).

Courtney Steinberg, member of CCDP and former treasurer of the party is also vying for one of the three open seats on the board.

Last month we hosted Congressional District 8 Candidate, Colby Watson. Also, the House District 82 candidate, Chris Bishopp, and April Cook for Senate 34 joined us, plus our resident elections guru, Martin Ericson, explained what we need to know for this November 3 and why voting early is your best bet.
If you missed this meeting, links to the videos of their talks will be in our special election Oct/Nov issue of our newsletter.

Our focus for the 2026 midterms is to build our ranks through outreach and sharing our institutional memory with others including people new to our area and younger activists because Experience plus Energy Equals Power! 

Never forget, we were the ones who marched for civil rights, integrated public schools, built Medicare, protested a war, formed unions, fought for women’s rights, protected our planet and so much more! We won’t allow this administration to erase all we have achieved!

Annual contribution is $20, $5 of which goes to the NC Senior Democrats which makes you a state member, too. To join or to contribute any amount, [click here](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/donation-form/become-a-member--2026) and make a single or recurring contribution.

events.title: Donate to Angelita for Portland

sponsor.name: Angelita Morillo for City Council (OR Working Families Party)

events.description:
My name is Angelita Morillo and I am running for re-election for Portland City Council, District 3 (SE Portland with a tiny piece of NE).

In my first year in office I fought corporate rental price fixing by passing the Algorithmic Price Fixing Ban, I held landlords who want to profit off of detention facilities (like ICE) in our community accountable, I pushed for fossil fuel contracts to be investigated, I funded the restoration of Parks bathrooms in District 3, I secured Portland Street Response’s place in our public safety infrastructure, I’ve centered the voices of unhoused and working class people in the City’s approach to homelessness, and I’ve pushed for local transportation funding.

I moved from Paraguay to the United States as a kid, and my experiences as a queer immigrant who has experienced homelessness have shaped and developed my interest in local government and policy. After attending Lincoln High School and Portland State University, where I studied Political Science and Legal Studies, I worked in Commissioner JoAnn Hardesty's office in Constituent Services and Tribal Relations policy. From there, I went on to do anti-hunger policy with Partners For a Hunger-Free Oregon. 

I am passionate about local government and ensuring that policy makers are led by the community they serve and not the other way around. I love Portland and all that it has given me and I want to give back to it so we can work together to make it a better place to live for all of us. Join me in creating a Portland that works for everyone and re-elect Angelita Morillo for District 3!

P.S. If you are a Portland resident, your first $25 donated will be matched TEN TO ONE by the city's Small Donor Elections program that helps benefit grassroots candidates like me! Read more about the program here.

events.title: Tell your member of Congress to co-sponsor and support the Freedom to Vote Act and the John Lewis Vo

events.title: Tell Congress: Protect the Vote. Defend the People’s Voice.
events.description:
The freedom to vote is the foundation of democracy. It is how we choose leaders, shape our future, and hold power accountable to the people.

But that freedom is under attack. Across the country, politicians and extremists are working to spread distrust in elections, intimidate election workers, restrict access to the ballot, and weaken the systems that allow every eligible voter to have a voice.

We cannot wait until the next election to defend our rights. The time to protect our vote, our election workers, and our democracy is now.

We are calling on lawmakers at every level of government to champion laws that protect voting rights, defend election officials and volunteers, stop voter suppression, strengthen election security, and fully fund fair, accessible elections.

Our vote is our voice. Our voice is our power. And democracy only works when every eligible voter can participate freely, safely, and equally.

Please take one minute to send a letter to lawmakers and urge them to protect the freedom to vote.

Voters can fill out their ballot and turn it in on the spot.  November 3rd is Election Day, but vast numbers will have already voted by then.

In the wealthiest nation on Earth, health care should never be a luxury reserved for those who can afford it. No one should be forced to choose between seeing a doctor, paying rent, buying groceries, or taking on medical debt just to survive. Yet every year, people in America suffer, delay care, go bankrupt, and die because our health care system puts profit before people.

Congress must act. We are calling on every member of Congress to co-sponsor and pass the Medicare for All Act so every person in the United States is guaranteed the care they need, when they need it. Medicare for All would save lives, lower costs, protect families from medical debt, and give people the freedom to choose their doctor without being trapped by restrictive networks or outrageous bills.

Health care is a human right. Send a message to Congress to build a healthcare system that puts people, dignity, and life ahead of corporate greed.

Everyone who is eligible should be allowed to own a gun. However, our state and federal laws need to be updated to better define eligibility:

Require background checks on all gun sales and ammunition sales

Have a red flag law

Prevent domestic abusers from accessing guns

Ban assault weapons

Limit magazine capacity

Require concealed carry permits

Restrict open carry

Ban firearms in libraries, schools, and hospitals

Have a waiting period

Take action to support: We deserve a community free of gun violence

Knock on every door in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

Encourage Democratic voters to get their ballots in the mail or ballot box asap.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

Questions? Contact SBSL at sbslcommteam@southbayswingleft.org

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

Your participation will be critical to winning the midterms and putting a check on the MAGA agenda. Together, we can transform how we talk with voters, rebuild trust, and swing the most competitive races.

events.title: Weekly Phone Bank with Madison Dems
events.description:
The most powerful thing we can do between now and November is talk to our neighbors. Every Wednesday from now through Election Day, Madison County Democrats are hitting the phones and we want you with us.

Whether you've never made a political call in your life or you're a seasoned caller, this is your space. Emily McGinty will be there every week to get you oriented, answer questions, and make sure you feel confident and supported before you dial your first number.

Here's how it works:

Join us on Zoom to get oriented and trained. Then make your calls from wherever you are. You can stay on Zoom or step away independently.

First-timers are strongly encouraged to stay on Zoom. It's a great place to ask questions, share wins, and feel connected while you're making a difference.

and make sure you feel confident and supported before you dial your first number.

Join Emily McGinty on Zoom to get oriented and make your calls from wherever you are. Stay on Zoom throughout or step away to call independently — whatever works best for you. First-timers are strongly encouraged to stay on Zoom as it's a great place to ask questions, share wins, and feel connected while you make a difference.

Drawing on his background as an educator, Darrin listens closely to his constituents and works tirelessly to deliver results that improve their lives. He won his seat in 2022 with our help, flipping the Senate and securing a Democratic trifecta for the first time in decades. With Republicans eager to take back control, re-electing Darrin is essential to ensure Michigan remains a stronghold for democracy.

Wisconsin Assembly District 89 is a key defensive seat that will shape Democrats’ path to a legislative majority under the state’s fairer maps. Ryan Spaude flipped this purple Green Bay–area district in 2024, proving voters are ready for pragmatic leadership focused on affordability and strong public schools. Defending this seat is crucial for a blue Wisconsin!

Why phonebank:

Come one, come all:

events.description:
# Standout for Justice: Burlington ICE Detention Center

**Join us to stand in solidarity with those detained and to alert the community to the I.C.E. facility in Burlington.**

The conditions reported inside are inhumane: no due process, no mattresses, no showers, and minimal food. Your presence makes a tangible difference—immigrants have reported that seeing supporters outside transforms their spirit from fear to hope and confidence.

### **Event Details**
*   **Time:** 10:00 AM – 12:30 PM
*   **Location:** Meet on the green at **1000 District Ave, Burlington**.
*   **The Action:** We gather at 10:00 AM outside the facility to show direct support to those inside. Bring fod which will be distributed to immigrants leaving the facility.  
*   **The March:** Once we have enough participants, we will move as a group to **Burlington Mall Road** to raise public awareness of this facility. 

> **Important Note:** Please arrive at the 1000 District Ave location at the start. We move to the Mall Road as a group based on turnout; arriving early ensures you find the team and can participate in the march.

### **What to Bring**
*   **Food for the immigrants:** Shared items for those being released.
*   **Protection:** Sunscreen, a hat, and appropriate gear depending on the weather.
*   **Footwear:** Comfortable shoes for standing and walking.
*   **Signs:** We provide a small number of signs, but feel free to bring your own! **Note:** If you are bringing several signs, you can drop them off at 1000 District Ave first before parking.

### **Parking & Transportation**
**Please Read:** Parking at 1000 District Ave is strictly for customers; vehicles identified as belonging to protesters **will be towed**. 

*   **Safe parking and public transportation options will be provided via email once you register for the event.**

events.title: Call voters for a virtual phone bank to call OR-5 with Indivisible OR and Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join Indivisible Oregon and Swing Left for a virtual Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters over the phone.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call all types of voters -- not just those who vote like us.

- Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. 

You can join and call from just your computer/tablet, but we recommend being prepared with a phone and earbuds as well!

––

About the program:
This isn’t traditional phone banking—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- Why we’re starting early: launching a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns are even off the ground.

- How we’ll go big: calling every voter, not just the ones we normally rely on, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

*Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.*

events.description:
Come join us at our Downtown AVL Community Meeting held on the second Monday of each month.

Many of us are frustrated or deeply concerned about what’s happening in our government right now — the erosion of trust, the lack of accountability, and the growing sense that our voices aren’t being heard. If that resonates with you, you’re not alone.

**Meet your neighbors. Share ideas. Get involved.** Connect with others who care about change. Learn about ways to take action that match your skills, schedule, and interests.

We know it’s easier to stay home, doomscroll, or tune out altogether, so...

**Why show up?** Change happens when you’re willing to go outside your comfort zone, meet your neighbors, and discern how you want to get involved.

**At this community meeting:** You'll learn how to make your voice heard regarding local issues, NC state races and how to get out the vote.

Come meet your neighbors and explore how we can make a difference together!

(Note: We meet in the basement of the brewery.)

events.title: VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCH | Zeeland | Hosted by: Good Trouble Indivisible

address_lines: LOOK FOR JAN's YELLOW JEEP in the parking lot.

events.description:
GOOD TROUBLE INDIVISIBLE’S

— VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCH —

SATURDAY, JULY 25, 2026
ZEELAND, MICHIGAN

Good Trouble Indivisible will coordinate a silent Voter Suppression March through downtown Zeeland.

Please register in advance. We provide all signs.

Please dress in black.

Our public-awareness signs expose the laws, policies, tactics, and deliberate barriers being used to suppress the vote and silence the voices of the American people.

Voting is the foundation of representative government.

When voting rights are attacked, democracy itself is under attack.


LOCATION:

📍 Meet in front of Zeeland City Hall.

LOOK for Jan’s yellow Jeep at 11:30 AM to sign in and pick up your sign.

The march will begin promptly, so please do not be late.


SCHEDULE

⏰ 11:30 AM — Sign-in and sign pickup

Good Trouble Indivisible provides all signs. Signs are not available once the lineup begins.

⏰ 11:45 AM — Lineup and instructions

You must be present for lineup and instructions to participate in the march.

⏰ 12:00 PM — Voter Suppression March begins promptly

⏰ Event concludes at approximately 1:00 PM

Water and protein bars will be provided by Good Trouble Indivisible.

Participants will march silently in a coordinated, single-file formation through downtown Zeeland while dressed in black and carrying voter-suppression public-awareness signs.

The march is accompanied only by the steady heartbeat drum.

Participants walk slowly and silently, directly in line with the person in front of them, emulating a funeral procession representing the death of our democracy.

We do not acknowledge passersby.

We look straight ahead.

We remain expressionless.

Our Safety Team will lead and flank participants, ensure safe street crossings, and help protect the formation.

At designated points throughout the march, the procession will stop, turn toward storefronts, restaurants, and the public, and raise our signs in silent witness before continuing forward.

No chanting.

No screaming.

No chaos.

Just silent, disciplined civic resistance.

This powerful visual style of protest has drawn attention throughout Michigan and across the United States. Other organizations have contacted Good Trouble Indivisible for help replicating these marches in their own communities.

Together, we are creating a Civic Resistance Ecosystem and building public awareness through our unique model of silent, disciplined protest.


WHAT TO WEAR:

Participants dress in black clothing.

Comfortable walking shoes are strongly recommended.


HOW TO PREPARE:

WE provide the signs.

YOU dress in black.

WE provide bottled water and protein snacks.


IMPORTANT NOTES:

• This is a silent march.

• Signs will be provided.

• Participants must attend lineup and instructions.

• Please remain respectful of pedestrians, motorists, local businesses, and members of the community.

• Water and protein snacks will be provided.

• Comfortable walking shoes are recommended.

• This is a structured performance action with a limited number of signs and positions.

• Registration is required.

If the group has the time, energy, and interest following the Voter Suppression March, an additional silent march CONSTITUTIONAL VIOLATIONS, may be held. The Voter Suppression March is the only scheduled and required march. If there is group interest in a second march it will be optional, not required. 

Together, we remain visible, peaceful, disciplined, and impossible to ignore.

We the People means ALL OF US.

WATCH OUR VOTER SUPPRESSION MARCHES

See examples of our voter-suppression signs and silent-march choreography here:

👉 https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61576925081008

ABOUT GOOD TROUBLE INDIVISIBLE

Good Trouble Indivisible is a Saugatuck and Douglas–based Michigan nonprofit grassroots advocacy organization committed to nonviolent action, democratic accountability, and the defense of human rights.

GTI has organized more than 200 public actions across West Michigan.

We show up — week after week — to defend democracy, voting rights, constitutional government, human rights, and the right to peaceful protest.

VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITY

Want to help organize actions like this?

Many volunteer roles can be performed from home.

Call or text Jan Cohen at (269) 932-8806 or email:

📧 Action@GoodTroubleIndivisible.org


CONTACT US:

☎️ Good Trouble Indivisible: (616) 287-2221

☎️ Jan Cohen: (269) 932-8806

📧 Action@GoodTroubleIndivisible.org

🌐 https://goodtroubleindivisible.org

OUR COMMITMENT TO NONVIOLENCE

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action that is community-led and grounded in moral witness, public accountability, and collective care.

We expect all participants to act lawfully, seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation, and avoid engaging with individuals who disagree with our values or attempt to disrupt the event.

Weapons of any kind, including weapons legally permitted to be carried, should not be brought to this event.

⚠️ Limited positions are available.

Registration is required because this is a structured performance action with a limited number of signs.

Call or text Jan Cohen with questions at (269) 932-8806.

events.title: Civic Watch: Anderson County Commission
events.description:
The Anderson County Commission is where many of the county’s biggest public decisions are made — budgets, appointments, policy decisions, spending priorities, and issues that shape daily life across Anderson County.

These meetings are public, and Civic Watch is a simple invitation to show up, observe, and stay informed.

County Commission typically meets on the third Monday of each month, with presentations beginning at 6:00 PM and the regular meeting starting at 6:30 PM. Public comment is held at the beginning of the regular meeting.

This is not a rally or organized action event. It’s civic participation through public observation.

What to expect:
• Presentations beginning at 6:00 PM
• Regular Commission meeting at 6:30 PM
• Optional public comment at the beginning of the meeting
• Observe discussion, votes, and public business
• Take notes if you'd like
• Learn how county government works in real time

Official County Commission agendas:
https://andersoncountytn.gov/county-commission-meeting-agendas/

Can’t attend in person? Watch live:
https://www.andersoncounty.tv/live

Past meetings are archived at:
https://www.andersoncounty.tv/

If you'd like to attend with others, we’ll gather a few minutes beforehand and sit together.

Open to anyone interested in transparency, local government, and civic engagement.

events.title: Knock on doors with SouthSide Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join other SouthSide volunteers (and friends) for a canvass with Ground Truth—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. Swing Left launched this [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how Democrats connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in a targeted precinct on the Southside of Columbus, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.
