events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Montrose Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome. 
* Bathrooms are accessible at the Coffee Bean close by. 
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

*in partnership with the California Democratic Party, CADEM Chicano Latino Caucus, Avance Democratic Club, and the Grassroots Democrats HQ*

events.title: Knock doors with Iris Bender for NC House
events.description:
Join us as we head out into the neighborhood to speak with voters about the November election.

No experience necessary, and training is provided! After you've signed up to canvass, register for an online training on canvassing with MiniVAN. Click [here to sign up](https://www.mobilize.us/ncdems/event/766304/?utm_source=rsvpemail) or [here to watch a recorded training](https://youtu.be/C4mAUovRFgs).

If you have never canvassed before, we try to pair you with someone who has experience, but you can also just bring a friend if you prefer. You will need a smartphone for the MiniVAN app which incorporates GPS to help find homes, shows your script, and lets you record responses so we have them in our database. While canvassing, you will have individual doorhanger bags of candidate information to leave with voters or at their doors, a handful of voter registration forms, and contact information on our area's current representatives. 

Most of our lists will require you to drive. Some canvassing lists will be clustered fairly close together while others may require driving from house to house.

Canvassing is statistically the single best way to turn an Unaffiliated voter into a voter for Democratic candidates, so we hope you join us.

location.venue: The Democratic Party of Brown County

events.description:
NUESTRA VOZ CUENTA

Trae a un Amigo: Conoce tu Boleta
Viernes, 9 de octubre | 6:00–8:00 p. m.
Oficina de los Demócratas del Condado de Brown

¿Sabes exactamente qué aparecerá en tu boleta este noviembre? ¡Ven y descúbrelo con nosotros!

Nuestra reunión de octubre de Nuestra Voz Cuenta será una noche informal y práctica para aprender sobre tu boleta, hacer preguntas y prepararte para votar con confianza. Trae a un amigo, vecino o familiar.

Durante la noche podrás:

Encontrar tu boleta: Busca tu boleta específica según tu dirección.

Saber quién te representa: Mira mapas de los distritos del Congreso, Senado estatal, Asamblea, Junta del Condado, municipios y distritos escolares.

Conocer a los candidatos: Tendremos varios candidatos presentes para conocerlos y aprender sobre los cargos que aparecerán en la boleta.

Entender los referéndums y preguntas electorales: Veremos el lenguaje de las preguntas y explicaremos claramente qué significa votar SÍ o NO.

Aprender sobre el referéndum de las Escuelas Públicas de Green Bay.

Prepararte para votar: Averigua dónde votar, cómo votar temprano, cómo devolver una boleta de voto ausente y qué necesitas saber para el Día de las Elecciones.

No necesitas ser experto en política. Esta noche está diseñada para cualquier persona que simplemente quiera entender mejor su boleta antes de votar.

Ven con tus preguntas. Trae a un amigo. Sal preparado para votar.

location.venue: Pedestrian Bridge accessed via bike trail behind the Hampton Inn

events.description:
Visibility Brigade Democracy Wave on Pedestrian Bridge over Route 50 in Bowie, MD

This an Indivisible Bowie and Beyond (IBBMD.org) event!

Come out and show support for our large letter signs promoting Democracy, facing both east- and west-bound lanes. Two signs with large letters for easy reading by passing cars will be in place. You are invited to show your support for these messages and to encourage the public to do the same. Your presence is a powerful message! This event will also connect you with your Democracy-supporting neighbors. You are not alone and YES, we can DO something!

What you can bring: 1) American flags, and as needed 2) Drinking water, 3) Weather gear (cold, wind, sun, heat), 3) Ear plugs (it can be loud up there), 4) Chair for yourself. The cars passing underneath make it windy.

We will cancel for unsafe or miserable weather conditions (high wind, ice/snow, hard rain, hail, lightning) so please watch your email the night and morning before the start time .  We will cancel for significant (~60%-100% chance) of storms or temperatures above 95F.

We are discouraging small hand-held signs because they can't be read from a distance or at 55 mph, and so can be an unsafe distraction to drivers. We can't leave anything behind on the bridge when we leave.

events.title: Let our VOICES be heard -- our FREE SPEECH is being denied!
events.description:
*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

**Eastlake Village Marketplace, located on Otay Lakes Rd.**  

BACKSTORY:  After being at the corner in front of Islands on Otay Lakes Rd. for over 16 months, our group has been told by the Sudberry Management team that "they" own the sidewalk and they no longer want us there!  
 
We had double the amount of protesters at the first ones, we reminded them that we are peaceful and that we will not be leaving until 11 so they will have to call the police  The police arrived and waited in the lot until afterward to show the coordinator a map that included the sidewalks (as in:  Sudberry owns it!!).  He also advised that since that is NOT the norm, she should look into it.   (I call non-emergency before each and every protest-they all know me).  

Thank you to all our detectives for doing all the legwork and the legal work ... turns out they were wrong ... the city owns the space!

We showed up in greater numbers, and basically the cops never showed up for them ... same the following weekend - I chatted with the property manager afterward and she switched her story up a little bit ... said, that we are blocking the ADA ramp and that they could be sued!  

After our "detectives" once again did the research.  Turns out their existing ramp isn't quite up to standards, but it isn't worth it to make a fuss -- on either of our ends. 

SO, that all being said -- we are still wanting greater numbers at this corner to show them that this community doesn't take kindly to having our First Amendment Right to peaceful protest being blatantly violated!

So here is the updated plan - based on the last few weeks:

**DO NOT PARK IN THE MARKETPLACE PARKING LOT!  Unless you have a handicapped placard!** 

Do NOT buy one thing from any of their shops or restaurants.

Instead, we park by Kohl's and meet right at that corner on Eastlake Blvd.  Cross the street and just march to Island's on the "forbidden" sidewalk, march across the street to McD's and cross over to the Arby's and we can go back the same way and do it all over again.  

We do not step on the grass, we don't leave anything personal on the ground, we pick up after ourselves ... We keep it cleaner than we found it. 

**MOST IMPORTANTLY:  STAY CLEAR OF THEIR RAMP!   We refuse to let them intimidate us, so don't give them even 1 reason.  We move out of the way of ANY passersby!  Don't even wait for them to have to say "excuse me" ... just make plenty of room for them ... we smile and we are friendly (they might want to join us!) ... ESPECIALLY if a walker or a wheelchair or even just a bike needs to pass!

Signs to consider - anything First Amendment/Free Speech themed ... maybe even call out Sudberry for trying to stifle us!  

 We want the community to stay away from places that don't honor our basic first amendment right to free speech!  

**Remember that driving by and beeping counts as RESISTANCE!  I can't say it enough, it's invaluable!  I know gas prices suck, but if you are nearby, drive by a few times and make a TON of noise!**

Also, this is for those of you who can't be physically on the streets, but you still want to RESIST from the comfort of your own home:

How about calling one or more of the restaurants in the Food Court that sees and hears our protests weekly ... to remind them that we refuse to do business when our voices are being silenced!   Here is the link for the names and the phone numbers:

https://shopeastlakemarketplace.com/

I ask to speak to the lead manager .. we are polite, but right to the point ... *we used to support your business, but no longer* is your message and then tell them whatever your reason is that your money will no longer be spent ... Remember that lots of them are on OUR side (I know Luna Grill is with us, for instance ... I also know that Great Clips is NOT -the owner harassed us over a year ago and was a real live one! -- feel free to call Great Clips repeatedly .................).  You don't need to give them your name, just tell them you are a customer and you are disappointed in their stance on free speech.  

The second part of this, is that if you can actually boycott as many of these places as possible, I guarantee the message will be heard!

See you Sunday -- tell your friends!  Make this the protest you come out and support for the next few weeks until they stop harassing us.

More information to consider:

*1 sign or whatever you can carry
*plan on walking back and forth, so be comfortable
*leave valuables in your car (license and cc or a few bucks if you want)
*wear sunscreen AND your hat
*clean up after your fur babies
*don't forget your water bottles

See you on the streets!
Janine
events.accessibility_notes: just be ready to walk ... we need to keep this protest moving because we don't want to give them even one reason to harass us!  Be comfortable!  Protect from the sun!

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Carlisle, PA (PA-10th District) to Elect Janelle Stelson
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass in Carlisle PA and nearby areas to help elect Janelle Stelson to the US Congress, rebuild trust in Democratic candidates more broadly, and flip the House Blue in November. Ground Truth (https://ourgroundtruth.org) is an innovative program that is revolutionizing how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on doors of persuadable voters, people who are not fully committed to voting for either Democrats or Republicans, are still making up their minds about whether to vote or who to vote for, and potentially open to voting for Democrats.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Learn why people are unsure about whether to vote or who to vote for and gain insights about what might persuade them to vote for Janelle Stelson and other Democrats on November 3rd. We'll share our insights with Democratic campaigns.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking doors of Independents, Republicans, and Democrats who might be persuaded to vote for Democrats.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Waunakee Weekly Rally for Democracy and Free Speech
events.description:
Join the Waunakee Democracy and Free Speech rally, where WE THE PEOPLE gather in a peaceful and family-friendly manner to stand for our shared American values in the rules and laws of our democracy. We rally against the MAGA regime’s unconstitutional actions.

While its getting cold, we all agreed to continue because the issues are so important. We must stop the harmful actions that threaten our families, communities, and nation. Take a stand for protecting Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, Federal agencies, National parks, the Free press, Judicial systems, Educational institutions, the Environment, Equity/Diversity/Inclusion, US Aid, Immigrant rights, and more...

Gather with our community Thursdays from 4:00 to 5:00 pm at the Waunakee Village Park (HW 19) near the 6 mile creek bridge and Village Waterworks Building. Parking is available in park. Sometimes we may have hot chocolate and snacks or go afterwards to a local cafe to warm up.

Bring signs that let others know what matters to you. Some signs are available for use. Dress for the Weather and bring your calendars so we can plan future events. We are joining Mazomanie, Middleton and many other communities in holding similar events to Rally for Democracy!

Please bring positive signs only. Some examples: Instead of "Stop defunding science" Say "Protect Research" "Immigrants make us stronger" "Housing for all" "Healthcare for all" "Save the planet"

Make signs about what you're standing up for -- whether that is the libraries, DEI, healthcare, women’s rights

Please no mocking signs, no swastikas

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!

See you every Friday engaging drivers in Clayton.

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

events.description:
**Woodbury Indivisible Monthly Meetup**

_Location provided upon signup_

**Are you a progressive neighbor looking to connect, get informed, and take action right here in Woodbury? Come join us!**

Woodbury Indivisible is a local, grassroots group of neighbors committed to preserving our democracy and living our progressive values — and we're thrilled to finally have a home right here in our community. We're part of a nationwide movement of thousands of Indivisible groups working together to make a difference.

At our monthly meetups, you can expect:

-What's happening — We share updates on issues at the federal, state, and local levels so you stay informed and know where attention is needed.

-Neighbor spotlights — Hear from fellow community members about the good work they're already doing. You might be surprised who's in your backyard! 

-Civic engagement 101 (and beyond) — We teach each other how to get involved, from city council meetings to calling your representatives.

-Opportunities to act — Whether it's through Woodbury Indivisible or other aligned organizations doing great work, we'll connect you with ways to plug in.

**No experience necessary. No litmus test. Just show up as you are, ready to meet your neighbors and make a difference.

New to the group? You are especially welcome here.**

*Light snacks provided.*

Indivisible Moscow is a local grassroots group affiliated with Indivisible.org. events.title: Call voters in Arizona CD 01 with Ground Truth!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth Phone Bank designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters over the phone.  (https://ourgroundtruth.org)

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call all types of voters -- not just those who vote like us.

- Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. 

You can join and call from just your computer/tablet, but we recommend being prepared with a phone and earbuds as well!

––

About the program:
This isn’t traditional phone banking—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- Why we’re starting early: launching a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns are even off the ground.

- How we’ll go big: calling every voter, not just the ones we normally rely on, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

*Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.*

events.description:
Volunteer with RISE UP AGAINST Domestic Violence

RISE UP AGAINST Domestic Violence is a community-led movement dedicated to raising awareness, increasing access to resources, advocating for legislative change, and creating spaces for healing, connection, and hope. This march brings together survivors, victims, advocates, family members, allies, and community supporters who have been impacted—directly or indirectly—by domestic, family, intimate partner, and interpersonal violence.

We are seeking volunteers to help both before and during the event. Opportunities include:

Posting and distributing flyers
Printing or donating copy services
Community outreach and resource gathering
Collecting water, snacks, and supplies for participants
Event setup and breakdown
Safety Team volunteers
First Aid and Emergency Response volunteers
Resource and information table support
Participant check-in and wayfinding assistance
General event support

This event is more than a march—it is a gathering rooted in community, healing, education, remembrance, empowerment, and collective action. Together, we honor survivors, support those currently navigating abuse, remember those we have lost, advocate for meaningful change, and celebrate the courage, resilience, and liberation that are possible on the healing journey.

Whether you can volunteer for an hour, a day, donate supplies, share resources, or help spread the word, your support helps create a safer, stronger, and more connected community.

Join us as we RISE UP, speak out, and stand together against domestic violence. 💜

Location: Seattle, Washington

Everyone is welcome. Survivors, advocates, service providers, community organizations, family members, friends, and allies are encouraged to participate.

events.title: Protect the Vote: Inside Poll Observer Training
events.description:
### This is the _Live on Zoom_ training, you can find the _On-Demand_ training here: https://mobilize.us/s/oQ3mL0

# Protect the Vote as a Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Inside Poll observers help ensure election laws are followed, identify potential issues, and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

### What You'll Learn

- Poll observer basics
- What to expect at the polling place
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role poll observers play in protecting voters

### Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Poll observers serve as our eyes and ears inside polling places, helping ensure election laws are followed and that voters can cast their ballots without unnecessary barriers.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

#### No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as a poll observer.



#### Important: This session is for NCDP Inside Poll Observers. 
If you are an **attorney, law graduate, or law student** looking to serve as an **At-Large Legal Poll Observer through the NC Voter Protection Alliance (NCVPA),** please sign up here: https://tinyurl.com/NC26LegalPollObserver

events.title: VOTEFEST 3.0 - MARCH TO THE POLLS
events.description:
2:00–3:30 PM — VOTEFEST IN THE PARK
3:30 PM — MARCH TO THE POLLS

October 24 is a big day: it’s the last day to register to vote and the first day of early voting. So we’re turning MacDonald Park into a celebration of participation — with music, signs, art, food, voter information, and HeadCount on site registering voters right up to the deadline.

At 3:30, we’ll pick up our VOTEFEST signs, carry them at the front, and take the energy of the park into the streets as we head to the polls together. Marching together to vote draws on a powerful American tradition, rooted in Black churches and communities in the South, where voting became more than an individual act — it became something communities did together, visibly and joyfully.

Before the march, VOTEFEST will fill the park with the Curtis Watts Trio, Great Neck Singing Resistance, the League of Women Voters, HeadCount, hands-on art projects, voter information, civic action, empanadas, and plenty of reasons to stay awhile.

Register. Sing. Make art. Get informed. Then at 3:30, we take it to the streets — and to the polls.

events.description:
Ready to make a real impact for Senator Judy Seeberger and Senate District 41? 

We are hitting the pavement to have the critical face-to-face conversations that win close elections. Door knocking is one of the most effective tools we have to turn out voters, persuade undecided neighbors, and make sure people know what Judy Seeberger has done for our communities. Judy knows exactly how much every vote matters. In 2022, she won this seat by just 321 votes. Those 321 votes were the difference between winning and losing, and they helped secure the DFL’s narrow one-seat majority in the Minnesota Senate. 

Today, the DFL still holds the Senate by just one seat, while the Minnesota House is evenly split. That means Senate District 41 is not just another race; it could help determine the balance of power at the Capitol. That is why this shift matters. Research and campaign experience have shown that strong direct voter contact can move turnout by up to 5 points, and in a district decided by only a few hundred votes, that impact can be the difference between victory and defeat. 

Every door we knock on brings us one step closer to re-electing Judy and protecting the progress we have made on clean water, public safety, consumer protection, strong schools, veterans, broadband, and support for working families. Judy brings the experience of a firefighter, paramedic, attorney, and state senator and voters deserve to hear directly why her leadership matters for Senate District 41. 

Whether you are a seasoned canvassing pro or this is your very first time, we will make sure you are fully prepared. We will start with a comprehensive training, go over our talking points, answer questions, and set you up with a partner if you would like. Campaigns are won by people talking to people. In a race this close, every conversation matters. Join us, knock a few doors, and help us build the voter engagement we need to deliver a strong win for Judy Seeberger in November.

Event Details
What to Bring: Please wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a fully charged cell phone. We will be using a mobile app to track our progress!

What We Provide: Training, literature, snacks, and plenty of team spirit.

Your voice is the most powerful tool we have. Let's get out there, meet our neighbors, and share our vision for the future!

events.description:
### 📞 Help North Carolina Recruit Poll Observers!

North Carolina will play a decisive role in determining control of the U.S. Senate and protecting the freedom to vote in 2026. Help us recruit the **Poll Observers** we'll need to meet that moment.

### What will I be doing?

We'll be calling North Carolinians who have volunteered with Voter Protection before or expressed interest in getting involved and inviting them to serve as **Poll Observers this fall.**

**And these calls work!** Nearly half of the people we've talked to about becoming a Poll Observer have said **YES!**

### We'll give you everything you need:
- A script and call list
- Training at the beginning of the phonebank
- Live support throughout the session

### Make an impact in North Carolina — from wherever you are.

This is a great way to support voter protection in a battleground state and make an immediate impact, no matter where you're calling from.

**No prior experience required. Come help us Protect the Vote!**

events.title: Postcard writing
events.description:
Join us every Tuesday morning for a postcard-writing party at Boston Bean, in Maynard from  9 - 11 am.

Just drop in for all or for part of the time.

Send hand-written postcards to voters in states that will play a key role in taking back Congress and in electing leaders who will fight back against the current authoritarian regime. Postcards educate voters, urge them to register to vote, and urge them to vote for specific candidates in special elections, primaries, and the November 2026 mid-term elections. Hand-written postcards have been proven in multiple studies to boost turnout enough to swing elections. Each packet of 15 postcards has everything you need, and costs $10 to cover stamps and cards for those who can afford it.

It's more fun to write together, but if you can't stay, you can also stop by and pick up postcards to write at home.

This a local Indivisible event! for more info you can check out or website indivisiblemayard.org or contact us at info@indivisiblemaynard.org

events.title: Compost Hub Support: Augustus Hawkins
events.description:
At our Compost Hubs, food scraps collected from the community are transformed into nutrient-rich compost, and we need your help to make it happen! As a Compost Hub Support Volunteer, you’ll gain hands-on experience working alongside our knowledgeable Compost Managers. Get ready to leave feeling accomplished, a little sweaty, and brimming with new compost knowledge. 

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
Roll up your sleeves and dive into a variety of engaging activities, whether it’s managing a three-bin system, tending to a compost pile, sifting finished compost, or exploring a mix of everything. There’s something for everyone, from beginners to seasoned pros! Plus, our Compost Hubs are situated in LA County’s most cherished green spaces: community gardens, urban farms, and beautiful parks. Join passionate community composters, learn to turn food scraps into rich compost, and connect with the local food system. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You will be working outdoors! Shade levels vary by site.
* Activity level can be adjusted to your comfort and abilities; just communicate with your Compost Manager.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* This location has bathrooms available
* If you sign up, we ask that you show up! We rely on volunteers, like you, to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under the age of 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 

VOLUNTEER WAIVER 
Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. You can access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver 

CODE OF CONDUCT
All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: Monthly Meeting/Huddle
events.description:
This a local Indivisible Maynard Area event!

We meet the 2nd Thursday each month at the Maynard Firehouse to get informed and to take action.  We alternate between trainings, speakers, and more traditional huddles but try to have some kind of action involved at each. Past actions included prepping for No Kings and other standouts, folding zines about reporting ICE, putting together whistle kits, signing petitions and postcard writing.

For our October meeting we are focused on the midterms.  Christine Brown of Indivisible Acton Area and TurnPurple2Blue.org will give a talk called  "What will it take to WIN the midterms -and how can YOU make a difference?" She will walk us through some key US races and final actions we can take to bring in a blue wave. We will also share some important information around election protection and will do some prep for our Oct 17 No Kings: Vote Early event at Haynes Court.

We collect canned and dry packaged food for Open Table at our meetings. Please bring something to donate if you are able.

events.title: Peaceful Standout Against Authoritarianism
events.description:
This a Indivisible Maynard Area event!

We meet the 3rd Saturday of every month to stand up against authoritarianism.  Between ICE's cruelty, attempts to affect the election, the Iran War, corruption and grifting by the WH, attacks on science and our democratic institutions, we have a lot to protest! 

Signs welcome, but we usually do have some extra to offer. Let's stand together as a community to fight for our democracy and our rights and give voice to those unable to speak. 

We moved to a new location!  We will be at the corner of Concord St. and Haynes St in the grassy area across the street from the Cat Cottage.  Parking is available on the nearby side streets or in the lot along the bike path behind Maynard Outdoor Store

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: Constitutional Observer Training
events.description:
## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

IMPORTANT NOTE: We are still working out a few details with the City of Wentzville. If anything changes you will be sent a notification via Mobilize.

Signage

Wentzville has an ordinance that limits sign dimensions to 24"x24", and a banner cannot exceed 8’wide and 3’ high. If the sign has a staff, it cannot be larger than 40” and must be blunt on each end. IWWP appreciates the professionalism of the Wentzville Police Department, so please help maintain a good relationship with them by complying with their ordinances.

Please be sensitive to the needs of businesses in the area and refrain from using the parking spots set aside for their customers. There is plenty of parking in Walmart’s lot.

There is an easy access point to the sidewalk between Walgreens and Applebee’s. Help show your appreciation to the local community by doing a little shopping or having a bite to eat before or after the protest.

events.title: Knock Doors in Sault Ste. Marie!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most! Doors don't take a break during the week and neither do we - join us Tuesday through Friday to talk to voters.

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Book Group: "One Day Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This" by Omar El Akkad
events.description:
Join us as we discuss "One Day Everyone Will Have Always been Against This" by Omar El Akkad.

Description from the publisher's website: 
NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER • NATIONAL BOOK AWARD WINNER • From award-winning novelist and journalist Omar El Akkad comes a powerful reckoning with what it means to live in a West that betrays its fundamental values.

“[A] bracing memoir and manifesto.” —The New York Times

“I can’t think of a more important piece of writing to read right now. I found hope here, and help, to face what the world is now, all that it isn’t anymore. Please read this. I promise you won’t regret it.” —Tommy Orange, bestselling author of Wandering Stars and There There

A NEW YORK TIMES NOTABLE BOOK • PALESTINE BOOK AWARD WINNER • FINALIST FOR THE NATIONAL BOOK CRITICS CIRCLE AWARD FOR CRITICISM

On October 25, 2023, after just three weeks of the bombardment of Gaza, Omar El Akkad put out a tweet: “One day, when it’s safe, when there’s no personal downside to calling a thing what it is, when it’s too late to hold anyone accountable, everyone will have always been against this.” This tweet has been viewed more than 10 million times.

As an immigrant who came to the West, El Akkad believed that it promised freedom. A place of justice for all. But in the past twenty years, reporting on the War on Terror, Ferguson, climate change, Black Lives Matter protests, and more, and watching the unmitigated slaughter in Gaza, El Akkad has come to the conclusion that much of what the West promises is a lie. That there will always be entire groups of human beings it has never intended to treat as fully human—not just Arabs or Muslims or immigrants, but whoever falls outside the boundaries of privilege. One Day, Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This is a chronicle of that painful realization, a moral grappling with what it means, as a citizen of the U.S., as a father, to carve out some sense of possibility in a time of carnage.

This is El Akkad’s nonfiction debut, his most raw and vulnerable work to date, a heartsick breakup letter with the West. It is a brilliant articulation of the same breakup we are watching all over the United States, in family rooms, on college campuses, on city streets; the consequences of this rupture are just beginning. This book is for all the people who want something better than what the West has served up. This is the book for our time

Let’s pick up the phones, connect with our community, and build sustainable power together!

Court ends: between 10:30 and 11:00 AM

ICE has stepped up enforcement in Robertson County. Families are being separated. Neighbors who have lived here for years are being pulled into deportation proceedings. Our presence at the courthouse, peaceful, visible, and consistent, does three things:

events.title: Protest ICE Deportations & the AROCC Detention Center at Mesa Gateway Airport
events.description:
## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

When local lawmakers recently conducted a surprise visit to the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center here at Mesa Gateway, they were sickened by what they found. Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

#### 📢 Join us on Saturday, October 24th to challenge the illegal, inhumane, and unconstitutional ICE removal operations!

    
--------------------------------------

## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- We have compiled public records, congressional oversight letters, and local reporting into one place. 
- Please read our complete [Mesa Valley Indivisible AROCC and ICE Air Deportations Fact Sheet](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/ice-deportationsarocc) to understand the full scope of our key concerns and see how you can take action.

--------------------------------------
## 🚨 Important! 🚨

- To ensure you receive all necessary information for the upcoming event, please make sure you have officially registered via Mobilize.
- All vital updates—including parking instructions, logistical changes, and additional details—will be sent to the email address provided during registration. 
  - If you have not registered on the platform, we will be unable to send you these updates.
  - Keep an eye out for emails from Mesa Valley Indivisible and check your spam/junk folder if you do not see them!
  - [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) prioritizes strategic visibility to ensure our message reaches the widest possible audience. To keep our movement growing, we protest at high-traffic areas where Mesa residents are most likely to see us and join the cause.

--------------------------------------------

The 2026 November General Election is around the corner on Tuesday, November 3. Now it’s time to turn your support for affordable child care into meaningful action. Let’s make sure Colorado voters are ready to show up for family affordability. 

Join Move Colorado Forward for a hands-on Get Out the Vote (GOTV) training focused on learning how to help voters understand what’s at stake this November and taking action together to reach voters and the people in our networks.

We’ll give you the tools, talking points, and confidence you need to have effective conversations with voters about Proposition NN, child care, and the November election- and then we’ll put those tools to work together.

This will be an action-oriented session. You’ll learn:

- What is GOTV and why is it important?
- How to talk with voters about Proposition NN and child care on their ballot
- How to connect with your own networks and reach voters in your community
- How to use the phone banking tools and resources you need to take meaningful action
- How to have clear, respectful conversations that help people make a plan to vote

After the training, we’ll spend time taking action together — reaching out to our networks and voters and building the momentum we need heading into November.

Whether you’ve never made a phone call before or you’re already a seasoned volunteer, there’s a role for you. You don’t need to be an expert - we’ll give you everything you need to get started.

events.title: Political Fundraising: Legal or a Scam?
events.description:
**Your donations could be going to a grifter, not a campaign or candidate.** 

Ever wonder why you’re getting so many political fundraising emails and texts? Have you wondered if they are legit or just a scam? 

ScamBusters is proud to offer a free (virtual) class to educate you:

- about good and bad political action committees (PACs), 

- why and how you're targeted

- how to identify potential fraudulent PACs, and 

- where you can be assured your hard earned money goes to the causes you care about, instead of grifters. 

This informative presentation ends with some instructions on how to 'throttle the noise', reduce unwanted spammy texts and emails.

events.description:

While virtual text banking is live, the advocacy team of ACLU of Indiana will host 30-minute Zoom orientations most Tuesdays and Thursdays. These training and helpline sessions will orient new volunteers and address any questions that arise for volunteers already trained and engaged in phone banking. 

ACLU of Indiana text banks are conducted remotely. No prior experience is necessary. You only need a phone, computer, and internet access to participate from the comfort of your home. You will use provided scripts and suggested responses to help voters register, inform them of what’s on their ballot or encourage them to turn out to the polls. 

Once trained, volunteers may text on their own schedule, while the text bank link is active, (and so long as calls are made within the hours of 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time of person being called).

We the People are stronger together. 
Join us to text bank! Action is the antidote to anxiety. 
~ ACLU Indiana Advocacy Team

events.description:
We will be working on restoration and landscaping every Monday and every 3rd Saturday in Wheeler. There is something for everyone--removing blackberry, ivy, knotweed; planting native species; and distributing woodchips!

For Saturday 9/19--we will be installing more holes and will need help using a post hole digger and restacking rocks around the culvert on the south section of the trail. Some of the larger railroad ballast had made its way back onto the trail, and we assistance cleaning that area up.

Please bring loppers, a rake, work gloves, water, and a snack for yourself. We will have extra tools and gloves if you do not own any. 

We will meet behind the railroad tracks on Marine Dr and Hemlock St (west side of Hwy 101) in Wheeler at 10AM.

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

events.title: Glenwood IN-PERSON letter writing to voters with SwingLeftHoCoMD
events.description:
This event is ONLY for IN-PERSON letter/postcard writing attendees. There is a separate zoom event for a monthly status update and letter/postcard writing on your own.

Starting in April '26 we will be writing Vote Forward letters. The Vote Forward team is piloting our latest program—New Voter Guides—with newly registered voters in Pennsylvania. Self-mailing so no envelopes needed!

The evening will start with a 10-15 minute status update. Then we'll dive into writing.

If LETTERS: We'll have the letters printed. You bring a blue and/or colored pens, 20 first class stamps, and sticker rounds or clear tape. NO ENVELOPES NEEDED !

If POSTCARDS: We'll have the postcards, and addresses. They encourage people to use multiple colors of pens to make the postcards more eye-catching. And bring 25 postcard stamps (61 cents).

Not a HCLS sponsored event.

and now for the small print: Join me for a letter writing party, where we'll be writing letters using an award-winning, proven tactic to reach potential voters in important upcoming elections.

RSVP here, and we’ll let you know how to join this party. Invite your friends, too and let them know that Swing Left is pioneering an innovative program, using letters to help volunteers like us turn out voters through our letter-writing affiliate, Vote Forward.

Think about it: if you help get a voter to the polls, that is an important step towards creating a more inclusive and equitable government and society. Looking forward to seeing you!

LOOK FOR: (White Honda Acura SUV with rear hatch lifted)

events.title: Deep Canvass for Democracy Phonebank
events.description:
Times are hard, and people are tuning out of politics in big numbers. But if people give up on our democracy, our communities will pay the price. That's why People's Action Institute's Deep Canvass for Democracy program is helping people rediscover their self-interest in political life. Democracy depends on ordinary people talking with one another about the issues that shape our lives. Yet many of us have never learned how to have conversations in a way that builds trust and understanding and leads to action.

At a time when so many people feel disconnection, distrust, and uncertainty, our ability to engage across differences isn’t just a skill - It's how we save our democratic norms.

Deep Canvassing is a tool that has proved we can build across differences and win the things we need in our lives. It uses curiosity and storytelling to give people a new perspective and energy to fight for change.

Whether you want to deepen connection as a community leader, neighbor, or within your own family, join us to learn how to Deep Canvass.

### National Hear America Canvass Day
On Saturday, October 10th, 11 member groups across 8 states will hold a day of action to go out, listen to voters' concerns, and contribute to our 300,000 conversation goal. So far, we are at 100,000 conversations and hope to make a huge dent in our goal today.
Launch starts at 12-1 Eastern, and the in-person canvass team returns at 4:30 pm Eastern to debrief our conversations from the day.

In this Deep Canvass training and phonebank, you'll learn about compassionate curiosity, storytelling, and dialer hours, and talk to real people to practice your skill set. No experience is needed.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join us and special guest **Beto O'Rourke** for the **Every Campus Counts** tour at **SHSU**! We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with existing and potential student voters
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone.

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, we ask all volunteers to arrive **60 minutes before Beto arrives** for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[10:00-11:00am]: Setup & Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals before the crowd gathers.

- **[11:00am-4:00pm] Voter Registration & Mobilization** | The main event! We hit the campus ground running and get folks set up on Reach (plus a special appearance by Beto!)

- **[4:00-5:00pm]: Takedown & Post-Event Debrief** | We will pack up our gear, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: TBD

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes

Let's keep building on our momentum and ensure every single campus counts. Sign up for a shift today!

events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join us and special guest **Beto O'Rourke** for the **Every Campus Counts** tour at **Rice**! We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with existing and potential student voters
- Register eligible voters on the spot
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Voter Registrar Requirements

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, _whether you are certified or not_.

- **Important Note**: If you want to physically register voters at this event, you **MUST** be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (VDR) in at least **Harris County**.

events.description:
# Knock Doors with Families Not Politics — Defend Colorado Kids and Families

This November, Colorado voters will decide two ballot measures that sound simple but aren't. Propositions 134 and 135 are being sold as measures about fairness and safety — but the fine print tells a different story, and voters deserve to know it before they vote.

Propositions 134 is so vague that it could subject *any* kid, in *any* sport, from kindergarten through college, to invasive verification just to prove they belong on the field. Propositions 135 hands medical decisions that belong to families and doctors over to politicians — and could block care for kids who aren't even transgender, including teens fighting cancer.

That's where you come in. Join Families Not Politics for a community canvass and help us have real conversations with Colorado voters about what these measures actually do. Our research is clear: when voters hear the full picture, they move — but it takes volunteers like you, at the doors, making the case.

No experience needed. We'll kick things off with training and a team briefing before heading out together, and you'll leave with everything you need to have a confident, meaningful conversation. Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and come ready to talk with your neighbors.

Every conversation moves a voter. Every voter we move gets us closer to defeating these measures in November. We hope you'll join us.

This is the ONLY Saturday voting that Caldwell County is hosting this season!
We need your help to get out the vote and get the information into people's hands!

Sign up for a shift, or stay for the day.
Make sure to pack enough snacks and water for your stay!
(We'll try, but we can't guarantee what will be there)

***A few things!
*Please come prepared to be insulted. It happens every season. 
*Be polite or grey wall negativity. Let them end up on the news for bad behavior, not us.
*If you speak Spanish, great! We do have Spanish speaking Democrats in the area, the more help they get to vote, the better.
*Be prepared for the weather.
*Be kind.
*Be helpful.
*Please don't fight, bicker, or debate. We're here to present a positive side of politics.
*Get out and meet your neighbors. This is a great way to find out who is in our corner.
*Help candidates get elected!

events.description:
**It's time to talk to Democratic voters in CA-22!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to win in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join Indivisible Yolo & fellow Yolo County activists, in partnership with the Bay Area Coalition, going door-to-door talking to Democratic voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our 2026 voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them. **$100 stipend** a day available to offset the cost of gas and lodging.

This canvass can be a one day canvass, departing Davis early in the morning, canvass for the day and return in the evening, or volunteers can also register for both Friday and Saturday and/or Sunday, canvassing and stay overnight on Friday and/or Saturday nights. 

  * Friday, October 9 | 9:30 to 6:00 pm or 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm
  * Saturday, October 10 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm
  * Sunday, October 11 | 9:30 am to 2:30 pm

Once you've signed up, a volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location, you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition Yes, You Can(vass)! workshop Tuesdays, 7 pm - https://www.mobilize.us/indivisibleyolo/event/987496/

events.title: Handmaids of Las Vegas STAND at HENDERSON DETENTION CENTER!
events.description:
Join the Handmaids of Las Vegas: Stand for Justice and Solidarity

Dear compassionate souls of Las Vegas,

We invite you to join the Handmaids of Las Vegas as we unite in a powerful demonstration of solidarity for immigrant rights on Saturdays at the Henderson Detention Center in Henderson, NV. Our stands will take place from 7:30pm to 8:30pm, where we will stand together, clad in the iconic red uniforms of the handmaids, to echo the call for justice and equality.

A Stand for Dignity and Humanity
Under the current Trump regime, immigrants and people of color have faced cruel and inhumane treatment. Families have been torn apart, and countless individuals have been subjected to unjust policies that strip away their dignity and rights. We believe that every person deserves to be treated with respect and compassion, regardless of their background or origin.

How You Can Show Support
Join Us: Wear red and stand with us in solidarity. Your presence will amplify our message and show that our community stands united.

Donate: Bring non-perishable food and clothing to help support our local community. Your contributions make a significant difference in the lives of those in need.

Together, We Rise
This is not just a call to action; it is a call to the heart. By standing together, we send a powerful message that we will not remain silent in the face of injustice. Let us continue to stand until justice prevails, and every individual is treated with the respect they deserve.

Join us, bring your compassion, and be a part of a movement that believes in the power of unity and love. Together, we can create a brighter, more just future for all.

With hope and determination,

The Handmaids of Las Vegas

Join us every Sunday as we mass lit-drop in support of Ian Schwartz for State Representative (District 62) and Joe Wessels for Clermont County Commissioner.

Meeting Time: Every Sunday at 3:45 PM

Meeting Place: The Milford Shopping Center (975 Lila Ave)

Canvassing Begins: 4:00 PM

Duration: 1-2 hours (expect to be finished before 6:00 PM)

What is lit-dropping?  It's even easier than canvassing - no door-knocking, complex lists, or apps required!  All you need to do is place a door-hanger on as many doors as possible on the street / area that you are assigned.

New to lit-dropping? No problem! You'll be paired with an experienced volunteer who will walk with you and show you the ropes.

We provide campaign shirts & buttons, the literature, and the areas to cover.

Remember to bring comfortable walking shoes and water.

events.title: Tucson Shutdown Committee, Sun., 9/13 and weekly thereafter
events.description:
Tucson Shutdown

Please join Shutdown Trump Committee meeting, by Zoom, weekly on Sundays. The Steering Committee meets from 7-730 pm each week, followed by the General Meeting, from 7:30-8:30 pm. All are welcome to observe the Steering Committee meeting, but only the Steering Committee members (active Working Committee heads and sponsoring organizational reps) participate and vote.  You will be given the zoom link after you sign up. This meeting is for anyone who wants to volunteer.

Trump has threatened to cancel the mid-term elections. This would be a crucial step in completing his authoritarian takeover. The only thing that has been shown to reliably stop such a takeover is large-scale, non-violent noncooperation. An historic coalition came together in St. Louis in late May to call for exactly such a shutdown–if he does try to cancel the election. MayDayStrong.org has 600 labor unions and community groups as members.  Seven representatives from Tucson organizations went to St. Louis, including Democracy Unites Us, Party for Socialism and Liberation, Tucson Democratic Socialists of American and the local African-heritage ministerial alliance. Nine cities representing 30% of the economy have already committed to disrupt their economies for two weeks in case he does try to cancel the elections, so called “Tier 1” cities. Some of us in Tucson seek to make us a “Tier 2” city, to support the national Shutdown by disrupting our local economy as much as possible, at or above the scale of January 30th, for as long as we can. 

Please join us as individuals or representing a group.

events.title: Get out the Vote with Dayenu and Center for Common Ground
events.description:
### Dayenu is a U.S.-based Jewish climate organization that advocates for bold climate action while also supporting voting rights and civic engagement as essential to building a more just and sustainable future. In this phone bank, they join forces with Center for Common Ground to reduce voting barriers and get out the vote for the 2026 midterm elections.

### We are calling Black voters in Georgia, encouraging them to vote in the upcoming midterm election and providing resources that make it easier to check where they are registered and find the voting information they need.

#### Make calls with us every Tuesday from 3 pm PT/6 pm ET to 5pm PT/ 8 pm PT. 

Beginning phone banker? We start each call with a training for anyone who needs it. You can also train yourself beforehand by checking out [our training slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGstUCSwjE/oWn7cjYLXJDiksQn6VbPww/view?utm_content=DAGstUCSwjE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f8f5f4824).

Experienced? You can start making these calls immediately and pop back into the zoom with any questions along the way.

You can also make these calls on your own time 9am-8pm within the target state's time zone - no need to wait for an event!

For more information about this phone bank, please visit the [CFCG Phonebank Page](http://centerforcommonground.org/phonebanks)

events.description:
Nobody understands what our neighborhoods need better than the people living in them.

You already see what's happening right where you live. Some of these challenges are big, like the cost of housing, access to affordable healthcare,  and whether our public schools stay fully funded. Others are challenges only the people who live here know and see. What connects them all is that too many of the decisions shaping our neighborhoods are made without us, and our communities deserve the resources we need to thrive.

No experience needed — just a willingness to listen, share, and build a stronger community together. This is where change actually starts. Come be part of it!

Join Indivisible Georgia District 10 and Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. Ground Truth is a new approach to voter contact that’s changing how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors (https://ourgroundtruth.org).

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

You’ll receive additional details, including the meeting location, after you sign-up. Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference. 

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Monday Night School: How Power Works?

Who makes the decisions that shape our communities—and how can we influence them?

Working Families Power hosts Monday Night School: How Power Works an interactive introduction to civics through a lens of organizing and power.

This isn't a traditional government class. Together, we'll break down how government works at the state, county, and local levels, explore who holds power, how decisions are made, and how everyday people can organize to shape the policies that affect our lives.

Whether you're new to organizing or looking to deepen your understanding, this session will give you practical knowledge you can use as an organizer, advocate, volunteer, or community leader.

We'll cover:

* How power works in our communities
* The roles of federal, state, county, and local government
* Who makes the decisions that affect our daily lives
* How organizing transforms people power into political power
* Ways to get involved with Working Families Power

You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how change happens—and the tools to help make it happen.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 7th Ave & Osborn in midtown Phoenix
events.description:
**Join us for our afternoon rally on 7th Ave & Osborne in midtown Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 4:00. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 5:30 PM. Some attendees meet up afterward at Mi Patio ($4.99 margaritas!), others go to Lix Uptown Ice Cream ($4 scoops!). We’re a friendly bunch.

🅿️ There’s plenty of parking in the Safeway lot on the NE corner. We haven’t had issues before, but parking enforcement is unpredictable. If concerned, check with others.

🚦🚶‍➡️ We gather on all four corners of the intersection, with the primary meeting spot on the northeast corner of 7th Ave & Osborn.

🖌️ One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.title: Knock Doors For Climate Champions in La Crosse
events.description:
Personal conversations are the most effective way to inspire voter participation. We will be talking to voters about the stakes of the election and connecting with them on important issues like affordability and data centers.

First time knocking doors? Canvassing is easy, fun, and rewarding! We'll provide training and everything you need to feel confident out there.

events.title: Abdul El-Sayed and William Lawrence Phonebank
events.description:
Michigan is going to be close, and Doctor Adbul El-Sayed and William Lawrence have cross endorsed! Medicare for All is possible if we elect them to Congress, so come phonebank for them for until election day!

Join us daily from 5 PM EST to 8 PM EST as we phonebank for both of these amazing candidates, starting on September 28th until Election Day, November 3rd.

events.title: Canvass with Julia Andrews for Vermont
events.description: Join Andrews for Vermont to knock on doors and talk to Vermonters about Julia's race to win back her House seat! Meet us on the Westford Common for a brief canvass training before heading out to talk with neighbors!

We meet in the back room at The Corner Cup Coffee shop on Main Street in Tucker. 

As we are moving into the election season, we are getting our team organized to begin canvassing, phone banking, and other activities to get more Dems out to vote this Fall. If we do this, we can win so many things! Come find out what we are doing and where you can plug in.

events.title: Northwood Fall Festival Parade Walkers
events.description:
Help us bring the campaign straight to the streets of Wood County! We're looking for volunteers to march in local parades this summer and fall, tossing candy to kids and handing out campaign literature to the crowds lining the route. It's one of the most fun, low-pressure ways to get involved — no experience needed, just enthusiasm and comfortable walking shoes.

What you'll do:

Walk the parade route with our campaign group/float Toss candy to spectators (kid-friendly, non-choking-hazard candy provided) Hand out campaign literature and answer quick questions from voters

What to bring:

Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing Water bottle Sunscreen or a hat (for daytime events)

What we provide:

Campaign t-shirts/buttons Candy and literature to hand out A great time and a chance to connect with your neighbors!

events.title: Holland Door Knocking!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!


This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.


Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.


Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.


Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ 7th St & McDowell in Central Phoenix
events.description:
**Join us for our Tuesday morning rally on 7th St & McDowell in Central Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 7:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 8:30 AM.

🅿️ There’s plenty of parking in the Safeway lot on the NW corner. We haven’t had issues before, but parking enforcement is unpredictable. If concerned, check with others.

events.description: Join Durham Dems Precinct 53-2 for an information-packed Get-Ready-to-Vote Ice Cream Social on Sunday, October 11, from 3:00-4:30pm at a neighborhood clubhouse in our precinct (location provided upon sign-up). This will be just 4 days before the start of early voting, and we’ll gather with our neighbors to eat ice cream and discuss everything we need to know to vote in the November 3 election. events.title: MCDP HQ Office Staff Volunteers
events.description:
We're Opening Our Doors — And We Need You Inside Them!

Madison County Democrats is establishing a community hub and party headquarters — a place where neighbors can come to get information, get involved, and get connected to the resources and candidates that matter to this county.

And we need volunteers to make it run.

We're looking for friendly, committed Madison County Democrats to staff the office in 2-hour shifts with a partner — someone to greet visitors, answer questions, and represent the best of what this party stands for. No experience necessary. Just a willingness to show up and talk to your neighbors.

This is democracy at its most local. A front door. A friendly face. A place where anyone in Madison County can walk in and feel welcome.
What volunteering looks like:

-2-hour shifts, scheduled in advance

-Two volunteers per shift 

-Simple tasks — greeting visitors, sharing information, directing people to resources

If you've been looking for a way to get more involved this election season, this is it. The simplest and most powerful thing we can do is open our doors and be present for our community!

# Join your neighbors each week and "make good trouble" at the Five Points intersection in Aston, PA

Stand with Aston Dems and No Kings Springfield. Stand up to protect voting rights, civil rights, and immigrant rights.

Defend our democracy, right here in Aston. Choose your corner (Pennell, Knowlton, Concord).

- Bring a friend
- Bring a sign
- Hydrate

### Don't have an hour? Drive by and offer horn support.

## When & where 

We meet weekly at the Five Points intersection in Aston, PA. We remain on public sidewalks and do not block traffic. Please bring signs or flags if you’d like.

## Our values 

This is a peaceful, nonviolent event. We ask all participants to engage respectfully, avoid confrontation, help de-escalate any tensions, and follow all local laws and safety guidance.

Everyone who supports constitutional democracy and peaceful civic engagement is welcome.

events.title: Arkansas Society of Freethinkers - Pint Nite / Humanist Happy Hour
events.description:
A casual, come-as-you-are gathering for freethinkers, skeptics, humanists, and anyone who enjoys good conversation over a drink or a meal. No agenda, no program — just an easy evening to meet people in your community who share a commitment to reason, compassion, and living ethically without reliance on the supernatural.
What to expect
Show up, grab a seat, and talk about whatever's on your mind — current events, books, life, the big questions and the small ones. Your host will be there to welcome you, introduce you around, and answer questions about the Arkansas Society of Freethinkers and the American Humanist Association if you have them.
First time? You're especially welcome.
A lot of people find Humanist Happy Hour an easier first step than a lecture or formal meeting. You don't need to identify as a humanist (or anything in particular) to come — just bring curiosity and an open mind.
About drinks
Alcohol is optional and never expected. The venue has non-alcoholic options and food, so come however you come.
Finding us
We meet on the third Monday of each month at 7 PM at the Flying Saucer in downtown Little Rock. Street parking is free but limited after 6 PM on President Clinton Ave. Additional street parking is free and usually available off President Clinton Ave, but may require walking a block or two. Paid lots and garages are also available in the area, including the library garage located in the same building as the Flying Saucer.
Hope to see you there.

events.title: Election Protection Poll Monitor Training 2026
events.description:
Thank you for your interest in Election Protection with the Ohio Voter Rights Coalition! Please register for one of the available trainings listed to become a nonpartisan Poll Monitor for the November General election. 

***Please note - you only need to attend one of the trainings listed here, not all of them!

Ohio's Election Protection program is part of the national 866ourvote.org program to promote the 866-OUR-VOTE hotline and ensure that all voters have an equal opportunity to vote and have that vote count. Trained poll monitors are a friendly face outside of polling locations to help voters if they have questions and report any issues.

Even if you have served as a poll monitor in past years, we do ask that you sign up and retake it again so you can be refreshed with the information and updated on new information relevant this year. If you are unable to attend, please register and keep an eye out for a follow up email that will come with a recording of the training and notes. 

Please reach out if you have any questions! Thank you again for helping out with Election Protection and poll monitoring with the Ohio Voter Rights Coalition.

events.title: Danville Weekly Canvassing & Phone Bank for MC - Mary Catherine Roberson for IL HD104
events.description:
# Your Vote Counts More Than Ever‼️
If you ever thought your vote didn't matter, know that just **TWO** short years ago, IL HD104 came down to **269** certified votes. A district that spans Champaign and Vermilion counties and includes all of Danville, parts of Urbana, Savoy, Rantoul, and all the gorgeous farmland in between. A district that houses almost 60k registered voters; **two hundred sixty-nine votes.**

‼️2-6-9 ‼️

That means every single one of us is a conversation away from changing who represents this community, and a real conversation on someone's porch is proven to move *far* more voters than any ad, mailer, or cold text ever will — because it comes from someone they trust, not a stranger.

## Be Like MC: One of Us, Doing the Work
These are our neighbors, the people we wave to, whose kids go to school with ours, who deserve better than what they're getting. This isn't a phone bank in some other state, it's your own block, where your knock matters more than almost anything else we could do.

The energy is there. The votes are there. The time is now. Your neighbors just need someone they trust to ask them to show up.

That's you.

Bring your shoes and your excitement. We'll bring the map.
