events.title: Thruway Banner Project
events.description:
Our Latham Bridge Brigade will be taking part in a special New York Thruway Project to remind NYS residents that their voices matter. Over 44 Thruway overpasses will be displaying 15-foot banners with messages encouraging voter participation. 

We will be displaying the banners from our usual spot on the Route 7 overpass at Old Loudon Road, rather than the Thruway, to take advantage of traffic heading for the Northway. 

Come be part of a state-wide visibility event, voicing concerns about democracy, the economy, and corruption in government ahead of the mid-terms. Folks will be holding banners on bridges across the NYS Thruway from Buffalo to Albany on four Saturdays ahead of the elections.

There are two banners to be used, so we need your help holding the banners in place. You can also bring your own signs or use one of ours. Bring noisemakers, bring a friend, bring family - all are welcome. 

Please sign up ASAP for one or more of the dates listed. This will be a fun and impactful protest, so we hope you can join us! As always, lots of free parking is available at St. Ambrose Church, just steps from the bridge.

Also, please note that the bridge brigade will start a bit earlier than usual on the NYS Thruway Project Saturdays.

events.title: Money Moves: A Financial Wellness Series
events.description:
Money Moves: A Financial Wellness Workshop Series

Take control of your financial future with practical tools, expert guidance, and real-life strategies. Join Hope Station and Goodwill Keystone Area for this free three-part financial wellness series designed to help you build confidence, make informed financial decisions, and create a stronger financial future.

Participants will receive Goodwill gift cards, and those who attend all three workshops will be entered into a drawing to win a Visa gift card. Food and beverages will be provided at each session.

Workshop Schedule

September 21 | 5:00–6:30 p.m.
Money Foundations: Budget, Save & Take Control
Learn how to create a realistic budget, track spending, build emergency savings, set financial goals, and make your money work for you.

October 27 | 5:00–6:30 p.m.
Credit, Debt & Protecting Your Money
Understand credit scores and reports, explore strategies for reducing debt, learn about credit cards and interest rates, and discover ways to protect your personal and financial information.

November 17 | 11:30 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
Digital Smarts: AI, Technology & Scam Prevention
Learn how AI is being used in everyday life, recognize AI-generated scams and fake content, avoid phishing attempts, protect your personal information, and safely navigate online banking, shopping, and payment apps.

Free One-on-One Financial Coaching

Participants will also have access to free personalized financial coaching through Goodwill Keystone Area. Whether you want to create a budget, improve your credit, manage debt, build savings, or increase your financial confidence, coaching is available to help you reach your goals.

Registration

Space is limited. Register today to reserve your spot.

Hosted by Hope Station and Goodwill Keystone Area

See you Mondays.

In this together,
Buddy Luce
On behalf of Indivisible TX-24

events.title: Staff the Community Outreach Booth (2026)

location.venue: Findlay - Hancock County Public Library Grounds (weather permitting)
address_lines: We pop up a table and canopy on the sidewalk outside the entrance to the library (weather permitting)

events.description:
Looking for an easy, social way to get involved locally?

We’re building a team of volunteers to regularly staff our pop-up Democratic booth outside the Library, typically on Saturday mornings and Sunday evenings.

People stop by to pick up candidate yard signs and literature, learn more about who’s running, ask questions, and find ways to get involved—and we need friendly volunteers there to welcome them.

You might help:

-Greet people who stop by
-Hand out yard signs and candidate literature
-Help visitors find information about our Democratic candidates
-Have friendly conversations about the people running to represent us
-Connect interested people with events and volunteer opportunities
-Keep signs and materials organized and stocked
-Help set up or pack up the booth
-Simply make our local Democratic Party feel visible, approachable, and welcoming

You do not need to be a political expert.

We’ll provide candidate information, literature, basic talking points, and experienced volunteers to help you get comfortable. You’re never expected to know every answer—or debate someone who wants an argument.

Sometimes the best response is simply:

“I’m not sure, but I can help you find out.”

And you don’t have to volunteer every weekend. Help once in a while, choose the dates that work for you, or become one of our regular volunteers who helps us keep the booth staffed consistently.

Whether you like talking with people, organizing materials, handing out signs, or just want a simple way to contribute a couple of hours, we can use your help.

Pick some shifts which work well for your schedule using the form below.

events.title: Post Election Review
events.description:
Minnesota takes election security seriously. Before the Election, we have the Public Accuracy Test. During the election, election judges ensure that the processes in the polling places follow the law. After the election, we have the Post Election Review. 

**[Minnesota Statutes 206.89](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/206.89)** states that after every state general election, Minnesota counties perform a post-election review of election results returned by the optical scan ballot counters used in the state.  The review is a hand count of the ballots for each eligible election (U.S. President, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, and Governor) in the selected precincts compared with the results from the voting system used in those precincts.

The post-election review is carried out by the County Canvassing Board, made up of the County Auditor (in St. Louis County, Nancy Nilsen), the Court Administrator of the District Court (Kim Vizena), the mayor/chair of the town board of the largest municipality in the County(Roger Reinert), and two County Commissioners (Patrick Boyle and Ken Musolf). 

Come witness this historic process. Our elections are precious. Maybe in prior years we could let this operate in the background. 2026 is different. 

Note: the starting time, 9 am is set, the ending time depends on how long it takes to review the selected precincts.

events.title: Jump Jam 2026 - Volunteers
events.description:
Jump Jam is back on Saturday, on November 7th (rain date from October 10th), and we'd love to have you on the team!

Hosted at the Subaru of Spartanburg Bike Park, Jump Jam is PAL's annual bike park fundraiser featuring kids' bike races, amateur and professional dirt jump competitions, food trucks, vendors, and family activities. Every dollar raised helps support the maintenance and improvement of the bike park while introducing more children and families to cycling and outdoor recreation.

It takes an incredible team of volunteers to make the day possible! Whether you're helping set up before the event, checking in kids for the races, assisting along the course, or helping us pack everything up at the end of the day, your time makes a real difference.

Three volunteer shifts are available throughout the day, and every volunteer will receive a PAL T-shirt. No previous experience is necessary - just bring comfortable clothes, closed-toe shoes, and a willingness to jump in and help!

Shift Descriptions:

10:00 AM - 1:00 PM | Set Up

Help transform the bike park for Jump Jam! Volunteers will assist with setting up tents, tables, banners, signs, inflatables, race course signage, vendor areas, and other event equipment before participants arrive.

1:00 PM - 4:00 PM | Kids Ride & Check-In

Help make the Kids Ride a success by checking in participants, distributing race T-shirts, lining kids up by age group, holding age group signs, directing riders along the course, and handing out finisher medals.

4:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Crowd Voting & Breakdown

Walk through the crowd with QR codes so attendees can vote for the Best Style competition, then stay after the awards ceremony to help the PAL team break down the event, pack equipment, and clean up the park.

Thank you for helping PAL create another unforgettable Jump Jam. We couldn't do it without you!

events.title: General Election Poll Challenger Training (Virtual)
events.description:
### Poll Challengers are critical to ensure that every Minnesotan can cast their ballot and make it count.

On Election Day, DFL-designated Poll Challengers are placed inside specific polling locations to protect voters' rights. This is done by observing the process for the DFL and working with the Voter Protection team to ensure elections are running smoothly. 

##### We will provide training and all the information you need! No previous experience is necessary, but Poll Challengers must:
- Be a resident of Minnesota
- Be eligible to vote in Minnesota 
- Be over 18 years old
- Be available on Election Day, November 3, 2026 

Share this opportunity with others you know who would be interested. 

We are very excited to work with you!

events.description:

The campaign will assign poll observers to serve at a polling location based on the poll observer’s availability and willingness to travel. In New Hampshire, poll observers are not required to be New Hampshire voters or residents.

This training is for volunteering for the General Election on Tuesday, November 3rd!

events.title: Learn about joining our Benefit Host Committee!
events.description:
If you know how to throw great parties that people can’t wait to attend, know a fantastic fundraising auction when you see one, or want to be part of an event that truly makes a positive impact in our world, we have an opportunity to share with you.

Each year, Food & Water Watch hosts an annual benefit event, Against All Odds, with an in-person New York City reception and an online virtual program — and we want your help! Against All Odds is all about coming together, cheering on our victories, and raising critical funds needed to protect our food, water, and climate. 

**Our Benefit Host Committee, a select group of dedicated Food & Water Watch supporters, not only helps make it all possible, they also make the event fun, exciting, and movement-building.**

Host Committee Members work directly with Food & Water Watch staff to shape aspects of the event that foster a sense of community, boost our fundraising efforts, and increase the reach of our donor-activists, ultimately resulting in a highly engaging and successful benefit. 

**Does this sound like something YOU want to be part of? Sign up to chat with our team and learn more about being part of the committee that makes it all happen.**

*Once you sign up on this form, you will be directed to schedule a time to speak with our staff via Zoom.*

events.title: Durham Canvass to Defeat Harmful Constitutional Amendments
events.description:
A handful of state lawmakers want to scam our community with two constitutional amendments on the ballot this fall. These amendments will let big corporations and rich people skip paying what they owe while working people pick up the tab. Neither amendment will save everyday people any money. If these amendments pass, it could mean billions of dollars in cuts to our schools, health care, and other public services. 

Durham For All and Durham Public School Strong are partnering to mobilize thousands of people to vote against these harmful amendments and demand that corporations and billionaires pay what they owe in taxes so our kids, educators, and communities have what they need to succeed.

Join us as we knock on our neighbors' doors or talk with people at community events to get the word out about these harmful amendments and make sure they are defeated at the polls! 

If you’ve never canvassed before, or if you just heard about these amendments yourself, that's okay! We will equip you with talking points and help you shape and share your story of why this matters to you. All canvassing will happen in pairs, so bring a buddy and/or come prepared to make a new friend.

There will be Spanish interpretation and childcare at the launch site for all weekend canvassing shifts.

events.title: "Flip Flops on the Ground" Literature  Drop
events.description:
Democracy is NOT a spectator sport—and Arizona can finally change!

Did you know the last time Democrats held the majority in the Arizona House was 1966? For nearly 60 years, single-party control has shaped our state, leading to issues that impact our families every single day:

Packed Classrooms: Composite state rankings consistently place Arizona public education near the bottom (48th to 51st). While state averages mask the crisis, actual core classrooms (Math, English, Science) regularly pack 30–35+ students into a single room with low teacher retention and bottom-tier funding.

Corporate Loophole: Arizona is now one of the least affordable states to live in, yet under state law (A.R.S. § 43-1111), over 80% of corporate filers pay only the $50 minimum state tax floor (JLBC data), leaving working families to carry the load.

We have the power to change this.

Tempe Rising Indivisible is organizing "Flip Flops on the Ground" Lit Drop shifts to get crucial campaign information into the hands of voters across key neighborhoods.

🎯 Our Target Districts
Protect & Hold (Keep Blue): Legislative Districts 9 & 12

Flip the House & Commission (Turn Blue): Legislative District 13 & Congressional District 5

👟 How You Can Help
Walkers: Come get your steps in! Whether you have 1 hour, 2 hours, or 3 hours, every neighborhood covered matters.

Drivers Needed: Prefer driving over walking? We urgently need drivers to transport lit drop teams and cover larger routes!

We provide all materials, turf maps, and a brief launch overview before you head out. Bring water, comfortable shoes, and a friend!

Together, we can flip Arizona. Sign up today or check out our latest videos to learn more:

Please note the address given is the meeting place.  Please be on time and or check the event chat.

👉 Arizona Can Finally Change  https://www.facebook.com/reel/2558078861283494

👉 Swing Districts We Can Flip
https://www.facebook.com/reel/2216252009226655

events.title: Creating Graduates Instead of Dropouts
events.description:
High school students who have learning disabilities, mild intellectual disabilities, emotional disturbance, severe dyslexia, or language acquisition problems are unable to read most regular textbooks. Students with serious reading problems are often excluded from the opportunities to learn algebra, geometry, biology, physics and chemistry, and other subjects because they cannot read the textbooks, supplemental materials, or the tests. It is not easy for teachers to find resources and texts that address grade-level standards, but are written at low reading levels.

That’s where Firelight Books comes in! The Elements Curriculum was designed by a teacher for students reading at second to fourth grade levels. The subject matter is the same as what their gen ed peers are learning, but it’s written in a way that students with reading challenges can understand. It reduces frustration, boosts confidence, and promotes positive behavior in and out of the classroom.

Please join us in learning how you can create graduates instead of dropouts by implementing the Elements.

events.title: Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success
events.description:
**Proactive Behavior Screening for Stronger Student Success**

Join Firelight Books for an informative presentation introducing the Nichols Behavior Checklist (NBC), an innovative universal behavior screening and intervention tool designed to help schools identify behavioral and emotional concerns early—before they become barriers to student success.

The NBC is an Internet-based, individualized screening instrument for students in 1–12 that is quick, user-friendly, cost effective, and highly informative. In approximately 10 minutes per student, the NBC provides individualized behavioral screening reports with practical recommendations to support intervention planning and behavior management.

This presentation will demonstrate how the NBC helps educators, intervention teams, counselors, administrators, and clinicians:

* Identify areas of behavioral and emotional concern
* Improve student behavior through early intervention
* Support positive school functioning and interpersonal relationships
* Strengthen data-driven decision making
* Monitor trends at the district, campus, classroom, or individual student level
* Provide meaningful documentation for intervention planning

Attendees will learn how the NBC can be used as both a proactive screening instrument and an effective intervention support tool to help improve student outcomes, classroom climate, and overall school success.

The Nichols Behavior Checklist provides schools with practical behavioral insight—turning data into positive action for students.
www.firelightbooks.com

events.title: Four Weeks of Power: Organizing Skills Training Series
events.description:
Join us for this introductory organizing training program that covers the basics of grassroots organizing skills, with a focus on base building, leadership development, and building strong committees.  

You will learn best practices in holding one-to-ones, conducting outreach, building strong local committees, and developing leadership, so they can build a broader, stronger base of parents taking action to defend and transform public schools. 

**Please make sure you sign up for all four sessions! Each session builds on the content from the previous sessions.**

## Week 1:  Community organizing to meet the political moment

Our first session grounds us in the political moment we’re in, unmasking the billionaires and autocrats driving the austerity agenda, and why we need to lean into organizing in this divisive political moment. We know the power of organizing in the face of authoritarianism; and so this session will provide an introduction to community organizing in the context of the rising authoritarianism we’re seeing in real time.

## Week 2:  The basics of base-building

Our second week will focus on the key skills needed to successfully grow a base of committed parents, educators and students that can take action to defend public education. We’ll cover the rigor, time and discipline needed to do effective outreach in order to build a crew to meet this moment, understanding what motivates your base to take risks and move into action. 

## Week 3:  One-to-ones – building deep relationships as an organizer

This session will anchor us in the deep relational work that organizers lead to bring community members together for a common cause. We'll deep dive into one-to-one conversations and best practices to engage people regularly and connect with them.

## Week 4:  Building a powerful team to take action

This session will do a deep dive on how to build and sustain a local team of leaders that vibe together and relate well, in order to build towards mutual accountability and support. Building strong teams helps us build the local power we need to advocate for the public schools our communities deserve, and build collective muscle in the face of growing authoritarianism. 

**This training is FREE of charge and is open to organizers and community members who want to deepen their organizing skills and build local teams to fight to protect and transform public education.**

*4 Weeks of Power is coordinated and led by Midwest Academy, Public School Strong, NYU Metro Center and organizers and leaders from Alliance to Reclaim Our Schools (AROS) member groups.*

events.title: Ballot Measures 101: Denver & Colorado
events.description:
Ballot Measures 101: Denver & Colorado

Join Indivisible Denver Action and the League of Women Voters for a nonpartisan deep dive into this year's Denver and Colorado ballot measures.

With so many measures on the ballot this fall, it can be hard to keep track of what's actually being decided and what a "yes" or "no" vote means. That's where the League of Women Voters comes in. As a nonpartisan organization, LWV doesn't support political parties or candidates — instead, they focus on giving voters clear, fact-based information so you can make your own informed decision.

What we'll cover:

* An overview of the most impactful Denver and Colorado ballot measures
* Fact-based background on each measure
* Arguments for and against (pros and cons)
* What a "yes" vote means, and what a "no" vote means

Time at the end for questions, including on any positions LWV has taken on specific measures (kept separate from the basic information so the two don't get mixed up)

Bring your printed ballot measure blue book guides guides to take notes!

Whether you're a first-time voter or you just want a refresher before Election Day, this is a great chance to get clear on what's on your ballot this year.

Details:
📅 Saturday, October 10, 2026
🕕 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM
📍 Eisenhower Chapel, 293 Roslyn St, Denver, CO 80230

Presented by League of Women Voters & Indivisible Denver Action.

sponsor.name: Good Neighbors Getting it Done in Western New York

events.description:
**Summary**

The Family and Politics workshop teaches participants how to preserve family bonds while staying true to their values and political beliefs. Although the focus is on family relationships, you can use these strategies with any loved one. You’ll have some fun in this workshop – it won’t be all serious. After all, we all come from quirky families.

**Goals**

- Insight into why family differences over politics are uniquely challenging
- Recognition of common roles that family members play in political conversations
- Strategies and skills for handling family political differences in a constructive way

**Who Can Attend**

The Family and Politics workshop is open to everyone who struggles over political differences with a loved one.

**What to Expect**

You will learn about the family dynamics of political differences, apply them to your family, and learn and practice effective communication skills with difficult family members.

- Strategies and skills for handling family political differences in a constructive way

You will learn about the family dynamics of political differences, apply them to your family, and learn and practice effective communication skills with difficult family members.

Join Target Majority (a local Indivisible & Swing Left Group) for a Ground Truth canvass in must-FLIP PA-08.   

We are knocking every door and identifying persuadable voters who Dems normally don't contact, in order to elect Paige Cognetti in a true toss-up race in a Trump '24 district where she's recently demonstrated a 1-point lead.

To help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House, Swing Left has launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the voters campaigns usually talk to

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, identifying net new voters for the Democratic Party and candidates  

- Add these new voters' partisanship scores, likelihood to vote, and contact info directly into the Democrats' voter database so they will follow up with persuadable folks

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to people’s needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re started early and will continue every year:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground. Likewise, we'll continue this important work through 2027 ahead of 2028. (And beyond.)

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ internal conflicts around voting and around party affiliation, getting to the “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

**A core principle behind all Target Majority events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.**

_By RSVP’ing to this event, you are opting in to having your contact information, including your full name, email address, and phone number, added to the contact list(s) of Target Majority NYC, An Indivisible & Swing Left group (TMNYC). TMNYC may send periodic communications using the contact information that you have entered._

events.title: CEJC Community Meetings
events.description:
The Columbus Education Justice Coalition is a collective of parents, students, educators, labor union members, and community partners who believe that access to a fair, just, well-rounded public education for all students, families, and staff in Columbus City Schools is a civil and human right.

We work to end inequities, oppose privatization, and build strong, community-based public schools where all students can thrive.

For the 2026-27 School Year, we will host monthly community meetings that are open to the public. Join us on the 4th Wednesday of the month at 7PM via Zoom. 

Each meeting will include an informational topic or training and the opportunity to meet and plan with pro-public education families, educators, and neighbors on your side of town. Learn to build your own campaigns to fight for your rights and needs at your school, in your neighborhood, in our city, community and across the state. 

*To maintain a safe environment for open communication, protect privacy, and safeguard proprietary or sensitive information the Columbus Education Justice Coalition strictly prohibits the unauthorized recording of virtual meetings and online events.
events.accessibility_notes: Please note that virtual sessions are held in English. However, we will make every reasonable effort to secure translators for attendees. Please let us know of your needs.

events.title: LIBERATED BODIES: LUGENIA BURNS HOPE TOUR
events.description:
Before there were programs or policies, there were neighbors showing up for one another.That legacy lives on today.

Join Color Of Change at the Liberated Bodies: Lugenia Burns Hope Tour at Jackson University for a day centered on community, wellness, and collective care.

Inspired by the life and legacy of Lugenia Burns Hope, this tour celebrates the ways Black communities have always cared for one another while connecting us with the people, organizations, and resources that continue that work today.

Whether you're looking for trusted health resources, meaningful conversations, ways to get involved, or simply a space to connect with your community, you'll find it here.

You'll have the chance to meet local organizations providing health, wellness, and community resources, and learn more about reproductive justice, bodily autonomy, and caring for ourselves and one another. The event will also offer space to explore mental health, healing, and survivor support resources, while connecting with Jackson State University students, community leaders, and local organizers. 

Location: Jackson State University Date: Oct 17 Time: 10-3pm

Bring a friend. Bring your family. Leave with new connections, trusted resources, and more ways to stay engaged.

Because when our communities have what they need to thrive, we all move forward together.

We hope to see you there.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early: Final Preparation for Election Defense
events.description:
Join the No Kings coalition for this training to prepare for engaging in sustained mobilization and results protection work depending on opposition response to election results.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.*

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

*By registering for this event, you agree: (1) that Indivisible and ACLU can contact you about No Kings and other ways to take action or support their organizations and otherwise use any data collected from or about you on this form according to the applicable privacy policy: Indivisible Privacy Policy (https://indivisible.org/privacy-policy) and ACLU's Privacy Statement (https://www.aclu.org/about/privacy/statement); and (2) subject to its privacy policy, Indivisible may also share the information you provide to other No Kings partner organizations, which may also contact you.*

events.title: Block by Block - RETURNER Phone Banks! (Let’s block MAGA and send progressive champions to Congress!
events.description:
## Candidate Schedule:

-   **Cooper for NC Senate** - 10/8, 10/24, 11/1
-   **Ossoff for GA Senate** - 10/13, 10/27, 11/1
-   **Lawrence for MI Congressional District 7** - 10/18
-   **Pearson for TN Congressional District 9** - 10/29, 10/31
-   **Colom for MS Senate** - 10/22

----------

## Come take action with SURJ!

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

*These are shorter 2hr bite-sized phone banks specifically geared toward returner callers to SURJ Phone Banks. Please attend a standard 2.15-Hour SURJ phone bank BEFORE attending one of these. Sign up for one [here](https://www.mobilize.us/surj/event/1007636/). These phone banks WILL NOT include a new banker training, just a brief moment for connection, call time and a debrief. Standard coaching support offered at all SURJ phone banks will still be available.*

**These races include:**

### SENATE:

-   **Michigan Senate** (Movement Champion Race) - **Abdul El-Sayed**, who is born and raised in Michigan, studied to be a doctor but then realized he wanted to dedicate his career to building government systems that actually work for Michiganders. He has secured free glasses for kids who need the,, removed lead from Detroit’s elementary schools, taken on Michigan's biggest polluters and made Narcan universally accessible. He has also spearheaded a program to eventually cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders over 2 years. He is a true fighter and is ready to take that to DC on behalf of the whole state!
    
-   **Maine Senate** *(Movement Champion Race)* - **Troy Jackson**, who is a logger from Allagash, a lifelong fighter for workers' rights, and former Maine Senate President who is running to put power back in the hands of working people and unseat Susan Collins.
    
-   **North Carolina Senate** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Roy Cooper**, the former Democratic Governor of North Carolina. He was born and raised in Nash County, North Carolina attending public schools. He has a deep commitment to public education and while governor worked to expand Medicaid, relieve over $4 billion in medical debt for North Carolina families.
    
-   **Georgia Senate**  *(Block the Right Race)* - **Jon Ossoff**, who is an incumbent democratic Senator for the state of Georgia. He was born and raised in Atlanta. He is focused on exposing and stopping governmental corruption all while being one of the few US Senators whose campaign refuses corporate PAC money.    

- **Mississippi Senate** *(Block the Right Race)* - **Scott Colom**, who is a District Attorney for the 16th judicial district of Mississippi. As DA, he has pursued policies like avoiding incarceration for non-violent offenses, was the first District Attorney in Mississippi to offer restorative justice for victims, and is currently on the Advisory Board of the VERA Institute for Justice, a partner that SURJ has worked with over the years. 

### HOUSE:

-   **Michigan Congressional District 7** *(Movement Champion Race)* - **Will Lawrence**, who is an organizer and coalition-builder with experience speaking truth to power and getting results at the local, state and federal level. Born and raised in Mid-Michigan, Will has fought tirelessly to protect people’s rights to housing (co-founder of the Rents Is Too Damn High Coalition), bring good, green jobs to the district (as a co-founder of Sunrise Movement) and to ward off data center greed.
    
-   **Tennessee Congressional District 9** *(Movement Champion Race)* - **Justin Pearson**, who is an organizer, born and raised in Southwest Memphis, Tennessee. He grew up in a working class family and has been advocating for his community since the age of 15, fighting for better education for his classmates. He has since formed Memphis Community Against the Pipeline (MCAP) to fight billion dollar oil companies that would have polluted over a million people’s drinking water, fought alongside workers for better wages and taken on the xAI data center for their illegal pollution.
    
-   **California Congressional District 22** *(Movement Champion Race)* - **Randy Villegas**, who is a 30-year old son of immigrants and activist for immigrant rights in his area. He is an elected school board trustee in Visalia, CA and political science professor who is running to represent California’s 22nd congressional district, representing Bakersfield and portions of the central valley.

----------

## Context:

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and **this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections** – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to ***put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people.*** **BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.**

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, **protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi** and **flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.**

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by **supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA** and **showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south** who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

----------

## About SURJ:

[Showing Up for Racial Justice](https://surj.org/) (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Hop on a bus: Mountain View to Delano! Flip the House (Randy Villegas, CA-22)
events.description:
Join lots of fired-up volunteers on a **bus to Delano in the Central Valley** to help flip the U.S. House.

We’ll be **knocking on doors for Randy Villegas in Congressional District 22 (CA-22), one of the few true toss-up House races in the country**. This race could be won or lost by a few hundred votes, so every knock counts! Randy is an energizing candidate who’s running to fight for working families and protect our democracy. And he refuses to accept corporate-PAC money. He wants to answer to his constituents…not special interests. Be part of the team that sends Randy to DC in January!

**Timing:**

- **6:30am: Depart Mountain View** (then we’ll stop in the South Bay to pick up more folks)  

- Roughly 11am-5pm: Knock on doors, with a break for lunch

- 9pm (at latest): return to Mountain View

*(If you would prefer to board the bus in San Jose, use this sign-up link instead: https://www.mobilize.us/swingleft/event/1014892/)*

**More details:**

- Yes, there's a bathroom on the bus!

- There is lots of all-day parking available at the Mountain View departure location

- We’ll provide breakfast, lunch, and dinner (and early morning coffee too)

- We’ll train you on the bus (and there’s training available in advance too)

- Local volunteers in the district will drive us to our canvassing locations

Closer to the departure date, your bus captain will provide many more details.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

Sign up now and help us fill the bus! And invite friends to register as well!

This is a **Ground Truth** canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. It's an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors. This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts. How do we "Go Deep"?  By practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth;”  we're not just checking boxes on a script.

This bus is organized by a group of Peninsula and South Bay organizations, including Swing Left Peninsula and South Bay Swing Left.

Please send any questions to [mobilize@swingleftpeninsula.org](mailto:mobilize@swingleftpeninsula.org)

*By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. Our emails share timely, impactful actions (letter parties, phone banks, canvasses, voter registrations, and more) for strategic, close-margin races that will help us win back the House, Senate, and other important races.*

*Every email we send includes an unsubscribe link. If you don't want to be on our list, we want you to unsubscribe! (Please don't mark this email as spam, or we will have trouble reaching the people who DO want to hear from us.) You won't be resubscribed by us.*

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Our elections are under attack — not from fraud, but from people falsely claiming there is fraud. When the President spreads lies about rigged elections, the real danger is that those lies get used to justify intimidation, disruption, or interference at the polls. We're not going to let that happen in Colorado.

Indivisible Denver Action and Indivisible Colorado Action Network have joined Common Cause Colorado on an election protection effort, and we need volunteers on the ground from November 1–3 to help keep our elections free, fair, and safe.

Common Cause runs a statewide hotline (866-OUR-VOTE) that takes reports of problems at polling places. When something happens near you, Common Cause alerts our team's three Response Mobilizers, who then send out a call to our Rapid Responders to head to the location.

If they're working this hard to make you doubt your vote, it's because your vote is powerful. So, let's use it.

Join Resistance Rising the ACLU of Massachusetts for straight answers on what's really happening this election, and what we can do about it together:

• What we know so far about federal monitors and ICE at the polls

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 15 participants.**

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: NoHo Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:

As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 

* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-waiver at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

events.title: New Member Orientation! (Fall Series)
events.description:
As a member-led youth movement, MOVE Texas Members are at the heart of our mission to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. **Born out of the student organizing movement in San Antonio in 2013,** MOVE Texas was founded by young people who saw a gap in civic engagement and decided to take action. What started as a small group of student leaders registering their peers to vote has since grown into a statewide movement of young people that trains, mobilizes, and empowers a new generation of progressive community organizers.

## Who are MOVE Texas Members?

MOVE Texas members are the backbone of the organization, reflecting the energy and diversity of young Texans leading the charge for a more just and equitable future for all Texans across race, class, and place.  As a youth movement, MOVE Texas members are under 35, and are either:


- **Students:** The original foundation of MOVE Texas, young leaders organizing on campuses across the state, running voter registration drives, educating their peers, and leading local issue-based campaigns.

- **Community Members:** Young Texans who are inspired by MOVE Texas’ mission and actively work to build power in their neighborhoods, from hosting events to advocating for direct local and statewide policy change.

## MOVE Texas members receive:

- Access to MOVE trainings, programs, and resources,

- Voting power for statewide and local campaigns,

- Exclusive invitations to MOVE statewide events,

- Connection to a network of peers organizing across the state,

- Exclusive members merch.


MOVE Texas membership is open to anyone who believes in the power of young people to lead and shape the future AND our present.

events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an innovative new program(https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

# The LGBTQ+ Summit During the New Jersey League of Municipalities is BACK this November!

Join us and the Garden State's new LGBTQ+ business association, the Unity Chamber of Commerce, at the Hard Rock Hotel & Casino in Atlantic City on Tuesday, Nov. 17, for the return of this special event.⁠
⁠
### Special Guests
#### Honorable Julien X. Neals
*United States District Judge, District of New Jersey*

Since 2021, Judge Neals has served as a US District Judge of the US District Court for the District of New Jersey. Before that, he served as County Counsel and Acting County Administrator for Hackensack, and the Business Administrator for the City of Newark. He is a staunch ally for LGBTQ+ equality.

#### Assemblywoman Luanne Peterpaul
*NJ Legislative District 11*

In 2023, Luanne Peterpaul became the first openly lesbian woman elected to serve in the New Jersey Legislature. While representing NJ's 11th Legislative District, she was the primary Assembly sponsor for a bill to expand access to HIV medication and a primary sponsor of the recently signed into law bill to shield reproductive and transgender healthcare.

#### Bernie Wagenblast
*Transportation Journalist and Voice Actor • Summit Emcee*

Bernie Wagenblast is a transportation journalist and voice actor. She's best known for being a voice millions hear daily on transit systems, including the NYC subway, the AirTrain at Newark Liberty International Airport and PATCO in South Jersey and Philadelphia. Since her transition in early 2023, she's become a highly visible advocate for trans folks. 

Attendees will receive a free lunch.

- Debrief: Return to the launch site to turn in materials and celebrate our outreach!

- A water bottle

- Weather-appropriate clothing

events.title: Caminata: Sonoma County 3-Day Walk For Immigrant Rights, Petaluma to Cloverdale

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
We are happy to invite you and your organization to participate in the Sonoma County Three-Day Walk For Immigrant Rights, on October 10-12, from Petaluma to Cloverdale!

As you know, Sonoma County still has much to do to respond to the attacks against immigrants, including stopping the Sheriff from continuing to turn people over to ICE, offering emergency aid to those who aren’t able to access State or Federal safety nets, and ensuring that immigrant surveillance through General Dynamics Corp. and Flock cameras stops.

Cities in Sonoma County must also do more to defend immigrants' rights.
For these reasons, we are putting together a strong coalition of individuals and organizations who agree that we must show the urgency of this moment by organizing a more dramatic action.

The demands of the Walk (“Caminata”) will be:

1. The Sheriff must stop collaborating with ICE immediately;
2. The County must support a community effort to create a cash fund for undocumented immigrants who cannot meet basic needs;
3. General Dynamics Corp. must leave Sonoma County;
4. The County must not utilize Flock cameras.

The Walk will start at Petaluma City Hall and end in Cloverdale.  We will walk approximately eight hours each day.  Walkers will return home to sleep and reconvene the next morning at a predetermined location.  Breakfast and lunch will be provided to the walkers.  The Walk will include Safety, Medics, and Route Leaders Teams. The Walk will end on October 12 with a cultural commemoration of Indigenous Peoples Day.

There are many ways to support this effort and get involved:

- Walking, 1-3 days.
- We will need donations to cover food and refreshments.

events.title: ChalkWalk | Beery Field, Downtown Douglas | Hosted by: Good Trouble Indivisible
events.description:
Good Trouble Indivisible’s ChalkWalk | Beery Field , Downtown Douglas 

Good Trouble Indivisible’s ChalkWalk is a creative public-awareness action using sidewalk chalk to encourage people to pause, read, think, and talk about what is happening in our country.

GTI ChalkWalks transform ordinary sidewalks into a continuing public message. As people walk across the bridge, they stop to read, take photographs and videos, ask questions, share their thoughts, and have meaningful conversations with us as we create our ChalkWalk.

These peaceful public-awareness actions help bring important issues out into the open—where they can be seen, considered, and discussed.

There are many ways to participate, and you do not need to be an artist or get down on the sidewalk to help.

👉 Help chalk or outline the prepared words.

👉 Hold a sign of your choosing about democracy, freedom, justice, or another current issue.

👉 Hand out Good Trouble Indivisible cards and information.

👉 Talk with passersby about current events and our work.

👉 Take photographs or video that we can share on social media and our website.

👉 Simply stand with us and help create a visible community presence.

Participants who would like to speak with the public will be given information and talking points.

Come help for the entire event or stop by for however long you can.

ChalkWalk is peaceful, lawful, protected FREE SPEECH…welcoming, and open to everyone who believes that public awareness matters—and that silence and inaction are not our only choices.

Bring a democracy sign to hold if you like. Chalk and handout materials will be provided by Good Trouble Indivisible.

We hope you will join us—and help turn our sidewalks into important conversations.

Good Trouble Indivisible is a Michigan nonprofit corporation and a chapter of the National Indivisible.

http://GoodTroubleIndivisible.org

Action@GoodTroubleIndivisible.org

(616) 287-2221

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same!

events.description:
Welcome to ARC’s (Antiracist Conversations) 12-week Virtual Read-Around Book Club.

 We will read Isabel Wilkerson’s book, The Warmth of Other Suns, which tells the epic story of America's Great Migration.

Our book club uses a unique format called a “Virtual Read-Around.”
No reading ahead is required: we will meet every Tuesday from September 8 through December 15, 2026, to read and experience Isabel Wilkerson’s The Warmth of Other Suns live as a group.

The book club will be facilitated by Jan, Pat, and Ms. Evelyn.

Together on live video, we will open each session with greetings and an icebreaker, and then we will read the book out loud.

There will be no verbal discussion during our weekly live meetings.

Important Note: Space is limited to 20 participants.  Registering for all book club meetings at once is the best plan. 

If you register and determine that you are unable to attend, please cancel your Mobilize registration so we can open your spot to someone else.

Weekly Meeting Schedule
We will meet every Tuesday for 90 minutes from September 8 through December 15, 2026. Find your local time zone below:

Pacific Time (PT): 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM
Mountain Time (MT): 9:00 AM – 10:30 AM
Central Time (CT): 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM
Eastern Time (ET): 11:00 AM – 12:30 PM


Meeting Timeline Breakdown
Every session follows this exact 90-minute structure (listed in Central Time):

10:00 AM – 10:10 AM: Open Zoom room, greetings, icebreaker, and tech check.

10:10 AM – 11:25 AM: Read out loud together as a group for 75 minutes.

11:25 AM – 11:30 AM: Wrap up and log off.

Reading and Journal Steps
We will cover about 30 to 35 pages together each week. 
 Confirm your attendance for the series by September 2, 2026. 

We’ll email additional information after you’ve confirmed your participation. 

Catching Up: If we do not finish the designated pages during our live read-around, please finish those specific pages on your own before the next Tuesday session.


Write Notes: After completing the weekly block, spend 10 to 15 minutes writing in a private journal while your thoughts are completely fresh.


Final Gathering: We will meet on Tuesday, December 15, at our usual session time for a final virtual gathering to share ideas from our journals and have a full verbal discussion.

See you on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.

With much appreciation,
The ARC Team

events.title: Dem Days Of Action
events.description:
# Nobody Is Coming to Putnam County to Do This for Us.

Five days. Two to three hours each. Doors and phones at Gobin Church — and no experience necessary.

*Sign up at the bottom of this page. ↓*

---

## There is no cavalry.

There's no army of paid staff driving in from Indianapolis. No national organization has Putnam County on their list. Nobody is coming.

The people who elect our candidates this year are the people who already live here. That's the whole plan. That's it.

So we're asking you for five days.

---


## Here's exactly what happens when you show up.

**1. Come to Gobin Church.**
Pick one day or come to all five. Wear comfortable shoes either way.

**2. Get assigned and trained.**
Tell us on the form whether you'd rather knock doors or make calls — we'll do everything we can to put you where you want to be. Then you're trained on site. You will not be handed a clipboard and pointed at a neighborhood.

**3. Work two to three hours.**
Then go home knowing you did the thing that actually decides elections.

---


**You get to tell us which one you want.**  If you have no preference, say that too — we'll put you wherever the need is biggest that day.

### 🚪 Door Knocking

**What to bring:** Comfortable walking shoes and your cell phone. That's it.

**You will never knock alone.** Every single door knocker is paired with a partner — no exceptions. If you come by yourself, we'll pair you with someone. If you come with a friend or your spouse, you can walk together.

**What to expect:** You'll be trained on site and given your route and instructions before you head out.

**Experience required:** None.

### 📞 Phone Banking

**What to bring:** At minimum, a phone and headphones. Ideally a phone, headphones, and a laptop or tablet so you can read the script from a screen.

**What to expect:** Full training before you make a single call. The script is written for you.

**Experience required:** None.

---


## Five Days of Action

All at Gobin Church. Two to three hours each.

| Date | Time | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Saturday, September 5** | 10:00 am | Kickoff |
| **Tuesday, September 22** | 6:00 pm | Evening shift |
| **Tuesday, October 6** | 5:30 pm | Early voting begins |
| **Saturday, October 24** | 10:00 am | Final Saturday |
| **Monday, November 2** | 5:00 pm | Election Eve |

*Keep scrolling to claim your days. ↓*

---

## This is the main work.

Not yard signs. Not social media posts. Not opinions at the coffee shop.

Knocking doors and making phone calls is how our candidates get elected. Real conversations, neighbor to neighbor, are what move people to the polls — and there is no substitute for them. Every serious campaign in America knows this. Most people never find out, because most people never show up.

Two to three hours, five times, is roughly ten to fifteen hours between now and Election Day. That is the difference between winning and wondering.

We need as many volunteers as we can possibly get across all five days for this to work.

---

## IN CASE YOU'RE HESITATING

**"I've never done this before."**
Good. Most people on these teams haven't. We train everyone, every day, before anyone talks to a single voter.

**"I'm not comfortable knocking on doors."**
Then take a phone. The form asks which team you'd prefer, and both teams matter equally.

**"I don't want to knock doors by myself."**
You won't. Every door knocker is paired with a partner, every time. Nobody walks a route alone.

**"I can only make one day."**
Take one day. One volunteer for one shift is worth more than a hundred people who meant to.

**"I already vote."**
Voting is the minimum. This is the part where you actually build something.

---

events.title: Canvass Curious: A Relaxed Guide to Talking with Voters
events.description:
### 20 minutes. 3 magic phrases. Real connections.

Knocking on strangers’ doors to talk politics might sound about as enjoyable as doing your taxes—but canvassing is the most powerful tool we have for winning elections. It can also be surprisingly satisfying and even fun!

Elizabeth Chur (author of _[The Joy of Talking Politics with Strangers](https://elizabethchur.com/)_) and Carol Blaney share real-life stories, demonstrate voter conversations, and show how empathy and a few simple phrases can create genuine connections.
 
Join us for a 20-minute glimpse of what can happen when we step outside our comfort zones, knock on a door, and listen—and how thousands of these conversations across the country can help win close races, reshape Congress, and save our democracy.

Zoom Link provided when you sign up for the event.

In Pennsylvania, Montana, and New York, Green Amendments have helped to win in court against fracking, uplift youth climate action, and stop environmental degradation before it starts.
 
Maya K. van Rossum is an award-winning speaker, advocate, and founder of both *Delaware Riverkeeper* and *Green Amendments for the Generations*. She will speak to the power of Green Amendments to give our environmental rights the strongest legal protection, the current effort to secure a Green Amendment in New Jersey’s state constitution, and lead a community discussion on how you can get involved.

https://forthegenerations.org/our-founder/

https://somaaction.org/climate

​S​wing Left Reno will be writing cards to infrequent voters who are Democrats or Democratic-leaning, which will be mailed in mid-October for maximum impact. Here in Nevada, we have a good chance of getting rid of our MAGA governor *if* we turn out our voters, so we want to contact as many of them as possible. Nationally, a strong blue wave will make a strong statement against Trump and MAGA and will enable Democrats to serve as a check against unbridled executive power.

RSVP here, and we’ll let you know how to join this party (including the location.) As always, I'll bring postcards, scripts, stamps, & writing supplies: you bring your enthusiasm for the Democratic ticket.

Think about it: if you help get a voter to the polls, that is an important step towards creating a more inclusive and equitable government and society. Looking forward to seeing you!

events.title: Eastside Progressives Book Club: This is the Plan by Ben Wikler
events.description:
If you are looking at the spiraling crisis of American politics in the Trump era and wondering how the hell we get out of this mess, This Is the Plan is the book you’ve been waiting for.

Ben Wikler led the Democratic Party of Wisconsin to a string of improbable victories in a state with a political system so rigged that it was dubbed a “democracy desert”―which is, coincidentally, Trump’s goal for the whole country.

Now, in This Is the Plan, Wikler distills lessons from the front lines in America’s most closely divided state to map out a comprehensive plan to dictator-proof American government, defeat MAGA at every level of the ballot, and build a future of democracy, opportunity, and freedom for all.

It will be a blast. The plan is to, as he writes, “have fun storming the castle―in a civil, metaphorical, and non-January-6th-y way.”

This Is the Plan reveals, year by year and step by step, a vision not only to end America’s collapse into authoritarianism but also to reconnect us to our neighbors―and, fighting side by side for democracy, to build meaning, community, and joy.

A political caravan is a dynamic, on-the-move campaign event where a group of political candidates, party members, and supporters travel together through various towns, cities, or regions to promote a political agenda, candidate, or platform. 

The caravan often consists of decorated vehicles, usually adorned with party symbols, campaign slogans, and vibrant banners. It creates a festive yet strategic atmosphere to energize grassroots support, engage with voters face-to-face, and increase visibility in the lead-up to an election, particularly in areas where traditional outreach might be less effective.

The event is both a celebration of political ideals and a show of strength and solidarity, aiming to build momentum and create a sense of community among supporters while swaying undecided voters with passionate speeches and personal outreach.

Jenny is an emergency and trauma nurse who has spent more than a decade caring for patients and families in some of their most difficult moments. If elected, she would be the first registered nurse to serve in the General Assembly, bringing a perspective that is too often missing in Springfield: someone who has seen firsthand how policy decisions affect patients and families.

Rep. Syed has a proven record. She has consistently stood up to the powerful interests that drive up healthcare costs and sponsored bills to make prescription drugs more affordable for Illinois families that are now law in our state.

We'll kick things off with a brief program featuring our candidates and healthcare professionals, then head out to knock on doors and talk with voters about why we need these healthcare champions in Springfield.

Join us, bring a friend, and help us elect Nabeela and Jenny!

Co-hosting organizations include: AFSCME Council 31, Communication Workers of America, Equality Illinois, Illinois AFL-CIO, Illinois Alliance for Retired Americans, Illinois Federation of Teachers, Illinois Nurses Association, Personal PAC, Planned Parenthood Illinois Action, and UFCW Local 881

events.title: Divisadero Median Beautification Day - 1100 block and 1200 block
events.description:
Join your Divisadero neighbors and San Francisco Public Works for a morning of greening and beautifying the Divisadero Street medians. Together, we’ll put in new flowering succulent plants and other drought-resistant local native flora. We will also plant up to 12 trees in empty sidewalk basins.

We typically start removing green waste at 10:45 AM. Please stay until the end so we can complete all the tasks.

### Agenda
- Safety talk 
- Curb cut demo, planting demo, and deadheading demo 
- Gardening, planting, weeding, pruning, cleaning
- Leave the green waste on the street 
- Rake green waste into large piles 
- Load green waste into the trucks starting around 10:45 AM. 

### What to Bring/Wear
- Bring a reusable water bottle 
- Wear sunscreen and closed toe shoes
- Dress in layers

### Community Partners
- SF Public Works
- District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood
- Divisadero Merchants Association
- North of Panhandle Neighborhood Association (NOPNA)
- Alamo Square Neighborhood Association
- Divisadero neighbors

California is one of the wealthiest places in the world, but working people are being asked to pay the price for devastating healthcare cuts while billionaires get more tax breaks.

Prop 40 is our chance to change that. It puts a one-time tax on California billionaires to replace lost healthcare funding, protect essential services, and invest in our communities.

Together, we're building a grassroots movement to mobilize one million Californians and win YES on Prop 40.

#YESon40 #TaxTheBillionaires

events.title: Election Protection Squads - Join now! / Equipos de protección electoral ¡Únete ahora!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The November 3rd general election is quickly approaching and it's up to us to protect our human right to voice our choice through voting. 

As part of a coordinated statewide effort through We Are California, we are putting together San Diego County Election Protection Squads to bring information and joy to voters, celebrate and affirm their right to vote, and observe, document and report any disruption. Squads will receive training, a t-shirt and/or hat identifying them as an election protector. You will be assigned to vote centers in pairs, learn to identify and report potential issues at the polls such as voter intimidation, misinformation, or procedural irregularities. Squads will also be supported by squad leaders and attorneys able to respond in real time to ensure a free and fair election. 

Alliance San Diego and We Are California, a statewide coalition of organizations, will train and mobilize hundreds of neighborhood voter protectors to monitor vote centers all over San Diego County on election day, Tuesday November 3 from 6:30 - 8:30pm. 

This is a nonpartisan, community effort that will ask volunteers to observe, record, and report...no intervention required. Together we can ensure a free and fair election! 

Sign up for a training now to ensure that no voter stands alone and every vote is counted.

- IN-PERSON Saturday, 9/26 at 10am-11:30am

- VIRTUAL Wednesday, 10/14 at 6pm-7pm

- VIRTUAL Sunday, 11/1 at 12pm-1pm

---------------------------------------------

La elección general del 3 de noviembre se acerca rápidamente y depende de nosotros proteger nuestro derecho humano a expresar nuestra voz a través del voto.

Como parte de un esfuerzo coordinado a nivel estatal a través de Somos California, estamos formando Equipos de Protección Electoral del condado de San Diego para brindar información y alegría a los votantes, celebrar y afirmar su derecho al voto y observar, documentar e informar cualquier interrupción. Los equipos recibirán entrenamiento, una camiseta y/o gorra que los identificará como protector electoral. Los equipos se asignarán a los centros de votación en parejas, aprenderán a identificar y denunciar posibles problemas en las urnas, como intimidación de votantes, desinformación o irregularidades procesales. Los equipos también contarán con el apoyo de líderes de equipo y abogados capaces de responder en tiempo real para garantizar una elección libre y justa.

Alliance San Diego y Somos California, una coalición estatal de organizaciones, entrenará y movilizará a cientos de protectores electorales para monitorear los centros de votación en todo el condado de San Diego el día de la elección, el martes 3 de noviembre, de 6:30pm a 8:30pm. 

Este es un esfuerzo comunitario no partidista que pedirá a voluntarios que observen, registren e informen... no se requiere intervención. ¡Juntos podemos garantizar elecciones libres y justas!

Regístrate ahora para un entrenamiento y garantizar que ningún votante se quede solo y que se cuenten todos los votos.

- VIRTUAL Miércoles, 10/14 de 6pm-7pm
- VIRTUAL Domingo, 11/1 de 12pm-1pm

events.title: Door Knocking
events.description:
We're knocking doors across District 10, block by block, and we need you.

This is how local races are won: neighbors talking to neighbors about what's actually happening on our streets. Theo Ellington is running for Supervisor because District 10 has the potential to be San Francisco's next great chapter — 20,000 homes ready to go on our waterfront, land for the jobs of the future, and neighborhoods that all want the same thing: safe streets, affordable homes, good jobs, and a future worthy of our kids.

No experience necessary. We'll train you on the doors and the app, pair you with a partner, and send you out with everything you need. Most volunteers tell us it's more fun than they expected.

What to expect:
Arrive at the campaign office at 5190 Third Street for check-in
15 minutes of training, turf assignment, and materials
2 hours of canvassing with a partner

What to bring: Comfortable walking shoes, a charged phone, water, and layers.

events.title: PHONE BANKING FOR GLADYS FLORES GARCIA - ASSEMBLY DISTRICT 133
events.description:
Thank you for your interest in volunteering with the Gladys Flores Garcia campaign! Our phone banks are among of the most effective ways to reach voters, share Gladys’ message, and build the support we need to win.

Gladys is running a tough race in Assembly District 133, and we truly appreciate all the help we can get.

No experience is necessary. We provide training, scripts, and live support before and during every shift! All you need is a phone, a second device (such as a tablet or laptop) for viewing scripts and voter information, and a reliable internet connection. Shifts are flexible, and you can sign up for as many or as few as you’d like.

Bilingual and multilingual volunteers are especially encouraged to sign up.

We are happy to provide documentation for school credit or community service for students upon request.

Contact Digital/Youth Campaigns lead Aki Benjamin at akiluxbenjamin@gmail.com with any questions!

events.title: Power & Purpose - South Bend Popular Education Summit

sponsor.name: American Civil Liberties Union of Indiana

location.venue: La Casa de Amistad South Bend IN

events.description:
We are in the fight of a lifetime to defend our rights, our freedoms, and our democracy and this is a moment that calls for courage, connection, and action.

Organizations and individual activists are invited to join the ACLU of Indiana’s South Bend Popular Education Summit on October 16. 

#### Free breakfast pastries and coffee, lunch, and snacks and refreshments will be provided. ####


This free, high-impact, one-day training experience is designed to give you the tools to organize, mobilize, and lead in this critical moment. Together, we’ll learn in community: strengthening our collective ability to cooperate across organizations, build solidarity for immigrant rights, and engage effectively in local and statewide campaigns that protect the civil rights of all Hoosiers.

This summit is for those ready to turn urgency into strategy and outrage into action. Our communities need bold leadership and we need you in the room.

Space is limited. We ask that you commit to the full day and bring someone with you. Organizing is relational, and lasting power is built together.

Now is the moment to stand up, link arms, and lead. Join us and be part of building durable power for immigrant rights and civil liberties across Indiana.

Brought to you by ACLU of Indiana, National Immigration Justice Center, and La Casa De Amistad.

#### The event presentations will be given in English. ####

---

Nos encontramos inmersos en la lucha de nuestra vida para defender nuestros derechos, nuestras libertades y nuestra democracia, y este es un momento que exige valentía, unión y acción.

Se invita a organizaciones y activistas a título individual a participar en la Cumbre de Educación Popular de South Bend de la ACLU de Indiana, que tendrá lugar el 16 de octubre.

#### Se ofrecera pan y café gratuitos para el desayuno, así como almuerzo, aperitivos y bebidas. ####

Esta experiencia, gratuita, educativa, de alto impacto y de un día de duración, está diseñada para proporcionarte las herramientas necesarias para organizar, movilizar y liderar en este momento crítico. Juntos, aprenderemos en comunidad: reforzando nuestra capacidad colectiva para cooperar entre organizaciones, forjar solidaridad en defensa de los derechos de los inmigrantes y participar de forma eficaz en campañas locales y estatales que protejan los derechos civiles de todos los habitantes de Indiana.

Esta cumbre está dirigida a quienes estén preparados para convertir la urgencia en estrategia y la indignación en acción. Nuestras comunidades necesitan un liderazgo audaz y te necesitamos allí.

Las plazas son limitadas. Te pedimos que te comprometas a asistir durante toda la jornada y que traigas a alguien contigo. La organización se basa en las relaciones, y el poder duradero se construye juntos.

Ahora es el momento de levantarnos, unir fuerzas y liderar. Únete a nosotros y forma parte de la construcción de un poder duradero en defensa de los derechos de los inmigrantes y las libertades civiles en todo Indiana.

Organizado por la ACLU de Indiana, el National Immigration Justice Center y La Casa De Amistad.

#### Las presentaciones del evento se realizarán en inglés. ####

events.title: Volunteer Phone Banking - Virtual
events.description:
Every vote matters, and we’re on a mission to make that a reality. That's why ACLU of Michigan volunteers will be calling voters whose ballots need to be cured to ensure their vote can be counted.
 
In Michigan, voters who vote via Absentee Ballot must sign their ballot envelope before their vote is counted. If there are any issues with the signature, the voter’s city or township clerk will notify the voter with instructions on how to fix, or “cure”, the signature issue. (Often, the voter forgot to sign the back of their Absentee Ballot.)
 
Studies have shown that voters are more likely to follow up on their clerk's notice if they receive a call from friendly volunteers, so join us to make sure that every vote counts!
 
No experience is required; we will provide the training. You will just need: 1) a computer or tablet, 2) a cell phone, and 3) a steady internet or Wi-Fi connection.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Every vote matters, and we’re on a mission to make that a reality. That's why ACLU of Michigan volunteers will be calling voters whose ballots need to be cured to ensure their vote can be counted.

In Michigan, voters who vote via Absentee Ballot must sign their ballot envelope before their vote is counted. If there are any issues with the signature, the voter’s city or township clerk will notify the voter with instructions on how to fix, or “cure”, the signature issue. (Often, the voter forgot to sign the back of their Absentee Ballot.)

Studies have shown that voters are more likely to follow up on their clerk's notice if they receive a call from friendly volunteers, so join us to make sure that every vote counts!

No experience is required; we will provide the training. You will just need: 1) a computer or tablet, 2) a cell phone, and 3) a steady internet or Wi-Fi connection.
