events.title: Plan to Vote Party
events.description:
The 2026 midterm elections are here, and it's time to organize.

Having the information to vote is one thing. Making a plan and helping others do the same is how we turn that information into action.

Join Color Of Change for a virtual Plan to Vote Training, where we'll learn how to help voters make a plan to participate in the 2026 elections. We'll walk through the key information voters need, including registration, important election dates and deadlines, early voting, voting by mail, polling locations, and what voters need to know before they cast their ballot.

This training is open to everyone, whether you're a returning volunteer or getting involved with Color Of Change for the first time. You don't need to be an expert. You just need to be ready to learn, organize, and help someone else get ready to vote.

The road to November starts now. Bring a friend, join the training, and let's make sure our communities have a plan to vote.

events.title: Knock Doors for Randy Villegas, CD22 | October 24+25 in Fresno!
events.description:
CA-22 is a must-win seat if we are to flip the House in November and groups from around the Bay Area are coming together to send **Randy Villegas** to D.C. As a result of redistricting, the district is more competitive than ever before. Join **Swing Left East Bay**, the **Bay Area Coalition** and other Bay Area partners to go door-to-door talking to voters in **Fresno** using **deep canvassing** techniques such as active listening and spreading the word about Randy.

The plan: carpool down Saturday morning, canvass in the afternoon, enjoy a group dinner, canvass again Sunday, and head home late Sunday afternoon. We’ll help coordinate rides and lodging. Support for carpooling is available and stipends and/or housing with local volunteers may be available for those for whom cost is a barrier. Cooling cars will support canvassers on hot days, and you'll get all the training you need to be successful.

Remember to bring comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, a well-powered smartphone, and a smile.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition Yes, You Can(vass)! workshop Tuesdays, 5 pm - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: Stitching with Care- October
events.description:
Stitching with Care

Because community is built one stitch at a time.

In times of uncertainty, gathering together can be a powerful act of care.

Stitching with Care is a relaxed, welcoming space to knit, crochet, stitch, mend, or simply sit in good company. There is no formal agenda and no pressure — just hands at work and the kind of conversation that unfolds naturally when people share a table.

This isn't a class or a structured lesson. However, experienced crafters are often happy to offer guidance if someone has a question. Bring a project you’re already working on, start something new, or simply come curious.

** Please RSVP to receive additional details and updates to the event **

It's an experiment in building community the old-fashioned way — by showing up, sharing space, and creating something with our hands.

If it grows, it grows. If it simply becomes a good afternoon together, that’s enough too.

Please bring your own needles and hooks.  You are welcome to work on your own project or simply enjoy the company. 

Some of us are participating in - and you're welcome to join - the red “Melt the ICE Cap” project — inspired in part by the Norwegian resistance hats worn during the 1940s occupation, and more recently by knitters in Minnesota who reminded us that resistance can take many forms: singing in the streets, lighting luminaries on frozen lakes, riding bicycles through city neighborhoods — and yes, knitting red caps.

.

📅 Sunday, June 14, 2:30-4:00pm

🔗 Please RSVP to receive additional details and updates to the event

events.title: Orlando Food Show: March 6th, 2027
events.description:
The 2027 SEPC Food Show Produce Rescue will occur on March 6th at the Orlando World Center Marriott in Orlando, FL.

Volunteers will glean fresh fruits and vegetables from the SEPC Southern Exposure Food Show.  All produce will be donated to those who struggle with food insecurity in Florida.  

This large indoor event requires bending, lifting, packing boxes, and working with others!  We are looking for up to 100 volunteers to help!  We will have two shifts available. 

The morning shift will begin around 8:30 am, and the second shift will begin at 6 pm.  The more volunteers we have the quicker we will finish, and the fresh food will be off to those in need!

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is the SEPC Food Show?

- This is an annual event hosted by the Southeast Produce Council (SEPC),  which is a large trade show connecting growers, distributors, retailers, and foodservice professionals to showcase new produce, technology, and trends in the fresh fruit and vegetable industry, featuring education, networking, and exhibits. 

SoSA is the food recovery recipient of the showcased food. Following the events, with the help of our volunteers, we pack everything up to be sent to various food storage and distribution agencies.  

#### 2. Who can attend? Are community service hours available?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve or receive community service hours. (Kids under 18 must be with an adult.) Please bring any community service paperwork to be signed at day of event.

#### 3. Can I take food if I would like to try it?

-  No. Contractually all food is sent to food banks and agencies that will distribute to people in need. If you know someone in need or are in need yourself, please let one of the SoSA Crew staff know that would like to take back. Food that is deemed "inedible" is available for volunteers to take as animal feed after all pounds are accounted for.

#### 4. What do I wear?

- Wear comfortable clothing that you can bend, lift and walk in. Closed-toed shoes are mandatory.

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need.

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates via email, sign up at: https://endhunger.org/get-involved/volunteer/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets
Please note- Please bring your own water. There will be restrooms. 

📢 Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen 
📞 (863)224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’ve launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that revolutionizes how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Roger Williams Park Conservancy is hosting a screening of No Country for Mothers, a documentary created by Moms First about what motherhood looks like in America today, at the Roger Williams Park Botanical Center. This event, which is free and open to the public, not only invites the community to sit down for an impactful and timely documentary, but also provides space for open dialogue and sharing local resources.

Joining us for the screening and a Q&A panel after the film are representatives from Collective Action for Education, Rhode Island Kids Count, and United Way of Rhode Island. Leading with the belief that education is a fundamental right, Collective Action for Education advocates for local youth, especially those in historically marginalized communities, to have access to high-quality schools. Rhode Island Kids Count has a mission of advancing equitable policies that improve the lives of all children in the state, regardless of race, ethnicity, disability, zip code, immigration status, neighborhood, or income. United Way has been serving Rhode Islanders in need for 100 years, with a mission of uniting community and resources to build racial equity and opportunities.

The visions of these organizations goes hand in hand with the film’s focus on the broken system that makes “motherhood in America impossible by design,” and the culture war sparking division and public scrutiny rather than support as moms navigate the myriad challenges of motherhood and trying to do what’s best for their children.

No Country for Mothers follows activist Reshma Saujani, who will introduce the film via recorded vide is the founder of Girls Who Code and Moms First, as she discovers the lies dividing American moms and chronicles a nationwide movement to bring them back together and win historic support. The film premiered in New York City on June 15, 2026, and has since seen more than 1,000 grassroots screenings in all 50 states. 

“One of our goals at the Conservancy is to bring value to the community through education about health and wellness for our families,” says RWPC Executive Director Melissa Carden. “We look forward to working with RI Kids Count, the United Way, and Collective Action for Education to bring this important film to the RWP Botanical Center.”

The intimate, family-friendly setting of the Botanical Center and presence of supportive community advocates at this screening embodies the film’s premise: that motherhood in America is not a private struggle but a collective one.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early [Rochester & Surrounding Areas]

location.venue: Corner of Rochester Road and Auburn Road

events.description:
We have the power and are claiming it together. No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early [Waterville/Winslow/Oakland/Fairfield/Benton]
events.description:
Our No Kings: Vote Early! October 17 activities here in the Waterville/Winslow/Oakland/Fairfield/Benton communities of Central Maine, hosted by Indivisible Mid Maine and beginning at 10am that day, will consist of three distinct but interlocking events. Participants can pick and choose which events they want to join! 

First, from 10 to 11:45am we will have a short march through downtown Waterville followed by a "signs of democracy" visibility event on the Ticonic Bridge. During this time we will also encourage Waterville voters to deposit their completed absentee ballots in the secure ballot box right nearby, at City Hall, where they will be welcomed joyfully by a group of enthusiastic greeters!

Second, from noon to 1pm, we will march from the same starting point into Head of Falls Park and across the Two Cent Bridge to neighboring Winslow, for a similar celebratory absentee ballot delivery by Winslow voters at the Winslow Town Office, and then will return to our starting point.

Finally, between 1pm and 4pm, we will have a Grand WE VOTE EARLY March, beginning at the same starting point, from Waterville all the way to the Fairfield Town Office (about 3.2 miles) for a celebratory ballot deposit by Fairfield voters there. This will be followed by another "signs of democracy" visibility event on the Fairfield-Benton bridge to end the day. 

Please sign up here AND also sign up for the event(s) on our Indivisible Mid Maine Mobilize site, where they are posted individually so we can have a sense of who is coming to what! 

Here are those links:

https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034710/

https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034712/
 
https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034713/

We will also have brief but still celebratory absentee ballot drop offs in Benton and Oakland that day, details still TBD. Please watch our Indiv Mid Maine Mobilize site for info on those!

Please join us for all or part of this special day, when we will show our commitment to democracy, the joyful act of voting, and voting early and securely in five different area communities!

Join the Maine Democratic Party Voter Access Team and help us build the team that protects the vote on Election Day! Whether you're a returning volunteer or making your very first calls, we'd love to have you.

events.description:
Bethel Municipal Center 11am-1pm
Register here:
https://mobilize.us/s/V096Eg

Here are just some of the exciting things planned for the Bethel No Kings:

Special Guest Speakers: 

Steve Kennedy
Organizing and Network Director for People’s Parity Project (PPP), 
https://peoplesparity.org/team/steve-kennedy/
 Check it out: https://peoplesparity.org/
“Lawyers Building a Legal Profession That Fights for Democracy”
https://peoplesparity.org/new-ppp-report-no-kings-the-urgent-need-for-court-reform/
PPP is organizing working groups of law students and  lawyers who are committed to ensuring our profession is on the right side of history.

Steve Kennedy is an organizer and lawyer whose current work focuses on democratizing the legal system as the Organizing Director at the People's Parity Project. Steve's writing can also be seen in national outlets like the New Republic, Slate, Talking Points Memo, Liberal Currents, and more.

Steve will discuss how community organizing and electoral mobilization support one another and how we can learn from historical movements to face our current crisis. 

Drawing on the history of the struggle for voting rights in the South since Reconstruction, his experience organizing to protect Allison Riggs’s victory in North Carolina’s Supreme Court election, and the sustained civic engagement of Bethel Defends Democracy since Donald Trump's second election, he will explore how people power can defend democratic institutions against attacks on political participation. 

The talk will examine how sustained, grassroots organizing builds the relationships, collective capacity and civic infrastructure necessary to protect democracy, both at the ballot box and in our communities, and how we can all fight for our democracy in the coming election.

Nancy Ryan
What could be better than to have such a longtime local election expert talk to us about our voting rights!
Nancy will talk about the three basic voting options we have in CT and how it is safe and secure.
She is a lifelong Bethel resident and worked for over 20 years as an Election Official in Bethel. She held various pollworker positions during that time including being a Certified Lever Machine Mechanic when we still used those. Nancy also spent four years as Deputy Registrar of Voters and then six years as Registrar of Voters Administrator of Elections. She continues to work for the current registrar of voters when needed. She also served the town as a member of the Public Site and Building Commission for over 20 years and chair for 10. 

Featured Musicians:
Greg Golda:


Gregory J. Golda has been the inspiration for having live musicians at our Bethel rallies.  It started in April 2025 when Greg asked to play a song at our “Spread Love, Note Hate" rally and we were all introduced to a fantastic rendition of (What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love And Understanding, by Elvis Costello.  Since then Greg has introduced us to so many amazing performers.  He also sets up the PA for us and is a frequent speaker himself.  Our very own Renaissance man!

Greg is a Clinical Instructor in the School of Communication, Media & the Arts at Sacred Heart University, where he has taught since 1999. He earned his M.A. in Broadcast Journalism and Digital Media Production from Sacred Heart University (2019), his M.Ed. in Art Education from Penn State (1998), and his B.A. from Buffalo State College (1997).

Golda teaches both undergraduate and graduate courses in multimedia production, television, and media theory, with an emphasis on project-based learning, creativity, and the ethical use of technology. His research and teaching interests include technological democratization, media literacy, and the relationship between media and democracy.

Beyond the classroom, Golda is an active media producer and founder of Construkt Media Studios. His recent work includes Future Focus, Project: Activate, and numerous collaborations with artists and musicians across Connecticut. His most recent public appearance was as a guest of CT State Senator Saud Anwar, discussing media literacy initiatives for K–12 schools on CT-N.com.

 He is also the organizer for 'Empathy is the Cure', which has monthly concerts at Molten Java raising money for local charities. Oct 11th will be a drive for the Autistic Self Advocacy Network.  November 8th will be for Dorothy Day, and the final concert will be for Danbury Unites for Immigrants (DUFI) on Dec 13th at Sugar Hollow in Danbury.  Events are 3-6pm.

Lenny Levine:


Lenny Levine has become a frequent performer and rallier at our weekly rallies so we are so excited to welcome him to this No Kings event. Lenny attended Brooklyn College, graduating in 1962 with a BA in Speech and Theater. Immediately thereafter, he forgot about all of that and became a folk singer, then a folk-rock singer and songwriter, and finally a studio singer and composer of many successful jingles, including McDonald’s, Lipton Tea, and Jeep. He has composed songs and sung backup for Billy Joel, Neil Diamond, Peggy Lee, Diana Ross, Barry Manilow, the Pointer Sisters, Carly Simon, and others. In addition, he performed for a number of years with the improvisational comedy group War Babies.

His work has been widely published in literary magazines and journals. He received a Pushcart Prize nomination for short fiction. His mystery novels Diehard Fan and Death in the Jingle Jungle are available in print, Nook, and Kindle on Amazon.com and Barnes and Noble.com. His website is lennylevinewriter.com.

events.title: Phone Banking

Call District 10 voters with Team Theo!

Theo Ellington is a third-generation San Franciscan, born and raised at Third and Palou in Bayview, running for Supervisor to deliver safe streets, affordable homes, and good-paying jobs for every neighborhood in District 10. No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the “girl boss” and “trad wife” labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. events.title: Wednesday Night Call-A-Thon 4 Nurse Lee!
events.description:
Join Team Elizabeth every Wednesday night as we reach voters across Arizona’s 5th Congressional District directly from the comfort of your own home!

Whether you’re a seasoned caller or making your very first phone calls for a campaign, phone banking is hands-down one of the single most powerful ways to get Elizabeth elected and build real power for working families in the East Valley.

### Why Phone Bank with Us?
We run a supportive, organized, and effective virtual operation so you feel confident and equipped throughout our two-hour session.

- **Fast-Track for Veterans:** Experienced callers can jump straight into a dedicated breakout room at start time, skip the main intro, and start making calls right away.
- **Everything Sent Ahead:** Receive a pre-shift checklist and your Zoom link in your inbox before Wednesday so you know exactly how to log in and prepare.
- **Tech & Call Coaching:** We offer full dialer training for beginners, showing you how to use our script as a conversational guide to connect voter stories to Elizabeth’s platform.
- **Support & Halfway Break:** We keep the main Zoom room open for real-time support and pause halfway through for a collective quick break to stretch, hydrate, and share how it's going.
- **Debrief & Connection:** Wrap up together to share overall call tallies, swap favorite voter stories with fellow volunteers, and recharge before signing off.

### What a Typical Shift Looks Like (2 Hours Total)

- **First 15–20 Mins:** Zoom welcome and full dialer training for new callers (or head straight to the Express Breakout Room to start calling immediately!).

- **Next 45 Mins:** First calling block with live tech support available in Zoom.

- **7PM Stretch:** Quick midpoint break to stretch, refresh, and check in.

- **Next 40 Mins:** Second calling block to keep building our momentum!

- **Final 10 Mins:** Rejoin the full group to tally our impact, debrief, and celebrate our wins.

### What You’ll Need

A fully charged phone and/or a computer or tablet with a stable internet connection.

A quiet space to make calls, headphones with a mic (optional), and a beverage of your choice.

First time phone banking? Don't sweat it, we’ll walk you through every step! Grab a drink, log in, and let’s talk to our neighbors.

events.title: Freedom Fridays
events.description:
Join us on Fridays at NOON at the Williamsburg James City County Courthouse, located at 5201 Monticello Avenue, Williamsburg, with your signs, a cold beverage, and a chair, if needed. Bring a sign that represents the theme you are most passionate about.

COMMUNITY NORMS: Please read before attending one of our events. One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. Please remain out of the median, per instructions from the police. Being in the median puts us at risk and potentially drivers as well. Do not block the right-of-way for others. If someone is on the sidewalk, please step back and let them pass. If an Urgent Situation arises, we will raise a straight arm with our Hand in a Fist to ask for Silence. PLEASE DO THE SAME TO QUIET THE CROWD. This way we can quickly relay an important message to all. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day.”
PLEASE DO NOT BLOW WHISTLES UNLESS ICE IS PRESENT. The purpose of the whistles is to alert the public to be vigilant. Otherwise, blowing them can falsely alert the crowd to a danger that does not exist! At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept. Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, COWBELLS, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave! As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers, who will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirt. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

events.title: Poll Observer Training with the Maine Dems Voter Access Team
events.description:
Poll Observers are the eyes and ears of the Voter Access Team on Election Day. When a machine goes down, a line runs long, or a voter is turned away, we only know about it because someone in the room told us. That is how we respond in time to fix it.

Training is required to be a Democratic Poll Observer, and it takes less than an hour. Every session covers the same material, so you only need to attend one.

### What you'll learn

- What you can and cannot do inside a polling place, and what your standing as a pollwatcher actually is

- How Election Day unfolds hour by hour, what to check on arrival, and how to observe the absentee canvass

- Where poll workers most often get registration and identification wrong, including why a student ID answers identity but not residence

- The issues that come up most often, from students and New Mainers to how a challenge actually works

- How to use LBJ, our reporting tool, and why it matters to log the problem you solved yourself

- What to do in rare situations, including evacuations and federal law enforcement near or in the polls

### Pick any session

Sessions run online from September 15 through October 30.

### What happens next

The week before Election Day, we will assign you to a polling place and give you the contact numbers you need for the day.

### Who can attend

Anyone interested, 18 or older. You do not need to be a Maine resident.

Questions? Email the Maine Democratic Party Voter Access Team at votersupport@mainedems.org.

sponsor.name: Building Bridges for America Action Fund

events.description:
## *Bad Law: Ten Popular Laws That Are Ruining America* by Elie Mystal

Join progressive grassroots organizers from across the county in reading and discussing *Bad Law: Ten Popular Laws That Are Ruining America* by Elie Mystal. 

In Bad Law, legal scholar and New York Times bestselling author Elie Mystal reimagines what our legal system, and society at large, could look like if we could move past legislation plagued by racism, misogyny, and corruption. Through accessible yet detailed prose and trenchant wit, Mystal argues that these egregiously awful laws—his “Bill of Wrongs”—continue to cause systematic and individual harm and should be repealed completely. With biting humor and insight, Mystal exposes the flawed foundations of the rules we live by.


## FAQ:

### 1. How can I order the book?

You can support Building Bridges For America with your purchase through bookshop.org by clicking **[here](https://bookshop.org/p/books/bad-law-ten-popular-laws-that-are-ruining-america-elie-mystal/768b049cbb747ca5?ean=9781620978580&affiliate=125978)**. Purchase or ownership of the book is not required to attend. Consider checking your local library (click **[here](https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/CommunityServices/find-libraries.aspx)** to find a library near you). 

### 2. What is the reading schedule?

For this book, we will have a 5 week session. Reading is not required to attend, but we highly encourage it. A Reading/Discussion Guide will be sent prior to each meeting to compliment our journey and discussion.

**WEEK 1 - SEP 28:**

* Introduction
* Chap 1 - Why Isn’t Everyone Registered to Vote
* Chap 2 - How Did Immigrants Become “Illegal”?


**WEEK 2 - OCT 05:**

* Chap 3 - Who Gave Away the Skies to the Airlines?

events.title: NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY  Public Assembly Winston Salem NC

sponsor.name: Camel City United Indivisible North Carolina

events.description:
From Neighborhood Action to People Power

Since our John Lewis Voting Rights Assembly, we’ve been organizing neighborhood by neighborhood—building relationships, hosting house meetings, knocking on doors, and developing Community and Voter Protection Ambassadors.

Now we’re putting that organizing into action.

OCTOBER 10 — KICKOFF

We will begin our week of action on October 10 with community activities focused on voting rights, voter education, and preparing our neighborhoods for early voting.

We are also planning a community screening of SUPPRESSED AND SABOTAGED, presented through Brave New Films, examining voter suppression and the continuing struggle to protect access to the ballot. Screening details are pending final confirmation.

Additional October 10 program and location details will be announced.

OCTOBER 17 — NEIGHBORHOOD ACTION DAY

10:00 AM–12:00 PM | Across Our Communities

October 17 doesn't begin at Corpening Plaza. It begins in our neighborhoods.

Teams throughout the community will spend the morning taking action: canvassing, phone banking, writing postcards, talking with neighbors, sharing voter information, identifying barriers to voting, and helping eligible voters make their plans to participate.

Every neighborhood team will keep track of what it accomplishes.

How many doors did we knock?
How many conversations did we have?
How many calls did we make?
How many postcards did we write?
How many people made voting plans?
What did our neighbors tell us?

Then we bring those results downtown.

AFTER THE ACTION — CORPENING PLAZA

Following the morning's neighborhood work, volunteers, neighborhood residents, partner organizations, and community members will come together at Corpening Plaza.

This is not simply another rally.

It is a community report-back and public assembly—a place to account for what we accomplished together, hear what our neighbors told us, recognize the people doing the work, and commit ourselves to what comes next.

Neighborhoods and teams will report their results. We'll hear community stories. We'll celebrate our collective work. And we'll ask people to make their next commitment to protecting voting rights and helping eligible voters participate.

There will be music, signs, community spirit, and celebration—but the centerpiece of the gathering will be the work our communities have done and the work we pledge to continue.

Because October 17 isn't the finish line.

It's part of a larger effort to build lasting relationships and stronger neighborhoods so that every eligible voter has the information, support, and opportunity needed to make their voice heard.

NO THRONES. NO CROWNS. NO KINGS. WE DECIDE.

We decide who represents us.
We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now we're taking the next step: turning people power into voter participation.

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early is not purely a protest. October 17 is a day of nonpartisan voter participation—bringing communities together, helping eligible voters understand their voting options, and making sure people have the information and support they need to participate.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and designed to increase participation among all eligible voters.

A core principle of No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. Participants are expected to act lawfully and seek to de-escalate potential confrontations. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to these events.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Detroit!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: 2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

location.venue: Donovan Hines Foundation of Exuberance Co

events.description:
2026 #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence

Beginning Wednesday, December 9, 2026 until the end of December, we will come together across the nation to host the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence.

These local events will be anchored by the 14th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.—held near the 14-year mark of the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting tragedy, when a 20-year-old gunman armed with an AR-15 hunted and murdered 20 first graders and six educators.

Across the country, vigils (as simple as lighting candles) and gatherings will honor lives stolen by gun violence, uplift survivors, raise awareness, and demand urgent action from our leaders to finally end this epidemic. From schools and workplaces to houses of worship, neighborhoods, grocery stores, homes, nightclubs, streets, and even our democracy itself—gun violence impacts every aspect of American life.

The theme of this year’s campaign is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

We stand in solidarity with over 1.4 million Americans who have been shot since Sandy Hook, with every community devastated by gun violence for decades. We will send a clear message to our local, state, and federal lawmakers, raise awareness, and help build the movement for common-sense solutions.

Let’s #HonorWithAction together. Let’s demand freedom from gun violence.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Boston
events.description:
**On Oct. 17, the people of Boston will come together to defend democracy. Our message is simple: Your vote is your power. Make it count.**

For past events, the No Kings Boston Coalition has asked you to mobilize on Boston Common for huge rallies. This time, we’re asking **you** to do the organizing.

Sponsor a voter registration drive in your neighborhood. Host a Know Your Rights training.

Gather your neighbors to cast ballots at an early voting station — then return to celebrate democracy with a block party. 

Decorate custom “I voted!” stickers. Set up an impromptu party outside an early voting station. Get into the spirit of creative resistance with an art activity or a protest music concert.

Help your community make a plan for what tools of nonviolent resistance you will use if our voting rights are threatened.

To align with the spirit of No Kings, keep your actions lawful, non-violent, and focused on the power of the vote. Within those parameters, you have creative freedom! We have lots of ideas to get you started at [nokings.boston](https://nokings.boston/).

Once you’ve planned your event, [register it on Mobilize](https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/c/no-kings-vote-early-/event/create/?utm_source=toolkit) to get it on the map and flag it [on our website](https://nokings.boston/) to access the No Kings Boston materials below.
 
**Why list your event with us?**
- Include your event on our No Kings Boston map (synced with Mobilize)
- Access No Kings Boston coalition assets like trifolds, stickers, a passport of actions and more
- Be part of our media advisory (for events registered by the week of 10/5)
- We may be able to help provide small amounts of funding depending on the action you’re organizing and what we are able to collect in donations.
- Get support from No Kings Boston Coalition organizers

**Not up for organizing your own action?** Check out the map on nokings.boston or right here on Mobilize and visit the activities happening around the city and across the state on Oct. 17! Wherever you go, take the time to cast your ballot — and make sure your friends and family do so, too.

events.title: Protect Voting Rights in Yuma County! 🗳️
events.description:
📅 November 03, 2026 ⏰ Shifts: 4 Different Shifts📍 Locations: Across Yuma County

Join Rural Arizona Engagement (RAZE) and help protect every voter's right to cast their ballot on Primary Election Day!

We're recruiting volunteers to serve as Election Protection Poll Watchers throughout Yuma County. This is an important, nonpartisan role that helps ensure voters can access the ballot free from intimidation or unnecessary barriers.

What You'll Do: - Observe polling locations from outside the 75-foot boundary - Report any voting issues or concerns you witness - Help support a fair and accessible voting experience for all voters

No experience is necessary! We will provide all the training, materials, and support you need before Election Day. Live and recorded virtual training options will be available, and volunteers will receive an Election Protection shirt before their shift.

Whether you can volunteer for a few hours or a full shift, your participation makes a difference.

Important: This is NOT a partisan poll observing inside the polling location. This is outside the 75-foot line and is nonpartisan Election Protection work.

Sign up today and help strengthen democracy in Yuma County! 💙🗳️

events.title: Team Shannon Blue Wave Phone Bank
events.description:
Join Team Hardin for our weekly phone banks as we connect directly with voters across Columbus ahead of the Nov 3 General Election.

This is one of the most important ways you can make an impact.
Volunteers will use our phone banking system, Scale to Win, to call voters, share key election information, and turn out the vote for Don Leonard, candidate for Congress (OH-15); Amy Acton, candidate for Governor; and Sherrod Brown, candidate for U.S. Senate. 

Whether you’re new to phone banking or have experience, we’ll make sure you’re fully prepared. Each session includes a brief training, a clear script, and support from our team so you feel confident every step of the way.

What you’ll do:
Call voters in Columbus using our online dialer (Scale to Win)
Share key details about the Nov 3 General Election and Early Voting (October)
Help voters make a plan to cast their ballot
Identify supporters and strengthen our outreach efforts

What you’ll need:
A phone (cell or computer audio)
A laptop or tablet
A willingness to connect with your community

Why it matters: Elections are decided by the voters we reach. Every call you make helps ensure more people have the information they need to participate—and helps build the path to victory.

Join us, bring a friend, and be part of the team working to deliver leadership that shows up and gets results for Columbus. 
Let’s get to work.

events.title: Protect the Vote: Outside Poll Observer On-Demand Training
events.description:
# Protect the Vote as an Outside Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Outside Poll Observers help identify potential issues outside voting locations and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

## What You'll Learn

- Outside Poll Observer basics
- What to expect outside a voting location
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role Outside Poll Observers play in protecting voters

## Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Outside Poll Observers help us understand what is happening around voting locations, identify potential barriers or concerns, and make sure issues are quickly reported to the appropriate team.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

## No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as an Outside Poll Observer.

### Recommended Prerequisite

We encourage you to attend a Know Your Rights training in addition to this session. It provides important background on North Carolina election law and voter protections that will help you succeed as an Outside Poll Observer.

Sign up here: https://www.mobilize.us/nc-coordinated/event/953390/

### After signing up, you'll be directed to the recorded training video and next steps.

events.title: Anytime Virtual Phone Banking: Clyde for Congress
events.description:
Phone Bank for Clyde on Your Own Schedule

We know your schedule is busy, so we have made it easier than ever to make a difference on your own time. Sign up to make calls for the Clyde Jones for Congress campaign whenever it fits into your day—whether that is for 15 minutes between errands or two hours on a Sunday afternoon.

Phone banking is the fastest way to scale our grassroots outreach and talk directly with voters across Alabama's 1st Congressional District about lowering healthcare costs, fighting for working families, and bringing accountability back to Washington. With our flexible phone banking system, you can pull up a list and start dialing whenever you have free time.

How it Works:

Sign Up: Register here to receive instant access to our virtual phone bank hub. Your confirmation email will include details for how to start making calls right away from wherever you are. 

Start Dialing: Log in from any computer, tablet, or smartphone. 

Log the Data: Simply select the outcome of your call on the screen, follow the script to chat with the voter, and click to move to the next neighbor!

What You Need:

A laptop, desktop, or tablet with internet access.

A quiet, comfortable place to make calls.

Your unique login link (sent immediately upon RSVP).

Every call moves us one step closer to victory. Secure your access today and start dialing when it works best for you! For technical support or questions along the way, our organizing team is just an email or text away.

events.description:
**Come meet Michael Melillo, candidate for San Jose Unified School Board, Area 4.**

You know Gini Bossenbroek. Now come meet the school board candidate she’s backing, and find out why. Join Gini and your neighbors at her Willow Glen home for an afternoon with Michael.

Michael’s no stranger to San José Unified or to the work of improving our schools. He’s a parent of two San José Unified students, both at Pioneer High School, and served on the San José Unified Board of Trustees in 2018, holding the same Area 4 seat he’s running for today. He has chaired the district’s bond oversight committee and currently serves as president of the Pioneer High School Education Foundation.

In his professional career, Michael has spent over two decades solving complex problems with data and evidence. He brings that same approach to the issues facing our schools: set clear goals, be honest about the results, and fix what isn’t working. He’s running to help every student reach their full potential, put student safety and well-being first, and rebuild trust between the district and the families it serves.

His campaign is proud to be endorsed by State Controller Malia Cohen, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, Assemblymembers Alex Lee and Patrick Ahrens, the South Bay Labor Council, and the Everytown for Gun Safety Action Fund, among many others.

Come spend an afternoon with neighbors who care about our public schools. Bring your questions. Michael will bring real answers.

**When:** Sunday, October 11, 1:00 PM

**Where:** Available upon RSVP

**Suggested contribution:** $50 to $250. Every contribution goes directly to reaching Area 4 voters before November 3. Contributions are not required to attend.

Can't make it but want to help? Contribute at melilloforsjusd.com.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Bowie, MD Visibility Brigade

location.venue: Pedestrian Bridge at Bowie Town Center

events.description:
Join your neighbors and community in Bowie for No Kings 4.0!!!! We'll reprise our DUELING BRIDGE BRIGADES to spread pro-democracy and pro-voting messages. 12-2pm!

Bridge 1: Pedestrian Bridge over Rt-197 at Bowie Town Center. Park in the Bowie Town Center off of Northview Drive. We'll be along the roadway and on the bridge, feel free to bring your own sign!

Bridge 2: Pedestrian Bridge over MD-50. Park at the Park and Ride off of Northview Drive or in the back of the old Bowie Movie Theater lot off of Major Lansdale Blvd. From the movie theater lot, follow the footpath behind the Hampton Inn, turn left at the fence and it's a short walk  (approx 4 min) to the bridge. From the Park and Ride, exit the lot, turn left, turn left onto the footpath, follow until the bridge (approx 8 minute walk). Due to motorist speeds and the height of bridge, individual signs cannot be read. We will provide the large letter signs, please bring flags, foam hands, pompoms, and things to wave. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
Indivisible Falmouth invites you to join us on the Village Green in Falmouth to again push for preserving democracy and to say NO KINGS!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Every week, we're reaching voters across VA-02 to make sure they're ready to participate in one of the most competitive House races in the country — and to vote on three constitutional amendments protecting reproductive healthcare, marriage equality, and voting rights. We'll help voters who have already requested mail ballots complete and return them on time, understand key deadlines, and make a clear, confident plan to vote, whether by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send follow-up texts with early voting, polling location, and ballot drop box information to those planning to vote early or on Election Day.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action—making sure ballots are returned and votes are counted.

Join us for an enlightening evening of conversation and community-building as we hear from candidates for the Leander School Board endorsed by the Travis County Democratic Party! Plus, our Democratic U.S. Congressional District and Texas House District candidates will be our special guests!

Free refreshments! 

This Meet & Greet is being held in the Round Mountain School, now a Community Center. The school was established in the 1870s as a one-room structure made of logs. It was refurbished over the years, until the students eventually transferred into the Leander School District in 1945. But from its inception, this structure has been at the heart of the Round Mountain community, standing as a symbol of the importance the residents have always placed on education.

•	Meet the Leander School Board candidates who share those values in public education. Hear their vision for today’s school system and ask them questions. 

•	Special guest, Claire Reynolds, is running to be our next Representative to the U.S. Congress in Congressional District 11. She’s eager to hear from attendees about what she can do for them in Congress.

•	Tom Luck, a retired pastor who lives in Fredericksburg, is running to represent HD 19 in the Texas House. Discover his story and the positive change he’d like to bring to our community.

events.title: Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm
events.description:
#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Mount Vernon, Washington

address_lines: Skagit County Court House, Lions Park, Intersection of Riverside Drive and Colleg Way,and Intersection of Colle Way and Laventure RoadMount Vernon

events.description:
Join Indivisible Skagit for Vote Early Sign Waving at key intersections and Ballot Drop Boxes in Mount Vernon.

**Bring signs: Vote Today, Don't Wait; Vote Early!; Use Ballot Drop Boxes!; This is the No Kings election; Friends Don't Let Friends Not Vote; Vote On Day One!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
### The election is around the corner. Let’s turn our anxiety into action!

We the Fighters is a group of everyday people who have decided to step up. In the face of injustice, we choose to act together over despairing alone. And we’re inviting you to join us.

We’ll be calling voters in our district to talk about our representative’s vote for the “Big Beautiful Bill,” what it has meant for our lives, and our chance to hold them accountable this November.

We’ll train you before your first call and support you along the way.

events.title: VOLUNTEER: Atlanta Pride Parade
events.description:
Chris Harden firmly believes in standing with the LGBTQ+ community, upholding equal treatment under the law, protecting freedom from discrimination, and ensuring everyone has the fundamental right to live openly and safely as their authentic self. Show your support too and march with us in the 2026 Atlanta Pride Parade!

Registration: Space is strictly capped at 100 walkers, so please sign up as soon as possible to secure your spot!

Event Details:
When: Sunday, October 11
Arrival & Lineup: Walkers must arrive at the assembly spot prior to 10:45 AM; no one will be allowed to enter the assembly area after 11:00 AM. Step-off starts promptly at 12:00 PM. We will be the first wave of the parade. Please plan for approximately 1 hour of walking time, but potentially more, as the 2.2 mile march takes time to complete.
Logistics & Travel: Street closures begin at 9:00 AM, so we strongly encourage making travel plans now. Taking MARTA is highly recommended—the Civic Center MARTA station exits directly into the parade assembly area. If you are ridesharing, it is recommended to be dropped off at the corner of Courtland and Ralph McGill (you will be in the correct section), or at Baker St and Peachtree, and then walk two blocks up to Peachtree and Ralph McGill. Our row assignment is Row J - it includes the street section running from the intersection of Ivan Allen and Ralph McGill Blvds to the intersection of Baker Street and Peachtree. Landmark buildings nearby include SunTrust Plaza and Porfirio's. 
Where & Route: The parade route marches down Peachtree Street and ends at the Charles Allen Gate entrance to Piedmont Park (1320 Monroe Dr NE, Atlanta, GA), where participants will enter the park. You MUST enter the park at the end of the parade. 
What to Bring: Plan ahead for weather (sunscreen, rain gear, etc.), stay hydrated, and bring snacks for the march.

What to Wear & Swag:
Gear Up: Deck out in your best Pride gear! You can order official Harden Pride-themed shirts and hats ahead of time at https://www.electharden.com/?anchor=ShowSupport to ensure they arrive before the parade, or wear your own Pride-themed clothing.
Campaign Swag: We will provide parade swag for walkers to hand out to crowd members along the route!

Come out for an incredible day of high energy, visibility, and community celebration. Lock in your spot today!

events.title: Honesty Coalition 2026 LGBTQ+ Youth Listening Session
events.description:
This session is for students and their parents. We'll have two rooms in the Zoom—so parents and students can speak freely with their peers!

The Belonging for Every Student Listening Campaign is a statewide effort to better understand how recent anti-LGBTQ+ laws are shaping the experiences of students, educators, and families across Ohio.

Over the past few years, laws like House Bill 8 have required all 611 school districts in Ohio to adopt new policies. While these policies are public record, what remains unclear is how they are being put into practice and how they are impacting real people in school communities.

This autumn, we are listening. We want to know: How are districts implementing these policies? Are schools going beyond what the law requires? How are LGBTQ+ students and families being affected? What changes are educators experiencing in their classrooms, materials, and ability to support students?

By gathering stories, insights, and data from across the state, this campaign will help build a clearer picture of what’s happening on the ground. These findings will directly inform advocacy strategies for the 2026–2027 school year, ensuring that efforts to support safe, inclusive, and equitable schools are rooted in the lived experiences of Ohio communities.

Please share with young Ohioans who have something to say about the experiences of LQBTQ+ students in our schools in the 2026-2027 school year.

events.title: Poll Greeting for Early Voting at Brambleton Center (1-2 hour shifts, NOT ALL DAY)
events.description:

events.title: Hop on the Bus to Maine to flip the Senate!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing State—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Troy Jackson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave South Station at 8:30am and return around 7:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

OCTOBER, 17, 2026 
10-12

About this event
NO KINGS VOTE EARLY RALLY!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Join Equality Florida at Apopka Pride 2026!

Equality Florida needs your help to reach our incredible LGBTQ community in Apopka! With the increase in polarization surrounding LGBTQ+ issues in Florida, we need all hands on deck to talk with LGBTQ+ supporters, collect petitions, recruit volunteers, and educate our community!

events.description:

_Join our weekly one-hour virtual training on having Conversations for Clean Water!_ You will learn how to have meaningful conversations with neighbors about the water crisis and next steps in the fight for clean water.

This year, Food & Water Action fought the Iowa legislature to restore our statewide water monitoring program and _sued the EPA_ to protect Iowa’s drinking water. Now, we’re talking to our neighbors statewide to understand how the crisis is affecting everyday Iowans and provide meaningful ways to fight back. **Help build the movement to fight for what Iowans deserve.**

Together, we'll learn about what we can do to keep our water safe and send a clear message to elected officials: **stop putting Big Ag ahead of working families.**

**No experience required; beginners welcome!**

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early DAYTONA BEACH, FL
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Southlake Saturday Visibility Hands Off Our Vote
events.description:
We’ve protested. Now we will CONNECT AND PROTECT our votes! 
LOCATION CHANGE BACK TO TESLA 

Trump and his Big Lie cronies and Musk are plotting to do everything they can to undermine our elections in 2026 and Texas is ground zero. In fact, last month, the new Texas Secretary of State suspended over 1.2 million Texas voters from the rolls!! 

Join us in Southlake Town Square as we share information with eligible voters on how they can check their voting status before the Oct 5 deadline. This is information that many voters are really wanting to know so this should be a gratifying interaction with our fellow Texans and a chance for you to really make a difference!

And since Musk has promised to meddle in the elections again, Indivisible Texas 24 is staging our new weekly Saturday morning initiative back on the sidewalk in front of Southlake Tesla on Sept 5.

Hands Off Our Vote is Indivisible’s national program to ensure all eligible voters get to cast their ballot, every ballot is counted, and the results are honored.

Whether it’s trying to end mail-in voting, targeting registration programs, blocking vote-counting, even trying to ban states from encouraging people to vote – it’s going to be no-holds-barred from them this year as they try desperately to block the free and fair elections. 

We’re going to be ready for whatever dirty tricks they try. And we’re going to do it together with community power starting this Saturday morning. That’s why we need you to join us!

Indivisible and its events practice peaceful and utilize de-escalation training. Weapons of any kind are prohibited. We follow city and state ordinances

events.title: No Kings 4 - Traverse City: Vote Early!
events.description:
Traverse Indivisible's No Kings 4: Vote Early is our biggest event yet, and we're building it with a broad coalition of community organizations, Indivisible groups from across MI-01, and allies coming from as far as Sault Ste. Marie. This is a big tent, and there's room for everyone.

Michigan early voting opens October 24. October 17 is your moment to make a plan. Come get informed, get registered, and walk away ready to vote early. Because in America, leaders do not get to choose who votes, whose voices matter, or what future our communities deserve. The people choose their leaders.

📆Saturday, October 17 | 11am-4pm
📍Grand Traverse Civic Center, Traverse City

ADA Access: We expect to have designated ADA areas and drop-off assistance available. More details will be posted as they develop. Questions? Email comms@traverseindivisible.org.

What to Expect
* Voter registration
* Election protection
* Live music
* Guest speakers
* On-stage games and contests
* Judged Spooky Election–themed Wagon Float Parade
* Face painting, and a kids activity tent
* Plus a broad mix of community org booths and a crowd of people who are ready to act.

Rain or shine. Free and open to the public. Bring the whole family!

Why Register?
Your registration helps us with critical event logistics and crowd estimates.

Parking
Parking on-site is limited. We encourage you to walk, ride a bike, or take the BATA bus when possible.

More Info Coming Soon
We'll have a full event info site live in the coming weeks. Keep an eye on traverseindivisible.org/event-info and follow us on social media for updates. New to No Kings? Learn more at nokings.org.

No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings. We Decide.

-----

A core principle behind all Traverse Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action and peaceful resistance. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation, and to act lawfully. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to this event.

events.title: The People's Tea
events.description:
Join us for “The People’s Tea,” a biweekly power hour where we’ll discuss what’s going on, what it means, and what we can do. 

At the People’s Tea, we will slow down, process the news, and make sense of what’s happening. We’re building a space where we can stay informed without losing our humanity (and sanity), and move from feeling overwhelmed and isolated toward understanding, connection, and collective action. 

We will meet every other Wednesday at 8 PM Eastern / 7 PM Central / 6 PM Mountain / 5 PM Pacific. There’s only one requirement to join. This will be a judgment-free space where we will show compassion and curiosity. We simply expect you to be respectful and non-judgmental. There are no expectations to have all the answers, know the “right” things, or even know where to begin. 

Come learn, listen, and connect.

events.title: Canvass for Michele Clark
events.description:
Join Citizen Action/Illinois for a canvass with Michele Clark who is ready to fight for affordable healthcare in Springfield.

Michele Clark is a lifelong resident of Chicago's northwest suburbs, shaped by parents who rose from modest farm beginnings in northern Wisconsin. Legacy of perseverance and advocacy runs through Michele's career and community work: as a former small business owner who built and ran an early childhood learning center, as COO of the Boys and Girls Club of Dundee Township during the pandemic, and now as Director of Development for the D300 Food Pantry, working to ensure no local child goes hungry. She remains active in her community as a board member of the Elgin Symphony Orchestra and a consultant to women-owned small businesses and nonprofits, channeling her mother's example into a lasting commitment to women's rights and equal opportunity.

We'll kick things off with a brief program featuring our candidate and healthcare professionals, then head out to knock on doors and talk with voters about why we need Michele as a healthcare champion in Springfield.

Join us, bring a friend, and help us elect Michele!

Co-hosting organizations include: 

AFSCME Council 31
Illinois AFL-CIO
Illinois Federation of Teachers
Illinois Nurses Association

events.title: Vienna/Fairfax VA Bridge Brigade - Weekly Wed. PM Rush Hour

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
We are the Vienna/Fairfax chapter of over 400 Visibility Brigades around the country. As a group of volunteers, we will display large messages on the bridge at Vaden Drive over I-66 on a regular basis, starting Wednesday, September 16, to encourage early voting and other pro-democracy actions.   

We will provide large signs facing I-66 traffic on the bridge.  Please do not post other signs (or stickers or anything permanent) on the bridge.  You do not need to bring anything other than your energy.  But if you want to bring hand-held signs, please display those for the traffic driving over the bridge on Vaden Drive.  

Other notes: 
- There are two garages backing onto Vaden Drive; one on the Vienna side of the highway and one on the Fairfax side.  You need a credit card or metro card to exit the garages; weekday parking is $4.95.   Neighborhood parking is very limited.
- Bring water, hat, snacks, folding chairs, and sunscreen as needed for your own comfort.  Please take any litter home with you.
- Please be cautious if you cross Vaden Drive for the other side of the bridge.
- There is a public restroom in the Metro station.
- Check your email in case there is a last minute change. The event may be altered due to rain or extreme temperatures.
- We will do one Thurs in Oct (the 22nd) because early voting at the Jim Scott Rec Center on Vaden Drive starts there Oct 22 and runs to 7 PM.
- Most drivers react positively to our messaging.  If you receive a negative reaction, please remain positive (or at least neutral) to avoid escalating the situation.
- We must not block pedestrians getting across the bridge, so please leave room on the back end of the bridge sidewalks for pedestrians.
- No weapons of any kind and no violence. 
- If you wish to bring friends or family members with you, they are welcome. Please familiarize them with our rules and safety tips.

Our mission is to bring visibility to specific issues we're facing under the Trump regime, encourage action, and foster a sense of community for those that feel disheartened by the state of our nation. Join us and help us fight fascism!

Learn more about the Visibility Brigade at www.visibilitybrigade.com

events.title: Queer Out the Vote Traverse City - Canvass for EQMI
events.description:
In 2025 and 2026 alone, more than 20 anti-transgender bills were introduced in the Michigan House of Representatives. Bathroom bans. Sports bans. A legislative package designed to strip access to transgender healthcare young people and families who need it in Michigan. We were able to ensure none of these bills passed because we showed up!

We know that previous gains can be lost and further progress can be jeopardized when we stop showing up. What happens this November will determine whether Michigan continues to be a place where LGTBQ+ people can live openly, access the healthcare they need to thrive, and be treated with dignity. 

When Equality Voters Turn Out, Equality Moves Forward!

When equality voters turnout, we move Michigan forward. And nobody is more equipped to engage the LGBTQ+ community and our allies than Equality Michigan. That’s why we need your help this summer and fall, knocking on our neighbors doors, meeting them face-to-face, making sure they have the info they need to vote and the inspiration they need to stay engaged long after November 3rd, to hold our elected officials accountable.

Sign up TODAY!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join One Team Michigan for a community canvass launching from the Campaign Office in Sterling Heights.

We’ll head out from the office to talk with voters in the community about the issues that matter most to them and share information about Democratic candidates on the November ballot, including Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General. Michigan’s general election is November 3, 2026.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you’re a seasoned canvasser, we’ll provide training and everything you need before heading out. You’ll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and time to ask questions before your shift.

Before you arrive:

• Download the MiniVAN Canvassing app on your phone.
• Bring a fully charged phone with a strong cellular connection, if possible.
• If you don’t have reliable service or would rather use a paper list, let us know ahead of time and we’ll make sure to print one for you.
• Wear comfortable walking shoes and dress for the weather. Canvassing will take place rain or shine.

We’ll meet at the Campaign Office before heading out to canvass. We look forward to seeing you there!
