events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Medford, WI
events.description:
We will gather along the highway to give visibility to our call to Vote with positive, non-partisan signs, songs, and good cheer.  

Everyone who comes will receive cards and flyers they can distribute that direct voters to a website with information on how to register, request an absentee ballot, find their polling place, etc.  These cards and flyers will match signs at the rally, as well as newspaper and online ads that will hit that day or soon after.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Cloquet, MN
events.description:
# Celebrate Our Neighbors & Vote!

Join us for a fun, community-centered celebration of voting and our neighbors in the Cloquet area!

We’ll celebrate the power of our voices, encourage **early voting**, and help each other make a plan to vote. Get the information you need to cast your ballot, learn about ways to encourage your friends and family to vote, and connect with other people who care about our community.

There will be **music, singing, movement, and plenty of opportunities to celebrate together**. Bring your friends, bring your family, and bring your enthusiasm!

Whether you’re already ready to vote or still figuring out your plan, **everyone is welcome.**

**Come celebrate our community, make your voting plan, and help get your neighbors ready to vote!**

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Virtual Phone Bank for Karen Bass for Mayor!
events.description:
Join us every Tuesday and Thursday evening for a virtual phone bank where we’ll call Los Angeles voters to talk about why this election matters for them, their community and our collective future.

No experience needed!  You can join from anywhere (even outside of LA), as long as you’ve got a computer, internet connection and a headset or earbuds. You’ll get a quick training, a call script, and a list of numbers to work through. It’s a high-impact way to help: every conversation moves a real voter closer to the polls in support of Karen Bass.

What to expect:

	•	Weekly shifts, Tuesday and Thursday evenings
	•	Brief training and script walkthrough at the start of each shift
	•	Calls made through our online dialer, no special equipment beyond your computer and headset
	•	Campaign staff or skilled volunteers on hand the whole time to answer questions
	•	Join from anywhere: home, dorm, couch, wherever you’ve got wifi

What you need:

	•	A computer with internet access
	•	A headset (for clear calls and to keep your hands free)
	•	That’s it. We’ll teach you the rest

Every shift gets us closer to the votes we need. Sign up for a Tuesday or Thursday slot now, we’ll send the Zoom passcode and call tool access before your shift starts.

Questions? Feel free to reach out to us at saskia@karenbass.com or volunteer@karenbass.com

Quick note - for safety reasons, you are not allowed to make calls from your car while driving.

events.title: KNOW MEANS KNOW: How to Turn Out the Local Vote
events.description: MAGA is working hard to meddle in our local elections this year, including school board races where the fate of sex education is often decided. Their entire strategy relies on us staying home. Our best defense? Hitting the doors, picking up the phones, and talking to our friends and neighbors. Join Becca Litt, EducateUS DIrector of Organizing, and experienced field organizer Natalie Dunn to learn what actually works when turning out the vote for down-ballot races. We'll break down how to get over the dread of talking to strangers, how to have genuine conversations with prospective voters, and how to mobilize our communities through relational organizing to protect our country before Election Day.

events.title: TX Together Apartment Knocking in Houston!
events.description:
*Join us Saturday morning for an apartment outreach Field Lab!*

**We’re testing a new approach to community outreach, and we want volunteers to be part of it. Too often, traditional outreach reaches the same people over and over again while other voices get left out of the conversation. This Field Lab is about changing that.**

We’ll meet up Saturday morning, do a quick training, and then head to a nearby apartment community to connect with residents who may not typically hear from campaigns or community organizations and invite them to learn more about RALLY’s paid community engagement program.

No experience is necessary — we’ll provide a training, script, and everything you need before you get started.

Come ready to talk to some neighbors, try something new, and share your feedback afterward so we can make the program better!

events.title: Don't Boo...Vote! A Family-Friendly Ballot Prep Party

location.venue: Whitney M. Young Magnet High School

events.description:
Let’s take the ~spooky~ out of voting this Midterm Election!

**Join us for a fun, family-friendly evening to get ready for the 2026 Midterm Election.** Whether you’re a voting pro or haven’t thought much about the midterms yet, this is a chance to learn what’s on the ballot, get familiar with important voting dates and deadlines, and make a plan to vote.

**Bring your mail-in ballot if you have one** and fill it out in a supportive, low-pressure environment. We’ll also have resources on early voting, voting deadlines, and how to make sure you’re ready for Election Day.

**Kids can join in their own Halloween-themed mock election!** They’ll cast a ballot, visit a kid-friendly voting booth, drop their ballot in the ballot box, and get an “I Voted!” sticker. We’ll even count the votes and announce the winners!

_Plus: Halloween decorations, pizza, candy, crafts, and music!_

Voting shouldn’t be scary. Let’s get prepared, get our ballots ready, and make this election about creating change.

All are welcome!

**Join Indivisible Pajaro Valley for our new Get Out The Vote roadside rally!**

This event is modeled on the Signs of Fascism protests but is all about encouraging people to register and vote. Here's what to expect:

- The protest will last about an hour 
- Please dress colorfully (perhaps in red, white, and blue!) and wear comfortable shoes.
- We will stand spaced 10-15 feet apart by the side of the road, and each person will hold one sign.
- Our signs are in English on one side and in Spanish on the other side, so we will periodically switch languages all at the same time.
- This is not a somber protest the way Signs of Fascism is! When possible, we will have music. Feel free to bring a flag to wave, and to dance!

We will need a minimum of 15 people to have the most impact. We have 20 signs, so we can have up to 20 sign holders - but we will need a few additional folks to record, keep an eye out for any hazards or disruptions, and keep the sign-holders coordinated.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early The Woodlands TX

address_lines: Six Pines Drive & Lake Woodlands Drive

events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

Join your neighbors and friends from Greater Woodlands Indivisible to gather and publicize Voting Early to our local community.  Bring your own family-friendly signs encouraging Early Voting in Texas between Oct 19 - Oct 30.  Learn yourself about the Early Voting locations and times!  Bring weather-appropriate clothing and water.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Secure Storage, Safer Communities: Bucks County Safety Forum
events.description:
Secure storage = safer communities. 

Firearms are now the leading cause of death for children and teens in America, according to the American Academy of Pediatrics, and almost 1 in 10 American children live in a home with unsecured guns.

The best way to prevent accidental shootings is to keep all firearms secured, and together we can work to make Bucks County safer from gun violence. 

Join CeaseFirePA, Bucks County Sheriff Danny Ceisler, and community partners for a free forum on secure storage and preventing firearm tragedies at home and in school. Learn how secure firearm storage and other proven safety measures can help reduce the risk of school shootings, unintentional shootings, youth firearm suicide, and firearm theft. See secure storage options demonstrated and leave with practical steps you can take to help create safer homes, safer schools, and safer communities.

Whether you own firearms or not, everyone has a role to play in creating a safer Bucks County. You'll leave with practical information, free resources, and opportunities to take action to help protect the people you care about.

RSVP today and invite other parents, caregivers, educators, and community members to join this important conversation.

events.description:
*Join us Saturday morning for an apartment outreach Field Lab!*

**We’re testing a new approach to community outreach, and we want volunteers to be part of it. Too often, traditional outreach reaches the same people over and over again while other voices get left out of the conversation. This Field Lab is about changing that.**

We’ll meet up Saturday morning, do a quick training, and then head to a nearby apartment community to connect with residents who may not typically hear from campaigns or community organizations and invite them to learn more about RALLY’s paid community engagement program.

No experience is necessary — we’ll provide a training, script, and everything you need before you get started.

Come ready to talk to some neighbors, try something new, and share your feedback afterward so we can make the program better!

events.title: Weekday Door Knocking in Brighton!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!  Doors don't take a break during the week and neither do we - join us Tuesday through Friday to talk to voters.

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Butte Door Knocking
events.description:

We'll have a list of doors for you to knock, the script for your conversations, and a handy reference sheet on Sam's background and platform that you can carry with you. After everybody has knocked doors for a couple hours, we'll reconvene to debrief how it all went with some cold refreshments!

You do not need to have knocked a single door before this event - this is for beginners and experts alike! Talking in person with voters is one of the most effective and rewarding ways to spread the word about Sam, and we'll make sure you have the skills and tools to feel confident to get out there!

events.description:
Early Voting is around the corner. It's time to show some Solidarity!

Stand in solidarity with friends, neighbors, and community members on **October 10, for Solidarity Saturdays (11am-1pm)**. Together we are stronger!

We will gather on the sidewalk of the Nevada Legislative Building to raise our voices, uplift one another, and show that our community refuses to be silent in the face of abuses of power.

Bring your protest signs, your passion, and your commitment to defending democracy. Whether you’re a seasoned advocate or showing up for the first time, your presence matters. Let’s stand together. Let’s speak out. Let’s make our voices impossible to ignore.

🦺 PLEASE NOTE: Our rallies are nonviolent. When there are one or more aggressive counter protesters at our events, the best way to respond is to ignore and de-escalate. De-escalation includes staying calm, maintaining your distance, using a calm voice, and having a neutral stance. If you are concerned about your or someone else's safety, please go tell a security team member in a yellow vest. Remember, counter protestors are exercising their first amendment rights just as we are-- but we also don't want a situation to escalate or to lead to any violent behaviors. 

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

We will gather on the sidewalk of the Nevada Legislative Building to raise our voices, uplift one another, and show that our community refuses to be silent in the face of abuses of power.

Bring your protest signs, your passion, and your commitment to defending democracy. Whether you’re a seasoned advocate or showing up for the first time, your presence matters. Let’s stand together. Let’s speak out. Let’s make our voices impossible to ignore.

🦺 PLEASE NOTE: Our rallies are nonviolent. When there are one or more aggressive counter protesters at our events, the best way to respond is to ignore and de-escalate. De-escalation includes staying calm, maintaining your distance, using a calm voice, and having a neutral stance. If you are concerned about your or someone else's safety, please go tell a security team member in a yellow vest. Remember, counter protestors are exercising their first amendment rights just as we are-- but we also don't want a situation to escalate or to lead to any violent behaviors. 

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Knocking on Doors in Ferndale!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Georgia GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
GA Ossoff Weekly Phone Bank — Every Thursday

Join us as we call Georgia voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

Every week, we're reaching voters across Georgia to make sure they're ready to participate in one of the most competitive Senate races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide the outcome—we're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll help voters who have already requested mail ballots complete and return them on time, understand key deadlines, and make a clear, confident plan to vote, whether by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send follow-up texts with early voting, polling location, and absentee ballot tracking information to those planning to vote early or on Election Day.

Volunteers will have real conversations with voters and help turn intention into action—making sure ballots are returned and votes are counted.

📞 Weekly phone bank: Thursdays at 12p.m. PT / 3p.m. ET (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed—training, scripts, and support provided.

This is how we win close races, by making sure every vote counts.
Your call could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Georgia!

events.title: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Series: Intro to Abolitionist Feminisms Panel
events.description:
Hear from organizers and advocates in a conversation about abolitionist feminism, transformative justice, incarceration, and what it means to build movements rooted in collective liberation. This panel will connect the ideas explored throughout the series to the work happening in our communities today.
Panelists include Florida NOW members Sana Hafeez and Amaria Smith, as well as Miss Mei with Decrim305 and Hugo with Success Stories, the program featured in the film we are screening, The Feminist on Cell Block Y.
Stay after the panel for a brief Q&A chat. The panel will be recorded and uploaded to YouTube.

events.title: Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club Discussion: Abolition. Feminism. Now.
events.description:
Join the Florida NOW Anti-Racism Book Club for a discussion of Abolition. Feminism. Now. by Angela Y. Davis, Gina Dent, Erica R. Meiners, and Beth E. Richie.

n this groundbreaking book, four leading abolitionist feminist thinkers and organizers explore the history and present-day practice of abolition, drawing connections between struggles against prisons, policing, racism, gender-based violence, and economic injustice. The authors examine abolition not simply as an effort to dismantle systems of punishment, but as a project of building the social, political, and economic conditions that allow communities to thrive.

The book brings together decades of feminist organizing, scholarship, and movement-building to ask what it means to imagine a world beyond punishment, and how we begin creating that world now.

Join us for a conversation about the book’s central ideas, the movements and histories it explores, and what abolitionist feminism can teach us about building a more just and liberatory future.

Monday, December 21st, at 6:30 PM on Zoom

All are welcome, whether you’ve finished the book, are still reading, or are joining the conversation to learn more.

Saturday, October 17, 2026

Immigrants, women, LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, workers, students, protesters, and vulnerable communities are facing attacks on their rights and protections. These are not isolated actions. Together, they threaten our democracy, our freedoms, and our communities.

events.title: Young People's Hearing on Sex Ed in Alabama
events.description:
Join us in Birmingham for a Young People's Hearing on Sex Ed in Alabama! This year Alabama Senate Bill 209 to mandate Abstinence Only Until Marriage Curriculum in all K-12 public schools and removing ANY sex ed from being taught K-4 passed. We, our young people, and our organizational partners mounted a 3-year legislative fight against this bill and it will go into effect on October 1, 2026. 

We will commune over dinner provided by URGE and start with a quick policy training on how to hold your state legislators accountable to the way they voted on this bill AND we'll have postcards right there :)  

The goal of this event goes beyond just legislative advocacy and is to create a safe space for our young 18-30 yo BIPOC LGBTQ+ member base to come together and hold their own People's Hearing on sex education in Alabama and share how it has shaped/does shape their lives. We'll close out with a relational organizing training by our State Organizer to discuss how we take the power we built back into our communities. 

For admission to the event, we are asking folks to bring menstrual products to support Yellowhammer Fund's community care work. No one will be turned away if they don't have a donation. 
Preferred products are Honey Pot pads & wipes, Playtex, U by Kotex, Cora, L. organic tampons, Monthly period panties.

To keep our community safe, you MUST register to attend this event, and we will close registration 24 hours before the event.

This event is a collaboration between URGE Alabama, Yellowhammer Fund, & the Alabama Youth Activist Alliance in the Alabama Reproductive Health, Rights, & Justice Coalition

events.title: Beyond the Ballot #3: Building Relationships with Legislators
events.description:
**The worst time to introduce yourself to your elected official may be when you desperately need their vote.**

Effective advocacy doesn’t begin with an urgent email. It begins with relationship.

**_Building Relationships with Legislators_** will show you how to move beyond one-time asks and begin building authentic, strategic relationships with the people elected to represent you.

How do you introduce yourself? What do you say when you don’t need anything? How do you handle disagreement? What makes a legislator remember you? And how do you become someone whose perspective matters when an important decision reaches their desk?

We won’t just talk about it. You’ll practice it. Through realistic scenarios, you’ll build confidence communicating with elected officials and learn what to do before, during, and after the conversation.

If contacting a legislator makes you nervous, come. If you’ve done it before but want to become more effective, come. If your congregation wants a stronger public voice, come.

This is Workshop 3 of **_Beyond the Ballot_**. We’ve moved from voting to advocacy. Now we’re building the relationships that make advocacy stronger. Next, we’ll learn how to bring one of your most powerful tools into those relationships: your story.

You don’t need special access. You are a constituent. That is your invitation.

Now learn how to use it.
events.accessibility_notes: ## Please use the Zoom link to join.

events.title: Beyond the Ballot #4: Storytelling for Change
events.description:
What if the story you almost decided wasn’t important enough to tell is _exactly_ the story someone needs to hear?

**Facts tell us how big a problem is. Stories show us who is living inside it.**

Behind every policy debate is a human experience: a parent struggling to find childcare, a teacher watching a student fall through the cracks, a young person wondering whether adults are listening, a family trying to stay housed.

Your experience may carry more power than you realize.

**_Storytelling for Change_** will help you turn lived experience into a story that can move hearts, illuminate an issue, and inspire action.

And you won’t just learn about storytelling. You’ll begin building a story you can actually use with an elected official, in your congregation, at a community meeting, or anywhere your voice could help move someone from understanding an issue to caring enough to act.

You don’t need to be a public speaker. You don’t need a dramatic story. And you don’t need to “perform.”

You already have a story. Come learn how to make it move.

This is Workshop 4 of Beyond the Ballot, and we are almost at the culmination. We’ve explored voting, advocacy, and relationships. Now we add story.

Then, in Workshop 5, we bring it all together.

Don’t stop one conversation short.

#### Beyond the Ballot
A non-partisan 5-part virtual workshop series equipping faith communities and everyday people to lead with purpose before, during, and long after Election Day.

events.description:
**What if we stopped trying to change the world alone?**

One person can vote. One person can call a legislator. One person can tell a powerful story, but lasting change takes all of us.

**_Building Beloved Community_** is where the entire **_Beyond the Ballot_** journey comes together. And after four virtual workshops, we’re gathering **IN PERSON**.

We’re going to practice building community. Across generations, faith traditions, race, culture, experience, and difference.

You’ll meet people you may never otherwise encounter, explore what builds trust and collective power, discover the gifts and influence already present in the room, and ask one big question:

**What could we accomplish if we stopped working separately and started working together? ****

If you joined us for the first four workshops, do not stop now. This is where the journey has been leading.

If this is your first one, come anyway. There is room for you here.

Children and families are facing challenges too big for isolated people, congregations, and organizations to solve alone.

**We need each other.**

This isn’t just the end of a workshop series. It’s the beginning of what comes next.

**Somebody has to build the community we keep saying we want. Why not us? Why not now?**

#### Beyond the Ballot
A non-partisan 5-part virtual workshop series equipping faith communities and everyday people to lead with purpose before, during, and long after Election Day.

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching a canvass in Athens, GA (https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

- Knock on **every door** in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather rich insights for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Gainesville & Alachua County, Florida!
events.description:
50501 GNV & No Kings GNV Coalition are hosting the next No Kings: Vote Early rally on Oct. 17th at Cora Roberson Park. 

The deadline to register to vote in Florida is Oct. 5th. Leading up to the event we are focusing on sharing voter registration information and once the deadline passes, we will focus on updating voter information and making a plan to vote early for you and your social circles. 

Sign up now for updates!
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Get Out the Vote to Elect Jeff Warren for State Representative - First Wave
events.description:
The Democratic majority in Harrisburg is fragile, relying on members who represent districts Donald Trump won by an average of 25% in 2024. Here in the heart of Northampton County, we have the key to creating a sustainable Democratic majority. House District 137 which encompasses Bethlehem Township, the Nazareth area, Palmer Township, Tatamy and part of Hanover, is held by Republican Joe Emrick. This district was a tie in 2024 and has been the most contested seat statewide in both 2022 and 2024.

Emrick has supported every abortion ban ever placed in front of him, backed Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election and voted against protecting residents from electricity price surges caused by data centers. Jeff will protect reproductive rights, mail-in voting and stand up for everyday Americans against price-gouging corporations and big money interests.

To win this campaign in the final hours, and secure Democratic control of the State House of Representatives, we need committed volunteers to help us reach out to every Democrat in the 137th district and help them make a plan to vote!

events.title: Volunteer as a Nonpartisan Election Challenger in MI!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Sign up here for an **in-person challenger shift** at an early voting site or Election Day polling place! 
 
As our eyes and ears on the ground, nonpartisan challengers are stationed at polling places, early voting sites, and absentee counting boards across Michigan to monitor the election process. Challengers must be registered to vote in Michigan and receive a credential from PTVF. Challengers have the right to challenge the actions of poll workers if the challenger believes that the poll worker is not following the law. Our pro-voter challengers make sure eligible voters can cast their ballots, free from interference and voter intimidation.  

Before your shift, you must complete our virtual, on-demand training. The training will be available starting in October. After you complete the training, we will send you your challenger credential and official shift assignment via email.

events.title: Indivisible Yolo Protect the Results Team Meeting
events.description: The best way to fight the regime’s massive voter suppression efforts is to have a turnout that is TOO BIG TO RIG. A close race opens the results up to scrutiny, recounts and scepticism which can boost false claims of election rigging. For that reason, we need a massive turnout so the results are irrefutable. And we need to take action to protect the results.  Indivisible Yolo's Protect the Results team will introduce volunteers to opportunities that will help voters vote and have their vote counted.  Options include poll observing, serving on voter hotlines, and "curing" ballots that are rejected for lack of a signature or a signature mismatch.  The team will meet weekly until the election to coordinate our work, discuss how our volunteer work is going and explore other options to help.

events.title: Get Out the Vote with Denise Powell and Christy Knorr
events.description:
# Knock doors with Denise Powell and Christy Knorr!

Christy Knorr is a hospice nurse and community advocate who has spent her entire life standing with people in their hardest moments. As a longtime Omaha neighbor, she knows firsthand what working families are up against: the rising cost of basics, the struggle to access care, and systems that too often leave people behind.

Now running for Nebraska's 12th Legislative District, Christy is driven by the same values that have guided her entire life, and a belief that every family deserves support to thrive, not just survive.

Denise Powell is a mom, small business owner, former corporate executive, public school champion, and healthcare advocate who knows that a strong work ethic and a love of family and community are the Nebraska way of life. She also knows the Good Life is getting harder to come by. After Trump’s election in 2016, she founded an organization that has supported hundreds of Nebraskans running for local office, protected our public schools and the families they serve, and helped stop extremists from passing abortion bans in the state.

Join us in getting out the vote for these two amazing candidates!

## What to bring:

- Charged Phone
- Water
- A positive attitude!

## What we will do:

- Knock on our neighbors doors and talk to them about the upcoming election!

events.title: Weekly Doorknocking with No Hate in WA State in Whatcom

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
What to expect

New to canvassing? That’s completely okay! No experience is required, and we’ll start every shift with a short training so everyone feels prepared before heading to the doors.

We’ll meet together at the Community First Whatcom office, go over the basics of the conversation, show everyone how to record who they spoke with at the door, and get paired up before heading out to canvass in the community.

For your first shift, you can shadow an experienced canvasser so you can hear how they talk with folks at the door and get comfortable before jumping into conversations yourself.

Most of the shift will be spent walking through a neighborhood and having short conversations with voters. You do not need to memorize a script or be an expert. We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need.

Please bring:

A fully charged smartphone
Comfortable walking shoes
Weather-appropriate clothing
Water and anything else you may need while walking

Additional details, resources, talking points, MiniVAN instructions, and arrival information will be sent after signup so you have everything you need to feel prepared for your shift.

Why door knocking matters

Most of us have had an election where the ballot showed up and we realized we hadn’t researched everything on it yet, or where voting almost slipped our minds altogether. One of the most effective ways to help people participate is simply reaching them before their ballot arrives, having a one-on-one conversation, and making sure they know what is on the ballot and why it matters.

Those conversations can make a real difference. Here in Whatcom County, the 2026 primary for the 42nd Legislative District Senate race came down to just four votes between two candidates.

If knocking on doors sounds intimidating, know that canvassing is typically a really positive experience. We’ll be reaching out to voters who regularly participate in elections and having short, friendly conversations with people in our community. You’ll also be out there alongside other volunteers, not doing it alone.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.title: TTU Tabling
events.description:
Are you serious about turning the tide in Texas? Are you tired of sitting on the sidelines and ready to make a difference? If you answered yes, then you have come to the right place!

You must complete a Zoom volunteer training for Reach App and Events if this is your first time working with Powered by People. This is a recorded training you can do at your own time Pre-Recorded Field Volunteer Training (Self-Paced))*

https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/ 
Live Training: https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/884993/

To register voters at this event, you must be a current 2025/2026 certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar in at least LUBBOCK COUNTY. Click here to sign up for VDR training (https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

NON-VDR VOLUNTEERS WELCOME TO ASSIST WITH REGISTRATION CHECKS You will help us make sure all registered voters are still active or if they need an update. You will also stay in contact with the voter until election day.

events.title: JDCA Michigan & Wisconsin Sunday Phone Bank
events.description:
UPDATED SCHEDULE:

10/11 - Jocelyn Benson for Michigan Governor

10/18 - David Crowley for Wisconsin Governor

10/25 - Jocelyn Benson for Michigan Governor

11/1 - David Crowley for Wisconsin Governor


Join JDCA every Sunday afternoon to call voters in Michigan & Wisconsin.

We will be talking to Jewish Democrats and independents about the importance of the 2026 midterms and why we should all support JDCA-endorsed candidates up and down the ballot.

Never made calls before? No problem! Whether you are a seasoned veteran or making calls for the first time, all you'll need is your computer and a phone. A short training will be provided at the beginning of each phone bank shift, and we also provide a script, talking points, and live support throughout the entire Zoom call. No experience required!

events.description:
Early voting will officially begin in Purcellville on October 18 and continues every day through October 31. We need volunteers like YOU to help us maintain a presence outside the Senior Center, hand out sample ballots to voters who need them, and talk with voters about the three Constitutional Amendments on the ballot. Sign up for two or three shifts between now and Election Day to Keep Loudoun Blue!

Thank you for participating in your democracy.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Eau Claire, Wisconsin
events.description:
**Join us at Owen Park on October 17th at 11:00 AM to protect our vote.**   

**No Kings 4 is a different fight.** This time it's not just about who shows up to march, it's about who shows up to vote. The national goal for this No Kings Rally is turnout for massive Election Action. Our goal is the largest Early Vote turnout in American history. Votes in numbers too large to manipulate.

**Harry Dunn gets us started in Eau Claire** on October 15, talking about what it takes to stand strong for democracy right now. Then, on Saturday, October 17, for **No Kings 4 Vote Early** itself, we bring it home:  **one brand-new march — straight to the Downtown Ballot Dropbox.** Then, we'll return to Owen Park to celebrate our community.  

We will have music, Hometown Heroes games for the kids, tabling to help neighbors get registered and vote, and local restaurants pitching in to welcome the community after the event! 

**Weather** is always a challenge in October so, remember, there's no such thing as bad weather, just bad clothing choices. Dress for the event because nothing is going to stop our early vote!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Impeach! Convict! Remove! [BEVERLY MA] 50501 Rally + Standout
events.description:
Remove the Regime is THE PLAN. The times call for direct action, and that's what people want. Protests with demands. Protests in front of those in power. Protests that disrupt. It's necessary that organizations who have the eyes and ears of the people start moving into direct action. 

Join Us at No Kings: Impeach! Convict! Remove! 10-17-2026 Odell Veterans Memorial Park, Beverly Massachusetts 

Please join us for our local standout and rally. You know the drill: we need safety marshals, first amendment spaces, safe marching routes, planning meetings, permits, speakers, music. We've already done this and you and your friends know what to do. This time we're demanding impeachment, conviction, and removal. Will it be difficult? Yes. Will we have to ask multiple times? Probably. Will it require all of us marching in the streets and then to the polls? Absolutely. Should we give up because it's hard? Never.

We're not asking you to start at the finish line. We are asking you to start this journey with us. Two more years is too many. Americans are dying. Democracy is eroding. We will demand a vote on impeachment from our reps, and a promise to impeach from our candidates. And conviction. And removal. This year, impeachment is on THE BALLOT!

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Bring Signs and Your Friends!! Sign Messages Recommended: Hands Off Our Votes, No Kings, Trump Must Go Now

This letter explains the case for impeachment: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dYTMsDQWOaS2N1jRFofa02D0V-4VnCkt/edit

In preparation for Oct 17, please support Flare USA by asking your community to send emails to your reps demanding impeachment here: https://edos.flareusa.org/ Please have them send these by Oct 7.

Join ECU for weekly **virtual** phone banks to help get out the vote for battleground candidates this November.

ECU will host biweekly virtual phone banks to support candidates running tight races in competitive districts across the country. **The first step in taking back the house is talking to voters!**

No experience necessary. We will provide a quick training with everything you need to know, including our script, dialer tools, and how to log your calls, and still have plenty of time for questions. You can join this virtual phone bank from the comfort of your own home, all you need is your cell phone and a computer/tablet. 

If the start time doesn't work for your schedule, feel free to drop in late! Training is available throughout the phone bank, and we will make sure you are ready to go before you make your first call.

Every voter we talk to brings us one step closer to victory. Sign up today, and let's get to work!

events.title: Hop on the Bus! Canvass for Villegas to Flip the House (Porterville): CD-22
events.description:
Sign up to knock doors in the Central Valley!  This is a special canvass as you can Hop on the Canvassing Lux Bus and ride in comfort there and back.  You leave Sat Oct 10th at 7AM and return Sun Oct 11th by 7PM.

You’ll be helping to build the grassroots power Democrats need to win in 2026 and to defend democracy long term.  Help Flip the House in 2026.  Get Randy Villegas elected!

Our Santa Clara County Democratic Party (SCCDP) team in partnership with Bay Area Coalition(BAC) and the Democratic Volunteer Center(DVC) will be heading to Porterville to Canvass for the Democrat candidate to help them win the House Seat for CD-22.  Why CD-22?  This district is in the top 7 nationwide seats that are flippable.  We will likely not win the House without winning in CD-22.  Will Porterville?  Porterville has a critical 5000 doors that need to be knocked to win this election.  Why Oct 9th-11th?  The ballots will have just been received in the mail.  You can help make this happen!

From the Bay Area, this canvass will be a two day and one night canvass.  You hop on the bus at 7AM Sat Oct 10th at the Democratic Volunteer Center (DVC) in Mountain View.  Training will be provided on the bus.  You will arrive ready to canvass in Porterville at 11AM.  Local drivers will be standing by to take you to your canvassing turf.   A dinner will be coordinated for all the canvasser.  Canvassers will make their own hotel reservation with the assistance our the canvassing concierge.  Sun morning we will canvass from 9:30AM-2:30PM then return on the bus and be back in Mountain View by 7PM.  $75/day ($150/trip total) stipends are available for lodging and food.

In the week before the canvass, you will receive an email and a phone call from the SCCDP/BAC volunteer canvass team with all the details about your canvass.   They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

If you've never canvassed before or just need a refresher, join the Bay Area Coalition canvassing workshop every Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

If you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early 650 Merchant Street, Vacaville, California
events.description:
We are joining No Kings Vote Early Visibility.  
This a peaceful event. Bring your signs to wave to get the message out to all that drive by. Don't engage with agitators. Don't take the bait! Stay focused on the message. Bring your Get Out the Vote signs, Vote Early.
Please do not jay walk. Do not engage with agitators. Don't take the bait! Stay focused on why we are here. Be loud & joyous! 
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Canvass for Virginia Democrats in Madison County!
events.description:
We're counting down less than 60 days till Election Day — and the road to            re-electing Senator Mark Warner and Congressman Eugene Vindman, plus Democrats up and down the ballot, runs right through Madison County.

This November's stakes are too high to sit on the sidelines. We're launching weekly canvasses right here in Madison County — running every weekend all the way through the weekend before Election Day. This is how we build the grassroots power it takes to win: door by door, conversation by conversation.

Whether you've canvassed a hundred times or never knocked a door in your life, this event is for you:

🗣️ Full training provided — no experience needed
📋 Updated talking points for veteran volunteers
🤝 A chance to stand with fellow Democrats every week as we head into the final stretch

Come once, come every week — whatever you can give. Bring a friend or neighbor along, and let's keep the momentum building weekend after weekend.

Address provided after signup.

Every door counts. Every conversation counts. 
Let's make Madison County a model for what sustained grassroots power looks like — sign up for this weekend (and mark your calendar for the next)!

events.description:
NOTE THE TIME CHANGE!

Interfaith Prayer Meeting for Peace is a collaboration of people of faith. We are upset enough about this administration’s assault on human dignity and life, and about ruthless corporate war profiteering, that we have banded together to call on aid from the Divine. We meet monthly in the shadow of the largest weapons manufacturer on the globe, and across the street from the largest luxury mall in the nation, to pray and bear witness that a better world is possible. 

This month, our meeting will be held in conjunction with a Peace, Justice, Sustainability NOW action. PJSN is also committed to peaceful, legal, nonviolent protest on this day. We will be doing a 20-minute prayer vigil to open the event and hope that you will bring your voice and your spiritual practice to enrich us!

As people of faith and conscience committed to peaceful, legal, prayerful presence, we agree to the following:

We agree to respect “that of God in every person” and refrain from hostile language and insults.

We agree to leave room for repentance in those with whom we disagree and to oppose violence, not people.

We agree to trust the Divine to bring about peace, shalom and wholeness in our world.

We agree to follow all legal instructions from law enforcement. 

We agree to quickly cooperate with peacekeeper and Meeting facilitator directions that are for our safety.

As an interfaith gathering, we agree to exercise freedom of expression and respect the freedom of expression of others. If you have a prayer, reading, song, or other activity, it will represent your faith and conscience with integrity. If someone else’s sharing does not align with your faith and conscience, you are free to abstain from participating during that moment.
events.accessibility_notes: This is an outdoor event on a slight slope. Please bring seating if you will not be able to stand for an hour.

We just had our 75th consecutive weekly gathering on May 23: we emphasize inclusivity for all, with extra effort made to enhance the opportunity for seniors and people with limited mobility to participate. events.title: Team Lori Phone Banking (In-Person)
events.description:
## Phone Bank for Lori Childs
Join Team Lori at the Marshfield campaign office every Thursday between now and Election Day to call voters and help elect Lori Childs.

Whether you’re an experienced caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll provide a quick training, a script, and support throughout the shift. 

Every conversation helps us share Lori’s message, identify supporters, and make sure voters have the information they need to vote.

Please bring a charged cell phone. If you have a laptop or tablet, bring that too—some people find it easier to have one device to look at and another device to make calls from. If not, no problem: we can make it work with your cellular device.

Prefer to call from home? We also host virtual phone banks on Zoom every Wednesday. You’ll receive the same training, materials, and support while making calls from the comfort of your own home.

Sign up for a shift, bring a friend, and help us build the people-powered campaign Lori needs to win.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early, 1305 Gause Blvd, Slidell, LA
events.description:
Join us for a honk and wave for early voting and election day turnout in our Slidell community. This is a non-partisan and joyful event of our democratic participation in using our voices at the polls. We the people choose our leaders!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

## Ready to turn the tide in CD35?

Join Johnny and the team as we call voters in Bexar County and ensure everyone gets to the polls in November!

## What to Expect

This phonebank is for anyone who is interested in having conversations with voters. 

#### Everyone is welcome!

New volunteers will get plenty of support to get up to speed alongside experienced volunteers. 

## Event Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact phonebank, we ask all volunteers (virtual or in-person) to arrive by 6:30pm (location provided upon RSVP).  

[6:30pm-7pm]: Quick orientation where we will review the program and do a quick refresher on Dialer.

[7pm -8:30pm]: We will call voters using Scale to Win Dialer, ask them about their issues, and talk to them about Johnny.

[8:30pm-9pm]: Debrief and pack up. We will review the day's numbers, talk about what went well and what we can improve, and celebrate our success!

events.title: YOUTH SUMMIT

location.venue: Queens College, City University of New York

events.description:
Young people have something to say about the future of immigration policy—and we’re ready to listen.

Join us for the Youth Talk Democracy Youth Summit, where 13 middle and high school students will present four original immigration policy proposals developed through six weeks of workshops, research and community action projects.

These proposals reflect the students’ own vision for addressing immigration issues locally. At the summit, you’ll hear directly from the young people who created them and learn how we can help advocate for their ideas throughout the school year.

Come support youth leadership, participate in the conversation and see what happens when young people are given the knowledge, tools and opportunity to make their voices heard.

Youth Talk Democracy is an extension of Let’s Talk Democracy, a grassroots organization dedicated to educating people about our government, encouraging dialogue about the foundations of our democracy and empowering citizens to make their voices heard.

We encourage you to fill out our Google Form in addition to RSVPing here. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/13pMkF35Lm61ZEL64x-_LCNtvQ1ztg6v9K79BDGBkb_Y/viewform?edit_requested=true

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Rally  -- Reston/Foxmill, VA
events.description:
Voting early is the best way we individually have to protect the election -- the more ballots "banked" the less impact the regime's shenanigans will have on election day.  
Defend Democracy Indivisible invites you to rally with us Saturday afternoon to remind people that voting is underway here in Virginia; polls are open Monday at the North County Gov. Center; to remind people not only to vote but to bring friends and neighbors.

For the rally, bring, signs, banners, or just yourself; funny costumes are always welcome! There is room for chairs.  And if you want, we will have special markers for car windows, to decorate with whatever slogan you want and then we can drive out of the parking lot together (or not).  

NOKINGS Says:

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Volunteer at the Polls on Election Day
events.description:
Help us cover every polling location on Election Day! Volunteers are needed to help pass out the Official Democratic Slate outside the polls on November 3rd.

Passing out the blue slate at the polls on Election Day is the single most impactful thing you can do to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot. Our judges do not have partisan affiliation on the ballot, and passing the blue slate helps ensure that Democrats know who to vote for.

The polls are open from 6:30 am - 7:30 pm. Are you able to cover a polling location all day? If you can, sign up for all 4 shifts.

Only able to help a part of the day? Sign up for the shift(s) that work best for you.

After you sign up, you will be contacted by a volunteer or staffer from HCDP to schedule you for a specific polling location. The outreach will not be immediate. Please include your phone number when you RSVP so we can call you. We ask that you be as flexible as possible with the location so we can cover as many of our polls as possible.

Note: If you are a precinct executive, you do not need to sign up here. Instead, reach out to your Ward or District Chair, or if you don't have their contact information, email HCDP's Executive Director Zophia Pittman at zophia@hamiltoncountydems.org.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Alameda, CA

location.venue: Alameda City Hall (pre-rally at Chochenyo Park 10a-12:15p)

events.description:
**Democracy and our right to vote do not defend themselves. So, WE MUST!**

Join [Indivisible Alameda](https://indivisible-alameda.org/)’s No Kings, as part of a necessary national surge to defend democracy, our right to vote, and the unabated swearing in of our duly elected representatives. Your participation will give courage to others to fight for our democracy and will show the administration and the people of this country (and the world) that we are standing strong. 

**On October 17th, we say, “No more Faux-King BS!”**

No Kings (IV) is a clarion call, the last stress-test of our community muscle pushing against tyranny. No Kings was never about only holding signs, marching and rallying, then going home. This endeavor has been you, me and all pro-democracy groups actively prepping for the worst case scenario; this administration’s all out assault on the voice of the people and our power to vote for our leaders. 

Showing up and speaking out on Saturday, October 17th is only a part of what is needed. We are going to ask more of you than ever before, because it’s absolutely necessary. We are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

More information will be emailed to registered attendees as we get closer to [Indivisible Alameda](https://indivisible-alameda.org/)’s No Kings which will include a family-friendly pre-rally event. Register to receive these updates.

**See you at Alameda City Hall on October 17th!**

The Indivisible Alameda Team

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*
events.accessibility_notes: This event location is the public plaza in front of Alameda City Hall. There will be food donation bins across the street. The plaza is a flat, paved area. There are a few benches at the location, but if you cannot stand for the duration of your time at the event, you are welcome to bring a lawn chair or camp chair. Just make sure to set your chair up in an area off to the side, not in the middle, for safety reasons. There is an adjacent bus stop, but will likely be closed during the hours around the event. The closest bathroom facilities are located at the Alameda Free Library at 1550 Oak St (a block away on an adjacent street). Parking will be sparse. Please use ride-sharing or public transit.

events.title: Save Our Democracy - Central Westchester Indivisible
events.description:
#### Central Westchester Indivisible (CWI) is part of a nationwide group of Indivisible chapters and many other organizations fighting to protect our rights and to stop and reverse the Trump administration’s damage to society. Thank you for being a part of that fight!

#### These protests are intended to show our sustained opposition to the many ways the Trump administration is trying to destroy our democracy and bring our country down.  People are welcome to protest about any of the heinous acts this administration is guilty of, including:
- Attacks on the Press, such as the FCC's threats to revoke ABC affiliate licenses. 

- The illegal war with Iran, which has devolved into a perpetual series of tit-for-tat strikes and counter strikes.

- Lawless ICE/CBP.  We demand that funding be stopped until they are completely reformed with the kind of accountability we expect from real law enforcement.

- Illegal tariffs that raise inflation while dragging down our economy and damaging relations with countries that have always been close allies.

- The Save Act, gerrymandering and other threats to our elections.

We are asking people to line the sidewalk in front of Richard Presser Park in Hartsdale, NY for a peaceful, nonviolent protest. Bring a sign (a folding chair if you want). Bring the kids, bring friends.

A note about parking – there is a parking lot in the park on Central Park Avenue at the south end of the park. Also, NO metal or wood poles – please.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Voter Assistance Hotline Training
events.description:
The statewide voter assistance hotline program helps ensure that every eligible New Hampshire voter has the proper information and opportunity to vote. The Hotline is a publicly advertised phone number that voters can call with questions.

Volunteers on the hotline assist voters across the state who call into our hotline with voting- and election-related questions.

In this training we will go over the basics NH Election Law, Frequently Asked Questions, and an overview of the call system. After the training volunteers can sign up for hotline shifts that work with their schedule.

events.title: Whitefish Door Knocking
events.description:
Nothing beats talking to a voter on their doorstep about Sam! Join Sam's Crew for a day of knocking doors around Whitefish. We'll meet at Baker Park, where we'll train you on how to knock doors for Sam and you'll get a chance to practice before you head out.

We'll have a list of doors for you to knock, the script for your conversations, and a handy reference sheet on Sam's background and platform that you can carry with you. After everybody has knocked doors for a couple hours, we'll reconvene to debrief how it all went!

You do not need to have knocked a single door before this event - this is for beginners and experts alike! Talking in person with voters is one of the most effective and rewarding ways to spread the word about Sam, and we'll make sure you have the skills and tools to feel confident to get out there!

events.title: Navigate Ballot Propositions with Pete Stahl on Oct. 11 with the Democratic Volunteer Center (DVC)

location.venue: DVC Headquarters (former REI store in Charleston Plaza in Mountain View)

events.description:
Puzzling over the ballot propositions? Not sure what they really mean? 
**Pete Stahl** has been helping voters navigate the confusing terrain of ballot props for 46 years. He digs into the details, so you don’t have to! 
Pete will provide the backstory on how each proposition got on the ballot. He will explain the implications of a yes or no vote and cut through the extreme claims and campaign rhetoric. 

Join us on **Oct. 11 at the DVC Headquarters in Mountain View, CA** to get your questions answered before you vote. 

Pete is the brains behind the eponymous “Pete Rates the Propositions” website (https://peterates.com), visited by tens of thousands of users every election cycle. He is non-partisan and unaffiliated with any candidate or organization.

We’d appreciate your RSVP so we can plan accordingly. And please share this with like-minded friends!

*Please note that this event may be photographed and/or video or audio recorded. By your attendance at this event, you agree that any image, audio or video recording of you may be used by the Democratic Volunteer Center (DVC) for use in its promotional materials.*

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Wisconsin
events.description:
**He Held the Line on January 6th.   
Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.**  

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

**Date:** Thursday, October 15th  
**Time:** 9:30 a.m.    
**Location:** Pablo Center, 128 Graham Avenue, Eau Claire, WI 54701   

Harry Dunn is joining citizens of the Chippewa Valley for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. Who just welcomed "Stop the Steal" organizer Scott Presler to campaign for them at our own Eau Claire GOP headquarters. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.  

**Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.**  

This event kicks off our **No Kings: Vote Early** weekend — three days of action in to protect this election and get Wisconsin voting early, building to the national Day of Election Action on October 17th.  

**Come have coffee and bagels with Harry!**   
This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.  Be ready to:  

- Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection  
- Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard  
- Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it  

Time and location to be confirmed — RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

events.title: Chapel Hill / Carrboro March to the Polls
events.description:
Chapel Hill - Carrboro March to the Polls! There are four locations on two days!!

PLEASE SIGN UP on our website to choose your date and route! https://bit.ly/4gZNGxq

Join us on either Thursday, Oct 15 at 4:30 pm (the first day of early voting!) and/or Saturday, Oct 17 at 10:00 am to inspire and empower people to exercise their right to vote, support civics education, and promote early voting in Orange County.

We're coordinating four simultaneous, family-friendly marches along public sidewalks on each date. Each march route will end at one of the four early voting polling sites in Chapel Hill/Carrboro (Chapel Hill Public Library, Seymour Center, Chapel of the Cross, and Drakeford Library in Carrboro), where eligible folks can register and/or vote. The march routes are all about .8 miles and should take people between 20 and 40 minutes to complete. 

We're encouraging participants to bring non-partisan (no candidates' names or parties) signs that raise awareness about early voting sites and dates. 

We will host a sign-making event on Saturday, Oct 10 from 9:30-11:30 am: 

https://mobilize.us/s/aMpVHT.

For more info and to check out the routes, please see our website at 

https://bit.ly/4gZNGxq

These events are being organized by the local demonstration group Franklin & Elliott, and are supported by Engaged Defenders 4 Democracy, Indivisible Orange County NC, The Community Church of Chapel Hill, United Church of Chapel Hill, and the Church of Reconciliation.
This local effort aligns with the Repairers of the Breach Coalition’s nationwide campaign: March. Educate. Vote.

events.title: Day of Action for EARLY VOTING 10/15-31: Phone Bank with Team Davis
events.description:
What we're doing:
Every conversation matters, even the ones that happen one phone call at a time. We're gathering on Tuesdays and Thursdays in-person, or Wednesdays virtually, to call Democratic and unaffiliated voters across NC-01 to listen to what's on their minds and earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again; What was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, and it will come down to who shows up and has the best conversations, whether at the door or on the phone.

We're not just asking for votes. We're listening first to what voters and their families care about, what's worrying them, and what they need from their next Representative. Then we're asking for their support, and making sure every single one of them knows: early voting runs October 15th–31st, and Election Day is November 3rd.

Why your help is essential:
You don't need a car, comfortable shoes, or even to leave your couch: just your voice and a little time. Phone banking lets us reach voters who might never answer the door, and every call you make is one more NC-01 neighbor who hears directly from our campaign instead of an ad.

The ask:
Join us in-person or virtually to make calls using our auto-dialer. Use the script as your guide, listen more than you talk, and invite voters to make a plan to vote early or on Election Day. 
No experience necessary, we'll train you, and our team will be with you the whole time.

What you'll receive:
Auto-dialer access
Call script
Zoom link for live training and support during your shift

*In-person Phone banking: please bring your fully charged tablet/laptop with you, along with your fully charged mobile device. 

Tuesdays and Thursdays will also offer an in-person session at Craven County Democratic HQ: 1232 S Glenburnie Rd, New Bern, NC 28562

Wednesdays will only be virtual sessions using the copied Zoom link.

events.title: Hands Off Our Vote! Protest - Indivisible Yolo
events.description:
In America, the right of citizens to vote and to have their vote counted is fundamental! We are a nation where the law rules--not a self-proclaimed king. "Hands Off Our Vote" are Yolo County Days of Action to stand up for the rule of law and the right of the people to elect principled leaders who will represent their interests--not those of the billionaires. 

On numerous Wednesdays leading up to the election, we're showing up in Davis at the corner of 5th and B Streets (in front of City Hall) from 4:30-5:30. Bring your signs and your voices! We will remind everyone to vote early and use ballot boxes! 

The President has made it clear that he will do anything to prevent the fair midterm elections that will undoubtedly serve as a rejection of his failed policies! He has gutted federal agencies whose mission was to protect the rights of the people to vote. He has even instructed the U.S. Postal Service to interfere in the election by refusing to mail state ballots to voters and by changing the age old practice of same-day postmarking. His masked, armed forces have indicated that they might show up to polling places under the pretense of enforcing immigration laws, but with the clear intent of discouraging voter participation. We need to be clear, the people will prevail! 

As a reminder, a core principle behind "Hands Off Our Vote" events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.
