events.title: Haz Llamadas por Dan Osborn!
events.description:
Dan Osborn se enfrenta al multimillonario Pete Ricketts y necesita nuestra ayuda para ganar. ¡Únete a nosotros para conectar con los votantes de Nebraska y fortalecer el movimiento!

Prepara tu bebida caliente favorita, ponte tu pijama más cómodo y conéctate con nosotros a través de Zoom. Comenzaremos con una breve capacitación y luego realizaremos llamadas en equipo.

📋 Cómo prepararte para el éxito: Para que tu experiencia haciendo llamadas sea fluida y sin complicaciones, por favor revisa estos requisitos antes de unirte:

Se requiere computadora: Por favor, conéctate desde una computadora portátil o de escritorio. (Nuestro software de llamadas no funciona bien en iPads o tabletas).

Requisitos técnicos: Necesitarás una buena conexión a internet, Zoom (es preferible usar la versión de escritorio) y un navegador web abiertos simultáneamente.

Recomendación: ¡Usar auriculares con micrófono y un ratón (mouse) facilita mucho la navegación!

Próximos pasos: Una vez que te registres, revisa tu correo electrónico para ver la guía de "Verificación técnica" que te ayudará a prepararte. ¡Nos vemos allí!

events.title: Tech Time: Maximizing VoteBuilder for Volunteer Management
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Thursday, October 15th from 1-2 pm ET for our free virtual live training: **Tech Time: Maximizing VoteBuilder for Volunteer Management.**

  

This session is designed to teach you the technical skills needed to effectively use VoteBuilder to create a virtual phone bank. Unlike our other virtual live trainings, this session focuses more on demonstrating hands-on, hard skills rather than high-level theory and strategy. If you already have access VoteBuilder, there will be opportunities to follow along and practice throughout the session.

  

We’re here to help, so join us to learn the following:

*   1\. Describe the role of My Campaign as VoteBuilder's volunteer management hub
*   2\. Identify best practices for building and maintaining accurate volunteer data in VoteBuilder
*   3\. Demonstrate how to organize and segment volunteers into targeted lists to support recruitment and escalation
*   4\. Demonstrate how to use VoteBuilder's Event Scheduler and Report Manager to track both campaign and volunteer performance

  

**This training is right for you if you're planning or managing a voter contact program using VoteBuilder/VAN.**

  

Learn more about our trainer [**Donald Riddle**](https://traindems.org/our-team#team/donald-riddle)**.**

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.description:
Join us on Saturday, October 10, for the California Fights Forward: Statewide Day of Action. Our success in the primary showed that we achieve more when we work together toward a shared goal. Join us as we knock on doors and make calls to elect Democrats down ballot and take back the House.

*In 2024 Adam Gray flipped the seat by only 187 votes. Let's talk to Democrats now to hold CD13 in 2026, as we take back the House majority!*

Once you've signed up, a volunteer will contact you with details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. At the staging location you will receive brief training and all the supplies you will need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks, and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a fully charged smartphone is a must.

Read more about how Adam Gray always puts the Central Valley first - https://gray.house.gov/

September 28

October 5

October 12

events.title: Hop on the bus from Chicago to Benton Harbor (MI-04) to flip the House!

address_lines: Rear Entrance - Look for Bright Horizons

events.description:
Join Indivisible Chicago and Vote Save America volunteers on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—Swing Left's new deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Michigan's 4th Congressional District—a must-win swing district—to talk to voters where it matters most. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: 
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don't worry if you've never done this before! Your bus captain will provide departure details, training, and the Ground Truth conversation guide. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

### What to expect:

- **Travel:** The bus will leave Chicago on Sunday, October 11 at 8:15am CT. Please be at the meetup point by 8:00am to ensure on-time departure (the Marathon is happening that morning, so leave extra time and consider taking the Blue or Pink line!). It's about a two-hour drive, but we lose an hour on the way there with the time change! We'll return to Chicago by 8:00pm CT. 

- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:30–4:00pm, with breaks as you need them!

- **Rally:** Join us for a post-canvass party in Benton Harbor! Trade stories with your fellow canvassers and celebrate your work.

The conversations we have could be the tipping point. Can we count on you to help us get this bus on the road? Sign up today!

Please note: 

- By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will.

- This bus trip is collaboration between Swing Left, Indivisible Chicago, and Vote Save America. By signing up you may receive communications from these organizations, and you can unsubscribe at any time. 

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

events.title: Tech Time: Last Minute Turf Cutting in VoteBuilder
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Wednesday, October 14th from 1-2 pm ET for our free virtual live training: **Tech Time: Last Minute Turf Cutting in VoteBuilder.**

  

This session is designed to teach you the technical skills needed to effectively use VoteBuilder to create a virtual phone bank. Unlike our other virtual live trainings, this session focuses more on demonstrating hands-on, hard skills rather than high-level theory and strategy. If you already have access VoteBuilder, there will be opportunities to follow along and practice throughout the session.

  

We’re here to help, so join us to learn the following:

*   Define turf-cutting and describe its role in door-to-door canvassing

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Westside Democratic HQ on the weekend of October 17-18 for a road trip to canvass for two days in San Diego for Dem candidate Marni von Wilpert!

Our mission is to flip Congressional District 48 blue and ultimately take back the House! With Trumpy Darrell Issa retiring, we need to help elect Democratic candidate Marni von Wilpert.  Marni is currently serving on the San Diego City Council and she is eager to oppose Trump's policies that are damaging the country and destroying human rights.

Her promise to the American people: "Whether it's stopping [ICE] from raiding our communities ... undoing the costly tariffs ... restoring affordable health care, I will stand up for our community against Donald Trump. And I'll do it every day."

Ballots have arrived in mailboxes, so the timing of this canvass in important.

We'll meet at the WDHQ (located in the Venice-Santa Monica area) to board transportation early on Saturday, Oct. 17, spend the weekend knocking on doors and talking with voters in Escondido, a city in San Diego County with middle-income and working class voters.  Then we'll return to LA the evening of Sunday, Oct. 18.

As a volunteer, you'll be participating in the Democratic Party's Statewide Day of Action and serving on the WDHQ's ground team for priority Congressional campaigns. This is important work and we would love to have you join us.

Meetup location will be shared after you register.  Partner organizations for this event are the the California Democratic Party (CADEM), the Los Angeles County Democratic Party, and Making Waves for Democracy.

events.title: Eyewitness to the Resistance: Photojournalists on the Front Lines of Protest

location.venue: San Francisco Main Public Library, Koret Auditorium

events.description:
Join us for **Eyewitness to the Resistance: Photojournalists on the Front Lines of Protest**, an extraordinary panel discussion hosted by Indivisible SF and Pro Bono Photo.

When history unfolds in the streets, photojournalists put themselves in the center of the chaos to document the truth. From the chants of resistance to the quiet moments of raw human courage, these photographers capture the images that define a generation.

In this compelling discussion, you will hear firsthand accounts from the front lines of activism. The panel will dive deep into:

**The Stories Behind the Shots:** The danger, the emotion, and the split-second decisions that go into capturing iconic movement photography.

**The Power of Visual Journalism:** How authentic imagery shapes public perception, fuels social change, and counters misinformation.

**The Ethical Front Lines:** What it means to bear witness to history while staying safe and maintaining journalistic integrity.

This event is free and open to the public. Please RSVP to receive notifications and updates prior to the event. SFPL link with more info: https://sfpl.org/events/2026/10/22/presentation-eyewitness-resistance

events.title: De-escalation Training
events.description:
If you've ever found yourself in a situation where someone was agitated or argumentative and you didn’t know how to defuse the situation, you may benefit from de-escalation training.

Our political divide in America has widened to a destructive degree. Conversations about politics with family, friends and neighbors have, unfortunately, become harder and harder in recent years. These types of conversations should be spirited but also respectful and productive, and too often that is lost to heated emotions.

This 60-90 minute session covers basic de-escalation techniques, including verbal and non-verbal, examples of what to do and what not to do; basic causes of escalating behavior; practice scenarios; and when (and who) to call for help.

Our trainer, Liz, is a practiced de-escalation educator and lawyer who practiced for 35 years in multiple public sector jobs. In her various roles, she also trained managers, supervisors, and employees, on how to deal with and respond to discriminating and harassing behaviors, including scenario-based training such as this de-escalation webinar.

Stop by our tables to grab a donut, check your voter registration, learn what you’ll need to bring to the polls, find your polling place, and get answers to questions about voting in Alabama. We’ll also have information specifically for college students who may be registered to vote outside Alabama.

Want to help us get out the vote? We need volunteers! Join us at Toomer’s Corner, or help distribute voting information and flyers around downtown Auburn and invite people to stop by for a free donut and make their voting plan.

There’s no purchase, sign-up, or action required to get a donut — they’re simply our treat to the community!

Whether you stay and volunteer or just stop by for a donut and some voting information, we’d love to see you. Democracy works best when we all participate. Let’s get Auburn ready to vote!

events.title: Get Out the Vote for Abdul, Jocelyn & Michigan Democrats in Marquette
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: NO KINGS ALISO VIEJO: Vote Early
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

Join us in Aliso Viejo to push back against authoritarianism and rally our community to vote!


For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.


Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.


Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 


*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 


**WHAT TO BRING** 

- your family, friends, and neighbors 

- your best signs (we'll have extras on hand to borrow) 

- water for you and/or bottled water to donate 

- snacks for you and/or packaged snacks to donate 

- a wagon if you're willing to help pass out drinks and snacks 

- a portable speaker with your best playlist

- a folding chair if you'd like to sit 

- and sunscreen.



**SUPPORT MUTUAL AID** - We're pairing outrage about the authoritarian takeover of our government with a call to action to support our local communities. **We'll be collecting food & essential items** for mutual aid to support our partner organizations. Requested items include: 

- cereal, pasta, rice, beans 

- sugar, salt, oil, flour, coffee 

- canned food, bottled water 

- soap, body wash, shampoo 

- toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant 

- toilet paper & paper towels 

- dish & laundry detergent 

- menstrual care products 

- baby diapers and wipes


**PARKING** - Park in the old Macaroni Grill lot by the theatre, then use the ramp to come down. We'll have the main tent set up on the grass below the Walgreens. We'll spread along Aliso Creek Rd. on all 4 corners.


**Aliso Viejo Resistance,** an [OC Indivisible Coalition team,](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition) is your host for this event. **The OC Indivisible Coalition** is a collaboration between the [Indivisible](https://indivisible.org/) groups in and touching Orange County, CA. We are non-partisan, all-volunteer, grassroots groups of residents in OC who are fighting fascism and holding elected officials accountable, from city councils and school boards all the way up to Congress. We partner with other community organizations to uplift and support our neighbors while we work toward progressive electoral change and a democracy that works for ALL people.


What began in 2025 as a single day of defiance has become a sustained national resistance to tyranny, spreading from small towns to city centers and across every community determined to defend democracy. Our peaceful movement is bigger than ever.

Let’s send Mike Croley to Congress for TN’s 6th District! Join us for a morning of community canvassing where we will knock doors and talk to our neighbors about why Mike Croley is the best choice for TN-06 this November.

9/12/2026: Sylvan Park
9/26/2026: Hillsboro
10/10/2026: Green Hills
10/24/2026: Edgehill

Every door we knock builds the momentum to win this election. Whether you can join one shift or every week, your support helps move the needle.

RSVP today and let’s make history!

events.title: Spring Branch BigWalk for SBOE6
events.description:
🚪 Let’s Talk to Our Neighbors About Michelle Palmer and other Dem candidates!

Join us for a neighborhood block walk to meet voters, listen to our neighbors, and introduce them to Michelle Palmer, candidate for Texas State Board of Education District 6.

Michelle is a teacher who understands Texas classrooms firsthand. She believes our students deserve fact-based, high-quality education and that educators should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape our schools.

This is about more than knocking on doors—it’s about building relationships, listening to our community, and making sure voters know what’s at stake for public education.

💙 No experience necessary—training and materials will be provided!
👟 Wear comfortable shoes and bring a friend.
🏡 We’ll walk together, talk with neighbors, and share why Michelle Palmer is the right choice for District 6.

Every door matters. Every conversation matters. Every vote matters.

Let’s get Michelle Palmer elected and flip Texas BLUE up and down the ballot!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Spring Branch for Talarico Block Walk!
events.description:
Join local Talarico supporters in Spring Branch (Houston) to knock doors together and hear from voters directly.

You'll be joined by a team of people who are working hard to elect James to be our next Senator and are already making a direct impact in our community.

During the block walk, volunteers will: 
-Identify Democratic supporters, 
-Share information about our Democratic ticket, and 
-Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities.

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots operation and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We'll provide training, materials, and turf (the list of addresses you’ll visit) when you arrive. Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend. RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.
events.accessibility_notes:
Thank you for signing up! Please watch your inbox for more details in the days leading up to the event. Looking forward to meeting/seeing you!
-Danielle

events.title: Get Out the Vote for Abdul, Jocelyn & Michigan Democrats in St Joseph
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Arlington TX
events.description:
Join the NO KINGS: EARLY VOTE - Arlington TX Rally!! Saturday Oct 17th - 10am-12pm Come early for easier parking We'll Meet in front of the Arlington Sub Courthouse 700 E Abrams St 
Voter Registration - fill out your form - check your Active Status - lots of VDR's and tables and info!
We'll be on the sidewalks - Bring your SIGNS and Wear your COSTUMES! Meet a bunch of your Candidates! Get their info and make your PLAN to VOTE! Share this fun loud silly gathering with your kids & neighbors! We'll be strolling down the sidewalks or hanging out in a lawn chair on the grass - staying out of the street - and doing a lot of hollering!! We are so thankful to be safely watched over by our friendly Arlington Police Officers and TC Constables - just in case we fall down and get a booboo!
Please SIGN UP and get a reminder email! See you 10/17 at 10AM at the Rally and 10/19 to 10/30 at EARLY VOTING or 11/3 on ELECTION DAY! Remember - the Arlington Sub Courthouse is an EARLY VOTING LOCATION!!!
Also - CHECK your VOTER status is ACTIVE on the Tarrant County Elections website - Voter LOOKUP - TODAY - call them immediately if you have been SUSPENDED!

events.title: Virginia Fall Wine Festival
events.description:
Get out there with a COVA Coalition Street Team to talk to voters at community events and show people that the resistance is alive and well! We'll share educational materials and discuss why it's important to vote "yes" on the 3 amendments to the Virginia Constitution that will be on the ballot this November; show people how to register to vote or check/update their voter registration on their phones; give out stickers; and encourage others to find their voice, take action, and protect democracy.

PLEASE NOTE that this activity involves standing and walking: We will NOT have a table at this event; instead, we will walk around and talk to people as they enter and leave the venue. We will not have tickets to attend the event, so we will not enter the park. Volunteers are welcome to purchase their own tickets to attend the event before and/or after their shift.

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
Dear friends,  

I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 

•USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)

•It was given less than 1 week of testing

•A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected

•The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message

We are saying NO to:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find your members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:  
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
 https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use this template (copy and paste)

Subject: UNTESTED. UNSAFE. UNACCEPTABLE. – Protect Mail-In Voting Now

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to take immediate action to protect mail in voting.

The new USPS ballot system is:

❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing

❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots

❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  

I ask you to:  

1.Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation

2.Co sponsor legislation to protect mail in voting rights

3.Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]  

Step 3: Send it!  

•Use your members’ official website contact forms (fastest)

•Or email/call their offices directly

events.title: BloomAIR Community Defense Training
events.description:
Our friends from BloomAIR will conduct a training covering three key topics:

1. Know your rights when interacting with law enforcement and federal agents

2. How to identify ICE

3. What to do if you see or hear about a potential ICE sighting. 

There will be time available for questions and answers as well. If you’re interested in organizing directly against ICE, or if you simply want to be prepared and empowered in the event of an ICE encounter, don’t miss this training.

Please arrive by 2:45pm so the training can begin promptly at 3:00pm.

### Photography and Video Policy
ISCI may take photos or videos at meetings and events to document, share, and promote our activities. When taking photos or videos, ISCI representatives will do their best to seek explicit consent before photographing individuals with their faces or names visible. We ask all participants taking personal photos or videos to seek consent as well and respect the wishes of those who do not want to be photographed or recorded. **Please note that in public settings, including protests, there is always the possibility of being identifiably photographed.** Ultimately, the responsibility for protecting our identity lies with each of us individually. If you are concerned about being photographed or recorded during Indivisible activities, we strongly encourage you to cover your face and other identifiable features.

events.description:
## ☎️ Phone Bank with us - Make as many or as few calls as you like.

### We are reaching out to Democrats in Houston County, Georgia to spread the word about the upcoming election. Make some calls to get out the vote for Jon Ossoff, Keisha Lance Bottoms, and Democrats all the way down the ballot. Early Voting starts October 13!

To participate in this virtual phone bank, you will need an ActionID. If you don't have an ActionID, create one at this link: https://myaccount.ngpvan.com/CreateAccount

Once you have your ActionID, you're ready to get started!

### How it works:

🍑Log into the phone bank with your ActionID

🍑Your first voter will be displayed

🍑Click the phone number to dial it automatically

🍑Read the script on your screen to your voter, or mark that you could not reach them and leave a message.

🍑Record the results, save, and go on to the next

🍑You can start and stop as you please - make 5 calls or 50, every vote counts

Thanks for helping to get out the vote for Georgia Democrats, let's win this election and flip Georgia Blue! 🍑

events.title: Get Out the Vote for Abdul, Jocelyn & Michigan Democrats in Orion
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to Get Out The Vote & talk with voters in your community!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

This fall, Michigan picks a new U.S. Senator, a new Governor, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Phone bank for Kelly
events.description:
Kelly needs your help so that she can help everyone in Northeast Indiana and win! Sign up and you can phone bank from home to help elect Kelly!

If you want to make calls with a Google Voice:

For Android and iPhone:

Sign up for Google Voice & get your number
Important: Google Voice doesn’t offer 1–800 numbers. 
Make sure that your phone is on and can get texts. To check, we’ll text you a code.
1.	Download the Google Voice app.
2.	Open the Voice app  .
3.	Sign in to your account.
4.	Review the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy    tap Continue.
5.	To pick your Google Voice number, tap Search.
•	You can search by city or area code. If numbers aren’t available, try a nearby city or area code.
6.	Next to the number you want, tap Select. 
7.	Follow the instructions.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Lodi, CA!
events.description:
Join us at the Kettleman/Lower Sacramento Intersection to add our voices to the movement! 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

We stay on the sidewalk, keep the walkway clear for pedestrians, stay out of driveways and the roadway, and follow all traffic signals.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Porterville, California
events.description:
Join us in standing up for democracy.  Democracy survives when we ALL vote!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Weekday Door Knocking in Ypsilanti!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!  Doors don't take a break during the week and neither do we - join us Tuesday through Friday to talk to voters.

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

## Pedal to the Polls: Welcome Amy & Dave to Chaska! 🚲🛶

### 40 days. 1,215+ miles. One canoe. And one incredible mission.

## Join us at Firemen’s Park in Chaska on Saturday, October 25 at 1:00 PM to welcome Amy and Dave Freeman as they roll into town on their statewide Pedal to the Polls journey!

Amy and Dave are biking more than 1,200 miles across Minnesota with a canoe in tow to raise awareness about protecting the Boundary Waters and encourage Minnesotans to get out and vote for Boundary Waters champions this November.

We’ll celebrate their arrival with a Pedal to the Polls rally, hear a little about their journey, grab a group photo, and then put the energy into action with a GOTV canvass.

### 🚲 What to expect:
- Welcome Amy & Dave as they arrive in Chaska with their canoe!
- Rally together and celebrate their incredible journey.
- Knock doors in support of getting voters engaged and out to the polls.
- Choose a 30-minute mini-canvass with an experienced volunteer or join us for the full canvass.
- Bring your friends, your bike, your enthusiasm and your love for Minnesota!

### Come for the rally. Stay for the door knocking. Help us turn 1,215 miles into 1,215+ doors!

Learn more about Amy and Dave's Pedal to the Polls journey and their work with the Save the Boundary Waters Action Fund: Learn more about Pedal to the Polls

### Saturday, October 25 • 1:00 PM • Firemen’s Park, Chaska
### Ride. Rally. Canvass. 
### Let's make every mile count!

https://www.boundarywatersaction.org/pedal-to-the-polls

events.title: Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This an at-home/online Indivisible event!

Dear friends,  
I am one of the millions of Americans who rely on mail in voting. But now, Our Votes Are in Danger! the government is trying to rush through a dangerous, untested USPS rule that could disenfranchise millions of voters who rely on mail in voting. Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here’s what’s happening: 
•	USPS built a brand new ballot screening system in just 3 months (normally takes over a year)
•	It was given less than 1 week of testing
•	A “zero failure” policy means: one barcode error = thousands of ballots rejected
•	The Trump administration has appealed to the Supreme Court to allow this rule to take effect before the midterm elections

📢 "Untested, Unsafe, Unacceptable" – That's Our Message
We are saying NO to:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment
We need to make our voices heard – NOW.

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find your members of Congress
•	Find your U.S. Representative:  
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative
•	Find your U.S. Senators:
 https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use this template (copy and paste)

Subject: UNTESTED. UNSAFE. UNACCEPTABLE. – Protect Mail-In Voting Now

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to take immediate action to protect mail in voting.

The new USPS ballot system is:
❌ UNTESTED – A system built in 3 months with less than 1 week of testing
❌ UNSAFE – One barcode error could reject thousands of ballots
❌ UNACCEPTABLE – Our votes are NOT your experiment

Over 250 current and former members of Congress have already urged the Supreme Court to block this executive order.Please join them.  
I ask you to:  
1.	Support Senator Blumenthal’s investigation
2.	Co sponsor legislation to protect mail in voting rights
3.	Call on USPS to pause and independently test this system

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.

Sincerely,  
[Your Full Name]  
[Your Address]  

Step 3: Send it!

events.title: Campaña de Alcance En Durham Para Rechazar Las Enmiendas Constitucionales Perjudiciales
events.description:
Un grupo de legisladores estatales quiere estafar a nuestra comunidad con dos enmiendas constitucionales que se votarán este otoño. Estas enmiendas permitirán que las grandes corporaciones y las personas adineradas eviten pagar lo que deben, mientras que los trabajadores tendrán que asumir la cuenta. Ninguna de las dos enmiendas le ahorrará dinero a la gente trabajadora. Si se aprueban estas enmiendas, podrían significar recortes de miles de millones de dólares en nuestras escuelas, la atención médica y otros servicios públicos.

Durham For All y Durham Public School Strong se han unido para movilizar a miles de personas a votar en contra de estas enmiendas perjudiciales y exigir que las empresas y los multimillonarios paguen lo que deben en impuestos, para que nuestros niños, educadores y comunidades tengan lo que necesitan para prosperar.

¡Únete a nuestros esfuerzos para tocar las puertas de nuestros vecinos o hablar con la gente en eventos comunitarios para dar a conocer estas enmiendas perjudiciales y asegurarnos de que sean rechazadas en las urnas!

Si nunca has hecho campaña puerta a puerta o si acabas de enterarte de estas enmiendas, ¡no te preocupes! Te daremos argumentos clave y te ayudaremos a moldear y compartir tu historia sobre por qué esto es importante para ti. Todas las actividades de alcance se realizarán en parejas, así que trae a un amigo o ven preparado para hacer nuevas amistades.

Habrá interpretación al español y servicio de guardería en el lugar de reunión para todos los turnos de alcance de fines de semana.

events.title: No Kings: North Carolina Door Knocking Weekend with the Workers Circle
events.description:
The 2026 midterms are a critical moment in our fight for free and fair elections. At the Workers Circle, we seek to build a truly multiracial, multicultural democracy and push back against all attempts at voter suppression. 

Join us this October on the ground in Charlotte, North Carolina as we get out the vote and fight voter suppression before the midterms. On Saturday, October 17, we will be on the ground knocking doors around Mecklenburg county from 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM (with breaks for lunch, snacks, and rest). Our goal is to ensure voters have the important, non-partisan, early voting, and voter ID information they need to cast their ballot. We'll conclude the day with an optional dinner together. 

Please let us know if you're interested by filling out this form: https://forms.gle/XfVhMpakV5sXtW4s6 

This event is a collaboration with Carolina Jews for Justice, Dayenu, the Center for Common Ground, Bend the Arc, JALSA, Team Unity, Baptist Joint Committee for Religious Liberty, Charlotte Muslim Caucus, Jews for Freedom, North Carolina Council of Churches, Interfaith Alliance, and more!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: 📞Tuesday phone banks at the WDHQ to flip the House BLUE!
events.description:
Join us at the Westside Democratic Headquarters on Tuesdays to call target voters in priority Congressional Districts CA-22 and CA-48 for, respectively, Randy Villegas and Marni von Wilpert.  These are both flippable districts and must-wins for us to take back the House!

"Flip the House" phone banks will be open at the Westside Democratic HQ on Tuesdays from 1 to 3 p.m. and from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.

To join the phone banks from home on Zoom, register here to receive the links:
  Afternoon (1-3 pm):  https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/1021227/
  Evening (5:30-7:30 pm):  https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/

In CA-22, call voters in a district that now favors Democratic candidates, and oust the Trumpy incumbent David Valadao.  Our candidate -- Randy Villegas -- is progressive, smart, and tuned into the needs of the residents of his district.

In CA-48, help us replace the Trumpy outgoing Rep. Darrell Issa with a strong Democratic candidate who will fight for California families. Marni von Wilpert is ready to fight for working families, older adults, and ALL Americans!

Gather with like-minded activists from the Los Angeles area to make a difference in the November election, reunite with old acquaintances, and make some new friends!

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way by our in-house phone bank coordinators. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient. 

You can bring your own computer, laptop or tablet -- or use one of the WDHQ's Chromebooks to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

events.title: Hands Off My Vote - No Dictators! Protest & Food Drive in Kona (Hawai'i Island)
events.description:
Please join Kona Indivisible & Matriarchy Rising for our 4th “No Dictators” protest in Kona. 

We will not allow the fascist, orange menace to steal our vote by disenfranchising voters using various methods. All voters must have a plan to ensure their vote is counted by placing your ballot in a secure drop box and voting early! 

This event is also a Food Drive for Aloha Latinos. 

Food Drive: Let’s show support and solidarity for our cherished local migrant Latino community who have been intensely impacted by the illegal and cruel actions of Donald Trump. Let’s help ease the pain for migrants who have been displaced and traumatized by ICE on Hawai’i Island. We are all in this together! 

Mahalo for your ongoing support and profound generosity! Profound and hefty! I’ve actually witnessed many of you carrying heavy bags of groceries along Queen Ka’ahumanu to the protests! 

Each giant protest has brought in such huge amounts of donated non-perishable food & diapers that we have transportation and storage challenges afterwards, so we are humbly asking for more cash donations instead of food & diapers whenever possible. ☺️

I can take cash, checks, PayPal, Venmo and, of course, we will have food bins at the next “No Dictators” protest. And again, a special mahalo to our monthly donors! 

Food Drive, Preferred Items for Aloha Latinos: 
	(Please make sure items are not expired — mahalo for your support!)

* Dried & canned beans (pinto & black) 
* White rice
* Spaghetti Pasta
* Pasta sauce
* Bread (shelf-stable)

* Canned chilies: chipotle & pickled jalapeño

events.title: Ms. Augusta Thomas Day of Action - GLCLC Labor2026 Walk: Sponsored by AFGE
events.description:
Join the KY State AFL-CIO for the Labor2026 program as we hit the pavement to build power for working families!

Elections are won at the doorstep. This election season, we are mobilizing union members across the Commonwealth to talk to our siblings and neighbors about the issues that matter most: protecting our right to organize, securing fair wages, and ensuring safe working conditions for every Kentuckian.

Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or a first-time volunteer, we need your voice. We will provide all the training, materials, and snacks you need to have meaningful, face-to-face conversations with voters in your community. By showing up for our endorsed candidates, we ensure that labor has a seat at the table in Frankfort and beyond.

Why Join a Labor Walk?

Strength in Numbers: Show our collective power as a unified labor movement.

Direct Impact: Research shows that peer-to-peer union conversations are the most effective way to turn out the vote.

Solidarity: Connect with fellow union members from across various trades and sectors.

In Solidarity,
The KY State AFL-CIO Labor 2026 Team

events.description:
Join us as we rally on North Common, and then Parade to the Polls, where we can VOTE EARLY IN PERSON at Town Hall, while encouraging everyone else to do it too!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

He's ready to fight to restore benefits for California's most vulnerable families and expose the horrible impact of Trump’s tariffs on consumers and small businesses.

In CA-22, call voters in a district that now favors Democratic candidates, and oust the Trumpy incumbent David Valadao. Our candidate -- Randy Villegas -- is progressive, smart, and tuned into the needs of the residents of his district.

As we work on campaigns in key Congressional districts with the goal of FLIPPING the House BLUE, we cannot afford to lose one seat.

As ballots begin arriving for the November 3 General Election, we’ll head into our communities to make sure voters have the trusted information and resources they need to participate.

No canvassing experience is necessary. We’ll provide training, materials, and everything you need before heading out. Whether this is your first time knocking doors or your fiftieth, there’s a place for you.

Schedule

* Doors at 8:30
* Program at 9
* Training at 9:30
* Canvass at 10:00
* Lunch Break
* Canvass at 1:30

**Democracy belongs to all of us. Come spend a few hours helping make sure it reaches all of us, too.**

events.title: Cal RCV Booth at the CicLAvia in the Heart of LA!
events.description:
Cal RCV is excited to be part of CicLAvia—and this time, we’ve adopted the Figueroa & 2nd intersection! We’ll be out there helping people navigate the intersection safely while starting conversations about ranked choice voting.

If you’ve never experienced CicLAvia, you’re in for a treat. LA’s streets are transformed into a massive people-powered celebration, with thousands of Angelenos biking, skating, walking, running, and enjoying the city without cars. The route comes down Glendale Blvd from Echo Park and becomes W 2nd after crossing the 110—bringing all that energy right to where we’ll be stationed.

And that gives us an incredible opportunity.

At a time when so many people feel that their voices aren’t being heard and that our political system isn’t working for them, we have a chance to introduce people to a better way of choosing our leaders.

Ranked choice voting gives voters more voice and more meaningful choices. It can help create elections where candidates compete for broader support, voters have more freedom to vote for the candidates they truly want, and elected officials are more accountable to the people they represent.

🌱 But change starts with awareness.

Before RCV can become a reality across California, more people need to know what it is, understand how it works, and see why it could make our democracy stronger.

That’s what makes CicLAvia so exciting for Cal RCV. Thousands of Angelenos will be right there with us—curious, engaged, and enjoying their city. Every conversation is an opportunity to spark an idea. Every new person who learns about RCV brings us one step closer to change.

🔥 Come be part of it!

Join us for a fun, energetic day of community, outreach, and action. Let’s meet people, share the idea, build connections—and show what’s possible when we work together.

One conversation can start something. Together, we can build the momentum to change how California votes.

events.title: No Kings - Vote Early - Riverhead, NY
events.description:
We the people have the power. We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensure every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.  We must reject recent and prospective threats to the free and fair process of our elections and their results.

For Riverhead — the seat of Suffolk County — that means a march through town, a rally on the steps of the Suffolk County Supreme Court with special guest speakers (TBA - stay tuned!), and a Celebration of Democracy Community Resource Fair where you can get your voting questions answered, sign up for upcoming election protection training, find real ways to plug in locally, and spend the afternoon together with live music along the way. This election will shape what comes next for all of us — so come get your plan to vote early, bring a neighbor, and let's head into November ready for whatever it brings. No thrones, no crowns, no kings.

**Meet us at the Suffolk County Supreme Court on Griffing Avenue at 2PM, march through town together, and head back for the rally and the fair. Park at the train station, Town Hall, or any nearby public lot.**

During the morning we are encouraging and supporting hyperlocal vote early visibility actions in East End communities. If you want to organize an event or are part of a service or activist group that wishes to participate in the Community Resource Fair, please write to: riverheadnokings@gmail.com

Brought to you by: East End Visibility Brigade, Indivisible Long Island, Indivisible North Fork, League of Women Voters, PEER/NYPAN: Progressive East End Reformers, Riverhead No Kings, together with activists and neighbors across the East End.

location.venue: First Unitarian Universalist Church of Austin

events.description:
**👻 The call is coming from inside the house. 👻**

The most chilling thing this October? Not knowing what's on your ballot!

Join us Saturday, October 17 for a family-friendly day focused on making voting information accessible, building community, and helping people feel prepared for the polls.

Activities throughout the day:

🗳️ Election Protection - Info on protecting your rights and help with voting issues

🚗 Make Your Vote Plan and sign up for a ride to the polls

👋 Sign up to work the polls for the county

💆 Spooky, election-themed palm readings and a raffle to support the work behind the event

☕ Food and beverage station with info on the ongoing boycott of Starbucks that Hands Off Central TX has endorsed

📜 The Giant Constitution and other interactive civic activities

🎧 DJ keeping the day moving

⚰️ The Democracy Graveyard, an art exhibit that symbolizes voting faux paux that we're leaving behind 

📸 Spooky photo booth

💀 Día de los Muertos ofrenda honoring voting heroes that have passed

👑 Drag Queen Story Hours — drag performers read books about Halloween and voting

📱Relational Organizing Training — learn to connect with friends, family, and networks to get them to the polls

🩹 Information and resources on Harm Reduction at the Polls 

🎤 Singing greeters welcoming you as you arrive

This is a nonpartisan event. There will be no candidate endorsements or campaign activities. The focus is on community, voter education, and making sure people have access to the information and resources they need for the upcoming election.

Bring your friends, family, and neighbors. Come for the activities, stay for the community, and get connected with people working to make civic participation more accessible for everyone.

All ages are welcome and costumes are encouraged!

Please note:
- no masks
- no weapons
- keep it non-partisan

RSVP for updates, and follow **@HandsOffCentralTX** on Instagram to be first to know extra spooky details.

events.title: Let Freedom READ! Banned Book Week Event

location.venue: Warren-Newport Public Library, Meeting Room A

events.description:
# "Let Freedom READ!" with NELC-Indivisible

Join us on **“National Let Freedom Read Day”** on October 10th to honor the close of **National Banned Book Week.**

## The freedom to read is under attack - so let’s do something about it!

Now more than ever, we need to encourage literacy, inclusivity, and freedom of choice. Join NE Lake County Indivisible as we come together for a "Banned Book Club" Meeting. Participants are invited to bring ANY banned book they have read and loved. We will meet to discuss our books and explore why they may have been censored. We will also strategize around how to help defend books from censorship and stand up for the library staff, educators, writers, publishers, and booksellers who make them available!

📅Date: Saturday October 10

🕝Time: 2:00-4:00pm

📍Location: Warren Newport Public Library, Meeting Room A

Let Freedom READ is a national effort. More information can be found here: bit.ly/LetFreedomReadDay

Looking for inspiration? Check out the following websites for book ideas: 
https://www.ala.org/bbooks/frequentlychallengedbooks/top10 
https://ncte.org/app/uploads/2018/09/TitlesChallenged2002-2018.pdf 

Want to take action NOW? Sign a petition here: https://uniteagainstbookbans.org/take-action

Have more time to give in support of BANNED BOOKS? Check out ideas for action here: https://bannedbooksweek.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/ALA_DayofAction_OneSheet_Final.pdf 

This year Banned Book Week is also pushing VOTER ENGAGEMENT, and they have provided this resource for action: https://bannedbooksweek.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/LFRD-Voting-One-Sheet.pdf 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Some quotes from past participants:
- "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"
- "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."
- "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."
- "Well organized. Liked the materials included in the kits. Good location. Nice people. Thank you very much!"
- "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others." 

## *ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:*

NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

### More about us can be found here:

### https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org
### https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

events.title: Become a Neighborhood Vote Protector
events.description:
*Español Abajo*
## Protect the vote in your neighborhood 
### Become a neighborhood vote protector. Every vote is a decision about our healthcare, housing, wages, and who gets to make the rules – which is exactly why it needs to be protected. The Trump administration is trying rig the outcomes of the election by creating chaos, fear and new roadblocks to keep us from voting. 

We Are CA is training thousands of Neighborhood Vote Protectors across the state to watch the polls in their communities, safely safely document and report incidents to legal experts, and make sure every voter knows their rights to cast a ballot without fear or intimidation. 
Join a short training to learn how you can look out for your neighbors, your block, and your local polling place.

Wed Sep 23 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 14 6-7:30pm

Wed Oct 21 6-7:30pm

Sat Oct 24 10-11:30am

-----

*Español*
## Protege el voto en tu vecindario
### Conviértete en un Protector del Voto en tu Vecindario. Cada voto es una decisión sobre nuestra salud, nuestra vivienda, nuestros salarios y sobre quién decide las reglas — y es precisamente por eso que necesita ser protegido. La administración Trump está tratando de manipular los resultados de las elecciones creando caos, miedo y nuevos obstáculos para impedirnos votar.

We Are CA está capacitando a miles de Protectores del Voto en todo el estado para vigilar los centros de votación en sus comunidades, documentar incidentes de forma segura a través de líneas directas legales, y asegurarse de que cada votante conozca sus derechos para emitir su voto sin miedo ni intimidación.

Únete a una capacitación breve para aprender cómo puedes cuidar a tus vecinos, tu cuadra y tu centro de votación local.

The National theme for No Kings 4 is VOTE EARLY! But in California ballots are mailed on October 5 and ballot drop boxes open October 6. So, our large letter freeway signs will be posted on both sides of the overpass saying **NO KINGS - VOTE NOW!**

These signs on 9 Hwy 50 overpasses in El Dorado County will be seen by 50 - 100 vehicles per minute! 60,000 - 120,000 cars & trucks will get the message 9 times in 16 miles. Massive early voting is our goal!

### Bring flags and signs if you like. Get creative with the VOTE EARLY message!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

events.title: The Pioneer Project: 4-Week Training Program
events.description:
The Pioneer Project is a four-week training program that teaches participants the fundamentals of legislative advocacy, including how to engineer a policy, how to propose that policy to legislators, and how to advocate for that policy after it becomes a bill. Legislative advocacy is a skill that allows everyday people to weigh into and lead political decisions for their community. Right now, politicians mainly hear from corporations and paid lobbyists when making their decisions and creating policy. Legislative advocacy opens the door for anyone to enter that conversation and make political change. 

The Pioneer Project spans 4 weeks, with two one-hour training sessions per week on Monday and Wednesday. Each training will be a remote webinar delivered live on Zoom by Pioneer Energy. The Zoom link will be provided to sign-ups before the start of the trainings. 

TRAINING TOPICS
November 16th: Welcome to Pioneer Energy
November 18th: Engineering a Policy
November 23rd: Preparing for the Project
November 25th: Researching your Legislature
November 30th: Lobby Meetings
December 2nd: Bill Drafting and Sponsorship
December 7th: Supporting the Bill
December 9th: Advocacy and the Home Stretch

events.title: Vote Forward Community Calls
events.description:
Vote Forward partners with volunteers to take evidence-driven, high-impact actions to strengthen our democracy by building trust in government and increasing voter participation. Everything we do is grounded in evidence: we rigorously test our tactics, learn from the results, and evolve. Our 2026 campaigns build directly on what we learned in 2025, and include some of our most novel and exciting work yet. We have ambitious goals, but we make it easy to get started.

**Join us for our Community Calls** — three sessions we're hosting before letters go out for updates about Vote Forward's active campaigns and opportunities for volunteers to talk to each other and to staff about the projects. Each session will highlight a different facet of Vote Forward's work. 

For those who like to write letters with some background entertainment, we encourage you to have some handy to write together while we spend some time together. **We won't have a letter writing how-to during these calls, but encourage anyone with any experience level to join us!**

**After you RSVP,** we'll email you detailed instructions about how to create a [votefwd.org](https://votefwd.org/) account, adopt voters, and download letters. 

**Before you hop on the community call:** visit [votefwd.org](https://votefwd.org/), create an account, and download letters.

We're writing letters now, storing them safely, and mailing them between October 1 and October 24, 2026 — timed to land during early voting and just before Election Day, when they'll have the biggest impact.

Bring a friend or family member and help them become a Vote Forward volunteer this year!

events.title: IA: Davenport Canvass for Clean Water
events.description:
### Join Food & Water Action every other Saturday to talk with our neighbors about Iowa's water crisis!

Iowa has _the fastest-rising cancer rates in the country._ We know this is linked to the pollution from industrial agriculture that flows into the waterways we get our drinking water from. Now, we’re canvassing our neighborhoods, asking people how they’ve been impacted by the water crisis and listening to their stories. 

Together, we will organize, talk to our neighbors, and share information about what we can do to keep our water safe, starting with electing candidates like Chris Jones for Ag Secretary, who will hold polluters accountable and clean up Iowa's water! 

We will meet at _Lafayette Park at 11 AM_ for a brief training session on how to have effective conversations.

Then, we will pair up and head out!

After everyone finishes their list/shift, we meet back up at Lafayette Park and debrief over pizza!

**No prior experience canvassing is needed!**

We use the website OpenField to track our conversations, so please bring a fully charged phone. We'll spend some time during the training familiarizing ourselves with OpenField.

events.title: Knock doors in Wisconsin with the Democratic Party of Oak Park!

location.venue: Democratic Party of Oak Park Headquarters (Parking Lot behind Building)

events.description:
As we head into critical 2026 midterms, we have a real shot at taking back the houses of government and finally rolling back Donald Trump's extreme, authoritarian agenda. But we'll only succeed if we're working together. We'd love you to come knock doors in Wisconsin with us!

**Meeting Location in Oak Park: 6941 W North Ave, Oak Park, IL**

Volunteers will meet at meet in Oak Park (meet us in the building's parking lot behind the building) before carpooling to Wisconsin to knock on doors!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using miniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

events.description:
## Ready to turn the tide in CD35? Want to get it Dunn in 121? Down to show some love for our future County Judge?

Join Johnny Garcia, Zack Dunn and Ron Nirenberg as we knock doors in Bexar County to ensure everyone gets to the polls in November!

### What to Expect
We'll be talking to voters about what issues are important to them, introducing the candidates, and making sure they have a plan to vote (ideally during Early Voting in October!).

Blockwalking is the most important thing we can do to get Democratic voters to the polls. The work you do with us will make a big difference in November!

#### Everyone is welcome!
New volunteers will get plenty of support to get up to speed alongside experienced volunteers. We will have a quick MiniVAN training, a briefing on the script, and provide talking points for the candidates.

### Event Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive by 2:45pm (location provided upon RSVP).  

[3-3:30pm]: On-site orientation where we will review the program and do a quick refresher on miniVAN.

[3:30-5pm]: We will knock doors individually or in pairs. Experienced blockwalkers will pair up with less experienced ones to make sure everyone is comfortable using MiniVAN

[5-5:30pm]: Debrief and pack up. We will review the day's numbers, talk about what went well and what we can improve, and celebrate our success!

events.title: Seeberger for MN Senate Weekly Phone Bank!
events.description:
Ready to make a real impact for Senator Judy Seeberger and Senate District 41?

Join us for our Weekly Volunteer Phone Bank and help us connect with supporters across the district. We’ll be calling constituents and supporters to spread the word, build excitement, recruit volunteers, identify lawn sign supporters, and find more people who are ready to support Judy and get involved with the campaign.

Judy knows exactly how much every vote matters. In 2022, she won this seat by just 321 votes. Those 321 votes made the difference between winning and losing, and they helped secure the DFL’s narrow one-seat majority in the Minnesota Senate. Today, the Senate is still closely divided, and Senate District 41 remains one of the most important races in the state.

That is why this work matters. Our opponent is already working hard, and we need to match their energy. Every phone call helps us connect with supporters, recruit volunteers, grow Judy’s lawn sign presence, and build the kind of grassroots support that wins close elections. In a race this competitive, even small actions can make a big difference.

Judy has delivered results for our communities on clean water, public safety, consumer protection, strong schools, veterans issues, broadband, and support for working families. As a firefighter, paramedic, attorney, and state senator, she brings real experience and steady leadership to the job, and voters deserve to hear why her leadership matters.

Whether you are an experienced volunteer or this is your very first time, we will make sure you are fully prepared. We will start with a training, go over the script and talking points, answer questions, and make sure everyone feels comfortable before we begin. Campaigns are won by people talking to people, and every conversation counts.

Event Details
What We Provide: Training, script, support, and everything you need to get started.

What to Bring: A charged phone and a willingness to help grow Judy’s campaign.

Questions? Please contact Laine at 218-392-0377 for more information.
Let’s get to work, connect with supporters, recruit volunteers, and build support for Judy across SD41!

Voting is our superpower. The idea that voting is a superpower emphasizes that every eligible citizen has the ability to shape their community, state, and nation through the act of casting a ballot. Many forces are working to undermine trust in our elections, weaken voting rights, and make it harder for people to have their voices heard.  Voting early gives us the power to make our voices heard on our own terms, before Election Day, before the last-minute chaos, and before anyone else can decide what happens next.

events.title: No Dictators: Vote Early; Kapolei, HI; Voter Education, Protest & Food Drive
events.description:
Join with us under the shade trees in Kapolei Regional Park to celebrate our ability to vote early and by mail, drop box, or in person at a voter center. Encourage others to vote early to minimize the effect of efforts to discourage or interfere with voting. Learn how to register to vote, check your current registration status, when to expect the arrival of your ballots in the mail and what to do if you don't receive them. Learn the locations, dates and hours of drop boxes and in-person voting centers. Learn when your ballots must be received, how to request replacement of lost ballots and how to track the receipt of your ballots. Also, learn how to report voter intimidation or obstruction, and volunteer to monitor drop boxes and voting centers from a legal distance to observe for and report efforts to discourage voting.

In addition to the emphasis on early voting, we will use this opportunity to join with many others to protest efforts to destroy our democracy and establish a fascist government. Please bring your own signs if at all possible because only limited sign-making materials will be available for drop-ins. There is one precaution that you should be aware of. In another very conservative state, citizens protesting ICE under the first amendment were charged, tried, and imprisoned. We do not expect that to happen here but can't promise it won't.

The protest line will start at the corner of Manawai St and extend northeast up the sidewalk adjacent to the park and Farrington Hwy. The sidewalk should be shaded as well. So be creative and show your inner selves by bringing T. rex and other costumes, your bubble machines, your songs and chants. There will be a music playlist so let's all have a good time while venting those pent-up feelings. Bring both your enthusiasm and civility. FYI: We will not be distributing American flags or whistles this time.

Also, please bring excess non-perishable food to help feed the hungry on the westside. We are grateful to all who donated at No Kings 3.0. The food will be distributed at the open food distribution shelves at St. John the Baptist Episcopal Church in Waiʻanae.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Walk with Hays Dems in Highpointe
events.description:
Each week, make a difference! If you can't spare the full 2 hours, even 30 minutes helps. If Saturdays don't work for you, come pick up some "turf" and you can walk in your own time the following week.

This Saturday, we'll walk in Highpointe. We'll meet in the parking lot of the amenity center, 410 Cool Spring Way, Austin 78737.

We're knocking doors of folks who may need a little encouragement to get out to vote in the midterms and giving them the trifolds from Hays Dems that has all our nominees on it, along with a QR to easily get them to our website.


We'll meet by 9:45 each week (Mobilize says 9:30, but that's because they only do times on the half hour.)
Hand out materials, go over the script, answer any questions, and hit the streets.
You can walk in pairs, or on your own, as you prefer.
BE SURE to have MiniVAN loaded and logged in before you leave your home.  If you're not familiar with MiniVAN, here's a short tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tv9-HHb1VQA

Most Saturdays, walkers are invited to stop by for a cooling dip in the pool at Kathi & Mark's home afterwards.

events.title: Voters  Matter
events.description:
We will decide who  and what comes next. Vote early and have a plan! We the people have the power and are claiming it - together . Join us!  How to Prepare for Your Event:  Bring  positive messaging signs or props → Make your message visible to vote!  Recruit friends → The more people, the more power.  There will be a voter registration table and music! 

Join us & make a  positive difference from 10-12 October 17th!

Down town Boulder Creek is a small beautiful mountain friendly community  in the Santa Cruz Mountains of about 3 blocks long. Join us to peacefully  connect with your neighbors and  local residents in Boulder Creek . To feel supported, uplifted  & safe.  Help us  send the clear message that voting is the most non violent method of power we  have.  

PARKING- Carpool if you can. There is parking behind the bank, sheriff and fire station, residential streets behind down town, by the elementary school, with the best along the streets by the Scarborough Lumber store with it’s Iconic lumber jack sign along the road. There is also a county bus ( Route 35/35x) that stops in down town BC every 30 minutes so you can park and ride from Ben Lomand, Brookdale, Felton etc. Restrooms are limited - portable potty at gas station,  if you buy a pizza at our local pizza parlor, a coffee at the Tree House etc.  

Please remember to cross our streets using our marked crosswalks, keep all driveways open, remain friendly, helpful and supportive of each other . Thank you, SLV Voices and Boulder Creek Voices  for Democracy.

And remember
