events.title: Postcards & Conversation With Our Down Ballot Candidates
events.description:
Join us for a series of special events with candidates.

**Joseph C. Damiani and Sylke Jackson, Candidates for Town Council, Clarkstown ,NY, will join us on Wednesday October 21st, at 8:00pm ET.** Clarkstown is a suburban town in Rockland County, NY on the west side of the Hudson River. Clarkstown sits in Congressional District NY-17 where Cait Conley is running to defeat incumbent Republican Mike Lawler. Clarkstown is governed by a Town Supervisor and 4 Town Council members. Clarkstown currently has a Republican Town Supervisor and 4 Republican Town Council members, despite the fact that there are more registered Democrats than Republicans. Past elections for Town Supervisor and Council were in off years with low turnout. With a shift to even-year elections and greater Democratic turnout expected this election cycle, there is a good chance to flip these seats. 

**Teresa Clifford, candidate for Town Supervisor, and Rita Romeu, candidate for Town Council, Somers, NY, will join us on Wednesday October 21st, at 8:30pm ET.** Teresa Clifford and Rita Romeu are running for local government in Somers, NY, as part of the Democratic ticket aimed at providing new leadership, increased transparency, and proactive community management.  If successful, their elections would shift the balance of power on the Somers Town Board to a 3-2 Democratic majority. Somers sits in Congressional District NY-17, a red-to-blue district NY Democrats are working hard to flip. Supporting these candidates helps them turn out voters for their local offices but also for Democrat Cait Conley who is working hard to unseat Republican Mike Lawler.


We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

If you are with the media and want to attend, you must notify us at markersfordemocracy@gmail.com at least two hours before the start of the event. All discussions are off the record.

This event is co-hosted by [Markers For Democracy](https://markersfordemocracy.org), [Downtown Nasty Women Social Group](https://linktr.ee/DNWSG), and [Team Min](https://linktr.ee/teammin
).

events.title: Get Out the Vote!
events.description:
Hi!
The time is now! We need to let people know how important it is to vote and when they can vote! Early voting starts October 17th.

By attending this event, you are committing to:
Nonviolence
Bringing signs not weapons
Ignoring disruptors
Being part of the group as opposed to standing alone
Paying attention to safety marshals (those wearing orange safety vests)
Allow only the safety leads to interact with law enforcement, if we are approached by them.
You participate at this event at your own risk.

We also suggest that you:
disable biometrics on your phone, like face and Touch ID
do not livestream.
video from a safe distance, with your phone locked. (If you video any disruptors, this would be for a record only, NOT for posting.)
listen to law enforcement officers and If you are videotaping them because of concerns, that you narrate what you're doing while videotaping.

events.title: HOP ON THE BUS to knock doors for Randy Villegas, CD22 | October 10 + 11 in Porterville!

location.venue: Hop on the Bus to Porterville!

events.description:
**Bus leaves from Mountain View!  You leave Saturday, October 10 at 7AM and return Sunday, October 11 by 7PM.  We can help with carpools to catch the Mountain View bus from other Bay Area locations!**

Sign up to knock doors in the Central Valley! This is a special canvass where you can **Hop on the Canvassing Lux Bus** and ride in comfort there and back. 

**Help Flip the House in 2026!!**  Join Santa Clara County Democratic Party, Bay Area Coalition, and the Democratic Volunteer Center to knock doors in Porterville.  Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term.  

 - *Why Porterville?*  Porterville has a critical 5,000 doors to be knocked to win this election!

 - *Why October 10 & 11?* Voters' ballots will have just have been received in the mail!

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools to the bus launch in Mountain View, hotel options, and other details about the canvass event! Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

This "Hop on the Bus" canvass will be a two day and one night canvass.  Your canvassing concierge will coordinate carpools to catch the bus on Saturday morning, October 10 from the Democratic Volunteer Center in Mountain View.  When you arrive in Porterville, local drivers will be standing by to take you to your canvassing turf.  A community dinner will be coordinated, but canvassers will make their own hotel reservations with help from your canvassing concierge.  Stipends of $150 trip/total are available for lodging and food.  

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

We're in the final stretch of one of the most exciting election seasons in Texas history, and winning up and down the ballot comes down to one thing: YOU, having conversations with every Texan you know.

A conversation with someone you know is more than twice as effective as one with a stranger. One real chat with a person in your network does the work of *ten* doors knocked.

Join us for a quick training, and a fun virtual friend bank. We'll get you set up on the Reach app and give you the tools to have these conversations with confidence. We'll chat for about 30 minutes, then spend the rest of our time together adding contacts and sending messages!

Zero experience required. All you need is a cell phone, a laptop if you have one, and a commitment to flip Texas blue. We'll teach you the rest. See you soon!

events.title: Virtual Friendbank to Battleground States

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
The most effective election defense is to rack up lots of wins with big margins - make the results **too big to rig!**

Stockpiling the early vote means bigger margins - and  **we're going to drive the largest early vote turnout in American history!**

You probably know a lot of "supervoters" - they vote every election, rain or shine. They are often the people who love to vote on Election Day. Well they now have a superpower: move their vote up by 2-3 weeks!

YOUR superpower is to activate your friends to vote early! 

Come to this virtual friendbank, and get all you need to drive up early vote numbers in your crew - and also to help *them* activate *their* friends.

We're focusing on a list of battleground states below, so please join us if you have friends or family in any of these states:

•	Alaska

•	Arizona

•	Florida

•	Georgia

•	Iowa

•	Maine

•	Michigan

•	North Carolina

•	Ohio

•	Pennsylvania

•	Texas

•	Wisconsin

When people vote *as early as possible,* they create social proof ("we're all voting!"), they can fix any ballot problems before it's too late, and will massively shrink the target for any Election Day sabotage. 

See you there!

events.description:
# Help Make Arctoberfest Happen! 🎃🍂

Arctoberfest is going to be an incredible evening of food, fun, community, and celebration — but we can’t do it without **YOU!**

It takes a lot of hands (and a lot of heart!) to make an event like Arctoberfest come together. Whether you can give us a couple of hours before the event, join us for part of the evening, or help us wrap things up at the end of the night, **we’d love to have you on the Arctoberfest team!**

No special skills required — just bring yourself, a willingness to help, and your best Arctoberfest spirit. 🍁

## 🎃 Setup Crew | 1:00–3:00 PM

Help us turn the space into **Arctoberfest!**

We’ll need extra hands setting up tables and chairs, decorating, organizing event areas, getting food and beverage stations ready, and taking care of all those finishing touches before our guests arrive.

Come early, crank up the music, and help us get the party started!

## 🍂 Event Volunteers | 4:00–8:00 PM

Want to be right in the middle of the fun? Join us during Arctoberfest!

We’ll have several ways to help throughout the evening, including:

* **Welcome Crew** – Greet guests and help everyone feel at home from the moment they arrive.
* **Seating Helpers** – Help guests find their way and keep things running smoothly.
* **Food & Hospitality Crew** – Help with food service, keeping things stocked, and making sure our guests are well taken care of.
* **Wherever-We-Need-You Crew!** – Events always have a few surprises. Be one of our flexible volunteers who can jump in wherever an extra set of hands is needed.

And yes — **you’ll still get to enjoy Arctoberfest while you’re helping!**

## 🧹 Cleanup Crew | 7:30–8:30 PM

Every great party eventually has to come to an end — and many hands make cleanup MUCH easier!

Help us pack up decorations, clear tables, straighten the space, gather supplies, and leave everything looking great. Give us one last hour and help us finish Arctoberfest strong.

This is the [National No Kings: Vote Early website, Event Map and Host Toolkit.](https://www.nokings.org/) There are training calls, graphics and planning resources.  If you like, **you can register and post your event on the map**; as local organizers, we're happy to help you navigate that process.
**Or, gather a few of your neighbors and friends in a less formal action**  - that's the hyper-local focus of this Oct 17th. 
### Lots of Great Vote Early action ideas so far. National Day of Action Oct 17, Locally, let's keep it going all the way through Nov 3rd!
- Honk and Waves - Your Ballot Drop Box is Here! Giant arrows! With or without Frogs, Jugglers, Balloons

- Car caravans, Bike Caravans - Dress up your vehicles and drive through town, head past a drop box.

- Run to Early Vote - gather your runner friends. Or skaters.. run to the dropbox.

- Voting is My Super Power - Dressing up as your favorite Superhero!

- Coffee shop - Vote in Public! At your favorite Food Cart pod, coffee shop, local pub...Bring friends, ballots, I Voted stickers, voter education info to share. Break bread with friends while you're at it.

- Chalk the Vote!  Sidewalk messages to lead folks to Drop boxes, Track Your Ballot, and County Elections websites

- Vote Party at the Park - celebrating folks who've already voted, help neighbors learn how to vote early themselves. You might want crafts, music, puppets..

- Overpass Bannering - Vote Early, Oregon Vote is Safe & Easy

- We Will Vote! Sing-a-Long

- Organize a Neighborhood Dropbox Karaoke Carpool and afterparty

- Block Party - Early Vote! BBQ, Voter Pamphlets, Election Resources

**Election Defense: Oregon's Vote By Mail systems are easy to use, safe and reliable.** But when a would be king continues to threaten our elections, we have a collective duty to protect the vote and make sure every ballot is counted.  In Oregon, you and your volunteers can join the [Common Cause efforts as Trusted Messengers, dispelling misinformation and as Election Box Monitors.](https://www.commoncause.org/oregon/actions/2001/)

From OR DOJ [Oregon rules regarding Drop Boxes, Campaigning activities](https://www.doj.state.or.us/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CJ-Election-Guide-CJ-BW.pdf)

Want to make a difference? Volunteer with [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) for our **No Kings: Vote Early rally on October 17th**! For "No Kings IV," our core focus is promoting early voting and ensuring our community meets crucial election deadlines.

If you want to help but aren't sure where to start, we provide all the instructions, guides, and templates you need so you are never on your own. If you haven't already, please make sure to fill out our [No Kings: Early Voting Volunteer Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1fQC8ILxTmU8QA6T9PgtDXMXKkyj_6hXEM2b80PqcTDg/edit). You can also review our list of [No Kings: Vote Early List of Volunteer Roles](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OhLbXZJQJzpFbGCAFeZetuk5l6rAYuHMHuv1R7fF_ps/edit?usp=sharing) to get a better idea of the available positions!

Join Mesa Valley Indivisible to go over these roles, responsibilities, and what to expect on the day of the event, as well as some final details and any questions you have!

If you cannot make it for this October 10th meeting, attend the same training on [Monday, October 12th at 5:30pm - 7:30pm](https://www.mobilize.us/mesavalleyindivisible/event/1034057/) instead!

events.title: Get Out the Vote for Jess Goldoni and Denise Powell!
events.description:
# Knock doors with Denise Powell and Jess Goldoni

Born and raised in Omaha, Democrat Jess Goldoni was shaped by a strong Nebraska work ethic and the belief that opportunity is earned. She put herself through college and built a 20-year career across healthcare, law, finance, and technology; managing billion-dollar budgets, leading teams, and helping families and small businesses cut through red tape and grow.

Now a candidate for Nebraska's 18th Legislative District, Jess is running to lower costs, strengthen schools and families, and move Nebraska forward with discipline, optimism, and common sense.

Denise Powell is a mom, small business owner, former corporate executive, public school champion, and healthcare advocate who knows that a strong work ethic and a love of family and community are the Nebraska way of life. She also knows the Good Life is getting harder to come by. After Trump’s election in 2016, she founded an organization that has supported hundreds of Nebraskans running for local office, protected our public schools and the families they serve, and helped stop extremists from passing abortion bans in the state.

Join us in getting out the vote for these two amazing candidates!

## What to bring:

- Charged Phone
- Water
- A positive attitude!

## What we will do:

- Knock on our neighbors doors and talk to them about the upcoming election!

Join us to canvass for Emily Gregory in House District 87!

You walk with a buddy, get fully trained, hand out a flyer, use a wonderful app to track your progress, and have fun doing it! It's not about going into deep policy discussions, just being a friendly neighbor to encourage awareness of Emily's platform for the November Midterm General Election.**

More about Emily...

Emily Gregory is a mother of three, a military spouse, and a small business owner with a professional background in public health and mental health services. She has dedicated her career to assisting new mothers and families facing economic hardship. After a career in public health, she built her company, FIT4MOM Palm Beach, to create a healthy and supportive community for new and expecting mothers.

Emily and her family chose to make Jupiter their home for its great schools, affordability, and sense of community. However, over the past seven years, she has witnessed the rising cost of living, increasing insurance rates, and threats to the public school system. Motivated by the concerns she hears from other parents and community members, Emily is running for State Representative to bring practical, results-driven leadership to Tallahassee.

Her campaign is focused on building a healthier, more hopeful future for all Floridians.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Arroyo Market Square (AM Time Slot) - Indivisible Las Vegas, NV
events.description:
Join Indivisible Las Vegas on Saturday, October 17 as we turn No Kings energy into **votes!**

We’ll be mobilizing at **eight designated early voting locations** across Clark County, with **two separate activities at each location:**

**STREET RALLY — Get Out the Vote.**  
Join our high-energy rally along the street and sidewalks to encourage people throughout the neighborhood to VOTE EARLY! Bring your enthusiasm and help us make early voting impossible to ignore.

**VOTER WELCOME TEAM — Encourage & Inform.**  
Closer to the polling site, volunteers will serve as our welcoming, nonpartisan “cheer squad” — greeting and encouraging voters and distributing approved voting information.

Register for your preferred **location and time slot**. Six locations will have morning and afternoon shifts; the two malls will be afternoon only. There is a separate Mobilize event for each.

**Our eight locations are: Arroyo Market Square, Blue Diamond Crossing, Craig Ranch Regional Park, Galleria Mall, Meadows Mall, Desert Breeze Community Center, Pearson Community Center, and Cardenas Market on East Bonanza.

**This No Kings is different. On October 17, the most important sign of protest is a ballot.**

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*Our community always brings the most creative signs to our events. We love them, but because No Kings Early Vote will be at voting locations, they must remain nonpartisan. That’s not our rule. It’s the law. We’ll be having signs made with voting language, but if you’d like to bring your own, it should focus on early voting. An example of an acceptable sign would be “Your Vote Counts” or “Vote Early Today.” Prohibited signs would call out a particular candidate or a generalized “F*ck Trump.”*

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

## 🛫 ICE & AROCC: Stop ICE operations at Mesa Gateway Airport!

For eight months, [Mesa Valley Indivisible](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/) members and a coalition of groups around the country have been working relentlessly to end Avelo Airlines’ involvement in the unlawful and inhumane deportation of primarily non‑violent immigrants via Mesa Gateway Airport. As a result, Avelo Airlines ended their contract with ICE in January 2026! 

Although Avelo Airlines has left our Mesa Gateway Airport, ICE deportation missions still happen every day and the Arizona Removal Operations Coordination Center (AROCC) continues to operate.

Despite being a transit hub meant for 12-hour stays, people were being held for weeks, packed like sardines on bare concrete floors with no beds or showers. While the administration continues to claim these are short-term facilities, the reality has proven to be gut-wrenching medical neglect and overcrowding.

Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

Greater Genesee County is all of Genesee County except Flint and Flint Township!

location.venue: Southern Hills Christian Church (Disciples Of Christ)

events.description:
Beyond the Buzzwords: Socialism, Communism, and Entitlements in an Election Season

Election season has a way of turning complicated ideas into very loud buzzwords.

Socialism. Communism. Entitlements. Medicare. Social Security. We hear these terms constantly from candidates, campaigns, pundits, and social media, but what do they actually mean?

Join Indivisible Edmond for a plain-English look at some of the most frequently used and misused political and economic terms of the election season.

We'll look at what socialism and communism actually are, how they differ from capitalism and social democracy, why the Nordic countries aren't quite what American political rhetoric makes them out to be, and what "entitlement" really means when we're talking about Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP, and the federal budget.

We'll also look at some of the claims you're likely to hear between now and Election Day and give you a simple way to separate the definition from the political spin.

**PLEASE TAKE NOTE OF NEW LOCATION**

Join the Madison NorthEast Dems to Get Out the Early Vote for the Midterm Elections! This is our time to motivate our neighbors to cast their early in-person or mail-in votes for our Democratic candidates.

The NED Team Needs You!

Our candidate slate for the state is great!
•	Governor – David Crowley

•	Secretary of State – JoCasta Zamarripa
•	Treasurer – Yee Leng Xiong

We will also be canvassing to GOTEV for our state assembly candidates, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford and Andrew Hysell and our Congressman Mark Pocan.

Have you heard?! There are 3 constitutional amendments on our ballot this November. We're voting NO on every one of these.

- Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment

Ballot language: Prohibits state government from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any person based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, education, contracting, or administration. 

Context: Wisconsin already prohibits discrimination under state and federal law; the amendment also bars “preferential treatment” programs aimed at equity. 

- Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee
Ballot language: Bars the governor from using the partial veto power to create or increase any tax or fee.

Context: When Republican State Legislatures have passed budgets eliminating the funding of programs that serve the people, a Democratic Governor has been able to use this power to ensure the program is funded. 

- Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies

Ballot language: Bars the government from closing gatherings at places of worship during declared emergencies, including public health emergencies.

 The NED team offers new canvasser training at the start of every shift. We will try to pair up new canvassers with more experienced ones as folks are available. We provide all the materials you need to canvass; literature, a list of voters, a script to follow, a bottle of water, and a snack. You just need to bring your smartphone. We'll be using the MiniVAN App to collect the voter responses and guide you through your turf. Please download the MiniVAN Touch or MiniVAN 9 App by NPG VAN and create and Action ID before coming to the canvass. Training on how to use MiniVAN is included in the new canvasser training. 

 Don't want to canvass, but you still want to help? Sign up and tell the NED team member who reaches out to confirm that you want to help in another way, such as making phone calls for volunteers, delivering yard signs, or assisting with canvass launches. There is a place for you on the NED team. 

 This year is our first opportunity in 16 years to win a trifecta of Democratic government in Wisconsin. We can win the State Assembly, Senate, and Governor's seat this November. With a Democratic trifecta, progressive priorities can become law. Lower taxes, higher wages, funded public schools, affordable health care, environmental protections, the overturning of Act 10, and more can be in our future by wining these November elections. events.title: Bridge Brigade — Monday Mornings
events.description:
Meet on the Tower Bridge Overpass over  WI-53 near Costco (off Black Avenue). Parking on Gooder & Tower, Eau Claire, WI 54703.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

See you at 7:30am for setup and 8:00am to wave!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

Voting is our superpower. And voting early? In massive numbers? That’s next-level power! And now we’re gearing up to use it – which means promptly, collectively and overwhelmingly exercising our right to vote. Because "We, the People," decide who represent us and the sooner that "We, the People," vote, the better!

So please leave your partisan signs behind and bring "vote early" signs instead – "I'm voting today," "early voting rocks," "my vote is my superpower" and so on. We'll have signs you can borrow, too, plus a supply of American flags. And plenty of civic energy to go around!

Join PRESCOTT INDIVISIBLE on October 17 and help us create this positive, joyful moment around elections and community and democracy. Together, we’ll exercise our voting superpower and encourage our neighbors to exercise theirs!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Rogers City, Michigan
events.description:
Rally at The Rogers City Courthouse 151 E Huron Ave, Rogers City, MI 49779

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY, Event #1 (Waterville, Signs of Democracy!)
events.description:
This is the FIRST of the No Kings: Vote Early events Indivisible Mid Maine is hosting on October 17 (a general description of our participation that day can be found at https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1020677/). You do not need to be a Waterville resident or voter to join us for this event!

For this first event of the day, interested folks should plan to meet at 31 Front Street (the parking lot of the Waterville Family Practice/Morning Sentinel Building near Head of Falls Park) at 10am. Starting at 10:15 we will march in a short loop through downtown Waterville over to Spring Street where we will stand for a Signs of Democracy Visibility Event (from 10:45-11:30) on the Ticonic Bridge. SIGNS WILL BE PROVIDED, but please feel free to bring your own upbeat, positive, celebratory signs about the importance of voting early! 

If you are comfortable doing so, and you are a Waterville voter, please also bring your completed absentee ballot to deposit on this occasion in the secure absentee ballot box behind Waterville City Hall, where cheerful greeters will welcome you with bells and whistles. With your permission they will also take your picture as you deposit your ballot, and pictures will then be put in a digital "I voted early!" frame and circulated on social media. We can send you copies if we have contact info. 

The visibility event will end at 11:30 and we will return to 31 Front Street by 11:45, at which point participants can head home or continue on to our second event of the day. NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY, Event #2 (Waterville to Winslow).

A core principle behind all IMM and No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Please contact Elizabeth at leonardelizabeth1957@gmail.com with any questions!

events.title: NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY, Event #2 (Two-Cent Bridge Parade from Waterville to Winslow)
events.description:
This is the SECOND of the No Kings: Vote Early events Indivisible Mid Maine is hosting on October 17 (a general description of our participation that day can be found at https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1020677/). You do not need to be a Waterville OR a Winslow resident or voter to join us for this event!

For this event, interested folks should plan to meet at 31 Front Street (parking lot of the Waterville Family Practice/Morning Sentinel building)! Starting at 12:15 we will march into Head of Falls Park, across the Two Cent Bridge, and over to the Winslow Town Office at 114 Benton Avenue.

There, Winslow voters who choose to do so can deposit their completed absentee ballots at the secure absentee ballot box in front of the town office and be celebrated by our cheerful greeters, who will welcome you with bells and whistles. With your permission they will also take your picture as you deposit your ballot, and pictures will then be put in a digital "I voted early!" frame and circulated on social media. We can send you copies if we have contact info. 

Some signs will be available for marchers with upbeat messages expressing the value and pleasure of voting early, but please feel free to bring your own!

We will depart the Winslow town office by 12:45 and cross back over the bridge either to return to 31 Front Street or go home. Please note: Event #3 for the day--the Grand We Vote Early March from Waterville to Fairfield--will begin at 31 Front Street at 1:15. You are welcome to join us for that event, or drive past as we march offering honks of support, but there is no requirement to do so!

If you have any questions, please contact Elizabeth at leonardelizabeth1957@gmail.com.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: NO KINGS: "WE VOTE EARLY" GRAND MARCH from Waterville to Fairfield (and visibility event)
events.description:

You do not need to be a Waterville OR Fairfield resident or voter to join us for this event!

For this final event of the day, interested folks should plan to meet at 31 Front Street (parking lot for the Waterville Family Practice/Morning Sentinel building) in Waterville at 1pm. Starting at 1:15 we will march the 3.3 miles--mostly along College Ave.--from Waterville to the Fairfield Town Office at 19 Lawrence Ave. This march is flat, there are sidewalks all the way, and it takes about an hour and fifteen minutes. events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in CA-48!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Phone Bank for Angie Carraway in HD 89
events.description:
Talking to voters is one of the simplest ways to help Angie’s campaign
reach more people across House District 89.

Join us online every Friday from 6:00–8:00 p.m. Central for our
virtual phone bank. You can call from home, talk with voters about
what’s happening in their communities, introduce them to Angie, and
make sure they know there’s a teacher and neighbor running to
represent them in Austin.

Never phone-banked before? That’s completely fine. We’ll spend the
first 30 minutes walking new volunteers through everything: how the
calling system works, what to say, what to expect, and what to do when
you get a question you don’t know how to answer.

And yes, calling strangers can feel a little awkward at first. Most
people get the hang of it pretty quickly. You’re not there to give a
speech. You’re there to have a conversation.

Please join from a laptop or desktop computer with a reliable internet
connection. A quiet place to talk and a pair of headphones will make
things easier.

We’ll send the Zoom link after you RSVP.

Come once. Come every Friday. Bring a friend if you want. We’ll get
you trained, get you comfortable, and get you talking to your
neighbors!

We will line rte. 70 and Haddonfield Rd (in front of the Wegmans shopping center in Cherry Hill) to send a clear message that ‘we the people’ can and must vote – EARLY, TOGETHER, and in RECORD NUMBERS! 

We will build community, spread joy, and mobilize South Jersey to vote – and VOTE EARLY – so we make the results TOO BIG TO RIG!

THE EVENT:
Starting at the corner of Rte. 70 and Haddonfield Rd, we’ll form a very visible line down each road.
-- Display signs, posters, and anything else expressing our VOTING messaging
-- Dance and sing to the tunes and chants of the Brass Uprising Band and South Jersey Justice Choir
-- Enjoy the peaceful, fun, and festive event as we build community and send our message 
--Support and inform our community with voting information tables 

All to help ensure every eligible South Jersey voter has a plan to vote early, understands their options for how to vote, and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

THE GOAL: build unity, joy, and bring the community together to TURN PEOPLE POWER INTO VOTER POWER!

PREPARING FOR OCT 17: Keep an eye out for Poster Making events (including one at the General Meeting on 10/13), No Kings: Vote Early car brigades, messaging ideas that we will post, all coming soon.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

# **PROJECT HALO: CELEBRATE. VOTE. CONNECT.**

Patriotic music and short remarks from Dickinson College President John E. Jones III, Veteran Joe Frantz, and other local leaders. Master of Ceremonies: Rick Coplen.

An instructional session in the barn on helping people feel safe, confident, and supported when they vote. Sign-up rosters, T-shirts, and materials available.

American beef on the grill. Grillmasters welcome. Stay and meet other volunteers.

Carlisle, PA. The full address is sent with your RSVP confirmation.

Sunday, October 11 at 3:00 p.m.

events.description:
Join us for a peaceful, nonviolent demonstration with opportunities to connect with local organizations committed to justice and equity.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Team Lauren Weekly Volunteer Call
events.description:
Join us every Monday at 6:30 PM CT for Team Lauren's weekly volunteer call on Zoom. This is the hub of our campaign's grassroots organizing operation and the space where we come together, share updates, celebrate wins, and show you how to get involved from across the district.

We are less than 2 months from Election Day on November 3, 2026, and early voting begins in just five weeks. With mail-in ballots going out soon, the work we do right now is what will determine the outcome of this race.

Lauren Jewett is a special education teacher running to unseat Steve Scalise and bring real representation to Louisiana's 1st Congressional District. She is running to lower costs, protect our coast, strengthen public schools, expand access to healthcare, and make Congress actually answer to the people it represents and not special interests in Washington.

Every volunteer who shows up to this call is part of what makes that possible. See you on Monday night!

events.description:
**Join States Win MA-RI to knock doors and talk to voters in New Hampshire to help elect Ben Ming!** 

Every Saturday in October, join the campaign in Hollis, NH for canvasses starting at 10am, 12pm, and 2pm. Drive up on your own, recruit some friends to go along. 


ABOUT BEN MING

Ben Ming is an attorney, former NH State Representative, a member of the Hollis Planning Board, husband, and father of four. He served in the NH House from 2022 to 2024, and was the first Chinese-American elected to the NH General Court.
 
Professionally, Ben practices law with a focus on real estate and estate planning. His experience on the Hollis Planning Board has given him firsthand insight into housing, growth, and local government issues affecting NH families.

events.title: NYC Labor Phonebanks: Every Tuesday & Thursday!
events.description:
Union members across New York are getting organized for the November 3 General Election, and NYC labor is joining the fight.

Every Tuesday and Thursday through Election Day, NYC union members can join virtual member-to-member phone banks supporting labor-endorsed candidates in statewide and key races across New York.

We’ll be calling fellow union members to talk about what’s at stake in this election, the candidates endorsed by our union movement, and making sure working people turn out to vote.

Never phone banked before? No problem. A quick training will be provided at the beginning of each Zoom before calls begin.

All you need is your cell phone plus a laptop, desktop computer, or tablet.

Pick a Tuesday or Thursday, sign up for a shift, and help get out the #UnionStrong vote.

These phone banks are hosted by the New York State AFL-CIO as part of labor’s statewide member-to-member GOTV program.

events.title: CO-08: Deep Canvassing with We The Fighters

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
We are canvassing in Greeley to hold Congressman Gabe Evans accountable!

This is one of the most competitive districts in this election, and we know that Gabe Evans only won by a few thousand votes. That is why We the Fighters, a grassroots team of volunteers, is holding weekly canvasses to talk to our neighbors in CO-08.

We are building a powerful movement to hold Rep. Evans and his allies in Congress accountable by organizing thousands of our neighbors across the district who are in danger of losing their healthcare or food assistance. Over the coming weeks, we'll be talking with people directly impacted by these cuts, helping them connect the dots between what has happened, who is responsible, and how they can hold Rep. Evans accountable.

Will you join us? Sign up to canvass with us! We'll provide training, scripts, and a partner, so no experience is needed.

events.title: Phonebank to Elect Justin J. Pearson for Congress!
events.description:
Join TIRRC Votes Action PAC as we call voters across the newly formed Congressional District 9 to inform them of their district and elect Justin J. Pearson as the new federal house district representative. Pearson has always worked to bring people together to solve real problems and his track record of standing up to the rich and powerful show he’s a champion for our communities who prioritizes lowering costs and delivering real change.

Pearson has been a candidate who has fought for clean air and water, gun reform, immigrant rights, and making life more affordable for all Tennesseans for years. Join us as we inform voters of their new districts and vote for a candidate who continues to fight for every single Tennessean, not just a select few.

Whether this is the first time you've phonebanked or you're an experienced caller, we NEED you. Let's stand for Justin J. Pearson the way he has stood up for our communities across the state.

Zoom link will be texted and emailed 48 hours before the event

Paid for by TIRRC Votes Action PAC P.O. Box 17149 Nashville, TN 37217 Not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:

events.title: Angie for Florida: Victory Leader Orientation
events.description:
A Victory Leader is ready to bump it up a notch!
You are willing to take on a larger area, commit more time, and help build the campaign's overall field operation. 
Commitment: Approximately 500 to 3,000 doors. Your area may extend beyond your immediate neighborhood. You will coordinate your work with the Regional Director assigned to your area. Victory Captains aren't expected to do all those doors alone. You're stepping into a larger leadership role by helping organize and support the people around you.

Victory Captains will be willing to:
- Help organize and run weekly canvasses with their Regional Director.
- Recruit friends, family, and additional volunteers to help cover their turf.
- Work directly with their Regional Director to plan and coordinate canvassing.
- Help motivate and support other volunteers.
- Assist with phone banks and help support phone-banking operations.
- Take on additional responsibilities as the campaign moves toward victory.

Your Support Team Gets Bigger
As a Victory Leader, you gain more support and more connection to the campaign's field operation.
You will work alongside your Regional Director, the campaign's field team, and other Victory Captains to make sure the larger areas are being covered.
You aren't just responsible for your own doors.
You're helping make sure the team gets the doors covered.

You only need to attend one of the trainings listed below at whichever date works best for you!

events.title: Poll Greeter - Clemmons Library
events.description:
#### Poll Greeters are the last contact with voters before they enter the polling location. They offer our Democratic candidate information, remind voters to vote for _all_ the Democrats on their ballot & NO on the 3 Constitutional Amendments, and watch for issues that may occur outside the polling place. ####

**_Please read all the information below before signing up._**


**Training**: Due to changes in voting regulations, all Poll Greeters must be trained, whether you've been a greeter many times or this is your first time. 

**Notifications**: After you sign up for a shift you will receive a confirmation email from Forsyth County Dems via Mobilize. It will include information about _Greeter Bag Pickup_ and _Training Options_.  Please read it carefully. You will also be sent important information via email. You need to be sure that you receive and read them. If you don't find your confirmation email, check your spam folder. Still not found? Check your Mobilize Notification Settings.

**Mobilize Notification Settings**: 
Be sure that your settings in Mobilize are set to receive emails and texts. Find your settings in the **Menu** at the top right of this page; scroll down to **Account and notification settings**; **For events you sign up for** – they should all be turned on (blue).

**To check your schedule**, go to **Menu** then **My schedule**. You can cancel your registration there if you need to.

**Include your cell phone number** when you sign up even though it says optional. The HQ Team needs to know your phone number!

**You must pick up your greeter supplies** from headquarters before your first shift (details in your confirmation email after signing up).

**Please Confirm**: The day before your shift you will receive a text and an email asking you to confirm that you are coming. Please do confirm either by text or email so that the HQ Team and Site Captain know that you will be at your shift.

**Consider volunteering for at least 3 shifts**. There are a lot of hours over 15 days of Early Voting at 14 locations. We need lots of volunteer-power! 💙


**_Thank you for your time and efforts supporting our candidates by being a Poll Greeter! Talk to your friends and invite them to sign up too!_**

events.title: Knock Doors for Gov Tina Kotek and Sen. Merkley in Redmond!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Democratic Party of Oregon in Redmond as we knock doors to re-elect Governor Tina Kotek, Senator Jeff Merkley and Democratic leaders up and down the ballot.   Every conversation counts. Sign up now, and let's keep Oregon blue!

No experience necessary: We will train you and send you out with campaign literature so you are prepared to talk to you fellow Oregonians. Please wear comfortable shoes, bring water, a charged phone, and your love for this state. 

Interested in canvassing but have questions? Reach out to Aimee@DPO.org for more information.

events.title: No Kings: Vote & Vote Early for Democracy

address_lines: Corner of San Pablo Dam Rd & Appian Way

events.description:
This is a local Indivisible West CoCo County (IWCCC) Event.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing West Contra Costa County together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Wednesday Texas Phone Bank
events.description:
### We are calling Black voters in Texas, encouraging them to vote in the upcoming November 3rd general election and providing resources that make it easier to check where they are registered and find the voting information they need.

Beginning phone banker? We start each call with a training for anyone who needs it. You can also train yourself beforehand by checking out [our training slides](https://www.canva.com/design/DAGstUCSwjE/oWn7cjYLXJDiksQn6VbPww/view?utm_content=DAGstUCSwjE&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=uniquelinks&utlId=h1f8f5f4824).

Experienced? You can start making these calls immediately and pop back into the zoom with any questions along the way.

You can also make these calls on your own time 9am-8pm within the target state's time zone - no need to wait for an event!

For more information about this phone bank, please visit the [CFCG Phonebank Page](http://centerforcommonground.org/phonebanks)

COMMUNITY RALLY & FOOD DRIVE

📅 Saturday, October 17th
⏰ Noon–2:00 PM
📍 Corydon Town Square
E Walnut St, Corydon, IN 47112

This rally is about something bigger than politics.

It is about US. Our families. Our neighbors. Our farmers. Our rights. Our community. And the country we are leaving to our children. ❤️

For more than a year, millions of Americans have stood together to say that this country does not belong to kings, billionaires, corporations, or politicians.

🇺🇸 It belongs to the people.

And that means ALL of us.

You are welcome here, no matter the party. 

This is a nonpartisan, peaceful, family-friendly community event. We may not agree on everything—and we don't have to. We can still stand beside one another when it comes to protecting our communities and the things that matter to everyday people.

🌾 We can stand with our farmers and rural communities and recognize how important they are to our families, our economy, and our food supply.

If you can give, please bring something.

When enough neighbors each do a little, together we can do a whole lot. 🤝❤️

🎵 Live music
🛡️ Security
🎁 Free goodies for the kids
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Family-friendly activities and atmosphere
🥫 Community food drive
🗳️ Voting and early-voting information
🇺🇸 A peaceful place to stand together and make our voices heard

No violence. No weapons.

Bring your family. Bring your friends. Bring your neighbors.

Bring a canned good or hygiene item if you're able.

Bring a sign.

Most importantly, bring your voice.

There is so much trying to divide us right now. But our communities become stronger when we remember that the person standing next to us is our neighbor before they are a political label.

We can disagree and still care about each other.

We can fight for our rights while helping someone put food on their table.

We can support our farmers, our families, our workers, our children, and our neighbors.

And we can demand better from the people who represent us.

❤️🤍💙 That is what community looks like.

On October 17th, let's fill Corydon Town Square with people who still believe in one another and in the power of our voices.

NO THRONES.
NO CROWNS.
NO KINGS.

🇺🇸 WE THE PEOPLE. 🇺🇸

Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

7:30pm-7:45pm: Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

7:45pm-11:00pm Voter Mobilization | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

11:00pm -11:15pm: Debrief | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

How to Prepare
Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our mandatory online volunteer training on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

What to Bring
To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

A water bottle to stay hydrated

Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle

Join the Madison NorthEast Dems to Get Out the Vote for the Midterm Elections! This will be our last big push to knock on every door to motivate our neighbors to cast their votes for our Democratic candidates.

The NED Team Needs You!

Our candidate slate for the state is great!
•	Governor – David Crowley 
•	Lt. Governor – Sarah Godlewski
•	Attorney General – Josh Kaul
•	Secretary of State – JoCasta Zamarripa
•	Treasurer – Yee Leng Xiong

We will also be canvassing to GOTV for our state assembly candidates, Dina Nina Martinez-Rutherford and Andrew Hysell and our Congressman Mark Pocan.

Have you heard?! There are 3 constitutional amendments on our ballot this November. We're voting NO on every one of these.

- Prohibit Government Discrimination or Preferential Treatment
Ballot language: Prohibits state government from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any person based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, education, contracting, or administration. 

Context: Wisconsin already prohibits discrimination under state and federal law; the amendment also bars “preferential treatment” programs aimed at equity. 

- Prohibit Partial Veto to Increase Tax or Fee
Ballot language: Bars the governor from using the partial veto power to create or increase any tax or fee.

Context: When Republican State Legislatures have passed budgets eliminating the funding of programs that serve the people, a Democratic Governor has been able to use this power to ensure the program is funded. 

- Prohibit Government Closure of Places of Worship During Emergencies
Ballot language: Bars the government from closing gatherings at places of worship during declared emergencies, including public health emergencies.

Context: Covid was very serious before the vaccines were widely available.  Superspreader events led to illness and death outside the circle of the attendees.  

---
 The NED team offers new canvasser training at the start of every shift. We will try to pair up new canvassers with more experienced ones as folks are available. We provide all the materials you need to canvass; literature, a list of voters, a script to follow, a bottle of water, and a snack. You just need to bring your smartphone. We'll be using the MiniVAN App to collect the voter responses and guide you through your turf. Please download the MiniVAN Touch or MiniVAN 9 App by NPG VAN and create and Action ID before coming to the canvass. Training on how to use MiniVAN is included in the new canvasser training. 

 Don't want to canvass, but you still want to help? Sign up for a shift and tell the NED team member who reaches out to confirm that you want to help in another way, such as making phone calls for volunteers, delivering yard signs, or assisting with canvass launches. There is a place for you on the NED team. 

 This year is our first opportunity in 16 years to win a trifecta of Democratic government in Wisconsin. We can win the State Assembly, Senate, and Governor's seat this November. With a Democratic trifecta, progressive priorities can become law. Lower taxes, higher wages, funded public schools, affordable health care, environmental protections, the overturning of Act 10, and more can be in our future by wining these November elections. You need to be a part of this effort.

We’d love for you to join us and help spread the word to parents, non parents, and allies in Riverdale and beyond.

events.title: Knock Doors in Gaithersburg!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Eau Claire
events.description:
**He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.**  

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

**Date:** Thursday, October 15th  
**Time:** 9:30 a.m. 
**Location:** Pablo Center, 128 Graham Avenue, Eau Claire, WI

Harry Dunn is joining citizens of the Chippewa Valley for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. Who just welcomed "Stop the Steal" organizer Scott Presler to campaign for them at our own Eau Claire GOP headquarters. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.  

**Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.**   

This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.  

**Come ready to:**  

- Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection  
- Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard  
- Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it  

Time and location to be confirmed — RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Indivisible Cypress, Tx
events.description:
Make a plan. VOTE EARLY! Beginning Monday, Oct. 19th through Oct. 30.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*
events.accessibility_notes: Sidewalks on all four corners for everyone to line. Sidewalks are easily accessed from parking lots.

events.title: VOTE EARLY!

location.venue: On the sidewalk in front of the Horry County Courthouse

events.description:
Now is when we can do more than talk: it’s time to vote! 

Our message at Coastal Democracy is simple: If we want America’s 250-year-long experiment of a government of the people, by the people, and for the people to continue, we must cast our votes.

We encourage EVERYONE to cast their vote early during this election season. Horry County provides for early voting from Monday (10/19) through Saturday (10/31)—excluding Sunday (10/25)—with photo ID.*

To both celebrate and assert our shared democratic rights, we are participating in the fourth nationwide No Kings day event by holding a demonstration on Saturday, October 17 from 11:00am to 1:00pm in front of the Horry County Courthouse. 

As we rally, it’s important that we are all clear regarding our tactics:

1. WE ARE BUILDING A BIG TENT. Our goal is to create new allies, allies who might have voted for the current regime in the past but have now grown uncomfortable with its authoritarian policies. Please make sure your signs are free of profanity, are nonpartisan (do not name elected officials or political parties), and appeal to the values of the widest possible Horry County audience (values that the current regime is now trampling underfoot). We especially welcome American flags. We want to avoid alienating people of good conscience or triggering defensiveness in those who are in the difficult place of questioning their past voting behavior. This is a critical strategic decision based on our particular local context.

2. WE ARE NONVIOLENT, EVEN IN OUR SPEECH. Most passersby will show enthusiastic support for our pro-democracy message, but some--including counter protesters--will curse us, and others will attempt to bait us into argument. Don’t fall for it! These engagements are not productive and create an atmosphere of escalating tension. Instead, we will smile and wave at everyone and ignore verbal challenges. 

3. WE MUST REMAIN ON THE SIDEWALK. The city of Conway has granted us a special event permit for the sidewalk. However, the Courthouse lawn is Horry County property, and we are not permitted to encroach upon it.

4. WE RADIATE JOY. Authoritarian breakthrough is deadly serious, and we must be prepared to struggle mightily if we want to keep our democracy. But we also want to model and experience the promise of a joyful community. Feel free to wear costumes and cheer loudly!

Join us—we’re looking forward to seeing you there!

For updates, follow Coastal Democracy on Instagram:
https://www.instagram.com/coastal_democracy?igsh=cTl1ZzFsNGNzM3F3&utm_source=qr  

or

Facebook:
https://www.facebook.com/share/1A969m5UKL/?mibextid=wwXIfr

https://scvotes.gov/voters/early-voting/

Use the public trail from the Rec Area parking lot; from the lot near the covered picnic tables, follow the trail through woods, then the Pondview Drive neighborhood, cross Moyer, walk through Belle Lane neighborhood, find the paved trail between #419 and #421, cross Stover Rd, through more woods, and you will be in the park on the north side of the Plaza property. Walk on the path to your left and you will be able to see us! 
Hints: Use GPS as a pedestrian. Lower Salford Township map of trails and sidewalks may help: https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/c9a67fbca2c44f5aa94594aab4824356/ 
If you choose to walk on Oak Dr, please use extra caution as there are few sidewalks.

- Street parking on the following nearby residential roads: Shirley Drive, Pamela Circle, Kathleen Circle, Florence Drive. Take Clemens Road, which is the light at the Plaza, and from there, turn left into the Shirley Drive neighborhood.

- Street parking on Belle Lane: From Main Street, turn at the light onto Oak Dr, then left onto Moyer Road, and left onto Belle Lane. In this residential area, you’ll enter the paved foot trail between homes #419 and #421. Cross Stover Rd, go through more woods, and you will be in the park on the north side of the Plaza property. Walk on the path to your left and you will be able to see us.

- Street parking on Stormfield Drive: From Main Street, turn at the light onto Oak Dr, then right onto Stormfield Drive. This residential area has no posted parking restrictions that I saw (but don’t block driveways, fire hydrants, etc!). Walk out of the neighborhood and turn left to walk on Oak Dr toward the light at Main Street. Please use extra caution as there are few sidewalks.

- If you decide to park at Meadowbrook Plaza: Be a customer. Make a purchase at a store and leave the bag visible in your car. Park away from the businesses. Note: For past rallies, the owner of the Plaza has expressed concerns about parking. Keep an eye out for tow trucks.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early | Woodstock, GA
events.description:
**No Kings: Vote Early | Woodstock, GA**

Saturday, October 17, starting at 2 p.m., in front of the Chambers at City Center in downtown Woodstock. Join NGA CAN on the sidewalk for No Kings: Vote Early, a nationwide day of action on the first Saturday of early voting in Georgia. Bring a sign, bring three friends, and march with us to vote early.

**About The Event**

Join us in front of the Chambers at City Center with signs, flags, and voting information for anyone who stops to ask. We'll begin lining up in single file at 2 p.m. This is a legal, peaceful, permitless, First Amendment protected gathering held entirely on the public sidewalks. We stay in single file, keep the walkway clear for pedestrians, stay out of driveways and the roadway, and follow all pedestrian and traffic laws. Please stand as far back from the curb as possible so people can easily walk past in front of you. Family friendly and open to everyone.

After sign waving, we'll march together in single file from downtown to the early voting location at 7545 North Main Street, Building 200, Woodstock, GA 30188. Anyone in line before 4 p.m. gets to vote. Georgia law prohibits campaign materials within 150 feet of a polling place, so we'll set our signs aside before we reach that area. Volunteers will be waiting just outside it to hold your sign, and you can pick it up after you vote.

**Why October 17?**

October 17 is the first Saturday of early voting in Georgia. Advance voting for the November 3 general election runs October 13 through October 30, and during that window you can vote at any early voting location in your county of residence. The Woodstock location serves Cherokee County voters, and neighbors from other counties are welcome to march with us and vote early in their home county. Georgia's voter registration deadline for this election is October 5.

**How to prepare**

* Check your registration and find your early voting locations at https://mvp.sos.ga.gov/ or check anywhere in the country at https://www.vote.org/am-i-registered-to-vote/
* Make your plan to vote at https://www.nokings.org/nkve-resources and pick your day, your site, and your backup plan.
* Bring your photo ID if you plan to vote with us.
* Recruit friends. We start in our own communities and neighborhoods, where voting happens. Triple your impact by inviting three people.
* Bring the basics: a sign, water, sunscreen, and comfortable shoes for the walk. We're out rain or shine.
* If you plan to vote, leave No Kings shirts, buttons, and hats at home or be ready to cover them before you go inside.
* Broaden your impact. Post photos and videos with #NoKingsVoteEarly and encourage others to vote.

**Questions?** Email hello@woodstockcan.org

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. On October 17th, No Kings: Vote Early is a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de‑escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Breakfast Briefing: Women, Money & Politics in 2026 - Who Gives and Why It Matters
events.description:
Please join us on Wednesday, October 14, at 8:30 a.m. ET on Zoom for our next Breakfast Briefing: Women, Money & Politics in 2026 - Who Gives and Why It Matters.

We will be joined by Kira Sanbonmatsu, Professor of Political Science at Rutgers University, Senior Scholar at the Center for American Women and Politics (CAWP), and author. Kira will share new data from CAWP’s 2026 Women, Money & Politics Watch project, which she leads, with a particular focus on donor demographics and what the data reveals about who participates in political fundraising and how those patterns may affect women candidates.

In addition to her research on gender, race and ethnicity, political parties, state politics, and money in politics, Kira is the author and coauthor of numerous books and reports on women’s political representation. She received her Ph.D. in Government from Harvard University and her B.A. in Political Science from the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

As we work to elect more women to office, understanding who funds campaigns and what those patterns mean for women candidates is critical.

events.title: Resist to Exist: Voting Block Party
events.description:
Voting is more than a civic duty—it’s a celebration of our community’s power!

Voting should never feel confusing, inaccessible, or like something we have to do alone. So we’re bringing joy to the polls with a Community Block Party in East Oakland!

📍 When & Where
Saturday, October 24
12:00–3:00 PM

Allen Temple | East Oakland
Allen Temple is an early voting center and will be open during the event. That means you can pull up, cast your ballot, and then stick around to enjoy the all-ages, family-friendly block party!

Oakland is the Town of resistance.

We’ve resisted gentrification, displacement, housing crises, mass industry and job loss, eminent domain, and the other forces that continue to make it harder for our communities to stay, thrive, and call Oakland home. We resist every day simply by being here, loving our people, and fighting for a future where Black and Brown, working-class, immigrant, and formerly incarcerated communities have the opportunity to belong.

Our vote is no different. Our vote is one way we resist. One way we show up. One way we say: we are here, and we matter.

Our grandparents and great-grandparents organized and fought for the right to vote. We are not far removed from a time when Black and Brown people were systematically denied that right. Today, our voting rights continue to face challenges that threaten equal access to the ballot.

We refuse to take our history—or our power—for granted.

We Choose Joy. We Choose Community. We Choose to Show Up! 

Voting should be something we do together! So, pull up to Resist to Exist, the Oakland Rising Voter Block Party. 

Bring your people. Bring your ballot. Bring your joy.
See you at the Block Party!

location.venue: Woodburn Transit Center Next to I-5 Exit 271

events.description:
There is no more important place to stand on Oct. 17 to advocate for the right to vote and live in a democracy than Woodburn. Why? Woodburn has the highest per capita ICE detention rate in Oregon. We are Oregon's Ground Zero. Many days, before 8 AM, another Woodburn parent has been detained and taken away. 

On this No Kings Vote Early Day, stand with Woodburn in a show of support for our city's grieving families, and to make it clear to everyone, that despite all the intimidation and losses we've lived through lately, we are still going to vote, and we are still going to vote early.

On this fourth No Kings Day, as we stand up for the right to vote and to live in a democracy, please come stand with the people of Woodburn. On October 17, it may be the most important place you could stand in the state of Oregon to fight for the right to vote and live in a democracy, where voters make the decisions, not dictators or their masked agents. 

Support our little city's effort to get out the vote despite all the adversity we currently are facing. Stand with Woodburn so everyone can see that we are unbowed, determined and not only ready to fill in our ballots, but we're ready to take our ballots to a ballot box early.

Oregon ballots arrive soon after Oct. 23 and Woodburn, Oregon is ready to vote early no matter what other challenges are happening around us. Come help us share that message on Oct. 17 from 10 AM to 1 PM.

address_lines: North Carolina 55 & Beaver Creek Commons Drive

events.description:
**Come join us at No Kings:  Vote Early Apex on Saturday October 17, from 9:30 – 11:00 AM** on the public sidewalks surrounding the entrance to Beaver Creek Commons (at the intersection of Highway 55 and Beaver Creek Commons Drive.)  

**Think of this Honk & Wave rally as your pre-game to early voting!** Come join us to get fired up and let everyone driving past us know how important it is to vote early this year.  Afterwards, you can head on over to the John Brown Community Center to cast your votes!

**Early voting is the safest way to make sure that your vote will be counted.**  There have been efforts to purge voters from the voter registration rolls.  If you discover this when you go to vote during Early Voting (from October 15 – 31), you can immediately use same-day voter registration to correct your voter registration record.  If you don’t discover this until November 3, though, you’ll be out of luck, as registration changes cannot be made on election day.  The best you could hope for then would be a chance to file a provisional ballot, but there is a high chance that it would be denied.
