events.title: New York's Youth Election Protection Training Series! (2026 General Election)
events.description:
You’ve seen the headlines: Threats of ICE at poll sites and in our neighborhoods, Supreme Court decisions greenlighting mid-decade gerrymandering to suppress Black voters, federal attacks on mail-in voting, and videos of long lines and broken machines at poll sites. With critical elections this year, New York voters are in the crosshairs of federal overreach in our streets and at the ballot box. 

It's going to be up to us to protect our democracy, defend free and fair elections, and make sure our friends, families, neighbors, and communities can vote with dignity, free from fear and intimidation, and that the will of the people prevails. Join Generation Vote and the Hands Off Our Vote NY Election Protection coalition to help protect our elections and become a trained volunteer for poll monitoring! 

At our 1.5 hour training you will understand your voting rights, challenges to youth voting rights, de-escalation techniques, and how to help voters at the polls. Come ready to join our movement of young people defending free and fair elections in New York and beyond. 

GenVote is sparking a movement of young people fighting for our right to vote and a just democracy for all. Since 2020, Generation Vote has been the leading (and one of the only) youth election protection training partners in the United States.  

Join GenVote and Hands Off NY Election Protection Coalition to become a trained volunteer for poll monitoring today!

events.title: Voter Support Team Informational Meeting
events.description:
## Volunteers needed!

### Threats to free and fair elections are coming from many directions, and **"We want YOU!"** to serve as a **Voter Support Team Volunteer on Election Day!**

Attend one of our brief Informational Meetings for an introduction to our Voter Support Team Program.

**Voter Support Teams are newly developed for the 2026 Midterms.** Teams will observe activities outside and inside polling places on Election Day. Training will be provided.

NE Lake County Indivisible has an active Action and Election Protection Team. Aligned with National Indivisible directives, we aim to engage members in a range of activities to get out the vote, educate voters, and hold rallies. 

Connect with us at https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org/newsletter/ to get all our action updates!

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### **ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:**

NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

More about us can be found here:

https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org

https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Some quotes from past participants:
- "It was great working with like-minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"
- "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."
- "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."
- "Well organized. Liked the materials included in the kits. Good location. Nice people. Thank you very much!"
- "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others."

events.title: No Kings - Promote the Vote

location.venue: Continental Square at the intersection of Market & George Streets

events.description:
For more than a year, millions of people have come together to send a clear message: in America, we have No Kings! Power doesn't belong to billionaires, strongmen, or politicians who think they're above accountability — it belongs to the people, but only if we use it.

Join us as we rally together once again – on October 17th to Promote the Vote.  We’re turning people power into voter power. We know voting is crucial in giving us the agency to make our voices heard. No Kings is about making sure every eligible voter has a plan to vote, knows their options, and is ready to make their voice count. Because in America, the people choose their leaders. Leaders do not get to choose who votes, whose voices matter, or what future our communities deserve.

For generations, everyday people have changed the course of this country by organizing, marching, and voting. Progress has always been won when people who have been pushed aside come together, claim their power, and demand to be heard. Our role as voters doesn’t end when we cast our ballot, either. We’ll participate in election protection efforts on November 3rd and afterwards if necessary.

No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings. We decide.

Join us on October 17th!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Dansville, New York
events.description:
Attention New Yorkers in the Western Finger Lakes region! 

Be part of the NO KINGS movement in Dansville by joining our event in support of EARLY VOTING, which starts October 24th in our area.

INDIVISIBLE ACTION NY and HEMLOCK RISING INDIVISIBLE are jointly sponsoring an event in Dansville on October 17th.

Bring your signs, your spirit, your determination! Sign up to find out how you can help protect our elections, and join us in urging our communities to VOTE EARLY.


**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Yardley Indivisible Breakfast Gathering - LET'S LEAVE IT ALL ON THE FIELD!
events.description:
TWO WEEKS. FOUR DAYS. LET’S LEAVE IT ON THE FIELD.

The clock is running—and we’re in the final stretch.

With just two weeks and four days to go, let’s gather over good food, lively conversation, and the company of people who are committed to doing their part.

This is our chance to reconnect, recharge, and refuel for the weeks ahead.
 
Leaving it on the field doesn’t mean doing everything or burning ourselves out. It means giving what we can give—one more call, one more door, one more postcard, one more conversation, one more person brought into the effort.

Every one of us has something to give. And we need all of it.
So come have breakfast with us, bring a friend, and let’s head into these final weeks with energy, purpose, and one another.

Let’s show up. Let’s do our part. And let’s leave nothing on the field.

And don’t come alone—BRING A FRIEND! There’s always room at our table for someone new.

COME FOR THE COFFEE. STAY FOR THE CAMARADERIE.  LEAVE READY FOR THE WORK AHEAD!

Order your own breakfast from the many delicious choices. Hope to see you there!

(*Look for the YI group table when you arrive)

events.title: Intro to Community Organizing: Growing to Win (MV)
events.description:
How do we win? How do we advance our goals for social change? We get organized! Community organizing is people power in action. It's about uniting around a shared goal to make a difference together. Anyone can be an organizer. You don’t need a degree or years of experience—just a passion for change and a willingness to listen and learn.

_Billionaires are already organized, and we can be too!_

In this training opportunity, facilitator Brian Eaton will lead participants in an exploration of Structure Based Organizing, a century-old technique for building power and creating durable solutions to issues that matter to a community.

Participants in this one-hour workshop will learn:

- How Structure Based Organizing works—its key principles and techniques

- How Structured Organizing Conversations act as the foundation of successful campaigns

- How Structure Based Organizing can enable us to build local power into a mass movement

**Note: Enrollment limited to 8 participants.**

events.title: National Coming Out Day Mega Mobilization

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Team Wiener, HRC, Equality California, the Alice B. Toklas LGBTQ Democratic Club, the CADEM LGBTQ Caucus, and the United Democratic Club for our biggest canvass launch of the campaign — a National Coming Out Day day of action to knock doors, talk with voters, and cover the entire Castro and surrounding neighborhoods for Scott Wiener for Congress!

This is a historic moment: electing Scott would make him the first openly LGBTQ member of Congress from not just San Francisco, but the entire Bay Area. We've already brought the Castro to Sacramento, with Scott standing as one of the most effective legislators in the country for the LGBTQ community. Now it's time to bring the Castro to Congress, so our community can keep leading the fight to protect LGBTQ people nationwide.

We're just over three weeks from Election Day, and this is a tight race — whether Scott wins depends on what we do between now and November 3rd. Every door we knock and every voter we talk to makes a difference, and the window to get involved is closing fast.

We're kicking things off in style: come for drag performances and high energy before we hit the pavement to knock doors. This is shaping up to be the most fun, highest-energy canvass launch of the whole campaign, and we want you there for it.

We'll meet at the top of Dolores Park, by the 20th St Muni stop, for a brief training and overview before we head out to knock doors. Whether this is your first time canvassing or you've done it many times before, you'll be fully supported every step of the way — no prior experience required. We'll provide all the materials you need and pair you with experienced volunteers if helpful.

This is a family-friendly, in-person event, and all are welcome. Come out (literally!) to meet neighbors, build community, and help elect Scott Wiener to Congress.

Voting is how we speak to power and how we assert our own. We vote our values and cherished ideals. We can and will steer America to be a more caring nation and principled society. Join us at this moment of truth  in our nation's history, and let freedom ring!  

Bring a sign to inspire others to take an active part in our democracy! Let your sign express our highest aspirations, why America matters to the world, and/or why you're proud that you're an American. Increase your visibility with a family-friendly costume, flags, and banners. Bring friends, family, neighbors, coworkers, and everyone you know of all ages for a fun morning of joyful community! Members of SoBoCo Indivisible will be available to help answer election questions! 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next, and together we will win!**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to the wanna-be-kings, billionaires, and politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early is not purely a protest. Instead, October 17th is a day of nonpartisan voter participation. We are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensure every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote, has the opportunity to make their voice heard, and understands the importance and impact of their vote.

No one person gets to decide our leaders. We the voters do! On October 17th, join us in Superior as other local events happen all across the country to Get Out the Early Vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: CRI General Meeting
events.description:
Join your fellow activists on Tues, Oct 13 for CRI’s last GENERAL MEETING before the midterms!  

During this HANDS-ON, INTERACTIVE meeting, we’ll be planning for NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY on Oct 17 and preparing for EARLY VOTING (Oct 24 – Nov 1), ELECTION DAY (Nov 3), and WHAT HAPPENS NEXT! 

After providing UPDATES AND ACTIONS, we’ll leave ample time for DISCUSSION AND QUESTIONS and then break out for CONVERSATIONS and COMMUNITY BUILDING with No King: Early Voting and Party to the Polls SIGN MAKING and PLANNING ACTIVITIES. 

So, grab a friend or two, some sign making materials, maybe a snack to share, and come out for an informative and fun evening, while preparing to save our democracy!

Our mutual aid group will be collecting items before the meeting to be used to help community members in need. Go to https://crinj.org/malist for this month's list of items.

Merch is back! Bring some cash or get your Venmo ready, limited CRI/No Kings merch will be available for purchase!

events.title: Blockwalk for SBOE6
events.description:
🚪 Let’s Talk to Our Neighbors About Michelle Palmer!

Join us for a neighborhood block walk to meet voters, listen to our neighbors, and introduce them to Michelle Palmer, candidate for Texas State Board of Education District 6.

Michelle is a teacher who understands Texas classrooms firsthand. She believes our students deserve fact-based, high-quality education and that educators should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape our schools.

This is about more than knocking on doors—it’s about building relationships, listening to our community, and making sure voters know what’s at stake for public education.

💙 No experience necessary—training and materials will be provided!
👟 Wear comfortable shoes and bring a friend.
🏡 We’ll walk together, talk with neighbors, and share why Michelle Palmer is the right choice for District 6.

Every door matters. Every conversation matters. Every vote matters.

Let’s get Michelle Palmer elected to the State Board of Education!

events.description:
RAIN OR SHINE, WE'RE BUILDING 1 TAMPA. 5,000 VOICES.
Join Gary Hartfield for Mayor and Tampa residents from across the city on Sunday, October 11 at 2:00 PM for the official 5,000 Strong Petition Launch, the public kickoff of our citywide effort to collect the petitions needed to help put Gary on the ballot.

We’re bringing people together, equipping community members with the tools and training they need, and sending teams across Tampa to collect petitions and engage voters where they live, work, worship, and gather.

Our first goal is 500 petitions toward 5,000.

Those first 500 signatures are more than an event-day goal. They represent the first major benchmark in a grassroots effort to build momentum across Tampa, grow a broad coalition of residents, and move Gary one step closer to the ballot.

But 5,000 Strong is about more than signatures.

Every petition represents a conversation with a Tampa resident. Every conversation is an opportunity to listen, bring more voices into the process, and build support around a shared vision for Tampa’s future. This is how a people-powered campaign grows, one neighborhood and one person at a time.

Whether you’re ready to collect petitions, organize your neighborhood, host a future petition party, or simply show up and be part of the launch, there is a place for you.

500 is our first milestone. 5,000 is where we’re headed. September 27 is where we begin.

Today we train. Today we deploy. Today we start building 5,000 Strong.

Register now to receive the location and be part of the movement from the very beginning.

If weather impacts our outdoor plans, the October 11 Petition Launch will become a hybrid event, giving you the option to participate in person or online.

ONLINE PARTICIPATION
If you participate online, you will receive access to our petition collector training and instructions for activating your personal network.
Your goal will be to connect with people in your network and secure 25 commitments from eligible Tampa voters who are willing to complete a petition to help Gary Hartfield get on the ballot.

After securing commitments, our team will coordinate with you to arrange petition pickup.

Once petitions are completed, they can be returned to the campaign office for counting and tracking.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early! Hyannis - Cape Cod, 12-2 Hyannis Airport Rotary, Hyannis, MA
events.description:
What began in 2025 as a single day of defiance has become a sustained national resistance to tyranny, spreading from small towns to city centers and across every community determined to defend democracy. Our peaceful movement is bigger than ever.


**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

When our families are under attack and costs are pushing people to the brink, silence is not an option. We will defend ourselves and our communities against this administration’s unjust and cruel acts of violence.

On October 17th, rise up, take to the streets, and say it loud: RISE UP, FIGHT BACK, WE WILL VOTE AND WE WILL VOTE EARLY!!! No one will stop us from exercising our right to vote.

And, early voting begins the day of the protest! Go to your early voting location from 9am and then join us!

Cape Cod Women for Change, Mid-Cape Indivisible ARE SPONSORING THIS Event as part of the national No Kings Day national protest.

Spread the word to your trusted friends and neighbors. This will be the largest protest in American history, continuing a time-honored tradition of non-violent, democratic opposition to a rogue regime gone off the rails. We want peace and justice, fairness and the Rule of Law.

This is our opportunity to show the power of the people. We are stronger than they are. There are more of us. We will prevail.

Join us October 17!

Join us in community as we protest this fascist regime!

Dress for the weather, this protest will take place rain or shine here at the Hyannis Airport rotary, and across the country.

Prepare to celebrate our growing army against this fascist oligarchic regime! It's important that we continue to send a message to Trump and MAGA that we are not going to back down.

This will be a national protest, and the participation may present logistical challenges unless you are prepared. 
Please CARPOOL if possible, and do not block traffic to drop people off. Please park in places that do NOT interfere with open businesses. 
Do not use the CVS parking lot. If you are capable of walking, the overflow at the Cape Cod Mall and the overflow at the Whole Foods (former K-Mart) plaza gives you crossing via crosswalks and sidewalk access. 
Do not park or walk through Luke's Liquor's Parking Lot - they don't want us near their business (remember that when you shop!)

The airport allows for paid parking that is not too expensive, $5 first hour $1 every hour after- $13 for 24 hrs. Airport parking gives access to several areas to stand.

During the protest we ask that you:

-Try not to cross roadways during the protest

-Respect and follow the instructions of safety marshals and police

-Don't engage with counter protestors

-And enjoy these two hours together like millions of others across the country and around the world!

It is helpful to know your rights and understand de-escalation – here are trainings given by ACLU before previous No Kings: -https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ji4Z4W2NV4U -https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YSKENhoOx0s&t=575s

Here is a pdf of tips about de-escalation: https://capecodwomenforchange.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/desecalation-tactics-aclu.pdf

We are not going to have guest speakers so we aren't asking people to cross roadways to hear them.

Musicians are invited to attend!

Costumes are welcome, we have several blow-up character costumes or bring your own.

Bring your sign or hold one of our many flags or signs.

Photography is welcome, this is a public space.

Would you like to volunteer to help us with safety? Sign up here: https://www.mobilize.us/indivisible/event/1034056/

events.description:
## NO KINGS - Vote Early
**Rally @ NE 28th & E Burnside**

NO KINGS is a coalition of many organizations, Indivisible included. Initially, the goal was to turn out millions of Americans in opposition to everything the Trump regime stands for -- and to demonstrate  that power doesn’t belong to kings, billionaires, or boot-licking politicians.

NO KINGS III, in October ‘25, saw a shift from massive centralized demonstrations to showing strength in an explosion of protests in neighborhoods, towns and cities – everywhere, all at once.

But gatherings are only a tactic. They are not a strategy. Single-day gatherings will not topple this would-be dictator. 

Now NO KINGS is poised, not for a tactical shift, but a strategic shift – from mobilizing people, to wielding people power. A successful NO KINGS - Vote Early will achieve the largest early vote in history, the largest midterm vote in history, and a result so massive it is unassailable.

Still the billionaire tech bros, white supremacists, corrupt grifters who surround the wanna-be king, and the mad king himself will not cede power without a fight, in the form of a predictable and entirely fabricated crisis.

It isn’t enough to vote, we must protect the results. That is why Indivisible Oregon is not just rallying, we are organizing. Our corner captains for NO KINGS - Early Vote will be circulating with A Pledge to Defend the Vote.

The Pledge is simple, “In the case of a call for a mass mobilization to defend the vote, I pledge to show up and I will come with three compatriots.”

So...Join Us! To raise voices as one - let’s line the streets. Bring family, neighbors, friends, signs, flags, noise-makers and banners to promote the Vote, especially the Early Vote. Then we vote. We vote early. We help our community vote. And we protect the results.

**Show up on October 17. Vote Early. Sign the Pledge.**

events.title: A Joint Letter to End Foreign Wars Together
events.description:
Dear Congressman Ro Khanna,

We write to thank you for your sustained efforts to end the Iran War. This cause is profoundly important for our nation and for every one of us.

The Iran War is destroying our lives — our wallets, our families, and our future. Every dollar spent on bombs is a dollar stolen from our schools, hospitals, roads, and homes. Congress must strengthen its oversight of the executive branch's power to initiate unnecessary wars.

We recognize your leadership and strong voice on ending foreign wars. This war is unconstitutional, drains our national resources, and harms ordinary families. We cannot bear another unnecessary war — now or in the future. We believe you can represent our voice and will work to end this war. 

We hope you will clarify your stance and your plan, including:

•	Clearly and publicly articulating the necessity of ending the Iran War.

•	Explaining how you will work to end this war.

•	Committing to continue your oversight role at the congressional level, ensuring war powers return to the constitutional framework.

•	Entering constituents' appeals and stories into the Congressional Record, so the people's voices become part of the official archive.

We the people are tired of foreign wars. Now is time to end it.

We look forward to hearing your response.

Respectfully,

Co-Sponsors:

Women Forward

Teachers Unify To End Gun Violence

Field Team 6

Davis Democratic Club

People Power United

50501 Supporters

events.title: Road to Black November "Boots on the Ground" Rally & Training
events.description:
Road to Black November is moving into the field—and we need all hands on deck!

The purpose of Road to Black November is simply to help increase voter participation in Jefferson County, Alabama.

Join Faith & Works for our virtual Boots on the Ground Rally and Canvass Training. This weekly gathering will prepare volunteers to go door to door across Jefferson County and help Black residents check their voter status, register or update their information, find accurate election information and make a plan to vote.

Faith & Works’ data identified more than 9,000 Black residents who are inactive or have been dropped from the voter file in the communities we are working to reach. Some residents may believe they are ready to vote, only to discover a problem when they arrive at the polls. We cannot wait until November 3 to reach them.

During the rally and training, you will:

Learn the Road to Black November canvassing strategy.
Practice how to introduce yourself and speak with residents.
Learn how to help residents check their voter status or register.
Review our canvassing tools, safety practices and volunteer expectations.
Get answers to your questions.
Choose upcoming canvassing shifts and invite others to join you.

No canvassing experience is required. Faith & Works will provide training, materials, scripts and support. Please bring your calendar so you can sign up for every shift you are available to serve.

Canvassing begins Saturday, September 26, and continues every day through Election Day, Tuesday, November 3—including Election Day. Our virtual Rally and Training will take place every Thursday at 7:00 p.m. Central Time.

We are not asking you to do everything. We are asking you to do your part. Invite a friend or family member to register, attend the training and canvass with you.

Road to Black November is strictly nonpartisan. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties, and we will not tell residents who to vote for.

Learn more at www.RoadToBlackNovember.com.

events.title: Help Flip Colorado CD-8: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Thornton!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an innovative new program that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

Knock on every door in the neighborhood, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to.

Have real conversations that listen deeply to voters’ concerns.

Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, a canvassing partner, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

About the program

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

Why we’re starting early: We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

How we’ll go big: knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

How we’ll go deep: practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

Tree Pittsburgh will provide all the safety gear and tools necessary to get the work done!  Boots or sturdy sneakers are always recommended at Tree Pittsburgh Events. Long pants and sleeves are encouraged. 

**New to volunteering with Tree Pittsburgh? All new volunteers must [complete this form](https://action.treepittsburgh.org/a/volunteer-agreement-form) before their first event with us.**

All volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult for the duration of the event. No need to register youth volunteers online, but we appreciate a heads-up by replying to your confirmation email!

Volunteer Events are held rain or shine, but events will be cancelled for extreme weather. Review Tree Pittsburgh's [Volunteer Event Weather Policy](https://www.treepittsburgh.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Tree-Pgh-Volunteer-Event-Weather-Policy.pdf) here and reach out with any questions!

events.title: Women of Michigan Action Network (WOMAN) October Action Meeting
events.description:
Special guests in October include candidates for Midland Public School board election - there are four candidates and only 2 seats. This may be the only public forum where voters can hear from multiple school board candidates. (Earlier plans for the meeting included Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet as a speaker, but her schedule has changed and she will not be at the meeting.)  

We'll also share details about our plans for No Kings Vote Early, which is coming up on Oct 17th.

Looking for a community to help you stay sane during Trump 2.0? 

Attended our No Kings events and want to get more involved? 

In need of ideas for how to help preserve democracy and friends to do it with? Come to a WOMAN meeting! 

WOMAN is an Indivisible group. Persons of any gender identity are welcome. (And check out www.indivisible.org to learn more about this great group.)

Our agenda usually includes time for community building as well as information about what's going on and where we can make a difference. We often have speakers about relevant topics and we hear from elected officials.  

Beverages are available to purchase from our MI Element hosts, Tony and Suzanne. Coffee, tea, beer, and bottled sodas available. Anyone is welcome to bring snacks to share.

NOTE: We usually meet on the second Tuesday of each month, but in September we will meet on the third Tuesday. The October meeting will likely return to the second Tuesday.

events.title: Hop on the bus from Providence to knock doors in NH!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing State—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Democrats. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** [DETAILS HERE]
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

# Love as Action: Supporting Palestine
## Bearing Witness, Building Hope

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to genocide and ethnic cleansing and for a just and lasting peace for decades. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Chicago area Friends to bear witness and show up for all those impacted by ongoing state violence, whether immigrants in our communities or Palestinians targeted by settlers and Israeli military forces in Gaza and the West Bank.

At 1 PM on Saturday, October 10th, we will gather outside Millennium Park on Michigan Avenue for one hour of silent public worship. Please sign up now and we will provide updates. 

Our intent is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We're gathering monthly across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us!

events.title: The All-of-the-Above Trap: Natural Gas Won’t Lower Your Bill—Clean Energy Will

sponsor.name: New Jersey League of Conservation Voters

events.description:
Join us Wednesday, October 14th at 6 PM for a Zoom webinar with energy experts on why expanding natural gas generation will not solve our affordability problem—and why clean energy is the fastest and most stable solution for meeting growing electricity demand.

Across the country, policymakers are being told that we need to build more natural gas plants to keep up with rising electricity demand and lower energy costs. But new natural gas generation is not a quick fix for affordability. Gas plants can take years to build, depend on fuel with prices that can fluctuate, and can lock consumers into decades of costly infrastructure.

At the same time, renewable energy and battery storage are providing an opportunity to bring more affordable electricity online quickly. Wind and solar have no fuel costs, helping protect consumers from the price volatility associated with fossil fuels. With investments in storage, transmission, and grid upgrades, clean energy can help meet growing demand while building a more reliable and affordable electricity system.

During this webinar, we’ll discuss why the conversation around energy affordability needs to change. Instead of asking whether we need more natural gas, we should be asking how we can get more affordable, reliable electricity online as quickly as possible—and how policymakers can make the investments necessary to do that.

We’ll also discuss the importance of protecting consumers from massive rate increases and ensuring that monopoly utilities and large new electricity users, including data centers, are held accountable for the costs they create.

Join us to learn why the fastest path to affordable reliability is investing in the clean energy, storage, and grid infrastructure that can be delivered this decade—not locking consumers into decades of new natural gas generation.

events.title: Fall Voter Mobilization and Training Series
events.description:
Dauphin County Democratic Committee: Fall Voter Mobilization & Training Series

This three-part virtual training series equips district leaders, committee persons, and volunteers with the necessary tools, state-level updates, and operational strategies to register and mobilize voters across Dauphin County. Will also have a hybrid in person option meeting at culture and commerce co working at 19 ½ N 4th st Harrisburg, PA

Program Overview & Strategy

Turnout Starts with Registration: Research indicates that for young voters (ages 18–24), the primary barrier to voting is navigating registration rather than lack of interest.

County-Wide Action Goal: District leaders will collaborate to coordinate at least four targeted voter registration drives across Dauphin County prior to the election.

Format: Three 60-minute virtual evening sessions featuring live operational training, state policy updates, actionable toolkits, and quick recaps of prior takeaways.

Official Portals: Direct all voters and volunteers to verify records using Dauphin County Registration & Elections or connect via the Dauphin County Democratic Committee

events.title: Finish Strong to Win BIG and flip MN-1! (Swing Left Twin Cities)
events.description:
This is it, folks! Our last chance to get out the vote for Jake Johnson and flip MN-1. 

This time we'll hit the streets in Zumbrota, MN – a town of 4,000 that went 60% for Trump in 2024. The Johnson campaign has not been active here, so we will use this last canvass to provide coverage there. 

Now... who's this guy we're canvassing for, anyway?

Johnson is a high school teacher seeking to follow in the steps of another teacher – Minnesota Governor Tim Walz – who flipped this district in the 2006 blue wave. Johnson has proven to be a strong candidate and is running competitively with Finstad, the Republican incumbent (and rubber-stamp for Trump's hare-brained schemes).

This race is absolutely within reach. But only if we get out there and do the work.

At this canvass, we’ll:
- Knock on **lots of doors**, not just the same voters campaigns usually talk to. Our target turf will be curated, but we're still casting a wide net.
- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.
- **Gently persuade** on-the-fence voters to vote for Democrats.
- Encourage likely Democratic supporters to **make a plan** to vote.
- **Gather insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

This isn’t traditional canvassing – it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Join us and help turn the tide!

-- 
Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
**On location in Renton, Washington**

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.description:
Join us to help ensure that likely Democratic voters in states such as Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio are able to cast their ballots this fall and have their votes counted!

In each shift, we will do phone banking to support current voter protection priorities for the Democratic Party in one of these key states. Our calls may include recruiting volunteers to serve as poll observers, helping voters who have been marked inactive or have other registration issues to update their registration, or helping voters whose ballots have been rejected to fix the issue, known as ballot curing.

We will meet on zoom and provide training, a script, and contact information for targeted voters through the OpenVPB system. No experience or background knowledge required. 

Hosted by the Massachusetts Democratic Party’s Campaign Services Subcommittee in partnership with VoPro Pros, a national volunteer organization focused on voter protection. Open to volunteers anywhere.

events.description:
Why not dress as your favorite political hero and gather to encourage your neighbors to Vote Early? Let's let the numbers in our movement go go over the top to defeat the efforts to prevent your vote from even being cast! Come in costume or not. Come with music or not. Come with intent! Lets celebrate our right to vote!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: CHUH School Levy Friends and Family Text Bank
events.description:
This November, there is a critical levy for the Cleveland Heights-University Heights public school district on the ballot. If it doesn't pass, the district will face millions of dollars in cuts that threaten the essential programs and staff – like teachers, nurses, librarians, and mental health counselors – that our kids rely on every day. We need your help to make sure that doesn't happen!

Please join us for a friends and family text bank, where we will provide training to equip you to reach out to your own CHUH friends, family members, and neighbors to talk to them about why this levy is so important and make sure they get out to vote in favor of it. Relational outreach (aka reaching out to the people we personally know) is the single most effective way to mobilize and boost voter turnout, and it’s a super easy way to help make sure the levy passes!

events.title: The Black Table: YDNC Black Caucus FIRST Annual Friendsgiving
events.description:
Pull up a chair and join the YDNC Black Caucus for our first annual Friendsgiving! The Black Table: An evening of community, connection, and joy. We will begin with our Black Caucus General Meeting and end with a Friendsgiving celebration.

 6:00–6:30 PM | BLACK CAUCUS GENERAL MEETING

We’ll kick off the evening with a brief Black Caucus meeting where we’ll:

- Share updates and upcoming initiatives
- Discuss our goals and priorities moving forward
- Talk about ways members can get involved
- Give members an opportunity to share ideas and connect

After the meeting, we’ll officially transition into our Friendsgiving celebration!

6:30 PM | THE BLACK TABLE: FRIENDSGIVING

Once the meeting wraps, it’s time to eat, fellowship, and celebrate!

We’re asking everyone who is able to bring a dish to share. Whether it’s your favorite family recipe, a holiday classic, a dessert, a side, or something completely your own, bring a little something to add to the table! This is a potluck-style celebration, so the more dishes, the better. 

WHAT TO EXPECT

🍽️ Friendsgiving Dinner
Bring a dish, grab a plate, and enjoy good food with good people.

🥂 Drinks & Mocktails
Enjoy an evening of drinks, conversation, and fellowship. We will have wristbands for anybody 21+

🎶 Music & Black Joy
Relax, socialize, laugh, and enjoy the evening with your Black Caucus family.

🤝🏾 Community & Connection
Build relationships with Black young professionals, organizers, leaders, creatives, and changemakers from across North Carolina.

WHO SHOULD ATTEND?

This event is open to Black Caucus members, prospective members, and Black young adults interested in connecting with the community. You do not have to be politically active to attend. Whether you’re an organizer, professional, student, creative, community member, or simply looking for a space to connect with other Black young adults, there’s a seat at our table for you.

👗 DRESS CODE

Friendsgiving Chic | Elevated Casual

Come cute, comfortable, and ready to fellowship!

WHY “THE BLACK TABLE”?

The table is where we gather.
Where we break bread.
Where we share stories.
Where relationships are built.

Come for the meeting.
Stay for the fellowship.
Bring a dish. Bring a friend. Bring your good energy.

There’s always room at the table. 🖤

Join the Young Democrats of North Carolina Black Caucus for our November General Meeting and FIRST Annual Friendsgiving as we come together to reflect on the work we’ve started, strengthen our connections, and build toward what’s next.

We encourage everyone to bring a dish to share! Whether it’s a family favorite, a holiday classic, a side, dessert, or something you simply love to make, bring something to contribute to the table if you’re able.

🍽️ 6:30 PM until 9 PM — Friendsgiving
📍 Raleigh, NC

events.title: Weekly Text Banking

**Text Bank for Hands Off Colorado — Weekly Shift**

Join us for a flexible, remote text banking shift in support of Hands Off Colorado! No experience necessary — everything you need is provided.

**How it works:**

*Every Monday, you'll receive an email with a link to that week's active campaign
*Commit to logging in for at least 1 hour sometime during the week — work whenever fits your schedule
*Scripts are pre-written, and responses to common questions are already prepared for you
*Just click the link, log in, and start sending texts to reach community members

*A computer or smartphone with internet access

### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Brooklyn WFP Canvass for Chris McCreight
events.description:
This upcoming Saturday, join us to knock on doors for Chris McCreight in Bay Ridge.

**Chris is ready to serve.** He's a former small business owner who has proven his commitment to good government. He's worked for Council Member Kayla Santosuosso and Council Member Justin Brannan before that. He's already a Democratic District Leader representing Southern Brooklyn, and he's also worked in the New York State Assembly before.

**Chris will fight for working families.** That includes affordable healthcare and childcare. That includes a fairer tax system. That means investing in transit system, and it means investing in our education system. It also means fighting to protecting immigrant rights, LGBTQ rights, and reproductive rights.

**Chris has a strong coalition behind him.** He's not only backed by local leaders like State Senator Andrew Gounardes and Borough President Antonio Reynoso, but also by statewide leaders like Attorney General Tish James. Unions representing nurses, teachers, and firefighters are backing Chris. Environmental groups, animal rights groups, and LGBTQ groups are backing Chris.

As Chris said at our September chapter meeting, **WFP can make the difference in this race.** Please join us.

events.title: Vote Ready Oklahoma: Voter Prep, Practice & State Question Info
events.description:
Vote Ready Oklahoma

Oklahoma's General Election is November 3. Early voting begins October 28. Vote Ready Oklahoma is your chance to walk in prepared.

Join Indivisible Edmond and Thanks For Voting OK for a nonpartisan community event built around one goal: getting every Oklahoman ready to vote.

Here's what's happening on-site:

🗳️ Mock election — walk through a real ballot start to finish. Great for first-time Oklahoma voters and anyone who wants to see what to expect before Election Day.

⭐ State Questions Info Session · 11:30 AM — a plain-language walkthrough of Oklahoma's 2026 state questions, hosted by Indivisible Edmond. Just what you need to know before you vote.

✍️ Notaries on-site — if you've already received your absentee ballot, bring it and we'll get it notarized so it's ready to hand-deliver or mail.

📋 Sample ballot walkthrough — bring yours or look it up on-site. We'll help you understand what you're seeing before you're standing in the booth.

❓ All-Things-Election Q&A — bring any question you have. Offices and what they do. How elections work. Where to find your precinct and polling place. When and where to vote early. If it's about voting, we've got someone who can answer it.

No party. No pressure. Just Oklahomans getting ready to show up.

Saturday, October 24 · 11:00 AM – 2:00 PM (SQ info session 11:30 AM)
Southern Hills Christian Church · 3207 S Blvd, Edmond, OK

Presented by Indivisible Edmond · In partnership with Thanks For Voting OK · Hosted by Southern Hills Christian Church

This November, Question 3 would replace our current primaries with a "jungle primary," where only the top two finishers advance to the general election, even if both are from the same party. The measure is funded by a small group of wealthy donors, mostly private equity executives. It would mean less choice for voters and more power for big money, and it would shut out minority and working class candidates from the November ballot.

Voters in other states rejected this same playbook in 2024. Help make sure Massachusetts does too.

What you'll do:

Join via zoom- link available upon sign up!

Call fellow Massachusetts voters, share why we're voting No, and ask for their pledge. Every conversation counts.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Madison County, Ohio
events.description:
Join us at the Madison County Courthouse in a show of solidarity to encourage folks to turn out and vote.

Please bring PRO Voting Signs or Signs with Polling Times. We will bring the music, cow bells, and snacks. 
Bring a friend or neighbor or your entire family. This is a pro-democracy engagement event!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Salmonberry Trail Guided Hike: Nehalem River Segment
events.description:
The confluence of the Salmonberry and Nehalem Rivers is an incredibly special place--we are excited to show you the River Segment of the future Salmonberry Trail! We should be seeing some fall colors from the big leaf and vine maples, maybe even some wild mushrooms!

**What to Expect:**
We will hike along the Nehalem River to Snark Creek (1.5 miles in), ~3 miles total. 
The vegetation in this segment is dense along the path, please weary sturdy, closed toed shoes and long pants.
Bring a snack and plenty of water for yourself.

**There’s no formal address and no cell coverage in the area, so here’s the most reliable description:**

Meet at the North end of the Foss Road bridge over the Salmonberry River

**Landmarks:** 15.2 miles east of Mohler, 13 miles south of Elsie
Nearest known point: Morrison Eddy Campground (the hike parking area is 1.3 miles south on Foss Road)

**Coordinates:** 45°44’60.0”N, 123°39’08.9”W

**Map link:** https://maps.app.goo.gl/TrfHCtE91yVFGeQZA

We want everyone to get into the canyon—and out—smoothly.

## How to Get There (Read This Part)

Coming from the Portland area:  
- Head west toward Elsie  
- If you reach the restaurant in Elsie, you’ve gone too far  
- Turn onto Lower Nehalem Road and stay on it all the way to the destination

Coming from Wheeler / Coast side:  
- Take Highway 53 to Miami-Foley Road  
- Follow Miami-Foley to Foss Road  
- Stay on Foss Road to the bridge

[Please read the volunteer waiver](https://salmonberrytrail.org/volunteer-waiver)

- A quick refresher on the Persuasion script and deep canvassing best practices
- Lots of time at the doors having real conversations with voters
- Logging each conversation in the app
- A short debrief with an organizer as you wrap up your shift

events.description:
YOU MUST REGISTER VIA RSVP Link below

Activism that Works”

Sunday, October 11
2:00-4:00
First Parish in Wayland, 225 Boston Post Road

Register for Workshop: https://forms.gle/vWKTmbBtkLwsY3b79

For more information, contact Kate Holland at kholland@uuwayland.org 
and visit https://classmatters.org/activism-that-works/

Betsy Leondar-Wright, social movement scholar
Anne Wright, climate activist

Do you wonder what resistance actions are the most effective in standing up to the Trump administration and the Republicans in Congress?

This interactive two-hour workshop will present theory and case studies that will help us explore the most effective actions and tactics that can be used to create social change – including addressing the current threat to democracy in the U.S. 

Specifically, the workshop will focus on 1) identifying and putting pressure on primary and secondary targets, 2) learning about the importance of communicating with unlikely allies and mobilizing passive supporters, and 3) using creative tactics that draw on cultural resonances of the target audience(s).

Interspersed with learning and studying campaign case studies will be small group discussions and exercises designed to help participants apply concepts to goals and projects they care most about.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Pledge - Orange Works, Hillsborough, NC
events.description:
## We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together raising our voices at marches and rallies to REJECT the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law. 

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early.

**WE** have the power to decide the future. And the more people who participate in our democracy through voting, the more powerful our democracy can be. 

**Why vote early?** With all the changes in election laws, voting early ensures that if there is a problem with your voter registration, you have time to get that fixed! North Carolina has same-day voter registration during early voting but not on election day. **If you wait until election day to vote and there is an issue with your registration, you will have to cast a provisional ballot and take extra steps to ensure your vote is counted.** 

Now is the time to raise our voices by voting! Join No Kings: Vote Early - Pledge to the Polls by signing up on Mobilize and choosing a time slot on the sign-up genius when you would like to vote early on October 17. Then make your plan and bring three people with you! Let's make this year the highest voter turnout ever!

## Ready to pledge? 
Pick a time slot on the [SignUPGenius for Orange Works](https://www.signupgenius.com/go/20F0D4AAAAE22A7F5C16-65989944-nokings#/).

Here's what to do next:

1. Find your people! Who should you bring?

2. Get ready to go! Bring your [photo ID](https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id)

3. Head to the polls!

4. Let us know you voted early!

events.title: Standout to SUPPORT IMMIGRANTS- No Fear Street Theater - Saturdays 11am-1pm

sponsor.name: No Fear Street Theater in MA

address_lines: Intersection of Mall Road and District Ave.

events.description:
Speechifying, Shakespeare, & Sea Shanties! Every week, we stand on Burlington Mall Road with signs, costumes and flags. We come out to show support for our immigrant neighbors, express our shame at ICE, and build community in opposition to the cruel and unconstitutional actions of our government. We are there to tell the world that there is a ICE CONCENTRATION CAMP just two blocks away. 

We are not there merely to make propaganda against ICE. We are there to make propaganda against fear.

Every car that honks in support as they pass is in a small way joining the Resistance. Many who honk may be expressing themselves against ICE terror for the first time. This breaks the ice, and makes it easier for them to take the next steps. It helps them help others to overcome their fear. We are there to cause a ripple effect. To fight against the terror visited on immigrants, we need to fight against our own internalized terror. We have nothing to fear. We are America, fighting back. If you REGISTER by FRIDAY, you will be notified of cancellations by email. All events held rain or shine & only cancel for large storms or high winds. We recommend dressing comfortably for the weather and bring a water bottle. Bring your sign in support of Immigrants or you are most welcome to use one of the ones we have on hand. 

This is a creative, participatory protest. If you support immigrants and their constitutional rights, join us!

https://www.nofearstreettheater.com/

https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61584725253124

PARKING, PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION & other INFO: This is an outdoor event held at our standout area at the CORNER of MALL ROAD & DISTRICT AVE. The sidewalk area has a paved area and also a grassy area with trees in the background. There is some PARKING about 2 blocks away. Please NOTE: parking that is closer to the standout is private parking & reserved for staff and customers of the businesses and shopping center. ( Some cars have been towed from the private parking, so we recommend that people chose other options.) Parking info. for the recommended parking areas will be sent to registrants. Public transportation is also available through the MBTA 350 route, LexExpress & LRTA all of which have stops within 1 block of our standout area.

events.title: Knock Doors in Hagerstown!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Pledge - Drakeford Library, Carrboro, NC
events.description:
## We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together raising our voices at marches and rallies to REJECT the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early.

**WE** have the power to decide the future. And the more people who participate in our democracy through voting, the more powerful our democracy can be.

**Why vote early?** With all the changes in election laws, voting early ensures that if there is a problem with your voter registration, you have time to get that fixed! North Carolina has same-day voter registration during early voting but not on election day. **If you wait until election day to vote and there is an issue with your registration, you will have to cast a provisional ballot and take extra steps to ensure your vote is counted.**

Now is the time to raise our voices by voting! Join No Kings: Vote Early - Pledge to the Polls by signing up on Mobilize and choosing a time slot on the sign-up genius when you would like to vote early on October 17. Then make your plan and bring three people with you! Let's make this year the highest voter turnout ever!

## Ready to pledge?
Pick a time slot on the [SignUPGenius for Drakeford Library](https://www.signupgenius.com/go/20F0D4AAAAE22A7F5C16-65988151-pledge#/).

Here's what to do next:

 1. Find your people! Who should you bring?

 2. Get ready to go! Bring your [photo ID](https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id)

 3. Head to the polls!

 4. Let us know you voted early!


*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. **Why vote early?** With all the changes in election laws, voting early ensures that if there is a problem with your voter registration, you have time to get that fixed! North Carolina has same-day voter registration during early voting but not on election day. **If you wait until election day to vote and there is an issue with your registration, you will have to cast a provisional ballot and take extra steps to ensure your vote is counted.**

# No Kings –Vote Early Burlington, VT!  October 17 Honk & Wave Events

## On October 17 from 11:00 a.m. – 12:15 pm, at five busy Burlington street locations, democracy advocates will gather with signs and noise makers to joyfully remind Burlington residents to mail their ballots by October 20 to ensure delivery by November 3.  We will also remind voters that ballots can be delivered to the Burlington City Clerk’s office and at ballot drop off boxes located around the city. Join Queen City Indivisible Vermont for the Vote Early - Honk and Waves at one of the five locations listed below. 

## 1. On Church Street in Front of City Hall (149 Church St.)

## 2. On the sidewalk at intersection of Pine Street and Marble Avenue (near 382 Pine St.)

## 3. On the North Avenue sidewalk at the entrance to Ethan Allen Shopping Plaza (1127 North Ave.)

## 4. On Main Street sidewalk next to UVM’s Davis Student Center (590 Main St.)

## 5. Large Banner Reveal at the Overpass on Rte. 127 (enter on the bike path at the end of Ethan Allen Parkway)

### Come with your Vote Early sign such as (Don’t Delay-Vote Today) (Mail Ballots before October 20) (Vote Early) (Make Your Plan to Vote) (VOTER PORTAL vote.vermont.gov) (Find Ballot - Vote Now) and be part of this No Kings nonpartisan voter action day. If you are so inclined come in costume, bring drums, bells, bubbles, anything that will bring attention to our visibility groups. We want a big presence and a festive atmosphere so invite friends and family to come along.

### Our job at this No Kings event is to urge Vermont voters to submit their ballots early to make sure their voice is heard. Remember, all registered Vermonters were sent mail-in ballots by the end of September. 
 
## Why attend?

### In America the people choose their leaders. Leaders do not choose who votes, whose voices count or what futures our communities deserve. Voting early gives us the power to make our voices heard on our terms, before election day, before any last-minute chaos and before anyone else can decide what happens next. Our democracy depends on every eligible voter having the freedom to participate without intimidation, inference or barriers.

events.title: Carrollton AREA Democrats - Nico Nights with Neighbors

location.venue: Nico's Cocina - Event Room (to right of restaurant)

events.description:
WELCOME to our once a month (third Wednesday) meeting of the Carrollton AREA Democrats Club.  Our focus is to get to know our Neighbors - to meet like-minded folks for fellowship, education, solidarity and purpose.  Learn how WE can shape our plans as we seek to SAVE OUR COUNTRY AND DEMOCRACY!  

Our November 18th meeting is a continuation of our mission to understand and get to know our neighbors better as we take a timely look at our "Mosaic of Carrollton" - people living in our community and how we can be Allies to Each Other. 

This month we have invited Madison Noelle McNair (she/her) to present "Disability & Democracy: Inclusion As A Core Value."  We will be discussing accessibility, inclusion, accommodations, activism, disability history, and how disability is intersectional with all causes.

Presenter's Bio:
Madison is 29, she was born & raised in the Dallas area, she has been disabled her entire life and is passionate about accessibility. She began her journey by volunteering starting at 5 years old, and started more dedicated advocacy at 18 years old. She has been honored to work with many non-profit and advocacy groups across Dallas including Sunrise Movement Dallas and Sunrise Movement Tarrant, Dallas For Change, La Colectiva NTX, El Movimiento, Viva Colectiva, Vecinos Unidos DFW, New Disabled South, Dallas Area Transit Alliance, and she feels extremely lucky to have worked for many more in addition to these. Madison is currently a part of the Class of 2026 and Cohort 7 of the LBJ Women’s Campaign School at UT Austin, on the Patient-Family Advisory Council (PFAC) at Parkland, and the Paratransit & Accessibility Advisory Group (PAAG) with DART.

Instagram: @monoqueenmadi 

We are looking forward to presenting additional educational topics at future meetings for all of us to learn about, understand, and appreciate our commonality. 

As always - we will give time to any candidates that are stopping by to introduce themselves and speak for a few minutes at the end of our meetings.

PLEASE NOTE - for those who can arrive early - about 5pm - you may participate in #CRAFTIVISM. If you arrive at 5PM or later - we will be creating "At Risk" packets to be distributed in our community for those who may be targeted by ICE. In addition - we have created "Whistle kits" for Allies.

THE MEETING WILL BEGIN A LITTLE BEFORE 7PM.

We are a Grass Roots Group dedicated to preserving our American way of Life that honors the Individual with Diversity, Equality and Dignity. Learn about ways you can participate in ACTIVISM.  Learn how you may participate in our HIVES (Precinct) project.  We are Creating FUN Caring Communities - and Winning Elections!  And we are building on our momentum from 2025 thanks to your growing enthusiasm! 

Let us help you find ways that you may use your skills, talents and strengths to participate in our fight to take back our country thru activism, demonstrations, precinct building, voter registration and much more.  

Our Goal is to be a source of Information to all Carrollton AREA Democrats so they may make informed and wise decisions at the voting booth. 

We now have a Web Site: https://www.carrolltondemocrats.com/. This will provide our Carrollton Democrats the resources they need whether they live in Denton or Dallas County.  

JOIN US every 3rd Wednesday of the Month:
Nico Nights with the Neighbors - Nico's Cocina (6:30 to 8:30). 

3065 N. Josey Lane, Carrollton, TX 75007

We meet in the EVENT ROOM to the right of the restaurant. 

Please sign up on Mobilize so we may prepare enough materials for everyone. 

If you wish to be placed on our email list, (only 3-4 a month) please SIGN UP on CarrolltonDemocrats.com.  And we'll be able to introduce you to your neighbors in your precinct.   

Again - we are happy you have found us - look forward to meeting you!

events.title: Road To Black November Phonebank Rally & Training
events.description:
Join the Road to Black November Phone Bank and help us increase Black voter participation across Jefferson County!

Volunteers will call residents to share accurate, nonpartisan voter information and help them prepare for the November 3 election. Before the October 19 registration deadline, we will encourage residents to check their voter status, register to vote or update their information. After the deadline, our calls will focus on helping residents find their polling place, make a voting plan and identify any assistance they may need.

During your shift, you will:

Receive training and a phone-banking script.
Call Jefferson County residents from an approved list.
Direct residents to www.RoadToBlackNovember.com.
Help residents find the information they need to prepare for Election Day.
Record responses so our team can provide appropriate follow-up.

Thousands of residents may not discover a problem with their voter status until they arrive at the polls. A short telephone call now can help someone check their information while there is still time to act.

No experience is required. We will provide the training, script and support you need. All you need is a telephone, internet access and a willingness to help your community.

Every call matters. Every voter matters. Sign up for a shift and invite a friend or family member to phone bank with you!

Road to Black November is a nonpartisan voter-participation initiative. We do not support or oppose any candidate or political party.

## No Kings: Vote Early Cumberland County                      
**A Community Mobilization & Mutual Aid Donation Drive.**
### THIS IS NOT A MARCH OR SPEAKING ENGAGEMENT. THIS IS A COME AND GO COMMUNITY EVENT AND MUTUAL AID DONATION DRIVE. 

Join [Fayetteville Resistance Coalition](https://linktr.ee/fayresistancecoalition) on October 17th as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next. We want everyone in our community to be informed and prepared to vote.

We are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early, ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard. Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. 


## WAYS TO PARTICIPATE

**Get Informed:** - Stop by to pick up nonpartisan voting info, look up your ballot, and check official early voting details.

**Get Involved:** - Connect with local community organizations to help protect the vote and discover ongoing ways to build community power.

**Get a Ride:** - Sign up or volunteer for transportation support to help ensure neighbors can reach polling locations.

**Demonstrate:** - Bring your signs and join the roadside demonstration to make the message visible.

## EVENT DETAILS
**Date:** Saturday, October 17, 2026

**Time:** 10am - 2pm 

**Location:** 369 Green Street 

## WHAT TO BRING

- Mutual Aid Donations: Please consider bringing non-perishable food items to support our Cumberland County neighbors. 

- Your Signs: Feel free to bring your signs and demonstrate with us, but please keep the focus on community care and voter mobilization.

**Handheld protest signs will be available at the event if desired.**

## GET VOTER READY!

**Visit [NCSBE.GOV](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to check your registration, learn more about voting, find your early voting locations, and to see your sample ballot.**

events.title: Voting Rights: The Struggle To Be Counted (a film & tribute to John Lewis)
events.description:
“Voting Rights: The Struggle To Be Counted 1619-2014” is a 35-minute film documentary, written and produced by Phil and narrated by his wife Pat Sloan. Through words, music, and vivid images, he tells the story of the historic, courageous and often brutal struggle by African Americans to obtain the unrestricted right to vote. Phil’s film begins with a moving pictorial tribute to Rep. John “Good Trouble” Lewis.

“Voting Rights: The Struggle To Be Counted” is a response to the U.S. Supreme Court’s June 25, 2013, 5-4 decision in the Shelby vs Holder Voting Right case which struck down Sections 4-5 of the historic 1965 Voting Rights Act which has led to the enactment of voter suppression laws that deny millions of our citizens of color the right to vote to this very day.  

Frederick Douglass, the great abolitionist, orator, and newspaper publisher once said, “slavery is not abolished until the black man has the right to vote”.  THIS IS THE CORNERSTONE OF EQUALITY.

This is a story that all Americans need to know, but especially African Americans who continue to have their vote suppressed and denied by enemies of justice who view voting as a privilege for a few, and not a right for ALL.  REMEMBER, A VOTELESS PEOPLE IS A VOICELESS PEOPLE!

Phil Portlock is a photographer, writer, film documentary producer, social justice activist, native Washingtonian. He began his photography/social justice career in 1968 after seeing Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. preach his last Sunday sermon on Sunday, March 31, 1968, at Washington, DC’s National Cathedral, less than a week before his death in Memphis, Tennessee on April 4, 1968.
