events.title: No Kings: Vote Early! Cumberland County
events.description:
## No Kings: Vote Early Cumberland County                      
**A Community Mobilization & Mutual Aid Donation Drive.**
### THIS IS NOT A MARCH OR SPEAKING ENGAGEMENT. THIS IS A COME AND GO COMMUNITY EVENT AND MUTUAL AID DONATION DRIVE. 

Join us on October 17th as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next. We want everyone in our community to be informed and prepared to vote. 

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law. Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. 

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation. We are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early, ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard. Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. 


## WAYS TO PARTICIPATE

**Get Informed:** - Stop by to pick up nonpartisan voting info, look up your ballot, and check official early voting details.

**Get Involved:** - Connect with local community organizations to help protect the vote and discover ongoing ways to build community power.

**Get a Ride:** - Sign up or volunteer for transportation support to help ensure neighbors can reach polling locations.

**Demonstrate:** - Bring your signs and join the roadside demonstration to make the message visible.

## EVENT DETAILS
**Date:** Saturday, October 17, 2026

**Time:** 10am - 2pm 

**Location:** 369 Green Street 

## WHAT TO BRING

- Mutual Aid Donations: Please consider bringing non-perishable food items to support our Cumberland County neighbors. 

- Your Signs: Feel free to bring your signs and demonstrate with us, but please keep the focus on community care and voter mobilization.

**Handheld protest signs will be available at the event if desired.**

## GET VOTER READY!

**Visit [NCSBE.GOV](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to check your registration, learn more about voting, find your early voting locations, and to see your sample ballot.**

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Sandoval County, NM
events.description:
Many of you have been asking about No Kings Day 4.  Are we going to have one?  If so when, where, and what will it be?  We finally received guidance from Indivisible National, and they are asking us to put down our protest signs and pick up our VOTE HERE TODAY signs.  The main day of action is October 17, and the main message is VOTE EARLY! If you believe in democracy, as we do, you understand that there is a time and a place to protest and there is a time and a place to take action to effect positive change.  The most powerful force that we have is the ability to mobilize millions of voters to vote for change.  

So what is Sandoval County Indivisible actually doing about this?  On Tuesday, October 6, outside the Sandoval County offices at the corner of Idalia Road and Highway 528 in Rio Rancho we will be holding a VOTE EARLY rally.  October 6 is the first day of early voting in NM, and the only early voting site open that day is at the Sandoval County Clerk’s office.  The rally will run from 10:00 AM to Noon.  We will have VOTE EARLY signs for all participants (VOTE EARLY, VOTE HERE TODAY with arrows pointing the way, and other signs as well). 

In addition, on Saturday, October 17, we will be holding another series of similar rallies at other early voting localities within the county, including at two early voting sites in Rio Rancho (Idalia Rd at 528 and St. Francis Episcopal Church, 2903  Cabezon Blvd.), one in Corrales (Corrales Rd across from the Corrales Village Offices, and one in Bernalillo (our Lady of Sorrows Gym, 319 S Camino del Pueblo).
 
Idalia Rd - 10:00 to noon 
St Francis - 10:00 to noon
Corrales - 12:30 PM to 2:30 PM 
Bernalillo - 12:30 PM to 2:30 PM

We need masses of people to show up at these rallies, and we are hoping that most of you will participate.  We will all have similar signs and will try to broadcast a united message.

events.title: LBDC General Meeting with Dave Min and the Ballot Review
events.description:
First, we will hear from Dave Min.  What’s happening in Congress and where he thinks this election will go.

After Dave, we will review the ballot from state to local candidates, propositions and measure.    The propositions are particularly difficult to understand and we foresee this is where will spend a fair bit of time.   So….BRING YOUR BALLOT and let’s fill them out together!  

We will have tables and pens so you may complete your ballot by the end of the evening.  And if you are up for it, we can car-pool to the ballot box and drop them off.  

PLEASE NOTE: We will be at the Neighborhood Congregational Church, not the LBDC Campaign HQ.  

Snacks and beverages will be provided so come, enjoy your ballot buddies and let’s vote!!

Check-in  6:00 to 6:30.  Program begins promptly at 6:30pm.

events.title: Knock Doors in Athens

sponsor.name: Georgia Youth Justice Coalition for Action

events.description:
Nobody understands what our neighborhoods need better than the people living in them.

You already see what's happening right where you live. Some of these challenges are big, like the cost of housing, access to affordable healthcare,  and whether our public schools stay fully funded. Others are challenges only the people who live here know and see. What connects them all is that too many of the decisions shaping our neighborhoods are made without us, and our communities deserve the resources we need to thrive.

When we talk about these issues with our neighbors, we stop facing them alone and start showing up together to transform our community and our state for the better.

That's why we're going door to door to talk to our neighbors about what important issues we’re facing right now and figure out the next steps toward real solutions.
 
No experience needed — just a willingness to listen, share, and build a stronger community together. This is where change actually starts. Come be part of it!

events.title: Faith on the Frontlines for Our Communities Prayer Call
events.description:
Community leaders know this truth: when people gather with intention, something shifts. We would be honored to have you on our midterm elections prayer call.

Join fellow believers as we prepare for early voting in-person and Election Day. This is a time to come together to hold space for our communities, our nation, and everyone showing up to participate in these elections. This is a time to ground ourselves in shared values—peace, wisdom, strength, and collective care—as we prepare to be heard.

Please invite other clergy, ministry leaders, and intercessors to join us. The circle grows stronger with every voice added. 

"For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them." — Matthew 18:20

We look forward to praying together with you.

events.title: Weekend of Action: Knock Doors in Prince George's!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

**Join us for our Weekend of Action!*

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  ** #TeamMaryland.**

#### Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday: Burnout @9am & This is the Plan @4pm -ZOOM

#### _This fall, The Ladle & Literature Society—also known as the Sorting Soup Book Club—this weekend 9/20 has  two (2) Book Clubs.. 9am and 4pm.

_We’ll gather around books that take both the personal toll of organizing and the practical work of winning seriously.

#### Let us know you will be attending either the 9am by RSVPing here -> https://mobilize.us/s/30D6NR

#### Sunday @ 9 am ..Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle

*Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle* by Emily and Amelia Nagoski explores why stress lingers in our bodies long after the immediate crisis has passed, and how we can interrupt the cycle through rest, connection, movement, boundaries, and joy. Organizers are regularly asked to absorb urgency, outrage, grief, and other people’s needs; without ways to process that load, exhaustion becomes a predictable political outcome. 

This discussion is for anyone who wants to build a practice of care sturdy enough to support the long haul—because a movement cannot afford to treat its people as disposable.

It is an antidote to doomscrolling and magical thinking: organized people change what looks inevitable by showing up, making a plan, and bringing others with them. 

#### Join the 4pm CDT we have  *This Is the Plan: How to End America’s Meltdown & Save Democracy* by Ben Wikler, turns toward the collective work of democratic renewal. Drawing from his organizing and political experience in Wisconsin, Wikler lays out a practical argument for building durable power, expanding participation, and addressing the systems that undermine democracy—not simply focusing on a single candidate or election. 

#### Join by Zoom .. The Literature & Ladle Society Sorting Soup’s (Book Club’s) Sunday sessions: Burnout - ZOOM at 9:00 a.m. & This is the Plan @4pm CST, -> https://bit.ly/NWSOFA-Zoom

We will join together with the millions of like-minded Americans across the country. Starting at 8am, we will be among the first in the country kicking off this Day of Getting the Vite Out Early! reminding everyone to get out and vote! We will have people ready to guide you through having conversations with people a bout how and why the vote is so urgent this year! Canvass people in the crowd, we always have newcomers to demonstrating!

VISIBILITY FREEPORT is a volunteer run group that has organized weekly - Tuesday 8-10am - “Stand for Democracy” demonstrations since the first of March at 134 Main St, Freeport, 04032. We meet, show our signs and participate in peaceful protest of the attacks of the administration on our democracy. We are not affiliated with any one national protest organization, rather have found our space as an umbrella for peaceful protesters from many groups. We have also participated and brought thousands of people together for each of the last National Days of Protest large and small. This NO KINGS! will be the biggest, for sure. It needs to be! Support our neighbors - bring non- perishables for the FCS Food Pantry, if you can.

See you Saturday, October 17, 8-11am
Get the message out - NO KINGS VITE EARLY!

events.title: Party to The Polls
events.description:
Cruisin’ to the Polls: Tempe’s Ultimate Party at the Poll! 🎉🚗💨

Get ready to turn up the energy, bring the color, and make your voice heard! Tempe Rising Indivisible, Keep AZ Blue, and Young Democrats are teaming up for an unforgettable, high-powered motorcade through the streets of Tempe straight to the polls at Arizona State University!

Decorate your ride, roll down the windows, and join the caravan as we cruise together to drop off our ballots and celebrate our democracy in style.

What’s Happening at the Polls:
🎤 Featured Guest Speaker: Hear directly from Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes!

🎶 Music & High Energy: Keep the momentum going with awesome tunes and great vibes.

🤝 Meet & Connect: Hubs for Keep AZ Blue, Young Dems, and Tempe Rising Indivisible to meet like-minded community members and activist leaders.

📋 Master Your Ballot: Get hands-on guidance on navigating tools like BeBallotReady.vote and learn why voting the whole ballot matters for local impact!

Whether you’re driving in the motorcade, meeting us at ASU, or coming to empower your vote, this is the place to be. Let’s show up, get informed, and celebrate our community strength together!

Need to check your registration or find voting information?

Check your registration, sample ballot, and voting options directly on BeBallotReady.vote.

For statewide voting details and official guidelines, visit the Arizona Secretary of State Election Information Portal.

events.description:
Celebrate No Kings Day by working to FLIP THE HOUSE! Join lots of fired-up volunteers on a **bus to the Central Valley**. We’ll be **knocking on doors for Adam Gray in Congressional District 13 (CA-13)**. Adam won by just 187 votes in 2024, and we’re working hard to protect his seat. This race could be won or lost by a few hundred votes, so every knock counts! 

**Timing:**

- **8am: Depart Mountain View**  

- Roughly 10:30am-4pm: Knock on doors, with a break for lunch

- 6:30pm (at latest): return to Mountain View

**More details:**

- There is lots of all-day parking available at the Mountain View departure location

- We’ll provide lunch (and early morning coffee too)

- We’ll provide a full training that morning (and there’s training available in advance too)

- Local volunteers in the district will drive us to our canvassing locations

Sign up now and help us fill the bus! And invite friends to register as well!

This bus is organized by a group of organizations, including Swing Left Peninsula, the Democratic Volunteer Center, the Santa Clara Dems, and the Bay Area Coalition.

Please send any questions to [ info@sccdp.org](mailto:info@sccdp.org)

*By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. events.title: NO KINGS Greeter Team Zoom
events.description:
NO KINGS: Vote Early is meant to encourage citizens to vote and to do so early, AND to bring more people into the movement to increase our "Power in Numbers."  The first step is to collect contact information from participants, and the second step is to introduce them to the movement in a relaxed way.  

Our NO KINGS Greeters help with BOTH.  Each Greeter will have an attendance list, notebook and stickers.  They will (1) check off anyone who is on their list so they are credited with attending.  They will (2) collect contact information from anyone not on their list.  They will (3) give the person a flyer inviting them to a Meet & Greet exclusively for NO KINGS attendees.  Finally, they will (4) give each a sticker that will help a Greeter determine whether someone has already been greeted.

Greeters are KEY to growing our movement!

We will go over details, perhaps do a bit of role-playing, and do further planning at a half-hour Zoom meeting on Monday 10/12 at 7 PM.

You will receive a Zoom invitation in a reminder email and text a couple of days before the Zoom.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Pekin, Illinois

location.venue: On the lawn of the Tazewell County Courthouse facing Court St.

events.description:
# The Mission
As citizens of America, we have a responsibility to show up **loud and proud** for the continuance of our democracy. We're a government for the people, by the people - and it's time to make that abundantly clear!

It's time to participate! Commit to **VOTE EARLY! NO KINGS IN AMERICA!**

## Get Out the Vote in Tazewell County!
People of Tazewell County, rally on October 17th to get out the vote! Celebrate our rockstar elections officials and appreciate their tireless work helping us engage in our right, privilege, and duty as citizens of the United States. Come join us at the Tazewell County Courthouse in Pekin, IL - bring a sign, good vibes, and maybe a costume and some candy for our little guys trick and treating the downtown business area.

We can help you check your voter registration and help out with updating your registration, or you can go straight to the experts at the County Clerk's office (McKenzie Building - 11 S. 4th St #203 Pekin, IL) next door!

Check out the excellent resources at [Vote 411](https://www.vote411.org) to help craft your voting plan!

## Sharing is Caring!
When you cast your ballot, shout loud and proud across your socials and networks: friends, family, coworkers, congregation, and beyond to let them know that you made a commitment for the future, and to ask them to do the same. Our students have drawn up some commemorative art for the elections - grab a pin and show it off!

## Rock the Early Vote at an Early Polling Site
Early voting for the midterms opens up September 24th, so don't feel as though you have to wait up.  Follow this link for early voting sites and times throughout Tazewell County: [Tazewell County Early Voting Information](https://tazewell-il.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-General-Early-Voting-Schedule.pdf)

events.description:
Join our Sunrise RGV group in planting native trees at Rio Reforestation to help restore the native ecosystem, which absorbs the impacts of climate change better than anything else. 

We will be coordinating a carpool from coffee shops in Edinburg & Alamo with pick up or ride share options available for folks! If you prefer to drive then we will meet you at the event! 

After the tree planting we will grab lunch at a local spot nearby (TBD during our general meeting on 9/30/26 smvmt.us/rgvgeneral)

PS. The Rio Reforestation tract crosses the border wall. Event organizers promise the event will be safe but individual discretion encouraged.

Heads up, there are 2 shifts: 1. for tree planting at Rio Reforestation and 2. for post-planting lunch hangs!

events.title: Knock on Doors with the Mitchell County Dems!
events.description:
Join Mitchell County Democrats for a neighborhood lit drop and voter outreach shift.

We’ll meet at MCDP Headquarters in Bakersville, get our routes and materials together, and then head out around Mitchell County.

Most stops will be simple: leave information from our candidates, remind neighbors that an election is coming up, and move on to the next house. If someone wants to talk, that’s great but you don't need to give a speech, debate anyone, or have an answer for every question.

We’ll partner up and go over the routes and materials. Bring a charged phone, water, and comfortable shoes. The plan is to be out for two hours, but teams are welcome to stay out longer if they’d like.

If talking to strangers at the door isn’t your strong suit, that’s okay. This is just a straightforward way to help get election information into people’s hands.

events.title: Vote Early Day: Benton County AR Election Commission HQ
events.description:
# Join us October 24

Thousands of communities are stepping up. Learning together. Empowering neighbors to vote early. You're part of that.

In 2026, over 40 states are restricting voting. Shorter windows. ID requirements. Fewer polling places. Mail ballot restrictions. That's exactly why we're here.

Learn your voting options. Check your registration. Make a plan to vote early on your terms.

It’s easy to check your registration, find a voting center, and even figure out what’s on your ballot before you go. The Arkansas Secretary of State has one site that will do it all: [Voter View](https://www.voterview.ar-nova.org/voterview)

**No lines. No waiting. You vote on your schedule.**

events.title: Poll Station Tabling – Early Voting - October 14–29
events.description:
About this event
Poll Station Table Volunteers are needed for Early Voting during the November election, October 14 - October 29. Volunteers will staff an information table at the Library poll station. It's our last opportunity to help voters hear about Democrats on the Ballot!
Note: You will receive Mobilize email about this event when you sign up.

Volunteers, a MUST READ, please!

Thank you for your commitment! However, if something happens and you cannot fulfill your shift, please give as much notice as possible by calling or texting 336-601-8183 or 865-469-1513.

Preparation

•	Wear comfortable clothing, such as a BCDP T-shirt, hat or similar top. We have BCDP buttons available to use for your shift if you don’t have BCDP logo items. Please leave the buttons for the next shift. 

•	You must cover up any political logos before entering the library, so bring an extra cover up shirt. 

•	Bring a beverage/water, snack, sunglasses or hat if you so desire.

Set Up

•	The table will be set up under the tree near the book drop-off. Please keep the sidewalk area clear so we aren’t impeding public access.

•	2 metal chairs are provided as well as 1 small table along with all the supplies. There is an umbrella, rain poncho and a plastic cover for the table.

•	In the case of rain, cover the table with the plastic cover and wait it out in your vehicle if you so desire. Either wait it out and reset when the rain has passed or call for table pickup 336-601-8183 or 865-469-1513. 

•	By Law, anything campaign related MUST BE 100 ft from the entrance of the polling location (in this case, the Library entrance)

Interaction with voters

•	Our mission is to interact with voters. To attract their attention, lots of friendly WAVING and SMILING as cars go by will help with getting them to stop by.

•	Use the buddy system, taking turns. Stay aware and alert. It’s great to get to know each other as you are at the table together, but please be sure you are paying attention to the visitors at the table.

•	Have visitors sign in on the sign in sheet. Ask them if they would like to volunteer with party and if so, circle the Yes in the last column and give them a Yellow Card to fill out with their preferences. Keep the card after reviewing to ensure their contact information has been provided.

•	Offer them the candidate information that is available. They may take it into the booth with them.

•	Ask the visitor if they are on our mailing list for our newsletter. If not let them know they can sign up for it on Blountdems.org

•	Ignore any haters. Do not interact with them in any way.

events.title: Weekday Canvassing in Troy
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!

events.title: Public Safety, Justice & Community Trust: A Forsyth County Community Forum

sponsor.name: Camel City United Indivisible North Carolina

events.description:
What does public safety look like when communities, law enforcement, and the justice system work together — and how do we strengthen trust and accountability in Forsyth County?

Join Camel City United Indivisible, The Pink Vote, and Fuerza Triad for a community forum on Public Safety, Justice & Community Trust in Forsyth County.

This will be a structured, moderated community conversation bringing together representatives and candidates from law enforcement and the justice system, along with community voices.

This is not a debate. It is an opportunity for Forsyth County residents to hear directly from people serving in — and seeking to serve in — important public safety and justice roles and to engage in a constructive conversation about our community.

Topics will include:

• Public safety in Forsyth County
• Community trust and accountability
• The relationship between law enforcement and the communities they serve
• Fairness and accountability in the justice system
• Cooperation among law enforcement and justice agencies
• How residents, community organizations, and public institutions can work together more effectively

Confirmed participant:
Forsyth County Sheriff Bobby F. Kimbrough Jr.

events.description:
*Multnomah, Clackamas, Washington counties. Do a neighborhood Early Vote Action on your block, corner, park, library, overpass, favorite coffee shop… Share Ideas and build connections with like-minded neighbors.*

### **NO KINGS Nationwide Day of Action - Voting Early in every precinct and every town.** 
The power does not belong to billionaires, strongmen, or politicians who believe they are above accountability. 
Power belongs to the people, but only if we use it. 
### Here's how you can help in your neighborhood.
**No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Oct 17th, it's a day of voter participation: Do an action. Bring friends and neighbors together to vote early and spread the word. Let's encourage every eligible voter to make their voice heard.**

This is the [National No Kings: Vote Early website, Event Map and Host Toolkit.](https://www.nokings.org/) There are training calls, graphics and planning resources.  **You can register and post your event on the map**; as local organizers, we're happy to share ideas, resources and help you navigate that process.

**Or, gather a few of your neighbors and friends in a less formal action**  - that's the hyper-local focus of this Oct 17th. 

### We're hearing lots of fun Vote Early action ideas so far. National Day of Action is Oct 17, Locally, let's keep it going all the way through Nov 3rd!
- Sidewalk Honk and Waves - Your Ballot Drop Box is Here! Giant arrows! With or without Frogs, Jugglers, Balloons

- Car caravans, Bike Caravans - Dress up your vehicles and drive through town, head past a drop box.

- Run to Early Vote - gather your runner friends. Or skaters.. run to the dropbox.

- Voting is My Super Power - Dressing up as your favorite Superhero!

- Coffee shop - Vote in Public! At your favorite Food Cart pod, coffee shop, local pub...Bring friends, ballots, I Voted stickers, voter education info to share. Break bread with friends while you're at it.

- Chalk the Vote!  Sidewalk messages to lead folks to Drop boxes, Track Your Ballot, and County Elections websites

- Vote Party at the Park - celebrating folks who've already voted, help neighbors learn how to vote early themselves. You might want crafts, music, puppets..

- Overpass Bannering - Vote Early, Oregon Vote is Safe & Easy

- We Will Vote! Sing-a-Long

- Organize a Neighborhood Dropbox Karaoke Carpool and afterparty

- Block Party - Early Vote! BBQ, Voter Pamphlets, Election Resources

**Election Defense: Oregon's Vote By Mail systems are easy to use, secure, and reliable.** But when a would be king continues to threaten our elections, we have a collective duty to protect the vote and make sure every ballot is counted.  In Oregon, you and your volunteers can join the [Common Cause efforts as Trusted Messengers, dispelling misinformation and as Election Box Monitors.](https://www.commoncause.org/oregon/actions/2001/)

From OR DOJ [Oregon rules regarding Drop Boxes, Campaigning activities](https://www.doj.state.or.us/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CJ-Election-Guide-CJ-BW.pdf)

events.description:

JOIN OUR NON-VIOLENT, NON-PARTISAN, FAMILY FRIENDLY, PEACEFUL EVENT THAT SENDS A MESSAGE TO OUR COMMUNITY TO VOTE YOUR VALUES and VOTE EARLY!

There were 250+ BALLOTS from Mason County alone that were NOT COUNTED in the August primary because the ballot was mailed using the USPS and MISSED THE POSTMARK DEADLINE!  Let’s get the message out to VOTE EARLY, AND/OR USE A BALLOT DROP BOX! 

If you believe in accountability, democracy, and a government that answers to the people, join us to share that message with our community!

SIGNS WILL BE AVAILABLE, OR CONSIDER BRINGING YOUR OWN SIGNS that focus on getting out the vote EARLY and/or related to specific VALUES that will resonate with ALL voters!  Suggestions:  No Kings - vote now…-vote today…-mail ballot NOW…-use ballot drop boxes.  Vote and be heard.  Don’t stay silent.  Your vote is vital. Vote your values; Vote out corruption; Vote 4 - honesty…-Justice…-We the people…-your kids…-rule of law…-Health Care…-our constitution…-our national parks…-our veterans.

Contact Mason County Indivisible, for more information about our ongoing, local actions, CCMCI2025@gmail.com.

IMPORTANT DETAILS BELOW…

DATE: SATURDAY, OCTOBER 17, 2026

TIME: 11AM-1PM

LOCATION: Kneeland Park, 100 Turner Avenue, Shelton, WA 98584

BE SURE YOU GET A STICKER SO YOUR ATTENDANCE IS COUNTED.  Stickers will be distributed along the sidewalk.

WE SUPPORT OUR COMMUNITY THROUGH FOOD AND SCHOOL SUPPLY DRIVES: IF YOU ARE ABLE, please bring NON-PERISHABLE FOOD and SCHOOL SUPPLIES to donate to our local food banks and school children. Many in our communities rightfully live in fear of, and are victims of, ICE activities. Our families are being torn apart because of that. Thank you for helping your neighbors.

SAFETY: We are first and foremost a non-violent movement. Should verbal abuse be directed at us, we do not engage in a disrespectful way. We do not escalate rhetoric toward violence, we de-escalate. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully, and respectfully, at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

The Shelton Police Department has been notified of our peaceful protest. You may see them cruise by on the highway and/or park in the area. Additionally, our local team of Peacekeepers with walkie-talkies and wearing yellow vests will be in place to assist. Seek them out if you need assistance of any kind.

We will line up along the Kneeland Park Hwy 3 sidewalk. As more people arrive, please spread out along that sidewalk so drivers can read your signs and be motivated to VOTE!  Be safe and considerate of pedestrians using the sidewalk, and do not lean into traffic or step off the curb into the bike lane.  

IN THE PARK:  At the Mason County Indivisible table, you will find extra signs, bottled water, snacks, first aid support and chairs if you need a respite.  Also, plan to visit the information tables of our coalition partners, League of Women Voters, Mason County Immigrant Support Network, etc.

RESTROOMS: are available in the park.  


PLAN FOR THE WEATHER: We are encouraging all able-bodied allies in possession of rain gear (and who isn’t in the PNW?!) to join us. Please bring your water and snacks to stay energized, and a folding chair if you’re more comfortable sitting.  What a fabulous witness it will be for our community to see a band of die-hard voters out there encouraging everyone to VOTE YOUR VALUES and VOTE EARLY! 

PARKING: Please carpool if you can. Parking is very limited along Kneeland Park. Additional parking is across Turner Avenue in the UPPER parking lot behind the Shelton Athletic Club and along neighboring streets. Let’s be good neighbors and not block any driveways.

Our coalition of partners across Mason County, and beyond, are excited to join with you on this day to show our community and the world we support democratic values.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Outside Mackey Arena, West Lafayette, IN
events.description:

events.title: PA: Springdale Data Center Public Meeting
events.description:
A massive hyperscale data center slated for Springdale, PA, has been approved at the local level. But it still has to meet Allegheny County’s land development standards — and the developer's current application will not meet the requirements for the county’s subdivision and land development ordinance, or SALDO.

If they plan to follow their own laws, Allegheny County officials should reject the data center application before any public hearing process begins! 

**Make your voice heard!** Join Food & Water Watch, your fellow Allegheny County neighbors, and allied organizations on October 28th for the Springdale Data Center Land Development Public Meeting!

Once you sign up, we'll send you instructions on how to register for public comment during the meeting and talking points, as well as info on requesting accommodations. We'll also keep you in the loop with updates on this issue and future actions you can take.

Your presence makes a difference. **When we show up together, we send a strong message: our future shouldn’t be decided by corporations looking for profit at our expense!**

events.title: Vote Forward x Stand Up America Letter Writing Events
events.description:
Join Stand Up America, Vote Forward, and volunteers across the country to write letters to voters!

Vote Forward partners with volunteers to take evidence-driven, high-impact actions to strengthen our democracy by building trust in government and increasing voter participation. Everything we do is grounded in evidence: we rigorously test our tactics, learn from the results, and evolve. Our 2026 campaigns build directly on what we learned in 2025, and include some of our most novel and exciting work yet. We have ambitious goals, but we make it easy to get started.  

Join us to learn about the available campaigns, and the strategy behind them.

The most common question we receive at Vote Forward is: "what should I write?" This letter writing event is the personalized, in depth answer to that question. Vote Forward staff will help you craft an effective, personal message to voters. Whether you’re writing letters for the first time or you’re an experienced letter writer looking to refine your message, this event is for you!

RSVP today, and we’ll let you know how to join this event. Invite your friends and family, too and encourage them to join in with Vote Forward! 

Never written with Vote Forward before? No problem! Visit [votefwd.org/instructions](https://votefwd.org/instructions) for all the information you need, and sign up for an account at [votefwd.org/standupamerica](https://go.votefwd.org/standupamerica).

We’ll be gathering petition signatures and spreading the word on the fight against data centers at the **Fall Farm Festival in Albuquerque on Saturday, October 10 from 11 to 3**. 

We're petitioning to demand the New Mexico legislature take action on a **state-wide moratorium on new and existing data centers.**

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Hi! Come be part of an intimate gathering of women, moms, and advocates for a screening and discussion of the documentary 'No Country For Mothers' - about what motherhood is like in America. It’s a space to connect, share, and talk honestly about our experiences as mothers.

Produced by MomsFirst - a non-profit organization fighting for affordable child care, paid leave, and an economy that works for families - I'm honored to be a part of their film tour as an Associate Producer.

This isn’t just about watching a film, it’s about being in a space where we can connect in community. 

Joined by Su Fern Khoo, Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, and a mom, we will be discussing one of life’s most profound transitions - motherhood and postpartum.

An evening connecting with film and community, we hope to see you there!

RSVP for exact address location - event held in Silverlake, 90026.

---
About ELIZABETH 

As an LA-based Actor, Producer, and Eco-mindfulness Facilitator, Elizabeth's production work spans from unscripted television to ecological storytelling. She has produced and hosted content for A+E Networks, and is currently developing The Fourth Trimester, a global docuseries exploring postpartum healing traditions across cultures. Liz brings a cross-cultural lens to stories about identity, care, and climate - work she continues through both her production practice and community initiatives like this screening. She is the founder of MamaBoo Studios (launching 2027), a storytelling studio for everything we mother - children, selves, and the planet. www.elizabethlazan.com

About SU FERN 

Su Fern Khoo, LMFT, is the founder of Khoo, Marriage and Family Therapy, Inc. She holds a Master's in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Divinity. Her clinical approach draws from person-centered, psychodynamic, Jungian-informed therapy, humanistic, existential, mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy and attachment-based therapy frameworks.

She works with both individuals and couples — and her work supports each person in developing a deeper understanding of themselves within their partnerships and/or their evolving identities as parents. www.skhootherapy.org

events.title: Hands Off My Vote - No Dictators! Protest in Ocean View (Hawai'i Island)

Join your neighbors in Ocean View on October 17 for a  community gathering celebrating the power of people coming together, participating in our democracy, and strengthening Kaʻū. This family-friendly event will focus on voting, civic engagement, community connection, and Kaʻū Strong. Your voice matters. Your vote matters. Our community matters. Everyone is welcome!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Albert J Boro Community Center, San Rafael, CA
events.description:
In Marin, we’re gathering near drop boxes and on overpasses to spread the word: **vote early**! That’s our message to everyone who passes by one of our gatherings. We’re asking everyone who attends one of the actions throughout Marin to bring their completed ballot in their sealed and signed envelope and deposit it in the drop box. We’re even making No Kings-branded “I Voted Early” to pass out to everyone who, you guessed it, votes early.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

*This is a no-host event. An ad hoc group of citizen volunteers are facilitating this opportunity for Marin residents to peacefully and safely assemble in line with their First Amendment rights. All participants agree to assume 100% responsibility for their own safety, conduct and well-being. Please review this guide, [“How To Protest Safely” ](https://www.nrdc.org/stories/how-protest-safely) in advance*

events.title: WIN the Midterms, ENFORCE the results: A SURJ Direct Action Training Series
events.description:
**This is a 3-part training series, please sign up for all three!**
**Recordings will be sent after the training if you have to miss any, though please try to be there live!**

As white people organizing for racial justice, we know what's at stake in this moment. We know that the billionaires see multi-racial democracy as a threat to their power, so they use race and class to divide us so that we don't join together to build the world we deserve - a world with clean air and water, fully funded schools, healthcare for all, free accessible childcare; a world of racial and economic justice. Power holders are so threatened by our power that they are not only scapegoating our black, brown, immigrant, and trans neighbors to distract us from their corruption, they are also working in earnest to dismantle our democracy in order to cement their wealth and power.

We know that white people have an outsized influence in both the electoral and political spheres, which is why Showing up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is working hard to move white people to both WIN the midterm elections by big margins so that they are hard to contest and then ENFORCE the election results.

In order to enforce our wins after the midterms, we will have to engage in direct action noncooperation by disrupting business as usual and refusing to cooperate with MAGA's attempts to steal our votes.

In these direct action noncooperation trainings we will learn:

**Training one:**

* Our strategy from now until the election

* Why we need to engage in noncooperation

* Why noncooperation is white people’s work

* What is noncooperation and why is it strategic

* What will our potential targets and actions be?

* Tips to build your crew who will take action with you

**Training two:**

* How to design a powerful action

* What roles are needed at actions

* Protest safety

**Training three:**

* Setting the tone for your action

* Messaging and visuals

* Documenting your action

* Media

Please join us for this three part series and be a part of our historic movement to block MAGA and build a world where we all thrive.

events.title: PR Committee Meeting - Democratic Party of Outagamie Co.
events.description:
DPOC Public Relations Committee Meeting

Join the Democratic Party of Outagamie County’s Public Relations Committee to help build the messages, visuals, outreach, and community connections that move local Democrats forward. We are an all-local, all-volunteer team within our county party, working to elect dems and further progressive values right here at home.

Whether you are a writer, designer, photographer, chronically online, spreadsheet organizer, metrics-minded planner, email design wizard or simply someone who wants to pitch in when you can, there is a place for you on the PRC. Most volunteer roles are designed for a manageable 2–3 hours per week, and monthly project-based assignments are available for people who cannot take on an ongoing role.

At this meeting, we’ll:

- Welcome new and returning volunteers and make space for quick introductions
- Share updates on social media, email, events, and current PR projects
- Review open assignments and volunteer needs
- Match people with roles based on their interests, skills, and availability
- Discuss ways to support DPOC events, candidates, Outagamie Action Teams, and local community partners
- Gather ideas for future content, campaigns, and projects

We are currently especially looking for volunteers interested in:

- Social media static & Carousel content design, videos, and engagement
- Copywriting, editing, proofreading
- Graphic design, Canva templates, print materials, and email design
- Photography, short-form video, and video editing
- Website updates and event information
- Project coordination, deadline tracking, and intake support
- Press releases, talking points, media relations, and rapid-response writing
- Event promotion, flyer distribution, and volunteer coordination

No prior committee experience is required. We can provide tools, templates, direction, and a supportive team, bring your skills, curiosity, and ideas. If you are not ready for a standing role, you can also join our Project Volunteer pool and opt into one-off assignments that fit your schedule.

The PR Committee is where we turn good work into clear, local, people-centered communication. Help us make sure Outagamie County voters know what Democrats are doing, where they can get involved, and why every election matters.

**Please RSVP so we can welcome you, share meeting materials, and help connect you with the right opportunities.**

***Meeting link sent upon sign up,

events.description:
NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY RALLY AND SOULS TO THE POLLS MARCH 

Indivisible LYH, the Lynchburg Voters League, NAACP Lynchburg Chapter, and the League of Women Voters of Central Virginia invite you to join us on October 18 from 2 to 4 beginning at Miller Park for a GET OUT THE VOTE  rally and Souls to the Polls March to vote early and in person at the Kemper Street registrar‘s office! 

For over a year, millions of people have come together to send a clear message: in America, we have no kings. No Kings: Vote Early is the next step: this is not purely a protest, it is a day of nonpartisan voter participation

Because in America, leaders do not get to choose who votes, whose voices matter, or what future our communities deserve. The people choose their leaders.

For generations, everyday people have changed the course of this country by organizing, marching, and voting. Power does not belong to billionaires, strongmen, or politicians who believe they are above accountability. Power belongs to the people, but only if we use it. On October 17, we are making sure every eligible voter knows their options for how to vote, has a plan to vote early where local law allows, and is ready to make their voice count. Join us.

No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings.

Check out indivisiblelyh.org for more information.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in St. Francis to flip WI-01!
events.description:
Join Swing Left Milwaukee for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Tijeras, Bernalillo Co, NM
events.description:
Indivisible Tijeras and Beyond invites you to join us in Tijeras for a rally and early voting in Bernalillo County. We will rally on the sidewalk, hand out our swag and answer any questions about the election. THEN -- after firing up our group we will go together to the nearest polling station and VOTE. Mountain residents will go to Tijeras Village Hall and Albuquerque residents will go to Four Hills. It's important you plan for voting after the rally. Hopefully we'll be standing in line! We want this to be the largest early vote in American history!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Breaking the ICE is a deliberate, breathless convergence, a strategic intervention that breathes life into the space between us. It unites women who move through entirely different worlds, weaving together the lives of Black, African Diaspora, Arab, Latina, White, and Asian WOMEN. We gather with intention, bridging the deep, silent divides of culture, faith, socioeconomic lineage, and raw lived experience.
This event is designed to be an intentional, transformative space where community organizing meets cultural celebration. Come ready to connect deeply, share a meal, learn from powerful organizers, and dance.

Event Schedule
4:30 PM  The Alchemy of the Kitchen (Intimate Cooking Gathering): Chef Tracy (Culture in a Bowl) guides us through the sensory, historical rhythm of creating Jollof Rice. Nearby, Amira Haidar, alongside the fierce presence of the Political Healers, will construct our International Charcuterie Board, layering flavors from across the globe.
6:00 PM – 8:00 PM The Feast, The Movement, The Truth: We transition into the main event. Join us for an International Dinner to nourish the body, the electric and communal spirit of Dabka dancing, and a deep, guided discussion facilitated by the wisdom of Elder Leslie.

events.title: Protest MAGA Tiffany before the Debate
events.description:
Tom Tiffany is coming to Milwaukee for his televised debate for Governor — and Birds on a Wire is showing up before he walks through those doors.

The debate will be held without a live audience, but that doesn’t mean Wisconsin voters have to be silent.

We’ll be outside — peaceful, joyful, loud and impossible to ignore.

Tiffany’s record in Congress will be part of what protesters are calling attention to. He voted for the 2025 reconciliation law that made major changes and reductions in projected federal Medicaid spending, while Tiffany has defended his vote as protecting benefits for vulnerable people and targeting waste and eligibility requirements.

We want Wisconsin voters asking questions about healthcare costs, Medicaid, reproductive freedom, immigration, public education, the cost of living, data centers, taxes, and whose interests our next governor will serve.

Bring your signs. Bring your friends. Bring your voice.

SHOW UP. STAND UP. SPEAK UP.

We have the power to make better possible — but only when we use it.

Join Birds on a Wire from 5:40-6:30 PM, immediately before the debate begins.

Let’s give the cameras something to see — and Wisconsin something to hear.

PEOPLE OVER BILLIONAIRES.
HEALTHCARE IS A HUMAN RIGHT.
WISCONSIN BELONGS TO ALL OF US.

This will be a peaceful, nonviolent protest.

One detail I’d consider adding to the event page: “The debate begins at 7 PM and will be televised statewide.” That gives people another reason to come—the protest is immediately before a major statewide media event. WISN says the debate will air in southeastern Wisconsin and be distributed to partner stations around the state.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early JOPLIN PROTEST
events.description:
**No Kings.**
**Just Voters.**

### THE JOPLIN PROTEST:
Join Indivisible Joplin for a No Kings: Vote Early Protest.

On **Saturday, October 17th,** meet us at **7th and Rangeline** between **11 am and 4 pm** (come and go as you are able).

**Bring your signs and stand up for democracy!**
Need a sign? No worries, we'll have plenty of supplies for you!

**What's different this time around?**
No Kings Vote Early focuses on increasing voter turnout and election protection.
So come ready to learn about early voting in Missouri and election protection programs available through Indivisible.

**What about safety?**
As always, Indivisible Joplin requests our attendees seek to de-escalate all conflict. We will have trained Safety Team members in yellow vests on site for the event; please let them know of any safety concerns and feel free to ask them any questions you have!

**Where do we park?**
Previous No Kings protests have packed out parking lots, so please keep in mind that there are still people trying to work and shop and be respectful of others and their businesses. Do not take parking spots directly in front of businesses if you don’t intend to shop there! We love our local businesses and want to make sure we are not impeding their operations during our event.


**RSVP on Mobilize** is not required but is helpful in planning and will sign you up for email updates for the event.

**Keep updated** on news about the event at our website or on our social media pages.
Visit our website for information about our group and other events.

**Interested in volunteering with us?**
Reach out to us by email/socials and monitor our social media pages for volunteer opportunities!

---

### THE MOVEMENT:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: ICE Out For Good Jacksonville, Florida
events.description:
On July 27th, 2026, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitian immigrants was rolled back. According to former Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem, Haiti no longer met the requirements for TPS.

Hardly a month later, a young man by the name of Pierre Damas Bel would pull his car onto the shoulder of Interstate 70 in Clark County, Ohio, and walk into oncoming traffic where he was hit by a truck and died at the scene.

It was 2024 when Bel and his family — along with many other Haitian immigrants — came to the U.S. seeking asylum due to the unstable conditions of the country. Even now, as of 2026, according to the official website of the U.S. Department of State "Travel.State.Gov", Haiti is deemed a level 4 "Do Not Travel" advisory. This means a very high risk of physical, sexual, or financial assault for both locals and U.S. citizens.

Despite Haiti being dangerous, TPS was rolled back. So, Pierre Damas Bel, someone who was not only an asylum seeker but also came to the U.S. in a legal manner, was issued an ankle monitor by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) shortly after July 27th. Within a month, Bel had his protected status revoked, was criminalized, shamed, and harassed. As a result, he took his own life on the morning of August 31st 2026.

There have been at least 10 suicides linked to ICE detention centers in 2025 and at least 2 linked to bullying regarding ICE.

This rally is intended to protest the fearmongering perpetuated by the current administration against all immigrants and people of color. We protest to demand restrictions on and/or the abolition of ICE. We demand to reinstate and extend TPS for Haitian and Syrian people seeking safety and asylum.

A broad coalition will organize on Thursday October 22nd 2026 at Friendship Fountain 1015 Museum Cir, Jacksonville, FL 32207. Rain or shine, let’s protest for justice and the safety of our communities. Remember to bring food and water bottles, as well as first aid if needed. Please also remember to abide by road rules, do not impede traffic or block parking lots or any safety vehicles that need passage. Do not do anything that puts you or your fellow protestors at risk.

*A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.*

events.title: Yes4EDR Town Hall - Pittsfield
events.description:
Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the Berkshire Athenaeum, Pittsfield's Public Library, to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
One night. One film. The founder of Moms First, in the room, in Denver.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased through Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

We need to talk about something bigger than the next dance floor. The culture wars have divided us — this is how we come back together.

MFT is proud to partner with Moms First to bring their film No Country for Mothers to Apollo Hall, Denver — with founder Reshma Saujani joining us live.

No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Since its June 2026 NYC premiere, the film has reached 1,000+ community screenings nationwide and holds the record for the most producers ever credited on one feature. On November 9, it's Denver's turn, with a live, intimate Q&A led by the film's Executive Producer and Moms First Founder & CEO, Reshma, in person.

Moms First is fighting for the policy change mothers deserve — paid leave, real childcare, structural support. We've spent years building the other half of that fight: the community, joy, and permission to come first that prove what happens when moms feel seen, resourced, and supported — we take on the world.

The night:

- Cocktail hour, charcuterie & cash bar
- Full screening of No Country for Mothers
- Live Q&A with Reshma Saujani
- Apollo Hall, Denver — Monday, November 9, doors 5pm
- $45 (+ fees) per ticket · 10% of proceeds go directly to Moms First
- Dress code: glam, elevated cocktail — wear something that makes you feel powerful. Can't swing it? No sweat, just bring the vibe.

Endless gratitude to Apollo Hall for donating their beautiful space and believing in this mission as much as we do — this night wouldn't be possible without them.

This isn't for a side. It's for every mother who's tired of being asked to pick one.

RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mft-moms-first-present-no-country-for-mothers-live-with-reshma-saujani-tickets-2002174965218

Only valid tickets purchased from Eventbrite will be admitted to this event.

events.title: Brown County Dems General Monthly Meeting at West High Commons
events.description:
Democrats for Community: 
Meet the Candidates • Know the Platform • Know Your Ballot

Curious about the election? 
Not sure who all the candidates are yet? 
Or just want a chance to hear from people running to represent our community?

Come join us for a friendly, informal evening focused on hearing from the people on the ballot and understanding a little more about the offices they’re seeking.

Our local Democratic candidates will introduce themselves, share why they’re running, and talk about the issues and values that matter most to them. We’ll also review our statewide Democratic candidates, walk through the ballot, and spend a little time on the amendments and referenda voters will see this fall.

And please know: you do not have to be a party member to attend. If you’re curious, still figuring things out, or simply want to become a more informed voter, you are very welcome!

After the program, candidates will stick around for informal questions, conversations, and photos.

Bring a friend, bring your questions, and come as you are. We’d love to have you with us.

Schedule: 
6:00 PM – Community Potluck - join us!
6:30 - 8 PM – Meeting

Bring a dish to share if you'd like, but no contribution is required to attend. See you there!

events.title: GOTV Towson
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.description:
Join Rainier Beach Indivisible on October 17th, Noon-2PM, to hold signs and provide education to our neighborhood on the need to Vote and Vote Early! We are a small but mighty group, dedicated to our south Seattle neighborhood! Join us to hold signs!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Knock Your Neighbors

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Get the Facts Community Coalition for a neighborhood literature drop to help Coloradans learn about Proposition 132 and get out the vote ahead of the November election.

We’ll start at the CCJRC office with a quick overview of Proposition 132, what it would change, and the key facts voters should know. We’ll also make sure you feel prepared to answer basic questions if someone wants to learn more.

Then we’ll load you up with Get the Facts materials to take back to your own neighborhood and distribute to your neighbors.

This is a lit drop, NOT a full canvass. You will not be knocking on doors or expected to initiate conversations with voters. The goal is simply to leave educational materials in your neighborhood so people have accurate information about Proposition 132 as they prepare to vote.

If you happen to encounter a neighbor who wants to talk or asks you a question, don’t worry! Before you leave, we’ll walk through what to say, how to share the facts, and where to direct people who want more information.

No campaign or canvassing experience is required. Just come to learn the facts, grab your materials and snacks, and help us get information about Proposition 132 and a reminder to vote into neighborhoods across the community.

Come learn. Grab some lit. Drop it in your neighborhood. Help your community get the facts and get out the vote.

events.title: Purple on Purpose: Improv for Civil Discourse

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Forget everything you thought you knew about Improv. It’s not frightening, scary or demanding. It’s a lesson in life and in these times, it will serve us well.

Improv for Civil Discourse isn't a debate. There's no topic, no "sides," and no one arguing politics in this room. Just an evening of discovering how "yes, and" might lead to a better tomorrow. We experience acceptance, not agreement. Curiosity, not division. 

Our facilitator for the evening is Will Dennis. Will leads the Unscripted Leadership wing of Unscripted Productions, Ltd. in Washington Crossing. He is highly skilled at changing rooms through deep listening, humor, practical skill building, and strategic facilitation. 

This incredibly fun and enlightening evening will explore innovative ways to increase communication, collaboration, problem solving, adaptability, and creativity.

No pointing fingers. No he said/she said. No accusation.
Just joy and fun, and connection!

The event is free however, donations are welcomed.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth and Bend the Arc Riverdale in Rockland County NY-17!
events.description:
Join Bend the Arc Riverdale and the Unity Democratic Club for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: NDCC Ballots and Brunch!

location.venue: New Direction Christian Church - Hickory Hill

events.description:
Congregation members are invited to review their sample ballots, research the candidates, and make their voting plan at our Ballots and Brunch!

Enjoy a meal as we break down where to find your election info, the office appearing on the November ballot, and the three constitutional amendments appearing on the November ballot. Sign-up so we can get a headcount on food and refreshments. 

Amendment 1 — Bail Would expand the circumstances in which a judge may deny bail. The amendment would remove the constitutional right to bail, when the proof is evident or the presumption great, for certain offenses including second-degree murder, aggravated rape, aggravated rape of a child, an act of terrorism, grave torture, and other offenses requiring at least 85% of a sentence to be served.

Amendment 2 — State Property Tax Would amend the Tennessee Constitution to prohibit the General Assembly from creating or permitting a **state tax on property.

Amendment 3 — Victims’ Rights Would expand and strengthen constitutional rights for victims of crime, including rights related to notification, participation in proceedings and the parole process, protection from harassment and intimidation, information about sentencing and release, restitution, and consideration of victims’ and public safety in release decisions.

events.description:
Community canvassing with Action Together NEPA is about more than just knocking on doors — it’s about building real connections with our neighbors. By having one-on-one conversations, we listen to what matters most to people, share important election information, and make sure every voice in our community is heard. These conversations are proven to be the most effective way to strengthen democracy and inspire action.


When you volunteer, you’ll be part of a supportive team, get quick training, and head out together to engage with your community. events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Fort Wayne. Indiana
events.description:
**'Join Indivisible Northeast Indiana and other nonpartisan groups at No Kings Vote Early**

At this event, we will be providing polling station information (both early voting and election day). encouraging early voting, election defense information provided and recruiting for election defense work.

We're also conducting a **Chalk the Vote** event where we'll have participants decorating the sidewalks with their GOTV message and their artwork.

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No King's Gonna Steal My Vote! Huntsville Protest and Activation

address_lines: Governors Drive Southwest & Harvard Road Southwest

events.description:
Oct 17th, Starting at 10am, Corner of Governors and Harvard.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No King's Gonna Steal My Vote is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote on Nov. 3rd, and participate in the electoral process as Poll Monitors, Poll Watchers, Poll Workers, Absentee Poll roles, participants in vote certification meetings, and candidate swearing in ceremonies.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: ALL OUT: Canvass, Rally, Benefit Show
events.description:
GO ALL OUT FOR TRANS RIGHTS!

Join us on Saturday October 10th as we go ALL OUT to protect the bodily autonomy and rights of kids across our state. We'll kick off with a group canvass launching from the State Capitol at noon, followed by a rally back at the Capitol from 2-4 PM featuring special guest speakers, and ending the day with the ALL OUT benefit show at D3 Arts in Denver’s Westwood neighborhood, featuring local queer and trans musicians starting at 6 PM / from 7-11 PM.

This Saturday 10/10, we'll use our feet and voices and joy to take a stand against ballot propositions 134 + 135. We'll go door to door in groups, sharing directly with our neighbors about these awful ballot measures. We'll hear moving speeches from community leaders, directly affected community members, and allies. Then we'll literally shake off the day by dancing in queer joy and liberation, while raising funds for a safe future for all of Colorado's kids.

The full timeline of the day's events:

11:30 AM - Meet at capitol 

12:00 PM - Canvass launch 

1:30 PM - Meet back at capitol 

2:00 PM - Rally starts 

4:00 PM - Rally ends 

6:00 PM - Doors open for the ALL OUT benefit show at D3 Arts (3632 Morrison Rd, Denver)

7:00 PM - Show starts and will end between 10 and 11

Forward this event to your chosen family and friends - tell them “I’m going ALL OUT this Saturday - will you?”

*Speakers at rally to be announced as we get closer to the date.
