events.title: No Kings Lit Pickup
events.description:
Heading to No Kings on Saturday, October 17? Help us get accurate, accessible information about Proposition 132 into the hands of more Coloradans while you’re there.

Stop by the CCJRC office anytime between 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM on Friday, October 16 to pick up Proposition 132 educational materials to take with you to No Kings.

With so many people gathering on October 17, this is a great opportunity to reach thousands of community members who are already showing up and engaged. We want to make sure they have the facts about Proposition 132 before they cast their ballots.

There’s no formal volunteer shift and no need to stay at the CCJRC office. Just stop by when it works for you, grab a stack of materials, and take them with you to No Kings the next day.

We’ll have materials ready to go and can give you a quick overview of Proposition 132 and answer questions so you feel comfortable sharing information with people you meet.

Already going to No Kings? Turn your trip into an easy Get the Facts action. Stop by, grab some lit, and help us get Proposition 132 information into the hands of voters.

events.title: Get Out The Vote at Kent State (Statewide OSA Action)
events.description:
Students could flip House District 72, Kent State University’s seat in the State House, but it’s up to YOU to make the difference. Join your classmates and students from around the state to canvass to GET OUT THE VOTE at Kent State on October 23rd, 11-4 PM, so we can elect someone who will ACTUALLY represent Kent State students and put pro-SB 1 anti-Kent incumbent Heidi Workman out of a job.

The choice is between Heidi Workman, the incumbent who voted FOR Senate Bill 1, the demolition order for everything that makes Kent State feel like home. It shut down the Multicultural Center, the Women’s Center, and the LGBTQ+ Center in a single day. Students lost scholarships they were already counting on. Professors can’t even strike anymore. Students report Africana students – a program that only exists because students organized for it – is being cut, and even the May 4th class at the May 4th school is under threat. She never met with students. She endorsed Vivek Ramaswamy, who’s talked about shutting Kent State down – her own alma mater – and wants data centers all over Portage County. Jeff Clapper is Kent City Council president; he’s anti-data center, his daughter graduated from Kent State; and he actually wants to make college and trades affordable so students like us can build a future here. Students are pledging to vote, and they’re voting Clapper.

Join students from around the state as we carpool and travel to Kent to knock doors so we can talk to students about the facts of this race and make plans to vote. If students win HD 72, along with other key districts statewide, we could end the supermajority of Republicans that makes it impossible to better our campuses. This is students’ chance to take back our power in Ohio, and it’s up to YOU. RSVP here to get more information so that YOU can make a difference this November. 

We will teach you how to canvass and provide lunch.

events.title: Let's Make Some Posters for our Waterville-area No Kings: Vote Early events)
events.description:
Come make posters with us for our October 17 "No Kings: Vote Early" events in the Waterville-area. Links for those events that day are here:

https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034710/

https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034712/

https://www.mobilize.us/indivisiblemidmaine/event/1034713/

Let's continue to build community AND make art together.

"No Kings: Vote Early" is all about getting out the vote, and voting early is a great technique for protecting our voting rights and ensuring that our votes get counted. The signs we make at this gathering--signs which will be used in our three events on Oct. 17--will all share the theme of voting early, voting safely, voting as an act of democratic participation, and why we love democracy and are determined to defend it. "We Vote Early!" "Oakland Votes Early!" "Waterville Votes Early and Securely!" "If you Love Democracy, VOTE!" etc. 

Poster making supplies will be available, but you should feel welcome to bring your own. And if you are able to bring a snack to share, that would be great! 

A core principle behind all Indivisible, Indivisible Mid Maine, and No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolence and non-violent action. Our events will adhere to this principle, and our posters will, too.

events.title: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays: ICE OUT of Great Neck!
events.description:
Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. When local police or sheriffs collaborate with ICE, it undermines trust, separates families, and makes all of us less safe.

***Our goal is simple and clear:***
No local resources for ICE. No contracts. No data-sharing. No collaboration.

At this event, we will:

1. Bring together neighbors, workers, and allies
2. Prepare to meet with local elected officials (or attend a public meeting)
3. Call on our [city/county/state] leaders to move forward policies that disentangle ICE from local law enforcement

Take concrete steps toward passing local protections

This effort builds on years of organizing led by immigrant communities nationwide — from the fight against 287g contracts to the sanctuary victories that have proven local action works. Cities and states that say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights.

There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

**Vote. Call. Text. Write. And we'll do it in PINK.**

October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It's also election season. And here's the truth: **Black women have higher mortality rates from breast cancer AND less political power to demand the healthcare access we deserve.**

This October 24, we're connecting both fights.

The Equity Alliance is hosting **Paint the Ballot Pink** - a full-day GOTV (Get Out The Vote) mobilization combined with Breast Cancer Awareness programming. We're calling voters, texting voters, writing postcards, all while honoring the fight against breast cancer and the fight for our votes.

### What You'll Do:

- ☎️ Make voter contact calls (we provide scripts and training)

- 📱 Text banking to reach voters

Many neighborhoods throughout the City of Clearlake still need voter outreach, and with a dedicated team of volunteers working together, we can make a tremendous impact in just a few hours.

Whether you've volunteered on a campaign before or are participating for the first time, we welcome you to join us. No previous experience is necessary.

At the beginning of the event, volunteers will receive a brief training covering effective voter engagement techniques and instructions on how to use the PDI app. Once training is complete, volunteers will be assigned walking routes and paired with other participants as needed.

This is a great opportunity to meet fellow community members, support candidates who are committed to Clearlake's future, and make a meaningful contribution to our local election.

Every conversation matters. When neighbors talk to neighbors, we build stronger communities and stronger campaigns. By working together during this organized canvassing event, we can reach more voters and create a stronger presence throughout the city.

events.title: Service At The Soup Kitchen With The Campbell County Democrats
events.description:
At the Campbell County Democratic Party, our motto is "Here For Good." That means we are here to serve our community and make it just a little bit better through our hands-on acts of service, showing up for our neighbors when it matters most.

We invite all community members, volunteers, and local Democrats to join us as we volunteer our time and energy at The Soup Kitchen on the second Monday of each month. Whether you are helping prepare meals, serving food, or assisting with cleanup, your presence makes a direct, meaningful difference for families and individuals in our area.

Come put our values into action alongside fellow community members who care deeply about lifting one another up.

What to Expect & How to Prepare

Tasks: Volunteers may help with food prep, serving guests, kitchen organization, and clean-up duties.

What to Wear: Please wear comfortable, casual clothing and closed-toe shoes. Aprons and hair restraints will be provided on-site if needed.

All Are Welcome: You don't need any prior volunteering experience, just a compassionate heart and a willingness to lend a hand!

Note: Please RSVP in advance so we can coordinate our volunteer count with the soup kitchen coordinators. We look forward to serving alongside you!

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Milwaukee
events.description:
**He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.**  

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

**Date:** Wednesday, October 14th  
**Time:** 10:00am  
**Location:** Milwaukee City Hall, 200 E. Wells St., Milwaukee, WI 53202    

Harry Dunn is joining citizens of Milwaukee for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.  

**Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.**  

This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.  

**Come ready to:**  

- Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection  
- Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard  
- Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it  

RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Green Bay
events.description:
**He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.**  

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

**Date:** Wednesday, October 14th  
**Time:** 2:00 pm   
**Location:** Brown County Courthouse, 100 S. Jefferson St, Green Bay      

Join State Representative Amaad Rivera-Wagner, Dr. Kristen Lyerly, Brown County Indivisible, and Harry Dunn for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. Who just joined the owners of a restaurant that organized a J6 bus from Green Bay. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.

**Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.**  

This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.  

**Come ready to:**  

- Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection  
- Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard  
- Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it  

RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

events.title: Phonebank to Elect Justin J. Pearson for Congress!
events.description:
## Hey friend, got a phone? Great. We need your help real quick!.

### Don't worry, you can help us from anywhere in the United States.

**The Equity Alliance Fund** needs you to grab your phone and make some calls with us. Here's why:

Tennessee's 9th Congressional District was redrawn, splitting Memphis across three congressional districts and leaving thousands of Tennesseans navigating new district lines. In fact, many voters affected by the changes were not expected to receive notices in the mail telling them their district had even changed.

We know this was a deliberate attempt to dilute our vote and our voices. So, this is where we need YOU...

We’re calling our people. We’re making sure they know their district, and we’re making sure Black voters understand the power we still hold, no matter how they redraw the map.

We need to make sure our communities know what district they are in, where they vote, what's at stake, and **why we're supporting Justin J. Pearson for Congress.**

Justin has shown us what it looks like to fight for Black communities, not just when cameras are watching, but when our neighborhoods, our families and our futures are on the line. 

Never phone banked before? We’ll show you how. 
Been doing this for years? We need you, too. 

Grab your phone, share this with your people, give us a little of your time and help us make a BIG impact.


_Zoom link will be sent via text and email 48 hours before the event._

## Event Format

We are going back to our chapter roots for this No Kings: Vote Early event. Just like we did at the Hands Off protest in April 2025 and so many other protests in early 2025, we will meet at S College and W Main before marching down Main St. Volunteers will be stationed throughout with information about early voting, getting involved in our elections work, and protecting everyone’s vote.

## Event Logistics
- Parking map available at https://www.indivisiblenewarkde.org/upcoming-activity/no-kings. Please leave closer spots for people who use a wheelchair, a walker, etc.
- The march is around 1.5 miles. Anyone who does not want to march can remain at the protest start location throughout.
- If you want your protest sign read by cars driving by, remember that large bold font and simple phrases are more visible.
- As usual, there will be a team of protest volunteers to help ensure the event runs smoothly.
- Do not engage with hecklers (which have been very rare thus far). Report hecklers to a Safety Team member (yellow vest) and do not engage with them.
- Help us care for this space—please don’t litter.

## Rationale Behind this Day of Action

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not a day of massive protest around the country. Instead, on October 17th, we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and to demonstrate that the people have the power.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

events.description:
Let’s Make Michigan History: No Kings-Vote Early!
Join Indivisible Huron Valley on October 17 for our next No Kings event—this time with one big, bold goal: to help drive the largest early-voting turnout in Michigan history.

We’re shifting from mass rally mode to people-powered community action. Early in-person voting begins October 24, but many Michiganders still don’t know when it starts—or where to cast their ballot, since early voting locations are often different from regular Election Day polling places.

That’s where we come in.

On October 17, we’ll come together to reach voters where they are—through canvassing, texting, and postcards. Whether you love knocking doors, prefer sending messages, or want to help from a table with a stack of postcards, there will be a role for you.

We’ll provide the contact lists, scripts, postcards, and materials you need. You bring your energy, your voice, and your commitment to democracy.

Let’s make sure voters are ready. Let’s make early voting visible. Let’s make October 24 the start of a turnout wave Michigan has never seen before.

We will meet at a central location for training and activities. After the work is done, we’ll celebrate together at a local venue—because building power should also build community. Stay tuned for details!

events.title: Knock Doors in Allegany County with Del. Joe Vogel!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and elect local Democrats in Allegany County!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Sweetwater Monthly Executive Committee Meeting!
events.description:
🌵 Sweetwater County Democrats Monthly Meeting

Third Thursday. 6 PM. Rotating towns, same crew. 💙

It’s our monthly Executive Committee meeting! Come hang out, catch up, and help keep the wheels turning for the Sweetwater County Democrats.

We’ll talk about what’s happening, what’s coming up, where we can lend a hand, and how we keep showing up for our community.

📍 Green River Library
🕕 6:00 PM
📅 October 15th, 3rd Thursday of the Month 


We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

events.title: Help the White Mountains Vote with Election Protection!
events.description: Join Common Cause Arizona for an in-person Poll Monitor Training in Show Low! Common Cause Arizona is hosting a series of in-person Election Protection Poll Monitor trainings across Northern Arizona! Northern Arizona is very rural and faces unique geographical and legal challenges. Poll monitors are the first line of defense against attempts to discourage voters and spread disinformation. events.description:
🌵 Sweetwater County Democrats Monthly Meeting

Third Thursday. 6 PM. Rotating towns, same crew. 💙

It’s our monthly Executive Committee meeting! Come hang out, catch up, and help keep the wheels turning for the Sweetwater County Democrats.

We’ll talk about what’s happening, what’s coming up, where we can lend a hand, and how we keep showing up for our community.

📍 White Mountain Library
🕕 6:00 PM
📅 3rd Thursday of the Month 


We’re keeping our monthly meetings moving around Sweetwater County so we can stay connected to folks across the county. That means we’ll see you in Green River in October, Rock Springs in November, Green River in December, and keep rotating from there.

📅 October 15 — Green River
📅 November 19 — Rock Springs
📅 December 17 — Green River

We’ll kick things off at 6 PM with a short meeting — usually just 10–20 minutes to cover the business we actually need to cover. Then? That’s when the good stuff happens.

Stick around to catch up with fellow Democrats, meet new folks, swap ideas, ask questions, or jump into a training or organizing project. Sometimes we’ll have a specific training planned; sometimes we’ll just figure out what our community needs that month.

No fancy credentials required. No secret handshake. Just show up, bring a friend, and help us build a county party that knows its neighbors and knows how to show up for them.

Come for the meeting. Stay for the friends. 💙

General elections are just around the corner, and we need your help! To implement a Working Families Agenda, we need a majority progressive City Council here in Seattle. events.title: Tacos & Treats: Your Vote, Your Voice, Your Fiesta
events.description:
**Join us for Tacos & Treats: Your Vote, Your Voice, Your Fiesta!**

Bring the whole family for a fun, welcoming, **nonpartisan civic fiesta** where community, food, and voting resources come together.

Enjoy **free tacos, Halloween activities, festive treats, music, local vendors, and a family-friendly Halloween contest**—all while getting helpful **voting resources** in one convenient place. Guests can check their voter registration, learn about voting options, find official ballot drop boxes, and get support creating a personalized plan to participate in the election.

After gathering together, we’ll offer a short community walk to a nearby official ballot drop box, with rides available for those who need them. Anyone who is ready to return their ballot can do so safely and securely on October 24!

Washington’s 2026 general-election voting period begins **October 16**, with ballots mailed to registered voters. Voters can use official ballot drop boxes, return ballots by mail, or access voting centers for in-person assistance. Official drop boxes are available throughout the state and accept ballots through **8 p.m. on Election Day, November 3**.

**Join your neighbors on October 24 for food, fun, music, conversation, and the information you need to make a voting plan that works for you.**

Come for the tacos. Stay for the treats. **Leave ready to participate!**

This event is in partnership with Poder Latinx, WCA, La Casa Hogar, NAACP and APIC.

events.description:

This feature-length documentary includes interviews with organizers and community leaders involved in the resistance to ICE in the Twin Cities and firsthand footage of the resistance in the streets and the January 23 mass strike showing the enormous power of the working class.

events.title: NO KINGS: EARLY VOTING IS YOUR SUPERPOWER!
events.description:
# **NO KINGS: EARLY VOTING IS YOUR SUPERPOWER!**

On October 17, the NO KINGS movement shifts from PROTEST to **ACTION**.  

Come show your community - your kids, grandkids, neighbors, and friends - what civic participation looks like, and how joyful it can be. **Your vote is your superpower—and your participation can help someone else discover theirs.**

Join Change Begins With ME for a fun, family-friendly morning celebrating the power of voting early.

Our inflatable Vote Early Super Squad will be joining us, too—and costumes are encouraged for kids and adults! It's an opportunity to show young people that voting isn't simply an errand we run every couple of years. It's our superpower!!

**FOR ADULTS:**
Bring your ballot - completed or still in progress.  If you're ready to vote early, you can return your ballot at the official ballot drop box at the nearby North University Community Library. You’ll also find reliable voting information and resources for tracking your ballot and knowing where to get help if a voting problem arises. 

We'll share information about Election Protection opportunities for those interested in being ready to help voters leading up to November 3 and afterward.

**FOR KIDS:**
Kids can get in on the action, too! At our Future Voters area, children's voting booths will offer age-appropriate mock ballots so younger children and older kids can experience making a choice, privately marking a ballot, and casting their vote.  

**FOR EVERYONE:**
Explore our interactive Superpower Stations, mingle and enjoy music, and celebrate civic participation together.  Click link for event map and additional details. Check back for updates. https://bit.ly/NOKINGS_UCMAP 

Help us create a community where voting is visible, shared, and celebrated.  Bring a friend. Bring a neighbor. Bring your family. Bring your ballot.

## **YOUR VOTE IS YOUR SUPERPOWER. USE IT. SHARE IT. PROTECT IT.**
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Sippin’ Pints & Speakin’ Politics
events.description:
## *Galt x Neighbors RESIST are fostering a new, welcoming space in Galt to get involved, remain informed, and have a greater voice in the local area!*

### ** *We are founded in centrist and left-leaning ideals, but open to all perspectives!* **

> ### ***LET’S RESIST DIVISIVENESS, TOGETHER!*** ✌️🦋💕💪

#### Come drop by River Rock Brewery on a 2nd or 4th Tuesday, and join your local community in discussing local and current politics! We also have local event fliers, campaign/action information, signatures for Medicare For All, occasional post carding, and so so much more! Come get involved! 💕

##### 🦋 *It’s hard to admit, but there are so many of us long-time Galtonian residents that have scattered further north and south in our activism ventures; Meanwhile, our city needs us right here and now!! If you’re interested in getting organized more locally, ***please***, come join us!!* 🦋

#### Sit with us at the table to partake in conversations about local & federal government, current events, campaigns, causes, activism, volunteering, local happenings, and ways we hope to achieve positive impacts in our community together!!

### 💪 ***Connect With Neighbors*** 
### 👀 ***Discuss Local News*** 
### 💕 ***Share Concerns*** 
### 🦋 ***Get Involved and Active***

In it, 37 Americans answer one question: What can I do? Artists, teachers, veterans, neighbors. Their answers are small, specific, and more powerful than you'd expect. So are ours.

**New date, better reason:** Bobby Roth will join us by Zoom from Los Angeles after the film for a Q&A. We moved the screening to make it happen.

Then we'll have a short conversation about where our own light can do the most good between now and the midterms.

This is a nonpartisan event, and everyone is welcome. If you're running for office, we'd love to have you, as a neighbor. Please leave the campaign pitch at home for the night.

$25 per person: [Chip in here](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cambridgeindivisible?amount=25&refcode=lightworkers)
Your donation keeps grassroots organizing going here on the Shore.

Good to know:

* We'll share the location in Cambridge with registered guests after you RSVP.
* The film will be shown outside, so dress warm, bring a blanket, and/or chair.
* Bring a friend. That's how this works.

events.title: How to Protect Our Votes and Our Democracy (Mpls,, MN)

location.venue: St John's Episcopal Church (Sponsored by Comma, a Bookstore)

events.description:
Free and fair elections are foundational to a vibrant democracy. As we face new federal challenges to our voting rights in this midterm election, we can protect everyone’s rights and freedoms if we act together, just as we’ve done before.

Join Na Eng of People For the American Way and author of The Art of Saving Democracy, along with Kate Wegener and Stephen Seidel of Indivisible Twin Cities, for an essential democracy protection training. They’ll provide context for what’s at stake, offer an overview of how elections work in Minnesota, answer your questions about voting rights and election security, and share concrete ways to be part of the solution immediately. 

The goal is for attendees to leave prepared to counter disinformation, empowered to understand and exercise their voting rights, energized to rally eligible voters across the state to participate, and ready to mobilize against any threats of federal interference. There are many ways to defend and strengthen our democracy—and this training will inspire and equip you to do your part immediately.

Note: This event is a second offering of the event held at Next Chapter Bookstore on October 6.

events.title: No Hate in Washington State - NO on I-001 & I-638 Phone Bank!
events.description:
There's no room for hate in Washington state!  

With two harmful initiatives on the ballot this November, we're asking you to join us to make phone calls to encourage Washingtonians to vote NO on both of them.

We'll be joining the No Hate in Washington State group to support their amazing work to fight back!

RSVP now to get info to join! 
____________________________________________________________
IL26-001 (also known as I-001) is a measure on the November 2026 ballot. It would weaken Washington State laws about parents’ rights, student privacy and records at school.

I-638 would require tens of thousands of elementary, middle and high school girls to undergo intrusive, potentially harmful medical sex inspections every year as a new part of sports physicals. It takes decision-making power away from parents, schools and athletic associations with a statewide ban excluding trans girls from participating in any sports at any level.



FIND OUT MORE ABOUT IL26-001 here: https://nohateinwastate.org/about-i-001

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Prep with NELC-I!
events.description:
## ** Join NE Lake County Indivisible Outreach & Elections Teams for prep before No Kings 4: Vote Early!**

The fight to protect voting rights never ends, and right now, we’re witnessing a Jim-Crow-era effort from politicians and their billionaire friends to restrict our freedoms, silence our voices, and consolidate power.

But in America, we choose our leaders. We will decide our future. The same spirit that fueled Selma, Montgomery, and the March on Washington lives on in our unified action.

### The national theme of this No Kings event is Vote Early to protect our vote and strike back against MAGA! NELC-I will be handing out non-partisan voting zines with information on why voting is so important and how to vote in Lake County, along with Know Your Rights information if you see ICE. We’ve printed 10,000 copies, so we need your help to fold and prepare them for distribution! 

Join us for socializing, light refreshments, and doing our part. We will provide all training and supplies, so just bring yourself (and a friend or two)! We may also be finishing up the Know Your Rights whistle kits and postcards to swing state voters to remind them to vote, so there’s a task for everyone. 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Some quotes from past participants:
- "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"
- "It was fun working with people who share your feelings about what's happening in our country and overseas. I find it inspiring and it gives me hope."
- "great turnout, super well organized. welcoming and fun."
- "I took action for NE Lake County IL Indivisible because last time we put together whistle kits, I was impressed by how organized the work was, how professional, encouraging and friendly the leaders were. It was the same this time. The leaders told us about other opportunities with the organization. They sat and chatted with the groups at each of the tables. The volunteers were all friendly. I felt able to speak freely. We didn't speak of frustrations. We talked of opportunity for helping others." 

## *ABOUT NE LAKE COUNTY INDIVISIBLE:*

NE Lake County IL Indivisible is a nonpartisan grassroots organization founded in 2025 in defense of democracy. We are Lake County residents working together to protect elections and neighbors. We aim to support targeted populations and take action on a local and national level to push back against authoritarianism. We welcome everyone, whether you voted this way or that way, or didn't vote at all in 2024.

### More about us can be found here:

### https://nelakecounty-indivisible.org
### https://linktr.ee/nelakecountyindivisible

- *These efforts cost money to put together! If you are able to financially support us, please consider making a donation here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblenelc1350105033*

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box.

events.title: HANDS OFF LUZERNE: Countywide Mass Meeting
events.description:
Many of us believe that we’re immune to election sabotage, or that only experts can and will ensure free and democratic elections. The truth is: We’re not immune and what happens next is up to us. Luzerne County is strongest when all of us show up, speak out, and refuse to be intimidated.

The Trump regime knows they’re losing, so instead of courting our votes, they are trying to keep us from voting to seize more power. They are creating fear through deploying ICE and federal agents. They are sewing chaos and confusion to control our elections so they can declare themselves the winners before we even cast our votes.

Join us for the HANDS OFF LUZERNE: Countywide Mass Meeting to learn what you can do between now and Election Day to protect our neighbors and our votes.

This is a family friendly event. 

. . . . . 

Muchos de nosotros creemos que somos inmunes al sabotaje electoral, o que solo los expertos pueden y van a garantizar elecciones libres y democráticas. La verdad es que no somos inmunes, y lo que sucede a continuación depende de nosotros. El condado de Lancaster es más fuerte cuando todos nos presentamos, alzamos la voz y nos negamos a dejarnos intimidar. 

El régimen de Trump sabe que está perdiendo, así que en lugar de buscar nuestros votos, está tratando de impedir que votemos. Quieren usar el caos y la confusión para controlar nuestras elecciones y así poder declararse de ICE y agentes federales. Quieren usar el caos y la confusión para controlar nuestras elecciones y así poder declararse ganadores antes de que siquiera emitimos nuestros votos. 

Únete a nosotros en la MANOS FUERA DE LUZERNE: Reunión Masiva de Todo el Condado para aprender qué puedes hacer entre ahora y el día de las elecciones para proteger a nuestros vecinos y nuestros votos.

events.description:
**Join us for the Currituck Canvass!** Connecting face-to-face with voters is one of the most effective ways we can build community and make our voices heard across Currituck County.

Whether you’re a seasoned canvasser or taking to the trail for the first time, we’ll provide all the training, talking points, and materials you need before we head out.

**We Need Everyone: Rookies and Vets**

If you are new to canvassing, don’t worry! You will never go out alone. Every newcomer is paired with an experienced veteran who will guide you every step of the way. We work in teams to ensure a supportive, collaborative entry into grassroots activism.

**Safe, Professional, and Guided**

Your safety and comfort are our top priorities.

-   Targeted Outreach: We use advanced data to ensure you are visiting voters who are ready for the No Kings message. Politeness First: A simple "Thank you for your time!" is all you need for any rare non-supporter; you are always in control of the conversation.
    
-   Full Training: We provide on-site training before every shift. You  
    will receive a professionally developed script and hands-on guidance on using the MiniVAN app.
    
-   Ongoing Support: For any difficult questions, you can immediately  
    contact your Canvass Organizer for assistance.
    

**An Inspiring and Energizing Experience**

Canvassing is more than just work—it is empowering, rewarding, and energizing. Our volunteers consistently return from their shifts fired up by the incredible stories and connections they’ve made with neighbors. Spending time with like-minded activists and standing up against tyranny to secure a win is an unmatched feeling.

## What to Bring

-   Comfortable walking shoes.
    
-   A fully charged smartphone with the MiniVAN app installed.
    
-   Sunscreen or rain gear, depending on the forecast.
    
-   Water and snacks.
    
-   Your passion for democracy and making a difference!
    

[Click here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fLkpSPnA_FJhqjpU1tHU_7na4djzYl7rFKeAEX9oBNc/edit?usp=sharing) for more canvassing tips.

## Ready to help lay the groundwork for victory?

Sign up today and help us build the unstoppable momentum we need for November!

events.title: Phone Bank Party with Iowa City SURJ

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!##

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:##

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?## 

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:## 

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:### 

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: Yes4EDR Town Hall - Cambridge
events.description:
Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the Cambridge Public Library to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Turn Up for Good Cause!
events.description:
** THIS VOTE HAS BEEN RESCHEDULED FOR THE NEXT COMMON COUNCIL MEETING OCTOBER 21ST ** After months of continued advocacy by Citizen Action CNY, the Utica Common Council will finally be voting on Good Cause Eviction at the next meeting, Wednesday October 21st at 7:00pm. 

Right now, too many renters are facing excessive rent hikes, non-renewals, or unfair evictions that are forcing them out of their homes and neighborhoods. Utica has seen rents rise over 20% over the last few years, one of the highest rates in the nation, and the effects of the housing crisis are seen every day. 

Good Cause Eviction allows more tenants to remain in their homes, combats excessive rent hikes, and reduces the burden on the housing courts. If you pay your rent and you follow your lease, you should be able to stay in your home! 

Turn out Oct. 21st at 7pm at Utica City Hall to show the Common Council that Utica needs Good Cause!

San Antonio NM ~> Stallion Gate 12 miles east

OUR LAND, OUR PEOPLE, OUR VOTE ! 


**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Talking to voters face-to-face is the best way to earn their support for Democrats up and down the ticket and beat Susan Collins.

You should also go to your App Store or Google Play Store and download the MiniVAN app and create an account if you don’t have one already.

iOS: https://apple.co/34ctpME

Android: https://tinyurl.com/androidminivan

Once you have MiniVAN downloaded on your phone, you can use this test list to practice using the map, finding the houses you are supposed to knock and who lives there, moving through the script, seeing the not home options, and navigating from house to house. Can't wait to see you soon!

events.title: Knocking on Doors Sundays in Westland
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!


This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.


Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.


Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.


Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Call Out Data Centers! Phone Bank with Team Vikki
events.description:
Data centers are moving into our communities rapidly, straining our water resources and power grid while everyday Texans worry about rising energy bills. 

Tax breaks for the corporations building data centers is projected to cost Texas nearly *$1.8 BILLION a year* by 2030. They’ll keep coming, and they’ll keep gobbling up Texas land and water with no regard for the people and animals who live here. 

Dan Patrick's answer? Stall. But we don't have time to wait on him.

**Vikki Goodwin [has a better plan](https://www.vikkigoodwin.com/datacenters): stop new data center construction *now*, until Texas passes real protections.** People and animals drink first. Data centers pay for their own water and electricity, so your bills don't go up. Counties get the power to protect their communities, and companies that hide their water use face real consequences. 

Voters across the state are worried about data centers moving in. They need to hear that Vikki Goodwin is the one with a plan to protect our water *and* our wallets.

Join Team Vikki on Saturday afternoons and Wednesday evenings as we call voters most impacted by data centers in their communities. 

No experience needed. We’ll train you, and you will not do it alone! Just bring your voice, a phone, and a laptop.

events.title: Souls to the Polls Elmira Community Center

location.venue: SW Corner of Hatch and Rauhut Streets

events.description:
Indivisible Alamance NC, in partnership with the Alamance NAACP and many, many others want you to vote EARLY!

This is open to everyone. Voters, supporters, candidates, families... you get the idea.

We know things are going to be a bit gonzo on election day. We know absentee and mail-in voting is under attack both nationally and right here in North Carolina.

Therefore, to encourage people to vote (and make it a little more fun and interesting) we are hosting early voting marches TO EVERY EARLY VOTING SITE!

## Getting Ready to vote

If you haven't registered to vote yet, you still can through October 9th. But wait, there's more! During early voting, you can register when you arrive at the early voting location and vote immediately.

If you're already registered, please [check your registration](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to be sure everything is accurate and you haven't been unexpectedly cancelled.

## The more the merrier!

You can sign up to join us for any or all of the events but you can only vote once.

## Elmira Community Center SOULS TO THE POLLS

This is the big one. If you haven't voted by now, please plan to vote here. We want to ensure the numbers support keeping this early voting location open for many years to come.

When: Sunday, October 15, Meet at 2:00 P.M. March at 2:30 P.M.

Where: Parking lot at the corner of Hatch St and Rauhut St, Burlington - [map link](https://maps.app.goo.gl/JkAR26inNgfJq5V47)

How: We'll start with a invocation, a short rally and a speaker At about 2:30, we'll begin marching as a group to the community center. We will provide flags. You are welcome to provide family-friendly signs with your voting message.

We'll provide a light meal, snacks and water for everyone (while supplies last) at the destination. Rides back to the start will be available for those who need them. We'll also have a follow vehicle in case anyone needs assistance getting to the polling site.

events.title: No Kings Bridge RIPY
events.description:
No Kings Day is Oct 17th, 2026! This time we are going out in the communities to spread the word about the importance of VOTING EARLY! No Kings: Vote Early is about making sure every eligible voter has a plan to vote early, knows their options, and is ready to make their voice count. We need folks on the bridge all day to reach as many voters on the highway as possible. There are 2 shifts available. Wear your patriotic gear! We will provide the main large sign. ***Please follow all safety instructions provided by the bridge host. You can park along the field of the school playground on E Ripy. Be careful crossing the street onto the bridge. Please watch the following video on de-escalation BEFORE attending the event. https://youtu.be/R2PSExM-NhU?si=V_K0zwKan0FGZtIh

Be sure to join our socials and share your pics from the event (please tag us and #visibilitybrigade, #nokings): https://linktr.ee/jointhe12

Bridge Brigades will cancel if the forecasted weather is: -Under 40 degrees -Rain is forecasted at 50% *Bridge host may cancel that morning if they arrive at the bridge and it is raining. We do not want to add to any traffic concerns in the rain. -Bridge Hosts will make a judgment call if inclement weather moves in while on the bridge. If lightning is within 6 miles of the bridge, hosts will ask all volunteers to leave immediately. Hosts will use their best judgement regarding wind gusts. Please listen to Bridge Hosts as your safety is a priority. -Bridge Hosts will make every effort to cancel the next day's bridge protest by 9PM the night before, if needed.

**We reject all forms of political violence and intimidation, no matter the source or the target. That’s not just a moral stance—it’s a strategic one. Movements that create lasting change do so by building trust, forging solidarity, and demonstrating discipline, even in the face of threats or attacks.

events.title: African Voices, Shared Futures: How Communities Build Peace in Times of Conflict
events.description:
Join members of the Salama Hub advocacy delegation for an inspiring evening of stories, dialogue, and reflection. Peacebuilders, faith leaders, researchers, and community advocates from the Horn of Africa will share how communities facing violence, displacement, political instability, and social division are building peace from the ground up through faith, courage, and collective action. The event will explore the power of local leadership, grassroots organizing, and global solidarity in creating more just and peaceful futures for all.

Hosted by the American Friends Service Committee, Atlanta Friends Meeting, Beacon Hill Black Alliance for Human Rights, CAIR-Georgia, Friends of the Congo, and Park Avenue Baptist Church.

Jen Todd represents the future Illinois’ 15th District deserves: practical leadership, real community connection, and a commitment to working people. Visit [jentodd2026.us](https://www.jentodd2026.us/) to learn more, get answers to your questions, sign up to volunteer, or make a donation to help elect Jen Todd and move IL-15 forward. 🦋🖇️🌊

events.title: October 24 Volunteer Tree-Wrapping Event! 9am at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens
events.description:
Join us for a morning of stewardship volunteering at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens! 

Help us protect the trees of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens from the busy beavers. As beaver activity increases this fall, volunteers will cut lengths of welded-wire fencing to size for approximately 252 trees near the ponds, pools, and wetland boardwalk. Each piece will be wrapped around a tree trunk and secured to form a sturdy circular barrier, shielding the bark from gnawing and damage. This hands-on project directly safeguards the park's beloved tree canopy, cultural integrity, and public viewshed that makes Kenilworth so special. 

Free registration, open to groups and individuals.

Space is limited for this event and pre-registration is required. 

Participate in a morning of park stewardship by taking on litter collection around the park. All tools will be provided. This event will run rain or shine—please dress accordingly and plan to work outside!

The park is accessible by car and there is a large visitor parking lot available for use. By Metro, the park entrance is 1.0 mile from the Deanwood Metro Station and 1.3 miles from the Minnesota Ave Station, both on the Orange Line. By foot or bike, access the park via the Anacostia River Trail.

We'll provide all necessary tools and supplies. We recommend you bring a water bottle, snack, hat, bag/backpack, a change of clothes, and sun protection. Please wear clothes and shoes you aren't afraid to get wet or muddy and dress according to the weather. We recommend that you do not wear jewelry.

We encourage families and students to join us. Volunteers under the age of 18 must be accompanied by an adult chaperone, parent or guardian. This event is eligible for Student Service Learning hours (SSL). Bring your form or email it to info@fokag.org.

Contact: For all other questions or concerns reach out to info@fokag.org.

More about Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens: Check out our website (www.kenaqgardens.org) and follow us on Instagram, Facebook and Twitter (@kenaqgardens).

PHOTO/MEDIA RELEASE- By registering for this event, you agree to the following: 

"I grant Friends of Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens, its partners, and representatives permission to use, publish, and share photographs, video, audio recordings, and other media of me for educational, promotional, and mission-related purposes. This includes use in print, digital, and social media. I understand that no compensation will be provided for such use."

events.title: CHICAGO CONCERT FOR DEMOCRACY
events.description:
We are proud to host a fundraising event for Partners For Our Communities! **The suggested minimum donation is $25 per person. Please visit this link:** https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mfdtix

All are invited to the 2nd annual Concert for Democracy, an afternoon of live music in support of grassroots activism on Sunday, Oct. 11 from 1 - 4 p.m. at Belvedere Banquets, 1170 W. Devon Ave., Elk Grove Village. Featuring acclaimed local rock, folk, jazz and blues artists and emceed by on-air personality Patti Vasquez of WCPT AM Radio 820, the event is raising funds for Partners for Our Communities, a Palatine-based nonprofit that empowers underserved and marginalized people to develop self-sufficiency and become leaders in their communities. 

**Suggested minimum donation is $25 per person, which may be paid ahead of the event at https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mfdtix, or at the door.**

**Musical line-up** is SK Horizon (featuring Steve Koerber and Summer Kwai); Dave Rudolf and Friends; Emma’s Revolution; Naüvoo; Chicago Rock Exchange; Billy Branch and the Sons of Blues. 

The emcee is **Patti Vasquez** from WCPT, AM Radio 820.  

The concert will also feature remarks from U.S. Rep. Delia Ramirez (IL-3),
Gen Z Podcaster Ishaan Srivastava and other elected officials and civic leaders. Throughout the afternoon, event-goers will be able to chat with representatives of local organizations who will be staffing tables, and register for volunteer opportunities, including get-out-the-vote activities affiliated with national No Kings Vote Early events on Oct. 17. 

The non-partisan event is collaboratively sponsored by eight chapters of the national Indivisible movement: Indivisible Elk Grove Township; Indivisible Niles Maine Township; Indivisible Des Plaines; Indivisible Evanston; Indivisible Highland Park; Indivisible NWSOFA; The People’s Post Alliance Indivisible Chapter; and Indivisible Illinois.

location.venue: Volunteer travel to the Fresno area!

events.description:
**CD22 GOTV is here!** Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect Randy Villegas in 2026 and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  **$100 stipend** a day available to offset the cost of gas and lodging.

 - Friday, October 30 | 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 31 | 9:00 am to 4:30 pm

 - Sunday, November 1 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Monday, November 2 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

 - Tuesday, November 3 | 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.

No experience is necessary. When you arrive at the staging location you will be trained and given all the supplies you need. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, snacks and water. Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Read more about Randy Villegas here - https://www.villegasforcongress.com

Never canvassed before or need a refresher?  Join the Bay Area Coalition *Yes, You Can(vass)!* workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

Or, if you are not able to knock doors, you can still support volunteer canvassers in the Central Valley - donate here https://secure.actblue.com/donate/centralvalleycanvassing

For more Bay Area Coalition actions: https://bayareacoalition.org/

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Coffee County
events.description:
On Saturday, October 17th, No Kings returns with another nationwide day of action. No Kings: Vote Early is the next step of reclaiming the power of the people.  

It's a day of voter participation and making sure every eligible voter has a plan, knows their options, and is ready to make their voice count. 

Event: No Kings: Vote Early Coffee County
Date: Saturday, October 17th
Early Voting Rally: 9 AM - 11 AM
Vote Early Door Knocking: 11 AM - 1 PM
Location: Tullahoma High School, 510 S Jackson St, Tullahoma

________

For over a year, millions of people have come together to send a clear message: in America, we have no kings. Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. 

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of voter participation: 

Early Voting Rally: 9 AM - 11 AM

We'll be rallying at the parking lot in front of Tullahoma  High School. Bring signs encouraging people to vote, and to vote EARLY! Early voting will run from October 14th to October 29th. Let's remind our community to use their most powerful right: the right to vote. Please leave negative signs at home. Signs about voting, unity, positivity, democracy, and putting People Over Politics are welcome. During the rally, our volunteers will be talking with attendees about the door knocking phase of the event which will start at 11 am. 

Vote Early Door Knocking: 11 AM - 1 PM

After the rally, we will put our people power to action by door knocking in neighborhoods around Tullahoma, to encourage folks to vote early. It is activities like this that will have a profound impact on the election. Attendees will be given simple instructions, and can be paired with experienced door knockers if needed. Bring a snack! After the door knocking, attendees are encouraged to swing by Ole Shed Brewery for a celebratory beer and to discuss the experience!

No one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in Tullahoma and local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no kings.

events.title: Early Voting Caravan to the Polls Graham NC
events.description:
Indivisible Alamance NC, in partnership with many, many others, wants you to vote EARLY!

This is open to everyone. Voters, supporters, candidates, families... you get the idea.

We know things are going to be a bit gonzo on election day. We know absentee and mail-in voting is under attack both nationally and right here in North Carolina.

Therefore, to encourage people to vote (and make it a little more fun and interesting) we are hosting early voting marches TO EVERY EARLY VOTING SITE!  

For this event in Graham, we're going to **CARAVAN** to the voting site (Graham Recreation Center, 311 College St.), so there's no need to even get out of your vehicle!  You can even vote curbside when you arrive, if you like.

### Getting Ready to vote

If you haven't registered to vote yet, you still can through October 9th. But wait, there's more! During early voting, you can register when you arrive at the early voting location and vote immediately.

If you're already registered, please [check your registration](https://vt.ncsbe.gov/RegLkup/) to be sure everything is accurate and you haven't been unexpectedly cancelled.

### The more the merrier!

You can sign up to join us for any or all of the events but you can only vote once.

## Graham Rec Center

When: Thursday, October 15.  Arrive to start the caravan at Bethany Church Rec Area any time between 8:45 and 10:30 A.M.  Departures begin at 9:00 A.M.

Where: Gather at Bethany Presbyterian Church Recreation Area, 1500 Swepsonville Rd., Graham.  Look for signs & yellow-vested smiling people to guide you.

How: This will be a driving caravan, leaving in small groups of a few cars at a time. We'll provide flags and a route map.  Bring a friend, signs to post in your windows, decorate your car if'n you can, and we'll have car-decorating chalk at the site to help you finish your festive look for the drive!  

We'll provide snacks and coffee for everyone before you depart for the caravan!

events.title: Orlando Community to Celebrate Culture and Early Voting at “Fall Fiesta” on Vote Early Day
events.description:
Vote Early Day: Fall Fiesta 

Voting early is one way to make your voice heard, and making a plan can help you feel ready to cast your ballot. That’s why Poder Latinx and community partners are hosting Fall Fiesta on Saturday, October 24: to bring our Orlando community together, celebrate Vote Early Day, and help neighbors take the next step toward voting.

Bring your family and enjoy live music, DJs, cultural performances, local food vendors, art, and fall activities. You can also visit our nonpartisan voter information stations to learn about your voting options, find an early voting location, and make a plan that works for you. Free transportation to an early voting location will be available for eligible voters who need a ride.

Join us for a day of community, culture, and civic participation!

events.title: NO KINGS:Vote Early Overpass Visibility Action -- Adams St. @I- 580
events.description:
### Join us to celebrate Early Voting and Election Defense!

Stockpiling the early vote is a powerful form of election protection. On NO KINGS Day, Oct 17, we’ll spread the message that everyone needs to vote early, everyone needs to tell their friends to vote early, and we all need to get ready to defend the election.

We'll be out waving to traffic for a joyful overpass visibility event to show our voting pride.

RSVP for updates!

Overpass actions are a great entry into the public resistance movement. The IEB Overpass Visibility Brigade has hosted messages from overpasses 5 times a week for over a year. We look forward to celebrating the right to vote with you on No Kings!!

Pop by for encouragement, no need to stay the entire time.

Want to start spreading the word NOW about voting early? [This resource guide](https://www.nokings.org/nkve-resources) has everything you need!

Want to get alerts about how to defend the vote in case of major election sabotage? Join this [announcement-only Signal group](https://signal.group/#CjQKIAYNo3cCgCscZMDbhZc1pmGrDQDpPoogP_SSlYF49MkKEhAl-bTHqIywsX5q_GoG0IV1).

Photos and video of this event may be shared publicly, please inform photographers and/or organizers if you don't want to be photographed.

We look forward to being visible with you! Rain or Shine.

** RSVP to get updates. **

Polls are open Monday at the Fairfax County Government Center and on October 22 at the McLean Government Center. Please remind people not only to vote but to bring friends and neighbors.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

Lots of parking at the McLean Community Center.

Northern Virginia Voices is a local group of neighbors around the McLean area who support the vision of the Declaration of Independence and the rule of the Constitution. If you'd like to get emails on ways to get active, email us at northernvirginiavoices@gmail.com

### Legacy Realigned 2026

As we build toward our Legacy picket, we need coworkers ready to lead on the line. No experience required, just a willingness to step up.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in the OC (CA-45)!
events.description:
Join Swing Left OC and other Swing Left groups for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We’ve launched an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

 - Listen for what is shaping each voter’s decision.

 - Persuade through deeper conversation, personal stories, and a clear connection between electing Democrats and what the voter cares about.

 - Mobilize voters who are leaning Democratic with the information they need to cast their ballots.

 - Record detailed notes so our phone callers and letter writers can continue the conversation through personalized follow-up.

First time? No worries. We'll provide training and all the supplies. And we'll pair you with an experienced canvasser! Lunch will be provided at the debrief.  Bring a lawn chair.  See you at the canvass!

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Wisconsin Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Wisconsin voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

events.title: Bradstock and W&J Dems Town Hall
events.description:
Southwestern Pennsylvania deserves a representative who listens.

Join Alan Bradstock and the Washington & Jefferson College Democrats for a community Town Hall in Washington, PA.

This Town Hall, co-hosted by the W&J College Democrats, is an opportunity for students, community members, and voters from across the area to ask questions, discuss the issues that matter most to them, and hear Alan’s vision for the future of Pennsylvania’s 14th Congressional District.

Come be part of a real conversation about the challenges facing our communities—from jobs and economic development to healthcare, veterans’ issues, Social Security, Medicare, and the future of Southwestern Pennsylvania.

events.title: Ballot Measures 101: Denver & Colorado
events.description:
Join Indivisible Denver Action and the League of Women Voters for a nonpartisan deep dive into this year's Denver and Colorado ballot measures.

With so many measures on the ballot this fall, it can be hard to keep track of what's actually being decided and what a "yes" or "no" vote means. That's where the League of Women Voters comes in. As a nonpartisan organization, LWV doesn't support political parties or candidates — instead, they focus on giving voters clear, fact-based information so you can make your own informed decision.

What we'll cover:

An overview of the most impactful Denver and Colorado ballot measures
Fact-based background on each measure
Arguments for and against (pros and cons)
What a "yes" vote means, and what a "no" vote means
Time at the end for questions, including on any positions LWV has taken on specific measures (kept separate from the basic information so the two don't get mixed up)

Bring your printed ballot measure blue book guides guides to take notes!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Hop on the bus to knock doors in Allentown (PA-07) to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Bob Brooks. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The next bus bus will leave from the Hudson Yards Area (600 W 34th St.) on Saturday, October 3 at 8:30 am and return around 7:30 pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:30 am to 5:30 pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

events.description:
Want to do your part to ensure the upcoming midterm elections are safe and fair? We know there is growing anxiety around our elections and a strong desire to understand what can be done to protect our democracy—to ensure that every eligible New Yorker can cast their ballot and have it counted.

Join us to become a trained volunteer for poll monitoring! With us, you will learn how to support your neighbors—and yourself—by understanding your voting rights, de-escalation techniques, and how to respond to issues at the polls.

NYS EP Coalition/ Hands Off Our Vote NY is a coordinated effort led by Common Cause New York and The Hudson Valley Huddle of the NYS Election Protection Coalition across the state.

We are far from powerless in protecting the lifeblood of our democracy—the right to vote. But it will take all of us doing everything we can: strengthening our laws, encouraging participation, and supporting voters at the polls. See you at the training!

This training is for new volunteers and experienced organizers alike. You’ll be able to take these materials and train your own community after participating.
