events.title: Census Rule Public Comment Office Hours
events.description:
Join Fair Count, ProGeorgia, Georgia Redistricting Alliance, and Common Cause GA to learn more about urgent proposed rule changes to the 2030 decennial census. In this virtual session you'll receive training and support to craft your own written statement in opposition to these changes during the public comment period. Comments are due by October 13, 2026 at 11:59 pm ET.

---

The 2030 Census is under attack—and your voice is the answer.

The Census Bureau has proposed a dramatic rules change that would exclude student visa holders, asylum seekers, and more from the 2030 apportionment count. The rule change also bans race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation questions from the short-form census.

The public has until October 13 to make comments for the U.S. Commerce Department's consideration. This is your opportunity to share your opposition to this rule change before it is implemented.

Can't make the training? Our friends at Common Cause have an [online portal](https://act.commoncause.org/letters/demand-an-accurate-2030-census/?source=partners) to easily submit your comment now.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Park City
events.description:
About this event:
The Pro-Active Alliance, in conjunction with other Wasatch Back pro-democracy organizations, is sponsoring No Kings: Vote Early on October 17th.

We'll gather at the pedestrian bridge over I-80 off Landmark Drive (near Whole Foods) at 10:00 am. We'll make signs, celebrate our right to vote, and we'll have a message on the bridge that encourages passers-by to vote early.

At 11:00 we'll march to the ballot drop box at the Sheldon Richins Building (Summit County Library — Kimball Junction Branch), 1885 W. Ute Blvd., to
cast our votes.

Ballots will be mailed to voters starting October 13. That means by October 17, many Summit County voters will have their ballots in hand — and the goal of this event is simple:
Bring your ballot. Drop your ballot. Vote that day.

Check your voter registration now at vote.utah.gov to make sure your information is correct and your registration is active!

Parking is available at the Kimball Junction Transit Center, the PEAK Center  and in nearby retail centers. Taking public transportation is encouraged!

This is not a rally where we tell people to vote "someday". This is a day where thousands of us literally cast our ballots together by marching them to the drop box as a public, visible, joyful act of collective participation. It's a celebration, an orientation, and an activation all at once!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.
Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. No Kings: Vote Early on October 17th is a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: ICE Out For Good Great Neck: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays
events.description:
Join The Beacon for Thursday Shine the Light, as we bring our voices to the street every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 PM.

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside. Don't have a sign? Don't worry! You can borrow one of ours.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity. We find joy in resistance through community, music, comedy and street theater.

Across the country, communities are organizing to disentangle local law enforcement from federal immigration enforcement. When local police or sheriffs collaborate with ICE, it undermines trust, separates families, and makes all of us less safe. Here in Nassau County, families continue to live in terror of separation, detainment, detention and deportation.

We stand weekly in opposition to this unprecedented assault on the rights, safety, and economic security of people in this country. For 30 minutes every Thursday, we say ICE OUT OF OUR COMMUNITIES!  ICE OUT FOR GOOD! and we stand in favor of compassionate democracy and against cruelty, fear and despair.

People that come together in solidarity and say NO to ICE are a critical bulwark against mass deportations and the erosion of civil rights. There is much that we can do locally. And there is much that our elected officials can do — if we demand courage and leadership. Join us!

There are Beacon groups all over the USA. Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 6:00-6:30 pm. We are joined by the Singing Resistance Great Neck to sing songs of solidarity and resistance, old and new.

For more information on The Beacon, visit www.beaconfordemocracy.org

A core principle behind all ICE Out For Good events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. All events should be held in public spaces or on public property.

Nonviolent at all times and lawful activities only
Community-led and locally grounded
Respectful of those grieving
Focused on accountability, not spectacle
Daytime events only

events.title: Fighting for Our Freedoms Countywide Canvass
events.description:
Join us in the fight for our freedoms! We've got 3 amendments on the ballot, and each launch will focus on one.

9 am: Voting Rights

Noon: Marriage Equality

3 pm: Reproductive Freedom

At 9 am, we'll be joined by Delegate David Reid, Delegate Marty Martinez, Delegate JJ Singh, BoS Chair Phyllis Randall, School Board Chair April Chandler, and Commonwealth's Attorney candidate Ryan Ruzic. At noon, the speakers will include Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Atoosa Reaser, Delegate John McAuliff, Leesburg Vice Mayor Todd Cimino-Johnson, and Candice Tuck. At 3 pm, our guests will be Congressman Suhas Subramanyam, Delegate Atoosa Reaser, Algonkian Supervisor Juli Briskman, School Board At-Large Member Anne Donohue, and Broad Run School Board Member Ross Svenson.

Even though each launch is focused on one of the amendments, we'll have materials available for all 3 as well as for Senator Warner, Congressman Subramanyam, and Vice Mayor Cimino-Johnson. We'll even have free t-shirts! (while supplies last)

This is the perfect opportunity to learn how to knock doors. We'll offer training at every launch and can even pair you up with an experienced canvasser. We will offer canvassing locations throughout the County, so you can choose to knock doors closer to home.

Let’s build the momentum to win big this November and ensure that Virginia votes YES on all 3!

events.title: Knock doors in Iowa: Drive Directly

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Drive directly** to Dubuque and knock some doors for Lindsay James and other Democrats in Iowa's 2nd congressional District!

We all know that farmers are the beating heart of America, and yet Iowans are disproportionately affected by Trump's Tariffs. The good news is that we finally have the chance to fight back against Trump's MAGA agenda. How? By driving on out to Dubuque to talk to Iowans! Let's make a difference! We'll be waiting for you!

If you arrive early or want to stay longer, no sweat! The office is wide open and would love to have you for as long as you're available to help!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will meet in Iowa at 123 Main St, Dubuque 52001 Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

We’re hitting the doors and talking directly with our neighbors about why we’re sending Scott Wiener to Congress!

events.title: Bridge North Texas Community Field Canvassing
events.description:
Join us every Saturday in October as we head out into DeSoto to knock doors, connect directly with voters, and build long-term power in our community!

Face-to-face conversations are the single most effective way to make sure our neighbors have a plan to vote. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or knocking doors for the very first time, we will make sure you have everything you need to feel comfortable, confident, and supported.

What to Expect:
Training & Briefing: We start every shift with a quick 20-minute training on our messaging and canvassing apps (Empower / Solidarity Tech).

Pairing Up: First-time canvassers will always be paired with an experienced buddy!

Knocking Doors: We’ll launch in pairs to talk to target voters across DeSoto.

Debrief: We’ll regroup at the end of the shift to celebrate wins, log our contacts, and turn in materials.

What to Bring / How to Prepare
1. A fully charged smartphone with the Empower and Solidarity Tech    apps downloaded.
2. Comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle.
3. A friend! (Canvassing is always more fun together.)

Meet up location details will be reshared to RSVP's closer to event dates.

events.title: No Kings: PROBLEMATIC
events.description:
Why Problematic? 


Well, the first elephant in the room- let's call him Pedro- Protests, stand outs, banner drops, and other visibility events are performative. They are. That doesn't mean they're not useful as a litmus test for who will show up when the shit really hits the fan, or as a networking and community building opportunity, but by and large we are preaching to the choir. There is an undeniable degree of back patting with folks who need to feel like they're doing something; the same sort of something that gives a person satisfaction from dutifully sorting the recycling so it can go to the landfill anyway.



Then there's the gate keeping. The platforming of the platformed. The policing of protesters (stay in this area, please, and don't interact with the racist Magas but don't stand there- no! keep off the grass and keep the aisles open). The chants that more and more feel like brainwashing. 



The theme of 'No Kings' this October is 'Early Voting' 



Next Elephant: let's call her Cheryl. 



The subtext of 'no kings' is if we can just get tRump out of power everything will be better. Identifying the would-be king as the whole problem ignores historic systemic realities. tRump is a SYMPTOM not the illness. The "illness" is that this entire country is built on exploitation and white supremacy. Full stop. So when we think in terms of just removing tRump from power, we are saying we just want all the pain and oppression to be hidden enough to ignore. Democrats are committing genocide along with is.real and every corrupt corporation they are beholden to. No Kings: get rid of the obvious harm so white people can be comfortable enough to cosign their own demise with the blood of the oppressed.



Third Elephant: Jamie



The official theme 'early voting' implies that the midterms are going to fix everything as if the regime that tested the waters on Jan 6 hasn't been blatantly gerrymandering and calling election results into question. We're all going to vote if we are safe to do so- but to expect that the results will just be honored is naïve (the fact that many will not feel safe to do so speaks volumes). There are many who, neglected by all US politicians regardless of "side", do not see the point in voting. They have screamed themselves hoarse and no one would listen. And there are many a comfortable stranger to tell them they should. The system that was DESIGNED to create the current situation can not be used to "fix" anything.

 

So we're all just gonna carry on believing that the midterm election is going to be fair and that the results will be gracefully accepted as the will of the people? PROBLEMATIC Don't then be all surprised when authoritarians act authoritarian.  

Oh we're gonna vote. Apparently the ways the current administration has undermined our "democracy" just isn't enough and we need more. We are going to choose our fighters- or choose the path of less harm as the case usually is- and then when they get sidelined maybe we'll all be shocked into collective action. Blood spilled to gain many of us the right to enter the ballot box and we honor the efforts of those who came before when we do. Our hope in doing so is not a free and fair election- it's a set up for this regime to do something else stupid and maybe, just maybe, the people will be mad enough to come together and stop being so polite about it. At the same time- those who don't feel safe to vote and those who understandably don't much see the point are valid in their perspectives- many things can be true at once.  

The history of the United States is littered with co-opted revolutions. 

The revolutionary war saw rich men get richer while soldiers like Daniel Shay faced crushing debts and foreclosure. When Shay took up arms against the government he helped to establish, the Massachusetts Riot Act was established which permitted sheriffs to kill rioters who did not disperse. 
After the Civil War, a presidential stalemate lead to backdoor deals- the Republican (then the party in the north with more liberal ideas) got the presidency in return for pulling federal troops out of the south (basically permission to establish jim crow). This is called the Compromise of 1877 and the recently emancipated Black Americans in the south were abruptly sold out by political elites to protect the status quo. 
During the Great Depression, revolutionary sentiment was strong and the threat of big bad socialism was popular- so we got the new deal. The new deal was great but it also was just enough to satisfy enough people to quell the revolutionary momentum and keep power structures in place. 

Right now we are at another impasse and our own history tells us that we need to be aware of people who seek to maintain the power structures. If we are being honest- No Kings does just that. 



So WTF are we doing hosting a No Kings Rally after all this criticism? 

Well first and most obviously, we are using the No Kings moniker as a vehicle for having these conversations and on the 17th we will be creating conditions for these conversations to continue if possible. 

We mentioned early on that these rallies are useful as a litmus test of sorts- how many people will show up in defense of their community. Right now New Bedford is under siege by Immigration Enforcement. ICE has been detaining people in Chicopee, Springfield, and West Springfield. The truth is not everyone who goes to a rally is actually willing to put themselves in danger or sacrifice their comfort but when we show up and see how many other people are willing to show up, we gain a little more courage. There is absolutely no chance of fighting anything without strong networks and communities and these rallies give people an opportunity to build solidarity across different lived experiences. A rally also functions as a resource fair with information on hotlines like LUCE, trainings, and local advocacy groups. The main reason we ever did standouts was to show people they aren't alone. 

We need to exercise our right to assemble. Exercise- as in practice it repeatedly to gain the muscle to assemble when it really matters. Call it calisthenics or the self normalization of showing up. 

Besides, who doesn't love a good performance?



Get comfortable being uncomfortable, we aim to be problematic 

....and maybe sing some songs. :)

events.description:
## BIJAN: Boston Immigration Justice and Accompaniment Network

How a grassroots volunteer led organization is responding to these fearful times and how you can help

IMC Immigration Justice Action Team Virtual Forum
Wed, October 14, 2026, 7 pm – 8:30 pm EST, via Zoom

Join us to learn about the extraordinary work that BIJAN volunteers are doing to support our immigrant neighbors across Massachusetts. BIJAN is a volunteer-driven network that provides transportation, accompaniment to immigration court and ICE check-ins, legal defense, bond sponsorship, and family outreach. 

During these difficult times, BIJAN is at the front lines, honoring people’s dignity and choices in a system that denies dignity and choice. To learn more about BIJAN, volunteer, or donate, go to https://www.beyondboston.org/. 

The IMC Immigration Justice Action Team (IJAT) holds our monthly Virtual Public Forum every 2nd Wednesday of the month, from 7 pm – 8:30 pm EST. Our monthly forums highlight organizations, campaigns, and practical actions that help build a more just and welcoming Massachusetts. 

## Guest Speakers: 

### Judy Wolberg

BIJAN Àccompaniment Team Coordinator; BIJAN Legal Fund Team Member, BIJAN Core Team Member


### Stella Ko

IMC IJAT Co-Lead for the Immigration Justice Action Team (IJAT), Indivisible Mass Coalition; Member, IMC Racial Justice Action Team; BIJAN Coordinator for the Chelmsford Immigration Court; Member, Indivisible Acton Area.

## Who We Are

Indivisible Mass Coalition (IMC) is a statewide organization of volunteers that provides resources, support, and services to the diverse Indivisible members and groups to strengthen constituent power in Massachusetts and improve democracy. Find more about what Indivisible Mass Coalition is doing by visiting indivisible-ma.org.

The IMC Immigration Justice Action Team serves as a statewide coordination and amplification hub within Indivisible Mass Coalition (IMC), supporting high-impact immigrant justice campaigns and actions that cross local group and coalition lines. We bring together Indivisible groups, immigration justice organizations, and the IMC Racial Justice Action Team to support and amplify efforts that protect our immigrant neighbors and communities.

Contact us at immigration-justice-action-team@indivisible-ma.org.

events.title: Meet the Candidates: Adams County
events.description:
Meet the Candidates: Adams County

Date: Saturday, October 10th, 2026
Location: West Union High School Auditorium
Time: 6:30-8:30pm
Doors open: 6pm


Appalachian Edge Ohio Indivisible, a non-profit organization who is fighting to protect our communities and everyone within them, is hosting a Meet the Candidates panel this October with the candidates of Adams County’s 2026 Midterms.

The panel is a non-partisan effort to ensure folks have the chance to meet and ask their candidates questions and to avoid bias as well as candidates to have a platform to speak to and meet their possible future constituents. This is the best time for Adams County Ohioans to come and ask a question or sit in and listen to what’s being discussed to develop a more informed decision on your votes this November. This election may be one of the most important local elections to show up and vote for who will truly represent us best. All candidates for the following races (listed below) in and for our county have been invited to participate in this Meet the Candidates panel.

At this event, candidates will be sat in chairs behind a table on a stage with a moderator to the side. If a candidate doesn’t show, their chair will be left empty. Audience members will sign up for a topic on entry of the building. They will also have the option to write a question down to be added to the discussion topic sheet the moderator will have. You will receive a marker, use this marker to show who you are when your name is called upon if you choose to ask out loud. Our moderator will be the one to keep us on track to ensure we get through everything wanted and needed to be discussed. Introductions and candidate statements will be at the beginning and the topic with the most interest will be discussed first leading us in and least will come later on. If we have time, we will have open discussions towards the end.

Topics may include but are not limited to:
Surveillance cameras, data centers, injection wells, education issues (policy, vouchers), security/Medicare/healthcare, war and genocide, property tax, tax abatements (NDA by elected officials), LGBTQ+ issues, election restrictions, small businesses, etc.

Candidates on the panel will prepare themselves with specific questions based on their areas of focus and will have a chance to answer them in front of the people.

U.S. House of Representatives, 2nd District:
Jen Mazzuckelli, Independent
David Taylor, Republican

Ohio House of Representatives, 90th District:
Colin Docterman, Independent
Justin Pizzulli, Republican

Adams County Commissioner:
Helen Cluxton Newman, Independent
Kelly Jones, Republican

Adams County Prosecutor:
David Osborne Jr., Independent 
Ariana Bowles Norris, Republican

Adams County Auditor:
Clayton Osborne, Independent
David Griffon, Republican

Adams County Judge:
Lisa Rothwell, Independent
Barbara Moore Holt, Republican

Livestream will be available. Attendees virtually will unfortunately not be able to choose a topic or ask a question.

The panel will be a structured process to ensure consistency, fairness and accuracy. This will help prevent biases and establish that all candidates are assessed against the same criteria and ensure that all candidates are evaluated on their abilities and qualifications as well as personhood.
Rules for attendees and candidates:
• No interruptions during questions and answers. Attendees will get one warning before being removed from the audience.
• If you have something to say or ask regarding the topic of discussion at the time, raise your hand and we could possibly get to you by the end.
• If you are called upon, please state your name and town or village you reside in and then begin your question.

Before and after the panel:
There will be a few tables set up outside of the auditorium before and after the panel. The tables listed below are here for you, please feel free to go up and see what will be there and what you may be interested in or want to ask questions about. Snacks and drinks will be available outside of the auditorium during the duration of the panel.

• New Medicaid Requirement Workshop table will be set up prior to the beginning of the panel and afterwards. During this time you can talk and learn about the changes, issues and concerns of Medicaid in Ohio.
• Local resources table
• There will be an area set up where you can check your sample ballot, polling location and other Ohio voting information. You’ll find educational materials about each political role and what they entail as well and more.
• Those who are putting this panel together will have information about a documentary they are wanting to do about our neighbors in Adams County and our struggle. 

We hope you are available to attend. Reach out to us at eoaohioindivisible@gmail.com if you have any questions. Candidates are to arrive no later than 15 minutes prior to the event.

All candidates for the following races (listed below) in and for our county have been invited to participate in this Meet the Candidates panel.

At this event, candidates will be sat in chairs behind a table on a stage with a moderator to the side. If a candidate doesn’t show, their chair will be left empty. Audience members will sign up for a topic on entry of the building. They will also have the option to write a question down to be added to the discussion topic sheet the moderator will have. You will receive a marker, use this marker to show who you are when your name is called upon if you choose to ask out loud. Our moderator will be the one to keep us on track to ensure we get through everything wanted and needed to be discussed. Introductions and candidate statements will be at the beginning and the topic with the most interest will be discussed first leading us in and least will come later on. If we have time, we will have open discussions towards the end.

Topics may include but are not limited to: Surveillance cameras, data centers, injection wells, education issues (policy, vouchers), security/Medicare/healthcare, war and genocide, property tax, tax abatements (NDA by elected officials), LGBTQ+ issues, election restrictions, small businesses, etc.

Candidates on the panel will prepare themselves with specific questions based on their areas of focus and will have a chance to answer them in front of the people.

U.S. House of Representatives, 2nd District:
Jen Mazzuckelli, Independent
David Taylor, Republican

Ohio House of Representatives, 90th District:
Colin Docterman, Independent
Justin Pizzulli, Republican

Adams County Commissioner:
Helen Cluxton Newman, Independent
Kelly Jones, Republican

Adams County Prosecutor:
David Osborne Jr., Independent 
Ariana Bowles Norris, Republican

Adams County Auditor:
Clayton Osborne, Independent
David Griffon, Republican

Adams County Judge: 
Lisa Rothwell, Independent 
Barbara Moore Holt, Republican

Livestream will be available. Attendees virtually will unfortunately not be able to choose a topic or ask a question.

The panel will be a structured process to ensure consistency, fairness and accuracy. This will help prevent biases and establish that all candidates are assessed against the same criteria and ensure that all candidates are evaluated on their abilities and qualifications as well as personhood. Rules for attendees and candidates: • No interruptions during questions and answers. Attendees will get one warning before being removed from the audience. • If you have something to say or ask regarding the topic of discussion at the time, raise your hand and we could possibly get to you by the end. • If you are called upon, please state your name and town or village you reside in and then begin your question.

Before and after the panel: There will be a few tables set up outside of the auditorium before and after the panel. The tables listed below are here for you, please feel free to go up and see what will be there and what you may be interested in or want to ask questions about. Snacks and drinks will be available outside of the auditorium during the duration of the panel.

• New Medicaid Requirement Workshop table will be set up prior to the beginning of the panel and afterwards. During this time you can talk and learn about the changes, issues and concerns of Medicaid in Ohio. 
• Local resources table 
• There will be an area set up where you can check your sample ballot, polling location and other Ohio voting information. You’ll find educational materials about each political role and what they entail as well and more. 
• Those who are putting this panel together will have information about a documentary they are wanting to do about our neighbors in Adams County and our struggle.

We hope you are available to attend. Reach out to us at eoaohioindivisible@gmail.com if you have any questions. Candidates are to arrive no later than 15 minutes prior to the event.

events.title: Voter Protection calls to Voters who need assistance
events.description:
Join VoPro Pros to help ensure that likely Democratic voters in states such as Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio are able to cast their ballots this fall and have their votes counted!  Please join us for important and impactful voter protection phone banks. 

In each shift, we will do phone banking to support the most critical and current voter protection priorities for the Democratic Party in one of these key states. Our calls may include recruiting volunteers to serve as poll observers, so that we can help solve voters’ issues at the polls in real time; helping voters who have registration issues to update their registration, who had issues with their ballots in previous elections know what to do so their vote counts this time.  Once mail ballots start being returned, we will help voters fix mistakes, known as curing, so their voted ballots count!  
We will meet on zoom and provide training, a script, and contact information for targeted voters.  For some projects we’ll call using the OpenVPB system, where you’ll call on your own phone or Google Voice (or a web based calling app); for some projects, we will use a dialer, so you’ll only talk to people who pick up the phone!   No experience or background knowledge required.

Come to our 2 hour phone banks and make a difference! We promise your calling will be the most critical of the moment.  We will try to update you here, if we know the project.  If you have questions, write to us at voterprotectionVPP@gmail.com

Upcoming phone bank topics, subject to change as needs change:

October 13 & 18 - OH pre-cure of mismatched data

October 14 - NV pre-cure 

October 15 & 17 - GA cure absentee ballot applications

events.title: Step Up for Democracy: New Haven GOTV Canvass
events.description:
Join the League of Women Voters of Connecticut and LWV New Haven for a nonpartisan door-to-door canvass to empower our community and ensure every eligible voter’s voice is heard!

With key elections approaching, we are knocking on doors across New Haven to make sure our neighbors are fully prepared to cast their ballots by November 3rd. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or taking to the doors for the first time, we will provide the training and materials you need to make an impact.

What We’ll Be Doing:

Voter Education: Sharing clear, trusted details on voting options, key dates, and election procedures in Connecticut.

Voter Empowerment: Helping community members make a concrete plan to participate on or before November 3rd.

Answering Questions: Helping voters check their voter status, locate their local polling information, and navigate general voter resources like VOTE411.org.

Schedule & Agenda:

1:00 PM: Welcome & Canvass Training: We will kick off with brief nonpartisan messaging training, review route assignments, pair experienced canvassers with new canvassers, and walk through our canvassing app.

1:30 PM | Door-to-Door Canvassing: Pairs will head out to assigned New Haven neighborhoods to engage local voters.

3:30 PM – 4:00 PM | Debrief & Material Return: Gather back at our starting hub to drop off materials and share stories.

How to Prepare:

What to Wear: Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing.

What to Bring: A fully charged smartphone, a water bottle, and a friend!

The League of Women Voters is a strictly nonpartisan organization that encourages informed and active participation in government. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties.

events.title: Get Trained at Power Back: A Movement School for Election Defense! (Gainesville)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
In America, most people believe that voters should pick our leaders, not the other way around. But right now, people in power are trying to keep us from voting so they can control our elections and seize more power for themselves.

But we won’t let them decide our future or define what democracy looks like for our communities. From August to October, GenVote and our allies are embarking on a first-of-its-kind national tour, *Power Back: A Movement School for Election Defense*.

Join us at the United Church of Gainesville for the ninth stop of the tour!

This tour stop is being organized in collaboration with local and statewide partners, including *Common Cause Florida, ACLU of Florida, All Voting Is Local, Florida Youth Action Fund, Fair Elections Center, Engage Florida, Florida Rising Together*, and more!

Together, we'll get trained on:

- Election Protection 101

- Know Your Rights

- Our Work Doesn't End on Election Day: Ballot Curing and Certification

- Creative Action Planning For Post-Election Scenarios

- Activating the Youth Vote

- Election Defense Lessons From Youth Movements Around the World

-  Reimagining a Just Democracy for All

**This tour stop is free and open to community members of all ages**, with a special focus on students and young people. **Light refreshments and lunch will be provided.**

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Get out the early vote! Let's Line Lake Street! Join us on the sidewalk to peacefully and joyfully encourage our neighbors to get out and vote.
Bring a “Vote Early, In Person” themed sign and join your fellow pro-democracy friends and neighbors. Your neighbors near East Lake Street will be out in force.  Let’s encourage early voting on Lake Street from Lake Street-Marshall Bridge to Bde Maka Ska. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Roll to the Polls to Vote Early
events.description:
# ROLL TO THE POLLS

**Deck out your ride. Roll out the vote.**

Streamers on the handlebars. Balloons on the golf cart. Pom-poms on the pickup. Bring your car, bike, trike, skateboard, wagon, or your own two feet, and dress it up to celebrate **early voting**. We'll gather at Long Wharf and parade together, horns honking and bells ringing, to the Dorchester County Board of Elections to cast our ballots on the very first day of early voting.

We're also bringing fresh donuts and coffee for the election workers who make it all happen. Want to add something sweeter? Bring a handwritten thank-you note, and we'll deliver it with the donuts.

**Thursday, October 22 · 8 AM**

Line up at Long Wharf, Cambridge

**Best Decorated wins bragging rights, and a prize.**

*Decorations should celebrate early voting, not candidates.*

**Voting at the end of the parade?** You'll need to be a Dorchester County resident.

First, [check your voter registration](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch).

Not registered? [Register online](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/OnlineVoterRegistration) by October 13.

Nonpartisan. Joyful. Everyone welcome.

events.title: Indivisible Santa Maria October Member Meeting: Brunch and Ballot!
events.description:
Brunch and Ballot Indivisible Santa Maria

Save this important date and time, Saturday, October 10 1:00- 3:00 pm. Gloria Dei, 4380 Orcutt Road, where we get to the heart of election issues and the importance that we all **VOTE EARLY**.  

Brunch will be provided as we lead our discussion with you as active participants!

- Discuss the candidates and ballot measures with local input from Joyce Howerton, community advocate and Former Mayor of Lompoc.  

- Consider election protection and how our local actions can deliver big results for our communities and for democracy this election year.  

- Learn how to ensure that your ballot is tracked as well as where to find your drop box locations. 

- If you haven’t already cast your ballot, bring your actual ballot or sample ballot as we share our Indivisible endorsements.

- A raffle will also add some pre-election day fun!


See you all on October 10th!

_Please bring donations for our immigrant community.  We are asking for donations of canned foods, peanut butter, cooking oil, dried beans, other cultural staples, hygiene products, diapers, paper towels, and toilet paper._

events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together.

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Data Center, Utility Bills, and YOU!
events.description:
Across Kentucky, more communities are being approached about hosting large data centers. We want you to know what exactly these data centers are and what they could they mean for your community.

Join Kentuckians for the Commonwealth (KFTC) for a FREE Community Data Center Workshop to learn the facts, ask questions, and explore how we can participate in upcoming decisions that shape our entire community.

During this workshop, we'll discuss:

events.description:
Join Swing Left Inland Valley, Swing Left Orange County, and other Swing Left groups for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

This a local Indivisible event!


Join Indivisible Fox Valley for Movie Night!!  As we head into the midterm election, we will hosting a screening of Democracy Under Siege. This 2025 documentary directed by Laura Nix, uses the sharp, witty political cartoons of Pulitzer Prize–winning editorial cartoonist Ann Telnaes to examine the deep structural challenges facing American democracy. Through commentary from leading political analysts, the film traces how constitutional roadblocks, executive overreach, judicial ethics crises, and widespread disinformation have shaped today’s political landscape. You're invited to the Civics Cypher, where hip-hop meets civic engagement. Road to Black November and Flourish are bringing local artists together to speak on community, power, and why your voice matters, all in a live cypher recording.

After the artists lay it down, it's your turn. Join us for the audience recording session, connect with the artists, share your perspective, and be part of the movement leading into Black November. Light refreshments will be served.

Influencers and content creators: come early! Pull up during artist setup to go live outside the cypher, capture behind-the-scenes content, and grab photos with the artists before the recording starts. Help us spread the word and show your followers what's happening in Bessemer.

Date: Sunday, October 11
Location: 1815 3rd North, Bessemer, AL 35020

Schedule:
2:00 PM: Artist setup (influencers and creators welcome)
3:00 PM – 4:00 PM: Live recording
4:00 PM – 5:00 PM: Audience recording session (audience please arrive by 3:40 PM)

Be there. Bring your people. Be part of it.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Independence, Missouri
events.description:
We are rallying 10/17/26; non-violently, safely & joyfully, civilly helping our entire community to vote early in an undeniably massive amount too big to rig; 
Do NOT wait until November to vote so we prevent all obstruction and interference, as election defense, in 2026.
This is a fun, safe, non-violent, non-partisan event, because we are all human. This rally is to motivate, to inform, to help our community vote early. We will check voter registration, make a plan to commit, create a group needing help, to vote early on or shortly after October 20, 2026. Let's Party.
+++Last day for US Citizens to register to vote for November 3, 2026 election in Missouri is October 7, 2026.+++ If you need to register, please email me as soon as possible. 
+++Volunteers are needed. Democracy is built and saved by people, neighbors, communities generation after generation, because defending it and deciding it is worthy of participation. 
+++We need volunteers, location(s) costumes, music, food, games and safety team. Indivisible and 50501 have links for safety teams and ideas too.
+++We must also create a rapid response team for November 4, 2026, through January 2027. Indivisible and 50501 have links.
Make your signs, tell your friends and neighbors and join us for No Kings: Vote Early Independence, MO, rally October 17, 2026. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Please join us for our weekly Happy Hour protest in Norwalk against everything this administration stands for!  Feel free to bring your own signs, banners or flags, we also always have extra that you're welcome to take with you.  We'll wave and enjoy all of the honks in solidarity from the passing traffic!  We're known to have Treats & Tunes so it's always a good time!!

We will keep this up until this regime changes their ways!!!!

Feel free to drop in when you can and leave when you need to :)

Please watch weekly reminders for any time adjustments, especially with the upcoming daylight savings, or weather updates!

Logistical information: - Always stay on the sidewalks and only cross roads at designated crossing points. - Parking available on Connecticut Ave at various locations nearby, as well as on Cedar St on the other side of the bridge.  

IMPORTANT: We continue to have have an overwhelming positive response from drivers by but in the rare occurrence there is an anti-protester, do NOT engage with any agitator.  We ask all involved with our group to remain calm, non-violent and peaceful.  There are always experienced protesters in attendance if anyone needs assistance de-escalating any situation.

events.title: Homicide Awareness: A Right to Heal – Access to Victims Compensation
events.description:
Join Miami Gardens ROSE Inc., Crime Survivors Speak, and Guns Down Voices Up Demanding Justice Inc. as we come together to honor the lives of those affected by homicide and support individuals, families, and communities healing from the pain of loss.

This community event will focus on remembrance, healing, awareness, advocacy, and access to resources. Attendees will also learn about Florida Victim Compensation, including what assistance may be available, who may qualify, and how to begin the application process.

Too often, surviving families learn about these resources only after they have already faced overwhelming emotional and financial burdens. Our goal is to help families become informed, supported, and connected.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Cedar Crest
events.description:
Please join East Mountains Resistance as we team up with No Kings to ring in the early voting season and celebrate our voting rights at this non-partisan No Kings Vote Early party in Cedar Crest. We will have information on how to be an agent of truth in your community, and how you can help secure our elections this fall. 

Come grab a voter guide. Come in costume and bring the kids for treats and coloring. Come make a sign to encourage others to:  Vote!  Vote early!  Vote now!  Vote loud!  Check those boxes!  Are you registered? Do you have a plan? Backup plan? vote411.org!

Join the party and help get the vote out with a procession to the polls afterwards.

*Out of respect for No Kings and the large tent we are building, please leave the ‘vote blue’  and political party related signs at home- we're on the people's side*

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in College Hill, Ohio!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Canvass to help strong Dem contender flip key district: NJ-07

address_lines: Meet up at NJ Transit gate area across and downstairs from ticket windows

events.description:
As Democrats work to flip the House, please join our Ground Truth canvass to knock on doors in crucial, swingable, Congressional District NJ-07. 

Ground Truth is a canvassing project that Swing Left developed after rigorously researching how canvassing models used in prior campaigns could be strengthened. The resulting "deep canvassing" approach equips us to find voters open to supporting Dems. We ask open-ended questions, listen closely, and learn about the real-world problems voters want their reps to solve. 

We've been doing this since last fall, with results that are directly informing Dem campaigns. And our canvassers are finding these excursions fascinating and rewarding! 

Now we're in "persuasion mode," speaking just with folks who haven't yet decided whether to vote, or how to vote. Listening to them closely remains key to our exchanges. 

In NJ-07, the House seat is up for grabs. Dem candidate Rebecca Bennett is a former Navy helicopter pilot with an MBA from U Penn's Wharton School of Business and business experience in the healthcare field. She's working to unseat Republican loyalist Tom Kean, Jr. 

Rebecca's platform -- broad and deep -- includes affordability issues, expanding access to healthcare, and tackling corruption in Washington, DC. Her bio and her website are truly inspiring:

https://rebeccabennettforcongress.com/priorities/growing-new-jerseys-economy/

The Ground Truth model was made for campaigns like this! Whether you're experienced in deep canvassing, or aren't but are ready to learn, you can help us connect directly with voters and identify who Rebecca's campaign should follow up with.

Logistics: NYC volunteers will meet at 9:45 at Penn Station and take a train to Rahway. Training will be reviewed en route. In a coffee shop, we'll sort out turfs. Then, canvass for c. 3 hours. (If you need to leave earlier, trains to Manhattan run often.) 

After you sign up, (PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR CELL #)more info about our canvass will reach you. You'll be warmly welcomed by our team!

We gather on the bridge. Look for the signs. Can't miss us!

**🪧 MESSAGING & FOCUS**

One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)
This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

The primary goal of this event is to encourage voter participation, but participants are welcome to bring any sign they wish. We will provide and display the main voting-related signs facing both directions of traffic. 

Bringing your own sign? Two large bars span the bridge. To make sure your sign isn't blocked, make it horizontal and no more than about 24" tall.

Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are commonly shared on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

**🅿️ RECOMMENDED PARKING**

Street parking is available along East Moreland Street throughout the surrounding neighborhood. There's also a parking lot at 10th St & Culver on the north side, but it may not be as "public" as we'd like. Stay vigilant!

**🚌 PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION**

Route 12

**📣 SPECIAL NOTES**

Because the event takes place on a pedestrian bridge over an active freeway, safety is our highest priority. Clear safety guidelines will be provided to ensure everyone's well-being on the bridge and prevent items from falling onto the roadway below. Safety notices will be posted at both bridge entrances, and all participants will receive safety information in advance of the event. 

Five weeks can make a difference! 

🥵 During hot weather, shade is limited. Bring water, sun protection, and consider a portable chair.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

events.title: Democracy Noir, Film Screening & Conversation
events.description:
Indivisible Fremont CA Presents Free Screening of Democracy Noir: A New Dawn Film and community conversation kick off the "Our Empowered Community Empowers Our Democracy" film and conversation series

Democracy Noir is a documentary telling the inspiring story of resistance in Hungary to Viktor Orbán's regime, and of his stunning defeat in a democratic election.

The film will be shown in the Niles Discovery Church's Sanctuary Theater. Afterward, guests are invited to the Fellowship Hall for refreshments and a community conversation about the film and what it means for protecting democracy at home.

"Protecting and securing our elections starts in the heart of every voter," said Lauren Teixeira, Co-Lead, Indivisible Fremont CA. “We are screening Democracy Noir on October 10th, just 24 days until the Mid-Term election on Tuesday, November 3.”

Our Empowered Community project will utilize documentary films to spark shared understanding and inspire dialogue as civic education—educating viewers while building connected, engaged communities. Focused post-screening conversations deepen this impact further, turning passive viewing into active reflection—transforming individual awareness into collective commitment and sustained democratic participation. 

IFCA is dedicated to promoting a welcoming and inclusive community, advocating for democracy and justice, empowering individuals to create positive change. To join our mailing list:  please visit, indivisible-fremont.org/join

events.title: October Community Meeting
events.description:
OCTOBER COMMUNITY MEETING

REGISTER TO JOIN US — IN PERSON OR ON ZOOM

November is coming fast. October is the final stretch.  

    October  5th Final day to register  
    October 14th 1st Day of Early Voting

We’ll be finalizing our NO KINGS: EARLY VOTE Action and organizing to turn October 17 into a powerful day of early voting, visibility and community action.  Find out how you can help. 

Why the focus on EARLY VOTING?

Because voting early gives us an advantage. We bank our votes early and free ourselves up to help others—giving rides, serving as poll observers, helping friends and neighbors vote, and making Election Day a day of service to our community.

And once people vote, campaigns can focus precious time, volunteers and resources on the people who still need to cast their ballots.

 HANDS OFF OUR VOTES -   We are continuing our discussion on how we prepare for the Midterms. We will discuss the practical ways we can organize, respond, and protect our elections.

👉🏽 What will we be watching between now and November?
👉🏽 What are red lines that could threaten a fair election?
👉🏽 How do we respond to voter intimidation and disinformation?
👉🏽 What can ordinary Tennesseans do **right now** to make sure every eligible voter can safely vote?

Knowledge and preparation turns into action.

Come find out where you fit in—and be ready for October 17, Early Voting and Election Day.

events.description:
HELP US RAISE AWARENESS!

Our group holds signs at places throughout Salem, where someone was abducted by ICE.

• Please register to RSVP and get address.

• Every Friday, rain or shine.

• Signs are handed out and locations are assigned at a meeting spot to be disclosed.

• Teams of two then set out for one hour of sign holding.

• Bring a friend or we’ll assign you a partner.

• After the hour is up, meet back at the original meeting spot to turn in signs and check in.

Our purpose is not only to raise awareness of our neighbors being taken from us, but to hold sacred space and honor those who have been abducted and for their families who are dealing with the trauma of their loss.

• We hold these signs for each and every person languishing in detention centers across the US.

• We hold these signs in defiance of the fascism and the hate.

• We hold these signs to use our white privilege, for those of us who have it, and be the best allies we can be.

More about why we do this:

ICE activity in Salem has resulted in many of our neighbors being abducted over the past 18 months. The exact number is difficult to obtain, as ICE does not share information, but the local Rapid Response Team and PIRC (Portland Immigration Rights Coalition) data supports the number as being over 100 since Trump took office.

• Across the state, ICE has abducted over 2,500 individuals, 700 in August of this year. • Across the nation, ICE is ramping up numbers; also in August, 51,000 people were taken. • Most of which have no criminal record.

• Abductees are being warehoused in over 200 privately owned detention centers in the US, where they are held for months, or years, in deplorable conditions.

• There are documented cases of rape, abuse, malnutrition, bad water and food, restricted access to medical care and lawyers.

• GEO Group and Core Civic; the corporations who own most of the detention centers, earn $150 - $175 per person per day.

• Both corporations earned over 2 billion dollars in total revenue in 2025, with net profits exceeding $200 million.

• Half of the total revenue comes from ICE contracts.

Want to help us raise awareness?

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Milwaukee
events.description:
He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

Date: Wednesday, October 14th
Time: 10:00am
Location: Milwaukee City Hall, 200 E. Wells St., Milwaukee, WI 53202

Harry Dunn is joining citizens of Milwaukee for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.

Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.

This event kicks off our No Kings: Vote Early weekend — three days of action in to protect this election and get Wisconsin voting early, building to the national Day of Election Action on October 17th.

This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.

Come ready to:

Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection
Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard
Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it
RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

events.description:
Tom Tiffany is coming to Milwaukee for his televised debate for Governor — and we will be showing up before he walks through those doors.

We want Wisconsin voters asking questions about healthcare costs, Medicaid, reproductive freedom, immigration, public education, the cost of living, data centers, taxes, and whose interests our next governor will serve.

SHOW UP. STAND UP. SPEAK UP.

We have the power to make better possible — but only when we use it.

Join Working Families Power and community organizations  from 6–7 PM, immediately before the debate begins.

Let’s give the cameras something to see — and Wisconsin something to hear.

PEOPLE OVER BILLIONAIRES. HEALTHCARE IS A HUMAN RIGHT. WISCONSIN BELONGS TO ALL OF US.

This will be a peaceful, nonviolent protest.

events.description:
Sunday, October 25, 2026

Hosted by ARC: “Voices of the Vote: An Open Mic on Voting Rights--via Poetry & Storytelling”

What is your voting story? With the 2026 Midterm Elections just days away, our collective voice has never been more vital. Behind every policy debate is a deeply human experience—and we are bringing those experiences to a shared national stage.

Join us on Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 12:00 PM to 1:30 PM CT for a captivating, virtual open mic.

We are building a truly cross-country virtual community. Whether you are dialing in from the East Coast, the West Coast, the South, or the Midwest, your regional perspective matters.

We are stripping away the digital noise. There will be no slides, no background music, and the text chat will be completely disabled. 

This is a space dedicated entirely to the raw power of the human voice—featuring an opening performance followed by an open floor for community members across the United States to share stories, spoken word, and poetry on the right to vote.

How it works:
The Open Floor:  The mic is open to anyone in our nationwide room. 
Bring a 3-minute story, personal reflection, spoken word piece, or poem about the right to vote.

Claim Your Slot Live: Once the floor opens, simply raise your hand on camera, and our host will bring you to the virtual stage.

Pure Visual Energy: Because the text chat is off, we ask all attendees to keep their cameras on and fill the screen with physical support—using visual snaps and jazz hands to celebrate each storyteller.

Taking Action Together: At the close of our event, our host will deliver a direct verbal call to action outlining how we can continue our collective energy by phone banking, text banking, and mobilizing our local communities back home—make a plan and vote!

Come to listen, stay to be inspired, and leave ready to continue GOTV actions. 

RSVP now to secure your spot. The secure Zoom access link will be delivered automatically upon registration.


Log-in Time: We will open the Zoom room exactly at 12:00 PM CT.

events.title: Cafecito con Nancy: Meet & Greet con Vecinos

sponsor.name: Nancy Martiz for Huntington Park City Council (CA Working Families Party)

events.description:
Join your neighbors for a Saturday morning with Nancy Martiz, your appointed City Councilmember and candidate for Huntington Park City Council, District 2.

Since joining the Council in April 2025, Nancy has stood up against unconstitutional ICE raids, passed fair housing protections that keep families in their homes, invested in our aging infrastructure, and expanded access to public spaces. Before joining the Council, she served as a Civil Service Commissioner, and she has been an engaged member of the community since moving to HP in 2012.

Like many of her neighbors, Nancy works a 9-to-5. Her career in HR and employee benefits has spanned the arts, higher education, health care, and global entertainment. Endorsed by the California Working Families Party, she believes local representatives should answer to working families, not special interests.

Come ask questions, share what matters to your neighborhood, and hear Nancy's plans for the next term. No speeches, just conversation. Light refreshments will be served, and everyone is welcome.

📅 Saturdays, October 3 & 24 · 🕗 8:00–10:00 a.m.
📍 Cruzita's Café & Deli
RSVP on Mobilize

Nancy does not accept corporate PAC money. This campaign is powered by neighbors. Learn how you can support her campaign for the working families of Huntington Park at nancy4hp.com.

Not sure which district you're in? Visit maphp.org

[Paid for by Nancy Cindy Martiz for Huntington Park City Council 2026. FPPC ID# 1495160]

 ESPANOL

Acompaña a tus vecinos un sábado por la mañana con Nancy Martiz, tu concejal designada y candidata al Concejo Municipal de Huntington Park, Distrito 2.

Desde que se unió al Concejo en abril 2025, Nancy se ha opuesto a las redadas inconstitucionales de ICE, ha aprobado protecciones de vivienda justa que permiten a las familias permanecer en sus hogares, ha invertido en nuestra infraestructura envejecida y ha ampliado el acceso a los espacios públicos. Antes de unirse al Concejo, fue Comisionada de Servicio Civil, y ha sido un miembro activo de la comunidad desde que llegó a HP en 2012.

Como muchos de sus vecinos, Nancy trabaja de 9 a 5. Su carrera en recursos humanos y beneficios para empleados ha abarcado las artes, la educación superior, la salud y el entretenimiento global. Con el respaldo del Partido de las Familias Trabajadoras de California (Working Families Party), Nancy cree que los representantes locales deben responder a las familias trabajadoras, no a intereses especiales.

Ven a hacer preguntas, compartir lo que le importa a tu vecindario y conocer los planes de Nancy para el próximo período. Sin discursos, solo conversación. Habrá refrigerios ligeros y todos son bienvenidos.

📅 Sábados 3 y 24 de octubre · 🕗 8:00–10:00 a.m.
📍 Cruzita's Café & Deli
Confirma tu asistencia en Mobilize

Nancy no acepta dinero de PACs corporativos. Esta campaña es impulsada por los vecinos. Descubre cómo puedes apoyar su campaña por las familias trabajadoras de Huntington Park en nancy4hp.com.

¿No sabes en qué distrito vives? Visita maphp.org

**Join us to celebrate early voting and election defense!** 

Stockpiling the early vote is a powerful form of election protection. On NO KINGS Day, Oct 17, we’ll spread the message that everyone needs to vote early, everyone needs to tell their *friends* to vote early, and we *all* need to get ready to defend the election. 

We will be in a residential cul de sac, joyfully doing a variety of activities to make a difference in this election. Activities will include filling out our ballots (bring yours!), using erasable chalk markers to decorate your car (if you want!) with pro-voting messages, providing information about how to participate in making sure all votes are counted, and more. 

We'll also wave signs at a nearby intersection to show our voting pride, and we'll hand out flyers so that everybody understands the power they have to make a difference.

events.title: Wind Changers Women's Gathering
events.description:
Wind Changers Women’s Gathering 2026:  2 night camp out. 

The “Wind Changers” represents a shift—a movement toward healing, restoration, connection, and renewed purpose. The Wind Changers Women’s Gathering is an intentional and sacred space created to bring women together for collective prayer, healing, meaningful connection, and empowerment.

In a world that can often feel isolating and overwhelming, this gathering provides a sanctuary where women from all walks of life can come together to build one another up, lift each other’s spirits, support one another, find motivation, and inspire each other.

The gathering is intentionally structured to help women move from isolation to community, creating an environment where women feel seen, heard, supported, and valued. Through shared experiences and meaningful connection, women are reminded that they do not have to walk through life alone.

The Gathering Will Provide:
Collective Prayer & Reflection: Creating a grounded and spiritually supportive environment where women can pause, reflect, reconnect, and renew their spirits.

Talking Circles: Providing safe and welcoming spaces for women to share their stories, express their experiences, release burdens, and receive mutual support without judgment.
Empowerment & Motivation: Creating impactful moments that inspire women to recognize their strength, build one another up, pursue their purpose with confidence, and encourage one another beyond the gathering.

Community Connection: Creating opportunities for fellowship, relationship-building, and meaningful connection so that no woman leaves feeling alone. The goal is for every participant to leave knowing she has a community around her.

We believe that when women have safe spaces to heal, connect, and grow, the impact extends far beyond the gathering itself. Women return to their families, communities, and neighborhoods renewed, strengthened, and empowered to become pillars of strength, hope, and positive change. 

At its heart, Wind Changers is about creating a shift within women that creates a ripple of change throughout families and communities. When women are supported, restored, connected, and empowered, they are better equipped to carry that strength, hope, healing, and purpose into the communities they call home.

Together, we can create a space where women feel seen, heard, supported, valued, and empowered—and where healing and connection become the beginning of lasting change.

events.title: Signs of Fascism Protest
events.description:
Good Trouble/Indivisible Norwalk and Greenwich Indivisible invite you to join us for a Signs of Fascism event on Saturday, October 10th from 11:15 AM to 12:30 PM.

Unlike our usual boisterous protests, this is some serious street theater, we're dressed in black, silently witnessing the hold fascism has taken on our country.

We've had a lot of positive response from the community, frequently calling it "very powerful". See what it's like in this video of our last event: https://tinyurl.com/4cww8ruj

We have the signs, date and location — all we need are 30 people willing to hold a sign for one hour to make this happen!

We'll meet and organize in the parking lot on the corner of North Avenue and Knight Street at 11:15 AM.

You'll choose your sign and we deploy to the street at 11:30.

We will be presenting our signs along North Avenue (Route 1) from High Street to Park Street. This Is a slow moving stretch of RT1 giving folks time to read the signs of fascism.

**Please dress in solid black** if possible — it looks powerful in formation.
No worries if you don't have all black, what matters is that you show up!
Please be a firm commitment when you sign up, since we'll stop recruiting if we get enough people in time.
There's nothing wrong with a sign being held by two people if we get a crowd, so bring a friend (the more the more powerful).
Let’s make this happen. Let’s make one hour count!

Rain date: the following day, Sunday the 11th, same time and place.

Please watch your email for any schedule or weather updates!

IMPORTANT: We continue to have an overwhelming positive response from drivers but in the rare occurrence there is an anti-protester, DO NOT engage with any agitator.

We ask all involved with our group to remain calm, non-violent and peaceful. There are always experienced protesters in attendance if anyone needs assistance de-escalating any situation.

Stay safely on sidewalks, making room for passers-by. Only cross roads at designated crossing points.

events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box. We partner with local organizations at every stop.

We will be part of the weekly Vigil for Immigrant Justice and the Call to End Section 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, which authorizes U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to delegate federal immigration enforcement authority to state and local law enforcement agencies. This is a time to reflect on what it means to stand witness and hold vigil as an act of participatory democracy. Calling for systemic change and an end to immigrant detention without due process, this vigil has taken place 50 weeks in a row, organized by faith leaders and people of conscience, standing in solidarity with other vigils across the state and nation.

This vigil is held in partnership with Interfaith Alliance of Florida, Voter Action Pinellas, the League of Women Voters of St. Petersburg, and the League of Women Voters of North Pinellas.

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.
