events.title: Sexual and Domestic Violence Awareness Workshop
events.description:
Sexual Violence and Domestic Violence Workshops are designed to help you build resilience, develop skills to keep you and your loved ones safe, and create bonds with those who have been through the same experiences as well as educating and informing the public for prevention. Survivors deserve active, accessible and affordable advocacy, support and the right to heal on their own terms.

This group is ran by peers and volunteers with a few experts coming to speak to us at certain times also. We started this group because we know we have a serious lack of education surrounding this and even sex education itself and in rural areas, we lack these resources and education even more. In a world where there is so much violence put on our children and ourselves as women, we must find and create spaces where we feel safe, comfortable, heard and overall have the support we all need.

Every last Tuesday of the month 5-6pm. The majority of our workshops will be at the Peebles Library in their meeting room. Depending on weather, we may have locations outdoors, at a park or hiking location for the woods or even the private 3rd space we created where our community aid garden is. Our lead, Taryn, will be there to greet you and get us started at each of these groups and workshops.
We are allies and accomplices here.

5-6pm Sexual and Domestic Violence Educational Workshops
6-7pm Women's Support Group

There are no age restrictions only to make this accessible. We don't want to make younger children or your children who may need this group to feel like they can't be apart of it just because of their age. If they have experienced hardship or need a safe space just like we do, we will not be turning them away. We do understand that this could potentially keep conversations from being too deep but if enough girls or younger women would like to attend, we can start a support group for our youth.

Our sexual and domestic violence workshops are to bring awareness to ourselves and our youth to help prevent further violence against children and women. Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around sexual violence and assault.

What to Expect:
Bonding, Venting and Relating
Mutual Support
Trauma-Informing to Foster Healing
Education on Women’s Health
Sexual Violence Awareness + Education Workshops
Skill Building
Sharing Resources
Safety and Confidentiality

Specific Workshop Examples:
What is Sexual Violence, What is and Can be Considered Sexual Violence, Consent 101, What is Grooming, What are Warning Signs, Women’s Health and Anatomy, Self-Defense and more. In hopes we keep our children and community safe.

There are no age restrictions. Everyone is welcome. We all need to learn these things to help with prevention. We want these workshops and the support group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more. We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. As soon as we find a better term to use for only women and non-binary folks, the name of this support group will change. We apologize to anyone who may feel left out or uncomfortable to the term Women's Support Group.

Coffee and snacks will be available. Possibly pizza or other foods for dinner. If you have allergies, please inform us. We hope to see you at one or the other or even both. It matters to our health to have support and we must create spaces that lead to prevention of violence against us.

Both of these groups will be for survivors as well as the general public, those who want to learn more to help with prevention and education around Sexual Violence and Assault. For more information on these workshops, you can find that on the event pages of the Sexual Violence Awareness Workshops and on our community aid page too.

We want this group to be as accessible as we possibly can, that includes rides and childcare. If you have children, you can bring them to the first group or workshop you attend if you need to. A kid’s club will begin once we find more volunteers to help us make this successful as well and we will have them during these times. Once we find enough volunteers and go through background checks, we will talk more about this at the our group meetings or workshops and spread the word more. We’re working towards bringing our villages back. We can't have a village without villagers.

Coffee and snacks will be available too. We hope you join us. We all need someone or something. We’re here for you. No shame, no judgement, no exceptions.❤️‍🩹

We want to add to ensure it's known, when we say women, we are always including trans women as well as non-binary folks who may also need a support system. As soon as we find a better term to use for only women and non-binary folks, the name of this support group will change. We apologize to anyone who may feel left out or uncomfortable to the term Women's Support Group.

Clayton’s Data Crew is the behind-the-scenes team turning petition signatures into clean, organized data that can be uploaded into our campaign databases. It may not involve knocking on doors or shaking hands, but this work is a critical part of building an organized and successful campaign.
Each week, we’ll enter petition signatures from paper sheets into spreadsheets, review and clean up data, collaborate, troubleshoot, and occasionally cut up and entertain ourselves through the madness of campaign season, together.
You don't have to be a data professional, but you do need to be:
•	Comfortable working on a computer
•	Detail-oriented and accurate
•	Familiar with spreadsheets or willing to learn
•	Able to follow data-entry guidelines
•	Reliable and ready to pitch in
•	VAN access and experience is a big plus!
We're looking to grow an already strong and capable team with volunteers who enjoy the kind of work where details matter and getting it right matters even more.
We'll meet every Monday and Wednesday on Zoom through Election Day, November 3, 2026.
Bring your laptop, your questions, your spreadsheet skills, and your willingness to get a little nerdy with us.
No cowboy boots required.
Come help us turn stacks of paper into organized data—and organized people into a powerful grassroots operation.
Join Clayton’s Data Crew. Let's get to work!

Join the No Kings movement to protect our elections against sabotage and turn out the largest early vote in US history! 

Easthampton has a high rate of registered voters, but recent elections have seen low turnout. Let's turn out like we did in the last Presidential Election in 2024. It's Up to Us. 

Easthampton Election & Voting Information: https://easthamptonma.gov/164/Elections-Voting

Bring a friend or two. Bring signs if you have them: Vote Early. Vote Early: October 17. No Kings! No Throwns! No Crowns! This is What Democracy Looks Like. No Kings, Just Voters. Our Elections are Under Attack: Vote Early!

We will have a supply of signs.

Voting early means your voice is locked in and safe, days before anyone else can decide what happens next, and it gives you room to fix anything that goes wrong, a signature mismatch, a missing form, waiting in a line that's too long, or not being able to make it if your shift runs late. 

No matter what the laws look like where you live, early preparation is universal. Cast your ballot at an early voting site (where available), request and return an absentee ballot, double check your registration, or make it a whole day! However you do it, our goal is to make a clear voting plan, and voting early.

events.title: Wenonah's Book of the Year: Author Talk with Zephyr Teachout [Livable Future LIVE]
events.description:
**Join us for a virtual conversation between Food & Water Watch Founder & Executive Director Wenonah Hauter and Zephyr Teachout, author of _Anti-Monopoly: A Citizen’s Guide_.**

_Anti-Monopoly_ is being called a “movement-defining” book that dives deep into the battle between the forces of oligarchy and the rise of the anti-monopoly movement. Zephyr explains how anti-monopoly sentiment cuts across traditional political lines, gives real teeth to economic populism, and offers actionable ways to use people power to solve this problem together. 

Zephyr Teachout is an award-winning author, constitutional law professor, and nationally renowned democracy and anti-corruption activist. _The New York Times_ called her “the godmother of the current moment of dissatisfaction with establishment politics,” and she has inspired anti-monopoly legislation in states across the country. Her additional writings include the books _Corruption in America_ and _Break ’Em Up_ and articles featured in _The New York Times_, _The New York Review of Books_, _Foreign Affairs_, and _The Nation_. Zephyr serves as Board Chair for Food & Water Action and sits on the board of Food & Water Watch, helping guide strategies on clean water, safe food, and climate advocacy.

- **You’ll get trained.** Staff and experienced volunteer leaders will walk you through everything you need to know before you start making calls—no prior experience required. 

- **We’ll make calls together.** You’ll be part of a supportive, welcoming group where we can encourage each other and build community along the way. 

- **We’ll provide the scripts.** You’ll have everything you need to feel prepared and confident when talking with voters. We’ll provide scripts and talking points. 

- **No personal phone number required.** All you need is a computer or tablet with an internet connection to make calls. 

- **Your privacy matters.** Our dialer is designed to help protect your personal information when reaching out to voters. 

- **We’ll make a difference together.** Every conversation is an opportunity to connect with voters and share important information!

events.title: Event Confirmation Call & Text Night
events.description:
### Join volunteers from across the country to support organizers and communities in states facing anti-trans ballot measures. 



This October, A4TE is partnering with incredible organizations—including the Ballot Initiative Strategy Center (BISC), the National LGBTQ Task Force, and more—to host weekly virtual phonebanks supporting states facing anti-trans ballot measures and other attacks.

**We’ll support organizers on the ground by reaching out to people who have signed up for upcoming events, confirming their attendance, and helping make sure everyone has the information they need to participate.** All we're doing is reaching out to folks who RSVP’d to confirm they’re still planning to attend the event they signed up for.

This is one of the easiest ways to get involved! 

### What to expect: 

- **You’ll get trained.** Staff and experienced volunteer leaders will walk you through everything you need to know before you start making calls or sending texts—no prior experience required. 

- **We’ll send texts and/or make calls together.** You’ll be part of a supportive, welcoming group where we can encourage each other and build community along the way. 

- **We’ll provide the scripts.** You’ll have everything you need to feel prepared and confident. We’ll provide scripts and any relevant information.

- **No personal phone number required.** All you need is a computer or tablet with an internet connection to make calls/texts.

- **Your privacy matters.** Our tools are designed to help protect your personal information when reaching out to people.

- **We’ll make a difference together.** Support organizers on the ground by helping confirm RSVPs and making sure people who signed up are ready to show up for these important events.

- 9:00 AM – 12:00 PM: Training and door knocking
- 12:30 PM: Press conference

The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box.

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

Join us at the Hackensack Hub where we will gather and march around the block, pausing at 371 to show our support of democracy! We will end up at Lucette and join in song. Lunch and snacks will be provided at the DFL office and you'll have the opportunity to meet your candidates and see how you can help!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Prepared and paid for by Cass County DFL
www.casscodfl.org

events.title: Running an Effective Campaign Debrief
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Tuesday, November 10th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **Running an Effective Campaign Debrief**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Discuss the essential data and performance metrics to review at the end of a campaign

2\. Review suggested practices for planning and facilitating a campaign debrief

  

**This training is right for you if you're concluding the planning/execution of a 2026 campaign.** 

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: So You Want to Run for Office?
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Thursday, November 12th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **So You Want to Run for Office**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Understand the steps necessary to run for office

2\. Explain best practices for choosing which office to run for

3\. Identify what kinds of support you'll need to run for office

4\. Prepare for sharing your decision to run with your support network

  

**This training is right for you if you're considering a run for elected office but haven't yet made the commitment to run or filed your candidacy.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [Getting Your Campaign Off the Ground](https://traindems.org/course-details/100/getting-your-campaign-off-the-ground).  
_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: Precinct Chair and Candidate Recruitment
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Monday, November 16th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on Precinct Chair and Candidate Recruitment. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1\. Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs

2\. Introduce tactics used by local leaders to grow and engage membership

3\. Review approaches for persuading first time candidates to run

  

**This training is right for you if you hold a leadership position in a Democratic club/committee or progressive organization that actively supports candidates seeking elected office.**

  

_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: Democracy for All: Ballot Proposal Training
events.description:
Want to get more involved in your community? Feel like you can lead conversations with your neighbors around voting?

Join us at the Fisher Theater for a train the trainers event, where we'll cover everything you need to know for the proposals on your ballot this November. Learn from experts, network with other interested volunteers, and make a plan to lead your community into midterm season.

events.title: Recovering from a Lost Election
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Tuesday, November 17th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **Recovering from a Lost Election****.** We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1.  Discuss productive ways to reflect on and debrief your campaign experience
2.  Plan a timeline for post-Election Day supporter engagement and goals for continued organizing efforts
3.  Explore ways to have an ongoing positive impact on local Democratic organizing, including the decision to seek election again in the future 

  

**This training is right for you if you are a candidate with some degree of desire to stay involved in political organizing, even if your bid for election is unsuccessful.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [The Fundamentals of Field Tactics](https://traindems.org/course-details/67/the-fundamentals-of-field-tactics)  
_Have accessibility questions? Reply to your registration email to confirm your requirements or request more information._

events.title: What is a Democratic Precinct Chair?
events.description:
Join the National Democratic Training Committee on Wednesday, November 18th from 1-2 pm ET for a free virtual live training on **What is a D****emocratic Precinct Chair**. We're here to help, so join us to learn the following:

1.  Describe the structure and purpose of local Democratic Parties
2.  Review common positions people hold in local Democratic Parties
3.  Identify key responsibilities of Democratic precinct chairs
4.  Introduce tactics used by local leaders to grow and engage Democratic Party membership

  

**This training is right for you if you aren't currently involved with your local Democratic party but are exploring ways to get involved in Democratic power-building in your community.**

  

A recommended (not required) course to take in our Online Academy is [Member Recruitment and Retention for Local Democratic Parties](https://learn.traindems.org/learn/courses/23/member-recruitment-and-retention-for-local-democratic-parties).

events.title: GOTV Downtown Baltimore City
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Suwannee Town Center Park, Suwannee, GA
events.description:
Come join Indivisible Gwinnett as we host our No Kings Vote Early event at Suwannee Town Center Park in Suwannee, GA on Saturday, October 17th from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m.! We will talk about why voting early matters, and attendees will be able to check their voter registration, see their sample ballot, find out where you can vote early, and make a plan to vote. We can de-mystify the voting process for you. Attendees can "Rock the Vote" at our rock painting station, and we'll provide refreshments and a freebie or two. Some of us will be wearing superhero capes to show that voting is our superpower. This will be a fun event celebrating the people exercising their power via the vote.

Bring a sign encouraging people to vote early or why voting matters, and you can wave it with us along the roadside to encourage the people driving by to vote and to vote early. Suwannee Town Center Park is less than a mile away from the early voting site at George Pierce Park, so you can make plans to vote the same day.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

Come join Indivisible Gwinnett and our partner, the North Gwinnett Democrats, on Saturday, October 17th, at Suwannee Town Center Park! We will be in the park near the intersection of Buford Highway and Lawrenceville Suwannee Road. You will be able to check your voter registration, see your sample ballot, find out where you can vote early, and make a plan to vote. It's easy and we'll guide you through it. Bring a sign to wave if you'd like, telling people to vote early and why voting matters. Keep in mind when making your signs that this is a non-partisan event.

George Pierce Park is an early voting location and will be open during our event. It is a short drive or a reasonable walk from our location, so you can easily vote the same day. 

This will be a fun, upbeat event and kids are welcome. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Gresham, Wood Village, Fairview, Troutdale, Corbett
events.description:
Multnomah East Indivisible “NO KINGS - Vote Early”
Rally, March and Ballot Drop

October 17, 2026 
10 am to noon
Gresham City Hall Plaza
1333 NW Eastman Parkway, Gresham, OR

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

The NO KINGS movement is taking the next step, turning people power into voter power, and MEI is inviting you to our East County “NO KINGS – Vote Early” Rally, March and Ballot Drop. This is not simply a protest.   Instead, on October 17th, we will demonstrate Early Voting.   Following a rally at Gresham City Hall Plaza, we will march along Eastman Parkway to NW 3rd St and into the parking lot of the old Gresham Library, where the ballot drop box is located. 
 
Voter Pamphlets and Ballots will be mailed no later than Oct 14, and we are asking people (if they can) to complete their ballot right away and bring it to the rally so they can drop it directly into an official ballot drop box.  No problem if you can’t complete your ballot by the 17th, we are setting an example, and will hold mini-events every following Saturday to repeat the same march and encourage voting. 
  
We will have music and entertainment at the library parking lot, where people can mingle and discuss their plan to vote and support each other as needed.  Following the march, people are encouraged to wander over to Main Ave for lunch or a snack before going back to your vehicle.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Kansas City
events.description:
As many of you have probably heard, the next **No Kings has been set for October 17, 2026!**  You have been wondering what the plan is, so here is the plan!

**What:**  Big Rally and GOTV (Get Out The Vote) action
 
**When:** 1pm Rally starts, 2pm GOTV action starts (Oct 17)
 
**Where:** Rally at Mill Creek Park (east side of the Plaza), with action-specific GOTV activities to take place elsewhere or nearby, as appropriate
  
**Who:** All of Kansas City is invited!  This is the time to save our Democracy, so YOU are invited!   

**How:** Door knocking!  Phone bank prep!  Postcards!  Business area canvassing! Pedestrian area literature!  And more!

This one will be different from past No Kings events.  Please come ready to work!  Bring your signs and other protest items too, but after the rally, we are going to get to work together to maximize the Early Vote.  This will be a mass mobilization effort.  If we all do our part, we will save our nation.

All necessary training and materials will be provided at the No Kings event.  Keep an eye out for more details on the GOTV action you signed up for in the weeks to come.

So mark your calendars.  And please help us spread the word. **No Kings is back, and it is going to be awesome!**  

Sincerely,

Your No Kings Kansas City allies


**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: No Kings Bridge- Arlington
events.description:
No Kings Day is Oct 17th, 2026! This time we are going out in the communities to spread the word about the importance of VOTING EARLY! No Kings: Vote Early is about making sure every eligible voter has a plan to vote early, knows their options, and is ready to make their voice count. This bridge will host TWO shifts: We need folks on the bridge from 7AM-9AM, and 5PM-7PM to reach as many voters on the highway as possible. Wear your patriotic gear! We will provide the main large sign. ***Please follow all safety instructions provided by the bridge host. *This is the Davis Drive bridge on I30 in Arlington. Parking is at 1601 N Davis Dr

Please watch the following video on de-escalation BEFORE attending the event. https://youtu.be/R2PSExM-NhU?si=V_K0zwKan0FGZtIh

Be sure to join our socials and share your pics from the event (please tag us and #visibilitybrigade, #nokings): https://linktr.ee/jointhe12

Bridge Brigades will cancel if the forecasted weather is: -Under 40 degrees -Rain is forecasted at 50% *Bridge host may cancel that morning if they arrive at the bridge and it is raining. We do not want to add to any traffic concerns in the rain. -Bridge Hosts will make a judgment call if inclement weather moves in while on the bridge. If lightning is within 6 miles of the bridge, hosts will ask all volunteers to leave immediately. Hosts will use their best judgement regarding wind gusts. Please listen to Bridge Hosts as your safety is a priority. -Bridge Hosts will make every effort to cancel the next day's bridge protest by 9PM the night before, if needed.

**We reject all forms of political violence and intimidation, no matter the source or the target. That’s not just a moral stance—it’s a strategic one. Movements that create lasting change do so by building trust, forging solidarity, and demonstrating discipline, even in the face of threats or attacks.

events.title: GOTV Annapolis
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at our office to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Maple Valley, WA

address_lines: 26520 Maple Valley Black Diamond Rd SE, Maple Valley, WA 98038

events.description:
Join us at Four Corners and help get the vote out! We will be at Four Corners for a peaceful rally - bring your VOTE EARLY signs - remember, this is about voting early and getting the news out. This is not a rally like other No Kings events - this is about encouraging our entire community to get out and vote!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Black Net AZ Party At The Polls in Phoenix!
events.description:
# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a evening party! Come for the books and the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join Black Net AZ for a celebration of civic power, music, and community spirit!

**THE VIBE:**

We are inviting a grown and sexy vibe to Grassrootz Bookstore and transferring that energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍 Grassrootz Bookstore (1145 E Washington St #200, Phoenix, AZ 85034)

📅 October 13th from 5 pm - 8 pm

**FEATURING:**

Music by DJ Kemiini, FREE Smoothies for the first 100 people, actives for yourself and your family, and of course, FREE SWAG!
**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.title: Walk for Change - Block Walk with West U Area Dems October 3, 4, 10, 11
events.description:
Big money TV ads can't stop grassroots activism. Come join us on Saturday 10/3, and/or Sunday 10/4 or Saturday 10/10 and/or Sunday 10/11 as we canvass to Get Out The Vote (GOTV) for the November 3rd election. Explain to voters why Democrats will improve people's lives and ensure they will get out to vote.

We will meet at the West University Community Center located at 6104 Auden and then block walk from 10:00 am – 12:00 pm on Saturday and then meet and block walk from 3:00 - 5:00 pm on Sunday. Plan on coming whether this is your first time to block walk or whether you have done it before. We will provide training and pair you with an experienced person.

You can also pick up turfs and walk or your own schedule.  Just let us know by contacting at at westuareademocrats@gmail.com

We will have lists of people to talk to, the scripts to use in discussing this election, plus literature to hand out concerning the election. You just need to bring your cellphones to download the MiniVAN app, wear comfortable clothes, and bring your special water bottle.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Greenville, SC
events.description:
NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY - UPSTATE SC
We've spent the last two years showing up in the streets. Now it's time to take that people power to the ballot box.
Early voting in South Carolina begins Monday, Oct. 19 and runs through Oct. 31. Voting early has many benefits, including helping mitigate voter suppression efforts and other barriers that can make voting more difficult.
So, on October 17, we're hitting the road, bringing No Kings: Vote Early to communities across the Upstate for a full day of voter visibility, education, and community engagement.
If the goal is to get people informed and ready to vote, visibility matters.
THE UPSTATE ROUTE
CHOOSE YOUR STARTING POINT
Anderson | 10:00 to 11:30 AM | Anderson County Courthouse | 100 S. Main St.
OR
Laurens | 9:30 to 10:30 AM | Lavonne Shopping Center parking lot | 102 Fleming Street
Easley | 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM | Corner of E. Main St. & S. Pendleton St. | Downtown
Lunch Break
Greer | 2:30 to 4:00 PM | Corner of Trade St. & E. Poinsett St. | Downtown
Simpsonville | 4:00 to 5:30 PM | Clock Tower Square | Corner of S. Main St. & W. Curtis St. | Downtown
Greenville | 5:30 to 7:00 PM | Rally at Falls Park Falls Park | 601 S. Main St. | Downtown
Laurens will be our vehicle decorating stop to turn your ride into a rolling reminder to vote early. The Anderson, Easley, Greer, and Simpsonville stops will be picket-style visibility actions on public sidewalks, putting the message where people can see it. We'll finish the day in Greenville with a community rally at Falls Park featuring topical speakers and music.
Bring signs about early voting, making a voting plan, election information, or factual reminders about participating in our elections.
Please skip "register to vote" signs. Voter registration ends October 4 at 11:59 PM, so hopefully everyone has visited SCVOTES.GOV to register and verify their registration before then!
The goal is simple: every community we visit should know more than they did before we got there.
WANT TO DO THE WHOLE ROUTE?
Yes, 5 cities in one day is a LOT.
We've mapped out a recommended travel schedule, including departure times and, because we're not monsters, a lunch break.
You don't have to travel all day. Join us at the stop closest to you.
One stop or 5 of your choice, help us take the message beyond Greenville and across the Upstate.
6 communities. One day. One message. No Kings. No Thrones. No Crowns.
The people choose who represents them. Make your plan. Vote early. Spread the word.

Hosted by: 50501 SC, Indivisible Upstate SC, C.A.R.E. 864, Community Heroes, Anderson County Democratic Party, and Laurens County Democratic Party

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

We’re hitting the doors and talking directly with our neighbors about why we’re sending Scott Wiener to Congress!

events.description:
### 22 days. 254 counties. 500,000 Texans.

We're in the final stretch of the most important election Texas has seen in years, and one of the most powerful ways to win it isn't another ad. It's people reaching the people they already know.

That's one of the ways Texas Together is organizing to win in November, **and it's where you come in.** We're recruiting volunteers in all 254 counties, each one reaching their friends, family, and coworkers to make sure they vote and volunteer in these final weeks.

Join our GOTV Reach Friend Bank kickoff call on Monday, Oct 12, at 6pm CT to get plugged in. We'll share our plan to mobilize voters in all 254 counties through the power of our personal networks using the Reach app, and how to plug in to reach your people, make sure they have a plan to vote and volunteer and help elect James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, Vikki Goodwin, and Democrats up and down the ballot.

All you need is a phone or laptop, a few hours a week between now and November 3, and a commitment to help flip Texas blue. We'll teach you the rest.

See you soon!

events.title: Listening Circle | Virtual Virginia Indivisible
events.description:
Virtual Virginia Indivisible (VVI) is a group of people who for whatever reason cannot do in-person organizing but would like to use their skills to build healthier communities. We are located in Virginia, but you do not have to be in Virginia to be involved. 

This event is our weekly Listening Circle on zoom (Saturdays at 7pm ET) for whoever needs to just be quiet or to share with others of common values. Listening Circle has presenters on occasion and have held vigils for those unjustly killed.

Our group supports these five principles:
	Democracy. 
	Inclusion.
	Collaboration.
	Intentionality.
	Nonviolence.

Currently, the issues we are focused on are Immigration/Criminal Justice Reform, Voting Protection, and (Dis)ability Rights.

events.title: Post Protest Car Parade - Newburyport "Hands Along High Street"
events.description:
The NDCC will hold our 61st weekly protest on Saturday, October 17th from 11 AM - 12 PM at the Bartlet Mall.

In honor of No Kings Day's Vote Early theme, starting at 12:00 PM we will host a car parade that will start at the Bartlet Mall (parking area behind CVS), proceed through town and over the Route 1 Bridge into Salisbury. We will proceed as a group along Route 110 and across the Chain Bridge back to Atkinson Common, where we will join our friends at I-RISE, who will be rallying at that location until 1 PM. We will reach out to registrants to see if you want to be a driver or a passenger, and all are encouraged to bring their signs about early voting along for the ride. events.description:
Join us on five October afternoons to let our neighbors know that it is critical that we Vote Early from Saturday, October 17 to Thursday, October 30 or Vote on Election Day on Tuesday, November 3.

Join the No Kings movement to protect our elections against sabotage and turn out the largest early vote in US history!

Easthampton has a high rate of registered voters, but recent elections have seen low turnout. Let's turn out like we did in the last Presidential Election in 2024. It's Up to Us.

Easthampton Election & Voting Information: https://easthamptonma.gov/164/Elections-Voting

Bring a friend or two. Bring signs if you have them: Vote Early. Vote Early: October 17. No Kings! No Throwns! No Crowns! This is What Democracy Looks Like. No Kings, Just Voters. Our Elections are Under Attack: Vote Early!

We will have a supply of signs.


Voting early means your voice is locked in and safe, days before anyone else can decide what happens next, and it gives you room to fix anything that goes wrong, a signature mismatch, a missing form, waiting in a line that's too long, or not being able to make it if your shift runs late.

No matter what the laws look like where you live, early preparation is universal. Cast your ballot at an early voting site (where available), request and return an absentee ballot, double check your registration, or make it a whole day! However you do it, our goal is to make a clear voting plan, and voting early.

events.title: Staging Location Director Training
events.description:
Want to help us elect James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, and Vikki Goodwin in November? Sign up to be a Staging Location Host!

Staging Locations are satellite campaign offices/canvass launch points set up in different parts of a district or community during our Get Out the Vote effort (GOTV). Your house, garage, or a local business could all be staging locations!

Staging locations expand our presence so that there is a campaign location easily accessed by volunteers in every neighborhood. They enable campaigns to deploy canvassers efficiently and monitor local polling locations without wasting precious time driving great distances.

This training will prepare you to host a Staging Location!

events.title: Phone Banking (Longmont)
events.description:
Join us at UCC Longmont to help GET OUT THE VOTE by phone banking!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through: 
- How to log into the phone bank platform 
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!) 
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses 
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**
Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

*Computer
*Headphones
*Enthusiasm for the cause!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - "Disco Night!"   "Silent Disco" online + we do GOTV volunteer tasks!
events.description:
No Kings Early Voting Disco Night!!  🪩🎉♥️🏳️‍🌈♿️🏳️‍⚧️🥰🎶
"Silent Zoom" disco party online, while we get stuff done!

Disco music plays, like a radio station.
GOTV is "Get Out The Vote" Radio!
Chitchat is kept in the Chat box, to keep vibes calm and help us get stuff done!

We do Volunteer tasks while the boogie heals our soul :)

"What kind of tasks do we do?"
* Check your voter registration,
* Fill out your Ballot, if you received it early by mail,
* Double-check your Poll Site hours, address, and Accessibility info,
* Help others finalize their Voting Plans!
* Do Get Out The Vote (GOTV) phone banks, text banks, and other Outreach - let's get people to Vote Early!!
* Catch up on organizing emails to GOTV,
* Make sure you're signed up to get your ballot early, by mail (if you can),
* Learn about your Ballot Questions and Candidates, so you know how you'll vote,
* Finish part-done tasks you've already started.
* Write GOTV postcards!

Work on whatever Early Voting / GOTV Volunteer tasks are on your personal GOTV To Do list!
Make dinner, do GOTV postcards, do Phone Bank calls, etc.
Do whatever GOTV work you'd be doing anyway, but let us and the music keep you moving :)
If you need help getting started, our host / co-hosts will point you in the right direction :)

This type of teamwork is Strategic:  
We're "body doubling" and co-regulating, by doing this work together, nationwide!
Our team has hand-written and mailed over 65,000 nonpartisan Get Out The Vote postcards in the past two years, and we're hoping to reach 75,000 in 2026!


Feel free to join this long-running "Disco Night" silent disco every Monday, Friday, and Saturday night, 7-9pm EST.
"GOTV Radio" broadcasts over zoom from Salem, Massachusetts, and is co-hosted by fellow volunteers all over the country.

"Why Disco?" 🪩🎉♥️🏳️‍🌈♿️🏳️‍⚧️🥰🎶
It's the joyful music of the movement!
Disco Music is known for a "4 on the floor" beat, just a little faster than a resting heartbeat.
Listening to disco, especially when stressed or dealing with trauma, helps regulate our nervous systems!
Our hearts beat to the time, slight elevated but not in danger.  
It reminds us that we're safe, in a good place, doing the stuff that matters, and we can be effective!
It connects us to activism through the generations, and anchors us in best practices.

This event is hosted by a Queer, Disabled Femme and fellow neurodivergent, Queer, BIPoC, or Disabled friends!  ♿️🏳️‍⚧️♥️🏳️‍🌈🪩
"Disco Night" started in 2024 to help volunteers push each other to make more calls, write more postcards, and do more tasks to remind people to Vote Early, check voter registration, etc.
We know that when more people vote, election results more accurately reflect the will of the People!
Voting early saves time, money, energy, and opportunities to help others do the same.

How to Join:
https://linktr.ee/RedCardsMoreLanguages
Click the Disco Ball icon to join the zoom!

Pajamas, no-video, no-interaction and other chill involvement are totally welcome.  
Come as you are, get stuff done, and Get Out That Vote! :)
Our shared goal:  Get people to Vote Early, Vote the whole ballot, and help others do the same!

Our one rule:
If you share something, keep it neutral or positive.  
We're all dealing with trauma and stress, esp. during the Fascism.
Let's help each other Move Forward, get stuff done, rather than clutch pearls.
If you're stressed out about an issue, share a related petition or action step with the group in the chat box!

Don't know what to work on?
Lauren, our host, will gladly assign you tasks!

The event will have lo-fi music playing throughout, plus the opportunity to learn more about other community groups in the area.

Accommodations

    A quiet table for folks who prefer a calm space and would like to be left undisturbed

Buttons to help everyone connect comfortably:

🟢 Crafty Teacher — This crafter is ready and willing to teach! Feel free to approach them to learn a new technique or get guided through a project step by step.

🟡 Chatty Crafter — This crafter loves good conversation! If you're looking to connect, swap ideas, or enjoy some lively chat while you create, this is your person.

🟠 Quiet Crafter — This crafter is here to soak in the creative energy and focus on their work. Craft alongside them and enjoy the peaceful vibe!

🔴 Accountability Buddy — These supportive crafters are here to cheer others on. Whether someone has been putting off a project or just needs a little push to reach their creative goals, the Accountability Buddy is in their corner to keep them motivated and on track.

We will dress in black (or wear black armbands) and silently hold signs with the pictures of those who were killed or died in ICE custody during 2025 and 2026. 

Please come to the southeast corner of Rt 155 and Rt 20 to pick up a sign and a flower. Black armbands will be available for those without black clothing. We will then spread out along Route 20 and in  respect, maintain silence.

events.description:
zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/86776950486?pwd=YMHeX9qcSl523ikMzWRAOptPzmMTKD.1

Contact your City Council Member and the Mayor ANYTIME

Better Ballot Sacramento supports the adoption of Ranked Choice Voting for Sacramento's City elections. We are working with the City Council to place a measure on the ballot to enact this crucial reform. Ranked Choice Voting will improve voter engagement, equitable representation, and attention to community priorities throughout Sacramento.

Calling your representative on the council and the Mayor signals popular support for this initiative and makes this reform a priority!

What to Do:
Take 60 seconds now to call or email your City Council member and the mayor! Your City Council member's number and email are below! You can also use this link to identify who your member is by your address: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/mayor-council/Find-Your-District 

What to Say:
Express your support for Ranked Choice Voting to the mayor and your representative however feels most authentic to you, just be sure to ask them to put it up for a vote! This is what we have said when we called:

"Hello! My name is [your name], and I am a voter in [representative's name]'s district. I'm calling to express my support for Ranked Choice Voting and request the council put this reform up for a vote, so the voters of Sacramento can choose to upgrade our elections. Thank you!"

events.description:

Where: Route 175 (Annapolis Road) and Gateway Boulevard

location.venue: Odenton Library - Anne Arundel County Public Library

events.description:
Before we gather at 11:00 for our No Kings Sign Wave event, let us help you make a voting plan! Stop by the Odenton Library any time between 10:00 am and 11:45 am. Trained volunteers will help you check your registration, answer your questions, and help you work out your plan: when, where, and how you'll vote.

Early voting runs October 22–29, 7 am to 8 pm. If you'd rather vote by mail, we can help you request a ballot before the October 27 deadline.

Missed the registration deadline? You still have options. In Maryland you can register in person (with proof of where you live) during early voting. We'll show you how.

While you're there, make a sign for our sign wave at 11. We'll have supplies, but bringing a poster board would be helpful!

Odenton families are feeling it at the grocery store, at the gas pump, and in every electric bill. Those in power make the decisions that directly affect us, and elections decide who holds that power. Voting early locks in your voice days ahead of time. It also gives you room to fix anything that goes wrong, like a signature mismatch, a missing form, or a shift that runs late on Election Day.

And it's not just about who you vote for: voting early in large numbers also sends a strong message that Americans still care about voting and about democracy.

events.title: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear friends,

I am one of the millions of Americans who believes that voting is a fundamental right—not a privilege reserved for those who happen to have the right paperwork. But right now, Congress is trying to pass the SAVE America Act, a bill that would make it harder for eligible citizens to register and vote.

Our Votes Are in Danger!

Here's what's happening:

•	The SAVE America Act passed the House 218–213 on February 11, 2026

•	It requires documentary proof of citizenship—in person—to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot

•	Over 21 million eligible American citizens do not have proof of their citizenship readily available

•	It is an unfunded mandate that would cost states hundreds of millions of dollars with zero federal funding

•	The Senate has repeatedly failed to pass it, and even Republican leaders admit the votes aren't there

•	President Trump is now demanding that the Senate abolish the filibuster to force it through

📢 "Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act" – That's Our Message

📝 Your Action: Write to Your Members of Congress

Step 1: Find Your Members of Congress

•	Find your U.S. Representative:
https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative

•	Find your U.S. Senators:
https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm

Step 2: Use This Template (Copy and Paste)

Subject: Save Democracy, Not the SAVE Act – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!

Dear [Senator/Representative Last Name],

I am a constituent from [City, State], and I urge you to vote NO on the SAVE America Act (H.R. 7296 / S. 1383).
The SAVE America Act is a solution in search of a problem. It is essentially a backdoor poll tax, forcing 140 million Americans without a passport to pay fees for documents they do not have.

I ask you to:

1.	Vote NO on the SAVE America Act – in any form, whether standalone, attached to the NDAA, or included in reconciliation
2.	Support dedicated federal funding for election administration if any new requirements are imposed
3.	Oppose efforts to abolish the filibuster to force this bill through
President Trump has made clear the goal is to keep Republicans in power. As he stated, the bill is about ensuring his party maintains control of Congress. Our democracy is not a partisan tool.

Please act now. Our votes depend on it.
Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Your Address]
[Your City, State, ZIP]

Step 3: Send It!

•	Use your members' official website contact forms (fastest)

•	Or email/call their offices directly

•	Call the Capitol Switchboard at (202) 224-3121 and ask to be connected


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Election protection and enforcement session for unions
events.description:
Our DC area unions are not only doing electoral work, but also making plans to be vigilant until January 2 and 3 when our local and national representatives begin governing. We will be part of a broad movement to stop him.
 
Our unions  together with Free DC will be hosting a half-day Election Protection strategy convening and training-of-trainers  the afternoon of Sunday October 25 on zoom.
 
Who is invited?

· Union leaders, political staff, or organizing staff responsible for internal member-to-member organizing.

· Non-political/organizing staff who are particularly interested in election enforcement and solidarity work

· Rank-and-file leaders who could be deployed to assist in election enforcement, and/or organize others to engage.

· IU staff who might be deployed to work in the local DC context in case of election enforcement need or an even larger surge of federal law enforcement, whether HSI, DEA, FBI, ICE, or other actors.

events.title: Protest Against Mesa City Council & NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center Campus!
events.description:
### 🚨Protest NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center! 🚨

On May 13, 2026, the Mesa Planning & Zoning Board quickly and quietly voted unanimously to recommend approval of the 2,257,581 sq ft [Mesa Data Center Campus known as the NTT Global PH10]( https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center). 

Mesa Valley Indivisible officially teamed up with our sister group, [Indivisible Mesa](https://www.indivisiblemesa.org)—who has been leading the charge against Mesa’s 287(g) agreement and predatory data centers, like the planned 2.2 million sq ft [NTT Mesa PH10 Data Center](https://www.mesavalleyindivisible.org/no-mesa-ntt-global-ph10-data-center)—to make our voices heard at City Hall.

As public turnout surged, city officials escalated their efforts to quiet community opposition: 

- **On June 8th**, A local activist was physically removed from a council meeting simply for silently holding a small sign. 

- At the next Mesa City Council meeting **on July 17th**, after the indoor sign bans forced us outside, police arrested a peaceful protester for using a megaphone despite the fact that she complied with their demands. She was charged with bogus charges and forced to spend a night in jail...FOR USING A MEGAPHONE. The charges were dropped at her 9/28/2026 court date. k 

- **On August 7th** when Indivisible Mesa recently pressed the City Council coordinator for answers, the city shifted its story yet again! They claimed the councilmembers will not be voting on the data center at all and that NTT can proceed administratively, but only after grassroots pressure began mounting.

If they won't let us show our signs inside, we will make sure they are impossible to ignore on the steps of City Hall. Mesa Valley Indivisible is pivoting this event to an outdoor protest starting at 5:00pm (meeting starts at 5:45pm). We will make our voices heard loud and clear from the outside!

## 📢 Calls to Action:

**Whether or not you can attend, please do the following three things:**

1. [Submit a comment here](https://us.openforms.com/Form/44ff3314-58bb-418a-a122-46fe7725feef)! Feel free to choose one of the concerns listed below if you do not want to write your own comment. 

2. [Email the Mesa City Council members by](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1llwS0FcrAfxBdC1DwOL0hayMQ9SWK1WJkHFZlxXYdQ4/edit?usp=sharing).** Contact info, directions, and scripts/templates provided!

3. [Call the Mesa City Council members](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qedOvsbfPZ9mG1N6BKkc7QvL3XeamSdmvA_oVY7bu8w/edit?usp=sharing)** and use the script provided or your own! 


## 🚨 Important: 

- We do not care whether or not the data center is on the agenda. MVI and other local activists know it is VITAL we voice our disgust every single council meeting in order to make sure they actually listen to their constituents! 


## ## 🔑 Key Concerns Driving the Protest:

- Massive Handouts, Tiny Returns: Similarly sized data centers receive over $100 million a year in tax subsidies. That is revenue stolen directly from our local community services and neighborhood improvements.

- Virtually No Job Creation: Despite taking up huge amounts of space, this massive facility will only create 40 to 60 permanent jobs paying $60,000 or less. Compared to advanced manufacturing or bioscience, data centers provide practically zero high-quality jobs per acre.

- We Pay Their Bills: The infrastructure improvements and utility upgrades required for this project will likely be passed on to everyday customers, not the multibillion-dollar company.

- Driving Up Local Costs: Developments like this artificially inflate land costs, making it harder for our local farmers, small businesses, and families looking for affordable housing to survive.

- A 2.2 million-square-foot facility requires an astronomical amount of energy and water to keep its servers cool. In our delicate desert environment, this level of resource consumption is completely unsustainable and directly threatens the capacity of our local utilities.

- This project threatens the safety and peace of our residential areas. The constant, 24/7 roar of massive cooling fans creates severe noise pollution, while the sprawling, windowless buildings will industrialize our local landscape and destroy our community's character.


## 🪧 Sign Ideas:

- We won't be silent!
- No more Mesa Data Centers!
- NO one wants Data Centers!
- Hate data centers = bipartisan 


## 📷 Pictures & Videos
- Make sure to always tag **Mesa Valley Indivisible** on our group [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1CFYV1DSaT/), [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/mesavalleyindivisible/), [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc), [BlueSky](https://bsky.app/profile/mesavalleyindivisi.bsky.social), and [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@mesa.valley.indiv?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc)
- Please also include #MesaValleyIndivisible #AbolishICE #CloseAROCC #RecuseBiggs #ReleaseEpsteinFiles
- Add all photos & videos to our [Google drive!](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hkgqf8L4uPRGBpwwLClceOBp63iS48It)

events.title: Texas Democratic Poll Watcher Trainings
events.description:
**Protect the vote in Texas by training to become a Poll Watcher!**

Poll Watchers monitor the elections process at Early Voting Locations and Election Day Polling Sites in every corner of the state, serving as the campaign’s eyes and ears on the ground. By being present and helping identify any issues right away, Poll Watchers play a vital role in protecting the vote -- and are as important as ever this election.

**Take the first step by signing up now to attend a Virtual Poll Watcher Training, hosted by the Texas Together Democratic Coordinated Campaign!**

At the training you will learn everything you need to succeed as a Poll Watcher, including what the role entails, what to expect, what to bring, and best practices. After completing the training process, you’ll be prepared to serve as a Poll Watcher during both Early Voting (starting October 19) and on Election Day (November 3).

*Please note that to serve as a Poll Watcher inside a voting location, you must be a registered voter in the county you are serving in, and you must complete an additional, separate training required by the Secretary of State (available at https://pollworkertraining.sos.texas.gov/). We recommend completing this training as soon as possible.*

**You only need to attend one Texas Together Democratic Poll Watcher Training session.

Obed's Parking Lot
170 Main Street

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. *No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: Dial In for Democracy: Virtual GOTV Phone Bank
events.description:
Every vote in our community deserves a reminder, a clear answer, and a little encouragement. Join Imagine Black from home to call voters across Multnomah County ahead of the November 3 election.

This is a nonpartisan phone bank. We won't be talking about candidates or ballot measures. Our job is simpler and just as powerful: making sure people have the facts they need to vote. We'll remind voters how Oregon's vote-by-mail works, walk through ranked-choice voting in Multnomah County, and encourage everyone to return their ballot by 8:00 PM on Election Day. Too many people sit out elections because no one reached out or they weren't sure how the process works. A single call can change that.

No experience needed. We'll welcome you on Zoom, give you a quick training, and get you calling with support close by if questions come up.

What you'll need:

Reliable internet
A laptop you can use for the full shift
A web browser other than Google Chrome (Firefox, Safari, or Edge work best)
Headphones, helpful but not required

When we organize, we win. Come call with us.

Indivisible Park County's NO KINGS-VOTE EARLY rally will be held on Saturday, October 17, from noon to 1 PM in Livingston at 5th and Park.

We will have a table with information on important voting topics, such as why voting matters, registering to vote, checking your registration, how to vote early, and tracking your vote. Volunteers will be at the table to answer questions.

events.title: Unify the Matriarchy Community Photoshop

location.venue: Stars & Stripes Park Bob Hope Pavilion

events.description:
October 10, 2026, 5:00-8:00 PM, at Stars & Stripes Park (Bob Hope Pavilion) | 3701 S Lake Hefner Dr, OKC, OK 73116

The Unify the Matriarchy Community Photoshoot is an Intentional Solidarity Event designed to bring people together from different backgrounds, cultures, and lived experiences in an atmosphere of mutual respect. Our premise is that solidarity does not happen by accident. Many meaningful relationships never form simply because our daily lives rarely intersect. This event intentionally creates opportunities for community members to meet, share their stories, and recognize one another's humanity. 

The first hour of the event will be emceed by DJ D. Chappell (employee of Power 103.5), while featuring breakout circles prompted by our partnered organizations concise presentations to encourage attendees to socialize with intent to find a partner they may not have otherwise encountered. Guest speakers, including N'Kyla Jasmine Thomas, Melissa Elder, and more will cover:  Maternal Health, Female Incarceration, Reproductive Justice, Women's Wages, Women's Voting Rights, Domestic Violence Awareness, and Inclusive Feminism.

The last half of the event will continue with music and free refreshments provided by Lelamae's Catering; while inviting attendees to stand together in solidarity with a new friend they met through the event to recreate their own version of the iconic photograph of Gloria Steinem and Dorothy Pittman-Hughes. The replicated photo represents the Unified Sisterhood's vision to build a more connected feminist movement by fostering intentional solidarity and bringing resolve to historical harms within the Movement's agenda. 

Donations for digital photographs and Lelamae's Catering are encouraged but not required. Printed photographs will be available for a predetermined donation amount.

We hope you will join us for this kickoff event! See you on Saturday, October 10th at 5 PM!

events.description:
Indivisible Park County’s No Kings:Vote Early rally will be held on Saturday, October 17, from noon to 1 PM in Gardiner at the intersection of Hwy 89 and Jardine Rd. 

For over a year, millions of people have come together to send a clear message: in America, we have no kings. Power does not belong to billionaires, strongmen, or politicians who believe they’re above accountability. Power belongs to the people. But only if we use it.

Being nonpartisan means we won’t promote or criticize any candidates, initiatives, or particular issues.

We will have a table with information on important voting topics, such as why voting matters, registering to vote, checking your registration, how to vote early, and tracking your vote. Volunteers will be at the table to answer questions. 

Please come with signs about making your voice heard, protecting our democracy, registering to vote, absentee ballots, voting, your vote matters, and voting early. 

We hope you can attend and bring a few friends, neighbors, or family members. Let’s take an hour to use our power and help create the biggest early voter turnout in US history. 

As always, a core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action and no civil disobedience. We ask all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.description:
The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance's nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box.

Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Vermont
events.description:
No Kings/Vote Early Honk and Wave:

Come join us for a fun, high-energy Honk & Wave right here in town! We’ll have live local troubadours filling the air with music, and we’ll provide plenty of great signs—or feel free to bring your own creative ones. It’s an easy, upbeat way to connect with neighbors, bring some serious joy to our main streets, and make a big splash together. Sign up to join the lineup today and let’s make some noise!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Love as Action: Kennett Square, PA
events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Kennet Friends Meeting to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On Saturday October 17 at 1:00pm we will gather in front of Kennett Friends Meeting for one hour of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Port Townsend, WA
events.description:
NO KINGS COMMUNITY PARTY and RALLY at the Jefferson County Courthouse Park hosted by Indivisible Port Townsend.  
Music and events begin 12:30 p.m.
Come in costume to a ‘Let Us Eat Cake” community party. Speeches. Tabling, Games, Prizes for Kids—and we’ll serve cake!
 Bring your completed ballot and join a celebratory procession to the county dropbox. Join a Rapid Response team to protect election results going forward. If we still have energy left we can round off the day waving signs along Sims Way.
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Many of us believe that we’re immune to election sabotage, or that only experts can and will ensure free and democratic elections. The truth is: We’re not immune and what happens next is up to us. We're strongest when all of us show up, speak out, and refuse to be intimidated.

events.title: Trans Kids Belong Here Denver Summit Pep Rally
events.description:
What’s happening now with Propositions 134 and 135 is bigger than an attack on trans participation in sports. These activists are turning women’s sports into a political circus, manufacturing controversies, dragging players and teams into culture-war stunts, and demanding that women's sports leagues police who belongs in women’s spaces. Their goal isn’t to protect women’s sports. It’s to weaponize women’s sports as a stage for attacking trans people.

But the unprecedented popularity of women's sports gives us an exciting opportunity. The NWSL regular season (as we lead into the Women’s World Cup in 2027) will be a major stage for demonstrating just how much support there is for trans people, trans athletes, and the simple idea that trans people belong everywhere, including in sports.

events.title: Tending Environmental Grief: Part One
events.description:
We are living in an era of significant environmental change and loss. In recognizing that these times are challenging to live in, adapt to, and cope with, it’s essential that we come together as a community to process our experiences. Supporting ourselves and one another is just as important as stewarding the land and waters. 

Join Sky Island Alliance and [Maria Renée](https://www.maria-renee.com/) on Thursday, Oct. 15, at 9:30 a.m. for a dedicated time to understand the terrain of environmental grief, work through our emotions, celebrate this beautiful region, and practice building resilience together. This free webinar kicks off a series of opportunities to contribute your creative responses to a changing region, whether they come from grief, hope, or anything in between. A follow-up webinar on Thursday, Dec. 10, at 9:30 a.m. will give participants a chance to share their reflections and experiences in response to a series of prompts.

events.title: Become a Great Canvasser: CA-22 / Villegas for Congress Edition
events.description:
You don’t have to be an expert—or have the perfect speech—to be a great canvasser. The key is knowing how to listen, connect, and make the most of each conversation.

In this interactive 75-minute workshop, experienced canvassers will share practical strategies for engaging with voters of all stripes—including strong Democrats, those who rarely or never vote, and Republicans and Independents who want to see new leadership in our country. This CA-22 edition includes Villegas-specific context, PDI, and working with the campaign’s canvassing script (without sounding scripted).

Through real-life stories, demos, and practice, you’ll learn how to ask great questions, listen with empathy, and build trust. You’ll learn when to keep a conversation short—and when to slow down and get curious about what matters to a voter. We’ll show you how to use what you hear to connect voters’ priorities with Randy Villegas’s vision and help them find their own reasons to vote for him.

A knock on a stranger’s door can become a conversation that earns their vote. And in a razor-thin election, conversations like these can add up to the votes we need to win.

Note: To get the most out of this training, we recommend that you download the latest version of the PDI app onto your phone before the workshop.
