events.title: No Kings
events.description:
Indivisible NWCT, in collaboration with Northwest CT Take Action, will hold a nonviolent community NO KINGS (Just Voters) rally on Saturday, October 17, from 10:00 to 11:30 a.m. at Coe Park in Torrington.

The rally will focus on the upcoming 2026 election and the importance of voting and participating in the democratic process.

“NO KINGS is about recognizing that power ultimately belongs to the people,” said a representative of Indivisible NWCT. “We want to encourage people to make a plan to vote and to understand the importance of participating in the upcoming election.”

The event will feature guest speakers, who will be announced at a later date, and will provide a peaceful public forum for community members to come together around the importance of voting.

“Voting is one of the most direct ways people can participate in our democracy,” the Indivisible NWCT representative said. “We want people to get informed, make a plan, and make their voices heard.”

The rally is nonviolent and family-friendly. Organizers encourage participants to bring their family and friends, flags and signs, and to show their creativity by wearing costumes. People from Torrington and the surrounding towns are invited to join the community at Coe Park.

events.title: NO KINGS! VOTE EARLY! in Estes Park Sat Oct 17
events.description:
“NO KINGS! - VOTE EARLY!” Demonstration in Estes Park

Day/Time: Saturday, October 17, 2026, 10:00 to 11:30 am.
Location:   South Sidewalk next to Bond Park in Estes Park, Colorado

JOIN OUR LOCAL EXPRESSION of "No Kings! - Vote Early!" in Estes Park for a visible, peaceful and joyful demonstration of WE THE PEOPLE working together to... defend our democracy, make our voices heard and transforming VOICES INTO VOTES for a massive BLUE wave of voter turnout for the Nov 3, 2026 election.

The goal of this "NO KINGS!" Demonstration is designed to encourage VOTERS to exercise and reclaim our Constitutional rights and responsibilities in deciding our Country's leaders and future. This national effort is purposely scheduled when Colorado and many other states are already in their EARLY VOTING STAGES.  

Our Local Demonstration will encourage voters to make sure they have a VOTING PLAN to make their voices heard and their votes counted, including: (1) making sure they are registered to vote; (2) voting early; (3) making sure their mail-in ballots are deposited safely and timely in drop boxes; or (4) choosing to vote in person at local Voter Centers. 

EVEN BETTER! Bring your BALLOT with you to the Day of the Demonstration and we'll cheer you on as you deposit it in the Official Ballot Drop Box just steps away from our gathering!

Instructions and Disclaimer: This demonstration is a non-partisan call to action. A core principle behind all demonstrations is a commitment to nonviolent action.  We expect all participants to remain peaceful at all times.  Please remain on the sidewalk and do not impede pedestrians or traffic. Do not block driveways, intersections, or access to Bond Park.   Please obey instructions from law enforcement, emergency personnel, and demonstration monitors. Also, obey all local restrictions, including no amplification (no mics or speakers/boom boxes), no tables or easels. events.title: Rally to Support Judges
events.description:
A federal judge received this message: "I know where you live and I know where your children go to school," another received an email saying he would be "skinned alive." Judges in America are currently under siege. More than 1,000 serious threats have been made against federal judges in the past five years. **This is happening in our own backyard. Chief Judge John McConnell, of the US District Court for the District of Rhode Island (who sits at the Federal Courthouse in Providence), has been one of the most outspoken members of the bench regarding his personal experience being the recipient of serious and terrifying threats.**  

This is not a partisan issue. Serious threats have been made to judges appointed by both Republican and Democratic presidents. Democracy functions only when all judges are free to make decisions based upon their understanding of the law - not based upon fear or coercion. 

Indivisible LAB members of Support the Courts invite you to join them for a rally outside the Federal Courthouse in Providence, Rhode Island on **Tuesday, October 13, from 12:30 to 2:30 PM** to show support for the safety of each and every judge. This is a rally of support for the judges, not a protest, and signage should be confined to this particular issue - the confirmation email you’ll receive after registering has suggestions for signs and information on parking and public transportation. 

The goal of Support the Courts is to demonstrate to judges that there is tremendous public respect for their role and concern for their safety.  This clip from NBC Boston (https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/medford-support-judges-rally/3807461/) about their rally last September outside the Chevalier Theater in Medford provides insight into who they are, and why you might consider joining them in Providence. 

For more information, email [protectourjudges@gmail.com](mailto:protectourjudges@gmail.com) or contact them through their website [supportthecourts.org](https://supportthecourts.org/).

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Evergreen, Colorado

location.venue: Main St Intersection / Bridge, Downtown Evergreen

events.description:
GET OUT THE VOTE 🗳️ Please join your neighbors in highlighting the importance of voting in the upcoming midterm elections.

Please join your neighbors at the intersection / bridge in downtown Evergreen, to celebrate democracy!  As part of the national No Kings movement, we will rally to stand up to authoritarian overreach, and encourage our community to participate in the upcoming midterm elections.  This will be a joyous, peaceful event.  Signs and costumes are encouraged but not required.  Bring your voice and instruments ~ open mic will be provided for speakers, musicians, and chants.  Water, coffee, and hot cider will be provided by Cactus Jacks.  Optional potluck - bring snacks to share if you'd like.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **Evergreen** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Save Your Spot: Bus to Harrisburg, PA to flip the House!! - GW Dems & Swing Left GWU
events.description:
Join GW Dems and Swing Left GWU on a planned day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to PA-10—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Janelle Stelson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

events.description:
Join Hands Off Colorado for a literature drop! This is fast, easy, high-impact volunteer work: we're getting our materials onto as many doors as possible, and you don't need any experience.

Hands Off Colorado is a movement to protect our neighbors, including our trans and immigrant communities, from government overreach. A lit drop means walking a set route and leaving literature at each door. There's no knocking and no conversations, just a quick hit at every house. The more volunteers we have, the more doors we cover.

**What to expect:**

We'll meet up for a 10-minute orientation, so first-timers are welcome
You'll get a turf map or access to a list in MiniVAN, a stack of literature, and instructions for placing it at the door
Most shifts run about 2 hours, and you'll cover a lot of ground
Go solo or team up with a friend, whichever you prefer

**What to bring:**

Comfortable walking shoes
Water and weather-appropriate gear
A charged phone for navigating your route with MiniVAN App downloaded

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early -- Lyle WA
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

The road to winning The House runs through young voter turnout, and turnout depends on young people registered to vote. events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Sacramento, CA
events.description:
Now's your chance to Protect the Vote and help create a voting tsunami in November!!! No Kings: Vote Early!

Bring a picnic lunch, a chair, your ballot and friends to McKinley Park on Saturday Oct. 17 from 10 am - 12 pm.  We'll meet under the trees by H Street between Alhambra and 33rd.  Information  will be available about the CA propositions, our local elections, how we can protect the polls and our right to vote. Once we complete our ballots we will walk as a group to the drop box at McKinley Library to deposit our ballots. We'll video the event so we can all share it on our social media accounts.

And, for anyone not yet registered to vote,  there will be opportunities to register to vote, and then Vote EARLY!
 
Following  the event you will be armed with information about the propositions, how to check your voting status on Vote.org, and you can reach out to neighbors and friends to help them make a plan to vote! And they can VOTE EARLY too!

We can amplify our vote by sharing the message with 10 friends or neighbors, and they can each share with 10 friends.   Our vote is our voice.  HEAR US ROAR!!!!
*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. events.description:
Southwestern Pennsylvania deserves a representative who listens.

Join Alan Bradstock for an open Town Hall meeting, co-hosted with the University of Pittsburgh, Greensburg Campus College Democrats, where students and community members can ask questions, discuss the issues that matter most to them, and hear Alan's vision for the future of Pennsylvania's 14th Congressional District.

🕕 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
📍University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg
     Mary Lou Campana Chapel and Lecture Center, 
     150 Finoli Dr, Greensburg, PA. 15601

Alan Bradstock is a U.S. Army veteran, former FBI Special Agent, and lifelong public servant running for Congress to bring integrity, accountability, and common-sense leadership back to Washington.

events.description:
**Drive directly** to Wisconsin and knock some doors for Rebecca Cooke (WI-3) and Ben Gruber (State Assembly district 51)

We’re just weeks away from the crucial 2026 Midterm elections where we have a once in a generation shot at electing for substantial Democratic leadership. Together, we’ll defeat Donald Trump’s extremist agenda once and for all, but we’ll only succeed with your help. 

We'll see you in there!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will meet at Railroad Park Gazebo, E. Front St, Muscoda WI 53573. Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.title: Knock doors in Fresno for Randy Villegas
events.description:
CA-22 is a must-win seat if we are to flip the House in November and groups from around the Bay Area are coming together to send Randy Villegas to D.C.​ With the district changes put in place by Prop 50, the district is more competitive than ever before and is the very best use of your time.

Join the Bay Area Coalition​ and other Bay Area partners to go door-to-door talking to voters in Fresno using deep canvassing techniques such as active listening and spreading the word about Randy.

Support for carpooling from Santa Cruz is available and stipends and/or housing with local volunteers may be available for those for whom cost is a barrier. Cooling cars will support canvassers on hot days, and you'll get all the training you need to be successful.​

Sign up for one, two, three or four days of canvassing, depending on your preference. Alternate start times can be accommodated as needed.

Remember to bring comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, a well-powered smartphone, and a smile.

events.description:
Calling all activists in CALIFORNIA! There is still time to register young Democrats before the Nov 3 midterm elections!!!

It's time to take a stand against the cruelty, the fascism, the oligarchy.
It's time for us to defend our democracy – by expanding it!
It's time to hold a voter drive!

Every Democrat we register breathes new life into our dreams for a better world. And all it takes is talking to people and filling out a short form.

No experience necessary. We'll start with an inspiring 15-minute training and deploy to a high-traffic area nearby. We'll have clipboards, forms, pens, and stickers! Just bring a little water, sunscreen, some comfortable shoes, and maybe a hat.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early with ‘Galt x Neighbors’ of California
events.description:
🚫👑📢 Please join us as we rally the community, to gather and recall the histories and significance of our voting rights, stand up to those who wish to rule over us, call out the injustices around us, organize to bring power back to the people, and help everyone remember to **vote early!**

👀🗳️ Sign up to be a poll worker or find other ways, locally, to help protect the polls! 

💪☮️ Please keep in mind that this will be a themed, non-partisan rally (we immensely encourage you all to resist divisiveness and practice nonviolence together)!

🙏💕 We would also highly appreciate it your signs and “gear” match the theme of getting the vote out early and nonpartisan, or no kings, related frustrations and concerns. Personally, I look forward to everyone’s creativity on this, I’m excited and we hope you are too!

‼️💡It is a good idea to bring your own chair (or picnic blanket) if you’d like a spot to rest or sit. Sun umbrellas, hats, lotion and regular hydration are all encouraged!! The grass may be difficult to walk on for some people. 

🚻🧻 The library down the block has public restrooms; We are also located next to carls jr, taco bell, and starbucks (please make a purchase if using their bathroom)!

‼️🚑😷🤧 If you are feeling ill, feverish, or light-headed at all, please skip this event for your own safety and others’, and then come to a future local event soon, or stop by the next Galt’s Pints & Politics to learn about more events and opportunities near you! (Poll working and other poll protection opportunities are out there, also!)

🪧🚦If we have the shade and the stamina, let’s be on all corners of the intersection, and do mini-marches to and fro, legally!! (obey traffic laws and leave space for people to pass by on the sidewalk, safely)

We are all so excited to meet and rally with you!! Please stay safe and remain informed out there!! Let’s work together to keep the polls safe and get everyone out to vote! 🗳️

💕🦋🪧☮️📢🦋💕

## And last, but not least, a message from our awesome sponsor…

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

## Thank you!!

events.title: Coastside United Indivisible Community Meeting: Focus on Voting

location.venue: Little Brown Church, Pacifica Historical Society

events.description:
It’s time to save our Republic! Join us at our October Community Meeting and prepare to Vote!

**Making Sense of Your November Ballot**
A Ballot-Help Workshop

Bring your November ballot, sample ballot, or voter guide. We’ll spend some time together stepping through some of the more confusing propositions and measures, finding reliable nonpartisan information, and answering practical questions about voting. This portion of our meeting will be unbiased and nonpartisan. Our goal is simply to help folks better understand their ballots and make their own informed choices.

In addition, CUI Member Adrienne Gulyassy will share some thoughts on keeping our cool when political conversations get emotionally charged — stepping back from assumptions, finding common ground, and staying curious even when we strongly disagree.

Plus, we will discuss our local "rapid response plans" for whatever happens after the election.

This is a hybrid meeting, sign up for the Zoom link!

This a local Indivisible event put on by Coastside United Indivisible

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Final Friday Film: Mr. Smith Goes to Wshington

location.venue: North East Bexar County Democrats Campaign Office

events.description:
Mr. Smith Goes to Washington is a 1939 American political comedy-drama film directed by Frank Capra, starring Jean Arthur and James Stewart, and featuring Claude Rains and Edward Arnold. The film is about a naive, newly appointed United States senator who fights against government corruption, and was written by Sidney Buchman, based on Lewis R. Foster's unpublished story "The Gentleman from Montana".[4] It was loosely based on the life of Montana US Senator Burton K. Wheeler, who underwent a similar experience when he was investigating the Warren G. Harding administration's Teapot Dome scandal.[5][6]

The film was controversial in the US when it was first released, with attacks from many politicians claiming that it brought Washington into disrepute, but it was very successful at both the domestic and international box offices, and it made Stewart a major star.[7]

Mr. Smith Goes to Washington was nominated for eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor, winning Best Original Story.[8] Considered to be one of the greatest films of all time, the film was selected by the Library of Congress as one of the first 25 films for preservation in the United States National Film Registry in 1989, for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".[9][10]

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Geneseo, IL

address_lines: South Oakwood Avenue & South State Street

events.description:
Join 50501GeneseoIL to rally and remind people to vote early!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early, Northeast Johnson County
events.description:
Boots on the Ground Midwest will host rallies at each of the early voting locations in Johnson County, KS. Join us to bring attention to early voting and showing up for our democracy! More details to come!

Johnson County Northeast Offices, 6000 Lamar Ave, Mission KS 66202 

Sponsored by People for Prairie Village

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join Rural Arizona Engagement for a celebration of civic power, music, and community spirit!

**THE VIBE:**

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍 Yuma Children's Museum 

📅 Saturday, October 23rd  at 5:30 pm

**FEATURING:**

Come join Rural Arizona Engagement for a fun, family-friendly Party at the Polls in Downtown Yuma! Dress up as your favorite superhero character and enjoy an evening of community, activities, food, music, and fun!

🎨 Family activities & crafts
📸 Photo booth
🌮 Food & refreshments
🏢 Community organizations & resources
🗳️ General civic & voting information

 Join us for a voluntary community walk to the nearby polling location.

Come dressed as your favorite superhero and celebrate the power of community! 🦸‍♀️ 

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

**Any food, entertainment, buttons, stickers, or any other free items at this event are available to voters and non-voters alike. This is a nonpartisan event.**

events.title: Stop the Illegal War on Iran
events.description:
Join us on October 20 as we demand an end to the illegal war on Iran.
 
On October 20, 2026, two weeks before the midterm election, people across the country will rally at congressional district offices to demand an end to the illegal war on Iran -- to block funding, uphold war powers, investigate war crimes, and support a peace deal.
 
In Atlanta, we will be rallying on the 17th Street Bridge at Atlantic Station to make our voices heard to Senators Ossoff and Warnock that we demand they do more to stop this war. Specifically we are calling on them to:
 
*Pledge to oppose any defense appropriation or authorization spending that fails to end the war against Iran. This unauthorized war has killed schoolchildren and American service members, destroyed civilian neighborhoods and water treatment centers, and caused energy prices to skyrocket, wreaking havoc both for everyday Americans struggling to pay for gas and basic goods, and for people living in poverty around the world. If the President won’t listen to Congress when it directs him to stop this war, then Congress needs to use its power of the purse to cut off the funds.
 
*Release a statement affirming the legally binding nature of the Iran War Powers Resolutions and support future war powers resolutions. The founders of our country assigned the constitutional power to launch war to Congress, not leaving it up to one person. The House and Senate have both passed resolutions directing President Trump to terminate unauthorized hostilities against Iran. Members of Congress should use their position to enforce.
 
*Publicly push for the full release of the Department of Defense’s investigation into the U.S. bombing of the Minab Elementary School. It has been months since this strike tragically killed 120 children and dozens more teachers and staff, yet the Department of Defense has still not publicly released its promised investigation into the incident despite it being complete for weeks.
 
*Publicly call for and support a peace agreement, which will require lifting sanctions and unfreezing assets. Economic relief is a necessary component of securing verifiable nuclear concessions and long-term de-escalation. Everyday civilians bear the brunt of U.S. sanctions and freezing of public assets, with significant impacts on access to food, medicine, and basic economic stability. Congress should avoid measures that deepen this humanitarian harm or undermine diplomatic progress.
 
We must act now to stop the war machine. Join us and make your voice heard.

events.title: Spark - Let's Discuss Mis(Dis)insformation!
events.description:
**Let's Discuss  Mis- (and Dis-) information and Solutions - A 
Spark Discussion**

Let’s get together and discuss the problem of misinformation and disinformation and share solutions. How can we battle the river of manipulative lies? Can we prevent or identify disinformation? Who should be accountable? How can instances be debunked without amplifying them? How can we avoid falling victim ourselves? How will this issue change as social media develops?

An expert on this topic will give a brief history, examples on how to spot material meant to deceive us and how (or not) to respond to it. Then we’ll discuss aspects of it - bring your discussion questions and topics.

**No prior reading needed – just interest in talking about this topic.**

Here are some recommendations if you want more information:

**Websites (with links)**

- [Barrington Indivisible Truth Brigade Resources- Resources for Effective Communication](https://www.indivisiblebarrington.org/resources/truth-brigade#h.i68tkhhn1245)

- [Disinfo-Busters Persuasion through Education](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1g7KnhlJQWwUVa8ihE69-GZcG07ulMgoM/edit#heading=h.nefp513xyh7k)

- [University of Michigan Resource Guide “’Fake News’ and Misinformation”
Articles](https://guides.lib.umich.edu/c.php?g=283063&p=4471741)

**Articles**

- ["Why Do People Believe in Conspiracy Theories?” by David Ludden in Psychology Today.](https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/talking-apes/201801/why-do-people-believe-in-conspiracy-theories)

- ["Why Do People Believe in Conspiracy Theories?” by Shweta Mishra in www.scienceabc.com](https://www.scienceabc.com/social-science/why-do-people-believe-in-conspiracy-theories)

- ["Contemporary trends in psychological research on conspiracy beliefs. A systematic review” by Irena Pilch et al. in the NIH database](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9945548/#S3)

- ["Have beliefs in conspiracy theories increased over time?” by Joseph Uscinski et al.](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0270429)

**Books**

- **The Death of Truth** by Steven Brill
- **How to Stand Up to a Dictator** by Maria Ressa (on how the Philippines fell victim to social media)
- **The Chaos Machine** by Max Fisher (on social media)
- **How Minds Change** by David McRaney

Join us on Wednesday, October 28, from 7-8:30. We’ll be at the Barrington Area Library in the Zimmerman Room.


*The Barrington Area Library provides Meeting Room space as a community service. The Barrington Area Library neither sponsors nor endorses this event nor the presenting individuals or organizations.*

ATTENTION HAVERHILL RESIDENTS:  Come to Haverhill’s NO KINGS event on the 17th to stand out AND vote early! You can vote early at City Hall, 9am-3pm that day. Vote early before the stand out, during the stand out, or join others after the stand out to walk up to City Hall!  Look for our *We’re Voting Early Today!* banners on the blocks on Main St. alongside the Library and GAR Park to join others from Haverhill who will be voting early that day!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

From the No Kings Coalition:
For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensure every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Join us to write postcards for Democratic candidate JoAnna Mendoza, running to flip AZ's Congressional District 6 from #redtoblue!

In 2020, President Biden won the state by 10,457 votes—which means every single vote in the Grand Canyon state counts.

2026 is the year we flip the AZ state legislature and the U.S. Congress blue!

We are Oregon's Ground Zero. Many days, before 8 AM, another Woodburn parent has been detained and taken away.

On this No Kings Vote Early Day, stand with Woodburn in a show of support for our city's grieving families, and to make it clear to everyone, that despite all the intimidation and losses we've lived through lately, we are still going to vote, and we are still going to vote early.

On this fourth No Kings Day, as we stand up for the right to vote and to live in a democracy, please come stand with the people of Woodburn. On October 17, it may be the most important place you could stand in the state of Oregon to fight for the right to vote and live in a democracy, where voters make the decisions, not dictators or their masked agents.

Support our little city's effort to get out the vote despite all the adversity we currently are facing. Stand with Woodburn so everyone can see that we are unbowed, determined and not only ready to fill in our ballots, but we're ready to take our ballots to a ballot box early.

Oregon ballots arrive soon after Oct. 23 and Woodburn, Oregon is ready to vote early no matter what other challenges are happening around us. Come help us share that message on Oct. 17 from 10 AM to 1 PM.

Questions? Need Help? WoodburnIndivisible@Yahoo.com

events.description:
Join Mom Dog, Woven and Juniper Green at The Old School Farm for a screening of No Country For Mothers: a documentary that explores what motherhood really looks like in America today.

The film examines the culture wars surrounding motherhood and why labels like “girl boss” and “trad wife” ultimately distract from the bigger issue at play in our society: the lack of support for American families. The documentary traces a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win historic support. 

The screening will be followed by an open discussion, led by Maddie Adams (Matrescence Coach and founder of Mom Dog), Whitney Gorbett (owner of Woven Events), and Molly Martin (owner of Juniper Green and The Old School Farm).

DETAILS:

This al fresco film screening includes open conversation, food from Nashville food trucks, and drinks from The Old School Farm bar. BYO lawn chairs or picnic blankets to create a space where you and your friends can enjoy the evening together. 

Guests are welcome to bring their own picnic dinner, but please note that outside alcohol is prohibited.   

5:00PM - Food, drinks and mingling at The Old School Farm
6:30PM - Film screening, followed by conversation

This night isn’t just about watching a film. 

It’s about being in community with other mothers, linking arms with our sisters to form stronger connections, and saying the things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly — because maybe some of what we’ve been taught to carry privately was never meant to be carried alone.

Join us for this special evening:

Step 1) Sign up below to attend.

Step 2) Purchase your ticket here: https://www.mom-dog.com/all-events/ncfm

events.description:
Join Byberry Friends Monthly Meeting for an Interfaith, non-partisan Civic Day of Action 
Saturday October 10th from 2:00pm – 5:00pm

Sponsored by Quaker Call to Action, Power Interfaith, American Friends Service Committee and lead by Promote the Vote PA

Since 2024, Promote The Vote's Vote Navigator Team has been a vital part of the PA Election Protection Coalition.

In collaboration with the Election Protection Hotline, the ACLU, Common Cause PA and The Lawyer's Committee, Vote Navigators handle escalated cases where 1:1 assistance is needed to get the voter across the finish line.

Vote Navigators assist with: - Registration Issues - Mail Ballot Applications or Troubleshooting Coordinate rides to County Elections Office or Dropboxes - Coordinate Designated Agents for Mail Ballots or Emergency Ballots - Assist with Rapid Response Calls/Texts

Join us for training that will prepare you to volunteer with the Vote Navigators for the PA Midterms!

In-person volunteers are needed to assist with: rides to Election Office, Drop Box or Polls; or help with obtaining/returning a Mail Ballot or Emergency Ballot. We'll show you how! 

Navigators handle escalated cases, working one on one with voters to assist with things like registration issues, coordinating rides to cast votes, and securing designated agents for mail and emergency ballots, and rapid response. 

We will also have an opportunity to canvass the local neighborhood (weather permitting) and fill out postcards to encourage people to Vote on Election Day, Nov. 3, 2026

Refreshments provided. Join us for Unplug & Recharge Campfire After! (weather permitting)

Sign up Today!

ATTEND NK EARLY VOTE EVENTS IN THE AM AND THEN COME CANVASS AND HAND OUT EARLY VOTE FLYERS IN RENS COUNTY, NY 19!

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

**Winning this district, NY 19, is critical in order for us to retake the House.**

__PLEASE DON'T GHOST US!__

+ YOU MUST HAVE A PHONE WITH THE MIC ENABLED.  

__Your confirmation email from Mobilize will include important training materials that will need to be reviewed and acted on before the canvass!__

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

events.title: Postcards to Get Out The Vote in Ohio!

events.description:
We are in the home stretch to the midterms!!  It’s time to remind voters in key swing states of how important it is that they get out and vote!  Ohio is a critical swing state that can influence election outcomes, including control of the Senate and the House.  Volunteer written postcards to voters have been shown by numerous independent studies to increase turnout, especially among voters who may not consistently vote in midterms, by 0.4% to 1.5 % in randomized trials. Join old friends and make new ones, to write postcards to Ohio voters and encourage them to get out and vote. We’ll gather on Saturday, October 10 from 1 to 4 in Florence for postcard writing, snacking and chatting! events.title: MEET YOUR NEIGHBORS!!! Merritt Island
events.description:
Dan Cicirelli is running for State House in District 31. He grew up here, he's a handyman in Cocoa, and he spends part of every week doing free repairs for older folks who can't afford to pay for them. He's running because the people we keep sending to Tallahassee stopped paying attention to what it costs to live here, or whether you can find a doctor, or what's happening to the lagoon.

Here's the honest part: Dan doesn't win this unless a lot of us do this, a lot. If we don't get out there and talk to people, we don't win.

A FULLY Charged phone with the MiniVAN Application installed
Water
Sunscreen
More water

events.title: Blue Wave Bookworms - "The Nerd Reich" by Gil Durán
events.description:
Blue Wave Bookworms – Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 1:30 pm.   
 
Selection – The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy • NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER
“This transfixing debut from journalist Durán investigates the antidemocratic ideologies espoused by tech billionaires linked to the second Trump administration...It’s an ominous look at an insular elite arrayed against American democracy.” —Publishers Weekly (starred review)

When Silicon Valley says it is ‘‘moving fast and breaking things,’’ the world interprets the chaos as a necessary cost of innovation. Gil Durán reveals something far more sinister: a decades-long campaign to replace elected governments with corporate rule.

Drawing on insider political experience and new investigations, Durán traces this ideology from its philosophical roots in The Sovereign Individual by James Dale Davidson and Lord William Rees-Mogg. He introduces its modern apostles—Peter Thiel, Marc Andreessen, Balaji Srinivasan, and Elon Musk—and shows how the promise of technological liberation has transformed into a global movement for digital feudalism, powered by cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence, and the algorithmic propaganda of social media.

The Nerd Reich explains the origins, strategies, and ambitions of Silicon Valley’s war on democracy for the first time. From San Francisco’s weaponized elections and secret billionaire projects to the White House, Durán exposes how the world’s richest men are building a new political order.

The Nerd Reich is more than a hidden history, it’s an urgent warning: democracy is being dismantled not by coups or tanks, but by code, capital, and the illusion of innovation. Durán insists there is still time to fight back—if we act now.

events.title: Become a Great Canvasser: How to Build Bridges to Voting
events.description:
**Learn practical strategies for helping voters uncover their reasons to vote for Democrats.** 

Some conversations are easy: the voter supports your candidate, they’re ready to vote, and your job is pretty straightforward. But what happens when someone is undecided or conflicted—or tells you, “I don’t vote”?
 
Join veteran canvassers and trainers Elizabeth Chur—author of [The Joy of Talking Politics with Strangers](https://elizabethchur.com/)—and Carol Blaney for this interactive one-hour workshop. Whether you’re relatively new to canvassing or looking to up your game, you’ll learn practical strategies for navigating more challenging conversations.

Through real-life stories, demos, and practice, **you’ll learn how to ask great questions, listen with empathy, build trust, and discover what matters most to a voter.** Rather than jumping in with the “perfect” argument or a bunch of talking points, you’ll learn to listen for points of connection between a voter’s priorities and your candidate’s vision—and build on those connections to help people find their own reasons to vote for Democrats.

**Turn a knock on a stranger’s door into a bridge to voting. In razor-thin races, these conversations can bring in the votes we need to win.**

_By signing up for this event you are giving permission to be added to the Swing Left Peninsula email list. Our emails share timely, impactful actions (letter parties, phone banks, canvasses, voter registrations, and more) for strategic, toss-up races that will help us win back the House and other important races._

_Every email we send includes an unsubscribe link. If you don't want to be on our list, we want you to unsubscribe! (Please don't mark our emails as spam, or we will have trouble reaching the people who DO want to hear from us.) You won't be resubscribed by us._

events.title: Browning Meet and Greet with Sam Forstag and Rep. Sharice Davids
events.description:
Join congressional candidate Sam Forstag and Congresswoman Sharice Davids of Kansas for a meet & greet and community feed on Saturday, October 10 at 12:00 PM at the Browning Stick Game Arbor. Sam and Congresswoman Davids will be joined by State Senator Susan Webber and State Representative Thedis Crowe.

Congresswoman Davids is a citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and, in 2018, became one of the first two Native American women ever elected to Congress. Raised by a single mother who served in the Army, she worked her way through community college to law school and has spent her career fighting for working families, tribal sovereignty, and Native communities across the country. She's coming to Montana because she knows how important it is for Indian Country to have a true partner in Washington.

Sam is a smokejumper and union leader running for Congress to make sure working people have a voice in Washington. He'll talk about the fight for the housing, healthcare, and childcare Montana families deserve, his commitment to honoring tribal sovereignty and the federal government's treaty and trust responsibilities, and what he's seen firsthand fighting for public lands and the public servants who protect them.

This is your chance to hear directly from Sam, Congresswoman Davids, and your local legislators. Come ask your questions, learn how you can get involved in electing Sam, and take part in a real conversation about what matters to you, your family, and your community.

Elders, families, and young people are all welcome. A meal will be shared. Bring your questions, bring your relatives and neighbors, and come be part of the conversation.

Dan Cicirelli is running for State House in District 31. He grew up here, he's a handyman in Cocoa, and he spends part of every week doing free repairs for older folks who can't afford to pay for them. He's running because the people we keep sending to Tallahassee stopped paying attention to what it costs to live here, or whether you can find a doctor, or what's happening to the lagoon.

Team Cicirelli out in the neighborhoods every day, knocking on doors and having real conversations with people about who Dan is and why he's running. People remember when a neighbor shows up at their door. They don't remember a mailer.

Here's the honest part: Dan doesn't win this unless a lot of us do this, a lot. If we don't get out there and talk to people, we don't win.

You don't need any experience. We'll walk you through it in about ten minutes, pair you up with somebody, and send you out with a list on your phone. Walk a few blocks and talk to some neighbors.

WHAT TO BRING

A FULLY Charged phone with the MiniVAN Application installed
Water
Sunscreen
More water
WHAT TO WEAR: 
1. Wear plain clothes, or a Dan Cicirelli campaign shirt. 
2. Wear WORKOUT oriented clothing. Shorts, t-shirt/tank top. Something that says "I am walking up to 2 miles in the 90 degree Florida sun) 
3. Bring something to carry your water and literature with if possible. A small tote bag will do!

If walking isn't your thing, come anyway. We need people at the table checking folks in and people making calls.

Mail ballots start hitting mailboxes at the end of September, and every weekend between now and November 3 counts. Sign up, show up, and bring somebody with you.

RSVP TODAY and our organizers will be in touch with more details soon!

events.title: Signal 101: Stay Connected and Safe (Beginner-Friendly Zoom Training)
events.description:
Want to stay in the loop when our community needs to respond quickly? Join us on Zoom for a friendly, step-by-step introduction to **Signal**, the free and private messaging app that organizers use to share updates and rapid response alerts.

This training is made for beginners. We'll go slowly, do every step together, and have helpers ready if you get stuck. **No tech experience needed!**

## You'll learn

- Why Signal keeps your messages private and how our network uses it
- How to download Signal and set up your account
- How to keep your phone number private
- How to join our group chats so you receive alerts

## Please bring

- Your smartphone (charged)
- Your Apple ID or Google password for the app store
- A pen and paper

Join Zoom from a computer or tablet so your phone is free for the setup.

All questions are welcome. We'll make sure you leave connected!

events.title: Save Your Spot: Bus to Harrisburg, PA to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a planned day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to PA-10—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Janelle Stelson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

This trip is currently unconfirmed—we need to reach a threshold of 25 sign-ups by October 9 to make this bus a reality. **By signing up here, you are saving your spot and helping make this trip happen.**

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### Here is the plan:
- **Sign up now and help us reach our volunteer goal:** As soon as we hit 25 volunteers, we will confirm the bus, finalize the departure details, and reach out to you immediately.
- **Ready to roll:** Once confirmed, your bus captain will provide departure details, training, and the Ground Truth conversation guide.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave [Launch site] on [Date and time] and return around [Return time].
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly [Canvassing hours].
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. Can we count on you to help us get this bus on the road? Sign up today!

—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early BALDWIN PARK, CA. OVERPASS BRIGADE

location.venue: Food4Less to Kaiser Bridge: Highway 10 OVERPASS

events.description:
Join Indivisible Rise and Shine for an OVERPASS BRIGADE on No KINGS/ VOTE EARLY Day. We will be on the bridge that goes over highway 10 from the Food 4 Less to the Kaiser. We will be on the East Facing side for easy access, but the West facing side is also available if we have enough people. We will have some signs available, and some large signage for the fence. You may bring SMALL signs to face towards the bridge traffic or LARGE signs to face towards the HIGHWAY traffic. Flags, bubbles, whistles, percussion are all welcome. It will be early so you may want a sweater and sunscreen. Bring water! Bring Coffee!!!You may bring a chair if needed but be aware that there will be foot traffic on the bridge and it may be necessary to briefly move for passersby.

Park in the Food 4 Less Parking lot in the spaces closest to the highway (behind taco bell) and you will need to walk up the overpass to get to a spot where the traffic will see us. While the event is wheelchair accessible, it is only for intrepid wheelchair users, as the incline is a little steep. If you wish to join us but the walk is an impediment, you are welcome to protest at the bottom of the bridge on the street by the TACO BELL, Food 4 Less Parking lot area. It will ALL be meaningful. If you cannot do either, consider sharing the post or driving by and honking or filming! (tag #indivisbleriseandshine) Everyone can do SOMETHING! And together we are unstoppable

We have done the overpass brigade before at this spot and the CHP and Baldwin Park Police have arrived but have not tried to stop us or aggressively interacted as it is within our legal right to protest on the sidewalk in Baldwin Park and a permit is not needed. We have checked.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next. **

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Early Voting starts on October 15. This is our moment, Catawba County!

Join us for one final GOTV rally before the first votes are cast. We’ll get everyone plugged in, make sure our Early Voting operation is ready to go, and get the team fired up for the home stretch.

At this meeting, we’ll:

*Fill the gaps: Make sure Early Voting shifts at every site are covered.

*Get Election Day ready: Sign up for poll greeting shifts at precinct locations.

*Get signs where they need to go: Help distribute campaign signs to Early Voting sites.

*Hear the latest: Get updates on the Voter Toter program and other GOTV efforts.

*Get organized: Make sure you know where to be, what to do, and how to plug in.

events.title: Phone Banking with Common Cause NC in Mecklenburg County
events.description:
It's time to phone bank to make sure every voter's voice is heard, and we would love to have you join us! We can make a major difference for our democracy by working together!


Common Cause North Carolina will be phone banking this election cycle in Mecklenburg County!  Stand up by joining us in building a movement through phone banking and engaging with your community on voter education through distribution of non-partisan voting resources!
 
How does it work? Here are some highlights, but we will send you more details once you sign up.


You are never alone! For every phone banking shift, you will have a lead organizer who helps you navigate the shift. We will provide training for the first 15-20 mins. of every shift to go over the phone bank program and scripts, the list of areas and to answer any questions!  You will be able to join us from anywhere to phone bank with us! Phone banks will happen via zoom. You will receive zoom details for the phone banking shift once you sign up! 
 
Common Cause NC is a nonpartisan grassroots organization dedicated to upholding the core values of American democracy.  We work to create open, honest, and accountable government that serves the public interest; promote equal rights, opportunity, and representation for all; and empower all people to make their voices heard in the political process. 
 
All phone bank information and scripts will be non-partisan!

events.title: Knocking on Doors in East Lansing!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!


This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.


Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.


Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.


Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Main St, Stowe, VT
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

The November 3 General Election will determine who represents Vermonters in Congress, statewide offices, the Vermont Legislature and county offices. 
Vermont voters will also consider two proposed constitutional amendments.

Whatever your views, whatever your party—or no party at all—your vote is yours, and it matters.

Join us Saturday, October 17 at 3 PM at the Akeley Memorial Building in Stowe, Vermont.
🇺🇸 NONPARTISAN 🇺🇸 COMMUNITY EVENT CELEBRATING VOTING AND ENCOURAGING EVERYONE TO PARTICIPATE.

Bring a NONPARTISAN sign about voting if you’d like! Please, no candidate, party or issue signs. We want to keep the message simple: VOTE.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Celebrate the Vote No Kings
events.description:
Be an ambassador for early voting by joining this special No Kings event on October 17. This is a fun, family friendly event with live music, games, jugglers.  Costumes are encouraged to share your favorite Democracy super hero and join in the costumed conga line.  

This will not be a rally, but instead be a lawful, non violent gathering of people who have had enough of all the stress and just want to get on with more early voting and the biggest voter turnout ever.  

You may wonder why we are encouraging early voting so much. Early voting is the best way to protect your vote and make sure it counts.  You can register online for a mail in ballot before October 14 at MyVote.wi.gov.  Or you can vote early in person at your city clerk between October 20 and November 1.  Check with your local clerk for their days and open hours. 

Through this fun, we will be promoting early voting, voting with a friend and confirming your voter registration.  Tools to share with others will include your voting rights and protection, talking points, the three amendments, the best online resource and a hotline for any voter disruption.  

Did we mention that costumes are encouraged?   It’s time to have some fun and Celebrate the Vote.  

This event is coordinated by Fox Valley Indivisible. It will be a peaceful, friendly public gathering designed to build visibility, solidarity, and hope throughout Northeast Wisconsin.

Now the following message from our national No Kings organization: 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Additional Info: 
This is a fun, celebration event, not a rally.  You may see multiple No Kings events in the area also planned for October 17.
📢: How to Prepare for Your Event:
✅: Update your voter registration → https://www.vote.org/am-i-registered-to-vote/
✅: Recruit friends → We start in our own communities and neighborhoods, where voting happens. Triple your impact by inviting three people.
✅: Broaden your impact  → Post photos/videos with #NoKingsVoteEarly and encourage others to vote
This a local Indivisible event!



*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.description:
It's time to knock on doors to make sure every voter's voice is heard and we would love to have you join us! We can make a major difference for our democracy by working together!
Common Cause North Carolina will canvass Mecklenburg County this election cycle! Stand up by joining us in building a movement through canvassing and engaging with your neighbors face-to-face on voter education through the distribution of non-partisan voting resources!
How does it work? Here are some highlights, but we will send you more details once you sign up.
You are never alone! For every canvassing shift, a lead organizer will be on site to help you navigate the shift. We will provide training for the first 15-20 mins. of every shift at the canvassing location to go over the canvass program and scripts, your turf, and to answer any questions! You'll be paired up or in a small group, so no experience is needed.
What to bring: comfortable walking shoes, weather-appropriate clothing, a water bottle, and a fully charged phone. We'll provide all materials and resources.
Common Cause NC is a nonpartisan grassroots organization dedicated to upholding the core values of American democracy. We work to create open, honest, and accountable government that serves the public interest; promote equal rights, opportunity, and representation for all; and empower all people to make their voices heard in the political process.
All canvassing information and scripts will be non-partisan!

Charleston County & Lowcountry Democrats, here is your chance to hear from the Charleston-area and statewide Democratic candidates who will be on your 2026 Midterm Election ballot...and have some fun while doing it!

The 2026 MIDTERM BLUE JAMBOREE!
SUNDAY, OCTOBER 18th, 2026, 3:00 – 7:00 pm

Brittlebank Park: 185 Lockwood Drive, Charleston, SC 29403

We look forward to seeing all of you on Sunday, October 18th for the Charleston County Democratic Party 2026 MIDTERM BLUE JAMBOREE! Join us starting at 2:30pm…and let’s show the Lowcountry and the State what a Charleston-sized Blue Wave looks like!

events.title: NK Vote Early Safety Training
events.description:
Safety Training – October 10

To help make sure all of our October 17 events are safe, welcoming, and productive for everyone, we’ll hold safety team training on Saturday, October 10 at 2:00 PM at Rogers Park. We’ll meet in the parking lot next to the covered pavilion.

We strongly encourage all safety personnel from our satellite locations to attend. Having everyone working from the same basic plan will help our teams communicate effectively and respond confidently if an issue arises.

Training will cover:

* Pre-event preparation
* Safety roles during marches and rallies
* Basic first aid
* De-escalation
* Safety team communication and coordination

Please plan for at least one hour, and preferably about 90 minutes to allow time for questions and discussion.

Our goal isn’t to anticipate problems—it’s to be prepared, coordinated, and ready to help create an environment where everyone can participate safely and focus on why we’re gathering.

Thank you to everyone stepping up to serve in this important role. Your preparation helps make the entire event stronger.

events.description:
**Bus leaves from Mountain View!  You leave Saturday, October 10 at 7AM and return Sunday, October 11 by 7PM.  We can help with carpools to catch the Mountain View bus from other Bay Area locations!**

Sign up to knock doors in the Central Valley and help Flip the House in 2026!! Join Santa Clara County Democratic Party, Bay Area Coalition, and the Democratic Volunteer Center to knock doors in Porterville. Let's build the grassroots power Democrats need to elect Randy Villegas in 2026 and to defend democracy long term.

Why Porterville? Porterville has a critical 5,000 doors to be knocked to win this election!
Why October 10 & 11? Voters' ballots will have just have been received in the mail!

Drive yourself, join a carpool from Santa Cruz (subject to availability), or hop on the Canvassing Lux Bus from Mountain View... Let us know your preference! The bus will leave Saturday, October 10 at 7AM and return Sunday, October 11 by 7PM.

Once you've signed up, a volunteer will contact you and help with carpools, hotel options, and other details about the canvass event! Bring your personal items like comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, and a smile. We will be using PDI and so a well-powered smartphone is necessary.

This "Hop on the Bus" canvass will be a two day and one night canvass. Your canvassing concierge will coordinate carpools to catch the bus on Saturday morning, October 10 from the Democratic Volunteer Center in Mountain View. When you arrive in Porterville, local drivers will be standing by to take you to your canvassing turf. A community dinner will be coordinated, but canvassers will make their own hotel reservations with help from your canvassing concierge. Stipends of $100/day are available for lodging and food.

RSVP today and invite a friend to join us!

Never canvassed before or need a refresher? Join the Bay Area Coalition Yes, You Can(vass)! workshop on Tuesdays - https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/596490/

CA-22 is a must-win seat if we are to flip the House in November and groups from around the Bay Area are coming together to send Randy Villegas to D.C. As a result of redistricting, the district is more competitive than ever before. Join Swing Left East Bay, the Bay Area Coalition and other Bay Area partners to go door-to-door talking to voters in Fresno using deep canvassing techniques such as active listening and spreading the word about Randy.

The plan: carpool down Saturday morning, canvass in the afternoon, enjoy a group dinner, canvass again Sunday, and head home late Sunday afternoon. We’ll help coordinate rides and lodging. Support for carpooling from Santa Cruz is available and stipends and/or housing with local volunteers may be available for those for whom cost is a barrier. Cooling cars will support canvassers on hot days, and you'll get all the training you need to be successful.

Remember to bring comfy shoes, sunscreen, a hat, a well-powered smartphone, and a smile.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Fox Valley Wisconsin

address_lines: West College Avenue & South Appleton Street

events.description:
Be an ambassador for early voting by joining this special No Kings event on October 17. This is a fun, family friendly event with live music, games, jugglers.  Costumes are encouraged to share your favorite Democracy super hero and join in the costumed conga line.  

This will not be a rally, but instead be a lawful, non violent gathering of people who have had enough of all the stress and just want to get on with more early voting and the biggest voter turnout ever.  

You may wonder why we are encouraging early voting so much. Early voting is the best way to protect your vote and make sure it counts.  You can register online for a mail in ballot before October 14 at MyVote.wi.gov.  Or you can vote early in person at your city clerk between October 20 and November 1.  Check with your local clerk for their days and open hours. 

Through this fun, we will be promoting early voting, voting with a friend and confirming your voter registration.  Tools to share with others will include your voting rights and protection, talking points, the three amendments, the best online resource and a hotline for any voter disruption.  

Did we mention that costumes are encouraged?   It’s time to have some fun and Celebrate the Vote.  

This event is coordinated by Fox Valley Indivisible. It will be a peaceful, friendly public gathering designed to build visibility, solidarity, and hope throughout Northeast Wisconsin.

Now the following message from our national No Kings organization: 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Additional Info: 
This is a fun, celebration event, not a rally.  You may see multiple No Kings events in the area also planned for October 17.
📢: How to Prepare for Your Event:
✅: Update your voter registration → https://www.vote.org/am-i-registered-to-vote/
✅: Recruit friends → We start in our own communities and neighborhoods, where voting happens. Triple your impact by inviting three people.
✅: Broaden your impact  → Post photos/videos with #NoKingsVoteEarly and encourage others to vote

events.title: Join APEN for Votes + Vibes: Host Your Own Ballot Party!
events.description:
## Get tips on how to organize your friends and family to vote 

Good energy is contagious, so is voting. Host a dinner, cocktail hour, or low-key hangout with your friends and family, and help them get their vote in. The most persuasive voice in politics isn't a TV ad or a candidate – it's you. People trust the voters they already know: a neighbor, a coworker, a cousin. So bring your people together and turn that trust into votes. We'll give you the toolkit, you bring the playlist. Sign up to get some tips and learn how to organize your own party!

*Español

## Obtén consejos sobre cómo organizar a tus amigos y familia para votar

La buena energía es contagiosa, y votar también. Organiza una cena, un cóctel o una reunión relajada con tus amigos y familia, y ayúdalos a emitir su voto. La voz más persuasiva en la política no es un anuncio de televisión ni un candidato - eres tú. La gente confía en los votantes que ya conoce: un vecino, un compañero de trabajo, un primo. Así que reúne a tu gente y convierte esa confianza en votos. Nosotros te damos las herramientas, tú pones la música. ¡Inscríbete para recibir consejos y aprende cómo organizar tu propia reunión!

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Calling All Postcard Writing Champions!

You’ve shown time and again your pens can make a difference! Our Postcard Writing Champions have stepped up in election after election—from Sussex County races in 2024, to the August 2025 Special Election, the Virginia state elections in November 2025, and Alonna Berry’s primary in September 2026.

Now it’s time to pick up our pens again—and this time, we’re focusing right here at home!

On November 3, Sussex County voters will help decide important state and local races—and there is a lot at stake.

In the Delaware House, Democrats are working hard to reelect current representatives and gain additional seats. Gaining just one more seat will result in a super majority for Democrats. That threshold can be especially consequential as Delaware considers constitutional protections involving voting rights and reproductive freedom.

Here in Sussex County, voters will also elect members of Sussex County Council, where decisions about growth, development, land use, infrastructure, and the future of our communities are made.

Let’s make November a Blue Wave in Sussex County!

Candidates will provide the postcards, voter lists, messages, and stamps. All you need to bring is your enthusiasm and your scribing skills.
 
Every postcard is a personal connection with a voter. Every voter reached matters. And every one of us can play a part.

Join your fellow Postcard Writing Champions on October 11 and help us reach Sussex County voters—one postcard at a time!

Register to Join Our Postcard Writing Party!

This event will be in eastern Sussex County. For security purposes, the location of the event will be emailed to you after you register. If you do not receive a confirmation email, check your spam folder.

events.title: Ogden Lit Prep & Postcard Night
events.description:
Not ready to knock doors? This one's for you. ✉️

Every canvass starts with a stack of literature, and we need a lot of it to get ready for the final weeks before Election Day. Come hang out at the Ogden office and help us get it done! We'll bundle literature for our canvassers, staple rubber bands to door pieces so they hang right on doorknobs, and write postcards to Weber County voters reminding them their ballots are on the way.

No experience needed. It's easy, social work you can do while chatting with your neighbors. We'll have all the supplies, sample messages for your postcards, and snacks. Bring a friend, put on some music, and stay for as long as you'd like!

Every packet you put together goes out the door with a canvasser, and every postcard goes to a voter right here in Weber County, used in races that will be decided by razor thin margins of just a few hundred votes!
