events.title: No Kings: Vote Early in Farmville, Virginia
events.description:
Join us as we celebrate early voting in Virginia and the start of early weekend voting in Prince Edward County!  Information on when you can vote on the weekends in PEC as well as the regular early voting hours can be found here: https://www.co.prince-edward.va.us/files/assets/county/v/1/voter-reg/documents/public-notice-of-voting-locations-for-november-3-2026.pdf .  Come join us and make a plan for you and yours to vote.  Also come join us if you have already voted!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Your ballot's here. Let's vote early together. 🗳️

Bring your ballot to the Ogden office and we'll make it a party. We'll have poster board, markers, and snacks so you can make a sign, plus a table where you can fill out and sign your ballot with friends.

Then we'll head downtown together to join No Kings: Vote Early at the Ogden Municipal Building, a nonpartisan community event helping every eligible voter make a plan to vote early.

Quick tip: don't forget to sign your ballot envelope! An unsigned envelope is one of the most common reasons ballots get rejected, so we'll have reminders at every table. Your ballot stays in your hands the whole time, and how you vote is always your own business.

Don't have your ballot yet, or already voted? Come anyway! Make a sign and join us.

10:30 AM: Sign making and ballot signing at the office

events.description:
_Here's what we've done:_ Down Jersey Coalition has created a **NO KINGS:  VOTE EARLY** flyer full of important information for NJ voters. 

_Here's what we hope you'll do:_  Please join us in our **MASS DISTRIBUTION** of this important voter information across Bridgeton!  Gather a friend or a few friends in your car, stop by our Bridgeton meeting location “hub” to pick up a stack of **NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY** flyers on Saturday, October 17th, pick a Bridgeton area destination (a festival, a neighborhood, a shopping center, a sporting event, or elsewhere) and head out together to distribute the flyers to the people you meet, your friends, your neighbors!  Help spread the word that the election is ahead and it’s important to make a plan to vote!  This year, it is particularly important to try to get your vote in early!  
_OPTIONAL:_  Once your flyers are distributed, consider stopping at an intersection with your *NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY* signs, flags, and noisemakers to spread the word to those passing by.  Want to dress like a frog or something else? You do you! 

In Bridgeton, we will have two flyer distribution shifts, as follows:  

SHIFT 1:  10-12:30 (the LAST half hour is spent with others at the “hub”, sharing your stories and getting to know like-minded people. 

SHIFT 2:  12-2:30 (the FIRST half hour is spent with others at the “hub”, hearing stories from the first shift and getting to know like-minded people.)

*IMPORTANT:*  
_Exactly where will you distribute flyers?_  When you arrive at the “hub”, you can tell us where you want to go, or we can help you decide so there won’t be overlap.  
_Does my friend have to sign up?_ Yes.  Please be sure EVERY person in your group signs up separately on mobilize.  We will print and distribute flyers based on the number of participants who sign up on mobilize.  Contact the host to make other arrangements.  

*Additional notes:* 
- Participants attend at their own risk.  Always keep safety in mind. 
- Local and national organizers are not responsible for personal injury or property damage.  
- While this event is adjacent to a local retailer, the retailer is not a sponsor of this event. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

events.title: Become a Great Canvasser: How to Build Bridges to Voting - PACIFIC TIME
events.description:
Some doors are easy: the voter supports your candidate, they’re ready to vote, and your job is pretty straightforward. But what happens when someone is undecided or conflicted—or tells you, “I don’t vote”?

Join veteran canvassers and trainers Elizabeth Chur—author of *[The Joy of Talking Politics with Strangers](https://elizabethchur.com/)* — and Carol Blaney for this interactive one-hour workshop. Whether you’re relatively new to canvassing or looking to up your game, you’ll learn practical strategies for navigating more challenging conversations.

Through real-life stories, demos, and practice, you’ll learn how to ask great questions, listen with empathy, build trust, and discover what matters most to a voter. Rather than jumping in with the “perfect” argument or a bunch of talking points, you’ll learn to listen for points of connection between a voter’s priorities and your candidate’s vision—and build on those connections to help people find their own reasons to vote for Democrats.

 A knock on a stranger’s door can become a bridge to voting. And in a razor-thin election, conversations like these can add up to the votes we need to win.

events.title: Dialing Days - Southern NV Union Member Phonebank
events.description:
Join the Nevada Labor movement to call fellow union brothers and sisters across the state in support of Labor endorsed, pro-worker candidates. 

Our phone bank event is a part of our grassroots member-to-member program informing fellow union members and their families of the candidates who earned labor’s endorsement — and why they earned it. We rely on union members to talk to fellow union members about these candidates so we can elect leaders who will fight to defend our contracts, our wages, and our ability to come together. 

Don’t worry if phones make you nervous; this event is for first timers and seasoned phone bankers alike and training is available at the start of the event. Our power comes from learning and working together. We will be thrilled to have you participate and will be there to support you throughout the entire event. 

All you need to participate remotely is a computer and a phone (headphones are helpful, but not required).  For those participating in-person, phones and computers will be provided. 

Together, we can help elect leaders who will fight for working families and build a stronger Nevada.

Join us online via Zoom or in-person at the NV AFL-CIO office.

events.title: 2026 Save Our Squares

address_lines: East Seminary Street & Buchanan Trail West

events.description:
Save Our Squares!

Save Our Squares is a peaceful protest held in a borough square of Franklin County each Saturday. Join us from 12-1pm as we maintain a presence on sidewalks with homemade signs warning others of the destructive activities taking place in our local, state, and federal governments. No sign? No problem! We have plenty with varied messages you may borrow.

Each protest doubles as a mutual aid event. IF you are able, please consider bringing non-perishable food to be donated to SCCAP food banks. No donation? No problem, there's always next time!

Dress for the weather! Our activists are dedicated to showing up for our democracy despite outside conditions. 

Don't have an hour? Can't stand that long? Not comfortable protesting yet? Be an ENERGIZER ACTIVIST. Drive through the protest area and honk your horn. Go around the block & do it again! This really energizes the crowd!

See you in the square!

events.title: Early Voting Hot Tips & What’s on the Ballot Training
events.description:
### Early Voting Hot Tips & What’s on the Ballot

We invite you to join Democracy NC on October 14 at 6:00 PM for a free virtual webinar with practical, hot tips for voting and everything you need to feel ready for the 2026 election.

- 🗓 **Wednesday, October 14, 2026**
- ⏰ **6:00–7:30 PM**
- 📍 **Online (Zoom)**

Hosted by Desmera Gatewood and Deputy Director Kyle Brazile, we’ll help you understand your voting options, know what to expect, and make a plan to cast your ballot.

We’ll cover:

- Voting options and important dates
- Voter registration, including same-day registration
- Photo ID requirements and what to expect when you vote
- What’s on the 2026 ballot, including the constitutional amendments
- How to make a voting plan and find trusted, reliable help
- How Democracy NC works to protect voters and defend the freedom to vote

We’ll also spotlight community organizations doing this work across North Carolina and make time for your questions during a live Q&A.

Whether you’re voting for the first time or just need a refresher, join us for hot tips, helpful information, and a chance to get ready to vote.

Bring your questions, make your plan, and invite a friend!

***Democracy North Carolina is a nonpartisan organization. We don’t support or oppose candidates or political parties. Our role is to make sure voters have the trusted, nonpartisan information.***

location.venue: Public area adjacent to South end of Walmart Supercenter, near Landis Ave.

events.description:
_Here's what we've done:_ Down Jersey Coalition has created a **NO KINGS:  VOTE EARLY** flyer full of important information for NJ voters. 

_Here's what we hope you'll do:_  Please join us in our **MASS DISTRIBUTION** of this important voter information across Vineland!  Gather a friend or a few friends in your car, stop by our Vineland meeting location “hub” to pick up a stack of **NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY** flyers on Saturday, October 17th, pick a Vineland area destination (a festival, a neighborhood, a shopping center, a sporting event, or elsewhere) and head out together to distribute the flyers to the people you meet, your friends, your neighbors!  Help spread the word that the election is ahead and it’s important to make a plan to vote!  This year, it is particularly important to try to get your vote in early!  

_OPTIONAL:_  Once your flyers are distributed, consider stopping at an intersection with your *NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY* signs, flags, and noisemakers to spread the word to those passing by.  Want to dress like a frog or something else? You do you!  

In Vineland, we will have two flyer distribution shifts, as follows:  

SHIFT 1:  10-12:30 (the LAST half hour is spent with others at the “hub”, sharing your stories and getting to know like-minded people. 

SHIFT 2:  12-2:30 (the FIRST half hour is spent with others at the “hub”, hearing stories from the first shift and getting to know like-minded people.)

*IMPORTANT:*  
_Exactly where will you distribute flyers?_  When you arrive at the “hub”, you can tell us where you want to go, or we can help you decide so there won’t be overlap.  
_Does my friend have to sign up?_ Yes.  Please be sure EVERY person in your group signs up separately on mobilize.  We will print and distribute flyers based on the number of participants who sign up on mobilize.  Contact the host to make other arrangements.  

*Additional notes:* 
- Participants attend at their own risk.  Always keep safety in mind. 
- Local and national organizers are not responsible for personal injury or property damage.  
- While this event is adjacent to a local retailer, the retailer is not a sponsor of this event.

events.title: Knock on Doors with EDF Action in Troy!
events.description:
Join One Team Michigan and EDF Action to talk with voters in your community about the issues that matter most!

This fall, Michigan picks a new Governor, a new U.S. Senator, and the officials who run our elections and enforce our laws — and the doors we knock now are how we win in November. We'll be talking with voters about our values as Democrats and about the team that will fight for them: Jocelyn Benson for Governor, Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate, Garlin Gilchrist II for Secretary of State, and Eli Savit for Attorney General.

Whether this is your first time knocking doors or you're a seasoned pro, we'll provide plenty of training and all the materials you need to feel comfortable and confident. You'll get a walk list, a quick run-through of the script, and everything you need to hit the doors.

Just like the post office, we talk to voters rain or shine — so come prepared with weather-appropriate clothing, your best walking shoes, and a fully charged phone.

Every conversation builds momentum, and every door brings us closer to victory. We can't wait to see you out there!

events.title: Team Massachusetts Canvass in Sudbury
events.description:
The Healey-Driscoll Campaign is launching a series of coordinated door-knocking canvasses across the Commonwealth to reelect Governor Healey, Lt. Governor Driscoll, Senator Ed Markey, candidate for State Representative Ravi Simon, and Democrats up and down the ballot.

Join us for the Sudbury Canvass in the final weeks before Election Day, with Team Simon. We're building the grassroots organizing effort that will power Democratic victories across Massachusetts, and we want you to be a part of it. Together, we'll have conversations with voters, identify supporters, and help make sure they have a plan to vote this November.

We'll begin with a brief training, where you'll receive your turf, materials, and everything you need to hit the doors with confidence. Whether it's your first time canvassing or your hundredth, we'll make sure you have the tools and support you need.

Electing Governor Healey, Lt. Governor Driscoll, candidate for State Rep. Ravi Simon, and Democrats up and down the ballot is how we continue delivering results for Massachusetts. We need all hands on deck.

We can't wait to see you there!

events.title: Biggest Little Action Group: October Planning Meetings
events.description:
Join us to discuss alternatives to the usual protests. If you're tired of standing on sidewalks waving signs at cars, we plan and perform meaningful actions designed to encourage and strengthen each other in opposition to fascism.

Some actions we've done include displaying portraits of the victims of ICE disappearances at the federal courthouse and at Reno's baseball stadium; creating and distributing Know Your Rights information to interstate passengers on Greyhound and Amtrak; calling for citizens to make public comment at the Board of Commissioners meeting to testify against the cooperation between ICE and the county jail; and displaying antifascist messages over I-80 during rush hour. Some of our members are involved in long-term campaigns like the Northern Nevada Community Defense Hotline, counting ICE hostages as they board deportation flights, local data-center issues, and banning ALPRs from our area. We do as much as we can and welcome new ideas and new members all the time.

We are nonviolent and non-vandalizing. We work in support of democracy and the Constitution, and against the fascist actions of the Trump administration, its supporters, and its enablers. Everyone can play a role in this fight. Come and see if you like our style.

events.title: Phone Bank Party in Woodacre

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Come phone bank with your neighbors, friends and SURJ!##

We are now in a decisive phase of the fight against authoritarianism, the threat is real and the stakes are high. And people are fighting back. Millions have protested, and we've watched powerful organizing coming out of Minneapolis, Chicago, and other cities that have borne the brunt of ICE's assaults on our communities. Mass anger exists, but mass organization does not yet exist at the scale needed to win. Movements become real when they reach millions: organized, trained, and acting together.

The stage for the midterm elections is set, and the stakes for our movement and democracy couldn't be higher.

**Join SURJ in doing our part to help flip the House and Senate and block MAGA while sending a crop of true movement champions to Congress.**

Come as you are! No experience needed! Full training & lots of support included!

## Logistics:##

- We're gathering to phone bank together at the address for this event (sent via email when you register). 
- You will log into a program with a script on your computer and bring your phone to make the calls (if you only have one device, still come!).
We have a robust training to give you all the information you need  — a script, technical support, and coaching throughout.
- People who have phone banked with SURJ before (Returners) can start early.
- You will receive an email with orientation materials ahead of time.

## Feeling Unsure?## 

- Our model works - learn from the best! Our phone banks have one of the highest rates of success in the country. No matter whether you're brand new caller or a seasoned organizer, if you join our banks, you can trust that you are putting your effort into a method that works. And you'll get to learn powerful organizing skills from seasoned leaders!
- Our conversations are based on open-ended questions and deep listening. You do not need to be an expert on the issues or a candidate - our phone banks are successful because we deeply connect with voters and make them feel heard.
- Want to hear what a phone bank is like? Ask your host to talk about their experience!

## Context:## 

As Trump and republicans defund the social safety net and peddle more racist lies, millions of people are increasingly feeling the effects of the billionaire agenda. We know this fight is on multiple fronts, and this fall we have an opportunity to harness the energy of the streets and rising resentment towards November’s elections – to not only wrest power from MAGA, but to put candidates in office who are willing to stand up to Trump and fight for working class people. BOTH the House AND Senate are in play for Democrats to take back control and this year we aim to put progressive working class champions in a position to WIN.

For the last six years, SURJ’s phone banking program has grown to be one of the strongest in the country, reaching millions of working class people with our vision of finding our shared interest in standing alongside people of color and rejecting white supremacy. This year is an opportunity to deliver strategic blows to the MAGA agenda and throw down a gauntlet to force the Democratic Party to reckon with true progressive, working class fighters.

To do this, protecting or flipping key Senate seats in North Carolina, Georgia, Maine and Mississippi and flipping critical house seats in Michigan 7, Tennessee 9 and California 22.

These races will affect millions of working class people this year. Riding the high from many wins for progressive champions throughout primary season, we are well positioned to send some of these same folks to the halls of Congress. We will continue to build power to stop MAGA, by supporting unapologetically progressive working class champions, while showing up in key races to block MAGA and showing up in solidarity alongside Black racial justice leaders in the south who are fighting back and beginning the long-build back from the gutting of the VRA. Alongside our partners across the country, this is the time for our movements to offer a bold vision and bring our people into it.

### About SURJ:### 

Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ) is the largest organization in the country that explicitly organizes white communities for justice. Instead of choosing racism, silence, or complicity, we help white communities choose justice. We have thousands of national members and 150+ chapters across the US and Canada.

events.title: 10/24 - Voter Mobilization & Get Out the VOTE - Sand Branch, TX
events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift in **Sand Branch, TX**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with voters during a _Get Out the Vote_ effort in the community
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone!

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[10:00am - 10:30am]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **[11:00am - 2:00pm] Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members and get folks set up on Reach. _After the event concludes, voters will team up in the community to caravan separately to early vote._

- **[2:00pm - 2:30pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.description:
Please join us on Monday, October 12th, 6:30 pm, at Presentation Hall in the Kilaga Springs Lodge for a screening of "Moms Club," an eye opening documentary about how our local school boards can become ground zero for much bigger political battles.  

"Moms Club" reveals how well-funded Christian nationalist groups - including the Heritage Foundation, Kock network, and DeVos family - can bring national political battles into small communities, fueling conflicts over LGBTQ+ rights, race, books and public education.

After the screening, there will be Q&A with the film's director and several of the Moms who championed the cause to keep extremism out of their school systems.

The United for ALL Students Coalition endorsed candidates for the Western Placer Unified School District board - A. Marioni, L. Cox, and M. Roskiewicz - will be present to discuss how they will lead our school system to prioritize students and teachers, not culture war issues.  

"Moms Club" tells a powerful story about democracy, inclusion and community - and the future of our children.  You don't want to miss this event!

On October 20th, thousands of people across the country will walk out to demand a freeze on AI development. With AI threatening our jobs, our safety, and our democracy, now is the time for a **people’s movement** to ensure all of us – not just a handful of Silicon Valley billionaires – have the say we deserve in our future. 

**Join us on October 20 at 1pm at the MA State House for the Freeze AI Walkout!** We’ll gather with fellow students, professors, workers, community members, and allies, with speakers sharing their testimony about how unregulated AI has impacted our lives, jobs, communities, and futures – and we’ll call for an immediate freeze on AI development. Because we the people deserve a **say, a stake, and basic safety** in the future of this dangerous, powerful technology.

Dozens of cities across the country will be walking out at the same time with us, to make sure Congress feels the pressure leading up election day! Now is the time to take action!

Bring your signs and your friends!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early WEHO-Fairfax Indivisible
events.description:
Join us to encourage people in the area to vote early. Bring your own signs OR make them with us (11am start time)! 
We will share basic CA voting information.
Fill out your ballot and walk with us (1pm start time) to the West Hollywood City Hall Ballot Box. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Knock on doors with Digital Ground Game and Ground Truth in Bristol (PA-01)!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Digital Ground Game and Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. 

There will be a morning shift, then lunch, followed by an afternoon shift. If you don't have a full day, feel free to participate in the shift you have time for.

We can flip PA-01 blue and replace Brian Fitzpatrick with **Bob Harvie**. Additionally, there's a real chance that PA Dems can win a trifecta for the first time since 1993. PA Republicans last had a trifecta 2011, which lasted until 2014 and caused a lot of problems that PA is now facing. If PA Dems win a trifecta this year they can raise minimum wage, secure stable funding sources for SEPTA and PRT, start much needed repairs and upgrades on rural highways and roads, and many more things. 

For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: AZ-01 GOTV Text Bank
events.description:
AZ-01 Weekly Text Bank, Every Monday

Join us as we text Arizona voters to help them return their mail ballots and make a final plan to vote before the November 3 general election.

Every week we reach voters across Arizona so they're ready to take part in one of the most competitive House races in the country. These are high-stakes elections, and turnout will decide who wins. We're making sure no voter is left behind.

We'll text voters who usually skip midterm elections to remind them of key deadlines and help them make a clear, confident plan to vote: by mail, early in person, or on Election Day. We'll also send voters who plan to vote early or on Election Day the information they need, including early voting sites, polling locations, and how to track their mail ballot.

Volunteers will have real one-on-one conversations with voters by text, answer their questions, and help turn intention into action so ballots get returned and votes get counted.

💬 Weekly text bank: Mondays at 6 p.m. PT (every week through Election Day)
🔥 No experience needed. All you need is a laptop. We provide training, scripts, and support.

Close races are won by making sure every vote counts. Your text could be the reason someone follows through. Sign up now and help power turnout in Arizona!

events.title: Win a Working Families Majority Phonebank
events.description:
# Phonebank to Take Back the People's House for Working People in November! 

Join People's Action Power and Team '26, a coalition of movement organizations across the country, to reach the working-class voters in must-win Congressional and Senate races that will decide who controls Congress -- and whether we save our democracy. 

## 📞Phonebank Schedule: 

###  🚒 Pennsylvania Tuesdays: Bob Brooks for Congress (PA-7)
A 20-year Bethlehem firefighter and former president of the firefighters' union, who fought a ten-year battle to win mental health coverage for his crew. He's taking on Ryan Mackenzie, who voted to cut healthcare for his own neighbors and constituents while cutting taxes for billionaires. 

### 🏥 Michigan Thursdays: Will Lawrence for Congress, MI-7, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate 

- Will Lawrence is the Sunrise Movement co-founder who helped win the largest green jobs program in US history and delivered hundreds of millions to Mid-Michigan. He co-founded Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High to win statewide renter protections. 

- Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a medical doctor who realized broken politics was making people sick, and he went to work fixing government: rebuilt Detroit's Health Department after bankruptcy, got lead out of the schools, and canceled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. He wrote the book on Medicare for All, and now, he's going to the Senate to make government work for you, not billionaires. 
 
The message from the primary season was loud and clear: Working Families candidates are winning. Working people aren't settling for just any candidate. They're demanding Movement Champions who answer to them, not big corporations and big money. 

Are you fired up? Sign up for the shifts leading up to Election Day. Share this link widely with your friends and family. 

No prior experience is required to join this phone bank. A laptop or tablet is recommended.

Let's go! Let's take back the People's House.

events.title: CANCELLED DUE TO WEATHER—Canvass Launch
events.description:

events.title: Boston ICE Tea Party 2.0
events.description:
Join the Boston ICE Tea Party 2.0!

We call upon all patriots to join us again on Dec 12th, 2026 for the second Boston ICE Tea Party on the ​​250th anniversary of our nation’s founding, to retrace the footsteps of this historic protest and declare once more - America has No Kings!

We will gather at 7:00pm at the Irish Famine Memorial Plaza, across the Old South Meeting House. We will march to Waterfront Plaza, by the Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum. And we will dump ice into Boston Harbor, to declare loud and clear: No Kings! No Tariffs! No ICE!

There will be clean ice provided for dumping. Please do not bring your own ice.

For over 250 years, Bostonians have refused to bow down to tyranny. When King George III forced soldiers into Boston’s streets, levied unjust taxes on imported tea, and refused to hear the people’s voices, the colonial patriots took a stand. On December 16, 1773, hundreds of colonists hurled tea into Boston Harbor in protest of King George’s tyranny, in what some call the single most important event leading up to the American Revolution.

Today, a President who behaves like a king occupies the White House. He has sent ICE to harass our city and kidnap our friends, families, and neighbors. He has levied unjust tariffs, and made our tea, our groceries, and our lives more expensive. Let us rise together once more to take down tyranny!

This a local Indivisible event!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: In the Name of Humanity: Who—and What—Are We Fighting For?

Join faith leaders and Refuse Fascism to delve into: What changes when humanity—not nation or self-interest is our compass, and what does it really mean to “refuse to accept” fascism? This webinar will grapple with the  moral grounding—and the political power—of the principle “In the Name of Humanity, We Refuse to Accept a Fascist America” and how the refusal of millions can drive the Trump fascist regime from power.

Through the weeks leading up to Election Day, join Refuse Fascism for a series of urgent conversations about what we are up against, what we are fighting for, how we stand together against fascist repression, and what it will take for millions to become a sustained, nonviolent force capable of compelling the removal of the Trump fascist regime.

A step too far by the regime—including an attempt to steal the elections—could awaken a sleeping giant, with millions pouring into the streets in sustained, determined, nonviolent resistance.

If that moment comes, will there be a force demanding—and settling for nothing less than—the removal of the Trump Fascist Regime?

events.title: November 9 Meeting of Bellaire/Braeswood and West U Area Dems with Jeremy Wallace
events.description:
Come join the Bellaire/Braeswood Democrats and the West University Area Democrats at the November 9, 2026 meeting with Jeremy Wallace of the Houston Chronicle.  Jeremy will analyze what just happened on November 3rd and what to expect will happen going forward because of the results.

Jeremy Wallace has covered politics and campaigns for more than 20 years. Before joining the Hearst Texas newspapers in 2017, he covered government and politics for the Tampa Bay Times, The Miami Herald and the Sarasota Herald-Tribune. Previously he covered Congress for the Boston Globe and Detroit Free-Press. Originally from San Antonio, he attended the University of North Texas and earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Missouri.

Jeremy also authors the Texas Take with Jeremy Wallace newsletter, where he shares insights from inside the Capitol.  Work on the Texas Take has him frequently on CNN, PBS, BBC America, MSNBC and statewide NPR stations.

Social time: 6:30 - 7:00 pm. Business time: 7:00 - 8:00 pm
Location: West University Community Center at 6104 Auden St. 77005

events.title: District 2 Neighbors Indivisible Monthly Meeting
events.description:
### This is our regularly-scheduled monthly meeting which takes place on the 4th Saturday of every month unless otherwise noticed.  

We are an extraordinary community of ordinary people in Portland City Council District 2, working together for justice, democracy, a fair economy, and the civil rights of all. Join us monthly to connect and plan good trouble together.

Our mutual aid group invites you to bring a pantry item or two with you to each monthly meeting. We'll share the items with families whose safety is at risk.  It's an easy way to show our collective support! Desired items include: rice, dried pintos or black beans, canned protein (e.g., chicken, tuna, etc.), masa, condensed milk, vegetable oil, baby food, and diapers (sizes, 2, 4, 6, 7).

🥐 Oh, yeah, and baked goods are always welcome for the coffee break! 

### 📣 Ain't no power like the power of the people, 'cause the power of the people don't stop! 📣

events.title: Hispanic Council Meeting
events.description:
Join us to celebrate the closing of Hispanic Heritage Month with a special virtual town hall featuring Congresswoman Delia Ramirez (IL-03). Hosted by the South Carolina Democratic Party Council of Hispanic Democrats and the High School Democrats of America (HSDA) Latino Caucus, this event offers a unique opportunity to engage with a trailblazing leader.

Congresswoman Ramirez, the first Latina elected to Congress from Illinois and the Midwest, will share her insights on key national issues. She currently serves on the House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, where she acts as the Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations. 

As the only member of Congress from a mixed-status family, Congresswoman Ramirez is a powerful voice for comprehensive immigration reform and a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers. Drawing on her extensive background in the nonprofit sector and her dedicated record of public service, she continues to champion critical issues including affordable housing, accessible healthcare, climate justice, and workers' rights.

Don't miss this opportunity to hear from a visionary leader and connect with organizers working to build a stronger, more inclusive future. Please sign up to receive the meeting link and join us for this important conversation.

events.title: Join us for a Glean in Mt. Dora, FL! (Multiple Dates)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Great Scott Farms is graciously extending a field to harvest fresh produce for families in need. This is a great way to way to give back, enjoy the outdoors, and share in meaningful community service.

All are welcome! The more hands we have to help- the more produce we can recover. 

🌱 What to Bring:

✅ Closed-toe shoes (required)

✅ Comfortable clothing that can get messy

✅ Hat, sunscreen, and gloves (optional but helpful)

✅ A reusable water bottle to stay hydrated

📢 RSVP or Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen
📞 (863) 224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is gleaning?

- Gleaning is collecting leftover crops from farms that would otherwise go to waste. These fresh fruits and vegetables are then donated to food banks and hunger relief groups.

#### 2. Who can attend?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve. (Kids must be with an adult.)

#### 3. Are tools provided?
- Yes! We’ll supply any tools and bags you’ll need to glean.

#### 4. What if it rains?

- We’ll monitor the weather and let you know if anything changes. Safety first!

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need. If you are an organization in need - reach out to the event coordinator to become a recipient. 

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates, visit: https://www.mobilize.us/endhunger/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets

events.description:
Join the League of Women Voters of Connecticut and LWV New Haven for a nonpartisan door-to-door canvass to empower our community and ensure every eligible voter’s voice is heard!

With key elections approaching, we are knocking on doors across New Haven to make sure our neighbors are fully prepared to cast their ballots by November 3rd. Whether you are a seasoned canvasser or taking to the doors for the first time, we will provide the training and materials you need to make an impact.

What We’ll Be Doing:

Voter Education: Sharing clear, trusted details on voting options, key dates, and election procedures in Connecticut.

Voter Empowerment: Helping community members make a concrete plan to participate on or before November 3rd.

Answering Questions: Helping voters check their voter status, locate their local polling information, and navigate general voter resources like VOTE411.org.

Schedule & Agenda:

1:00 PM: Welcome & Canvass Training: We will kick off with brief nonpartisan messaging training, review route assignments, pair experienced canvassers with new canvassers, and walk through our canvassing app.

1:30 PM | Door-to-Door Canvassing: Pairs will head out to assigned New Haven neighborhoods to engage local voters.

3:30 PM – 4:00 PM | Debrief & Material Return: Gather back at our starting hub to drop off materials and share stories.

How to Prepare:

What to Wear: Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing.

What to Bring: A fully charged smartphone, a water bottle, and a friend!

The League of Women Voters is a strictly nonpartisan organization that encourages informed and active participation in government. We do not support or oppose candidates or political parties.

Starting Wednesday, October 14, Navajo County begins verifying signatures and counting early ballots, and we need eyes in the room to make sure every ballot is handled correctly and counted.

events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Trenton and Princeton Meetings to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On October 10 at 12 noon we will gather at Burlington Meeting House for 45 minutes of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Share Mark Pinsley's videos (Easy!)
events.description:
Democrats have not controlled the Pennsylvania Senate for three decades. Their path to flipping it likely runs through the Lehigh Valley and Bucks County (SD-16), where Mark Pinsley is running against Republican incumbent Jarrett Coleman.  Mark is ahead by one point, according to the latest polls.  

Mark's videos are funny and interesting.  You don’t have to be a tech wizard or even a social media fan to increase the reach of the videos that can change voters’ minds.

### Click here to [Watch, Like, Comment, and Share Mark's Facebook videos](https://www.facebook.com/VoteMarkPinsley/reels/). 

You can also find Mark on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markpinsley/)
 and [Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/@voteformarkpinsley).

Here are six simple steps that go a long way.

1. WATCH the video till the end. This tells the algorithm people are liking and engaging with it.

2. LIKE the post, with the “love” or “wow” emojis rather than a simple “like.”

3. COMMENT on the video. Explain why you like it, using first person and emotive terms. For example: “This is why I love candidate Mark Pinsley – he tells it like it is."

4. SHARE the video on your social media feeds if you have them. Sharing is worth 30x more than a Like on the latest Facebook algorithm.

5. REPLY TO POSITIVE COMMENTS
Be emotive and use the first person. Do NOT respond to negative
comments or get into online arguments as this wastes your time and rewards their trolling.

6. AMPLIFY other comments by liking them, pinning them to the top of the comment thread or replying to the comment with phrases like “Right on! We need more people who will go out and vote like you will.” Follow up questions encourage others to comment, creating a “comment thread” which tells the algorithm the post is getting attention and should be offered to others. “My friends are all stoked to vote for candidate Mark Pinsley. Are you seeing the same enthusiasm?”

These are steps you can take easily, on your own schedule, whenever a candidate or volunteer posts something watchable. Instant gratification for you and an instant boost for your cause.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

events.title: No More Drug War – Using Opioid Settlement Funds to Protect Our Communities

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early in Cayuga County, NY
events.description:
Join Indivisble Cayuga on Saturday October 17 at 2 pm for a pro-voting rally on the Cayuga County Courthouse steps, 152 Genesee Street in Auburn.  

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: Hatfield Overpass - Multi-State Get Out the Vote Messaging
events.description:
Concerned about the mid-terms? Outraged about the state of our country? Join a massive multi-state overpass visibility campaign to promote voting for the upcoming midterm election on Saturdays October 10 and 31. Our messages will build impact as drivers see sign after sign the longer they drive. The Hatfield overpass will be one of a host of sites on I-91 and across the northeast. The campaign spans from Boston, all the way west on the Mass Pike, across New York state to Erie, PA, as well as north-south from CT and RI to VT on high visibility routes including I-93, I-91, 495, Route 128 and more. Join us!!

If you live out of the area, check with your local Indivisible group to find a site near you.

More Info:

What: Just show up and wave at passing traffic. Flags welcome, no signs please. We will provide the large signs so that drivers can see them as they pass under the overpass. 

When: Saturdays October 10 and 31 Time: 11am to 12:30 pm ET. Come for any length of time that works for you.

Where: Mountain Drive Overpass, Hatfield, MA

Additional Instructions: Park on the side of the road on either end of the overpass.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We expect all participants to uphold this commitment. events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Lindstrom, MN
events.description:
Join us in Lindstrom, MN at Oberstar Plaza (beginning of US Hwy 8 split) from 12-1 pm on Saturday, October 17th. Bring signs to vote early and sign with reasons why we all need to vote.
We will remain on public property on the plaza and on public sidewalks without blocking businesses entrances.  

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: James Malone PA SD36 Postcard Distribution
events.description:
Swing Blue Alliance's efforts in Pennsylvania include work to flip the State Senate and to flip three key congressional districts, crucial for Democratic control of the US House. Join us for this final postcard campaign before the midterms!

After his historic special election victory in March 2025, State Senator James Malone became the first Democrat to represent this district since 1890. He is also the first Latino State Senator in Pennsylvania.

We're working to support Sen. Malone to keep his seat in an historically red district. Democrats have a chance to counter Republican redistricting and add up to 4 Democratic members of Congress by flipping the Pennsylvania state senate to Democratic control and winning a trifecta, one of the top priorities in PA this election cycle. 

Our state legislative candidate cards have also been shown to have up-ballot impact and will help increase votes for Democratic congressional and state-wide candidates.

Malone's priorities are those of his constituents. From public school access to affordability to common-sense gun laws, he truly is a champion of the people. He is endorsed by Governor Josh Shapiro and Lt. Governor Austin Davis and has been endorsed by labor unions across his district.

The postcards are easy to complete: they only require writing a few words and placing an address label and stamp on the card.

The Malone campaign is paying to print the postcards but Swing Blue Alliance has committed to raisinng funds to offset that expense. Please consider donating $6.50 per packet (the campaign’s cost) at https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mailformalone

Indicate the number of packets (25 postcards each) when registering and please consider ordering two or more packets if possible. Cards should be mailed directly by you by October 22nd.

Join Tree Pittsburgh this Fall in the Mon Valley for a free tree education series!

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, December 2026
events.description:
Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.

events.description:
VOTING IS OUR SUPERPOWER!
Please note the NEW LOCATION this year, on the parking lot and sidewalks near Petrack Park, and across the street.
Costumes are encouraged.
We would like your signs to be about voting and defending our democracy. 
Unlike the previous No Kings, please don't bting anti-Trump or anti-ICE signs. That is not our focus this time. Be creative, have fun and bring a friend or ten!
After the rally, we will drop off our filled-in ballots at the community center nearby. Early voting starts Saturday at 10 a.m. You can do this too if you are local.
As always, we pledge to remain calm and non-violent, and not engage with anyone seeking trouble.
Please sign up and we'll ee you on the 17th!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early PineHilladelphia
events.description:
Come together with your fellow frustrated neighbors for No Kings 4! Join us for a day of solidarity and support. Let's vent some anxious energy, see proof of our true numbers, and coordinate plans for voting in November! In addition to the standard music, sign making, and highly encouraged tactical frivolity, we will also be setting up local carpools to make sure everyone can get to the polls. As usual, this is a fixed location protest, so feel free to bring a chair if you need one. Any and all costumes are welcome, but if you need some inspiration, I recommend attending as a witch. Witches represent pathologized feminity, forbidden knowledge of medicinal herbs, and refusal to conform to the "one acceptable way of life" societal influence machine. Let's bring back the season of the witch, and embrace being weird, strong willed, defiant, and inconvenient to the ruling class. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*
events.accessibility_notes: We are a fixed location protest, so feel free to bring a chair if you need one! This location is grass that is lined with a paved sidewalk. There is a gazebo for shade, and there will be water and snacks available to help maintain blood sugar and blood pressure. You are not obligated to stay the whole 3 hours, I use this window to give everyone time to come and go as they need. Please make sure you are counted! I'll be the witch in pigtails making my rounds with a yellow clicky counter. Parking is on the side streets surrounding the intersection. Pine Hill PD will be on the scene to guide people. If you park in a store's parking lot, please purchase something from the store as a thank you for their support.

events.title: The Games People Play

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Breaking the ICE is a deliberate, breathless convergence—a strategic intervention that breathes life into the space between us. It unites women who move through entirely different worlds, weaving together the lives of Black, African Diaspora, Arab, Latina, White, and Asian women. We gather with intention, bridging the deep, silent divides of culture, faith, socioeconomic lineage, and raw lived experience.

This event is designed to be an intentional, transformative space where community organizing meets cultural celebration.

This time, we gather around the table.

Every game has its players. Every player has a strategy. There are rules spoken aloud and rules you only discover once you are already in play. There is power in knowing when to move, when to wait, when to protect your queen and when it is finally time to take the king.

The Games We Play is an intimate evening of strategy, pleasure, competition, and political discovery. Across scattered tables, women will gather over chessboards, cards, and games designed to make us think differently about power. We will laugh, challenge one another, break bread, and uncover the quiet calculations behind the political world we move through every day.

Because politics has always had its games.

Who gets invited to the table? Who knows the rules before the game begins? Who has spent years quietly learning the board? And what happens when women from entirely different worlds sit across from one another and begin sharing what they know?

Event Schedule

5:00 PM–8:00 PM | The Board, The Players, The Power and light dinner.

Take your seat.

Move between tables filled with games, conversation, food, and connection. Learn the seductive discipline of chess—patience, sacrifice, protection, anticipation. Enter Political Healing Monopoly, where those who have spent years doing the work help reveal how power, relationships, resources, and organizing actually move through our communities.

And somewhere between the laughter, competition, and the next move, we will enter a deeper conversation about the games of politics to the rules nobody writes down, the rooms where decisions are made, the relationships that shift the board, and the strategies communities have used to survive, organize, and build power.

Come curious. Come competitive. Come ready to teach something and ready to be taught.

The board is already set.
The question is: how will you play?

Because once you understand the game, you can begin to understand the board.

Host Committees & Partners

Brought to you in powerful solidarity with:

* Fems for Dems
* Arab Americans for Progress
* Reproductive Freedom for All
* ABISA

events.description:
Come knock doors in Iowa with us to knock doors for Democrats in competitive congressional, gubernatorial, and U.S. Senate races!

We'll be carpooling from Naperville to Iowa at 9:00 AM. You may also *drive directly* to our Iowa-based launch location, where we will meet at 12:00 PM. 

No matter what you choose, you'll be canvassing with the same people in the same place! We'll see you there!

### Please download MiniVAN

If you haven’t canvassed before (or if you have and you want to review) you will find it helpful to download the MiniVAN User guide and application in advance of your canvass (links below).

MiniVAN is the application we use to keep track of what happens during the canvass. It tells you what doors to knock, who you’ll be speaking to, provides the script for you to use, etc.

If this is your first time using MiniVAN, you'll receive an in-person training on-site during the canvass training!

- [MiniVAN User guide](https://www.ngpvan.com/blog/canvassing-with-minivan/)
- [MiniVAN on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&pli=1)
- [MiniVAN Touch on Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547)
### Staging Location

Volunteers will either meet in Naperville or drive directly to Iowa (Address to be shared prior to event). Please plan to arrive when the shift begins (give yourself plenty of time to drive up and grab a coffee!).

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Enfield
events.description:
October 17th noon to 4 pm at 1010 Enfield Street - the Alcorn School No KingsDay/ Get out the vote

This event will be held at the former Alcorn school. It is no longer a school and we have permission from the town manager to have our protest there as we have in the past. This event will be held rain or shine so bring your umbrellas and ponchos if needed. Our chief of police has always been very cooperative and make sure that the community policeman are there and we have never had any incident whatsoever where they had to step in. No negative behavior will be accepted, and you would be asked to leave.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Overpass Rally at Exit 44 in Marion, VA. We'll have signs.
This will focus on a **"Vote Early"** message which is a bit different that our Tuesday gatherings.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

The Pride Parade begins at Magic Island at 3pm, proceeds via Ala Moana Blvd and  Kalakaua Avenue through Waikiki, and ends at Kapiolani Park.  There will be a Festival at the Shell following the parade or you can stay on the truck back to Magic Island.  Join our contingent by 2.  The parade is huge and line-up is often confusing.

Most of the contingents in this parade represent large companies and NGO's that consciously reject "political messages". That's not us - and each year the crowds welcome our message, grab for leaflets, chant with us, and photograph our banners and signs. Join us in getting out our urgent message to thousands of people - and have a lot of fun doing it!

Our Refuse Fascism truck will be in line by 1pm. Come early and help decorate it!  You can ride on the truck, walk, skate, skateboard, or bike. The route is flat and smooth so wagons, strollers and wheelchairs work.

Join Stand Up America & Vote Forward for a letter writing party, with special guests, Jess Craven and Vote Forward's Data & Research team.

Jess Craven is an activist, organizer, and author of the [Chop Wood, Carry Water Daily Actions Substack.](https://chopwoodcarrywaterdailyactions.substack.com/)

Vote Forward partners with volunteers to take evidence-driven, high-impact actions to strengthen our democracy by building trust in government and increasing voter participation. Everything we do is grounded in evidence: we rigorously test our tactics, learn from the results, and evolve. During this event, you'll hear directly from Vote Forward's Data & Research Team, who are behind some of our most novel and exciting work yet. 

We have ambitious goals, but we make it easy to get started.  Join us to learn about the available campaigns, and the strategy behind them.

The most common question we receive at Vote Forward is: "what should I write?" This letter writing event is the personalized, in depth answer to that question. Vote Forward staff will help you craft an effective, personal message to voters. Whether you’re writing letters for the first time or you’re an experienced letter writer looking to refine your message, this event is for you!

RSVP today, and we’ll let you know how to join this event. Invite your friends and family, too and encourage them to join in with Vote Forward! 

Never written with Vote Forward before? No problem! Visit [votefwd.org/instructions](https://votefwd.org/instructions) for all the information you need, and sign up for an account at [votefwd.org/standupamerica](https://go.votefwd.org/standupamerica).

events.title: 🎨 Crafting Change: A Voting-Inspired Arts & Crafts Night 🗳️✂️
events.description:
# 🎨 Crafting Change: A Voting-Inspired Arts & Crafts Night 🗳️✂️

### **About this event**

Join us for a relaxing, creative evening of community and civic expression! 🌟 We are gathering at **The Dovetail** in Warren on **Thursday, October 30th, from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM** for an open arts and crafts collage night centered around civic power and voting. 🗳️✊

Whether voting means defending your community, fighting for bodily autonomy, honoring civil rights leaders, protecting public education, or speaking truth to power, art is one of the most powerful ways to make our voices visible! 🗣️💫

We want to explore the personal spark behind our ballots:
* 🗳️ **Why do you vote?**
* 💡 **What issues, people, or future visions inspire you to take action?**
* 🤝 **Why is community participation essential for our collective future?**

**All materials will be provided free of charge!** 🆓✂️ We’ll have cardstock, magazine clippings, prints, markers, glue, scissors, and decorative craft supplies ready for you. No prior art or collage experience is needed—just bring your ideas, your story, and your vision! 🖍️✨

---

### 🖼️ **What happens to your art?**
You are welcome to take your finished collage home that night, or you can lend it to us to be featured in an art installation display at our **November monthly meeting**! 🏛️🎉

---

### **Event Details:**
* 📅 **Date:** Thursday, October 30th
* ⏰ **Time:** 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM
* 📍 **Location:** The Dovetail (29200 Hoover Rd, Warren, MI 48093)
* 🎟️ **Cost:** Free & open to all!
* ✂️ **Supplies:** 100% provided

Space is limited, so please RSVP to help us ensure we have enough craft supplies and seating for everyone! 📝 Bring a friend, grab a beverage or treat ☕🍪, and let’s turn our passion into art! 🎨✨

events.title: Early Voting Kickoff Canvass Launch with Troy, Hannah, and Matt!
events.description:
Join Troy Jackson, Hannah Pingree, and Matt Dunlap for an Early Voting Kickoff & Canvass Launch!

Talking to voters face-to-face is the best way to earn their support for Democrats up and down the ticket. Join Troy, Hannah, and Matt to knock on some doors and talk to voters about the importance of electing Democrats up and down the ballot!

Don't worry if you've never canvassed before — there will be training and Q&A before the shift starts. We'll meet at the Lewiston Democratic Committee Office at 621 Main Street to get trained, and then hit the doors to speak with voters.

Just bring yourself, a fully charged phone, and plenty of energy for a great day of canvassing!

If you haven't already, go to your App Store or Google Play Store, download the MiniVAN app, and create an account before you arrive.

iOS: https://apple.co/34ctpME

Android: https://tinyurl.com/androidminivan

Once you have MiniVAN downloaded on your phone, you can use this test list to practice using the map, finding the houses you are supposed to knock and who lives there, moving through the script, seeing the not home options, and navigating from house to house. Your Field Organizer will also go over all of this with you in the training.

Can't wait to see you soon!

events.title: Community Conversation: Data Centers & The Law
events.description:
Please join the Ohio Democratic Rural Caucus for a community conversation about data centers and what the current law entails, moderated by Judge Marilyn Zayas, with Ohio's First District Court of Appeals, as well as Marc Dann, former Ohio Attorney General. 

What happens when the interests of local communities, utility customers, and major energy users collide? What part does the Ohio Supreme Court play in the litigation, ballot measures, and rate increases due to data centers coming to your community? We look forward to discussing these questions and more at this informative, nonpartisan event. All are welcome to attend!

events.description:
Join us in Schuyler for a listening session with Chris Backemeyer and Jocelyn Brasher. Share your concerns and priorities, and what you need in your elected officials.

Please join us for a conversation with Chris Backemeyer for Congress!

For over 20 years, Chris served our country in national security, working behind the scenes to keep Americans safe. Now, he's running for Congress because politicians in Washington are taking this country in the wrong direction.

Jocelyn Brasher is a proven leader ready to fight for Nebraska families. With a bipartisan approach to justice, she will protect consumers, strengthen public safety, and respect the will of voters. Jocelyn is a former prosecutor and consumer protection attorney who spent five years as an Assistant Attorney General in the Nebraska Attorney General's Office before it was turned into a platform for political games. She's running to return the office to its real mission: serving and protecting all Nebraskans: our children, our seniors, our farmers, our workers, and our communities, with independence and integrity.

Nebraskans know that with grit and hard work, a win is always within reach. It’s time for leaders who work as hard as the people they serve.

events.title: People Powered Maine & Indivisible Bangor Canvass: BANGOR
events.description:
Come join fellow volunteers from **People Powered Maine** and **Indivisible Bangor** to knock doors in Bangor and talk to our neighbors about the issues that matter most to them for the November election. Whether you're a seasoned volunteer or a first-time canvasser, every door we knock makes a difference.

**Never canvassed before? Newcomers welcome!**

* **In-person training:** We start promptly at 1:00 PM in the Crofutt Room to walk through scripts, the app, and tips.
* **Buddy system:** Every newcomer is paired with a veteran canvasser. You won't have to go alone.

**Schedule**

* **1:00 PM:** Check-in and training at Bangor Public Library (Crofutt Room, 145 Harlow St)
* **1:30 PM:** Pair up, grab materials, and head out to canvass
* **4:30 PM:** Wrap up canvassing
* **5:00 PM:** Food, drinks, and debrief at Mason's Brewing Company (15 Hardy St, Brewer)

*People Powered Maine is an independent, volunteer-led 501(c)(4) building a permanent grassroots organizing group in Maine, county by county. We organize year-round around a seven-point economic and human-rights platform.*

*Indivisible Bangor is a group of residents in Bangor and surrounding communities invested in promoting social justice and democracy.*

*Visit [People Powered Maine](https://peoplepoweredmaine.org) and [Indivisible Bangor](https://indivisiblebangor.org) to learn more.*

events.description:
Join us for a late afternoon honoring Dia de los Muertos and our lost loved ones whose memories live on through our families, traditions, and stories shared.

Together we will honor the lives taken by harmful policies and practices across many social justice issues: violent immigration enforcement, environmental injustice, labor injustice, reproductive injustice, and all other threats to human rights and our communities.

We welcome you to bring your family, memories, stories, and a picture of a loved one to place on the altar. We will have pan dulce, champurrado, and more to celebrate this holiday.


Español Abajo

Acompáñanos a compartir una tarde en conmemoración del Día de los Muertos, honrando a nuestros seres queridos que ya no están con nosotros, pero cuyas memorias siguen vivas a través de nuestras familias, tradiciones y las historias que compartimos.

Juntos honraremos las vidas que hemos perdido a causa de políticas y prácticas dañinas relacionadas con distintas luchas por la justicia social, incluyendo la violencia de las políticas migratorias, la injusticia ambiental, la injusticia laboral, la injusticia reproductiva y todas aquellas amenazas contra los derechos humanos y nuestras comunidades.

Te invitamos a traer a tu familia, tus recuerdos, tus historias y una fotografía de un ser querido para colocarla en nuestro altar. Tendremos pan dulce, champurrado y más para compartir en comunidad y celebrar esta hermosa tradición.

Brushy Creek Lake Park 
3300 Brushy Creek Road
Cedar Park, TX 78613

When:	

Friday, Oct. 16, 6-9 pm

Decorated posters taped to the inside of your car windows also look great, so bring a few blank posters to decorate if you prefer to do that.

Non-partisan messages, please. (If your hot rod already sports candidate bumper stickers, that's fine)
