events.title: Make Vote Power Signs for No Kings
events.description:
This is a local sign-making event in Mountain View, CA, to prepare for **No Kings 4 events across the Bay Area on Oct. 17**.

This No Kings is going to look a little different! **No Kings 4 is focused on the power and importance of voting: getting people to vote, encouraging people to vote early, and reminding people that protecting democracy requires all of us to participate.** Some events will be marches and rallies, others will be neighborhood gatherings and celebrations, but voting will be at the center of all of them.

That means your old protest signs may not be quite what's needed this time. :) These are **nonpartisan voter-mobilization events**, so leave the anti-Trump, anti-Republican, and candidate-specific signs at home and come make something new!

We’ll be making **Vote Power signs**: signs that celebrate voting, remind people that their vote matters, encourage people to vote early, and speak to the importance of showing up to defend our democracy. They can be joyful, serious, urgent, funny, patriotic -- whatever message about voting you want to bring to Oct. 17.

We’ll use paint, markers, color tape, construction paper, whatever works best. There will be different poster sizes available. Let your creativity fly! And if your creativity is tapped out, that’s fine too: we’ll have plenty of easy-to-make sign ideas and inspiration.

**Blank posters and art supplies will be provided**, but if you can bring your own supplies (especially jumbo markers!), that would be appreciated. We will be mostly indoors, and outside if possible. Snacks will be served, and food brought to share is always welcome.

Come help us make the power of voting impossible to miss on Oct. 17!

P.S. There are many No Kings events happening around the Bay Area. Our event, [Vote Early Neighborhood Celebration](https://www.mobilize.us/itsblueturn/event/1046430/), is in Mountain View from 2–4 pm. We’re bringing neighbors together for an afternoon of music, treats, activities for kids, voting information, community organizations, and a little bit of joyful civic silliness. See you there!

events.title: 10/3 - Voter Mobilization with HCDP @ Casa Verde

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **Casa Verde**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Register eligible voters on the spot
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Voter Registrar Requirements

- **All volunteers are welcome!** There are plenty of vital roles for everyone, _whether you are certified or not_.

- **Important Note**: If you want to physically register voters at this event, you **MUST** be a certified Volunteer Deputy Registrar (VDR) in at least **Harris County**.

- _Not certified yet?_ Don't worry! You can still participate in outreach or get certified ahead of time by signing up for our [VDR Training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908495/).

### Shift Schedule & Flow

Pre-run: 10 AM | 3010 Milam St Post-run social: 11:30 AM–2 PM | Casa Verde

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[10:45-11:00am]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **[11:00am-2:00pm] Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **[2:00-2:15pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, turn in completed registration forms, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, voter registration forms, and training cheat sheers will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.description:
Join the HD-82 campaign’s **Van Wert County Anytime Canvass** from **October 4 through November 3**.

The Anytime Canvass is designed to make volunteering flexible. Instead of signing up for a specific scheduled shift, you can help when it works for you—whether you have an hour after work, a free afternoon, or several hours on a weekend.

Volunteers can choose how they would like to participate:

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
The film, No Country for Mothers, explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the "girl boss" and "trad wife" labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families.

This isn’t a film meant to be watched or shared only by mothers; we’ve all had a mother and we all have friends, partners, colleagues, neighbors, and relatives who are mothers. Therefore, we all have a valid POV & contribution to make.

The event is being held at Fuegos LA, and their delicious empanadas, full menu and drinks will be available for purchase.

The film runs for 78 minutes, and we’ll have some group discussion pre- and post-film.

If you can’t make it, please share with anyone you know who would love to be there!

events.description:
Get Out the Vote with Indivisible Goshen!

Join Indivisible Goshen for a Get Out the Vote event focused on helping neighbors make their voices heard. We’ll stand up and remind the community to VOTE & VOTE EARLY( 12PM - 1 PM), and then head out for door-to-door canvassing to distribute door hangers with Early Voting dates/locations (1PM - 4PM). 

Whether you’re a seasoned volunteer or brand new to canvassing, there’s a way to get involved. Come out, connect with your community, and help make sure voters have the information they need to participate!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Civic Engagement Ministry Leaders - Virtual Training
events.description:
Join the Civic Engagement Ministry

Scripture reminds us that faith without works is dead. The Civic Engagement Ministry, part of The Road to Black November, puts that faith to work. We're bringing together churches, faith leaders, and community members to make sure every eligible voter in our community is registered, informed, and ready to vote this November.

When you register, you become a member and a team leader. You'll get the tools and support to organize the people around you: your congregation, your family, your coworkers, and your neighbors.

As a member, you'll:

Build and lead your own team
Help people register and check their voter status
Share trusted, nonpartisan information about what's on the ballot and how to vote
Connect with other faith-driven organizers across the community
Help get people to the polls on Election Day

You don't need experience, just a willingness to serve. We'll organize and strategize together.

Alabama's voter registration deadline is October 19, 2026. Every conversation counts, and the time to start is now.

The community needs you. Let's get to work.

events.title: Volunteer to Phone Bank Canvass for Endorsed Candidates
events.description:
### **Saturday Weekend Action Days: Canvass & Phone Bank!**

**Join us every Saturday to make a real impact in our community!** Whether you prefer talking to neighbors face-to-face or reaching out over the phone, we need your help to power our grassroots movement. 

You can sign up for a single day or secure your spot for multiple Saturdays to keep our momentum going. 

#### **Shift Information**
* **Standard Shift:** 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM
* **Flexible Hours:** We want to work with your schedule! If you are available to help outside of our standard hours—such as an afternoon shift from **2:00 PM – 7:00 PM**—please sign up for a regular shift and reply to your Mobilize confirmation email to let the event contact know your preferred hours.

#### **What to Bring & Expect**
* **Time Commitment:** If you can't stay for the full shift, that is not a problem! If you can manage about **45 minutes for training** and then phone bank or canvass for **about an hour**, that is sufficient to make a big difference.
* **For Canvassing:** Comfortable walking shoes, a fully charged smartphone, and a water bottle.
* **For Phone Banking:** We have **5 phones and tablets available** for volunteer use. However, if you are comfortable doing so, we highly encourage you to **bring your own laptop and mobile phone**. 
* **Audio Gear:** A headset (microphone and headphones) with a **traditional headphone jack** is highly recommended to help you make calls easily, but it is **not required**.


*Training and materials will be provided at the start of every shift. No prior experience is necessary!*

**Choose your dates below and shift into action with us!**

events.title: Goodyear Ballot Party with GATHER & Save Our Schools Arizona
events.description:
Arizona's 2026 ballot is long, and parts of it are confusing. You don't have to work through it alone.
 
GATHER and Save Our Schools Arizona are teaming up to host a Ballot Party in Goodyear. Come research and talk through the candidates and propositions with your neighbors, in a relaxed and friendly setting. Most early ballots arrive in the days just before this, so it's a good night to fill yours out and get it turned in.
 
This year it matters more than ever to vote your whole ballot, all the way down, and to return it early. Voting is how democracy works. We'll help make it a little less confusing.
 
### Dos
 
- Do bring your ballot.
- Do bring your questions.
- Do bring a laptop or phone so you can look things up.
- Do check out the resources we'll email you after you sign up.
- Do keep your own ballot pages with you, and don't mix them up with anyone else's.
### Don'ts
 
- Don't expect everyone to agree.
- Don't worry about covering every single race.
- Don't collect or turn in anyone else's ballot. Everyone returns their own.
- Don't wait to turn in your ballot. Mailing it early also means fewer calls, texts, and mailers for you.
**Free and open to everyone. RSVP so we know how many people to plan for.**
 
### Hosted by
 
- GATHER (Growing Arizona Together for Humanity, Equity & Respect)
- Save Our Schools Arizona

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Oswego County, NY
events.description:
RALLY ON THE BRIDGE OSWEGO COUNTY!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
### Ready to go out and meet the voting public? Join us at the Galveston ArtFest right on the Strand. This is the weekend leading into the Early Voting period and a great opportunity to connect with voters from across the entire Houston Gulf Coast area.

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—this bustling event in Galveston’s historic downtown is perfect for meeting our fellow Texans right where they are.

Here are details about the event,
https://www.visitgalveston.com/events/annual-events/artoberfest/

Join Team Talarico Volunteers, Powered by People and the Galveston Island Democrats for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization for Talarico and the Democratic slate** on Galveston’s Historic Strand between 20th and 24th on Post Office **! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, and create excitement for James Talarico and the entire slate of Democratic Candidates. We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting?
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico and the Democratic slate of candidates.
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:

- **[10:00AM - 10:30AM]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals.

- **[10:30AM- 1:00PM] Hotspotting & Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **[1:00PM - 1:30PM]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. 

This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: Covex Coffee 2312 Market St, Galveston, TX 77550

- ** Volunteer Parking**: Most of the parking in the area is either a paid lot or paid street parking

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, voter registration forms, and training cheat sheers will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Travelers Rest, SC
events.description:
NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY - UPSTATE SC
We've spent the last two years showing up in the streets. Now it's time to take that people power to the ballot box.
Early voting in South Carolina begins Monday, Oct. 19 and runs through Oct. 31. Voting early has many benefits, including helping mitigate voter suppression efforts and other barriers that can make voting more difficult.
So, on October 17, we're hitting the road, bringing No Kings: Vote Early to communities across the Upstate for a full day of voter visibility, education, and community engagement.
If the goal is to get people informed and ready to vote, visibility matters.
THE UPSTATE ROUTE
CHOOSE YOUR STARTING POINT
Anderson | 10:00 to 11:30 AM | Anderson County Courthouse | 100 S. Main St.
OR
Laurens | 9:30 to 10:30 AM | Lavonne Shopping Center parking lot | 102 Fleming Street
Easley | 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM | Corner of E. Main St. & S. Pendleton St. | Downtown
Travelers Rest I 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM I Corner of S. Main & McElhaney Rd. I Downtown
Greer | 2:30 to 4:00 PM | Corner of Trade St. & E. Poinsett St. | Downtown
Simpsonville | 4:00 to 5:30 PM | Clock Tower Square | Corner of S. Main St. & W. Curtis St. | Downtown
Greenville | 5:30 to 7:00 PM | Rally at Falls Park Falls Park | 601 S. Main St. | Downtown
Laurens will be our vehicle decorating stop to turn your ride into a rolling reminder to vote early. The Anderson, Easley, Greer, and Simpsonville stops will be picket-style visibility actions on public sidewalks, putting the message where people can see it. We'll finish the day in Greenville with a community rally at Falls Park featuring topical speakers and music.
Bring signs about early voting, making a voting plan, election information, or factual reminders about participating in our elections.
Please skip "register to vote" signs. Voter registration ends October 4 at 11:59 PM, so hopefully everyone has visited SCVOTES.GOV to register and verify their registration before then!
The goal is simple: every community we visit should know more than they did before we got there.
WANT TO DO THE WHOLE ROUTE?
Yes, 5 cities in one day is a LOT.
We've mapped out a recommended travel schedule, including departure times and, because we're not monsters, a lunch break.
You don't have to travel all day. Join us at the stop closest to you.
One stop or 5 of your choice, help us take the message beyond Greenville and across the Upstate.
6 communities. One day. One message. No Kings. No Thrones. No Crowns.
The people choose who represents them. Make your plan. Vote early. Spread the word.

Hosted by: 50501 SC, Indivisible Upstate SC, C.A.R.E. 864, Community Heroes

Saturday, October 17th (Early Voting Day) from 1-3pm on the Charlton Town Common.

Something different is happening in Charlton on October 17.

Join us Tuesday or Thursday and help us elect Democrats across the Northern Valley!

events.title: No Tyrants: Vote Early Solidarity Rally - Canterbury, UK
events.description:
The midterms are coming. The world is watching. Here in Canterbury, UK we are inviting US citizens living, studying, visiting or on pilgrimage to Canterbury to take a stand for a better future. On 17 October, we're planning to come together to celebrate our voting power and stand in solidarity with communities across the US and the world that are working tirelessly to get out the vote for the midterm elections.

Early voting is essential. Whether you've voted already or will be sending your ballot in shortly, please join us. Register and make your plan to vote TODAY! On 30 Sept.2026 one of us already received confirmation that ‘Your ballot was received and accepted for counting' by MI elections. A completed ballot made the 3,280 mile journey from Canterbury, UK across the Atlantic to MI elections. We challenge all US citizens to register and to vote early. Let’s see whose ballot travels the furthest. 

On October 17th, join us in local events across the world as we get out the early vote. 

Join us in The Buttermarket (Opposite the Christ Church Gate main entrance to Canterbury Cathedral, Canterbury, UK.  CT1 2JJ)

**Please note that this event is from 12PM – 1PM BST/local time**

When signing up to attend this event, you must use a United States ZIP Code 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**
For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Tyrants/No Kings actions, No Tyrants/No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Kanawha County IEP Circle
events.description:
IEP Circles WV is a parent-led community where families of exceptional learners come together to find support, build knowledge, and create change. If you're navigating an IEP, 504 Plan, evaluations, school communication, or accessing services, these gatherings are designed to help you feel informed, connected, and supported.

Each meeting brings caregivers together with experienced advocates, education attorneys, and community partners who provide practical guidance, answer questions, and facilitate meaningful discussions. You'll have opportunities to share experiences, learn from other families, discover helpful resources, and build lasting relationships with people who understand the challenges you face.

Beyond individual support, IEP Circles helps families understand the larger issues affecting special education. We'll explore how school funding, staffing shortages, IDEA funding, and state and federal policy decisions impact the services available to students. By connecting personal experiences to these broader challenges, families can better understand why obstacles exist and how they can work alongside educators and other parents to improve public education.

For those interested in taking the next step, IEP Circles also offers opportunities to develop advocacy skills through workshops on legislative advocacy, storytelling, public speaking, community organizing, and civic engagement. Whether you simply want support or hope to help shape the future of special education in West Virginia, you'll find a welcoming community where your experiences are valued and your voice matters.

Together, we can strengthen support for our children, build stronger communities, and advocate for a public education system that works for every student.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early NEK - Newport, VT

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Celebrate democracy at this all-ages, community-building, action-oriented, drop-in event, where you and your family can:

- Enjoy snacks, art projects, live music, and other fun activities to celebrate & protect our democracy. 
- Register to vote or check your voter registration, know your voting rights, learn how to VOTE EARLY in your town in-person or in official drop boxes. 
- Sign up for voter hotlines or phone banks from home, to become an election observer, or other needed actions to protect the vote in VT & other states
-Prepare for collective action in case of election interference before, during, or after election day, Nov. 3.

Stop by anytime 2-4pm. Everyone in support of democracy is welcome! 

Please email NEKIndvisible@proton.me if you would like to volunteer at this event (we are especially seeking a face painter and someone to lead banner making!), or if you would like to receive our monthly e-newsletter. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**
For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early, and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: FOTV Canvass in Tioga County - Part One
events.description:
Dear Friends,

As we push our way into the final weeks of the general campaign, we are looking to join forces with the Coordinated Campaign to ensure every possible vote is contacted before election day. Join us and a team of volunteers from CC to knock on doors and encourage our voters to get out and vote!

Materials and training will be provided. We will get fresh GOTV walk lists generated by the Shapiro/Davis campaign as well as talking points. At this stage, we are no longer trying to persuade voters. We are simply reaching out to those who support our Democratic candidates and make sure they cast those votes!

You should be feeling excited as we enter this final phase. Enthusiasm for our Governor, for our State House and US Congressional candidates, and, indeed, for Democrats all across the country, is growing. The mood is shifting and the people are ready for, and demanding, change. Now.

Join us. This part is so important, and we need you! Thanks in advance!

Gabe Hakvaag
Chair
Tioga County Democrats

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Canvass for Abdul at Plymouth Farmers Market

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and canvass for Abdul El-Sayed at the Plymouth Farmers Market from 9 AM to 11:30 AM. 

Organize and Win Michigan is our program to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state. 

Senator Sanders says it best: 

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few. 

Right now, our movement is winning. Why? 

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges. 

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement. 

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up. 

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us. 

Let’s get to work. 

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

Please join us to rally to increase awareness of the vital importance for Early Voting in the November election. Early voting begins at the Weston Town Clerk's Office on Saturday, October 17th. Bring your sign and your enthusiasm to support this essential vote.  And then walk up the hill and vote!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Rally Against The Regime - Election Season

location.venue: I-5 Overpass & NW Stewart Parkway (on the sidewalk)

events.description:
# Rally Against The Regime – Election Season

## 🗳️ Election Season Is Here, and We're Taking It to the Overpass

From now through the November election, our weekly **Rally Against The Regime** moves to the **I-5 Overpass at NW Stewart Parkway**. Thousands of drivers pass this spot every day, and we want every one of them to see our message:

**Vote the Trump administration and its Republican enablers out of power. End fascism. Take our country back to the democracy it was meant to be.**

Ballots are coming. This is our moment, and it starts at the mailbox.


## 📍 When & Where

- **When:** Saturdays, **12:00 pm – 2:00 pm**, through the election

- **Where:** **I-5 Overpass & NW Stewart Parkway** (on the sidewalk)
  3599 NW Stewart Pkwy, Roseburg, OR 97471


## 🧰 What To Bring

This isn't just a protest. **It's people power on display.**

### 📣 Make Your Voice Visible

**Go BIG.** Drivers are moving fast, so **large signs with short messages** in thick, high-contrast letters work best. Here are some ideas:

- **VOTE EARLY. VOTE THEM OUT!**

- **MY BALLOT IS MY VOICE!**

- **DOUGLAS COUNTY VOTES BLUE!**

- **FILL IT OUT. MAIL IT IN. VOTE EARLY!**

- **REPUBLICANS HAD THEIR CHANCE!**

- **HONK IF YOU'RE VOTING EARLY!**

- **BALLOTS ARE HERE. USE THEM!**

- **REAL CHANGE STARTS AT THE MAILBOX!**

👉 Or create your own. **Be bold. Be direct. Don't hold back.**

### 🎨 Get Creative

- 🪆 Giant puppets

- 🎭 Creative props

- 🧥 Costumes

- 🚩 Banners & flags

- 🎶 Street-theater vibes


### 🥤 Stay Comfortable

- 💧 Water

- 🍎 A snack

- 🕶️ Sunglasses & sunscreen

- 🧢 Hat or umbrella for sun or rain

- 👟 Comfortable shoes

- 💊 Any medications you need

⚠️ **No bathrooms on site. Plan accordingly.**


## 🕊️ Our Commitment to Nonviolence

This is a **peaceful, nonviolent demonstration**. Please:

- **Stay on the sidewalk** and keep it clear for people walking by. Never step into traffic.

- **Secure your signs and banners** so the wind can't carry them onto the roadway below.

- **Don't engage with counter-protesters**, and help calm things down and de-escalate if tensions rise.

- **This is a non-violent action. Leave all weapons at home.**

---

**See you on the overpass. Let's vote them out.** 🇺🇸

**Note on Parking:** To access the overpass facing the Northbound I-5 traffic, park in the empty lot all the way at the top of Boulder Drive on your left (go up the curved road behind Oregon Pacific Bank off of Edenbower Blvd and Boulder Drive) or along the roadway. Crossing to the other side of the overpass (facing Southbound I-5 traffic) is done at your own risk.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: KNOCK-tober Sterling Heights Canvass Launches
events.description:
It's KNOCK-tober! Now is our last chance to reach the early voters we need to talk with to ensure we take back control of Congress this November.

We need YOU to step up for our community right NOW, put on your walking shoes, and join us to talk with our neighbors about the real issues facing working families right here in Macomb County — and about Christina's plan to lower costs, protect families, and clean up corruption.

Sign up to canvass and you will meet our team of organizers and trainers for some door knocking. We'll do a quick training before anyone goes out, you'll be paired with a team or a partner if you prefer to canvass in pairs, and there will be snacks!

If you've never volunteered on a campaign before, this is a great place to start. If you have, we'd love your help welcoming people who are newer to this, and making our final push into the homestretch to reach the voters we need to deliver a win for working families here.

The last time this seat was open, the previous Democratic nominee lost by only 1,600 votes. We can't afford to leave any gas in the tank between now and November 3rd— not that any of us can really afford gas right now. Help us put a stop to these insane prices hikes and out of control corruption. Come out, meet the team, and get out into your community before it's too late!

events.title: BOONTON: Be an Early Voting Poll Watcher with the Morris County Dems
events.description:
Join the team in protecting our Democracy and ensuring the polls are open, functioning, and free of voter intimidation. We will be staffing polls across the county. 

What is a poll watcher? 

A Poll Watcher or "Challenger" is a person appointed to observe the conduct of an election on behalf of a candidate, political party and/or the proponents or opponents of a question.

The integrity of elections is a concern of all citizens and although poll watchers may represent particular candidates, political parties or specific questions, their main interest is in the conduct of a fair and honest election.

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Organize and Win Senate Phonebank

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
From now until Election Day we are doing everything we can to elect progressives to the United States Senate. Abdul El-Sayed, Peggy Flanagan, and Angie Nixon are all Senate candidates in key states who Senator Sanders has endorsed.

Letter from Senator Sanders: 

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few. 

Right now, our movement is winning. Why? 

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges. 

We now have candidates all over the country who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement. 

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up. 

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us. 

Let’s get to work. 

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Postcards for PA State Senator James Malone
events.description:
Join Swing Blue Alliance’s final postcard campaign before the midterms, don't sit this one out! Malone is the first Democrat to represent his district since 1890, and the first Latino in the PA State Senate. Malone’s re-election is key to flipping the PA State Senate, countering Republican redistricting across the country, and adding up to 4 Democratic members of Congress.

The postcards are easy: write 10 words and affix an address label and stamp. Postcards are free because the Malone campaign is paying for them. You will need to buy postcard stamps (65 cents each) separately. Mail your completed postcards by October 22. 

Postcards come in packets of 25 postcards each. Signup for the pickup date and number of packets you want (and consider doing more than 1 packet). You will receive a calendar invitation from “Swing Blue Alliance via Mobilize” (check your spam folder) with pickup info including my address in Sharon, MA.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. *No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Jacksonville, Oregon

address_lines: East California Street & South Oregon Street

events.description:
Join us In Jacksonville on Saturday, October 17th 11a-1p. We'll gather again at the corners of Oregon and California Streets. 

NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY.  Stand up for our Voting Rights.  Bring your signs, voices and ballots to mail or deliver to our nearest drop box at 1101 West Main, Medford out side the Elections Office.  
See the Complete Guide link for more ideas!

[Complete Guide](https://open.substack.com/pub/peoplepowerunited/p/a-complete-guide-no-kings-vote-early-october-17-2026-map?utm_campaign=post-expanded-share&utm_medium=web)

FYI:  Voter pamphlets go out Oct. 7-9.  Ballots mail Oct. 14...if people study their voter pamphlets and plan ahead, they CAN vote by 10/17!  Voting early really helps the Elections Dept. 
(**as Chris Walker will tell us Oct. 14 at our JV Town Hall, 6pm, library**)
Preliminary ballot prep can happen and speed up election results!  (no ballot vote counting begins until after 8pm on election Day, Nov. 3, but earlier preliminary ballot preps: opening envelopes, flattening the ballots, checking and confirming signatures...all done and double checked by bi-partisan teams of elections workers...means faster and more complete results that night.

Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Texas Together Midland County Block Walk
events.description:

Help James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa get elected. During this block walk, volunteers will go door-to-door to introduce themselves, party information, and have friendly conversations with residents about the issues that matter most.

No experience is necessary. Before heading out, we'll provide a brief training covering canvassing best practices, how to use campaign materials or apps, and tips for having productive conversations. Volunteers will be paired with experienced canvassers if desired.

Please wear comfortable walking shoes, dress appropriately for the weather, and bring a fully charged smartphone if you'll be using a canvassing app.

Every conversation helps strengthen our community and increase voter engagement. Whether you're a first-time volunteer or an experienced canvasser, we'd love to have you join us!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Mountain View Wyoming
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

## Door Knock with Dr. Krish and Rep. Alex in HD49A! ##

Ready to make a real impact? We are hitting the pavement to have those critical face to face conversations that win elections! Every door we knock brings us one step closer to our goal, and we need your energy to keep the momentum going.

Whether you are a seasoned canvassing pro or this is your very first time, we’ll make sure you’re fully prepared. We will start the event with a comprehensive training session, go over our talking points, and set you up with a partner if you’d like.

Let’s get to work!

events.title: Multi-State Get Out the Vote Overpass Bannering - Longmeadow, MA

location.venue: Bark Haul Road (at the I91 overpass)

events.description:
Concerned about the mid-terms? Outraged about the state of our country? Join a massive multi-state overpass visibility campaign to promote voting for the upcoming midterm election on Saturdays October 10 and 31. Our messages will build impact as drivers see sign after sign the longer they drive. The Longmeadow overpass will be one of a host of sites on I-91 and across the northeast. The campaign spans from Boston, all the way west on the Mass Pike, across New York state to Erie, PA, as well as north-south from CT and RI to VT on high visibility routes including I-93, I-91, 495, Route 128 and more. Join us!!

How to Get There: The address Bark Haul Road will get you there if you're using Waze. (Bark Haul Road is off Route 5.) The event is on the I-91 overpass. There's plenty of parking at either end of Bark Haul Rd, and parking on the overpass is discouraged.

No signs can be attached to the overpass fencing so be prepared to hold your sign. Never drape anything over the fence, even with ropes, because it would be very dangerous if it accidentally fell onto the highway.

Please take everything you brought away with you and leave the site totally clean.


When: Saturdays October 10 and 31 Time: 11am to 12:30 pm ET. Come for any length of time that works for you.

Where: Bark Haul Road at the I91 Overpass, Longmeadow, MA

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We expect all participants to uphold this commitment. We recommend that all participants review our safety and security resource before the event: https://indivisi.org/safety.

sponsor.name: Joz for Fontana Mayor & Fontana United

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Know Your Ballot
Saturday, October 10th
Election Day is around the corner, and your ballot may have more on it than you expect. Join us for a community conversation to help you walk into the voting booth informed and confident.

What we'll cover:

A walkthrough of everything you'll see on your ballot, from top-of-the-ticket races to local measures
Plain-language explanations of each proposition: what a "yes" or "no" vote actually means
Who's running for each seat up for election, and what those offices do
Meet your local candidates. Several candidates on your ballot will be there in person, so you can hear from them directly and put faces to the names you'll see in the voting booth.

Whether you've voted in every election or this is your first time, you're welcome here. Bring your questions, your sample ballot, and your neighbors. Refreshments will be provided. This is a space for open discussion, not persuasion, so come ready to listen, learn, and share.

Date: Saturday, October 10th
Time: 9am - 12:30pm
Location: 15251 Boyle Ave., Fontana, Ca 92337
Cost: Free and open to the public

Hosted by:
Joz Sida for Fontana Mayor
Joe Alvanez for Fontana City Clerk
Kamal Namou for Fontana City Treasurer
Nubia Diaz for Fontana City Council District 1
Ben Vasquez for Fontana City Council District 4

events.title: Phone Banking (Fully Virtual)
events.description:
Join us online to GET OUT THE VOTE by phone banking!

**What to expect:**

We'll be using an online dialer platform that connects you directly to voters — no need to dial numbers yourself. Once you're connected, you'll read from a simple, conversational script designed to help you have real conversations, not a robotic pitch. The script walks you through an introduction, a few key talking points about what's at stake, and a couple of questions to gauge where the person you're speaking with stands.

Before calls begin, a trained lead will walk everyone through: 
- How to log into the phone bank platform 
- How the dialer works (it does the dialing — you just talk!) 
- A walkthrough of the script and how to enter responses 
- Tips for handling common questions or pushback

**Why it matters:**
Every conversation helps us identify supporters, share accurate information, and build the coalition we need to protect trans and immigrant Coloradans. Phone banking is flexible, low-pressure, and a great option no matter your schedule or experience level.

**What you need:**

*Computer
*Headphones
*Enthusiasm for the cause!

events.title: Get the Flock Out! A Forum on Technology and Mass Surveillance
events.description:
## Our privacy is not a privilege. Our rights are not optional. Our freedom is not for sale.

More than 200 Flock cameras and counting are watching Johnson City. Their growing presence raises serious questions about privacy, transparency, who can access the system, how officers use it, and the protections guaranteed by the Fourth Amendment.

Who has access to information about our movements? Who oversees the people using these systems? Where do we draw the line?

Those questions have real consequences. They concern one of our most basic constitutional protections: the right to live free from unreasonable government intrusion.

Our forum on Technology and Mass Surveillance will bring these issues into the open and examine what Johnson City’s expanding surveillance network means for individual privacy and constitutional rights, as well as where this technology could lead us.

We should not allow constant surveillance to become normal simply because the technology makes it possible. Nor should we assume a system is safe or appropriate simply because police officers or city officials tell us it is.

The cameras are only one part of the concern. The larger question is what happens when surveillance becomes routine, and technology allows the government to track where people go with little meaningful public oversight.

Whether someone commits a crime on camera misses the point. People should be free to move through their community without having their movements routinely recorded, searched, or shared by government agencies and private companies.

The surveillance state has arrived in Johnson City. We still have a choice about whether we allow it to become permanent.

🔥 GET THE FLOCK OUT
A forum on Technology & Mass Surveillance
📍 Langston Centre
📅 Tuesday, October 13
🕕 6:00 PM

Speakers will include local candidates fighting to Deflock Johnson City. List to be added upon confirmation.

events.title: Hyper Local 101 Training
events.description:
Wisco, a friend and ally from MN is one of the people instrumental in creating the area’s Community Defense Network known as “Hyper Locals,” which were created in response to the ICE surge in the Twin Cities that began in December of 2025.

Hyper Locals are independently created and run community-based groups that covers any size community up to an entire town with the 
purpose to connect, organize and train community members to be ready to respond to whatever threat may surface in their area.

Hyper Locals serve not only as community 
defense, but as a means to strengthen and support communities through collective action and connection. Like most states combating the overreach of ICE, CT is dealing with a similar own set of challenges keeping our communities safe from ICE. Hyper Locals would connect and communicate with established Immigrant Defense orgs around the state doing amazing work & offer support however and whenever possible. 

Wisco will be conducting a Training on how to build a Hyper Local in your community. This training will include an explanation of what a Hyper Local is, how to form one, what it can look like to fit your communities needs, structure, setting up signal chats, vetting, patrols, dispatching, training & more. A Q&A will follow as well as hands on help for anyone who needs assistance setting up Signal. Attendees will also be able to join a state-wide Signal chat for Hyper Locals to keep everyone connected.

A newly formed Hyper Local in Milford & The Perseus Project will be on hand to speak to the work they are doing and how they created their groups based on this model. Information will also be provided for many of the areas Immigrant Defense organizations.

Following the training there will be time for a Potluck. We encourage attendees to bring something to share and spend this time getting to know one another, building our community and our connections.

events.title: Rush-hour Resistance Rally @ Thomas & Central

address_lines: North Central Avenue & West Thomas Road

events.description:
**Join us for our Thursday morning rally on Thomas & Central in Midtown Phoenix!**

*Rush-hour Resistance Rallies happen every Monday–Friday during rush hour across the Phoenix metro area. Check out [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us) for the latest locations!*

Here are the particulars for this rally:

🕥 The rally starts at 7:30. You are free to show up anytime, but we recommend arriving a few minutes early to introduce yourself. We end promptly at 8:30 AM.  

✴️ We gather on the huge sidewalk on the NW corner, but some walk to the SE corner (to avoid the sun) or the NE corner. Lots of room! Look for the signs. You can't miss us.

🅿️ There's an abandoned parking lot on the NW corner, just south of the dispensary. Alternatively, the stores at the south end of the shopping center, on the SE corner, aren't open until later in the day.  

🪧 One of RhRR’s strengths is that people feel free to express themselves. Ideally, your signs would help articulate any of our three pillars:

* Defending democracy and the rule of law
* Encouraging voting
* Protecting neighbors and communities (e.g., immigrants, LGBTQIA+ people, workers, and veterans)

This approach keeps signs aligned with RhRR’s purpose, while preserving personal expression and emotional authenticity.

🇺🇳 Flags, banners, and even inflatable costumes are welcome. Some blow lots of bubbles. While our mission is serious, humor and camaraderie matter.

😷 RhRRs are peaceful, public events. Most attendees don’t hide their faces, though some do; participate at your comfort level. Photos and videos are common on social media, but you can ask posters to remove accidental appearances.

Thanks in advance for joining us. See you on the streets! ✊

**More about RhRR and why we do what we do every day of the week:**

📣 Rush Hour Resistance Rally began with a clear idea: neighbors, gathering peacefully and regularly on busy nearby streets, could remind our communities that democracy is essential and that silence is unacceptable. Over the last year, RhRR expanded from a handful of participants to multiple locations across the Valley, reaching thousands of pedestrians and motorists each week. This momentum is significant, as is the duty it brings.

🗳️ As we approach the midterm elections, our united mission is to safeguard free and fair elections and promote civic participation, particularly in local and primary races where every vote carries weight. Our weekly rallies are more than outlets for frustration; they are consistent, visible commitments that normalize voting and democratic engagement as neighborly expectations.

🕊️ RhRR is a peaceful, nonconfrontational movement. Our goal is to reach the broader community, not to confront those seeking conflict. When tensions surface, we withdraw, stay composed, and look out for one another. This discipline keeps our rallies inviting and helps newcomers feel secure joining us.

🫂 Most of all, RhRR is about people caring for one another while standing up for the future of our democracy. Every person who shows up, every sign held, and every conversation sparked on a street corner is part of something larger and deeply hopeful.

More info at [RhRR.us](https://rhrr.us).

### NO KINGS VOTE EARLY CAR RALLY ADDITION!
Can't stand on the sidewalk? Activate voters from your car! Circle past the simultaneous sidewalk rally to add impact -- Mission: Get Out the Vote!

The purpose of these Sidewalk and Car Rallies is to promote the value of voting; to get out the vote; and to encourage voting EARLY as the safer choice. 

### ADDITIONAL INFO:

HERE'S HOW TO PARTICIPATE

1. Decide on a time to participate for at least 20-30 minutes between 1-3pm.
2. Pack your car with sign-waving friends. Suggested signage: "Vote Early!"
3. Form your own mini-parade! Recruit additional carloads of friends to caravan together!
4. Decorate your car at home so that you will function as a moving rally along your route towards the sidewalk event site.
5. Drive through the rally intersection at least 5 times.
6. Wave, give thumbs up, honk your horn, and wave your signs.
7. Park afterwards and join the sidewalk activists if you can, or just drive away after your shift.

### IMPORTANT! FOR YOUR SAFETY

Be a responsible driver and activist during the No Kings Vote Early Car Rally Addition!

Use a vehicle with no ticketable offences: no broken tail light, expired registration sticker, etc.

Carefully obey ALL traffic rules, for example: - keep to the speed limit - signal to turn - yield when necessary - don't text and drive

Do not respond to counter-protesters: no shouting, no rude gestures, etc.

The goal of the No Kings Vote Early Car Rally Addition is to offer a safe and positive alternative for activists who want to support democracy but are unable to stand on the sidewalk, so please help us keep it as safe and as positive as possible.

events.title: Canvass with us in Indiana Congressional District 5!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
CD-5 is the most flippable red seat in Congress in Indiana - but we need YOUR help talking to voters to make that happen. 

In 2022, Indiana had the LOWEST midterm voter turnout in the country at 40%. There is a pervasive sense of "Indiana is red and always will be." But in truth: 

**Indiana is a purple state that DOESN'T VOTE.** 

We have the chance this month to use our votes to end the corruption. End the violence. End the lies. A House majority would give Democrats the ability to rein in Donald Trump.

And so...we are going on offense.

**Join one or more of our canvassing shifts to knock on doors in Congressional District 5 to help elect J.D. Ford.**

The voters we will canvass are just folks who need a little nudge to remind them to vote blue. You won't be talking to anyone MAGA or hard right. 

Democrat J.D. Ford is a well regarded and well liked sitting Indiana State Senator who is running against CD-5's current congressperson, Republican Victoria Spartz, for the congressional seat just north of Indianapolis. Rep Spartz has a reliable voting record in support of Donald Trump's agenda. 

So what can you do?

**You can join us.** 

If you haven't canvassed before, we will make it easy. You show up for your shift at a meeting spot with a shift leader and other canvassers to get your voter addresses and instructions. 

**Feeling shy, but you want to try it?** 

Simply sign up for a canvassing shift and a link to a general training about talking to voters will be sent to you. We can pair you with another canvasser, or you can bring a friend to walk with you while you knock on doors. 

Upon arrival at the meetup location, you will receive canvassing tips and JD Ford handouts to share at each door. You will be able to easily enter results as you canvass into the [MiniVAN app](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tv9-HHb1VQA) on your smartphone. 

A lot of canvassers like to make a fun day out of it: you can bring a friend and go out together for lunch or dinner after your shift. You can feel the satisfaction of doing your part for our democracy while getting in quality time with a friend. Win-win!

Registering for one or more shifts confirms that you agree to our [Code of Conduct and our Volunteer Waiver](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cpXG6qbL36S10EYFRqAVAIzfdSFiOG0utHdCFWdZ-9E/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.l1k2qhtuewim).

events.title: R-MWC For Melissa
events.description:
## R-MWC for Melissa: Virtual Phone Bank + Reunion Reception

  

Join fellow Randolph-Macon Woman’s College alumnae and friends of Melissa Zehner for an afternoon of calling voters, a little friendly Odds vs. Evens competition, and a virtual reception afterward with Melissa.

  

**Order of Events:
4:30–7:30 PM EST — Virtual Phone Bank**

  

Drop in when you can, stay as long as you like, and make some calls from home. You do not have to be online for the entire phone bank. Come and go as your schedule allows.

  

We’ll start with everything you need to get comfortable making calls, then spend the afternoon encouraging voters to vote ZEHNER in North Carolina Senate District 1. First-timer? Completely fine. We’ll have guidance available throughout.

  

And because this is R-MWC, it’s a class rivalry, baby!

  

**ODDS vs. EVENS.**

  

We’ll keep track of which side makes the most calls, with updates and assorted prizes throughout the evening. Expect hydration breaks, fun check-ins and possibly a little Parks and Recreation Leslie Knope inspo’ along the way.

  

**7:30 PM — Virtual Reception with Melissa**

  

Once the calls are done, the work portion ends and the virtual reception begins!.

  

Join us for:

  

Conversation and Q&A with Melissa  
Surprise music & guests!

R-MWC Jeopardy - hosted by comedian Lianna Carrera

Odds vs. Evens bragging rights

A fall beverage of your choosing - BYOB!

Mingling with classmates and friends

  

We’re still determining the official beverage situation, but given that it’s October, we feel strongly that something festive should be happening on your end of the camera.  
  

  
  
  
  

**How to Join**

  

Can’t phone bank but still want to support Melissa? [Make a suggested donation to the campaign of $50 (or whatever you can) and come straight to the reception.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melissazehner)

  

Participation in the phone bank includes admission to the virtual reception. No one will be turned away.  
  

The virtual event link will be sent to registered guests before the event.

  

Questions, comments, compliments? Let us know:

  

[annelhaley@gmail.com](mailto:annelhaley@gmail.com)

[carrera.lianna@gmail.com](mailto:carrera.lianna@gmail.com)

  

See you there!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Covington, LA
events.description:
NO KINGS VOTE EARLY with St. Tammany Indivisible and Community Partners - as we help St. Tammany voters make their plan to Vote Early!

**We have the power - the power of the vote!**

We will be at the Old Covington Courthouse (510 E Boston in Covington) from 9am until 11am with your VOTE EARLY plan - everything you need to be ready to vote early this fall - where to vote early (and on Election Day), sample ballots, what all those Constitutional Amendments mean, how to vote if you find out your status is "inactive," and more!

We will have treats for kiddos and voter ed for everyone! Voting is your SuperPower - come out and join us to make sure you're ready to exercise it this fall. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
Help us win Oregon House District 15!

Join Democratic, Independent, and Working Families Party nominee Joanna Robinson as we knock on doors to gather support and turn out voters!

📅 Thursdays | 4:00 PM

📍Location | Grand Prairie Park, 2530 Grand Prairie Rd SE, Albany

Canvass Flow:

> *All products need to be unscented and new.*

> - Laundry soap

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Greensburg, IN
events.description:
We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next ✊! This rally will be a mixture of letting your voices be heard, and hearing from speakers about the importance of voting!

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.description:
**It's time to talk to voters in CD22!** Let's get out the vote to elect **Randy Villegas in 2026** and to defend democracy long term. Join us in going door-to-door talking to voters.  We'll employ **deep canvassing techniques** such as active listening to open our voter conversations and learn which issues are important to them.   **$100 daily stipend** is available to offset your out-of-district travel costs.

 - Friday, October 16 | 12:30 pm to 4:30 pm

 - Saturday, October 17 | 9:00 am to 12:30 noon and 1:00 pm to 4:30 pm 

 - Sunday, October 18 | 9:00 am to 1:00 pm

New to canvassing?  We will train you (and we are lots of fun).  Bring a friend.  Or two.  Be a part of the change we're all looking for.

Once you've signed up, a Bay Area Coalition volunteer will contact you and help with carpools and/or housing options ... and we have cooling cars if the weather is warm. They will also give you details about the meeting location and names of people running the event.  Alternate start times can be accommodated as needed.

events.title: South Shore Bridge Brigade

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Meet on the 794 PEDESTRIAN overpass just North of Howard Avenue.

We provide physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters - to VOTE EARLY. Prepare to wave and generally have a good time.

Rules and Protocols

We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.
We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep clear to allow them to pass.
We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.
We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.
We are NOT allowed to attach the signs to the fencing on the overpass. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.
If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.
We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.
Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.
Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!
The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.
See you at 3:30 pm for setup and 4:00 pm to wave!

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.description:
**Bus leaves from Mountain View!  You leave Saturday, October 17 at 8:00 am and return by 6:30 pm.  We can help with carpools to catch the Mountain View bus from other Bay Area locations!**

Sign up to knock doors in the Central Valley! This is a special canvass where you can **Hop on the Canvassing Bus** and ride in comfort there and back. 

**Help Flip the House in 2026!!**  Join Santa Clara County Democratic Party, Swing Left Peninsula, Bay Area Coalition, and the Democratic Volunteer Center to knock doors in Modesto.  **We’ll be knocking on doors for Adam Gray in Congressional District 13 (CA-13).**  Adam won by just 187 votes in 2024, and we’re working hard to protect his seat. This race could be won or lost by a few hundred votes, so every knock counts!  

**More details:**

 - There is lots of all-day parking available at the Mountain View departure location

events.title: Texas: Social Media Monitoring Training
events.description:
We cannot afford to sit back as bad actors flood social media with misinformation. 

Join Common Cause Texas, the Election Protection Coalition and Voter Protection Corps to learn how to fight back. 

This training will focus on how election misinformation and disinformation show up online, how to identify and document concerning narratives, and how volunteers and community partners can help strengthen the broader response to misleading election information.

We’ll also spend time on the issues and narratives that are most relevant in Texas, with space to discuss what partners are already seeing and what may be helpful to monitor in the weeks ahead.

During the training, we’ll cover:
-How to recognize common forms of election misinformation and disinformation
-What to look for when being in online spaces
-How to document and report concerning content
-How monitoring can help identify emerging narratives and patterns
-How this work connects with broader election protection and response efforts

This session is open to anyone interested in learning more about election misinformation, social media monitoring, and ways to support voter protection work in Texas.

NO KINGS: EARLY VOTING IS OUR SUPERPOWER!

This No Kings action is going to look a little different and be a LOT of fun.
On October 17, we're adopting four Early Voting locations across Nashville and turning them into celebrations of early voting.  

Instead of one big march or rally, we'll be out where the voters are lining sidewalks, waving signs at passing traffic, wearing costumes and creating the kind of positive energy that makes someone driving by think:

Voting early gives people more days and more opportunities to cast their ballot. It gives us time to deal with the unexpected things that can get in the way on Election Day.

And when we vote early, we're free to spend Election Day helping others like: giving rides, serving as poll observers, sharing accurate information and helping our neighbors vote.

🗽 NOW FOR THE FUN PART: COME IN COSTUME!

Superheroes. Suffragists. Lady Liberty. Uncle Sam. Ballot boxes. Inflatable dinosaurs. Your own completely ridiculous Democracy Superhero.
Capes encouraged. Creativity encouraged. Fun absolutely encouraged.
Our goal isn't to intimidate voters or tell anyone how to vote. No Kings: Vote Early is nonpartisan. We're there to make voting feel welcoming, safe and worth celebrating and to encourage every eligible voter to participate.
Bring a sign. Bring a friend. Bring your best costume.

Bring folding chair.

🦸 SUIT UP. SHOW UP. VOTE EARLY. 🗳️

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Canvass for Abdul at St. Joe Farmers Market

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and canvass for Abdul El-Sayed at the St. Joe Farmers Market from 9 AM to 2 PM. Pick a time in this window and bring a smile! We'll bring the rest.

Organize and Win Michigan is our program to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state. 

Senator Sanders says it best: 

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few. 

Right now, our movement is winning. Why? 

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges. 

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement. 

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up. 

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us. 

Let’s get to work. 

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Call Out Data Centers! Phone Bank with Team Vikki and Candace Valenzuela
events.description:
**Special Guest Phone Bank with Candace Valenzuela!**

Tax breaks for the corporations building data centers are projected to cost Texas nearly *$1.8 BILLION a year* by 2030. They'll keep coming, and they'll keep gobbling up Texas land and water with no regard for the people and animals who live here.

Dan Patrick's answer? Stall. But we don't have time to wait on him.

**Vikki Goodwin [has a better plan](https://www.vikkigoodwin.com/datacenters): stop new data center construction *now*, until Texas passes real protections.** People and animals drink first. Data centers pay for their own water and electricity, so your bills don't go up. Counties get the power to protect their communities, and companies that hide their water use face real consequences.

But giving counties that power only works if we elect local leaders ready to use it. That's why we're teaming up with Candace Valenzuela, candidate for Denton County Commissioner, Precinct 2. Candace has served as an educator, local school board trustee, and Regional Administrator at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Now, she's running to help families find opportunity through affordable housing, smart infrastructure, and accountable government.

Voters across Denton County are worried about data centers moving in. They need to hear who has a plan to protect our water *and* our wallets.

Join Team Vikki and Candace as we hop on the FairShot Texas dialer and call voters in the region. You'll hear from Candace herself, then we'll all make calls together!

No experience needed. We'll train you, and you will not do it alone! Just bring your voice, a phone, and a laptop. Let's protect Texas water, keep our bills down, and get Vikki and Candace elected.

events.title: FMAD October Club Meeting -- Topic: Data Centers
events.description: Join us for our monthly club meeting. At this month's meeting we'll be talking about Data Centers. Simon Mathew, who is an IT Infrastructure & Systems Engineer at Virbac with 10+ years experience in solutions architecture, threat management & vulnerability remediation, will be presenting. North Texas is seeing a rapid wave of data-center development, from Dallas and Fort Worth to Garland, Mesquite, Westlake, Keller, and other suburbs. This presentation asks whether our cities are prepared to handle the real impacts: water use during drought, massive electric demand, noise, diesel generators, tax incentives, limited permanent jobs, and the long-term cost of building infrastructure for private companies. Data centers may bring investment and tax revenue, but cities need to ask harder questions about who benefits, who pays, and what protections residents receive. Before more projects are approved, North Texas needs transparency, enforceable safeguards, and regional coordination. The first half hour (6:30-7pm) is for socializing & snacking. Feel free to bring something snacky to share. The presentation will start promptly at 7pm. Sign up and let us know you're coming.
