events.title: Bethel Defends Democracy- We Stand With Survivors: Break The Silence. End the Violence.
events.description:
Please join us for our 83rd consecutive community rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel.   Our overall theme is Defending Democracy.  

On Saturday, Oct 10th,  11am - 12:30pm (90 mins), we will support Bethel’s SafeWalk, the premier event by the Center for Empowerment and Education (CEE). The core message of the event is to unite the community to stand with survivors, raise critical awareness, and fund life-changing, no-cost, and confidential support services for individuals impacted by domestic and sexual violence. The recent news about the Cornell students, including someone from Bethel, makes this an even more timely theme. 

We Stand With Survivors: Break The Silence. End the Violence.


(Tip: If viewing on facebook or mobilize, it is easier to read the full Bethel rally announcement with pictures here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1plKay3K3WR8JYHp3Nndap-STPlgFxMiX3H5iUn-w2iM/edit?usp=drivesdk

Let’s make signs with messages for them, cheer when they pass by or  join them on the walk when they pass by!   We will stop our other protest messages to show solidarity and support for this extremely important cause.


You can make signs ahead of time and we’ll also have our sign-making supplies on hand at the rally.  Some suggested messages:


Domestic & Sexual Violence Awareness Slogans
• Break the Silence. End the Violence.
• Love Shouldn’t Hurt.
• Every Survivor Deserves a Safe Space.
• Stand with Survivors, Empower the Future.
• No Excuse for Abuse.


Others:
• Walking for a Future Free of Violence.
• Step by Step, We Build Safer Communities.
• United for Peace, Safety, and Education.
• Empowering Survivors with Every Step.

VOTE EARLY!!

In America, we have no kings. The people choose their leaders. Leaders do not get to choose who votes, whose voices count, or what future our communities deserve.


….or disruptions by the regime on election day could jeopardize your ability to vote!

Voting early gives us the power to make our voices heard on our own terms, before Election Day, before the last-minute chaos, and before anyone else can decide what happens next.

Election day is 24 days from this week’s rally. But we don’t have to wait until then.  We can start voting in 9 days from this week’s rally!!


Let’s focus on getting everyone to vote early and having every vote counted.


There are millions more of us than there are of them. And when we act together, our power is bigger than anything.

events.title: Hand Out Flyers Near the South Pearl Street Farmers Market — Vote NO on 83
events.description:
Here's the thing: most Denver voters have never heard of Amendment 83. It's buried deep on a very long ballot, and ballots are already sitting on kitchen tables.

So we're heading to South Pearl on Sunday mornings to talk to people. Grab a coffee, bring a friend, and spend a couple of hours handing out flyers to folks picking up their produce. No experience needed. If you can say hi to a stranger, you can do this.

What it looks like: You'll stand on the sidewalk near the market and offer flyers to people walking by. Most people just need one sentence: "Have you heard about Amendment 83? It could bring back steel-jaw traps Colorado voters banned back in 1996." That's usually enough to get them curious.

Before you come:

Print a stack of flyers at home ([flyer link]). 50 to 100 copies is plenty.
Wear comfy shoes and dress for the weather. Fall mornings on Pearl can be chilly.
Bring a friend if you can. It's way more fun in pairs.

A few ground rules, so everyone has a good time:

Stay on the public sidewalk, not inside the market. The vendors are there to sell, and we're there to talk.
Keep at least 100 feet away from any ballot drop box. It's the law while voting is happening.
Hand flyers to people directly. Never put them in mailboxes (that's a federal no-no).
If someone disagrees, smile, say thanks, and let them go. We're not here to argue, just to make sure people know what they're voting on.

Why it matters: Amendment 83 needs 55% of the vote to pass. We just need to keep it under that. Every person who reads the fine print before they vote gets us closer.

Questions? Reply to your confirmation email, and we'll get back to you.

See you on Pearl!

Learn more at VoteNo83.org

Paid for by Animal Wellness Action.

Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: 🌻Colorado Stands with Ukraine: An Evening with Sunflower Seeds Ukraine
events.description:
🌻 Join us on Zoom for a conversation with guest speaker Chip Heldman of Sunflower Seeds Ukraine, a Boulder-based nonprofit run entirely by volunteers in both the US and Ukraine! Chip will explain why this work matters: Ukraine's military is so large that it can't efficiently supply every soldier with everything they need, so Sunflower Seeds Ukraine works to fill the gap. 🩹 That means medical supplies and equipment like Individual First Aid Kits (IFAKs), 🥽 protective gear such as eye and ear protection, rain gear, and gloves, and 🎒 tactical gear including backpacks, boots, drone detectors, and night vision devices. Beyond the front lines, the group converts ☀️ solar panels into USB chargers, sends 🏕️ kids to summer camp, supports a 🏫 school boiler project, and ships 🎣 fishing nets used to protect roads.

📦 You'll also get a behind-the-scenes look at how aid travels from Colorado to Ukraine. Donations are stored in donated warehouse space in Aurora, where volunteers gather every two months to repack items onto pallets that fill a 40-foot shipping container. 🚛🚢🚂 From there, the container is trucked to a US port, shipped by sea to Poland, sent by train to the Ukrainian border, and trucked to a warehouse in Ukraine. The US team handles fundraising, awareness, donor relations, newsletters, purchasing, and shipping, while the Ukraine team receives and distributes aid based on vetted online orders, sending it to the nearest frontline location. 💪 The impact is real: more than 6,000 solar panels delivered to schools, medical facilities, and frontline areas with little or no electricity, 10,000 IFAKs placed in soldiers' hands, and 10 shipping containers sent in 2026 alone, with over 1,000 requests arriving each month and roughly 500 processed monthly. 💛💙 Come learn how you can help by signing up for the newsletter, volunteering at events, sharing their story with friends and family, and donating!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.description:
**Event Title:** Canvass for Change: Persuasion Canvassing with Hands Off Colorado

**Description:**

Join Hands Off Colorado for a day of voter persuasion canvassing! We'll be knocking doors and having real conversations with voters to build support for our communities, including trans and immigrant neighbors who are directly impacted by the policies on the ballot this year.

This is persuasion canvassing, which means we're not just checking in with supporters. We're talking to voters who are undecided or leaning against us, listening to their concerns, and having genuine conversations that can change minds. No experience necessary. We'll train you on everything you need to know before we head out, including how to have effective, empathetic conversations at the door.

**What to expect:**
- Brief training and script walkthrough at check-in
- Canvassing in pairs or small groups (great for first-timers!)
- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing recommended
- Snacks and water provided
- Bring a charged phone with the MiniVAN App Downloaded

**Why this matters:**
Every conversation we have moves us closer to a Colorado that stands up for all of its communities. Persuasion canvassing is one of the most effective tools we have to shift public opinion and win elections and we need volunteers like you to make it happen.

Sign up below and help us knock doors, change minds, and build the Colorado we want to live in.

We’re registered. We’re ready. Now it’s time to VOTE.

Join us October 17 as we rally for the candidates we support and bring attention to the amendments on Missouri’s November ballot.

Bring your candidate signs. Bring signs about the ballot issues that matter to you. Come help our community get informed, make a voting plan, and get ready to vote early.

No-excuse early voting begins October 20.

Saturday, October 17 | 1–3 PM Battlefield & Glenstone | Springfield, MO

Know your ballot. Know your candidates. Make your plan. Then VOTE EARLY!

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

events.title: GOTV Power Hour Phone Bank
events.description:
Join Team Hardin for our GOTV phone bank as we connect directly with voters across Columbus ahead of the Nov 3rd General Election.

This is one of the most important ways you can make an impact.
Volunteers will use our phone banking system, Scale to Win, to call voters, share key election information, and turn out the vote for Don Leonard, candidate for Congress (OH-15); Amy Acton, candidate for Governor; and Sherrod Brown, candidate for U.S. Senate. 

Whether you’re new to phone banking or have experience, we’ll make sure you’re fully prepared. Each session includes a brief training, a clear script, and support from our team so you feel confident every step of the way.

What you’ll do:
- Call voters in Columbus using our online dialer (Scale to Win)
- Share key details about the Nov. 3rd General Election and Early Voting - (October)
- Help voters make a plan to cast their ballot
- Identify supporters and strengthen our outreach efforts

What you’ll need:
A phone (cell or computer audio)
A laptop or tablet
A willingness to connect with your community

Why it matters: Elections are decided by the voters we reach. Every call you make helps ensure more people have the information they need to participate—and helps build the path to victory.

Join us, bring a friend, and be part of the team working to deliver leadership that shows up and gets results for Columbus. 
Let’s get to work.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Campton, NH!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Full Pantries, Full Plates: Community Food Drive
events.description:
Help feed Mid-Michigan families! Drop off non-perishable food and spices on Friday, October 16 from 12:00 - 1:00 PM as demand rises from SNAP cuts and record food costs.

Mid-Michigan families need a hand, and Michigan Families For Fair Care is ready to lend one. 

Food pantries are seeing more need this fall. The Republican tax law cut SNAP, and food costs are at record highs. Congressman Tom Barrett, voted for that law and supported tariffs on food that helped create this crisis. 1.5 million Michiganders rely on SNAP, and over 40% of those households have kids. And as the weather turns cold, families are squeezed between grocery bills and heating costs.

There are two ways to take part:

🥫DONATE: Drop off unopened, unexpired non-perishables or spices. 

🛒 RECEIVE: Anyone is welcome to come pick up donated items to stock your own shelves. 

Any leftover donations will go to Punks With Lunch to keep helping families through the season.

🥫 Event: Full Pantries, Full Plates: Community Food Drive

✊ Host: MI Families For Fair Care

🤝 Partner: Punks With Lunch

📍 Location: Punks With Lunch (809 Center St, Lansing, MI 48906)

📅 Date: Friday, October 16

⏰ Time:  12:00 - 1:00 PM


🥫 Non-Perishable Food (Please bring unopened, unexpired items. Plastic or cans are preferred; no glass)

- Canned vegetables and fruit

- Peanut butter and jelly

- Canned tuna or chicken

- Canned soups and stews

- Rice, pasta, pasta sauce, and dried beans

- Shelf-stable milk or milk alternatives

- Cereal and oatmeal

- Shelf-stable milk

- Boxed meals

- Cooking oil

- Flour

- Spices (salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, chili powder, paprika, Italian seasoning, cinnamon, adobo or seasoned salt, bouillon cubes)

events.title: [VIRTUAL] Twin Cities Election Update & Phonebank

sponsor.name: The Committee to Protect Health Care

events.description:
We're only a few months out from a consequential health care election, with premiums spiking, Medicaid funding cuts hitting states, and reproductive care under active legal threat. The decisions voters make this November will determine whether these harms continue or not. Let's connect as health care professionals to discuss the election and how we can make a difference. 

We will hear from Dr. Krish Subrahmanian, a pediatrician running for Minnesota State Senate in SD49, on what drove him to run for office and how his campaign is going. Senator John Marty will share why he continues to work for health care for all in Minnesota. Dr. Erin Stevens will give a quick debrief on using social media to effectively advocate. We'll end with a virtual phone bank to encourage other health care professionals to vote in the midterms due to all that is at stake for patients and practices. Don't worry - we'll give you instructions and a script!

Sign up to help us advocate for pro-patient policies!

Want to join us in-person in Minneapolis instead? Sign up here: https://www.mobilize.us/committeetoprotect/event/1055482/

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early / Brooklyn, NY / Election Protection Procession

address_lines: ACROSS the street, INSIDE Prospect Park, behind the eagle

events.description:
For No Kings 4 join fellow Brooklynites for a grand procession led by a giant bald eagle puppet, monarch butterfly puppets and other art that were made by hundreds of Brooklyn volunteers. This is the same art you may have seen at the front of No Kings 1, 2 and 3 in NYC.

We will proclaim the importance of Early Voting and protecting our elections. And we will distribute information about how to to protect and defend our elections.

START NOW by: 1. sign up for this event, 2. check your voter registration at https://vote.gov/ 3. Tell people in hot spot states to do the same. 4. And, tell them to VOTE EARLY https://electioninnovation.org/research/dates-for-2026-early-in-person-and-mail-voting/.

OCTOBER 17th at 2pm: Gather opposite TD Bank, inside the park, at Prospect Park Southwest. Make sure you are behind the giant eagle.

*This event is led by Brooklyn Resisters, an all volunteer Indivisible group.

______________________________________________________________
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Poll Observer Training with Anne Carney!
events.description:
Join the Maine Dems Voter Access Team and special guest Senator Anne Carney for Poll Observer Training on Saturday, October 10, at 10:00 am.

Poll Observers are the eyes and ears of the Voter Access Team on Election Day. When a machine goes down, a line runs long, or a voter is turned away, we only know about it because someone in the room told us. That is how we respond in time to fix it.

Training is required to be a Democratic Poll Observer, and it takes less than an hour. Every session covers the same material, so you only need to attend one.

## What you'll learn

- What you can and cannot do inside a polling place, and what your standing as a Poll Observer actually is
- How Election Day unfolds hour by hour, what to check on arrival, and how to observe the absentee canvass
- Where poll workers most often get registration and identification wrong, including why a student ID answers identity but not residence
- The issues that come up most often, from students and New Mainers to how a challenge actually works
- How to use LBJ, our reporting tool, and why it matters to log the problem you solved yourself
- What to do in rare situations, including evacuations and federal law enforcement near or in the polls

## Can't make this session?

Poll Observer Training runs online through October 30. See all sessions at https://www.mobilize.us/mainecoordinated/event/1021719/

## What happens next

The week before Election Day, we will assign you to a polling place and give you the contact numbers you need for the day.

## Who can attend

Anyone interested, 18 or older. You do not need to be a Maine resident.

Questions? Email the Maine Democratic Party Voter Access Team at votersupport@mainedems.org.

events.title: Yes4EDR Town Hall - Concord
events.description:
Join Common Cause Massachusetts for a Town Hall at the First Parish Church in Concord to discuss what a YES on ballot question #4 (Election Day Registration, or EDR) would mean for Massachusetts! Bring yourself and a few friends to this discussion.

About the Campaign

Election Day Registration (EDR) is a straightforward, secure, and proven reform to increase voter turnout and strengthen our democracy by allowing eligible voters to register to vote and cast a ballot on Election Day.

​To ensure EDR becomes law in Massachusetts, a coalition of nonpartisan, nonprofit groups that advocate for voting rights have formed the Yes 4 Election Day Registration ballot question committee. Members include Common Cause Massachusetts, League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, MassVOTE, Mass Voter Table, and the ACLU of Massachusetts. These groups have been leading the campaign for Election Day Registration in Massachusetts since 2008.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Hot Springs, AR.
events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

There will be signs, flags, water, snacks, voter information, singing resistance group, Chants, and more!

# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join the Atlantic City Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. for a celebration of civic power, music, and community spirit!

**THE VIBE:**

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍 Quaremba Hall 

📅 November 3, 2026 at 4 - 8pm

**FEATURING:**

It is never too early or and never too late to get CIVICALLY ENGAGED!!

Join The Atlantic City Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. for a fun filled “Party at the Polls” election night celebration designed to bring our community together. build voter awareness and make civic engagement a family affair. 

Get informed. Get registered. Get engaged.

Our voter education activities will help community members:
Check their voter registration status 
Learn more about the voting process 
Get information on registering to vote for the next election 
Connect with resources to become more informed and civic engaged 

And because civic engagement can be fun, come out and enjoy food vendors, music, face painting for kids, family, friendly activities, and community connections. 

Our goal is simple, increase rotor mobilization and strengthen civic education throughout our communities one informed and engaged resident at a time your voice matters your participation matters, our community matters!

**LET’S VOTE TOGETHER!** 

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

events.description:
# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Friends Meeting of New Orleans to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On Saturday, October 17th we will gather on the neutral ground on South Carrollton & Freret Street for one hour of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.title: Weekend of Action in Beaufort County
events.description:
What we're doing:
Eye-to-eye conversations are crucial. This weekend marks 30 days before in-person early voting begins in North Carolina: 10/15-31. We're heading out into NC-01 in force to knock on doors, visit Democratic + unaffiliated voters to listen + learn what's really on their minds this year, + to earn their support for Congressman Don Davis.

Why it matters:
This district has shifted again: what was once rated R+3 has been redrawn to R+5. That's a real challenge, but it also means this race is winnable, + it will come down to one thing: who shows up and has the best conversations at the door.

Thirty days out is a turning point. It's the moment voters start paying closer attention, making their plans, + deciding whether this election is worth their time. We want NC-01 to hear from us first.

We're not just asking for votes. We're listening first to what voters and their families care about, what they're worried about, + what they need from their next Representative. Then we're asking for their support, + reminding every single one of them: early voting runs October 15–31, + Election Day is November 3rd.

Why your help is essential:
Every conversation you have could be the one that moves a voter, a family, a whole household. Campaigns aren't won by ads alone, they're won door by door, by real people willing to show up and talk to voters. That's YOU. A big turnout this weekend sends a message: to voters, and to our whole team, that we're ready for the final stretch.

The ask:
Come knock doors with us this weekend. Use the script as your guide (not your script to recite), share literature, + invite folks to vote early or on Election Day.

No experience necessary: we'll train you, + our team will be right there with you every step of the way.

And a bonus: a walk is good for the spirit, and a real conversation with another human being is good for the soul. Come get both.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Are you ready to elect Emily Gregory? Do you want to show off your cool costume?

Well, come join us as we canvass in our costumes for Emily Gregory in House District 87!

You walk with a buddy, get fully trained, hand out a flyer, use a wonderful app to track your progress, and have fun doing it! It's not about going into deep policy discussions, just being a friendly neighbor to encourage awareness of Emily's platform for the November Midterm General Election.

More about Emily...

Emily Gregory is a mother of three, a military spouse, and a small business owner with a professional background in public health and mental health services. She has dedicated her career to assisting new mothers and families facing economic hardship. After a career in public health, she built her company, FIT4MOM Palm Beach, to create a healthy and supportive community for new and expecting mothers.

Emily and her family chose to make Jupiter their home for its great schools, affordability, and sense of community. However, over the past seven years, she has witnessed the rising cost of living, increasing insurance rates, and threats to the public school system. Motivated by the concerns she hears from other parents and community members, Emily is running for State Representative to bring practical, results-driven leadership to Tallahassee.

Her campaign is focused on building a healthier, more hopeful future for all Floridians.

### It's High Time For a Change

**Dan Patrick banned it. Vikki Goodwin will regulate it. Together, we'll make our voices heard**

Overnight, Dan Patrick made Delta-8 a Schedule I drug in Texas, the same category as heroin and put thousands of Texas hemp businesses out of work. He used the power of the Lieutenant Governor to force through a prohibition crusade backed by the alcohol lobby.

Vikki Goodwin has [a better plan](https://act.vikkigoodwin.com/hemp/): a sensible regulatory framework instead of outright prohibition. Real age limits, honest labeling and testing, products kept away from schools, and legal protection for Texas hemp jobs.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early (Lincoln, ME)
events.description:
This will be a non-partisan, non-violent street demonstration

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Paid for by Blue 15 PAC.

events.title: Umbrella Walk Against Genocide
events.description:
We walk against genocide, past, present, and future. Other messages are certainly welcome; our grievances are many.

We will walk from Columbus Circle at Union Station in Washington DC to the National Museum of the American Indian.

Grab an umbrella. Get to Washington DC. Be seen.

The only way out of this mess is through Congress. We must focus our energy on the center of gravity: the U.S. Capitol.

Join We the People Walk and Indivisible. Show your support of the Constitution. Demand that Congress step up to the role of co-equal branch of government. We seek justice and peace through our elected representatives.

Grab an umbrella. Get to DC. Be seen.

We ask that all participants carry umbrellas. These can have messages, as you would have on protest signs, or they can be without a message. The umbrella is the message.

We have found the best way to decorate an umbrella is to use acrylic paint markers. The 15mm markers are what work best. Be sure to let the pain dry before folding the umbrella after decorating it.

You can find more information about We the People Walk and the Umbrella Walk 4 Change at UmbrellaWalk4Change.org

events.description:
Join us for a No Kings - Vote Early event on the pedestrian bridge over Hwy 287 just north of South Boulder Road.

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard. **Please leave partisan or explicit signs at home as this event focuses on Getting out the Vote and Voting Early.** (And you don't need to bring a sign anyhow, as we will have large format letters for the overpass. Bring a flag pom-poms, or just yourself and wave!)

We look forward to you joining us!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: No Kings: The People's Ballot Party - Denver, CO
events.description:
# The People's Ballot Party

## Join the Colorado Criminal Justice Reform Coalition, ACLU of Colorado, and COLOR Latina for The People’s Ballot Party!

**Bring your ballot if you’ve got it**, and bring your questions. We’ll have food and refreshments, good company, and subject matter experts sharing information about the 14 statewide measures on Colorado’s 2026 General Election ballot.

Every choice on our ballot directs political power and public resources somewhere. We can use public policy to punish, prohibit, and restrict, or we can invest in what our communities need to thrive.

The people most directly affected by public policy should be at the center of the conversation. Come learn what’s on your ballot and make your voice heard this election.

**Food & refreshments provided**

**Bring your ballot if you’ve got it!**


**About NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY EVENTS**

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

_No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters._

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

This event is part of No Kings: Vote Early, a nonpartisan national day of action on October 17. Join us at our family-friendly [VoteFest](https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1040990/) celebration that Saturday too.

### From the national No Kings coalition:

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Phone Bank for Talarico: Comparing Approaches
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth GOTV phone bank. Every conversation we have between now and Election Day is aimed at one thing: turning out voters for Talarico. In this phone bank, you will be reaching out to voters to either mobilize them to get out the vote, or to persuade them to support Talarico through our innovative deep listening program that is changing how phone banking works and delivering insights into voters' concerns and needs to vote.

Our goal: to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the Senate. We're building necessary qualitative understanding one phone call at a time, having real conversations with real people. During Ground Truth phone banks, we will talk to as many people as possible.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

- Call persuadable voters -- oftentimes voters who don't always vote like us.

- Have real conversations that LISTEN deeply to voters’ concerns.

- Connect voters to information about James Talarico's platform to answer voters' concerns and energize them to vote.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just come prepared with your phone and laptop or computer!

We recommend using earbuds or speakerphone to free up your hands as well! 

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Rally at Pedestrian Overpass, I-95 & 147th Street, Miami, Florida

location.venue: 147th Street pedestrian overpass on I-95 in Miami
address_lines: near Thomas Jefferson/Biscayne Gardens K-8 Academy, 525 NW 147th Street, Miami, FL 33168.

events.description:
This is a high visibility rally on the NW 147th Street pedestrian overpass on I-95 in Miami to encourage people to VOTE EARLY! We will have large signs to display for drivers going north and south bound, but please bring your own! Costumes also welcome.

This event is from 11am-2pm, rain or shine, so be prepared. Parking is on the east side of I-95 on NW 6th Avenue and all around the Thomas Jefferson K-8 Academy which is at NW 147th Street and NW 6th Ave. Take the pedestrian ramp at 147th Street up to the rally. We will follow all applicable Florida laws, which means no bullhorns.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing Miami together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: FLIP the SENATE: Phone Bank with Ground Truth & TMNYC
events.description:
Join Target Majority NYC for a Ground Truth GOTV phone bank into crucial, must-win Senate races run by Swing Left—and then listen deeply to understand how you can share candidate information that will resonate with each voter to help Democrats win this year. 

This innovative program is changing how phone banking works and delivering insights into voters' concerns and needs to vote. In fact, at this  unique phone bank, we'll be following up with folks who already spoke to a Ground Truth canvasser on their doorstep! We can see the specific notes from that conversation, and pick up right where they left off. 

All the training and materials you need are provided at the start of every shift, so there's no need to be an expert or even know much about Ground Truth yet! Just come prepared with your phone and laptop or computer! We recommend using earbuds or speakerphone to free up your hands as well.

You'll quickly get the hang of it. Then TMNYCers will all join our own breakout room, where we can dial together and share our experiences in the chat.

Our goal: to help Democrats rebuild trust, win tough races, and flip the House. We're building necessary qualitative understanding one phone call at a time, having real conversations with real people. During Ground Truth phone banks, we will talk to as many people as possible and focus on listening, making the case for Democratic candidates, and making a plan to vote.

At this phone bank, we’ll:

 - Call persuadable voters -- oftentimes voters who don't always vote like us.

 - Have real conversations that LISTEN deeply to voters’ concerns.

 - Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

 - Connect voters to the Democratic Candidate and their platform to answer voters' concerns and energize them to vote.

Phone bank paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

October meeting's guest speaker is **Akemi Flynn, Managing Director of the Immigrant Protection & Empowerment Network (IPEN) at Amigos de Guadalupe**. events.title: Democracy Hub Canvass with Friendship Baptist

sponsor.name: Milwaukee Innercity Congregations Allied for Hope

events.description:
This isn’t just any election year. Our ability to make decisions for ourselves, our democracy is at risk. In the leadup to the November 2026 election, MICAH’s We All Belong Committee is calling on people of faith to rally neighbors, friends and family to vote – and to vote their values! We All Belong was created to protect democracy, reject white Christian nationalism, and build the Beloved Community. As part of that mission, We All Belong is inviting congregations to join the Democracy Collective.

The Democracy Collective is designed to strengthen congregations’ ability to educate and activate voters while creating deeper relationships, inside and out of the congregation. Central to the Collective are Democracy Hubs: neighborhood canvasses anchored by a MICAH congregation, organized in collaboration with other congregations. Canvassers receive training and food. 

Maybe your congregation is ready to get involved and looking for a good entry point. Maybe you are looking to get more engaged as a person of faith. We're excited to have you.

events.title: PEN DEMS: Lunch w Rahm Emanuel at Bay Street Biergarten
events.description:
We’re taking over Bay Street Biergarten for lunch and a conversation with Rahm Emanuel, one of the most influential and famously unfiltered voices in the Democratic Party.

Rahm has seen modern Democratic politics from just about every angle. He was an adviser to President Clinton, member of Congress, chief of staff to President Obama, mayor of Chicago and U.S. ambassador to Japan.

Lately, he’s been making waves again with a steady run of blunt arguments about where Democrats go next: rebuild the middle class, get serious about education and affordability, clean up government and speak like normal people. He is not exactly known for holding back. He joined Pen Dems for a meeting earlier this year, and we're happy to welcome him back. 

Join Pen Dems for a Friday lunch and a real conversation with someone who has been in the room for some of the biggest political moments of the last 30 years and has plenty to say about the future.

Space is limited. RSVP now.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early in DC's Ward 4

address_lines: Kansas Avenue Northwest & Georgia Avenue Northwest

events.description:
Join Free DC's Ward 4 Team at 11:30am at Paul Robeson Triangle Park (across from the Petworth Library).

We'll joyfully take up space and share info on early voting and election protection plans. Bring your ballot to vote early with your community! 

Coffee, donuts, and kids activities will be provided! 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Chalk the Walk and Vote
events.description:
Join Us for Chalk the Vote: Make Your Mark! 🎨✨
Turn sidewalks into a canvas for democracy!
Come out for a family-friendly, creative time where we use colorful sidewalk art to spread the word about voting in DuPage County. Whether you are an artist or just want to pick up a piece of chalk, you can help us inspire our community to make their voices heard.
While we decorate the pavement with vibrant, positive messages, we are also here to make sure you are election-ready! Stop by to:
• 📝 Check your voter registration status in just two minutes
• 📍 Find your exact polling location so you know exactly where to go
• 🗓️ Learn about early in-person voting—consult official DuPage County election resources to verify the early voting schedule, learn how it fits your calendar, and understand the importance of making your plan to vote.
No art experience required—just bring your energy and community spirit! We will provide all the chalk, templates, and helpful voter guides. Let’s vibrant-up our walkways and walk the walk all the way to the ballot box!

events.title: NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY Merrimac MA
events.description:
Celebrate Our Voting Rights!

Join us to celebrate early voting and election defense! Join our joyful, peaceful sidewalk stand out with your voting rights signs to show our voting pride and spread the message that everyone needs to exercise their right to vote and VOTE EARLY! Stockpiling the early vote is a powerful form of election protection. Together, we will inspire others to stand up and vote, remind people that they are not alone, and get ready to defend the election.

ATTENTION MERRIMAC RESIDENTS: Come to Merrimac's NO KINGS event on the 17th to stand out AND vote early! You can vote early at Merrimac Town Hall from 10am-4pm that day. Vote early before the stand out or during the stand out or after the stand out! Join others from Merrimac who will be voting early that day! events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to CA-48—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Marni von Wilpert. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Corona around 9:00am and return around 5:00pm. 
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 10:00-4:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

events.title: A Panel on Voting Rights and The Centrality of Elections for Democracy
events.description:
**A panel on voting rights and the centrality of elections for democracy**

In the context of the inauguration of the exhibition “The Revolutionary Idea: A Window on Voting in America” by Anna Rotty & Greg Miller, we present a panel on voting rights and the centrality of elections for democracy.

Inspired by Frederick Douglass’s 1852 speech “What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?,” “The Revolutionary Idea” brings together the work of Anna Rotty and Greg Miller, two photographers who independently turned their attention to the people and spaces that make elections possible. Through photography, audio, printmaking and found materials, their work considers the voters, poll workers and election officials whose collective labor sustains our democratic process.

_Speakers:_

- Judge Andy Gaona, Arizona Court of Appeals

- Greg Miller, Photographer and Educator, Guggenheim Fellow 

- Anna Rotty, Artist and Educator, University of New Mexico

- Gregory Sale, Artist and ASU educator, co-lead #ArtistsWhoVote 

- Margaret Shultz, Researcher, Worker Power

- Cathy Sigmon, Co-Director, Civic Engagement Beyond Voting


---------------------------
Event contact: Mehrdad Mirzaie, mmirzaie@asu.edu

https://asuevents.asu.edu/event/panel-voting-rights-and-centrality-elections-democracy

# Love as Action: Resisting Authoritarianism

### Quaker public witness has stood in opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again. 

Please join the American Friends Service Committee and Friends Meeting of Austin to bear witness and show resistance to the authoritarian actions in our country. 

On October 17 at 10am we will gather at the Texas Capitol for one hour of silent public worship.

Our hope is that our presence will give hope to all who see us – to show that we can choose resistance - and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

We gather monthly in communities across the country, showing our communities love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

Join us! 

To find our more about Love as Action nationally and get more resources visit us at [afsc.org/love-action](www.afsc.org/love-action)

events.description:
This No Kings action is going to look a little different and be a LOT of fun.  On October 17, we're adopting four (4) Early Voting locations across Nashville and turning them into celebrations of democracy.

Instead of one big march or rally, we'll be out where the voters are, lining sidewalks, waving signs at passing traffic, wearing costumes and creating positive energy.

LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!
Create change. Then let’s celebrate. 

Esōes is turning 5, and we’re celebrating the only way we know how: by creating change and throwing a really good party while we’re at it.

For five years, we’ve turned our passion into action. This year, we’re taking that same energy to the ballot box.

events.title: Salinas Hwy 101 Bridge Overpass Protest, this Friday, from 4:30 -5:30 pm

location.venue: Hwy 101 overpass behind Mt. Toro High School

events.description:
Join us for our Hwy 101 Bridge Protest on Friday.
We meet on top of the Hwy 101 Overpass Bridge located behind Mount Toro High High School from 4:30 - 5:30 pm
We will already have huge easy-to-read messages to set up facing the highway which will be seen by thousands of cars on highway 101 as well as the cars going over the overpass. Those who attend can wave their hands and cheer on support from cars below and on the street behind us

The Visibility Brigade (VB) is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability*. You participate with this understanding. See VB guidelines below:

VB guidelines and protocal are in this doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/12vigayVE4sCN922zsWbsq4wcKgDKEmNFMFlNWb1F6Yk/edit?usp=sharing

*Minors are required to have a waiver signed by a confirmed (parent or guardian) prior to participation. Copies of form are available at the event or at link below:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o4xNJUnh6abwHFhNnAzI4C7JUn0H_Ypbpxqj3tgNSlc/edit?usp=sharing

Bring: Yourself (and friends), a windbreaker, and a clear mind as the bridge is narrow and you'll need to be able to have enough balance to stay out from cars rushing past. The wind is generally forceful at this location so be mindful of the fact that larger signs can act like a wind sail and try to blow you into traffic (so smaller signs are safer generally).

Parking: The gravel parking entryway is below the bridge. It is only accessible from the right side from the north flowing traffic on 330 Sherwood Drive, Salinas CA 93906. Just before you enter the parking area you will see the sign that says, "Home of the Toros" and "Be More". Please park on the right-hand shoulder.

Bathrooms: Ensen Community Park 600 Sherwood Drive for bathrooms about 2000 feet away from the event.
events.accessibility_notes: The ramp up to the bridge might be steep for a person with mobility issues

events.title: Save Your Spot: Bus to Maine to flip the Senate!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a planned day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Troy Jackson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

This trip is currently unconfirmed—we need to reach a threshold of 25 sign-ups by October 9 to make this bus a reality. **By signing up here, you are saving your spot and helping make this trip happen.**

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### Here is the plan:
- **Sign up now and help us reach our volunteer goal:** As soon as we hit 25 volunteers, we will confirm the bus, finalize the departure details, and reach out to you immediately.
- **Ready to roll:** Once confirmed, your bus captain will provide departure details, training, and the Ground Truth conversation guide.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave [Launch site] on [Date and time] and return around [Return time].
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly [Canvassing hours].
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. Can we count on you to help us get this bus on the road? Sign up today!

—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

_Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft.org](http://swingleft.org/), not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee._

events.description:
Join us for a canvass with WA Working Families Party. We're knocking doors with our endorsed candidates in Washington's 37th legislative district! The Nov 3rd election is a month away- help us get the word out to our neighbors about these incredible working peoples' champions!

Location: We will be meeting at Columbia Park ( right outside of the Columbia City PCC) at 11am!

Kelabe Tewolde (LD37 - House Seat 1) is a child of refugees who advocates to stop redlining and environmental racism on the Seattle Planning Commission and an educator who mentors and uplifts youth of color with Rainier Scholars, and is challenging a 27-year-incumbent who has voted to increase rents and lower taxes on corporations. Kelabe, in contrast, is by community and for community.

Jaelynn Scott (LD37 - House Seat 2) is a Black trans activist and proud socialist who serves as Executive Director of the Lavender Rights Project, a national black trans feminist advocacy organization advancing justice for gender diverse communities. She has spent years working in community, organizing, responding to crisis calls, helping people find sanctuary, and trying to help folks navigate the confusing, frustrating, broken system of social services.

If it’s your first time, no worries! Each session starts with a brief training & Q&A. Don't be afraid to reach out with questions!

events.title: No Kings: Get Out and Vote Arnold Missouri
events.description:
Join 50501 and No Kings on Saturday, October 17, from 3:00–5:00 PM in Arnold, Missouri at the Church Rd. Overpass, as we come together to make our voices heard and encourage our community to get out and vote!

We believe that meaningful change starts with participation, and one of the most powerful ways to make our voices heard is at the ballot box. Whether you’re passionate about candidates, ballot amendments, or the issues affecting our communities, we invite you to show up, stand together, and make your voice count.

BRING YOUR SIGNS!

Participants are encouraged to bring signs ballot amendments, or causes they believe in. This is an opportunity to stand in solidarity, engage with our community, and remind one another that our voices matter. Some signs will be provided.

Nonviolence is one of our core values, and we remain dedicated to peaceful, respectful, and inclusive action. We ask everyone attending to help us maintain a welcoming environment where people can express their views without intimidation, harassment, or violence. We may disagree, but we can stand together for the kind of change we want to see.

DIGNITY DRAWERS DONATION DRIVE

We will also be collecting donations for Dignity Drawers, a local initiative working to address period poverty by providing accessible menstrual hygiene products to those who need them.

If you would like to contribute, please consider bringing:

* Pads
* Tampons
* Panty liners
* Other menstrual hygiene products

Every donation helps support dignity, accessibility, and our neighbors in need.

Whether you’re coming to hold a sign, connect with candidates, support voting efforts, or donate to Dignity Drawers, we would love to have you join us!

Bring your signs. Bring your voice. Let’s show up for our communities and make our voices heard. Change starts with us, and it starts at the ballot box. ✊

📅 Date: October 17, 2026
⏰ Time: 3:00–5:00 PM
📍 Location: Arnold, Missouri (Church Rd. Overpass)

Please share this event and invite others to join us!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Banned Book Club - To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee
events.description:
Join us each month for a new book from our ever growing banned or challenged book list. Where we choose a new title each month and combine reading out loud in a group setting, reading alone, and discussing how the books might correspond to the world around us.

This month we will spend the first half discussing Civil Disobedience by Henry David Thoreau and the second half will be focused on the beginning of To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee.

October 19th & 26th, will be dedicated to starting To Kill A Mockingbird by Harper Lee and we will finish it throughout November. 

Please make sure to add any suggestions to the Google spreadsheet shared in the Zoom chat before the third week of the month to have a chance at it being selected for the next month. The event name will be updated once the title is selected.

The meetings are 90 minutes long and broke down into 3 parts. The first half hour is spent discussing the section that was designed or our anticipations on what the book might be like. The middle section we read out loud, and the last half hour is spent going over what we read and assigning the next section.

So far we have read the following titles and discussed how they correlate with our present day. 

The Diary of a Yong Girl – Anne Frank 
1984 – George Orwell 
Animal Farm – George Orwell 
Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury 
Looking Backward – Edward Bellamy 
The Age of Reason - Thomas Paine 
Howl and Other Poems - Allen Ginsberg

All are welcome and even if you haven’t picked up the book feel free to join us for the discussion and reading.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Pro-Democracy Task Force
events.description:
Our democracy is in trouble. Our voting rights are under attack. This administration is trying to take us backwards and undermine our civil liberties. 

But we are not powerless. Their agenda can only succeed if we comply or idly stand by. 

With upcoming congressional and state house elections, we have a unique opportunity to stop the coalition of regression from growing their power. 

Elections are one of the main levers of our democracy. We must take action now to keep it that way.

Join us to learn how you can build community power to protect elections in your neck of the woods. 

We will provide a series of trainings to help you understand what we are up against, discuss election protection and what role everyday people can play, develop a county-based strategy and build community with individuals participating in this effort in different parts of the country.

“The arc of the moral universe bends towards justice - but only if we pull it.”
-MLK Jr.

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Madison

address_lines: Capitol Building, State Street Entrance, Madison, WI

events.description:
He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

Date: Wednesday, October 15th
Time: 1:00pm
Location: Capital Building, State Street Entrance, Madison, WI

Harry Dunn is joining citizens of Madison for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.

Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.

This event kicks off our No Kings: Vote Early weekend — three days of action in to protect this election and get Wisconsin voting early, building to the national 
This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.

Come ready to:

Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection
Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard
Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it
RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

Safety Volunteers Needed for WACO NO KINGS – LET'S VOTE! 

We need Safety Volunteers for our last Freedom Corner Protest before the Election, 17 October, 10:00 am to 11:30am at the corner of North Valley Mills Drive and West Waco Drive .

We need up to 12 Safety Volunteers to assist us in keeping the protest safe and distribute voter guides and other Election information..  This a a great job for all of you that have helped us as Safeties in the protests since Jan 2025!

Safety Volunteers wear reflective vests, carry whistles and may have radios for a large protest and stand behind the line to make sure that our safety protocols are followed.  They also monitor surrounding areas for any potential problems.

As always, this is a 100% nonviolent and safe action.  Protesters stay on the sidewalk along Valley Mills Drive and at the corner. Stay out of the street. Don't waive your signs and flags out into the street.  Do not impede passers by or vehicles in the parking lot. Deescalate any tense situation.  Park in authorized parking spaces.  Obey pedestrian traffic signals.  

Cheerfully engage with opponents, but, If things get too heated, stop talking, turn around, walk away.  Leave if you perceive danger.  Absolutely no weapons, not even legal ones. We will follow the instructions of law enforcement.

You should arrive at 9:45am to get your vest and a quick briefing.  We will  be done packing up and gone by 12:00 Noon.   

If you would like to help us encourage safety, sign up here!

events.title: Camp Verde ALPR Community Discussion & Next Steps
events.description:
The conversation continues — and we need you there.

Join your Camp Verde neighbors for a community discussion about Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology currently being used in our community.

📅 Saturday, November 7
⏰ 9:00 AM
📍 Camp Verde Community Library
130 N. Black Bridge Loop, Camp Verde, AZ

This meeting is an opportunity to come together, share what we’ve learned, ask questions, and talk about what comes next.

We’ll discuss:

🔹 What we know about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde
🔹 Questions and concerns from our community
🔹 What we’ve learned so far
🔹 How we can continue educating our neighbors
🔹 What steps we can take to encourage the Town to reconsider this technology
🔹 How YOU can get involved

You don't need to be an expert or have followed this issue from the beginning. If you care about privacy, transparency, and having a voice in decisions that affect our community, you are welcome.

📚 Want to get caught up before the meeting?

Visit: CampVerdePrivacy.org.

There you can learn more about the ALPR technology being used in Camp Verde, read background information and previous meeting materials, find educational resources and literature, and sign our community petition.

Whether you're just learning about this issue or have been involved from the beginning, there's a place for you in this conversation.

Come bring your questions, your ideas, and your voice.

❤️ Together, let's figure out what comes next.

events.title: 10/10 - Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization @ Pasadena Indoor Flea Market (Houston)

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Election Day, November 3rd is around the corner! Come make a huge difference with us!  Create awareness in the community about the consequential midterm election. 

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization** shift at **Pasadena Indoor Flea Market**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Check voters’ status on the spot
- Register eligible voters when we have a VDR at the event. Or hand out the paper voter registration form.
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:

- **1:00-1:30am: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals.

- **1:30am-3:30pm: Hotspotting & Voter Registration** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, register voters, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **3:30-4:00pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, turn in completed registration forms, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

**We’ll table so meet us at the table with “Talarico for Texas “ banner inside the flea market.**

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**:  We’ll table so meet us at the table with Talarico sign in the flea market.  


- **Volunteer Parking**:  Parking available at flea market parking lot. 

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, voter registration forms, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

### Join Texas Together in Grand Prairie as we ramp up the action to Get Out The Vote and knock doors to support **Texas Democratic** nominees up and down the ballot. 

It’s time to organize, unify, and build the movement that will carry us through the last 31 days until Election Day, November 3, 2026.

During the block walk, volunteers will:

- Identify Democratic supporters

- Share information about our Democratic ticket

- Listen to voters about the issues impacting their families and communities

Every door knocked strengthens our grassroots efforts and brings us one step closer to winning up and down the ballot.

No experience necessary! We’ll provide training, materials, and turf at the start of each shift. 

Just bring comfortable shoes, a fully charged phone, water, and a friend.
**RSVP today and be part of the team building Democratic wins in Texas — one conversation at a time.**

Community kickoff event for Count Me In Wilkinsburg + Civics Workshop

Too often, decisions about what happens in communities happen without the people who live in those communities. 

This year and next, we’ll work with a collaborative of local partners to listen and learn from residents about their needs and how to do a better job of supporting their well-being.

Come meet your neighbors and learn how to get involved.

But, this is more than just a meet and greet. We will spend some time learning how to make change in our community.

Food will be provided and fun przes awarded!
