events.title: No Kings: McKinney Morning Caravan - Get Out The Vote!

location.venue: Starting Near Wholefoods at 380/University and Custer

events.description:
## NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY

### McKinney Traveling Action - Saturday, October 17, 2026

### Six stops. One community. One message: YOUR VOTE MATTERS.

Join us for a rolling No Kings: Vote Early action through McKinney!

Rather than staying in one place, we're taking the message to several parts of our community. We'll decorate our cars, travel together from stop to stop, and spend 30 minutes at each location holding signs that encourage people to VOTE EARLY and tell them YOUR VOTE MATTERS, along with info about voting.

You can join us for the entire route or meet us at whichever stop works best for you.

#### 🚗 THE DAY'S SCHEDULE

#### 1. 9:30 AM — CAR DECORATING & MEET-UP
We'll gather, decorate our cars, get organized, and get ready to roll.
#### 10:00–10:30 AM — STOP 1
📍 Whole Foods — University & Custer

We'll kick off the traveling action with our signs and our message: VOTE EARLY. YOUR VOTE MATTERS. INFORMATION ABOUT VOTING.

#### 2. 11:00–11:30 AM — STOP 2
📍 H-E-B — Eldorado Pkwy

We'll take the Vote Early message to another busy part of McKinney.

#### 3. 12:00–12:30 PM — STOP 3
📍 Near Panera — Eldorado & US-75

Another 30 minutes of visible, peaceful voter encouragement.

#### 4. 1:00–1:30 PM — STOP 4
📍 Near Sprouts — Virginia Pkwy & US-75

We'll keep moving north and bring the message with us.

#### 5. 2:00–2:30 PM — STOP 5
📍 Downtown McKinney — near MPAC / the downtown square

We'll make our final community stop downtown before heading to the day's big gathering.

#### 6. 3:00 PM — FINAL STOP / JOIN THE BIG PROTEST
📍 US-75 & University

**We'll finish our caravan by joining the larger No Kings action near University and US-75.**
https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1024569/

### WHY WE'RE DOING THIS

No Kings: Vote Early is a nonpartisan voter-participation effort. On October 17, we're turning people power into voter power by bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early, understand their options for how to vote, and make sure every eligible voter has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

We're taking that message directly into our community.

We're not just holding signs in one place. We're bringing the message with us.

🚗 Decorate your car.
📣 Bring your signs.
👋 Bring your friends and neighbors.
🗳️ Make a plan to vote early.
🗳️ Remind people that their vote matters.

Whether you come for the whole caravan or meet us at one stop, we'd love to have you with us.

### SIX STOPS.
### ONE COMMUNITY.
### ONE MESSAGE.

## VOTE EARLY.

## YOUR VOTE MATTERS.


_No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters._

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

#NoKingsVoteEarly #NoKingsVoteEarlyMcKinneyTx

events.description:
Conestoga Valley Democrats is looking for volunteers for Election Day poll observers and greeters. 

The poll observer’s role is to watch and report any irregularities, without directly interfering with election workers or voters.

The greeters inform people who come to vote, answer any questions, and hand out the “Voted” stickers. 

Shifts could be: 
 
- all day
- half day (morning)
- half day (afternoon / evening) - peak hours 7-9am;
- peak hours 9am-12pm;
- peak hours 12-2pm; 
- peak hours 2pm-5pm; 
- peak hours 5pm-8pm 

Training will be provided. 

Sign up and we will send additional training information. 

Plan to join for in person training on Wednesday October 24 or Sunday November 1.

events.title: Phone Bank with Scotland Dems
events.description:
Did you know nearly half of eligible voters sit out midterm elections, even though these races decide who controls Congress, state legislatures, school boards, and more? We're changing that, one call at a time!

Join us for a friendly, low-pressure phone bank where we reach out to voters who've skipped past midterms and help them commit to voting this year. No experience needed! We'll provide a simple script, talking points, and a quick training before every shift.

What we're asking callers to do:

*Make warm, respectful calls to identified midterm-skippers in our target area
*Invite people to make a personal pledge to vote
*Help callers find their polling place or request a mail ballot if needed

Why it matters:
Research consistently shows that a friendly personal contact, especially one that invites someone to make a concrete pledge is one of the most effective ways to boost turnout. You don't need to be a political expert. You just need to be willing to have a conversation.

Details:
📅  Mix of Wednesdays and Mondays, 6:00–8:00 PM
📍 Virtual: Link sent upon RSVP
💻 Laptop/phone with a headset recommended for virtual shifts

Whether you can make 10 calls or 100, every conversation helps someone turn "I usually skip midterms" into "I'm voting this year." Sign up for one shift or make it a weekly habit,  we'd love to have you.

events.description:
**Join Us for a Postcard Writing Party! 🗳️✍️**
Hosted by Jennifer Guthals and Annmarie Izuel Evans 

Come write postcards that make a difference! We're teaming up with Blue Wave Postcards for an afternoon of community, snacks, and civic action.

Postcards are one of the most effective and personal ways to reach voters — and we'll have everything you need to get started: pre-printed postcards, addressed voter lists, pens, and talking points. No experience necessary, and Blue Wave Postcards volunteers will be on hand to help first-timers get the hang of it.

**What to expect:**

A brief welcome and overview of the campaign and why this outreach matters
Pre-sorted postcards and voter lists ready to go
Light refreshments and good company
A relaxed, social atmosphere — write at your own pace, chat with fellow volunteers

What to bring:

Yourself! (And a friend, if you'd like — this is more fun together)
Your own pen, if you have a favorite

Why it matters:
Handwritten postcards get noticed. Research consistently shows that personal, handwritten outreach increases voter turnout more than mailers or digital ads alone. Every card you write is a small act that adds up to real impact.

Whether you can stay the whole time or just drop by for twenty minutes, every postcard counts. We'll have a table set up so you can jump in whenever works for your schedule.

RSVP below to save your spot — we can't wait to write with you!

events.title: Carleton and St. Olaf excursion to Farmington
events.description:
*Come take a walk on the wild side!*  Farmington, 13 miles up the road from Northfield, is an entirely different community. Come help distribute postcards in support of Mark Legvold and Ed Fellows to targeted addresses throughout Farmington.  This will be a fast-moving project, and we need a lot of people to knock it out in one day!

We will launch from a private home in Farmington where you'll choose a route, fill your coffee cup and your water bottle, and head out.  We'll be using the miniVAN just as you do for door knocking, except this is simply a literature drop: we just leave a postcard in the front door, record it in the app, and move on.  Routes vary in size, pick what is comfortable for you.  You can work in pairs if you'd like, but it's not necessary.

**Meet in the El Triunfo parking lot (200 2nd St W) at 9:00am.** A shuttle will pick you up and deliver you back.  Your driver is Denny Haines you can text him at 952-299-8582.

We'll buy pizza before taking you back to Northfield.  End time is flexible, could be before or after 2pm.

Prepared and paid for by Dakota County DFL 20/58, P.O. Box 142, 113 Elm St, Farmington MN 55024, in support of Mark Legvold and Ed Fellows.

events.title: Show Our Strength Labor Phone Bank
events.description:
Help us mobilize union members for the November General Election!

Join the Metropolitan Washington Labor Council, AFL-CIO every Tuesday and Thursday in October as we phone bank fellow union members about Question 1 – Arbitration Reform for State Employees, a critical ballot question on the November General Election ballot.

This is a union-to-union organizing effort. We’ll be reaching out directly to our fellow union members, talking with them about what Question 1 means for public employees and the importance of standing together to protect collective bargaining and workers’ rights.

No previous phone banking experience is necessary. We’ll provide everything you need—including training, talking points, and support. All you need to bring is your voice, your commitment to the labor movement, and a willingness to have conversations with your fellow union members.

Join us on Tuesdays and Thursdays throughout October. Every call matters. Every conversation matters. And when union members stand together, we can win.

Sign up today and help us make sure union members are informed, engaged, and ready to vote YES on Question 1!

Help us mobilize union households for the November General Election!

Join the Metropolitan Washington Labor Council, AFL-CIO on Saturday mornings in Southern Maryland to knock doors and talk directly with fellow union members and union households about Question 1 – Arbitration Reform for State Employees, a critical ballot question on the November General Election ballot.

No canvassing experience is necessary. We’ll provide training, materials, talking points, and everything you need to have effective conversations at the doors.

Bring your comfortable shoes, your labor movement spirit, and a willingness to talk with your fellow union members. Every door we knock is an opportunity to build union power and win in November.

Sign up today and join us Saturday mornings in Southern Maryland!

When union members knock doors together, we win together.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in East Greenbush/NY 19
events.description:
HELP GET THE WORD OUT ABOUT EARLY VOTING AND SUPPORT FOR JOSH RILEY!
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats rebuild trust and win back power in the Midterms and beyond. We’re launching an [innovative new program](https://ourgroundtruth.org) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

**Winning this district, NY 19, is critical in order for us to retake the House.**

__PLEASE DON'T GHOST US!__ 

+ IF YOU HAVE TO CANCEL, PLEASE LET US KNOW ASAP. 
+ RESPOND IF WE TEXT YOU.

__IMPORTANT INFORMATION:__ 
+ PLEASE WATCH FOR EMAILS WITH IMPORTANT PREPARATIONS TO DO BEFORE CANVASS DAY 
+ IF YOU PLAN TO BRING A PARTNER PLEASE HAVE THEM SIGNED UP HERE ON MOBILIZE! 
+ YOU MUST HAVE A PHONE WITH THE MIC ENABLED.  

__Your confirmation email from Mobilize will include important training materials that will need to be reviewed and acted on before the canvass!__

At this canvass, we’ll:

- Have real conversations that **listen deeply** to voters’ concerns.

- Gather insights to share with campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we’re starting early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns got off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* knocking every door, not just the ones the voter database tells us to, so every conversation builds a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* practicing empathetic listening and real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Bridge Brigade event in Mineral Wells, WV
events.description:
We are going to make sure as many people as possible know when early voting starts in West Virginia!  On Saturday, October 17th, join us for a Bridge Brigade visibility event on the Mineral Wells exit overpass on Interstate 77.  We will be out there from 11 am to 12:30 pm, holding up large individual letters to spell out our message to the folks traveling south on Interstate 77.  In addition, we will be holding banners and signs promoting early voting for the people traveling on the overpass, heading into and out of Parkersburg.

The message on the banners and signs will be  "Beat the Horde. Vote Early."  Some of us will be dressed as zombies. Everyone is welcome to dress as a zombie, or not, dressing up is optional. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

Please leave signage that is partisan at home.  No signs promoting candidates, or issues that are identified as party specific are allowed at non-partisan events.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*
events.accessibility_notes: This event is outdoors.  There is no bathroom available.  There is a slight slope to get from the parking area up to the overpass bridge but no steps.  There is no sidewalk from the parking area up to the overpass.

events.title: James Byrd Senate Debate

events.title: Protect the Vote: Inside Poll Observer On-Demand Training
events.description:
### This is the _On-Demand_ training, you can find the _Live on Zoom_ training here: https://mobilize.us/s/lADmOM

# Protect the Vote as a Poll Observer

Every voter deserves the chance to cast a ballot and have it counted.

Inside Poll observers help ensure election laws are followed, identify potential issues, and report concerns so they can be addressed quickly. Most shifts are calm and routine, and you will never be expected to handle situations on your own. We'll provide the training, resources, and support you need to be successful.

### What You'll Learn

- Poll observer basics
- What to expect at the polling place
- Updated guidance for situations observers may encounter this fall
- What to look for and how to document issues
- How to report concerns and get support
- The role poll observers play in protecting voters

### Why It Matters

With critical elections ahead, we need trained volunteers in every corner of North Carolina.

Poll observers serve as our eyes and ears inside polling places, helping ensure election laws are followed and that voters can cast their ballots without unnecessary barriers.

Whether you've done this work before or are brand new, we'll help you get ready.

#### No Prior Experience Required

We'll provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel confident serving as a poll observer.

### After signing up, you'll be directed to the recorded training video and next steps.

#### Important: If you are an **attorney, law graduate, or law student** looking to serve as an **At-Large Legal Poll Observer through the NC Voter Protection Alliance (NCVPA),** please sign up here: https://tinyurl.com/NC26LegalPollObserver

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early in Boone County, Indiana
events.description:
One Day -- October 17, 2026
Two Asks -- Vote Early and Feed the Hungry
Three Towns -- Zionsville, Whitestown, and Lebanon
NO KINGS!!

We will be encouraging everyone to vote early. We will show them how to access their registration information and their polling locations.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing people in Boone County together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard. 

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, NO KINGS! Vote early to be sure your voice is heard.

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

Indivisible Boone Indiana wants to ensure that our neighbors have access to nutritious food. Participants will be encouraged to support food banks that serve our area.

FYI- This event is a roaming event starting in Zionsville, moving to Whitestown and finishing in Lebanon. See below for timing.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events. Signs for the streetside events should encourage Early Voting, refrain from promoting individual candidates and be free of profanity.*

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

Let's make this a joyful and fun day with your friends. Feel free to dress up in a fun costume and most importantly, wear a smile!

events.title: Reach Your Friends. Help Pat Win.
events.description:
The most powerful political conversation isn’t always with a campaign volunteer or an advertisement, it’s with someone you already know and trust.

That’s why Team Halpin is launching Reach, a simple tool that lets you connect with friends, family, neighbors and coworkers who live in the district and personally encourage them to vote.

With Election Day just weeks away, we need supporters like you helping us have thousands of real, personal conversations about what’s at stake in this election.

Here’s how it works:
1. Sign up here on Mobilize.
2. You’ll receive a link that takes you directly into the Reach App
3. Reach will help you identify people you know who may live in the district.
4. You can then send them information about the campaign, use content and videos for social posts. 
5. Follow up and make sure they have a plan to vote.

You don’t need a script. You don’t need campaign experience. And you can do it from anywhere.

Even reaching out to 5 or 10 people you know can make a difference.

This is one of the most important midterm elections of our lifetimes. The decisions Washington makes over the next two years will affect the cost of living, healthcare, housing, Social Security and Medicare, public safety, our environment, and the future of our democracy.

The best messenger to someone you know is YOU.

Sign up, open Reach, and start a conversation today.

Let’s win this one conversation at a time.

events.title: Raise Your Voice: Civic Engagement for Environmental Justice

events.description:
### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a **Voter Mobilization** shift at **"Faith on the Front Lines" film premiere at the Angelika Theatre**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **[5:00pm-5:30pm]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **[5:30pm-6:30pm] Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, and get folks set up on Reach.

- [Movie 6:30 pm - 8:00 pm] 

Website: https://www.faithonthefrontlinesfilm.com

 
- **[8:00-9:00pm]: Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, and get folks set up on Reach.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing


Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

address_lines: East Capitol Street Northeast & First Street Northeast

events.description:
Daily from 12:15-12:30pm 
US Capitol East Front Plaza

RAIN OR SHINE, GRAB AN UMBRELLA AND BE SEEN.

When you arrive at the East Front Plaza of the U.S. Capitol, simply walk around and take in the scene. Do not gather in a static group, sit down, or set your umbrella on the ground; keep moving naturally along the wide public plaza perimeter maintaining a respectful physical buffer from other participants.

You are free to carry any umbrella, whether plain or bearing a message. Remain silent and avoid speeches, chanting, or loud noise. 

Circulate the Front East Plaza perimeter at your own pace until about 12:30pm, then simply turn and disperse as an individual, leaving the grounds just as quietly and seamlessly as you arrived.

Don't worry if only a few people show up, after all you are just out for a stroll. Keep coming back!

Umbrella Walk 4 Change

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Lisbon, NH!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

events.title: Hop on the bus from NYC to knock doors in NY-17 to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to NY-17—a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Cait Conley. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Hudson Yards at 9:30am and return around 6:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Fairfax Honk and Wave
events.description:
Our regular Saturday Honk and Wave will be a No Kings: Vote Early event. Please bring signs appropriate for encouraging participation in our Democracy by voting. Information on why to vote, where to vote, and how to cast your ballot. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.description:
We know the best way to protect our rights is to exercise them. So on October 17, we’re organizing thousands of our fellow St. Louisans to ensure every eligible voter has a plan to vote early, knows their options for how to vote, and is ready to help defend the results.

Instead of multiple protests, we're coming together for one all county event at 270 and Olive. We'll be lining the sidewalks with signs and messages designed to motivate early voting.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Berlin, NH!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Cherokee County Texas
events.description:
Rally Out the Early Vote: Cherokee County Texas

Here in Cherokee County, Texas, our power is in our turnout. Every registered voter who casts their ballot early brings us one step closer to protecting our communities, defending working families, and countering the outsized influence of billionaires and corporate interests.
Change doesn’t begin in Washington—it starts right here at our local polling places. When we show up early, we build momentum, take pressure off Election Day, and ensure every voice is counted.  
Help us counter the trillionaire (Musk) and billionaires who are trying to buy our elections.  High turnout is the single most effective way everyday working people can challenge deep-pocketed special interests. 


**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

Are you ready to elect Emily Gregory? Do you want to show off your cool costume? 

Well, come join us as we canvass in our costumes for Emily Gregory in House District 87!

You walk with a buddy, get fully trained, hand out a flyer, use a wonderful app to track your progress, and have fun doing it! It's not about going into deep policy discussions, just being a friendly neighbor to encourage awareness of Emily's platform for the November Midterm General Election.

More about Emily...

Emily Gregory is a mother of three, a military spouse, and a small business owner with a professional background in public health and mental health services. She has dedicated her career to assisting new mothers and families facing economic hardship. After a career in public health, she built her company, FIT4MOM Palm Beach, to create a healthy and supportive community for new and expecting mothers.

Emily and her family chose to make Jupiter their home for its great schools, affordability, and sense of community. Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few.

Right now, our movement is winning. Why?

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement.

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up.

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us.

Let’s get to work.

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.description:
USE YOUR SUPERPOWER — VOTE EARLY!
Early Vote Walk + Rally
Saturday, October 24, 2026 • 11:00 AM–1:00 PM
Hawthorne, NJ
Exact gathering location and route details will be provided to registered participants.

Your voice matters. Your vote matters. And your vote is your superpower.

Join The Resistance Alliance — Hawthorne, NJ as we kick off early voting with a joyful, nonpartisan Early Vote Walk + Rally celebrating one of our most fundamental rights as citizens: the right to make our voices heard at the ballot box.

This event has two parts — and everyone is welcome to participate.

PART ONE: WALK TO VOTE

We’ll gather at 11:00 AM in Hawthorne and make our way together toward the early-voting location.

If you are a registered Passaic County voter, come vote early with us! We’ll walk together in a celebratory show of civic participation before transitioning from rally participants to voters as we approach the voting location.

CHOOSE YOUR ROUTE

We’ll have two walking options so people can participate at the level that feels right for them:

💎 Diamond Trail — the longer walk for those who want the full route.

🐰 Bunny Trail — a shorter, easier option for anyone who prefers less walking or needs a more accessible route.

Both groups will come together as we make our way toward early voting.

IMPORTANT FOR VOTERS

Our walk and rally are pro-democracy and nonpartisan. Signs should focus on voting, democracy, civic participation, and using your voice — not candidates or political parties.

Before we reach the voting location, we will have a designated person collecting rally signs so anyone entering to vote can do so without signs or political materials. Signs can be retrieved afterward.

PART TWO: STAY AND RALLY

Not a Passaic County voter? Come anyway!

This event is open to supporters from throughout New Jersey. Those who cannot vote at the Hawthorne early-voting location are welcome to join the walk and/or stay for the rally as we encourage others to exercise their rights, participate in our democracy, and make their voices heard.

Bring an American flag or create a nonpartisan, pro-democracy sign celebrating voting and civic participation.

Some ideas:

USE YOUR SUPERPOWER — VOTE!
YOUR VOICE. YOUR VOTE. YOUR FUTURE.
DEMOCRACY NEEDS YOU.
VOTE EARLY. MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD.

We’ll be together from approximately 11:00 AM–1:00 PM.

The exact Hawthorne gathering locations and additional logistical details will be shared with registered participants before the event.

Come walk. Come vote. Come rally. Come remind our neighbors that democracy works when we show up and use it.

SIGN UP. SHOW UP. STAND UP FOR THE CONSTITUTION.

- **Date: Monday, October 12**
- **Time: 5:30 PM  - 7:00 PM**
- **Location: Goler Memorial AME Zion Church,  3894 Northampton Drive, Winston-Salem, NC 27105**

The film offers a powerful look at what’s possible when ordinary people turn their civil rights goals into collective action. A panel discussion will follow the screening, creating an opportunity to reflect on the film and connect its lessons to the work happening in our communities today.

Come watch, connect, and be part of building the power we need to create change.

events.title: Your City. Your Data. Your Voice: De-Flock Lynn
events.description:
Date: Tuesday, October 13

Time: 3:00 PM-4 PM (Public Comment); 5PM-7PM (Public Action and General Council Meeting)

Location: Lynn City Hall, 3 City Hall Square, 4th Floor, Lynn, MA 01901


YOUR CITY. YOUR DATA. YOUR VOICE.
Lynn is having a public conversation about the use of Flock surveillance cameras in our city—and community members need to be part of it.
In August, an audit of Lynn Police Department's Flock system identified a “concerning pattern in some searches.” Two officers were subsequently placed on paid administrative leave while an Internal Affairs investigation was opened. The department has since restricted access to the system and announced additional auditing and oversight measures

Across Massachusetts, other communities have also reconsidered their use of Flock. Hopkinton ended its contract after a legal review, while Framingham's contract expired and its cameras were turned off. New Bedford temporarily suspended its system following an investigation into alleged misuse.

These developments raise important questions for Lynn:

Who should have access to Flock data?

How long should information about people's movements be retained?
What safeguards are sufficient to prevent misuse?

Who gets to decide how surveillance technology is used in our neighborhoods?

What level of transparency and public oversight should Lynn residents expect?

Join us before the Lynn City Council meeting to learn more, connect with your neighbors, and make your voice heard about the future of surveillance in Lynn!

📍 Lynn City Hall — 3 City Hall Square, 4th Floor
 📅 Tuesday, October 13
 🕔 3:00 PM-4 PM (Public Comment); 5PM-7PM (Public Action and General Council Meeting)
Your city. Your data. Your voice.
[RSVP ON MOBILIZE]

events.title: Florida NOW Film Screening: Reimagining Safety
events.description:
Join us as we close out the series with a screening of Reimagining Safety, a documentary filmed in the aftermath of the 2020 murder of George Floyd and the worldwide protests that followed. The film brings together 10 experts, including abolitionists, social workers, scholars, a former LAPD detective, and a former district attorney, to examine how policing and incarceration shape our ideas about safety.

The film revisits the 2020 protests and the growing calls to defund and abolish the police, while exploring the history and ongoing impact of police violence, racism, mass incarceration, mental health crises, housing insecurity, and the criminalization of poverty. It also highlights restorative justice, violence prevention, community responders, and other approaches that seek to build safety through care, accountability, and community rather than punishment and isolation.

Stay after the screening for our final community reflection and conversation in this series.

events.title: Michigan Voter Registration Calls with Rust Belt Rising
events.description:
Join Rust Belt Rising to help make sure that everyone is able to vote in this year's General Election!

Rust Belt Rising's innovative voter registration programs helped thousands of Great Lakes state residents register the last three cycles and will do so again this year.

Here's how it works: RBR partners at Civitech find targets of people who would likely vote our way but are unregistered at their current address as they compare commercial mail lists and voter files. They will mail these targets a pre-filled voter registration form with a motivational flyer and postage to their clerk. That's where we come in. In addition to our texting them, we need volunteers to call these targets to encourage them to complete the easy process of registering.

We would love for you to be part of a team that makes these calls to Michigan voters as part of our virtual voter registration chase! 

We'll teach you everything you know over Zoom and get you calling to remind voters to register because there is an election coming up!

location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

Join us as we mark one year of gathering every Sunday outside the Pinellas Justice Center as part of the broader national call to action through Disappeared in America. 

For a full year, people of faith and community members have gathered weekly to bear witness and call for an end to detention without due process, justice for immigrants, an end to 287(g) agreements, and more. 

This anniversary vigil will include an ofrenda, music, and a welcome back to the faith leaders who have led vigils throughout the past year. We’ll take time to look back at what we have built together — reflecting on the goals we set, the work we have done, and the successes and lessons of this past year — and to look ahead to the work still to come.

As we join this national call to action, we’ll come together in movement and community, renewing our commitment to the work ahead. Co-sponsored by the LWV of the St. Petersburg area, Interfaith Alliance of Florida, and Indivisible chapters across Pinellas County, Florida.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: 24th Annual ReLeafing Day at Glen Leven Farm!
events.description:
Join the Nashville Tree Foundation for the 24th Annual ReLeafing Day!

Held each year on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, ReLeafing Day is our signature community tree-planting event. Following the devastating 1998 tornadoes, our founders launched this initiative as a major restoration effort - raising $1,000,000 in six months and planting over 6,000 trees across the city. Today, that legacy continues as we focus on planting new trees in Nashville every November.

This year, we invite you to dig deep and plant trees at the beautiful Glen Leven Farm on Saturday, November 21st. We are proud to be supported by Root Nashville, helping drive the citywide goal of planting 500,000 trees by 2050, and funded by the Cumberland River Compact.

Whether you are an experienced tree planter or a first-time volunteer, this is the perfect way to connect with nature, meet fellow tree lovers, and actively grow our urban forest!

What to Expect: 
We will start the morning with a brief introduction and an overview of the day's goals. Our team will provide a step-by-step tree planting demonstration and review essential safety guidelines so you feel completely confident. Then, we'll plant our trees!

events.title: TEAM BERNIE: Canvass for Abdul at Fulton Street Market

sponsor.name: Organizing to Fight Oligarchy / We The Fighters

events.description:
Join Team Bernie and canvass for Abdul El-Sayed at the Fulton St. Farmers Market on Friday, October 9th in Grand Rapids from 9 AM to 12 PM.

Organize and Win Michigan is our program to elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate on November 3rd. We are building a powerful grassroots organizing program in communities across the state. 

Senator Sanders says it best: 

Friends,

Over ten years ago, we set out to create a political revolution in this country. You showed up because you believed in a simple principle that we must build a government that represents all Americans, not just the wealthy few. 

Right now, our movement is winning. Why? 

Whether it is a corrupt campaign finance system, unprecedented income and wealth inequality, a broken and wildly expensive healthcare system, the enormous threats posed by AI or an immoral and destructive foreign policy, progressives are talking about the real issues facing working families. And we are providing real solutions while establishment Democrats continue to tinker around the edges. 

We now have candidates in New York, Ohio, Maine, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Montana, Minnesota, Florida, Michigan, California, Colorado, Arizona, and New Jersey who are winning by running campaigns to change the broken political and economic system. And they have the guts to stand up to the billionaires and corporations who only want more political power and money.

But this isn't going to be easy. Right now the billionaire class, Donald Trump, and the Republican Party Establishment are spending millions of dollars to defeat our progressive movement. Why? Because they believe that their money can stop our people-powered movement. 

We know that organized people can beat organized money, but organized people need to show up. 

So what can you do? I am asking you to show up, organize events, and get out the vote for our progressive candidates before November 3rd. This movement has never been about me. It’s about us. 

Let’s get to work. 

In solidarity,

Senator Bernie Sanders

events.title: Youth Action for Trans Rights
events.description:
Join Amnesty International USA and New Era Action Fund in a day of youth action to turn out the vote this election. 

We will educate voters about two ballot measures that sound simple but aren't. Propositions 134 and 135 are being sold as measures about fairness and safety — but the fine print tells a different story, and voters deserve to know it before they vote.

Propositions 134 is so vague that it could subject any kid, in any sport, from kindergarten through college, to invasive verification just to prove they belong on the field. Propositions 135 hands medical decisions that belong to families and doctors over to politicians — and could block care for kids who aren't even transgender, including teens fighting cancer.

That's where you come in. Join Families Not Politics Coalition for a community canvass and help us have real conversations with Colorado voters about what these measures actually do. Our research is clear: when voters hear the full picture, they move — but it takes volunteers like you, at the doors, making the case.

No experience needed. We'll kick things off with training and a team briefing before heading out together. You'll leave with everything you need to have a confident, meaningful conversation. Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and come ready to talk with your neighbors. Our hosts will have breakfast and lunch for all volunteers to ensure everyone is well fed before and after their shift.

Every conversation moves a voter. Every voter we move gets us closer to defeating these measures in November. We hope you'll join us.

events.title: A District That Works for Children, Youth, and Families
events.description:
**What would it take to build a District that truly works for all children, youth, and families?**

That’s what we will be asking at our end-of-year summit on **Thursday, December 3, from 6:30-8:00 pm.** At DC Action, we’re bringing together the DC Out-of-School Time Coalition, Under 3 DC, and the Youth Economic Justice Coalition to lead a bold conversation with the mayor-elect and elected leaders from across the District, and we want you to join us. 

This is a critical moment for the District, with a new mayor for the first time in a dozen years, major turnover on the council, and continued uncertainty about the economy. The budget and policy decisions made over the coming months, and the plans carried out in the next few years, will impact the District for generations to come. 

It’s vital that the needs of Black and brown children, youth, and families be at the center of these discussions. That’s why this event will be led by young people, parents, and direct service providers from the three coalitions, who will share their experiences and what they want to see from our elected leaders, from making child care more affordable, to expanding out-of-school time programs, and committing to ending youth homelessness.


**Doors open at 5:30pm.**

events.title: Troy Indivisible Sidewalk StandOut for Early Voting
events.description:
The next No Kings is all about  Promoting Early Voting  for the midterms! 
The success of No Kings: Vote Early will not be determined by the size of rallies, but rather by the unprecedented number of voters we motivate to vote early.  This National Day of Action involves thousands of local events across the country, encouraging Americans to use  their vote as their voice.
Help us promote the vote! Join Troy Indivisible for a non-partisan Sidewalk StandOut around the Farmers Market to boost early voting. Our goal is to raise awareness about the early voting option (it starts 10/24) and to get more voters to cast early ballots. We want to see the largest early voting turnout in history! Voting information and voter registration will be available throughout the event, along with sign-up information for election protection training.


So make a sign and meet us in the empty lot at the corner of River and Fulton Streets in downtown Troy at 9:45am. From there, we’ll break into groups and walk to designated StandOut stations surrounding the Farmers Market. Some pre-made signs will be available, but bring your own creative design if you can. Stay the whole time or just pop in for as long as you want. Either way, we hope to see you out there on October 17th!


Important Note: This is a non-partisan, family-friendly event, so please keep signs simple, clean, and focused on voting or voting early. This is not a protest, it’s a Sidewalk StandOut to inform and mobilize voters. Please leave partisan signs at home!

Easy Sign Suggestions: VOTE, VOTE EARLY, JUST VOTE, VOTE OCT 24th, YOUR VOTE IS YOUR VOICE, WANT CHANGE?—VOTE, DEMOCRACY DEPENDS ON US, FLEX YOUR POWER—VOTE, DON’T FORGET TO VOTE, YOUR VOICE MATTERS, YOUR VOTE MATTERS. (Look online for more ideas!)


Specific Instructions to Participants:

✅  How to Prepare for the Sidewalk StandOut  ✅
Leave home early to be sure you have time to find parking—downtown Troy will be busy! The 5th Avenue garage and the River Street garage may have spots open and garage parking is free on the weekends.
Please arrive by 9:45am at the vacant lot at River & Fulton Streets in downtown Troy. Groups will be assigned and instructions given at 10am (see below for late arrival instructions).
Bring a sign! (see important sign guidelines and suggestions below).
Bring family, friends, and neighbors!
Be sure to dress for the weather conditions and bring any essentials you may need, including a chair if standing is a challenge.
Double-check your own voter registration at www.vote411.org and make a plan to vote early!


Late Arrivals: If you arrive after 10am, proceed to the corner of River Street and 3rd Street for further instructions.
Accessibility: We’ll be standing on flat sidewalks at multiple stations around the perimeter of the Farmers Market. If you have mobility concerns, email us at troynyindivisible@gmail.com and we’ll make sure you’re assigned to the closest spot.


Sign Guidelines: This is a non-partisan, family-friendly event, so please keep signs simple, clean, and focused on voting or voting early. This is not a protest, it’s a Sidewalk StandOut to inform and mobilize voters. Please leave partisan signs at home!
Easy Sign Suggestions: VOTE, VOTE EARLY, JUST VOTE, VOTE OCT 24th, YOUR VOTE IS YOUR VOICE, WANT CHANGE?—VOTE, DEMOCRACY DEPENDS ON US, FLEX YOUR POWER—VOTE, DON’T FORGET TO VOTE, YOUR VOICE MATTERS, YOUR VOTE MATTERS. (Look online for more ideas!)
Nonviolent, people-led movements are the most successful path to real change. Every No Kings event is grounded in that commitment: organizers trained in de-escalation, safety coordinators on site, and actions that are lawful, disciplined, and rooted in the strength of our communities.

events.title: VOTING INFORMATION CARDS & REGISTRATION
events.description:
Hand out voter information cards with the Minnesota Secretary of State website.      
Inform people what the website can help with: registration, polling places and times, sample ballot, other ways to vote.
Beautiful park with great playground. Lots of young parents!
Just need to be friendly and can approach people in pair---bring a friend!

Suggested opening statements:
Find a greeting if you can..
“Cute dog you have.”   “I see that you are a biker/walker. Monticello has some great parks! Is this your favorite?”    “ Isn’t this a great playground? Do you kids like to come often?”

Then move to:
Hi, my name is Sue. I’m out reminding folks to vote this fall…are you planning to vote? 

Respond to their answer, then:
I have this card (show SOS side) that has the Secretary of State website on it. 
There is a lot of information there, such as:
Is your registration up to date?  Where to go vote? 
Where are the early voting times and places?  And even a sample ballot for your area,
Could you use any of that information?
   If not…please pass this on to anyone who might need it. OR
You just type in your address and a whole list of options appear!

Closing:
“Thanks for your time.
Do you have any questions?
We also suggest you vote early–no crowds, easy to do and safe. The website will have info on dates and time.   Enjoy your…walk, run, bike, dog, ….”

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early [Colby , Kansas
events.description:
Northwest Kansas Vote Early

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Listening at the Door - Reflective Listening Earns Trust and Votes
events.description:
Join John Sabin and Ken Stanley for a hands-on Zoom session on reflective listening, the skill behind the best conversations at the door. As canvassing shifts from talking to listening, this is one of the most useful skills a canvasser can build, and you can make real progress in about an hour.

We'll start with quick introductions, then practice in a supportive, low-pressure setting, taking turns sharing and reflecting back what we hear. We'll close with a conversation about how we can all keep growing as canvassers. This workshop is designed for experienced canvassers. 

John Sabin is an expert in motivational interviewing, the listening-centered approach Elizabeth Chur draws on in The Joy of Talking Politics to Strangers, and he brings years of experience from his work with Citizens' Climate Lobby. Ken Stanley has been knocking doors since his first campaign at 16 in 1974, trained with Marshall Ganz, and has had well over a thousand conversations at the door, many recorded and reviewed with Swing Left's Script Iteration Team.

If you haven't heard of it, Swing Left is a national network that helps people find high-impact ways to support Democratic candidates. We focus on the most flippable races as an important step toward the progressive change needed to create a more inclusive and equitable government and society.

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Keene, NH!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

-**Offer vote swapping** to voters who remain unconvinced to vote Democrat - giving them the opportunity to lodge a protest vote in MA, in exchange for voting Democrat in NH!

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Adopt a Day Laborer Corner Volunteer Check in
events.description:
Hello Volunteers!

Across the nation, community members are standing in solidarity with day laborers, getting to know the workers in their neighborhood and accompanying them at their local corners. Some of these Adopt a Corner groups are celebrating a year of visiting corners; some are just getting started; some groups are launching new and exciting projects, and some groups are asking how they can do more. Wherever you and your corner team is at, please join us! In this call you can expect to hear from groups around the nation; learn more about what you can do next, and have an opportunity to connect and to see how we can support each other.

This effort is part of a broader campaign led by the National Day Laborer Organizing Network (NDLON) to support workers, build grassroots power, and transform our communities from the ground up.

We’re looking forward to connecting with all of you. Let’s keep building, together.

— The NDLON Organizing Team

events.description:
Join our upcoming office hours to learn more about MoveOn's innovative Adopt A District Program, which allows you to contact the voters who are most critical to winning in our priority districts and flipping the House blue this year. 

You'll be able to contact MoveOn members who skipped the 2024 election, sharing details about our endorsed candidates and how to vote, and motivating them to turn out via postcard, call, text, or even a door knock if you live in the district.

Already signed up for Adopt A District, but hit a road block? Office Hours are a space where you can come to troubleshoot MiniVAN, workshop your spiel on early voting, or even roleplay knocking on your first door! Our experienced team of organizers are on hand to make sure you feel prepared and have everything you need to get started.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early
events.description:
Join us in Chelsea to get out the vote!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Manchester, NH (NH-1)

location.venue: Beech St Elementary School parking lot

events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

-**Offer vote swapping** to voters who remain unconvinced to vote Democrat - giving them the opportunity to help an Independent win in MA-1, in exchange for voting Democrat in NH-1!

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.description:
WE HAVE 28 DAYS UNTIL THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

However, we have a chance to make a real difference in just 8 more days.  Early in person voting in Iowa starts on Wednesday October 14th, at your county auditors office, and we would like to make a strong union showing on the first day.

We are asking your officers, staff and any available union members who live in Polk County to join us on Wednesday October 14th at 9 am to cast your ballot with other sisters & brothers.  We have a chance to set an example that voting this election cycle is important and that early voting is quick and easy.

You can find a list of labor endorsed candidates here : https://voteunioniowa.org/vote-union-iowa-2026/

Vote NO on Amendment 1

We ask that you join us on the first day of voting and help spread the word through your local area so that we can demonstrate union and solidarity.

Please join the George Mason University chapter of the American Association of University Professors (GMU-AAUP) and the League of Women Voters (LWV) to obtain voter information, register to vote or check your registration, make a voting plan, and pledge to Vote Early!

Our Vote is our Voice! Our Vote is our Power!

We the People decide who represents us. We the People decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 14th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. Join us as we get out the early vote and say it loud: No Thrones, No Crowns, No Kings!

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

events.title: Weekend of Action: Knock Doors in Charles County!
events.description:
### Welcome to #TeamMaryland. 

**Join us for our Weekend of Action!**

### We will be meeting at the Laurel Springs Regional Park 1st parking lot

We’re so excited you’re interested in knocking on doors to re-elect Governor Wes Moore and to elect Democrats up and down the ballot!

**First time volunteering?** No worries. Each canvass shift starts with a training with an organizer who will be there to help you out. We’ll send you out with a buddy so you can knock on doors together. 

**Are you a pro canvasser?** GREAT! Join us at Laurel Springs Regional Park parking lot to pick up some lit and a packet and we’ll get you out on the doors! 

### What you’ll need. 
**Before you knock on doors with us, you’ll need some things.**
1. A smartphone so you can download the MiniVAN Touch app, the Democratic Party’s canvassing app. Download it on [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/minivan-touch/id352087547) or [android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.voteractivationnetwork.minivan&hl=en_US&gl=US).
2. A full water bottle! We’ll have water but always best to come prepared
3. Weather-appropriate clothes and good walking shoes!

**Who are you bringing along?** The more folks we have on the doors, the more voters we will be able to bring. So forward this event to a friend or two...or three? Or share it on social media using the hashtag  **#TeamMaryland.**

events.title: Care in Action Virtual Phonebanks for NC!
events.description:
Care in Action is mobilizing tens of thousands of voters in North Carolina to the polls in this decisive election.

Join us on Wednesday October 14 from 6-7:30 PM and Saturday, October 17 from 11 AM - 1 PM EST for our volunteer phone banks! Volunteers in-state and around the country can join our virtual phone banks to engage voters in NC with critical information on the election, lift up the important races that will have a big impact on our state, and what’s on the ballot, including two harmful constitutional amendments. Care in Action works to address issues of long-term care, childcare, and affordability, and you can volunteer with us to ensure that we engage as many voters as possible and activate them around these issues.

Never phone banked before or don't know much about the upcoming election? No worries, we have you covered! We will provide training at the beginning of the phone bank to go over the tools we will use, and the talking points to prepare you to have effective and meaningful conversations. Phone bank with us and learn more about other opportunities to volunteer with Care in Action this election season!

events.title: October 16 at 1:00 PM: Signs of Solidarity/Get Out the Vote canvassing in Congressional District CD8
events.description:
Event: Join us on October 16 at 1:00 PM for Signs of Solidarity/Get Out the Vote canvassing in Congressional District 8
The three Signs of Solidarity-GOTV canvasses we’ve held so far were big successes.  Our final pre-election canvass will be on Friday, October 16.  Join us!
As with all Signs of Solidarity canvassing, we will be providing local businesses with crucial information on their rights and how to plan for and respond to an ICE raid. But this time, we will also be providing information about registering to vote and the importance of the midterm election in CD-8. 
We will be canvassing in Thornton or Westminster the afternoon  of Friday October 16. New canvassers will meet at 1:00; experienced canvassers will join us at 1:30.. We'll pair up and go out to businesses on a pre-prepared canvass list. You’ll receive details on the meeting location after you register.

events.description:
## Si se puede! Yes we can!

### Door Knocking in Waukegan and North Chicago

Support Get Out the Vote efforts through our partner **Mano a Mano** with their important **residential canvassing work.** Mano a Mano is working tirelessly over the next few weeks to **"Get Out The Vote"** to our **disenfranchised neighbors in Waukegan and North Chicago.** We encourage folks to sign up directly with Mano a Mano for phone banking and door knocking any time between now and Midterms here at their Sign-Up Site: www.bit.ly/LakeCountyVotes 

*These "Democracy in Action" efforts are sponsored by Mano a Mano, ICIRR, and Hispanic Federation.*

We will be collecting a group of our own **NE Lake County Indivisible volunteers** for **Saturday October 24**. Sign up for the morning or the afternoon or BOTH! :)

**Training and supplies will be provided.** Participants are encouraged to **dress for the weather and wear comfortable shoes.** 

We will be targeting households where individuals are registered to vote but rarely show up at the polls, reaching our most disenfranchised neighbors. Canvassers will ask the simple question, "How do you think things are going right now?" in sharing the nonpartisan encouragement to "Get Out the Vote!"

*Registration can be done here with our Mobilize to receive reminders and updates, or you may register directly with Mano a Mano at their site www.bit.ly/LakeCountyVotes .*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early   Ontario, Oregon
events.description:
11:00 am to 1 pm at Lion’s Park.  Bring your signs.  We will march to City Hall and back and then have a few speakers at the park. 

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Parma/Cleveland West Suburbs "The Early Bird Gets the Vote"
events.description:
Please join Indivisible's Citizens Against Tyranny for this fun, friendly community event.  We will line the streets in front of the shops with signs and costumes reminding others to vote early.  Our them is "The Early Bird Gets The Vote!  Flock to the Polls!", so bring your best feathered costume or a sign to remind others to cast an early ballot.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: North End Detroit Canvass Launch with Katie and Sam
events.description:
📣 **NORTH END, LET’S GET TO WORK!** 📣

Join Katie and Sam at Detroit People’s Food Co-op for an **Abdul Canvass Launch in the North End!**

We’re hitting the doors, talking with our neighbors, and building the grassroots movement **one conversation at a time.**

🍂 **Dress for fall, bring water, and bring a friend!**

We’re proud to launch this canvass from Detroit People’s Food Co-op — a Black-owned, community-focused grocery co-op right here in the North End.

The Co-op has recently reached out to the community for support, as reduced income and consumer spending have made it harder to keep its shelves fully stocked. **If you’re able, please consider shopping there or joining the co-op!** It’s a welcoming, healthy place to shop for groceries and an incredible community institution that deserves our support.

Fun fact: **they host DSA events and other community events upstairs!** ❤️

Let’s support the places that invest in our communities while we organize for a government that works for **working people, families, and all of us.**

**Knock doors, meet your neighbors, spread the word about Abdul, and help us build the movement!**

Learn more about the Co-op:
