events.title: Indivisible Greater Grand Rapids Community Meeting with "Ask a Muslim" Discussion
events.description:
We are all seeing a lot of misinformation and disinformation about Islam on social media and in election campaign materials. In a time when we should be coming together as a community, we are seeing efforts to further divide us. At our October 26 community meeting, we are honored to have a panel discussion and Q&A with several Muslim women who will provide a brief Islam 101 presentation followed by a frank discussion of myths about Islam. We will also have an "Ask a Muslim" Q&A for community members to become further educated about Islam and how Muslims practice their faith. This session will prepare us all to be allies to the Muslim community by providing us with tips and tricks for answering questions about Islam in an appropriate way.
Social from 6:30 pm to 7:00pm. Discussion will start at 7:00pm. Please bring a snack to share!

events.title: Meet and Greet with Mark Proctor at the Marler's
events.description:
Join our hosts, Linda and Jim Marler, for a neighborhood gathering to meet Mark Proctor, ask questions, share your ideas, and learn more about his vision for our community. 

About Mark:

For more than 25 years, Mark had the honor of serving Tennesseans with the Tennessee Highway Patrol, working every day to keep our families safe.

He led hundreds of troopers across the state, managed critical divisions, protected three Tennessee governors and served as Captain, Major and LT Colonel over our troopers that protected our legislators and visitors to our TN State Capitol and Legislative offices.

That experience taught him something simple but powerful: leadership is about protecting what matters most — people, families, and the communities we call home.

Mark lives in Nashville with his husband, Adam, and their two daughters.

RSVP here, and we’ll let you know how to join this event. Invite your friends, too and let them know about Vote Forward, a pioneering and innovative program using letters to help volunteers like us turn out voters. 

Never written letters before? Go to votefwd.org and make an account; download twenty letters; and we’ll show you how to write them at our event!

Letters to underrepresented voters are a fun, easy, and highly effective way to strengthening our democracy by encouraging citizens from underrepresented communities to vote. Looking forward to seeing you!

events.title: No Kings: McKinney Morning Caravan - Get Out The Vote!

location.venue: Starting Near Wholefoods at 380/University and Custer

events.description:
## NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY

### McKinney Traveling Action - Saturday, October 17, 2026

### Six stops. One community. One message: YOUR VOTE MATTERS.

Join us for a rolling No Kings: Vote Early action through McKinney!

Rather than staying in one place, we're taking the message to several parts of our community. We'll decorate our cars, travel together from stop to stop, and spend 30 minutes at each location holding signs that encourage people to VOTE EARLY and tell them YOUR VOTE MATTERS, along with info about voting.

You can join us for the entire route or meet us at whichever stop works best for you.

#### 🚗 THE DAY'S SCHEDULE

#### 1. 9:30 AM — CAR DECORATING & MEET-UP
We'll gather, decorate our cars, get organized, and get ready to roll.
#### 10:00–10:30 AM — STOP 1
📍 Whole Foods — University & Custer

We'll kick off the traveling action with our signs and our message: VOTE EARLY. YOUR VOTE MATTERS. INFORMATION ABOUT VOTING.

#### 2. 11:00–11:30 AM — STOP 2
📍 H-E-B — Eldorado Pkwy

We'll take the Vote Early message to another busy part of McKinney.

#### 3. 12:00–12:30 PM — STOP 3
📍 Near Panera — Eldorado & US-75

Another 30 minutes of visible, peaceful voter encouragement.

#### 4. 1:00–1:30 PM — STOP 4
📍 Near Sprouts — Virginia Pkwy & US-75

We'll keep moving north and bring the message with us.

#### 5. 2:00–2:30 PM — STOP 5
📍 Downtown McKinney — near MPAC / the downtown square

We'll make our final community stop downtown before heading to the day's big gathering.

#### 6. 3:00 PM — FINAL STOP / JOIN THE BIG PROTEST
📍 US-75 & University

**We'll finish our caravan by joining the larger No Kings action near University and US-75.**
https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/1024569/

### WHY WE'RE DOING THIS

No Kings: Vote Early is a nonpartisan voter-participation effort. On October 17, we're turning people power into voter power by bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early, understand their options for how to vote, and make sure every eligible voter has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

We're taking that message directly into our community.

We're not just holding signs in one place. We're bringing the message with us.

🚗 Decorate your car.
📣 Bring your signs.
👋 Bring your friends and neighbors.
🗳️ Make a plan to vote early.

No Tyrant/Kings: Protect the Vote

Americans in Belgium are participating in the global day of action by organizing a NO TYRANTS Protest on Saturday, 17 October 2026 from 2 to 4 pm (CET). The event will take place at Carrefour de l'Europe in Brussels, Belgium (across from the Central station).

With the US midterm elections in just a few weeks, it is important that we say loudly and clearly for all to see that we are paying attention and will be voting to preserve our democracy and the rule of law.

Whether you have an hour or want to hustle with us all day, join us to talk to voters, make calls, write letters, text voters, mobilize your friends, and help get our community engaged ahead of November.

The Hamilton County Hustle will include 7 stations:
1. Check-In
Get signed in, meet the team, and find the best way to plug in.
2. Canvass Packet Pickup
Grab a packet and head into the community to talk directly with voters.
3. Phonebanking Station
Make calls and connect with voters across Hamilton County.
4. Letter Writing Station
Help us reach voters with handwritten letters.
5. Kids Corner
Bringing the family? We’ll have a dedicated space for kids while you get involved.
6. Mobilizing Your Friends Training
Learn simple ways to activate your own network and get your friends, family, and neighbors engaged.
7. Close Out & Reshift
Finished one activity? Come back, check in, and jump into another!

This election will be powered by people showing up and doing the work. Come for one station, tackle a few, or make your way through the entire Hamilton County Hustle.

Sunday, October 18 | 10 AM–6 PM
7915 Spring Valley Dr. | Cincinnati, OH 45236

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Thomas, WV

location.venue: Old bank parking lot and pavilion

events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Tyranny Tuesday 10-13-2026: We Are The Resistance: Americans Who Stood Up, 1765-2026

location.venue: Bruce R. Thompson Courthouse and Federal Building

events.description:
**📣 Tyranny Tuesday • October 13, 2026 • Indivisible Northern Nevada**

*✊ We are the Resistance: Americans Who Stood Up: 1765-2026

🪧Every right we exercise on this sidewalk was won by ordinary Americans who organized, marched, boycotted, petitioned, and refused to stay quiet. As our nation marks its 250th year, here is our family tree. We stand on their shoulders.

🪧1765–1776   SONS AND DAUGHTERS OF LIBERTY
When Parliament imposed the Stamp Act in 1765, colonists formed the Sons of Liberty to fight taxation without representation with street protests, petitions, and pressure on royal officials. The Daughters of Liberty organized boycotts of British goods and spun homespun cloth so the colonies could live without imports. Boycotts, public demonstrations, and committees that spread the news town to town became America’s first protest playbook.


🤝 1830s–1850s   ABOLITIONISTS AND THE FREE SOIL PARTY
The American Anti-Slavery Society (1833), William Lloyd Garrison’s The Liberator, Frederick Douglass, and Harriet Tubman on the Underground Railroad took on the most powerful economic interest in the nation. Abolitionists flooded Congress with so many petitions that the House passed a “gag rule” (1836–1844) to silence them. They kept petitioning. In 1848 the Free Soil Party ran on “Free Soil, Free Speech, Free Labor, and Free Men” to stop slavery’s spread west, and its members helped found the Republican Party in 1854.

🏠1870s–1938   THE GILDED AGE, THE POPULISTS, AND LABOR
Mark Twain called it the Gilded Age: gold on the surface, rot underneath. Railroad and oil monopolies bought legislatures while workers labored 12-hour days and children worked in mills and mines. Farmers answered with the Grange and the Farmers’ Alliances, and in 1892 the People’s (Populist) Party demanded a graduated income tax, direct election of U.S. senators, and the secret ballot. Called radical then, the income tax and direct election were both in the Constitution by 1913.
Workers built the Knights of Labor, the American Federation of Labor, and the IWW, and fought for the eight-hour day through Haymarket (1886) and the Pullman Strike (1894). The 1911 Triangle Shirtwaist Fire killed 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women, behind locked doors, and it led to new workplace safety laws. The payoff: the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938, which brought a federal minimum wage, overtime pay, and limits on child labor. The weekend was brought to you by organized labor.

💙1848–1920   WOMEN’S SUFFRAGE: DIVIDED, BUT ONE GOAL
The movement split in 1869 over the 15th Amendment. Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Susan B. Anthony’s National Woman Suffrage Association pushed for a federal amendment, while Lucy Stone’s American Woman Suffrage Association worked state by state. They reunited in 1890 and then divided again over tactics: Carrie Chapman Catt’s NAWSA lobbied politely, while Alice Paul’s National Woman’s Party picketed the White House as the “Silent Sentinels” and endured jail and force-feeding. The movement was far from perfect, and Black suffragists like Ida B. Wells had to fight for a place in its own parades. But the inside-outside pressure worked, and the 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920. Nevada women, led by Nevada’s own Anne Martin, had already won the vote in 1914.

🤝1909   THE NAACP TAKES ON JIM CROW
After a 1908 race riot in Springfield, Illinois, an interracial group including W.E.B. Du Bois, Ida B. Wells, and Mary White Ovington founded the NAACP. Jim Crow meant segregation, poll taxes, literacy tests, and lynching. The NAACP fought back with journalism (The Crisis), anti-lynching campaigns, and the courts. Its lawyers, led by Thurgood Marshall, won Brown v. Board of Education in 1954.

1942–1970s   THE CIVIL RIGHTS MOVEMENT
CORE (1942) pioneered nonviolent direct action and launched the 1961 Freedom Rides. SCLC (1957), led by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., organized the Birmingham campaign and the Selma-to-Montgomery march. SNCC (1960), born from the student sit-ins and mentored by Ella Baker, registered voters in Mississippi during Freedom Summer, and its chairman John Lewis bled on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. The Black Panther Party (1966, Oakland) confronted police brutality and fed tens of thousands of children through its Free Breakfast for Children program. The FBI’s COINTELPRO spied on and disrupted these groups, but the movement won the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

💙1963–1970s   SECOND-WAVE FEMINISM
Betty Friedan’s The Feminine Mystique (1963) named “the problem that has no name,” and in 1966 she co-founded the National Organization for Women as its first president. Bella Abzug won a seat in Congress in 1970 declaring “This woman’s place is in the House — the House of Representatives!” Gloria Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine in 1972, and in 1971 Friedan, Abzug, Steinem, and Shirley Chisholm launched the National Women’s Political Caucus. Their victories include Title IX (1972), congressional passage of the Equal Rights Amendment (1972), the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (1974), which let women get credit in their own names, and the Pregnancy Discrimination Act (1978).

📣2011   OCCUPY WALL STREET
Three years after the banks that crashed the economy were bailed out, protesters took over Zuccotti Park in New York on September 17, 2011. Their slogan, “We are the 99%,” spread to hundreds of cities. Police cleared the camps within months, but Occupy put economic inequality at the center of American politics, and the Fight for $15 minimum-wage campaign followed close behind.

🤝2013–Today   BLACK LIVES MATTER
Alicia Garza, Patrisse Cullors, and Opal Tometi started #BlackLivesMatter in 2013 after the acquittal in Trayvon Martin’s killing. Ferguson followed in 2014. After George Floyd was murdered in 2020, an estimated 15 to 26 million Americans marched, one of the largest protest movements in U.S. history, and independent researchers found that more than nine in ten of those demonstrations were peaceful.

Always   THE BACKLASH
Every movement on this page met resistance from those in power, from the Pinkertons and the Klan to COINTELPRO. Occupy was dismissed as “class warfare” and its camps were cleared by coordinated police raids. Black Lives Matter was answered with “All Lives Matter” and “Blue Lives Matter,” with armed militia and Proud Boys counter-protesters, and with the 2017 “Unite the Right” rally in Charlottesville, where a white supremacist drove into a crowd and killed counter-protester Heather Heyer. Since 2020, dozens of states have considered bills that raise penalties on protesters. Backlash is not a sign of failure. It is a sign the movement is working.

💙2016–Today   INDIVISIBLE: THE NEXT LINK IN THE CHAIN
Indivisible began in December 2016 when former congressional staffers Ezra Levin and Leah Greenberg published a guide showing everyday citizens how to hold their members of Congress accountable. Today there are local groups in every state, including ours. We use the tools every movement on this page handed down to us:
Boycotts like the Daughters of Liberty. Petitions like the abolitionists. Ballot power like the Free Soilers and Populists. Solidarity like organized labor. Inside-outside pressure like the suffragists. The courts like the NAACP. Nonviolent direct action like CORE, SCLC, and SNCC. Community care like the Panthers’ breakfast program. Our own media like Ms. And showing up in numbers like Occupy and Black Lives Matter.
We also share their bravery. None of them knew they would win. They showed up anyway. So do we.

WE ARE THE RESISTANCE!
Bring a sign, bring a friend, and bring your voice.

🌟 You Are Part of This Story

✅ Your 2026 Voting Checklist

- 📝 Oct. 6 is the last day to register by mail or in person.** You can still register online through Election Day, or in person during early voting and on Election Day.

- 📬 Watch your mailbox.** Return your mail ballot early, or use a drop box by 7 p.m. on Election Day.

- 🗓️ Early voting:** October 17–30  *Election Day:** Tuesday, November 3

- 🔍 Check your registration** at [nvsos.gov](https://www.nvsos.gov) or [washoecounty.gov/voters](https://www.washoecounty.gov/voters/)

✊ JOIN US

events.title: 10/11 - Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization @ Korean Festival at Discovery Green

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Election Day, November 3rd is around the corner.  Come make a huge impact with us! Approximately 85K people from all over greater Houston area attend the Korean festival at Discovery Green especially young people.  Create awareness in community about the consequential midterm election.  We have 2 SHIFTS for this event! Select the shift you are available for.  General admission is free.

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization** shift at **Korean Festival at Discovery Green Park**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico
- Create Midterm Election awareness
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Check voters’ status on the spot
- We will NOT register voters until after November 3rd. We’ve shifted to GOVT
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:
**Starting Oct 6th, we will NOT register voters until after November 3rd. 

_This huddle time frame is based on 1st shift so we’ll spend 30 min to huddle & 15-30 min to huddle to debrief._
 
- **[12:00-12:30pm]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals. 

- **[12:30-3:00pm] Hotspotting** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **[3:00-3:30pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total Reach sign-ups/adds, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: provided once registered 
- **Volunteer Parking**: more details will be provided closer to event day by host.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity. Starting Oct 6th, we will not be registering voters until after Nov 3rd so does not applied for this event

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to encourage voters to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. #  Virtual GOTV Phonebank Kickoff w/ Dr. Anna V. Eskamani

The November 3rd election is less than a month away, and it's time to make sure young voters across Florida are ready to make their voices heard.

Join People Power for Florida for our **Virtual GOTV (Get Out The Vote) Phonebank Kickoff** as we launch our largest youth voter outreach effort of the year. Our goal is ambitious: reach more than 100,000 young voters before the election on November 3rd and we need your help to make it happen.

## What We'll Be Doing

✅ Call young voters across Central Florida

✅ Encourage voters to make a plan to vote

✅ Informing young people about the impacts of Amendment 3

✅ Share important election information and deadlines

✅ Build momentum for a strong youth turnout in 2026

## No Experience Necessary

Whether you've made thousands of calls or never phonebanked before, we've got you covered.

## Why It Matters

Young people have the power to shape the future of our communities, but too many eligible voters sit out local elections. By volunteering just a few hours, you can help ensure that thousands of young people have the information and encouragement they need to participate.

✅ Help us reach more than 100,000 young voters before early voting begins

✅ Make a direct impact on voter turnout in your community

✅ Connect with volunteers from across Central Florida

✅ Be part of a growing movement of young people making change

Together, we can build a stronger, more engaged generation of voters.

**Sign up today and help us reach 100,000 young voters before early voting begins!**

events.title: VAYD POTS Awareness Month Virtual Roundtable
events.description:
Join the Virginia Young Democrats during POTS Awareness Month for a conversation focused on supporting our members living with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and advocating for the broader POTS community!

Attorney General Jay Jones will kick off the event by discussing how he and his office are working to uplift and support Virginians with disabilities. We will then host a roundtable discussion featuring young people with POTS, who will share their experiences and perspectives on how VAYD can better support and advocate for people living with POTS.

Recognized through bipartisan legislation during Virginia’s 2020 legislative session, POTS Awareness Month provides an opportunity to build awareness and strengthen our commitment to supporting those affected by this condition. POTS disproportionately affects people assigned female at birth, and approximately 80% of those affected are under the age of 50. VAYD is committed to working alongside members affected by POTS, amplifying their voices, and using our platform to advance awareness, understanding, and advocacy.

events.title: New York, NY: GasFreeNYC Training
events.description:
**We're in a climate crisis and our bills are too damn high! We need a GasFreeNYC!**

Buildings are New York City's largest source of greenhouse gas, in large part due to fossil fuel use. While Local Law 97 is successfully reducing pollution from large buildings, it does not cover the City's thousands of 1- and 2-family homes. 

The GasFreeNYC campaign is the next essential phase to moving off fossil fuels: expanding public funding and passing requirements to help homeowners get rid of their dirty old boilers and move on to clean-energy heat pumps. 

At the meeting, we'll discuss what we've won so far, what's next, and how you can be involved in winning a GasFreeNYC!

_Sponsors: New York Communities for Change, NYPIRG, Food & Water Watch_

events.title: Hope and Action NO KINGS VOTE EARLY Rally - Hollywood
events.description:
NO KINGS — Let’s Get Out the Early Vote!

Join Hope and Action for the NO KINGS nonpartisan community event encouraging everyone to VOTE EARLY!

📅 Saturday, October 17 | 11:30 AM–1:30 PM
📍 Stirling Rd. & N. 46th Ave., Hollywood

Bring your early voting signs, your energy, and a friend! Together, let’s spread the message and help make this the biggest early voting turnout ever!

Show up. Speak up. VOTE EARLY!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Carpool Canvass from Boston to Maine!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with Ground Truth—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to Maine—a must-win Swing State—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Troy Jackson. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

Knock More Doors: We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.

Deep Listening: We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built.

Capture Insights: You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

What to expect:

The Trip: For this weekend (10/11), Boston-based organizer Isabelle will pick up volunteers from the Medford/Somerville/Cambridge area between 9:00-10:00 am. Pickup and carpool captain details TBD following this weekend; option to carpool with friends from your own town to meet Isabelle there is always there!

Canvassing: We'll be knocking on doors in from roughly 12:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.

Preparation: You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your carpool captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus!

—

Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read Swing Left's waiver and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will.

Paid for by Swing Left, swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Brownsburg, Indiana
events.description:
No Kings: Vote Early Brownsburg, Indiana
This will be a visibility event where we will be in front of the town center on Green Street encouraging people to vote on Monday October 19 when voting is available in Brownsburg.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Lee County School Board Meeting
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Meeting

Join the Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we show up, stay informed, and engage with the decisions impacting Lee County students, educators, families, and public schools.

The School Board of Lee County sets the policies and rules that govern the administration of the District. The Board operates according to Florida law and Florida Department of Education regulations, and it sets policy when members meet in official session.

That makes School Board meetings an important place for our community to be present and engaged.

Whether you are a parent, educator, student, or community member, we invite you to join FSPS-Lee to:

📚 Stay informed about decisions affecting Lee County public schools
📣 Make your voice heard on issues that matter to students and families
🤝 Connect with other public education advocates in Lee County
🏫 Support strong public schools and help build a stronger local network of advocates

You do not need to be an expert or have experience speaking at School Board meetings to participate. Showing up matters.

Together, we can make sure families and community members have a voice in the decisions shaping our public schools.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice.

💙 Join FSPS-Lee and show up for Lee County public schools!

events.title: 💸 Rigged by Design: The Upward Redistribution of Wealth and Who's Getting Paid for Your Work?🤔
events.description:
💸 Since 1979, American workers have become far more productive, but most paychecks haven't kept up. 📈 Productivity has grown almost three times as fast as pay for a typical worker. CEO pay at the largest companies has gone from 21 times a typical worker's pay to 325 times. And the top 1% now hold more of the country's wealth than at any point since the Federal Reserve started tracking it in 1989. 🏦 So where did the gains go, and why?

🗣️ Join us on Zoom for "The Great Divergence: Productivity, Pay, and Power Since 1979," an hour on structural inequality, stagnant wages, and the policy choices that moved money upward. We'll follow the money with charts, go over how to answer the most common pushback, and finish with concrete things we can do together. 💪 No economics background needed, just bring your questions and your experience. 🤝 Everyone's welcome!

events.title: Lee County School Board Workshop
events.description:
Join FSPS-Lee at the Lee County School Board Workshop

Join Families for Strong Public Schools – Lee Chapter as we attend the Lee County School Board Workshop to stay informed and engaged in the conversations shaping our public schools.

What is a School Board Workshop?

A workshop is different from a regular School Board meeting. Regular meetings are where the Board takes formal action and votes on agenda items. Workshops are primarily working sessions where Board members receive information, ask questions, discuss issues in greater detail, and explore potential policies or decisions before they may come back for formal action.

That makes workshops an important part of the public decision-making process.

By the time an issue reaches a final vote, Board members may have already spent significant time discussing it during workshops. Attending or tuning in gives families and community members an opportunity to understand what is being considered earlier in the process—not just when it is time for a vote.

Why Tune In or Attend?

📚 Get informed early about issues and proposals that could affect Lee County public schools.

👀 See the process in action and hear the questions, concerns, and priorities Board members raise as they consider an issue.

📝 Be better prepared to advocate when an issue moves forward for future discussion or action.

🤝 Stay connected with FSPS-Lee and other community members working to support strong public schools.

You don't need to be an education policy expert to participate. You can simply attend, listen, learn, and become more familiar with how decisions affecting our schools are made.

Strong community engagement doesn't begin when the Board takes a vote. It begins by paying attention throughout the process.

Our schools. Our community. Our voice. 💙

Join FSPS-Lee at the workshop or tune in and stay informed about what's happening in Lee County public schools.

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early North Park Hill, Denver, CO
events.description:
Join Colorado Friends of Democracy for coffee and donuts in Park Hill. Bring your non-partisan signs encouraging folks to vote early and use  a dropbox. ("Hands Off Our Vote," "Vote Early," "Use a Dropbox," "No Kings!") We will stand on the sidewalk and wave to passersby, hand out information about voter registration, share donuts and coffee. This will be joyous, peaceful and happy event. Be there!










**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*
events.accessibility_notes: We will be standing. You are welcome to bring your own chair.

events.title: [Winton, NC] Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

Join us on October 24 as we call out the inhumanity, immorality and illegality of ICE actions and detention centers.

Meet at the Hertford County Courthouse, which is directly across from the Rivers/Winton ICE detention center. We will gather there and spread out along the road by the detention center. Bring your signs! We will also livestream the event; please register for information on how to connect.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Co-sponsors include: The Cultivator, Stop Detention Centers North Carolina, Democracy Out Loud, The Workers Circle, NC Council of Churches, Durham Congregations in Action, Fuerza Triad NC, NC Stop Torture Now.

events.title: Hop on the bus from NYC to knock doors in PA-01 to flip the House!!
events.description:
Join Swing Left on a day trip to knock doors with **Ground Truth**—our deep-listening canvassing program. We're heading to PA-01 —a must-win Swing District—to knock on doors and build trust to persuade voters to support Bob Harvie. You don’t need to be a policy expert—just a good listener!

### The Mission: Deep Listening
This isn't your standard canvass. Through Ground Truth, we are changing how Democrats talk—and more importantly listen—to voters:

- **Knock More Doors:** We don't narrowly target likely Democrats. We cast a wide net and  to truly understand the pulse of the community - and find people open to voting for Dems.
- **Deep Listening:** We have real, two-way conversations. We’re not pitching or arguing; we're listening to voter experiences, fears, and values. Then we're sharing a bit about our candidate to win them over once trust is already built. 
- **Capture Insights:** You’ll be taking detailed notes on the voters you meet. These insights help us identify persuadable voters and provide campaigns with the deep intelligence they need to win.

### What to expect:
- **The Trip:** The bus will leave Hudson Yards at 9:30am and return around 6:30pm.
- **Canvassing:** We'll be knocking on doors in the district from roughly 11:00-5:00pm with a break in the middle.
- **Preparation:** You’ll receive all training materials, location details, and support from your bus captain. You will be walking door-to-door, so comfortable shoes, a water bottle, and weather appropriate clothing like sunscreen, a hat, and an umbrella/poncho are recommended.

The conversations we have today could be the tipping point. See you on the bus! 


—

_Please note: By signing up you certify that you have read [Swing Left's waiver](https://swingleft.org/waiver-bus) and fully understand its contents. You are aware that it is a release of liability and a contract and you agree to it of your own free will._

Join Johnny and the team as we knock on doors in Bexar County to ensure everyone gets to the polls in November!

### What to Expect
This blockwalk is for anyone who is interested in having conversations with voters.

#### Everyone is welcome!
New volunteers will get plenty of support to get up to speed alongside experienced volunteers.

To ensure a smooth and high-impact event, we ask all volunteers to arrive by 10am.

[10:30am -12pm]: We will knock doors individually or in pairs. Experienced blockwalkers will pair up with less experienced ones to make sure everyone is comfortable using MiniVAN

[12pm-12:30pm]: Debrief and pack up. We will review the day's numbers, talk about what went well and what we can improve, and celebrate our success!

events.title: John Lewis: Good Trouble, Film Screening & Conversation
events.description:
John Lewis: Congressman, Activist and Civil Rights Icon. 
Sometimes change calls for a little trouble.

John Lewis: Good Trouble, as part of the film and community conversation series "Our Empowered Community Empowers Our Democracy." 

The film will be shown in the Niles Discovery Church's Sanctuary Theater. Afterward, guests are invited to the Fellowship Hall for refreshments and a community conversation about the film and what it means for protecting democracy at home.

"Protecting and securing our elections starts in the heart of every voter," said Lauren Teixeira, Co-Lead, Indivisible Fremont CA. Please join us on Saturday, October 24th, at 1 pm.

Our Empowered Community project will utilize documentary films to spark shared understanding and inspire dialogue as civic education—educating viewers while building connected, engaged communities. Focused post-screening conversations deepen this impact further, turning passive viewing into active reflection—transforming individual awareness into collective commitment and sustained democratic participation. 

IFCA is dedicated to promoting a welcoming and inclusive community, advocating for democracy and justice, empowering individuals to create positive change. To join our mailing list:  please visit, indivisible-fremont.org/join

We are EXHAUSTING our lists of Democratic voters in districts 13, 45, and 48 to make sure we get everyone to follow through on their plan to vote in this very important midterm.  Winning in these California districts is critical to the plan to gain the House majority and turn Trump into a lame duck!

On Sunday evening (5:30-7:30 p.m.), we're calling voters in districts 45 and 48 for, respectively, Congressman Derek Tran and candidate Marni von Wilpert.

On Monday evening (5:30-7:30 p.m.), we're calling voters in districts 13 and 45 for, respectively, Congressmen Adam Gray and Derek Tran. 

Whether you’re a seasoned phoner or brand new, you’ll be supported every step of the way. We use a dialer call system to make the calls more efficient so you'll need a computer, laptop or tablet and internet access to make the calls.

Bring a friend and be part of the movement shaping the future of our state and our country. Join us and help Take Back the House!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Ardmore OK
events.description:
Join us in Ardmore to rally to Vote Early.  In the final days before the midterms,  we will encourage everyone to get out and vote.

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing **our community** together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.* 

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

events.title: Hands Off Pennsylvania — Messaging & Creative Briefing
events.description:
Many of us believe that we're immune to election sabotage, or that only experts can and will ensure free and democratic elections. The truth is: We're not immune, and what happens next is up to us. 

Pennsylvanians are fed up — with data centers draining our grid, with grocery prices squeezing families, with leaders who answer to Big Tech billionaires and greedy corporations instead of our communities. We have the anger. Now we need the story, the strategy, and the people who can carry it.

This briefing is for trusted messengers — organizers, neighbors, advocates, and community members — who are ready to do the real work of building power before the midterms. We're not here to hand you a script. We're here to align on the message that moves people, give you the tools to cut through the noise, and build a concrete plan together. 

When you leave this briefing, you'll know exactly what to say, who to say it to, and what commitment you're ready to make.

events.description:
**On location in North Bend, Washington, hosted by Snoqualmie Valley Indivisible**

Bonus activity: After the training, SVI members will walk over to North Bend Way and Bendigo to do some get out the vote sign-waving!

## _Do you know what to do if you see ICE in your community?_

**This 1-hour* basic class will show you what to do if you happen to see immigration enforcement activity.** It’s like taking CPR training: you hope you’ll never need it, but it’s good to know what to do in case of an emergency.

**Topics include:**

* The role and responsibilities of a Constitutional Observer
* Key constitutional rights relevant to observation and documentation
* How to use the V.I.D.E.O. framework for clear, consistent reporting
* How to identify immigration agents
* Best practices for personal safety and non-interference

The course runs 1 hour. Please allow yourself a total of 90 minutes for the class + Q&A

This training was developed by Indivisible Eastside, Seattle Indivisible and West Seattle Indivisible, with support from ACLU-WA and WAISN.

**You can sign up and bring a friend with you to this training!** Just indicate the total number of people that you will be bringing in the "Are you signing up a group?" field when registering.

There is no parking at the bridge itself. **Please park only where it says you can park.** :)

📍 **University Park (closest — about a 15-minute walk)**
Park in the neighborhood near **Michelson Dr & University Dr**. Cross University Dr at Michelson and walk east on the University Trail to the bridge (~0.6 mi · ~15 min walk / ~5 min ride).

📍 **Quail Hill (south side of the 405 — about a 20-minute walk)**
**Quail Hill Trailhead** – 34 Shady Canyon Dr
Walk west on the Juanita Moe Trail to the bridge (~1 mi · ~20 min walk / ~5 min ride). The lot is small and fills early.

📍 **Woodbridge (north side of the 405 — about a 20-minute walk)**
**Windrow Community Park** – 285 E Yale Loop
Walk south on the Jeffrey Open Space Trail to the bridge (~1 mi · ~20 min walk / ~5 min ride).

**Overflow (longer walk, east on the University Trail):**
- **University Community Park** – 1 Beech Tree Ln (free) · ~1.75 mi · ~35 min walk / ~10 min ride

- 💧 **Water**
- 🧴 **Sunscreen**
- 👒 **Hats**

events.title: 10/10 - Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization @ Korean Festival at Discovery Green

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Election Day, November 3rd is around the corner.  Come make a huge impact with us! Approximately 85K people from all over greater Houston area attend the Korean festival at Discovery Green especially young people.  Create awareness in community about the consequential midterm election.  We have 2 SHIFTS for this event! Select the shift you are available for.  General admission is free.  

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization** shift at **Korean Festival at Discovery Green Park**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico 
- Create Midterm Election awareness
- Engage directly with voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Check voters’ status on the spot
- We will NOT register voters until after November 3rd. We shift to GOVT
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:
**Starting Oct 6th, we will NOT register voters until after November 3rd.**

_This huddle time frame is based on 1st shift so we’ll spend 30 min to huddle & 15-30 min to huddle to debrief._
 
- **[12:00-12:30pm]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals. 

- **[12:30-3:00pm] Hotspotting** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to community members, and get folks set up on Reach.

- **[3:00-3:30pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total Reach sign-ups/adds, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**: provided once registered 
- **Volunteer Parking**: more details will be provided closer to event day by host.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

- **If you are a VDR**: Your VDR certificate/number for the counties where you have VDR reciprocity. Starting Oct 6th, we will not be registering voters until after Nov 3rd so does not applied for this event

_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.description:
**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

events.title: OC Knock on doors with Ground Truth in Cerritos (CA-45)!
events.description:
Join Swing Left for a Ground Truth canvass—designed to help Democrats flip Congress in 2026, and rebuild trust for the long term. For this year, we launched an [innovative new program](https://swingleft.org/ground-truth) that will revolutionize how we connect with voters and potential voters at their doors.

At this canvass, we’ll:

- **Listen deeply** to voters’ concerns, regardless of party affiliation.

- **Persuade voters** using a data-proven approach of exchanging personal stories and making the case for how electing Democrats connects to what they care most about.

- **Gather actionable insights** for campaigns, so they can be responsive to voters’ needs and smarter with their messaging, targeting, and outreach.

Don’t worry if it’s your first time canvassing—training, materials, and support are all provided. Just bring comfortable shoes, a charged phone, and your passion for making a difference.

––

**About the program**

This isn’t traditional canvassing—it’s a whole new way of talking to voters. Together, we’ll gather authentic insights from communities, use cutting-edge tools to capture what we hear, and share it back with campaigns to strengthen their efforts.

- *Why we started early:* We launched a year ahead of the midterms to build power before campaigns were even off the ground.

- *How we’ll go big:* We’re going to a wide range of voters’ doors—not just likely Democrats—so every conversation starts to build a more complete picture of the electorate.

- *How we’ll go deep:* Canvassers practice empathetic listening and have real conversations that uncover voters’ “ground truth,” not just checking boxes on a script.

Paid for by Swing Left, Swingleft.org, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee.

events.title: Postcard Writing Party
events.description:
**Join Us for a Postcard Writing Party! 🗳️✍️**

Come write postcards that make a difference! We're teaming up with Blue Wave Postcards for an afternoon of community, snacks, and civic action.

Postcards are one of the most effective and personal ways to reach voters — and we'll have everything you need to get started: pre-printed postcards, addressed voter lists, pens, and talking points. No experience necessary, and Blue Wave Postcards volunteers will be on hand to help first-timers get the hang of it.

**What to expect:**

A brief welcome and overview of the campaign and why this outreach matters
Pre-sorted postcards and voter lists ready to go
Light refreshments and good company
A relaxed, social atmosphere — write at your own pace, chat with fellow volunteers

What to bring:

Yourself! (And a friend, if you'd like — this is more fun together)
Your own pen, if you have a favorite

Why it matters:
Handwritten postcards get noticed. Research consistently shows that personal, handwritten outreach increases voter turnout more than mailers or digital ads alone. Every card you write is a small act that adds up to real impact.

Whether you can stay the whole time or just drop by for twenty minutes, every postcard counts. We'll have a table set up so you can jump in whenever works for your schedule.

RSVP below to save your spot — we can't wait to write with you!

events.description:
Knowledge is Power is an inclusive and accessible group of progressive learners who are working to educate ourselves about the issues facing us today. From Central Ohio politics to climate change, we are arming ourselves with knowledge to actively work to better our world. More importantly, we are building community and supporting each other in these challenging times!

YOU ARE INVITED TO JOIN US! We meet monthly in Central Ohio to discuss a topic chosen by the group members. We offer multiple ways to access materials for each topic, from books and articles to podcasts and documentaries– because everyone learns best in different ways!

This topic came straight from suggestions by several group members, and it’s a hot one! For years, Gil Duran has been doing the heavy lifting of decoding and sifting through the flood of Silicon Valley weirdness. In his new book, The Nerd Reich, he pulls it all together and shines a bright light on it. Trust me, it’s even stranger than you think!  We will be reading excerpts from his recently published book, The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, as well as listening to an interview with him on the "Why Is This Happening?" podcast. The links are below.

P.S. - I am building the plane while flying it, so please bear with me.  If you have issues/suggestions/feedback, feel free to drop me an email at anaunderman@gmail.com

events.title: White Christian Nationalism: How did we get here? What can we do about it?
events.description:
Pastor Jonathan D. Riedel will lead a discussion on the origins and goals of Christian Nationalism on Saturday, October 24 at Newaygo Congregational United Church of Christ, 432 Quarterline St, Newaygo, 4937. 

The doors open at 10am for refreshments and networking, with the program from 10:30 – 11:30am. This is part 2 of Pastor Jon’s research and discussion. All religious faiths and the public at large are welcome.

The Baptist Joint Committee for Religious Liberty state that Christian Nationalism “is a political ideology that is inherently incompatible with religious freedom because it seeks to merge Christian and American identities, distorting both the Christian faith and America’s constitutional democracy. Christian nationalism is not simply about belief. It is a political project. And that distinction matters.” (https://bjconline.org/christiannationalism/).

According to Copilot Search, White Christian nationalism is a specific ideology that combines Christian beliefs with a sense of racial identity, asserting that the United States was founded as a Christian nation and should remain so, often at the expense of non-white and non-Christian populations.

“Many Christian Churches in America have been struggling with an often silent but powerful force that has affected how they govern themselves and how they interact with the world around them,” states Pastor Jon. “Many churches have been complicit in spreading white Christian nationalism out of fear and out of the hope of sparking a sort of spiritual revival. This reinforces the impact that this pernicious philosophy has had on our politics.”

National and regional faith based organizations are taking collaborative efforts to assess the effects of Christian Nationalism on their own congregations, and on the politics of our country. One such local group is Michigan Christians Against Christian Nationalism, who state “We believe that Christian Nationalism threatens our faith and country. We are an independent local group affiliated with the national organization, Christians Against Christian Nationalism, and work on awareness, advocacy and local organizing.” They have a following on Facebook under their group’s name. The National organization can be found at https://www.christiansagainstchristiannationalism.org/.

A Michigan native, the Reverend Jonathan D. Riedel is known as a “weaver of stories”, and contributes to the Fremont Times Indicator Religious Column on a regular basis. He has served Newaygo Congregational United Church of Christ since 2010. 

Pastor Jon will bring information about white Christian Nationalism from the perspective of a Christian Pastor to the program, and will discuss the counter actions needed to deal with “this distortion of the Christian Faith.”

For questions, please contact: IndivisibleNewaygoCo@gmail.com.

We'll hold the text banks in Zoom. Each text bank shift is 2 hours long, and we stay in the Zoom together the whole time to answer questions and provide support.

We'll be using a user-friendly, web-based platform called Scale to Win to send the messages, so text bankers will need a laptop, computer, or tablet (and your personal phone number will not be used for texting).

Each text bank will begin with a brief training on how to use the platform and how to respond to questions from voters. All volunteers must attend the full training during their first shift before beginning text banking, so please arrive on time! 

Additional information about the text bank, including the Zoom link, will be shared via email prior to your shift(s).

On Saturday, Oct. 17, we will text county-level early voting information to voters in eleven Down Home counties.

On Saturday, Oct. 24, we will text lower-propensity voters who have not yet voted with their closest early voting site if they live in a county with four or more sites (six Down Home counties).

On Monday, Nov. 2, we will text voters who have not yet voted with their election day polling location and hours.

Thank you for joining us!

events.title: VOLUNTEER : Atlanta Pride Parade
events.description:
Lauren Jones believes in standing by the equality and unity of the people no matter the community. She comes into Pride this year endorsed by Georgia Equality and representing District 15! Come show your support, and march with us in the 2026 Atlanta Pride Parade!

Registration: Space is strictly capped at 100 walkers, so please sign up as soon as possible to secure your spot!

Event Details: When: Sunday, October 11 Arrival & Lineup: Walkers must arrive at the assembly spot prior to 10:45 AM; no one will be allowed to enter the assembly area after 11:00 AM. Step-off starts promptly at 12:00 PM. We will be the first wave of the parade. Please plan for approximately 1 hour of walking time, but potentially more, as the 2.2 mile march takes time to complete. Logistics & Travel: Street closures begin at 9:00 AM, so we strongly encourage making travel plans now. Taking MARTA is highly recommended—the Civic Center MARTA station exits directly into the parade assembly area. If you are ridesharing, it is recommended to be dropped off at the corner of Courtland and Ralph McGill (you will be in the correct section), or at Baker St and Peachtree, and then walk two blocks up to Peachtree and Ralph McGill. Our row assignment is Row J - it includes the street section running from the intersection of Ivan Allen and Ralph McGill Blvds to the intersection of Baker Street and Peachtree. Landmark buildings nearby include SunTrust Plaza and Porfirio's. Where & Route: The parade route marches down Peachtree Street and ends at the Charles Allen Gate entrance to Piedmont Park (1320 Monroe Dr NE, Atlanta, GA), where participants will enter the park. You MUST enter the park at the end of the parade. What to Bring: Plan ahead for weather (sunscreen, rain gear, etc.), stay hydrated, and bring snacks for the march.

What to Wear & Swag: Gear Up: Deck out in your best Pride gear! You can order official Harden Pride-themed shirts and hats ahead of time at https://www.electharden.com/?anchor=ShowSupport to ensure they arrive before the parade, or wear your own Pride-themed clothing. Campaign Swag: We will provide parade swag for walkers to hand out to crowd members along the route!

Come out for an incredible day of high energy, visibility, and community celebration. Lock in your spot today!

events.title: Fold Zines to Protect the Election

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
## Election Day is coming. We must do everything we can to ensure election integrity.  

### Like what?

In his newsletter this week, Indivisible co-director Ezra Levin included  a zine called, *"What if you see ICE at the polls?"*

We don't have polls, but we *do* have ballot drop boxes. If voting rights organizations are stationing monitors near drop boxes–and they are–why wouldn't ICE? (Especially during a surge.) So, what would you do if you saw ICE near a ballot drop box?

Illustrated by acclaimed comic book artist Greg Pak, this new zine provides a pocket-sized guide on safety steps for voting, crucial First Amendment rights and protections, and what to do if you’re stopped by law enforcement. 

**This is a must-have for every voter.** 

To get the zine into the community, we need to start *now* and we need *YOUR* help to do it. 

**Please come help fold zines.** Come for 20 minutes, come for the whole session. We'll have cookies! We'll laugh! We'll feel good that we've done our part to protect democracy. 

Then, take a stack home to pass out to neighbors and friends. Put them in a Little Free Library. Leave some at you favorite coffeehouse-- you're going there anyway, so how hard could that be? 

**If you can't fold, stop by to pick up a stack to give away.**

Can't stop by? Print and fold some yourself, then pass them around. 
Find the zine [here](https://indivisible.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ice-at-the-polls-zine-v1-2026-10-05.pdf)
Find some how-to-fold instructions [**here**](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2LDyKQLEMtw)

And, most important, **VOTE**! 
Return your vote via drop box ASAP.

A democracy takes many hands. We need *yours* to help save ours. 

Hope to see you Tuesday.

events.title: 2026 Virtual Voter Workshop | Fulton County
events.description:
Voting can feel confusing, but it doesn't have to be.

Join **Mid Fulton Democrats** on **Thursday, October 15 at 7:00 PM** for our **2026 Virtual Voter Workshop**, a free, 45-minute session to help you understand what's on your ballot and prepare to vote early. 

While races like the U.S. Senate and Governor get most of the attention, lesser-known offices like Public Service Commissioner, Insurance Commissioner, and State School Superintendent directly affect your utility bills, insurance costs, and public schools.

## Here's what we'll cover:

1. **What’s On Your Ballot:** Understand each office, what it does, and why it matters.

2. **Understand the 3 Ballot Questions:** We will explain the constitutional amendments and local measures in plain English.

3. **Get Your Personal Voting Plan:** Learn key early voting details, rules for inside the voting booth (like bringing handwritten notes!), and ask questions during our live Q&A.

4. **Know your rights at the polls:** Learn what to do if you encounter ICE, federal agents, or problems while voting.

## Who Needs to Be in the Room? (Hint: You!)

**- Fulton County Voters:** You want clear answers before filling out your ballot so every selection reflects your choices. 

**- Community Champions:** You want to make sure your family, friends, and neighbors have the right information to vote with confidence.

**- Local Advocates:** You care about local issues and want to ensure our community's voice makes an impact on every level.

## Get Ready to Early Vote With Confidence 🗳️
Whether you’ve voted in every election or are still learning about local races, you’ll leave with practical information you can use and share.

Invite a friend or family member and register today to receive your Zoom link.

_Need to check your voting status, sample ballot, or polling locations? 
Visit [My Voter Page](mvp.sos.ga.gov)._

events.title: 10/14 - Hotspotting for Talarico and Voter Mobilization @TSU Tiger Walk Path

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
### Early Voting is in less than 2 weeks.  Come make a huge impact with us!  Create awareness about early voting on campus, in the community about the consequential midterm election. 

Real change in Texas happens face-to-face. By targeting high-foot-traffic hotspots—like transit centers, shopping districts, community plazas, and busy neighborhoods—we meet Texans right where they are to build lasting progressive power.

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Team Talarico Volunteers and Powered by People for a high-impact **Hotspotting and Voter Mobilization** shift at **TSU Tiger Walk Path**! This is a Talarico volunteer-led-meet-up for “hotspotting” to connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico.  We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is registered and ready to make their voice heard.

### What is hotspotting? 
Hotspotting is the process of reaching voters where they are—in everyday life, events, and where communities naturally gather.  Volunteers connect with prospective voters, check their voter registration status, create excitement for James Talarico, and develop a continued line of communication with the voters.

At this event, we will: 

- Connect with prospective voters and create excitement for Talarico and Dems down ballot
- Create awareness and provide information about upcoming midterm election - Early voting, Election Day, Ballot info and any questions students have. 
- Engage directly with student voters in high-density, high-foot-traffic areas across the community
- Check voters’ status on the spot
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Hotspotting event day schedule: 

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle.  Here is what to expect:
**Note:  Starting Oct 6, we’ll NOT register voter until after November 3rd.**
 
- **[1:00-1:30]: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, start training on time, get assigned to your hotspot location, and align on our goals.

- **[2:30-3:30] Hotspotting** | The main event! We hit high-traffic areas, talk to students & community members, and get folks set up on Reach. Create awareness in the community about the consequential midterm election. 

- **[3:30-4:00pm]: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total sign-ups, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

**We’ll table and be partisan for Talarico and down ballot Dems.  Starting Oct 6, we’ll NOT register voter until after November 3rd.  We are in GOTV mode and will be focusing on adding voters to Reach and get voters to the polls.  We’ll be outside at Tiger Walk path near Student Center.**

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### Where to Meet & Park

- **Meeting Location**:  The exact location & address will be provided once you register for the event.  We’ll be at table on Tiger Walk path near the student center address.  Well table at TSU Tiger Walk path very close by which doesn’t have an address.
- **Volunteer Parking**:  More details closer to event day.
### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing


_Note: Clipboards, pens, literature, and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a hotspotting shift today!

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early Barrington, Rhode Island
events.description:
Barrington Interfaith Partners invites you to join our nonviolent, non-partisan NO KINGS – VOTE EARLY rally on Saturday, October 17, from 12:00 – 1:00 pm. We will gather on the sidewalks lining County Road starting in front of Town Hall (283 County Rd) and stretching south to ward Police Cove Park and north toward the Presbyterian Church. Parking is available behind Town Hall, at the Presbyterian Church (400 County Rd) and in the REAR lot of St. John's Church (191 County Rd). Use caution at this last location because there will be children in the pumpkin patch! There will be a physician at the First Aid table in the flag plaza. There will be a police detail to manage traffic. and monitors along to route to answer questions and provide assistance. Bring your voices and signs.

*We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.*

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early,  is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation and bringing communities together to encourage people to make a plan to vote early and in person. 

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings. 

*No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.*

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.*

We are entering the most crucial moment of our shared project to save science and democracy in America: next month’s midterm elections.

### Stand Up for Science (SUFS) is honored once again to partner with No Kings to host and produce the official virtual and accessible rally as a launch for our sprint toward electoral victories on November 3rd. Following the speakers, we are hosting a mass get out the vote action.

- **Theo Braddy**, veteran disability rights advocate and movement leader, Executive Director of the National Council on Independent Living (NCIL)

But in this run-up to the midterm elections, accessibility is also about ensuring all voters have **access to a ballot**—in early voting or overseas voting by mail—and **access to the voting booth itself** on election day, unimpeded by Trump’s multi-front assault on our cherished American right to vote.

events.title: No Kings - Vote Early: East Greenwich, RI

We are now called repeat their patriotism, in a peaceful display of democracy. We shout "No Kings!" by voting early in Rhode Island, from October 14 through November 2, ahead of Election Day, November 3. 

October 17th is a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing the West Bay together to help every eligible voter understand their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

On October 17th, join us in East Greenwich as we gather peacefully and joyfully to get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

Bring your signs rejecting kings, corruption and voter suppression, along with joyful costumes and a cooperative spirit.

events.title: Democracy Defenders Training
events.description:
# Democracy Defenders Election Protection Training with Common Cause Arizona

## What Are Democracy Defenders?

Our Voice Our Vote Arizona's Democracy Defenders program is preparing community volunteers to help protect access to the ballot throughout the 2026 election.

This virtual training, provided with Common Cause Arizona, will prepare Democracy Defenders for election protection activities during early voting and on Election Day.

Participants will learn about:

- The role of election protection volunteers
- What volunteers can and cannot do at voting locations
- The 75-foot boundary at Arizona voting locations
- How to assist voters without interfering with the voting process
- How to recognize and document potential voting problems
- When and how to use the 866-OUR-VOTE Election Protection Hotline
- How incidents should be reported and escalated
- What to expect while serving at a voting location
- How Democracy Defenders will be assigned to shifts and locations

Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders primarily serve outside the 75-foot limit as voter helpers and line monitors. Volunteers may help answer basic voting questions, provide Know Your Rights information, monitor conditions such as long lines or unexpected closures, document problems, and connect voters with the Election Protection Hotline when appropriate.

No previous election-protection experience is required.

Training must be completed before serving a Democracy Defenders Poll Defender shift.

After training, Our Voice Our Vote will follow up with participants about available volunteer opportunities and deployment information.

## Who Should Attend

Anyone interested in volunteering with the Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders program, including:

- New Democracy Defenders
- Level 2 Defenders interested in election protection shifts
- Level 3 Captains and Captain candidates
- Community members interested in helping voters during early voting or on Election Day

## Format

Virtual training via Zoom.

Registration is required.

## What Happens Next

After completing the training, Democracy Defenders will receive information from Our Voice Our Vote about upcoming volunteer opportunities, available shifts, site assignments, and additional program-specific orientation or Q&A sessions.

Questions about Democracy Defenders can be directed to the Our Voice Our Vote Democracy Defenders Program Director.
