Join the Springfield Chapter of Neighbor to Neighbor for our Social Justice Book Club! Hosted by:  Neighbor to Neighbor Springfield Chapter

This Fall 2026, we are reading: "Emergent Strategies" written by Adrienne Maree Brown! *If support is needed to get the book, please reach out - copies available at N2N or at Olive Tree Books and Voices*

Our first gathering will be IN PERSON, on Saturday, October 17, 2026 from 6:30-7:45pm! We'll meet at the N2N Office downtown Springfield (Address: 1350 Main St., Floor 3, Suite 300)

This round, we'll discuss the first 3 chapters of the book! Readers of diverse reading levels are WELCOME!  

We intend for this book club to be a place where folks from all backgrounds can gather together around a central text and learn, connect and grow together. Social Justice is defined and understood differently by many people, but at the heart of Social Justice is the idea of equity, inclusion, power-building and change. Therefore, in addition to diving into this beautiful book, this book club will center discussion questions and themes around those ideas. The ideas shared within this book should not be considered a reflection of Neighbor to Neighbor's plans of action, but should instead be reflected on deeply by readers to guide how you understand resistance, revolution, community organizing and history as it relates to today. 

**Bring your whole self into this space** - your curious self, your radical self, your activist self into this space - heck, bring a friend (and make sure they sign up)! 

We'll bring snacks and a comfy place to connect together!

**SPECIAL THANKS TO OLIVE TREE BOOKS N VOICES for sponsoring this book club! Olive Tree is the ONLY Black Owned bookstore in Springfield, located at 97 Hancock Street, Spfld,MA. 

We STRONGLY ENCOURAGE participants to purchase/ order your copies from Olive Tree to support local entrepreneurship and small BIPOC owned businesses.

events.title: Canvass for Chris Backemeyer - Pick Up Your Walk List
events.description:
Want to knock doors for Chris Backemeyer but need to do it on your own time?

This one’s for you. Stop by and grab your own walk list, then canvass whenever it works for you: an evening after work, a Saturday morning, or a walk with your dog.

How it works:
Drop by during pickup hours.  We'll have all of the materials ready for you and connect you with a turf (just let us know if there’s a neighborhood you’d like).

We’ll walk you through the script and get MiniVAN loaded on your phone. It takes about 10 minutes.

Knock your doors on your own time, ideally within 5 days. Most lists take 1–2 hours.

Your results sync automatically through MiniVAN. Bring back any leftover lit when you've made it through your list.

What to bring when you canvass: A charged phone, comfortable shoes, and weather-appropriate layers. We’ll provide the lit and everything else.

New to canvassing? Perfect. Our short script makes it easy, and most conversations are friendly and quick. You’re welcome to bring a friend and split a list together.

With Election Day on November 3, every conversation counts. Mike Flood is counting on voters in NE-01 staying home. Let’s make sure our neighbors know there’s a choice who will show up for them.

events.title: 10/14 - HOT GIRLS READ Voter Mobilization @ Ani's Day & Night [OUTDOOR]
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **[Ani's Day & Night]**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **5:45-6pm: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **6-9:45pm Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

- **9:45-10pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.title: No Kings, No Flock

NO KINGS, NO FLOCK

This is a March and Rally against the escalating erosion of human rights in America. Flock, ICE, war, the dismantling of critical food and pharmaceutical regulations; the elite are squeezing us dry for an extra dollar. We will take to the streets and show Sonoma County representatives that we reject Flock, and that we stand with Americans all over the country who are marching for accountability and justice on this day. No Kings, No Flock, No Data Centers, no more turning a blind eye to our demands!

Where: March begins at SRJC (Santa Rosa Junior College, at the Grass on Mendocino Avenue) and ends at Juilliard Park, where a rally will take place. The march will pass by the Halloween Market at old Courthouse Square, further amplifying awareness.

Let's get out there and galvanize the county - we cannot overstate how important voting in this election is.

Hosted by Sonoma County Democratic Socialists of America, endorsed by: Yes We Can Indivisible, 50501, and Sanctuary Coalition

events.title: Vote Ready Oklahoma: Voter Prep, Practice & State Question Info
events.description:
Vote Ready Oklahoma

Oklahoma's General Election is November 3. Early voting begins October 28. Vote Ready Oklahoma is your chance to walk in prepared.

Join Indivisible Edmond and Thanks For Voting OK and Yes, It Affects You for a nonpartisan community event built around one goal: getting every Oklahoman ready to vote.

Here's what's happening on-site:

🗳️ Mock election — walk through a real ballot start to finish. Great for first-time Oklahoma voters and anyone who wants to see what to expect before Election Day.

⭐ State Questions Info Session · 7:00 PM — a plain-language walkthrough of Oklahoma's 2026 state questions, hosted by Indivisible Edmond. Just what you need to know before you vote.

✍️ Notaries on-site — Still holding your absentee ballot? We'll get it notarized so you can hand-deliver it.

📋 Sample ballot walkthrough — bring yours or look it up on-site. We'll help you understand what you're seeing before you're standing in the booth.

❓ All-Things-Election Q&A — bring any question you have. Offices and what they do. How elections work. Where to find your precinct and polling place. When and where to vote early. If it's about voting, we've got someone who can answer it.

No party. No pressure. Just Oklahomans getting ready to show up.

Tuesday, October 27 · 6:30 PM - 8:30 PM (SQ info session 7:00 PM) 
NE OKC Community and Cultural Center 

Presented by Indivisible Edmond and Yes, It Affects You · In partnership with Thanks For Voting OK

# Phonebank to Take Back the People's House for Working People in November! 

Join People's Action Power and Team '26, a coalition of movement organizations across the country, to reach the working-class voters in must-win Congressional and Senate races that will decide who controls Congress -- and whether we save our democracy. 


### 🏥 Michigan Thursdays: Will Lawrence for Congress, MI-7, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed for US Senate 

- Will Lawrence is the Sunrise Movement co-founder who helped win the largest green jobs program in US history and delivered hundreds of millions to Mid-Michigan. He co-founded Michigan Rent Is Too Damn High to win statewide renter protections. 

- Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a medical doctor who realized broken politics was making people sick, and he went to work fixing government: rebuilt Detroit's Health Department after bankruptcy, got lead out of the schools, and canceled $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders. He wrote the book on Medicare for All, and now, he's going to the Senate to make government work for you, not billionaires. 
 
The message from the primary season was loud and clear: Working Families candidates are winning. Working people aren't settling for just any candidate. They're demanding Movement Champions who answer to them, not big corporations and big money. 

Are you fired up? Sign up for the shifts leading up to Election Day. Share this link widely with your friends and family. 

No prior experience is required to join this phone bank. A laptop or tablet is recommended.

Let's go! Let's take back the People's House.

events.title: Angie for FL: Brevard Dems Turf Pickup at Rockledge HS
events.description:
We are asking you to visit Democrats (or other party affiliations that have indicated they would vote for a Democrat) in your community. We'll provide you with a list of names and addresses (aka Turfs). Most answer the door and are glad to see you. We're reminding our neighbors to make a voting plan for the midterms. Plus, many people do not realize that all Vote-By-Mail (VBM) requests are deleted every two years. Voters must proactively request a VBM every election cycle. 

Remind voters that requesting a mail ballot doesn't mean they have to use it. They can still vote in person if they prefer. It's just good to have that additional voting method in case something unexpected happens that prevents them from voting in person (hurricane, health issues, etc.). That's where we can help.

No experience needed. We'll train you. We'll pair an experienced canvasser with you until you're comfortable with your skills and knowledge. Volunteers needed to knock on doors and/or drive for a canvasser. 

Turfs are handed out, and training is scheduled during this Turf pickup event. Then, the volunteer canvasser canvasses at their own pace during the coming week. If no trainer is available to partner with you at your Turf pickup event, then call trainer Sherri Hudson (321-960-4609) to schedule a canvass training date/time.

If this is your first canvass, please download the 'Mini Van' app (and create your account; it's free) to your smartphone as this is the tool we use to canvass.

Thank you for volunteering! This is what Democracy looks like.

events.title: NO KINGS: Vote Early - Democracy Corner @ Fruitvale Ave & MacArthur Blvd in Oakland
events.description:
**Join us to celebrate early voting and election defense!** 

Stockpiling the early vote is a powerful form of election protection. On NO KINGS Day, Oct 17, we’ll spread the message that everyone needs to vote early, everyone needs to tell their *friends* to vote early, and we *all* need to get ready to defend the election. 

We'll be out waving signs for a joyful sidewalk takeover to show our voting pride, and we'll hand out flyers so that everybody understands the power they have to make a difference. 

Together we are going to smash early vote records and protect the heck out of this election!!

**Want to start spreading the word NOW about voting early?** https://www.nokings.org/nkve-resources has everything you need!

**Want to get alerts about how to defend the vote in case of major election sabotage?** Join this [announcement-only Signal group](https://signal.group/#CjQKIIENVA3mo0-RkRmJMMY6CAwzw-lPLJR9QgiLK6a1RwG3EhDh94n2beMvYZrMG17L9yaZ).

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Singing The World We Love: Hands Off Our Vote!
events.description:
We vote for us! 
Join Singing Resistance PDX in joyful defiance as we sing the world we love into action. 

One of Singing Resistance's goals is to mobilize large numbers of people into the movement to defeat authoritarianism. 

Join us at The Lantern to sing together and build community, get out the vote, and learn what you can do to move our election defense organizing plan forward. 

We need all votes on deck, and your voice matters.

"Singing doesn’t solve the crisis in front of us; it keeps us human while we face it. It steadies hands for the work, widens the room for grief, reminds the body that it belongs with other bodies." 
–Ahlay Blakely

We've got the power.
We were made for these times.
May the singing help us remember, resist, and remain.*

This is a free, all-ages, ADA accessible event. Donations to help cover the cost of the space are gratefully accepted, but not required.

sponsor.name: Robbie Hardingham for Indian River County Commissioner

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Robbie Hardingham is knocking doors in Fellsmere, and he wants you out there with him.**

Robbie's running for Indian River County Commission, and this seat is on every ballot in the county, not just District 2. His opponent is Jennifer Pippin, the Moms for Liberty chair who led the push to pull books from our school libraries. She barely got through her own primary in August, so this race comes down to who turns out. We want Fellsmere voters hearing from Robbie face to face.

**Bilingual canvassers, we need you.**
A lot of folks in Fellsmere are more comfortable in Spanish, and we want a real conversation at every door, not just a flyer. If you speak Spanish well enough to talk with a voter at the door, you're exactly who we need on this one.

Only speak English? Come anyway. We'll pair you with a Spanish speaker so every team can take any door.

**¿Hablas español? Te necesitamos.**
Vamos a tocar puertas en Fellsmere con Robbie Hardingham, candidato a la Comisión del Condado de Indian River. Muchos vecinos de Fellsmere se sienten más cómodos hablando en español, y queremos platicar de verdad en cada puerta, no solo dejar un volante. Si puedes conversar en español, eres justo la persona que necesitamos. No necesitas experiencia. Damos una capacitación rápida al empezar y salimos en parejas.

**Never canvassed before?**
That's fine. We'll train you at kickoff and you'll have a partner the whole time.

**What Robbie's running on**
- Stop overdevelopment from swallowing up our farmland and open space
- Bring the Indian River Lagoon back so people can fish it again
- Get septic to sewer help to working families, starting in Gifford
- Ban Flock surveillance cameras in our county
- Take better care of our veterans

**Election Day is Tuesday, Nov 3.**

events.description:
We are all Jane Doe!

Join us as we gather to raise awareness as we prepare for the mid-term elections. We will stand in solidarity for survivors of sexual violence, including Jane Doe at Cornell University, Kendall Francis at Louisiana State University, Epstein survivors, and every person whose experience has been dismissed. 

You don’t have to be a woman to experience sexual violence. We can all fight for changes. 

THIS FIGHT IS FOR EVERYONE!

Too often, survivors are asked to carry the burden of proving what happened to them while institutions, universities, systems, and people in positions of power fail to protect them or hold perpetrators accountable.

We're calling for systemic change and calling on institutions — from the frat house to the White House and beyond — to stop protecting abusers and their reputations at the expense of our safety.

This is a peaceful public demonstration. Participants will stay on the public sidewalk and keep pedestrian access clear.

Bring a sign, bring water, bring a friend, or simply show up. 

This a local Indivisible event!



*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

# **LET’S PARTY AT THE POLLS!** 🗳️

*Celebrate our community. Cast your vote.*

We’re turning the ballot box into a block party! Come for the community, stay for the fun, and let’s make our voices heard together. It’s time to celebrate our power and show up for the neighborhood we love.

Join the SIXTH EPISCOPAL DISTRICT OPERATION VOTER TURNOUT for a celebration of civic power, music, and community spirit!

We’re bringing the energy to the ballot box! Whether you’re voting early or on Election Day, come hang out, meet your neighbors, and celebrate democracy in action.

**WHERE & WHEN:**

📍 RON ANDERSON RECREATION CENTER 

📅 OCTOBER 20, 2026 AT 8:OO AM

**FEATURING:**

Join us for a day of free food, upbeat music, and community fun as we stroll to the Polls at our Party at the Poll!

Bring a friend, meet the community, and let’s make it count.

events.title: Election Protection (In-Person)
events.description: Free and fair elections are essential to a healthy democracy, and protecting them takes preparation, awareness, and collective action. events.description:
Community members and organizations are invited to come together in Memphis on Election Day to make sure that every Tennessee voter casts their ballot and makes their voice heard!

events.title: Utah Veterans Town Hall & Roundtable
events.description:
The Veterans of Foreign Wars, Department of Utah, presents a nonpartisan town hall and roundtable with veterans who are running for office and elected leaders from both parties. The panel will take part in a moderated discussion about veterans services, military policy, and the responsibilities shared across federal, state, and local government.

On the panel: Drew Howells, Jonny Larsen, Rosemary Lesser, Dave Calder, and Shana Anderson, all veterans and Democratic candidates, alongside Republican candidates and candidates in nonpartisan races.

Discussion topics will include:

VA healthcare accountability and access
Disability compensation and benefits reform
Veteran employment and workforce development
Housing stability and ending veteran homelessness
Government efficiency and better coordination (UDVMA and MIDA)
Strengthening Utah’s military installations and economic impact

Schedule:
6:00 to 6:45 PM: Open conversations with town hall participants
7:00 to 9:00 PM: Program

A Veterans Resource Area will be open in the lobby before and after the event, with veterans organizations, service providers, and community partners.

This is a public event. Veterans, military families, and anyone who cares how Utah treats the people who served are welcome.

Participation does not constitute an endorsement by the Veterans of Foreign Wars of any candidate or political party.

The event will be held in the MFEC 101 Auditorium

events.title: Indivisible JAX Riverside Community Gathering
events.description:
Join Indivisible JAX Riverside's monthly gathering.  Everyone is welcome. No experience required 🙂. Gather with other like-minded individuals to "Do Something."

This month .... 
## Get inspired to turn out the Early Vote

Learn how close the midterm races are from Sean Freeder, Director of UNF's Public Opinion Research Labs.   

Mr. Freeder is frequently quoted in the news as having his finger on the pulse of Florida and local elections.  Learn what the polls are saying and how we should direct our final efforts to turn out the vote.  

We still have time to make a difference.  Let's win the midterms.  Join us on Sunday and come ready to roll up your sleeves to turn out the vote early.

## About Us
 
Indivisible JAX Riverside is a non-partisan, grassroots organization focused on building a more inclusive and progressive democracy. We engage local activists, build coalitions, and advance progressive policies and candidates.

We look forward to welcoming you.

events.title: Make Your Voice Heard
events.description:
Join your community of like minded folks and make your voice heard!!!

To be heard is not just to have your words acknowledged. It’s to feel seen, valued, and understood. It’s to know that your presence matters.

Our voice is more than what we say. It’s our identity. Our power. For some, that voice shows up with bold resistance. For others, it’s the quiet courage to speak up after years of silence, to challenge injustice, and to stand in solidarity.

When we speak with clarity, we create space for connection and growth. It’s a practice that deepens how we show up in life and for others.

So let’s make our voices heard and fight for positive change!

The award-winning Declaration of Independence Banner Brigade will be participating in Vienna's Halloween Parade this year, and we'd welcome additional folks to join our group of "regulars" as we display the text of the Declaration on our artistic, home-made banners. The parade is rain or shine.

About the Banner Brigade: We're an informal group of friends/neighbors and other volunteers who have come together numerous times in the past year--with the goal of raising awareness of the Declaration's words, including our founders’ rejection of the abuse of executive powers. 

Please bear in mind that an accurate headcount is essential for the Brigade to work smoothly, so if you register—which we hope you will!—we’ll be expecting you to definitely show up, unless you notify us ahead of time that your plans have changed (we understand that last-minute things arise). There are so many banners to carry that everyone who signs up plays an important role.

We’ll meet at 5:45 for the lineup, though if you need to arrive a little later, that could be arranged. You’ll receive more logistical/attire info after registering. Hope you will join us!

This a local Indivisible event!

events.title: Poll Observer Training with Hannah Pingree!
events.description:
Join the Maine Dems Voter Access Team and special guest Hannah Pingree for Poll Observer Training on Thursday, October 22, at 2:00pm.

Poll Observers are the eyes and ears of the Voter Access Team on Election Day. When a machine goes down, a line runs long, or a voter is turned away, we only know about it because someone in the room told us. That is how we respond in time to fix it.

Training is required to be a Democratic Poll Observer, and it takes one hour. Every session covers the same material, so you only need to attend one.

## What you'll learn

- What you can and cannot do inside a polling place, and what your standing as a Poll Observer actually is
- How Election Day unfolds hour by hour, what to check on arrival, and how to observe the absentee canvass
- Where poll workers most often get registration and identification wrong, including why a student ID answers identity but not residence
- The issues that come up most often, from students and New Mainers to how a challenge actually works
- How to use LBJ, our reporting tool, and why it matters to log the problem you solved yourself
- What to do in rare situations, including evacuations and federal law enforcement near or in the polls

## Can't make this session?

Poll Observer Training runs online through October 30. See all sessions at https://www.mobilize.us/mainecoordinated/event/1021719/

## What happens next

The week before Election Day, we will assign you to a polling place and give you the contact numbers you need for the day.

## Who can attend

Anyone interested, 18 or older. You do not need to be a Maine resident.

Questions? Email the Maine Democratic Party Voter Access Team at votersupport@mainedems.org.

events.title: FROM THE NEWS TO HARD TRUTHS: Media Literacy with Janai Norman
events.description:
JANAI NORMAN USED TO DO THE NEWS. NOW SHE REPORTS UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTHS.

Former TV anchor and reporter discusses why she wants you to understand how media can be used for manipulation this Sunday on Catty Chats Live. 

If you’re like us, you’re a media cat who takes in a lot of media from mainstream and independent sources. But can you read between the lines?


Every week on Catty Chats Live, we talk to people trying to make things suck less. Janai Norman does that by teaching us how choices about the words, facts, or framing are used to tell a story change how you understand it – and even what you believe.

A former journalist, Janai spent more than 15 years with ABC, many of them as an anchor on Good Morning America Weekend. Now, she’s using her social media platform to educate us all in media literacy, lifting the curtain on the ways the news is written and reported.

We’re excited to have her share her expertise and tips with us this Sunday, Oct. 11, on Catty Chats Live. The conversation begins at 7 p.m. EST/4 p.m. PST on YouTube, Substack, and Facebook. It’s free, and we welcome your questions and comments during the livestream! Sign up now on Mobilize for more info and reminders.

In her series called “Facts & Uncomfortable Truths,” Janai shows viewers how to look at story framing, word choices, questions asked (and unasked), and more. She outlines how spotting these uncomfortable truths can help media consumers figure out patterns, giving them the tools to evaluate the media they watch and read.

Janai also uses her platform to highlight mental health, especially among Black women. In January, her memoir, “Breaking: News, Barriers, Stigmas” will be published, telling the story of her media career, the mental health episode that changed her life forever, and how she began to live in a way that honors her whole self.

We can’t wait to talk to Janai this Sunday, Oct. 11, on Catty Chats Live. Bring your questions and join us at 7 p.m. EST/4 p.m. PST on YouTube, Substack, and Facebook! Sign up on Mobilize for all the details and to get a reminder.

Learn more about Janai at her website, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube.
Watch on Substack here: https://open.substack.com/live-stream/402890

Watch on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jN7DhVudCno

events.title: Bad Faith 2026: Christian Nationalism In Power Online screening and Panel
events.description:
# FREE LIVESTREAM:  FILM & PANEL #

In the lead-up to NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY Day of Action on October 17 and the 2026 Midterm Elections, **you are invited** to the public online **premiere** of the documentary **BAD FAITH 2026: CHRISTIAN NATIONALISM IN POWER**. The screening will be followed by a live panel with film participants **Rev. Dr. William Barber II**, **Anne Nelson**, **Steve Schmidt**, and **Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove**, discussing how to combat Christian Nationalism by voting early in the 2026 election.

**Date**: Wednesday October 14

**Virtual Film Screening**: 1pm ET/10am PT

**Live Virtual Panel Discussion**: 2:30-4:00pm ET/ 11:30am-1pm PT

The live event will be **hosted by Steve Schmidt on The Warning**, with the event also shared across partner platforms.

**Sign up** to get the live stream link and invite your networks to join as well! 

## THE FILM ##
BAD FAITH is a feature-length documentary that explores the dangerous rise of Christian Nationalism in the United States. Part archival chronicle, part exposé, the film reveals the secretive political machinery that has relentlessly sought to weaken and destroy American democracy in order to promote its authoritarian vision.  Learn more at [badfaithdocumentary.com](https://www.badfaithdocumentary.com/).

## THE PANELISTS ##
### Reverend Dr. William Barber II ###
**Protestant Minister / Social Activist**

Rev. Dr. William J. Barber II, pastor and activist, co-founded the Poor People's Campaign, a National Call for Moral Revival. His organization was inspired by Martin Luther King Jr.'s last campaign in 1968, the Poor People's March on Washington demanding equal access to jobs and housing for the poor. Founding Director of the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale Divinity School. His latest book, with Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove, is *White Poverty: How Exposing Myths About Race and Class Can Reconstruct America*.

### Anne Nelson ###
**Investigative Journalist**

Anne Nelson is an award-winning investigative journalist who has written extensively about human rights and the defiance of totalitarian regimes. She is the author of *Shadow Network: Media, Money and the Secret Hub of the Radical Right*; the film's unprecedented exposé of the covert Council for National Policy and its top secret membership rolls was made possible by her ground-breaking investigative work.

### Steve Schmidt ###
**Republican Strategist**

Steve Schmidt, former Republican campaign strategist and co-founder of the Save America Movement alongside Rev. Dr. William J. Barber II and Rev. Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove. Schmidt is also founder of THE WARNING, and has been on the front lines sounding the alarm that the Christian Nationalist Republican Party under Trump is openly seeking to destroy American democracy.

### Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove ###
**Faith Activist**

Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove is an activist, associate of Rev. Barber, and author of *Reconstructing the Gospel and Revolution of Values.* Assistant Director at the Center for Public Theology and Public Policy at Yale Divinity School. His latest book, with Rev. Dr. William J. Barber, is *White Poverty: How Exposing Myths About Race and Class Can Reconstruct America.*

## Can't make the live event? ##
Sign up and we'll send you a link to the recording afterwards, available October 14th through the November election.

events.title: Legal Observer Training
events.description:
Know Your Role. Help Your Community.

📅 Wednesday, October 21, 2026
⏰ 5:00 PM
📍 Camp Verde Community Library
130 N. Black Bridge Loop, Camp Verde, AZ

🍕 Pizza will be provided!

It's time to step up and be there for members of our community.

The more we can raise awareness, accurately document what is happening, and report it, the better we can support our neighbors and help ensure situations are handled appropriately.

Join us for a community legal observer training focused on learning how to safely observe and document events and interactions involving local, state, and federal law enforcement or government agencies.

What a legal observer does — and doesn't do

We'll cover:

How to safely observe and document events

What information is important to record

How to respond if someone is detained or arrested

How to stay neutral, safe, and out of the way

What to do if something goes wrong

How we can support and protect our neighbors — the right way

Legal observers are trained witnesses. You don't need to be a legal expert or have previous experience. This training is about knowing your role, being prepared, and learning how to be there for your community when it matters.

Know Your Role. Help Your Community.

Co-sponsored by Indivisible Rimrock & Indivisible Cottonwood, Cornville & Clarkdale (Indivisible CCC).

This training is presented using ACLU legal observer training materials.

events.title: Tesla Takedown - Pop-up Block Party for Democracy
events.description:
Tesla Takedown – Pop-Up Block Party for Democracy
------------------------------------
Saturday, October 10, 2026
11:00 am – 1:00 pm
5180 Mayfield Rd.
Lyndhurst, OH 44124

This is an outdoor event – in the event of rain this will be canceled. 

NOTES:
Parking is available at Messiah Lutheran Church, 5200 Mayfield Road. Please be respectful and park on the EAST SIDE of the lot first (away from the Tesla Store). Additional parking is available at the Lyndhurst Community of Faith Church, 5312 Mayfield Road. Please enter the EAST DRIVEWAY as the west driveway is exit only. Local street parking is also just a short stroll away. Bring a chair if you need one.
------------------------------------

What is a Pop-Up Block Party for Democracy?


We’re bringing art supplies, good company, and a little civic spirit to parks, coffee houses, libraries, and other public gathering places around town. Drop in for a few minutes or stay the whole time.

Keep it as simple or as hands-on as you like. You can sit down and make something with us, grab a kit to work on at home, or take a finished piece to keep, give to a friend, or leave somewhere in your neighborhood for someone else to find. If you’d rather just hang out and chat, that’s great too. No art skills needed.


Activities change from pop-up to pop-up. Here are some you might find:

- Flock to the Polls: Crafty birds carrying a message and a QR code that helps people get ready to vote.

- Rock-ing the Vote: Painted rocks with messages about voting and democracy, made for hiding around town.

- Make & Take Yard Signs: Signs like our Ready, Set VOTE! design, with a QR code neighbors can scan to check ID rules, find their polling place, and more.

- Dogs for Democracy: A bandana or sandwich board sign for your dog, with your own message. Great for marches, rallies, or a walk around the block.

- Next 2sday Whistles: Decorative ICE whistles you can wear like everyday jewelry, so one’s always on hand. They’re also great noisemakers at rallies.

- The People’s Assembly: Make a collage about what democracy means to you. It joins a larger community art piece we’ll display in the future.

Plus other hands-on projects, depending on the day.


Defending our democracy is hard work, especially right now. Making something together is one way to find a spark of hope, and have some fun along the way. Come join us!

Doors open at 2:30pm.  There will be a talkback after the performance.

All proceeds to benefit Southend Indivisible, Renton Civic Theatre, and Riverton United Methodist Church.

events.title: Día de los Muertos Vigil at Greene County Sheriffs Office/Jail: End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos (Sunday Nov 1st), join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We will gather at the Greene County Sheriffs Office & Jail for a Vigil where we morn the loss of the 6,000 people who have been taken from our community with a display honoring those who have been taken.

Various churches around Springfield will be making a bag to honor each person who has been detained in the Greene County Jail. Bag making will take place during or following service at various churches and will be displayed outside the churches.

We will then gather the displays and bring them to the Greene County Jail for a sunset vigil.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones. We will also grieve for those how have not died, but whose lives here have ended because of the work of ICE and the Greene County Sheriff.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Justice for Wang Wang: Animal Protection Demonstration

location.venue: Sam Houston Statue at Hermann Park

events.description:
JUSTICE FOR WANG WANG 🐾

Saturday, October 17, 2026
11 AM–1 PM
📍 Sam Houston Monument at Hermann Park, Houston

We are raising our voices in Houston and looking for volunteers to help with the Justice for Wang Wang peaceful public action.

This demonstration is dedicated to Wang Wang and her puppies, CowCat, and all animals who have suffered severe cruelty. We are standing alongside advocates in China and around the world calling for stronger animal-protection laws, meaningful accountability for cruelty, and an end to animal-torture content being treated as entertainment or used for attention and profit.

Keeping these stories visible matters. By gathering publicly, we can raise awareness, encourage people to take action, and show support for Chinese activists working toward comprehensive animal-protection legislation.

What volunteers can help with

* Bring or carry signs and banners
* Join the march and chants through Hermann Park
* Hand out informational cards
* Help attendees scan petition and action QR codes
* Help at the action tables
* Take photos and document the event
* Talk with attendees and encourage people to get involved
* Help keep the group organized as we move through the park

Event plan

We’ll meet at the Sam Houston Monument and march peacefully through Hermann Park, including the Reflection Pool and Memorial Monument area, before continuing toward the Houston Zoo parking area.

Along the route, we’ll use signs, banners, chants, and conversations with the public to keep attention on Wang Wang’s case and the broader need for stronger protections for animals.

The event will also include informational materials, petitions, QR codes, and opportunities for attendees to take further action.

Main public action

SCAN. SIGN. SPEAK UP.

Attendees will be encouraged to:

* Scan the QR code
* Sign the petition supporting stronger animal-cruelty protections in China
* Learn about additional ways to take action
* Stand in solidarity with animal advocates in China and around the world

Animal torture is not entertainment. Severe cruelty should carry meaningful consequences, and stronger protections for animals can also contribute to a safer society more broadly.

Volunteer arrival

Please come ready to help wherever needed. Signs, informational materials, QR codes, petitions, and action tables will be part of the event setup.

Saturday, October 17
11 AM–1 PM
📍 Sam Houston Monument, Hermann Park

events.title: [Ann Arbor, MI] Celebrate Election Day at Bach Elementary School
events.description:
On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, Project HALO will be at Bach Elementary School in Ann Arbor to celebrate one of our most important shared American traditions with the voters who make it happen.

Swing by when you vote, or bring your family and neighbors. You'll find veterans, faith leaders, legal professionals, and community members creating a welcoming, nonpartisan presence outside the polls. It's about participation, not politics, and about our community showing up for each other.

Where: Bach Elementary School, 600 W. Jefferson St., Ann Arbor, MI 48103
When: 10am-8pm

Want to help? RSVP to volunteer for a shift. No experience is needed, and we'll cover the logistics when you arrive. As we mark the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this is what Project HALO is about: neighbors showing up for one another. Learn more at halovote.org.

This event is nonpartisan and open to everyone. Any food, entertainment, or free items are available to voters and non-voters alike.

Whether its your first time, or if you're a phone banking veteran, our team will be there to help you get connected and start making calls. Phone banking is a great way to reach voters directly and share your passion for Angie and her campaign to be Florida's next great Senator.

All you need to get started is a phone to make calls and a computer to join our meeting. That's it!

events.title: 2026 CT WFParty Virtual - Post General Elections Debrief Celebration

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Connecticut Working Families Party for a Virtual Post General Elections debrief celebration on Tuesday, November 10th from 7pm-8pm as we reflect on the results of the 2026 Connecticut General Elections, celebrate the work that made these victories possible, and talk about what comes next.

We’ll discuss key lessons from the General Elections, the power volunteers and organizers built across the state, and how we keep growing a movement that delivers for working people; on public schools, affordable housing, healthcare, workers’ rights, and more.

This is a space for volunteers, supporters, candidates, and community members to hear what happened, share reflections, and get ready for the work ahead as we build toward November.

Come celebrate, learn, and help shape the next chapter of our movement.

events.description:
The City Council is slated to approve the rezoning amendment to allow data centers in Laughlin Ranch. 

To that end, the boss City Manager, Toby Cotter, has already broadcasted his intent to create an ordinance to allow Data Centers here to destroy our water availability and quality of life with little or no regulations. 

MEC has already asked for a large power user application we believe for a data center. We have challenged them asking them if they have received an NDA (non-disclosure agreement) for this large power anticipation. 

What we are asking: 
1. Vote NO on the city's general plan on your ballot in November to slow this down! 
2. Please help us spread the word on VOTING NO on the General plan. 
3. Meet us at the City Council meeting n Bullhead City at 5:30pm. We will have signs or bring your own to show NO DATA CENTERS here.
4. Have a short statement prepared to speak on this issue OR use one of ours already prepared for you! We will have a few short statements for others to read as to why we are opposed to data centers here.

events.title: Phone Bank: Tell Kathy Hochul to say NO to the federal tax scam!
events.description:
*Our New York leaders need to hear from us now. Join our phonebanking event to tell Governor Hochul and state legislators that we refuse the federal tax voucher scam. Call today to make your voice heard!*

NY Governor Kathy Hochul is considering opting our state into a terribly harmful federal voucher tax scam that will take money out of our public schools to line the pockets of the ultra-rich. 

This federal tax scam lets wealthy families use hard-earned taxpayer dollars to send their kids to private schools. Not only does this siphon public funds away from public schools, it offers unnecessary subsidies to families who already had access to private schools. This will be detrimental to the 2.5 million students in the NYS public school system, and millions more to come in the future.

This program will drain resources from public schools, sending them to the pockets of wealthy individuals with an interest in privatizing public goods. Private schools do not have to meet the same standards as public schools, and they do not have the same responsibility to serve every child. That means public money can end up flowing to schools that lack basic accountability and can turn away students who need support. That means fewer public resources for the schools our communities actually rely on, and more power for a private system that leaves too many children behind. RSVP today to join our phonebanking event and help stop this.

events.description:
A March & Press Conference for Accountability
Tired of higher bills haunting you? WE’RE NOT SCARED ANYMORE!

Another electricity bill. Another grocery trip that costs more than the last. Another month of watching your paycheck disappear before you can even catch up.
For too many Pennsylvania families, the scariest thing isn't a haunted house. It's the cost of everyday life.
And we're done being scared into silence.
On Friday, October 30, from 3:00–5:00 PM, join GoodPower Action in Harrisburg as we take our frustration to the streets and march to the Pennsylvania State Capitol for Scary Perry's House of Bills & Chills!
We're bringing the nightmare of rising household costs to life with a larger-than-life haunted-house installation featuring the bills that keep Pennsylvania families up at night: electricity, groceries, and healthcare.
But this isn't just about scary bills. It's about accountability.
We'll spotlight Congressman Scott Perry's voting record, question the decisions affecting Pennsylvania families, and demand answers from the people elected to represent us.

Here's what to expect:
A community march to the Pennsylvania State Capitol, bringing neighbors together around the rising cost of living.
Our House of Bills & Chills installation, a creative, powerful visual showing the everyday expenses haunting Pennsylvania households.
A public press conference, featuring community voices and a call for accountability.
A chance to take action, connect with other Pennsylvanians, and show that our communities refuse to be ignored.
Bring yourself, family and friends to voice your frustration with bills that keep climbing.

With the November 3 election just days away, the stakes couldn't be clearer. Our elected officials' decisions have real consequences for our families and communities.

This election, votes have consequences. And accountability matters.

We're not scared anymore. We're getting organized.

RSVP TODAY and march with us!

We'll share additional information about the meeting location and event logistics with registered participants.

Paid for by GoodPower. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. GoodPower.org

events.description:

https://sjafs.org/calendar/floridas-resource-grab/

Investigative journalist Jason Garcia (Seeking Rents) will give the keynote. Garcia broke the Schools of Hope colocation story and exposed Ken Griffin’s role in pushing school privatization.

-Cathy Antunes (The Detail, WSLR) on megadevelopers

-Carol Lerner (Support Our Schools) on school privatization

FREE and open to the public, with free childcare.

events.description:
Join Food & Water Action to knock on doors in Congressional District 17 to take back the House and stop data centers by electing Cait Conley.

You'll get trained on how to canvass, have fun, and chat with your neighbors!

Why join us? Rep. Mike Lawler is voting away our rights to clean water, a safe climate, and healthy food.

He was among the deciding votes on the disastrous Big Ugly Bill that gutted essential services while giving handouts to fossil fuel companies and billionaires.

He voted to kick 10,000 households in his district off food assistance and to take healthcare away from thousands more.

He co-sponsored a bill to take federal funding away from local government wastewater systems and facilitate wastewater privatization, which can lead to higher bills for households and local businesses.

He voted to cut funding that would protect children from lead poisoning and to make it easier to fast-track the approval of dirty fossil fuel infrastructure and expansions (like the Enbridge pipeline that runs through his district) that will raise our utility bills.

These actions are despicable and will directly impact thousands of New Yorkers who call the lower Hudson Valley their home.

Join us to talk to our neighbors across Congressional District 17 about why Cait Conley is the best choice to win data center regulations in Congress, stop new nuclear from being built at Indian Point, and stop cuts to food assistance and clean water funding.

No prior canvassing experience is necessary. We'll train you before the canvass starts - join us!

events.title: Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
events.description:
Lee County Public Schools Coalition Launch
Saturday, November 14, 2026
1:30 PM – 4:00 PM
Fort Myers Regional Library — Meeting Rooms (Separate Building)
Fort Myers, Florida

Families for Strong Public Schools Lee invites local organizations, community leaders, parent groups, educators, advocacy organizations, and other partners to join us for a collaborative gathering focused on one shared goal:
Strengthening public schools in Lee County.

This will be an opportunity for groups from across our community to come together, build relationships, share priorities, and strategize about how we can more effectively support students, educators, families, and strong public education.

We know there are many organizations throughout Lee County already doing important work. Rather than working in separate silos, we want to create opportunities to connect our efforts, share information, identify common goals, and build a stronger coalition for our public schools.

What to Expect

Join us for light refreshments and an informal but productive conversation about:
The biggest challenges currently facing Lee County public schools
Opportunities for collaboration between community organizations
Supporting and amplifying educators, parents, students, and school
communities
Improving public awareness and engagement around education issues
Coordinating advocacy and community outreach
Identifying shared priorities and opportunities for collective action
Creating stronger communication between organizations working to support public education

This is not about every organization agreeing on every issue. It is about finding the areas where we do agree and determining how we can work together to make a greater impact.

Who Should Attend?

We welcome representatives from parent and family organizations, education advocacy groups, teacher and employee organizations, civic and community organizations, neighborhood and grassroots groups, student organizations, nonprofits, faith and community partners, and other organizations whose work intersects with our children.

In addition to viewing the film, you'll come together with a diverse group of women where we can say (scream?) the quiet part out loud, feel seen/heard/held, and walk away hopeful about making real and meaningful change for our kids' futures.

We will start with 15 minutes of pre-election somatic processing and the 75-minute screening will start promptly at 10:30AM PT / 1:30PM ET. Afterward, we'll split into (optional) small groups for discussion.

Come as you can, and come as you are. Cameras always optional. 

**As always, we will hold to Society of Working Moms' shared community values of reciprocity, generosity, authenticity, vulnerability, and empathy. (Bigotry in any form does not have a home here.)**

This event is free and open to the public -- whether you are a member of Society of Working Moms (or even a working mom) or not, you are welcome here!

events.title: Vote for Kids: Rob Sand Textbank
events.description:
Save the Children Action Network believes every child deserves a strong start in life. Our policy makers have the power to ensure more children have what they need to thrive by expanding access to high-quality early childhood education and fighting child hunger. 

That’s why we need to elect strong champions for children this year! 

Rob Sand is running for governor in Iowa and is dedicated to making kids and families a top priority. We think he is the best choice for our future. 

**Join volunteers from across Iowa for SCAN’s “Vote for Kids: Support Rob Sand” textbank** where you will have the opportunity to reach potential voters, remind them about upcoming elections, encourage them to make a plan to vote for Rob, and have a lot of fun along the way. 

With your help, we can make sure more people have the information they need to get out to vote and elect champions for children this year!

**Participation Note:** For best participant experience, we recommend joining the Zoom call on your computer, and using your computer (rather than your phone) to send text messages through our online software.

*Paid for by Save the Children Action Network, 899 North Capitol Street NE, Suite 900, Washington D.C. 20002 | Mark Shriver, Executive Director | Not authorized by any candidate, candidate’s committee, or ballot issue committee.*

events.title: SOI Leaders Monthly Meeting: Día De Los Muertos
events.description:
Día de Muertos is a beautiful tradition that allows us to remember, celebrate, and honor those who are no longer with us. This year, our observance carries a particularly powerful meaning. Across the country, we will honor individuals whose lives have been lost as a result of ICE enforcement and our immigration system.

These are not just numbers or headlines. They have names. They have families. They have stories. Their lives matter.

We hope you’ll join us as we prepare to turn this important tradition into an opportunity for remembrance, community, and action.

events.title: No Kings: Broadway, VA
events.description:
Gather at Veteran's Memorial at the corner of Broadway Avenue & Rt. 42 in Broadway! Join Willie and George to stand for freedom at the ballot box! Bring your NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY signs!

We hope to see you there on October 17th!!

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.description:
This is a weekly event. PRO Democracy and Freedom. NO WAR/ No ICE  protest. Local indivisible group: Rise ‘N Shine: Basset, Baldwin Park, West Covina, La Puente, CA. THIS IS A PROTEST, NOT A MARCH. Bring your sunscreen, your water, your sign, your friends and family, your enthusiasm!! Feel free to bring a chair. Flags are welcome!! So are bubbles and bullhorns! Don't have a sign? Use one of ours!!!

We have added NO DETENTION CENTERS, NO DATA CENTERS to our litany of issues as we stand against the atrocities in Gaza, Venezuela, and Iran. While we are focused on No War/ No ICE, you may focus on any of the horrible policies or events that you feel strongly about. Our protests are more important than ever!!!! WE STAND WITH MINNEAPOLIS!! WE STAND AGAINST THE SAVE ACT, and the $1.8 billion Slush Fund! We stand with victims against the EPSTEIN CLASS!! We stand for just representation and free and fair elections. Come for the whole time or come for a while. Just come!!!! If you can’t come, send someone else. If you can’t do that, drive by and HONK!! If you can't drive by and honk, share on social media! Together we are unstoppable!! We are meeting near the YUM YUM Donuts. There is parking in that strip mall, across the street and on the streets.

This a local Indivisible event! We will be on the sidewalk (where we can legally protest without a permit) and hopefully have enough people to occupy all 4 corners. If you arrive early, you can start or wait for others. Sometimes people arrive a little late, but they will arrive. Feel free to bring umbrellas, personal fans, spray bottles of water, pop-up tents, whatever you need to be safe. Also, bring a sweater. Wheelchair accessible. Bathrooms at Chris' burgers, and maybe other businesses as well,

IF IT RAINS THE EVENT WILL BE CANCELLED.

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.title: LIVE from the Bus, with Leah Greenberg and Skye Perryman
events.description:
Live from the bus in Pennsylvania, we are hosting a virtual call on October 13 with dispatches from our first week on the road. Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward, and Leah Greenberg, Co-Executive Director of Indivisible, will join us, and we will close with a call to take part in No Kings: Vote Early on October 17. Join us, because the vote is sacred, and democracy needs people of faith.

The Vote Is Sacred 2026 is Interfaith Alliance’s nationwide effort to protect our democracy and empower people of faith to get out the vote in the midterm elections. At the heart of The Vote Is Sacred is a cross-country bus tour, launching October 6 in Omaha and running through Election Day: a month on the road in the communities where the freedom to vote is under the most pressure, with public gatherings that platform local clergy and faith communities, election protection trainings, voter registration and canvassing anchored at the bus, and vigils standing against fear and intimidation at the ballot box.

events.title: Textbank for No on 3 - Voter Rights MA
events.description:
Don’t let billionaires buy our elections.

This November, Question 3 would replace our current primaries with a “jungle primary,” where only the top two finishers advance to the general election, even if both are from the same party. The measure is funded by a small group of wealthy donors, mostly private equity executives. It would mean less choice for voters and more power for big money, and it would shut out minority and working class candidates from the November ballot.

Voters in other states rejected this same playbook in 2024. Help make sure Massachusetts does too.

What you’ll do:

Join us on Zoom (link available upon sign up!) for a quick training, then respond to texts from fellow Massachusetts voters who’ve replied to our outreach. You’ll answer their questions, share why we’re voting No on 3, and ask for their pledge. No experience needed: we’ll provide suggested responses and support the whole time. Every conversation counts.

events.title: DAY OF ACTION
events.description:
THIS IS THE DAY BEFORE EARLY VOTING STARTS!!!
You would be surprised how many people know absolutely nothing about this election going on. They've literally never heard of Talarico or any statewide office, let alone county judge or district clerk. True story!

We need Democrats, Independents, and folks who might sit this out to show up at the polls. We need folks who know about the election and know the stakes. That's where we come in.  

Starting at our Democratic HQ at 17301 El Camino Real
2-4pm we'll be block walking in Heritage park and Autumn Lakes. this involves the MiniVAN app to help you know which house to knock and which house to skip.

4-5pm at HQ we'll be making phone calls to older voters to help them make a voting plan (vote by mail, curbside voting, where's the best polling location and more)

5-6pm we'll serve some pizza at HQ and chat about the day

6-7pm we'll go to to some very democratic leaning apartment complexes and hang our doorhanger on every door. This requires no talking to voters and no app, but may involve walking up stairs.

You can join us for any or all of the events that day.

events.title: Voter Mobilization @ The Bloc Patio Bar [OUTDOOR]
events.description:
⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!

Ready to do the work that actually works?
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact Voter Mobilization shift at [The Block]! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will:

Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
Connect with voters using Reach, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day
Shift Schedule & Flow
To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

7:30pm-8:15pm: Team Huddle | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

8:15pm -11:00pm Voter Mobilization | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

11:00pm -11:15pm: Debrief | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

How to Prepare
Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our mandatory online volunteer training on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

What to Bring
To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

A water bottle to stay hydrated

Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.title: Block Walking - Civic Engagement - Southeast Texas Minority Alliance
events.description:
# 🚶🏾‍♀️ Block Walking: Your Voice. Your Community. 🚶🏽‍♂️

**Hosted by the Southeast Texas Minority Alliance**

📅 **Saturday, October 10**
⏰ **10:00 AM – 12:00 PM**
📍 **100 Gilham Circle, Port Arthur, TX 77642**

Election Day is close, and the most powerful thing we can do right now is **knock on our neighbors' doors.** Not a text. Not an ad. A real conversation with someone who lives down the street.

Join us Saturday morning as we walk Port Arthur together, talking with neighbors about what's at stake, making sure they have what they need to vote, and reminding every household that **their voice matters.**

**No experience? No problem.** We'll pair you with a partner, give you everything you need, and send you out ready. If you can smile and say hello, you can block walk.

### What to expect
- ✅ A quick training and walk packet at check-in
- ✅ Walking in pairs or small groups — nobody goes alone
- ✅ Two hours that make a real difference

### What to bring
- 👟 Comfortable shoes
- 💧 A water bottle
- 🧢 Sunscreen and a hat
- 📱 A charged phone
- 😊 Your energy!

**Power in our community. Stronger communities, together.** Bring a friend, bring your family, bring your neighbor — and let's show up for Port Arthur. 💪🏾

👉 **RSVP below so we know you're coming!**

---

# 🚶🏾‍♀️ Caminata de Puerta en Puerta: Tu Voz. Tu Comunidad. 🚶🏽‍♂️

**Organizado por la Southeast Texas Minority Alliance**

📅 **Sábado, 10 de octubre**
⏰ **10:00 AM – 12:00 PM**
📍 **100 Gilham Circle, Port Arthur, TX 77642**

El Día de las Elecciones se acerca, y lo más poderoso que podemos hacer ahora es **tocar las puertas de nuestros vecinos.** No un mensaje de texto. No un anuncio. Una conversación real con alguien que vive en nuestra misma calle.

Acompáñanos el sábado por la mañana mientras recorremos Port Arthur juntos, hablando con los vecinos sobre lo que está en juego, asegurándonos de que tengan lo necesario para votar y recordándole a cada hogar que **su voz importa.**

**¿No tienes experiencia? ¡No hay problema!** Te asignaremos un compañero, te daremos todo lo que necesitas y saldrás listo. Si puedes sonreír y saludar, puedes participar.

### Qué esperar
- ✅ Una breve capacitación y tu paquete de materiales al registrarte
- ✅ Caminatas en parejas o grupos pequeños — nadie va solo
- ✅ Dos horas que hacen una verdadera diferencia

### Qué traer
- 👟 Zapatos cómodos
- 💧 Una botella de agua
- 🧢 Protector solar y gorra
- 📱 Tu teléfono cargado
- 😊 ¡Tu energía!

**Poder en nuestra comunidad. Comunidades más fuertes, juntos.** Trae a un amigo, a tu familia, a tu vecino — y demostremos nuestro compromiso con Port Arthur. 💪🏾

👉 **¡Confirma tu asistencia abajo para saber que vienes!**

events.title: Capitol Police Hero Harry Dunn: Defending Democracy in Green Bay
events.description:
He Held the Line on January 6th. Now He's Coming to Wisconsin to Do It Again.

U.S. Capitol Police Officer Harry Dunn stood between a violent mob and the heart of American democracy. He was called slurs, threatened, and beaten — and he didn't move. Now he's bringing that same fight to Wisconsin, because it isn't over here either.

Date: Wednesday, October 14th
Time: 2:00 pm
Location: Brown County Courthouse, 100 S. Jefferson St, Green Bay

Join State Representative Amaad Rivera-Wagner, Dr. Kristen Lyerly, Brown County Indivisible, and Harry Dunn for a powerful conversation about what it really means to defend democracy — and why that fight isn't over. Because right here at home, we have elected officials who still won't say the 2020 election was legitimate. Who voted against certifying the results. Who just joined the owners of a restaurant that organized a J6 bus from Green Bay. This isn't ancient history — it's who's representing us right now.

Harry Dunn knows exactly what election denial costs. He's lived it. And he's not backing down — and neither should we.

This event kicks off our No Kings: Vote Early weekend — three days of action in to protect this election and get Wisconsin voting early, building to the national Day of Election Action on October 17th.

This event is for anyone who believes the truth about January 6th still matters, that accountability isn't optional, and that democracy is worth showing up for.

Come ready to:

Hear directly from a Capitol Police officer who lived through the insurrection
Learn what election denialism looks like when it shows up in your own backyard
Connect with neighbors who are ready to do something about it
RSVP now to be the first to know, and to help us gauge turnout for the room we book.

This is going to be powerful and inspiring. Don't miss it.

events.title: The Long Game Screening & Talkback with SBOE Candidate Tiffany Perkinz
events.description:
# 🎬 Free Screening: *The Long Game*, Who's Really Playing With Texas Public Schools?

**Hosted by Tiffany Perkinz, Candidate for State Board of Education**

📅 **Monday, October 12**
🚪 **Doors open at 6:00 PM | 🎥 Film starts at 7:00 PM**
📍 **The Jefferson Theatre, 345 Fannin St, Beaumont, TX 77701**

State takeovers of local school districts didn't happen by accident. They're one move in a much longer game.

***The Long Game*** is an investigative documentary that traces the Texas education privatization movement from the 1970s to today, showing how decades of policy shifts turned public education into a multi-billion-dollar target. It connects the dots behind TEA takeovers, appointed boards replacing elected ones, and the push to move public dollars away from public schools.

Beaumont families know what it feels like when decisions about our kids get made in Austin instead of here at home. **This film explains how we got here, and what it will take to change course.**

### 🗣️ Stay for the talkback
Right after the film, join a **live community talkback** with Tiffany Perkinz and other **pro-public-education candidates**. Ask your questions, share your story, and hear directly from the people running to protect our schools.

### Why you should be there
- 🎥 See the story most Texans have never been told
- 🗳️ Meet the candidates fighting for public education, face to face
- 💬 Be part of the conversation in the talkback
- 👕 Pick up **campaign merch** and show where you stand
- 🤝 Connect with parents, teachers, students, and neighbors who care about our schools

Whether you're a parent, a teacher, a student, a retired educator, or someone who believes every child deserves a strong neighborhood school, **this night is for you.**

**Bring a friend. Bring a teacher. Bring a parent who needs to see this.** 💪🏾

👉 **RSVP now so we can save your seat!**

---

# 🎬 Proyección Gratuita: *The Long Game*, ¿Quién Está Jugando Realmente con las Escuelas Públicas de Texas?

**Organizado por Tiffany Perkinz, Candidata a la Junta Estatal de Educación**

📅 **Lunes, 12 de octubre**
🚪 **Puertas abren a las 6:00 PM | 🎥 La película comienza a las 7:00 PM**
📍 **The Jefferson Theatre, 345 Fannin St, Beaumont, TX 77701**

Las tomas de control de los distritos escolares locales por parte del estado no ocurrieron por casualidad. Son solo una jugada en un juego mucho más largo.

***The Long Game*** es un documental de investigación que recorre el movimiento de privatización de la educación en Texas desde la década de 1970 hasta hoy, mostrando cómo décadas de cambios en las políticas convirtieron la educación pública en un blanco de miles de millones de dólares. Conecta los puntos detrás de las tomas de control de la TEA, las juntas nombradas que reemplazan a las juntas electas y el impulso para desviar fondos públicos de las escuelas públicas.

Las familias de Beaumont saben lo que se siente cuando las decisiones sobre nuestros hijos se toman en Austin en lugar de aquí en casa. **Esta película explica cómo llegamos aquí y qué se necesitará para cambiar el rumbo.**

Justo después de la película, únete a un **diálogo comunitario en vivo** con Tiffany Perkinz y otros **candidatos que apoyan la educación pública**. Haz tus preguntas, comparte tu historia y escucha directamente a quienes se postulan para proteger nuestras escuelas.

- 🎥 Conoce la historia que la mayoría de los texanos nunca ha escuchado
- 🗳️ Conoce en persona a los candidatos que luchan por la educación pública
- 💬 Participa en la conversación durante el diálogo
- 👕 Llévate **artículos de campaña** y muestra tu apoyo
- 🤝 Conéctate con padres, maestros, estudiantes y vecinos que se preocupan por nuestras escuelas

Ya seas padre, maestro, estudiante, educador jubilado o alguien que cree que cada niño merece una buena escuela en su vecindario, **esta noche es para ti.**

**Trae a un amigo. Trae a un maestro. Trae a un padre que necesite ver esto.** 💪🏾

events.title: Baldwin Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather at the North Lake Processing Center and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones. Last December, Nenko Gantchev died at North Lake because of the GEO Group's medical neglect. On September 20th of this year, ICE killed Mario David Coronado Juárez when they pursued his vehicle in Grand Rapids. Just days after that, they kidnapped more members of Mario's family.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

A Dispatcher would sign up for a shift, then simply go about their day. 

When a local group reports a sighting they also notify the dispatcher who creates a chat group and posts that chat as a link to all the participating groups in the county. They can then monitor the chat providing informational support as needed. Once finished they close the chat.

This is open to anyone inside or outside Clackamas County and does not require you to leave the house.

Sign up if you'd like more information or would like to join us as a ClackWatch dispatcher!

events.title: No King's Protest Early Voting
events.description:
Although we do not have early voting in PA, you can get a mail-in ballot or check your voter registration status at vote.pa.gov. And it is never to early to make a plan and VOTE.

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: It's Up to Us: Early Vote Phone Bank
events.description:
It’s up to us to make sure every voter in our community has a plan to make their voice heard! Join Indivisible Ogle County for our virtual Get Out the Early Vote  phone bank. We will be reaching out to local voters to ensure they know when, where, and how to cast their ballot early and share information regarding endorsed candidates Paul Nolley and Julianna Stratton.

Whether you’re a seasoned caller or phone banking for the first time, we’ll start with a brief training, walk through the script together, and support each other live on Zoom while we make calls.

## Before You Join: Required Tech & Setup
To ensure a smooth experience, please complete these two steps before the event begins:

Create an ActionID Account:

Our calling platform uses ActionID to secure your account and save your progress. If you don't already have one, please create an account ahead of time at VAN ActionID Login. - Directions will be sent upon sign up.

Prepare Two Devices:

For the best phone banking experience, you will need two separate devices:

Device 1 (Laptop, Tablet, or Computer): To log into Zoom for our team check-in, live support, and to view the call script/voter list.

Device 2 (Cell Phone): To make the phone calls.


## What to Expect
First 15–20 Mins: Welcome, ActionID check-in, and quick training on the script.

45–60 Mins: Live phone banking with the group (on mute in Zoom, but with chat/support available if you have questions).

Final 10 Mins: Quick wrap-up, debrief, and celebrating our impact!

# Every call counts. Sign up today and help us lock in the early vote!

events.title: Flyering for Yes on 2! Money out of Politics @ Kentwood District Library

sponsor.name: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics

location.venue: Kent District Library - Kentwood (Richard L. Root) Branch

events.description:
Come volunteer to get the word out about voting YES on Proposal 2 to get corporate cash out of Michigan politics. We have an amazing opportunity to ban monopoly utilities and major government contractors from "donating" to state lawmakers... BUT we need to make sure everyone knows to flip over their ballot and VOTE YES ON 2! 

Sign up for a shift to help us inform the public at Kent District Libraries across the county. Library parking lots and sidewalks were excellent sources for petition signature collection this year, and so we also need to educate these voters on Prop 2 having gotten on the ballot now. We'll hand out literature on sidewalks, in parking lots, and under the covered entrance during rain (more than 10ft from the door). We have stickers for kids and flyers for voters as they approach the entrance. 

Come dressed in layers for rain or shine and the October weather. Tell them to Vote Yes On 2 and make the candidates work for you!
