events.title: NO KINGS: VOTE EARLY Rally in Central PHOENIX
events.description:
For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law. Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power!  
For the first time, No King is not a protest. Instead, October 17th is a day of nonpartisan voter participation!

We’re gathering from 10:30am-12:30pm in front of 7 Leaves Cafe at the northwest corner of 7th Avenue and Osborn.  (They’re democracy-lovers too!) 
We’re creating a fun, celebratory vibe to bring attention to voting early!
We’re motivating our neighbors to use their power to vote early. So bring a poster that expresses your values in a nonpartisan way
(not a political one). “Vote early” makes a great sign too!

Please dress in red, white and blue attire or fun, silly or celebratory garb. We can take away manufactured fear about voting, and voting early just by our festive appearance.

We have both a 🇺🇸 flag to wave for all and a member/artist’s gift for you that is beautifully symbolic.
We’ll also be decorating cars for a ride (or walk) to the post office following this event, parade-style.

So, on October 17th, join us to make our own local event a vibrant part of countless local events across the country as we message to get out the early vote and put people voting power front and center.

We’ll send parking guidance prior to this event along with any additional information . So please sign up ASAP. 
We’re grateful to be in this together with you!

events.title: Indivisible Crystal Lake:  Candidate Forum with Suzanne Ness and Michelle Clark
events.description:
Join Indivisible Crystal Lake for a focused, 45-minute Informational Forum as we talk with Suzanne Ness and Michelle Clark—candidates running to represent our community in the State. 

This is your opportunity to hear their visions firsthand, understand their legislative priorities, and get answers to the questions that matter most to our district.

🗓️ When: Sunday, October 18, 2026
📍 Where: Panera Bread: 5950 Northwest Highway, Crystal Lake, Illinois 60014
⏳ Duration:  3:45 pm-4:30 pm (45 minutes)
⚠️ Note: Space is limited. 35 people max. Register early.

Why You Should Attend
Hear Direct Perspectives: Get clear, concise updates on where the candidates stand on the state-level issues affecting our daily lives.

How to Submit Your Questions
To ensure that as many voices as possible are heard within our 45-minute timeframe, we will not be taking questions from the floor. 

Instead, all questions will be vetted and moderated using the following two formats:

Submit early questions: Email your questions to the host via this Mobilize event page by Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

Bring one question: Come prepared with one question to present live to our Leadership and Education Teams.


“Suzanne Ness currently serves as the State Representative for Illinois' 66th House
District. 

Prior to this, Suzanne served as a McHenry County Board Member for District 2 from 2018-2020. In her role as State Representative, Suzanne has brought more than $34 million dollars to the district and has successfully sponsored and passed 14 bills, most signed into law. 
She secured the remaining $30 million necessary for the Longmeadow Parkway Bridge, eliminating the need and therefore the burden of tolling. 

She consistently advocates for the needs of her constituents and supports legislation that has made Illinois a leader in environmental sustainability, voting rights, and access to reproductive healthcare.


Michele Clark is a former successful small business owner of a child care company and served as Chief Operating Officer of the Boys and Girls Club of Dundee Township during the COVID-19 pandemic, managing a multimillion-dollar budget and guiding her team through a critical time for families and kids.

 Today, Michele Clark is the Director of Development for the D300 Food Pantry, working to ensure no child in our district goes hungry. If elected, Michele Clark will put families, children, and seniors first.

Michele Clark knows the rising cost of living is a serious burden for families across Illinois, especially in the suburbs. From groceries and childcare to healthcare costs, it feels like people are being squeezed from every direction. 

As your state senator, Michele will fight for policies that lower costs and taxes. She is running to make everyday life more affordable for working families, believes that Springfield should work for taxpayers, not special interests, and make childcare and healthcare more affordable

Indivisible Crystal Lake is hosting Suzanne Ness and Michele Clark in an informational forum on October 18th from 3:45-4:30 at Panera in Crystal Lake. Come hear what they have to say!


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Second Line to the Polls with Claws Out NOLA, Ole & Nu Style Fellas, and Les Fous du Carnaval!
events.description:
*Party to the Polls*

Music, neighbors, and a second line to the polls to GEAUX VOTE! Let’s make an afternoon of it.

Join Claws Out NOLA, the New Orleans chapter of Cat Ladies for America, on Saturday, October 24, as we join Ole & Nu Style Fellas Social Aid & Pleasure Club, Les Fous du Carnaval, and Sportsmen’s Kids for a second line from Tremé to City Hall, early voting, and community speakers.

We’re joining **Put the Party Back in Politics** and other community partners to bring people together in a way New Orleans knows well: out in the streets, with music and good company!

Wear a costume, bring a parasol, put on your cat ears, or come as you are. Bring a friend. Bring 3! Bring ya mom’n’em! You’re welcome whether you’re voting that afternoon, have already voted, or are coming to support your neighbors.

**THE PLAN**

*This signup is for the downtown route.* [See companion second lines happening that day.](https://www.mobilize.us/mobilize/event/1039437/)

• Saturday, October 24: Gather at **12:30 pm**.

• Meeting point: **Tremé Center**, 900 N. Villere St., New Orleans, LA 70116.

• **1 pm**: Second line departs for City Hall.

• 2 pm: Parade disbands at 1300 Perdido St. Make time for early voting and speakers at the City Hall gathering.

THE ROUTE

Tremé Center → N. Villere Street → left on Basin Street → Loyola Avenue → right on Perdido Street → City Hall.

Can’t join us for the whole route? Join the second line at any point along the way, or meet us directly at City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., around 2 pm for the gathering and early voting. You don’t have to walk the parade route to participate!

GOOD TO KNOW

Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Costumes, parasols, and cat ears are encouraged, but absolutely optional.

This is a nonpartisan community event, with no candidate or political party campaigning as part of the programming. Everyone is welcome!

RSVP for gathering details and event updates.

Part of Put the Party Back in Politics’ series of community voting events. Find more at NOLA.vote.
events.accessibility_notes:

Can’t join us for the whole route? Join the second line at any point along the way, or meet us directly at City Hall, 1300 Perdido St., around 2 pm for the gathering and early voting. You don’t have to walk the parade route to participate!

We are still confirming route accessibility and the availability of accessible restrooms and seating. If you have access questions or need an accommodation, please contact Laurie / 504.410.7556 so we can discuss arrangements before the event.

events.title: Tunkhannock Community Canvass: Knock on doors with Action Together!
events.description:
Community canvassing with Action Together NEPA is about more than just knocking on doors — it’s about building real connections with our neighbors. By having one-on-one conversations, we listen to what matters most to people, share important election information, and make sure every voice in our community is heard. These conversations are proven to be the most effective way to strengthen democracy and inspire action.

When you volunteer, you’ll be part of a supportive team, get quick training, and head out together to engage with your community. It’s a fun, energizing way to make new friends, build skills, and create real change right here for NEPA families. Let’s make sure that local voices shape the future of our region!

One more reason to canvass: all of our canvass volunteers get a free t-shirt! Be sure to include your size when you sign up so you can complete your fit when you head out with the team to knock on doors.

events.title: Anytime Virtual Phone Bank - Rachel Grage for Congress (FL-05)
events.description:
Help Team Grage reach voters before Election Day!

Click the "Get Started" button on this event to open our phone bank where you can start making calls anytime you wish between 8am-8pm, 7-days a week.

If you need training on the OpenVPB system and other aspects of phone banking, please attend our Tuesday phone bank.

events.title: Friendbank to get out the Early Vote with Fitchburg Progress
events.description:
Bring a phone! Bring a friend! We’ll be connecting to friends, coworkers, and neighbors with reminders about early voting and the Fall Election on November 3rd. **YOU are the best messenger** to people in your circle because they know and trust you.

We have calendars, campaign notes, amendment explanations, and the REACH app to help make sure you have the answers your friends need to be informed voters. Drop in and help us get out the early vote. Every single vote will matter to elect Dems up and down the ballot!

Drop in and join us at these friendbanks:

- October 13 9:30-11:30am Fitchburg Library

- October 18 Noon-1:30pm Barriques

- October 20 1-3pm Rolling Pin Bakery

- October 27 6:30-8pm The Rusty Bee

events.title: USF Stroll to the Polls
events.description:
Join us as we walk together to vote early at the USF polling site on campus! We will be meeting on campus at the Crescent Hill Patio and then walking over to the voting site on campus to cast our votes together!

Not sure what is on your ballot? Join us! We will go over everything that's on your ballot and help make sure that you make the most informed decision at the ballot box. Lets make sure our voices are heard this election!

Email mackenzie@peoplepowerfl.org with any questions.

As attacks on voting rights and democracy continue, communities must be prepared to protect access to the ballot box safely, strategically, and collectively. events.title: Team Shawn P2P Text Banking Kickoff: Get Ready for Early Voting!
events.description:
## Help Reach Voters in GA-14! Get Ready for Early Voting!

**Early voting begins October 13**, and Team Shawn is launching our **P2P Text Banking Program** to help voters across Georgia's 14th Congressional District get ready to cast their ballots!

Personal conversations can make a difference, and text banking is one of the easiest and most flexible ways to get involved. From your own computer or tablet, you can connect with voters, share reliable election information, answer questions, and help people find out when, where, and how to vote early.

**Join us for Team Shawn's first P2P Text Banking Kickoff and Training!**

**During this session, you'll:**

- Learn how peer-to-peer (P2P) text banking works.
- Get trained on our campaign texting platform.
- Learn how to share early voting information and respond to voter questions.
- Send your first messages with support from our team.

**No previous campaign experience is required!** We'll provide training, instructions, and approved messages. The texting platform protects your personal phone number, and you can participate from home.

Once you're trained, you'll have opportunities to join future text banking efforts. Whether you have 30 minutes or several hours, there are ways to get involved that fit your schedule.

**Ready to help voters in GA-14 get ready for early voting? Sign up today for our first P2P Text Banking Kickoff!** Get trained, send your first texts, and help connect voters with the information they need to make their voting plans.

**Leadership Matters!**

events.title: Setauket GOTV Postcard Party
events.description:
Sign up and bring a friend to join Team Gallant and community members to write and address postcards to voters about Chris Gallant's record of service and the November 3rd election! 

We will provide everything, but we please ask that you bring some postcard stamps to share with the group!

Hope to see you there!

events.title: Atlanta  Día de los Muertos Day of Action - End the ICE Age
events.description:
This Día de los Muertos, join us to honor and remember the lives taken by ICE and Border Patrol — and to demand an end to the violence.

We'll gather and grieve publicly for the people who have died in ICE custody and been killed by ICE and Border Patrol agents, drawing on the Día de los Muertos tradition of honoring loved ones.

This action is part of End the ICE Age, a national day of action happening in cities across the country October 31–November 2. We're demanding Congress get ICE out of our communities, redirect ICE funding, and shut down ICE detention centers for good.

A core principle behind all Disappeared In America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Member Messages: Nevada State AFL-CIO Postcard Writing Party
events.description:
When was the last time you received a handwritten letter in the mail? When was the last time you got one from a union brother or sister reminding you to vote? A handwritten postcard to a union member from a union member can do a lot – and is proven to get people to the polls. 

For this important election, the Nevada State AFL-CIO is throwing a postcard writing party for union members to union members. Join us! We’ll have messages ready to go (but encourage you to put your own spin on it), addresses already printed, and everything prepared for you to make an impact. You’ll get to hang out with a group of fellow unionists, write a few post cards, and have a whole lot of fun doing it. What could be better?

Join us for an evening of union solidarity - dinner provided.

events.title: Patio Party for Justice: Re-Elect Judge John Stevens!
events.description:
# 🍸 Patio Party for Justice: Re-Elect Judge John Stevens!

**With special thanks to our hosts: Bernsen Law Firm & Gilbert Adams Law Offices**

📅 **Thursday, October 15, 2026**
⏰ **5:00 PM – 7:00 PM**
📍 **Hearsay's on the Patio, 461 Bowie Street, Beaumont, TX**

Wrap up your workday the right way. Join friends, neighbors, and supporters on the patio at Hearsay's for an evening of good company, great conversation, and a chance to stand behind one of the most experienced judges in Southeast Texas.

**Judge John Stevens** has spent his career making sure our courtroom works for everyone:

- ⚖️ **20 years** as a federal prosecutor
- 🏛️ **19 years** as Criminal District Judge
- 👩🏾‍⚖️ Presided over **620+ felony jury trials**
- 📂 Disposed of **50,000+ criminal cases**

That kind of experience doesn't happen overnight, and it's worth keeping. Come meet the Judge, enjoy the patio, and help power his re-election campaign.

### Why you'll want to be there
- 🤝 Meet Judge Stevens in a relaxed, friendly setting
- 🌆 Enjoy happy hour on one of downtown Beaumont's favorite patios
- 💬 Connect with community leaders and fellow supporters
- 🗳️ Help keep experience on the bench!

Drop in anytime between 5 and 7, and bring a friend! 🥂

👉 **RSVP below so we know you're coming!**

events.title: Knock Doors with Team Manny and Mo Dower for HD 64
events.description:
Come knock doors with Manny Rutinel for Congress and Mo Dower for HD 64!

Manny is a longtime advocate and attorney who grew up working class. And now he’s working to ensure our communities have an honest shot at success. As a State Representative, attorney, and former economist for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, he’s learned that making progress requires working with others and working hard to get things done. He plans to use facts and evidence to fight for working families and deliver results that make your life better.

Mo Dower grew up the daughter of frugal, Depression-era parents in a suburb surrounded by farm fields—running the neighborhood until nightfall while also milking cows on Christmas Eve—an upbringing that instilled a strong work ethic, a practical mindset, and a passion for caring for humans and animals. As a large animal veterinarian, she spent her career working alongside horse owners, farmers, and ranchers, later becoming a nationwide subject matter expert for complex medical cases—demanding work built on quick thinking and showing up to get the job done. She's carried that same mindset into raising her family in Northern Colorado and into her service as a Berthoud Trustee and Mayor Pro Tem, which reinforced her belief that leadership should be grounded and community-focused, not driven by personal gain, and that public servants should represent their constituents as fellow citizens.

events.title: Wifi Coop in Gaza City - Learn, Engage, Support
events.description:
Support grassroots democracy and lifesaving opportunities in Gaza City.

Since 2024, Jreas Lab has run a free wifi and training center for students and freelancers in Northern Gaza, yes, in the midst of bombs and destruction.  It is now re-forming as a democratically run cooperative and needs your support.  You can simply learn about this incredible group, the resilience of the remote tech team and the students learning under difficult circumstances; and also volunteer to practice English together, and perhaps share the story with those in your network who might be interested in hiring contractors or who could help as board members or advisors.

Having access to the Internet is a lifeline for many who have every other avenue cut off.  And they have learnings about risk management you could not believe.  Learn and discuss how this kernel of hope and action can grow.

events.description:
Join us at Tuesday, October 13th, from 6 PM to 8 PM to make signs for the upcoming Early Voting event. Art supplies will be provided.

Feeling frustrated with the state of the world? Come turn that frustration into art, community, and a little resistance! ✊

Join us for a No Kings, Vote Early poster-making party! Whether you're a seasoned protester or nervous about attending your first event, this is a low-pressure way to meet people, make connections, and get involved at your own pace.

 Come for the arts and crafts. Stay for the community.

We'll have poster-making supplies available, but feel free to bring your own if you have something special in mind. Make something funny, bold, creative, or impossible to ignore!

events.title: 10/11 - Voter Mobilization @ Oak Lawn UMC (Indoor)
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift at **Oak Lawn United Methodist Church**! We have been invited to an after-service tabling and are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with congregants
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **11:45am-12:00pm: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **12:00am-1:00pm Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

- **1:00-1:15pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable shoes and casual attire

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

events.title: Door Bellingham - No Hate in WA State
events.description:
This is a special event to join canvassers across Bellingham for a fun morning Kick Off where you can hear from local organizers and elected officials before you begin knocking for No Hate in WA State. We will attend the kick off together and then we will knock doors together as a group!

Join Speaker of the House Laurie Jinkins, Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove, leaders from around the state, community activists, and volunteers to knock doors to help stop the statewide initiatives funded by a conservative hedge fund manager.

This day includes a rally, a canvass training, and door knocking, followed by volunteer appreciation. Food and drinks will be provided. No experience needed; we’ll train you!

SATURDAY, OCTOBER 17 – DoorBELLINGHAM
Hotel Leo, Bellingham
Starts at 11:00 am

What to expect

New to canvassing? That’s completely okay! No experience is required, and we’ll start every shift with a short training so everyone feels prepared before heading to the doors.

We’ll meet together at the Community First Whatcom office, go over the basics of the conversation, show everyone how to record who they spoke with at the door, and get paired up before heading out to canvass in the community.

For your first shift, you can shadow an experienced canvasser so you can hear how they talk with folks at the door and get comfortable before jumping into conversations yourself.

Most of the shift will be spent walking through a neighborhood and having short conversations with voters. You do not need to memorize a script or be an expert. We’ll provide the information, materials, and support you need.

Please bring:

A fully charged smartphone Comfortable walking shoes Weather-appropriate clothing Water and anything else you may need while walking

Additional details, resources, talking points, MiniVAN instructions, and arrival information will be sent after signup so you have everything you need to feel prepared for your shift.

Why door knocking matters

Most of us have had an election where the ballot showed up and we realized we hadn’t researched everything on it yet, or where voting almost slipped our minds altogether. One of the most effective ways to help people participate is simply reaching them before their ballot arrives, having a one-on-one conversation, and making sure they know what is on the ballot and why it matters.

Those conversations can make a real difference. Here in Whatcom County, the 2026 primary for the 42nd Legislative District Senate race came down to just four votes between two candidates.

If knocking on doors sounds intimidating, know that canvassing is typically a really positive experience. We’ll be reaching out to voters who regularly participate in elections and having short, friendly conversations with people in our community. You’ll also be out there alongside other volunteers, not doing it alone.

## 🎉 It's a Party at the Polls! 🎉

Voting isn't a chore. It's a celebration, and we're throwing the party!

Grab your friends, your family, your church crew, and your neighbors, and join the **Southeast Texas Minority Alliance** for an afternoon of food, fellowship, and community spirit during Early Voting. We'll be outside **two Beaumont early voting locations** with good food, good music, and good people. Then we'll walk in and vote **together**.

**Saturday, October 24, 2026**
**Noon – 3:00 PM**

**Johns Library**
4255 Fannett Rd, Beaumont, TX 77705

Texas requires an approved photo ID to vote in person. Acceptable forms include:
- Texas Driver's License or Texas Personal ID Card
- Texas Election Identification Certificate
- Texas Handgun License
- U.S. Military ID with photo
- U.S. Citizenship Certificate with photo
- U.S. Passport (book or card)

Don't have one? You can still vote by signing a *Reasonable Impediment Declaration* and showing a supporting document, such as a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or voter registration certificate.

When we show up together, we're stronger. This is our community, our county, and our future. Let's celebrate it, protect it, and vote for it, side by side.

events.title: Urgent Opposition to Livestreaming Nidal Hasan’s Execution – Write to Your Members of Congress NOW!
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Dear Representative [Last Name],

I am writing as your constituent to express my profound objection to the Pentagon’s announced plan to livestream the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, scheduled for December 3, 2026. This would be the first military execution in more than 60 years and the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century. I strongly urge you to publicly oppose this decision and to exercise congressional oversight to prevent the Department of Defense from turning a solemn act of military justice into a public spectacle.

I want to be clear: my objection is not rooted in sympathy for Hasan or in any doubt about the gravity of his crimes. He murdered 13 unarmed soldiers and wounded more than 30 others at Fort Hood in 2009, and he has never claimed innocence. The families of the victims and the survivors deserve justice and closure. But justice and spectacle are not the same thing, and the decision to livestream this execution is a profound mistake that will harm our nation’s moral standing, endanger our security, and undermine the very principles we claim to uphold.

The livestream would violate fundamental human rights standards.

The United Nations human rights office has warned that livestreaming an execution would amount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition on torture under international law. A UN spokesperson described the prospect of a government executing someone “in front of live cameras” as “abhorrent”. Amnesty International has condemned the plan as “reprehensible,” noting that international human rights bodies have long found public executions incompatible with the prohibition on cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. The United States should not join the ranks of nations that carry out public executions; according to Amnesty International, only Iran and Afghanistan are known to have done so in 2025. This is not who we are—or who we should aspire to be.

The livestream would make us less safe, not more.

Senator Jack Reed, Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, has warned that livestreaming the execution “only gives the shooter what he wants: more attention and more control” and that it is “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters”. Congressman Jason Crow, a former Army Ranger, has similarly stated that a public execution “only gives our adversaries fodder for anti-American propaganda that makes us less safe”. Hasan has said he acted to stop soldiers from deploying to Afghanistan; broadcasting his death to a global audience would hand extremists a powerful recruitment tool and validate their narrative that America is at war with Islam. The last thing our national security needs is a propaganda victory for those who wish us harm.

The livestream would degrade our military and our legal system.

Army Regulation 190-55 governs who may witness military executions and does not provide for unrestricted public attendance. There is no regulation or precedent for a military execution to be livestreamed, and experts have noted that public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instill fear and demonstrate government power. Republican Senator Thom Tillis has said that public executions are what “oppressive dictatorships do” and called the plan “beyond disgusting”. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy accused the Secretary of Defense of “mimicking ISIS”. When lawmakers from both parties use the same language to describe an American policy that they use for our enemies, something has gone deeply wrong.

The livestream would traumatize victims and survivors.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former Army sergeant who was shot seven times during the attack and who plans to attend the execution in person, has said he does not agree with making the event publicly available without censorship. The families of the fallen and the survivors deserve to mourn and to seek closure in a manner that respects their dignity, not to have their trauma broadcast to the world as entertainment. As Senator John Curtis has warned, a civilization “erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment”.

What I am asking of you. I respectfully urge you to take the following actions:

1.	Publicly denounce the Pentagon’s plan to livestream Hasan’s execution and call on Secretary Hegseth to reverse the decision. Bipartisan voices—including Senators Reed, Tillis, Murkowski, and Curtis, and Representatives Crow and Smith—have already spoken out. Your voice would add needed weight.
2.	Exercise congressional oversight. The House and Senate Armed Services Committees should demand transparency regarding the legal authority for this livestream, the financial arrangements (including any potential monetization), and the consultation process that led to this decision. A letter from former national security officials has already raised serious questions about whether the execution could be used for “commercial gain or partisan political propaganda”. Congress must investigate.
3.	Support legislative or regulatory action to ensure that no future military execution is livestreamed or otherwise made available to the public for entertainment or political purposes. The default should be the solemn, limited-witness procedure prescribed by Army Regulation 190-55.

The death penalty itself is a matter of serious moral and legal debate, and I respect that Americans of good faith disagree on it. But whatever one’s position on capital punishment, livestreaming an execution is beyond the pale. It is cruel, it is dangerous, and it is beneath the dignity of the United States. Hasan’s crimes were horrific, but responding with a public spectacle does not honor his victims—it exploits them. It does not strengthen the rule of law—it makes a mockery of it. And it does not make us safer—it makes us a recruiting poster for our enemies.

I urge you to act swiftly and forcefully. Please let me know what steps you plan to take.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Email Address]
[Phone Number]


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Scranton
events.description:
**Join Action Together NEPA for this local No Kings: Vote Early event!** 

This time around, No Kings actions will look a little different — that's a good thing! Instead of large scale rallies, we're hosting opportunities to take action and get out the vote. Let's help folks make their plan to vote, whether that means finding a drop box, voting on-demand at a county polling site, or getting their ballot in the mail with enough time to arrive by Election Day!

**We're taking the power that we've built in NEPA over the last two years and turning it into action.** We'll have a brief speaking program, get everyone fired up, then split off into ways that attendees can help Get Out The Vote!

We'll be at Courthouse Square in Scranton, then we'll invite folks to head to Black & Brass for some GOTV activity! We encourage all attendees to support the downtown Scranton businesses while you're in the area for No Kings. Let's truly make this a day of community! 

Note: this event is crossposted on Mobilize on the national No Kings map so more folks can find it! If you see it there, please be aware that yes, it's all the same event!

**We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.**

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to reject the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

Because no one person gets to decide our leaders before voters do. On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

No Kings: Vote Early events are nonpartisan and are designed to increase participation from all eligible voters.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

events.title: Indivisible Boca Raton presents “Immigration at a Crossroads”
events.description:
Immigration detentions by ICE and local law enforcement is surging in the country, South Florida, and in Palm Beach County. Family separation is rampant, detention centers are overcrowded and ripe with serious human rights abuses. People are dying from ICE shootings and in ICE custody.

The data shows that the overwhelming majority of the immigrants being detained are hard-working, family oriented, and net contributors to our community. They are our neighbors, not criminals.

This immigration enforcement regime can only exist by taking away people’s constitutional rights and by covering up their immigration operations from public view. On Monday, November 16, 6:00- 7:30 PM, at the Dr. Andre Fladell Civic Center, 16700 Jog Rd., Delray Beach, FL 33446 come hear the experts.
Moderator: Barbara Eriv, Indivisible Immigration Coalition (PBCIIC).
The current immigration policy landscape and possible policy change opportunities from the 2026 midterms and into the 2027 municipal election-Renata Bozzetto, Deputy Director at the Florida Immigrant Coalition
A profile of the immigrants in our community and the effects from family separation: Ruth Rosa MACP, Post-Release Services Clinician at Urban Strategies.
The legal and constitutional rules of the current administration and impacts on detainees and families-Jennifer Smith, Senior Litigation Attorney at Americans for Immigration Justice.
The longer term consequences to our community and economy-Philip Lewin, Associate Professor of Sociology, Director of Graduate Studies at the Florida Atlantic University (FAU)

events.title: Protect the Vote: Volunteer & Poll Observer Info Session (On-Demand)
events.description:
# Get Involved in Voter Protection: On-Demand Info Session

Whether you're brand new to voter protection or have volunteered with us before, this on-demand information session is your entry point into the North Carolina Democrats' Voter Protection Team.

**Watch anytime, at your own pace, and learn how you can help protect the vote in 2026.**

### Learn How You Can Protect the Vote

We'll introduce you to our Voter Protection program and the different ways you can get involved, then take a closer look at one of our biggest volunteer programs this fall: **Poll Observing**.

You'll learn what Poll Observers do, what to expect at the polls, how training and scheduling work, and how you can help protect the vote in your community.

### More Ways to Get Involved

Poll observing isn't the only way to help! We also have opportunities to support voter outreach and education, volunteer recruitment, voter assistance, and behind-the-scenes program operations.

Whether you're ready to sign up or just want to learn more, this session will help you find the role that's right for you.

### How It Works


### How It Works

This is a **recorded, on-demand information session**, not a live Zoom meeting.

After registering, you'll be directed to the recording so you can watch whenever it's convenient for you.

**Please note:** This is an introductory information session, not Poll Observer Training. To serve as a Poll Observer, you'll need to complete the separate required training.

### Ready to Take the Next Step?

- **Become an Inside Poll Observer:** Register for a [live or on-demand Poll Observer training](https://tinyurl.com/NC26PollObserver).
- **Explore other volunteer opportunities:** Find [upcoming Voter Protection trainings, phonebanks, and events](https://tinyurl.com/NC26VoProEvents).

Questions? Contact **pollobservers@ncdp.org**.

events.title: Gwinnett: Election Protection Training
events.description:

Help support Georgia voters this election season by joining Common Cause Georgia, Latino Community Fund, and GALEO for a poll monitoring training. Learn what to look for at polling locations, how to document potential issues, and how to help voters access election protection resources.

During this training, you’ll learn how to:

 - Monitor polling locations and use our poll monitoring checklist.
 - Identify and report potential voting issues.
 - Share information about the Election Protection hotline: 866-OUR-VOTE.
 - Prepare to volunteer during early voting and on Election Day.

No prior experience is necessary! We’ll provide guidance and resources to help you feel prepared for your volunteer shift.

Light refreshments will be provided.

Come learn, connect with fellow volunteers, and help support voters in your community. We hope to see you there!

Whether you’re a longtime volunteer or joining us for the first time, this is a great way to meet like-minded people, make a real impact, and help power a people-first campaign.

What to expect: Brief training before we head out. Canvassing in solo or in pairs. Campaign materials provided. A fun, welcoming environment for both new and experienced volunteers!

What to bring: Comfortable walking shoes, water bottle, fully charged phone, sunscreen/hat if needed - your energy and enthusiasm! Every conversation matters — come help us turn out voters and keep fighting for the future Florida deserves.

events.title: American Motherhood Tour: Film Screening of No Country for Mothers
events.description:
Comunidad Materna en Utah is hosting a screening of a documentary about what motherhood really looks like in America today.

This isn’t just about watching a film; it’s about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we’ve been carrying quietly, and realize we’re not alone.

Here at Comunidad Materna we are dedicated to connecting mothers with the resources and support they need to thrive. Our mission is to strengthen and empower expectant mothers through maternal health education, access to resources and continuous support throughout pregnancy, birth and postpartum. 

We invite all who share our passion and would to connect with us in this work. Together we can make the world a better place for mothers, and in-turn make a better world for everyone. 

Would love for you to join.

Comunidad Materna en Utah organiza la proyección de un documental sobre cómo es realmente la maternidad en Estados Unidos hoy en día.

No se trata solo de ver una película; se trata de compartir un espacio donde podamos expresar en voz alta aquello que hemos llevado en silencio y darnos cuenta de que no estamos solas.

En Comunidad Materna, nos dedicamos a conectar a las madres con los recursos y el apoyo que necesitan para prosperar. Nuestra misión es fortalecer y empoderar a las futuras madres mediante la educación en salud materna, el acceso a recursos y un acompañamiento continuo durante el embarazo, el parto y el posparto.

Invitamos a todas las personas que compartan nuestra pasión a unirse a esta labor. Juntos podemos hacer del mundo un lugar mejor para las madres y, a su vez, un mundo mejor para todos.

Nos encantaría que nos acompañaras.

events.title: Texas Together Volunteer Community Night: Organizing for Talarico & Hinojosa
events.description:
Looking for your people this election? 

Join us at the Fort Bend office for Volunteer Community Night - a weekly gathering for anyone who wants to connect with neighbors and make a real difference before November 3.

Whether you've knocked hundreds of doors or have never volunteered before, there's a seat for you. Come meet the volunteers already organizing, hear what's on the ballot, and learn how James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa, and Democrats down the ballot are fighting for Texas families.                                                                         

At each Community Night you'll:
• Meet other volunteers who live near you
• Learn about the races and candidates on your ballot
• Ask questions and share what you're hearing in your community
• Plan a block walk or other event with others.
• Get trained and leave ready to do your part before election day.

From time to time, special guests - including candidates and campaign leaders - may stop by to meet volunteers. Watch your confirmation emails for updates.

No experience needed. Bring a friend, bring your questions, and bring your neighbors. Light refreshments provided.

We win this election one conversation, one door, and one neighbor at a time. Let's do it together.

events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization** shift outside of the Zoo**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **10:30-10:45am: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **10:45am-1:00pm Voter Mobilization** | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

- **1:00-1:15pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

Make a friend. Find someone. Come for the drag. Leave with a voting partner.

​Rope In The Vote is a Pride Eve drag night with Pepper Insult, Gyna Gunt, and Byanka Bangsum. Kick off Pride weekend with drinks, speed friending, Ballot Bingo, prizes, and a room full of people who all showed up for the same reason you did.

​Ballot Bingo comes with a bonus — a brand-new Chatham County chapter of LGBTQ+ Democrats of North Carolina launches that night! Want in? Say yes on the form when you register, or on the interest card at the door. That card is also your door prize entry.

​About those prizes: two 5-day passes from Pittsboro Yoga at The Plant are up for grabs! The rest are surprises, but a hint: they could help with some pride weekend purchases at The Plant.

​Not playing? Come anyway! Seats for the games in the Wheelhouse are limited, but there's plenty of room to hang out: the Fair Game tasting room is right next door and the whole Plant campus is yours to roam. Grab a drink, make a friend, and socialize before Pride weekend gets going.

​​Come hungry. Grab dinner from Ta Contento or Kingston 99 before doors open, then find us in the Wheelhouse, the room right off the Fair Game tasting room. After bingo we spill out into the Fair Game tasting room for a last hour: get to know your new friends, make a plan to vote, plot your Pride weekend together.

Hosted by Cambridge Indivisible Resistance. Joined by BVOCAL singers. 
We ally ourselves with the national NoKings Vote Early day on Oct 17th.

Those who sign up here will be notified of any changes due to weather. 

In Massachusetts, Oct 17 is the first day of the early in-person voting for the Nov 3 general election. 

.Please join us as we encourage passersby to vote early and register to vote if they haven’t. After 30 minutes in Harvard Square of holding signs, handing out flyers, and a few songs, we will walk a leisurely 0.5 miles to the main library -- one of 3 Cambridge in-person early voting sites. At the library we will join another vote-early group.

Why Vote Early?
       1.  More flexibility: In Cambridge you can vote in person 7 days a week between Oct 17 – Oct 30.
        2.  Avoid any Election Day problems: bad weather, sickness, last-minute glitches, or disruptions.

How to Vote Early in Cambridge:
In person
https://www.cambridgema.gov/departments/electioncommission/earlyvoting/earlyvotinginperson

By ballot drop boxes 
https://www.cambridgema.gov/departments/electioncommission/earlyvoting/ballotdropboxes

By mail
https://www.cambridgema.gov/departments/electioncommission/earlyvoting/earlyvotingbymail

We decide who represents us. We decide what comes next.

For more than a year, millions of people have come together to REJECT the idea that power belongs to kings, billionaires, or politicians who believe they are above the people and the law.

Now, we are taking the next step, turning people power into voter power. Unlike previous No Kings actions, No Kings: Vote Early, is not purely a protest. Instead, on October 17th, it's a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard.

No king gets to pick our leaders. The choice is ours through the vote.  On October 17th, join us in local events across the country as we get out the early vote and say it loud: no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

events.title: 10/11 - Meet the Candidates @ The Texas Greenhouse w/ Vikki Goodwin & Clayton Tucker
events.description:
_⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTE: Powered by People is halting all voter registration activities at our events from October 5 (the Texas voter registration deadline) to Election Day. During these events we will be helping voters make a plan to vote and answer their questions ahead of this important election!_

### Ready to do the work that actually works?

In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered. We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.

Join Powered by People for a high-impact **Voter Mobilization & Town Hall** shift at **The Texas Greenhouse with Vikki Goodwin & Clayton Tucker**! We are showing up to talk to voters, spark meaningful conversations, and make sure every eligible Texan is ready to make their voice heard.

At this event, we will: 

- Engage directly with attendees/passerby's
- Ask people if they are active and have a plan to vote
- Connect with voters using **Reach**, our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day

### Shift Schedule & Flow

To ensure a smooth and high-impact day, please plan to arrive early for our team huddle. Here is what to expect during your shift:

- **11:45am-12:00pm: Team Huddle** | Arrive early to grab your materials, meet the team, and align on our goals for the event.

- **12:00am-1:30pm Voter Mobilization & Town Hall** | The main event! We engage community members, check their voter status, add people to Reach, and immediately answer questions related to the upcoming election (poll locations, time, ballot, etc.)

- **1:30pm-1:45pm: Debrief** | We will reconvene, tally our total number of Reach adds, make sure all voters are texted and tagged, celebrate our wins, and talk about next steps.

### How to Prepare

Before you arrive, please make sure you attend our **[mandatory online volunteer training](https://www.mobilize.us/poweredxpeople/event/908390/)** on Zoom. This training will get you fully up to speed on the flow of our events and teach you exactly how to navigate the Reach app.

### What to Bring

To set yourself up for a successful shift, please bring the following items:

- Your fully charged smartphone with the Reach app already installed

- A water bottle to stay hydrated

- Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

_Note: Literature, giveaways (when applicable), and training cheat sheets will be provided during the huddle_

Let's keep building our momentum across Texas. Sign up for a Powered by People voter mobilization shift today!

## ** Join NE Lake County Indivisible Outreach & Elections Teams for our final prep push before No Kings 4: Vote Early!**

The fight to protect voting rights never ends, and right now, we’re witnessing a Jim-Crow-era effort from politicians and their billionaire friends to restrict our freedoms, silence our voices, and consolidate power.

But in America, we choose our leaders. We will decide our future. The same spirit that fueled Selma, Montgomery, and the March on Washington lives on in our unified action.

NELC-I will be handing out non-partisan voting zines with information on why voting is so important and how to vote in Lake County, along with Know Your Rights information if you see ICE. We’ve printed 10,000 copies, so we need your help to fold and prepare them for distribution! 

Join us for socializing, fun, and doing our part. We will provide all training and supplies, so just bring yourself (and a friend or two). We have just 1,000 to go but only 4 days until No Kings so we need your help!

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Some quotes from past participants:
- "It was great working with like minded people who care so much about what's going on in our country. We want and are working for change that helps all Americans"

events.title: Write to Win: Postcard Party with SETX Democratic Women

Texas elections are won and lost by small margins. Personal outreach raises turnout, and turnout is how we win in Jefferson County and across Southeast Texas.

**Let’s Knock Doors for Tina Kotek—with Special Guest Shasti Conrad!**

Join us for a canvass kickoff with Shasti Conrad, Chair of the Washington State Democrats and Vice Chair of the Democratic National Committee! We’ll hear from Shasti, get fired up, and head out to talk with our neighbors about reelecting Tina Kotek.

Adopted from Calcutta and raised in rural Oregon by a single mom, Shasti’s commitment to building a stronger, more inclusive democracy has taken her from organizing campaigns to serving in the Obama White House. She’s worked on four presidential campaigns and made history as the first woman of color and youngest person to lead the Washington State Democrats—and the first South Asian woman to chair a state Democratic Party anywhere in the country.

Under her leadership, Washington Democrats won every statewide office, reelected every Democratic congressional incumbent, and expanded their legislative majorities in 2024. Now she’s bringing that organizing energy back to Oregon to help us turn enthusiasm into votes for Tina Kotek.

The conversations we have at the doors can make the difference in this race. Whether you’re a seasoned canvasser or joining us for the first time, we’ll make sure you have what you need to get started.

events.title: GOTV Canvass for Virginia Democrats in Culpeper County!
events.description:
This is it: the final stretch before Election Day! 🗳️

Months of work come down to these final days. From Saturday, October 31 through Election Day on Tuesday, November 3, the VA26 Coordinated Campaign will be knocking every door we can across Madison, Culpeper, Greene, and Orange counties to re-elect Senator Mark Warner and Congressman Eugene Vindman.

These last few days are all about turnout. We’ll talk with supporters to make sure they have a plan: where their polling place is, what time they’re going, and how they’re getting there. On Saturday, we’ll get folks to early voting before it closes. On Election Day, we’ll knock until the polls close at 7pm.

What to expect:

Quick welcome and canvass training (first-timers welcome!)
Walk lists and materials provided
Team up with fellow volunteers, so nobody knocks alone

What to bring:

A fully charged phone with the MiniVAN app downloaded
Comfortable walking shoes and weather-appropriate clothes
A friend or two. Every extra pair of hands means more doors!

events.title: Indivisible ADK/Saratoga Chapter meeting:  Hands Off Our Vote!
events.description:
In addition to the usual benefits of attending a chapter meeting (joining together in community, staying in the loop about the ways in which we're organizing, and learning the ways you can get more involved), we will be offering an informational meeting about **Hands Off Our Vote!**  

Join us for this very special event with **We Get Out the Resistance**, one of our local organizing partners!

We know that Trump and his Big Lie cronies are plotting to do everything they can to undermine our elections in 2026. Whether it’s trying to end mail-in voting, targeting registration programs, blocking vote-counting, even trying to ban states from encouraging people to vote – it’s going to be no-holds-barred from them this year as they try desperately to block the free and fair elections.

But we’re going to cut through the noise, and we’re going to be ready for whatever dirty tricks they try. And we’re going to do it with community power and preparation, not panic.

There is only one force powerful enough to topple a dictator: **WE THE PEOPLE!!**

*Hands Off Our Vote is Indivisible’s national program to ensure all eligible voters get to cast their ballot, and that those ballots get counted. With our new PowerPoint we’ll help you be ready to respond to any attacks.*

Please note that this is a HYBRID MEETING! **You will receive a zoom link after you complete your registration**, in case you'd prefer to join us virtually.

*Indivisible ADK/Saratoga is a local chapter of [Indivisible](http://Indivisible.org), active in NY's Warren, Washington, and Saratoga counties, that welcomes people with our shared values and goals. We organize and mobilize for actions that safeguard and advocate for vulnerable communities, protect human rights, guard our planet, elect progressive candidates, and protect democracy. We are committed to non-violence as a guiding principle in everything we do.*

Find us online:

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in Ridgecrest
events.description:
**The No Kings Alliance is mobilizing urgent, nationwide action in response to the Republican government shutdown. Join us this weekend as we provide mutual aid and care to our neighbors hurt by the Republican government shutdown.**

Right now Republicans are refusing to protect critical healthcare and nutrition programs which will result in 42 million Americans losing the benefits that keep their families fed. When those in power hoard resources and use our government to punish people, we answer with collective care and resistance, feeding our bodies and fueling our movement.

Join us at 132 N China Lake Blvd from 9-11am to donate food, household, and personal care products to support families in need. Donations will be delivered to Salvation Army.

Salvation Army has requested the following goods: Rice-a-roni, Cup of noodles, pasta, canned protein (tuna, chicken, beef, beef stew), cereal & granola bars, cans of nuts, boxed cookies & crackers, dried fruits, beef jerky, dry milk, bottled water, mac & cheese, single serving cups of fruit & pudding, cereal, oatmeal packets, and jelly/jam (no peanut butter, they have enough.)

Donation drop off by the shopping center sign.

Find more out about our group at ridgecrest50501.com

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in WHITTIER,CA!
events.description:
Join the Whittier Indivisible Chapter at Michigan Park in Whittier, CA on November 15th, from 11-12:30pm to gather together and DONATE non-perishable food to support families in need. 

Our Chapter will also host a fundraising campaign for the entire month of November to help those in need - ALL proceeds to the Chapter will be sent to a local food pantry. You can donate here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblewc1368840224

Let us support and love on our community! Thousands in our own cities will be affected by the ending of SNAP benefits, and we want to help them. Will you join us?

Additionally, if you cannot make this Mutual Aid Drive & Potluck event on November 15th, we will be hosting various “pop-up tables” throughout the La Habra/Fullerton/Whittier areas to gather donations throughout the month. Please view our Facebook and Instagram pages for information on locations of these tables. All donations will be delivered to the Santa Fe Springs Interfaith Food Center.

All attendees will be sent more details, including the specific list of necessary food items, upon registration! We hope to see you there.
**PLEASE NOTE: We will be hosting TWO FOOD DRIVES at Michigan Park: November 15th and November 22nd (which is why you will see 2 Mobilize events.)
Thanks for joining us!
